item.title: Team Amnesty - Event Day Volunteer
item.description: Team Amnesty is a network of human rights defenders who come together to support Amnesty International UK’s human rights work at various challenge events around the UK. Team Amnesty comprises of our incredible event participants who run, cycle, trek, swim, weight lift and much more all to raise vital funds for Amnesty International UK’s human rights work, and also our fantastic event volunteers who offer inspirational support to our participants on the day through dedicated and enthusiastic cheering, cheerleading, camaraderie and organisational skills. We are looking for reliable, organised and enthusiastic individuals to join our Team Amnesty Event Day Volunteer Team to cheer on and support our event day participants. If you are interested in volunteering with Team Amnesty and providing support on event days, please fill out the form below: Sign up be an Event Day Volunteer with Team Amnesty Please note: volunteers for our events must be based in the UK. Due to limited capacity, we will not be able to respond to applications from overseas. Thank you in advance from the Community and Events Fundraising Team
item.dc:creator: Amnesty International UK

item.title: Student leader – Student Action Network Committee (multiple positions available)
item.description: The right to protest is under threat. Across the UK and beyond, governments are restricting dissent and criminalising activism. It is becoming harder for people to speak out, and students are on the frontline of that shift. Amnesty UK’s Student Action Network (STAN) brings students together to fight back, and student organising is at the heart of that work. We’re looking for Student Leaders to join the STAN Committee and help lead our student movement. Campuses are often where the chilling effect is felt most, but they’re also where collective action can make a real difference. This is a role focused on organising. You’ll work with student groups across the country, supporting them to take action, run campaigns, and build momentum around issues like Defend Dissent and wider human rights work. As part of the committee, you’ll take responsibility for a region of the UK. That means building relationships with student groups, helping them grow and developing leaders, and connecting their work into a wider national movement. You’ll also help shape national campaigns and moments where students come together to organise and take action. The aim of the STAN Committee is clear: to build a strong, visible student network that can respond to threats to human rights and create real pressure for change. Nations: Wales, Northern Ireland, Scotland England Regions: North East, North West, Midlands, South East, South West, London. You believe in the power of students coming together to create change, and you want to play a role in making that happen. You might already be involved in activism, or you might be looking for a way to take that next step. What’s important is you’re someone who takes initiative, works well with others, and is motivated to support and inspire those around you. You don’t need extensive experience in campaigning or organising. What matters most is your commitment to human rights, your willingness to learn, and your ability to bring energy and creativity to the work. You’re interested in the challenges facing the right to dissent, and you’re excited by the idea of helping to build a strong, student-led response. You want to develop your leadership skills, support others to take action, and be part of something collective, purposeful, and impactful. This is a chance to develop real organising skills while being part of a movement that's fighting for something important.

item.title: Rehoming Centre Manager
item.description: Rehoming Centre Manager Beagle Welfare is looking for an experienced, compassionate and highly organised Rehoming Centre Manager to lead the daily operation of our Rehoming Centre, based in Burton-on-Trent. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a visible difference to the lives of beagles, adopters, volunteers and colleagues by creating a centre where excellent welfare, effective rehabilitation and successful rehoming are at the heart of everything we do. As the lead on site, you will manage and develop staff and volunteers, oversee safe and efficient centre operations, and help ensure every beagle in our care receives the right support to progress towards a happy, secure future. You will also represent Beagle Welfare externally and contribute to the continued development of our rehoming work across the UK. About the role You will be responsible for the leadership, performance and smooth running of the Rehoming Centre, including staff and volunteer management, health and safety, site maintenance and the implementation of operational procedures. With rehoming at the centre of your decision-making, you will use data, strong people leadership and sound operational judgement to help improve outcomes for beagles and the people who care for and adopt them. Key responsibilities · Lead, motivate and develop a committed team of staff and volunteers, creating a positive, inclusive and high-performing culture. · Oversee day-to-day centre operations, ensuring high standards of dog welfare, customer service, health and safety, security and compliance. · Drive rehoming activity by supporting case progression, promoting beagles effectively and helping minimise the time beagles spend in our care. · Manage resources, reporting and administrative processes accurately and responsibly. · Build productive relationships with adopters, visitors, animal welfare organisations, and community partners. · Use data, feedback and quality assurance processes to identify improvements and support consistent application of procedures. About you We are looking for a confident manager with experience leading diverse teams, delivering against targets and managing a varied operational workload. You will be comfortable working around dogs, including beagles with different welfare and behavioural needs, and able to balance compassion with practical decision-making. Strong communication, organisation, collaboration and stakeholder management skills are essential, as is experience in supporting continuous improvement. You will also need a UK manual driving licence and be comfortable driving our van. Experience in a kennel or animal welfare environment would be advantageous, but above all you will share Beagle Welfare’s commitment to improving the lives of beagles and supporting the people who care for them. Working pattern and location This role is based at the Rehoming Centre and offers employment that includes employer provided accommodation (3-bedroom cottage) as part of the compensation package. The centre operates between 08:30 and 17:00 every day of the year, so weekend and bank holiday working will be required on a rota basis. Why join Beagle Welfare? You will join an organisation driven by purpose, teamwork and a shared commitment to dog welfare. This is a hands-on leadership role where your decisions, energy and care will directly support better outcomes for beagles, adopters, volunteers and colleagues.

item.title: Outreach Manager
item.description: Location : Remote; able to travel into London easily Beneﬁts : Flexible working, private healthcare, 35 days annual leave (in addition to bank holidays), £500 contribution towards work laptop Reporting to: Director About the Schools Consent Project The Schools Consent Project is a UK-based charity dedicated to educating young people about sexual consent and healthy relationships. We deliver workshops in schools and educational settings led by trained volunteer lawyers. By introducing consent literacy at school, young people are more likely to make informed, ethical decisions and are less likely to experience or perpetrate sexual violence in later life. Through this hire, we aim to scale access to high-quality consent education. Role Summary The Outreach Manager is responsible for driving the expansion of the Schools Consent Project’s reach, engagement, and impact across London and the South East. Acting as the organisation’s lead “sales” and business development professional, you will contribute to and manage our strong pipeline of partner schools and organisations, convert leads into confirmed bookings, and maximise long-term engagement. You will own the end-to-end outreach and partnership journey: from prospecting and lead generation, through relationship development and negotiation, to repeat engagement and retention. Key Responsibilities Business Development & Lead Generation • Develop and execute a proactive outreach and growth strategy to increase workshop bookings. • Develop and maintain relationships with existing schools; ensure SCP’s workshop content remains responsive and reactive to the emerging concerns of young people when it comes to sex, consent and the online world. • Generate leads through cold outreach, referrals, events, and campaigns. • Contribute to and maintain a pipeline of new schools and educational settings. • Reinvigorate historic relationships with schools. Account Management • Convert enquiries and prospects into confirmed programme partners. • Present the charity’s offer and impact to senior school leaders, safeguarding leads, and decision-makers. • Manage key accounts and ensure high levels of partner satisfaction and retention. • Promote additional workshops and programmes where appropriate (eg. teacher training; parent workshops). • Track booking trends eg. seasonal vs. reactive bookings; develop a communication strategy around each ‘type’ of school, involving timely booking reminders. Pipeline, Targets & Performance • Manage outreach targets for bookings, partnerships, and regional coverage. • Monitor conversion rates, pipeline value, and performance metrics. • Produce regular forecasts and performance reports. • Use data and insight to refine sales strategies and improve outcomes. Marketing & Promotion • Help develop compelling outreach materials and campaigns. • Deliver presentations, webinars, and pitches to prospective educational partners. • Represent the organisation at conferences, networks, and sector events. • Help gather case studies, testimonials, and impact data to support outreach and fundraising. Delivery Coordination • Work closely with our Volunteer Manager and Operations Manager to match supply with demand. • Ensure smooth handover from booking to delivery. • Anticipate capacity constraints and manage partner expectations. Team Leadership & Development • Contribute to the development of outreach systems, processes, and tools. • Share insights and learning across the organisation. • Oversee team members currently managing school outreach. Person Specification Essential Criteria • Proven experience in sales, business development, partnerships, or outreach roles. • Experience working with schools, education providers, or youth services. • Track record of meeting or exceeding targets. • Excellent communication skills. • Strong relationship management and account development experience. • Highly organised, with strong CRM and data management skills. • Ability to work autonomously and drive results. Desirable Criteria • Experience working in the charity, education, or public sectors. • Knowledge of safeguarding and child protection frameworks. • Understanding of social impact measurement. Values and Approach We are looking for someone who: • Is committed to our mission and values. • Demonstrates empathy, professionalism, and integrity. • Works collaboratively and inclusively. • Is proactive, adaptable, and solution-focused. Safeguarding and Equality The Schools Consent Project is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. We ask applicants to draft their applications without using AI (save for checking spelling or grammar), so that we can get a real sense of your suitability for the role.
item.dc:creator: Schools Consent Project

item.title: Co-CEO (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Job description Responsibilities People and Team Leadership Line manage the Fundraising Manager, providing regular supervision, support, and performance development Lead the planning and delivery of all-hands meetings and team development programmes, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team culture Maintain oversight of team resource mapping, ensuring capacity is well-managed across the organisation Impact and Evaluation Lead the design and ongoing development of Routes' impact evaluation framework, ensuring it captures meaningful data about the difference our work makes Oversee the collection, analysis, and interpretation of impact data throughout the year, using findings to inform programme development and organisational decision-making Write and produce Routes' annual impact report, communicating our work and outcomes compellingly to funders, partners, and the wider sector Income Generation Support the Fundraising Manager with grant applications, funder relationships, and income generation activity as needed Manage the sales pipeline for the mentoring programme, including prospecting, relationship development, and conversion of corporate and organisational clients Source and manage CSR partnerships, building relationships with corporate partners and ensuring existing partnerships are well-stewarded Operations Lead on the creation, review, and approval of organisational policies, ensuring Routes' policies are up to date, legally compliant, and reflective of our values Oversee day-to-day office administration and organisational housekeeping Manage organisational insurance, ensuring appropriate cover is maintained and reviewed annually Oversee staff IT, laptops, phones, and software subscriptions, including troubleshooting and managing supplier relationships Draft and manage organisational contracts, including supplier, partner, and service agreements Lead on the conversion of Routes from a CIC to a CIO, working with legal advisors, the board, and relevant statutory bodies to manage the process Strategy Contribute to the development and delivery of Routes' organisational strategy, bringing insight from your areas of responsibility Lead on the development and implementation of Routes' income generation strategy, working closely with the Fundraising Manager and Co-CEO Communications Leadership Development and Learning Take ownership of your own professional development, using the annual training budget to attend relevant training, events, and sector learning opportunities that strengthen your contribution to Routes and the wider sector There are some areas of responsibility that sit under the other Co-CEO, but we would expect the person in this role to maintain some oversight or involvement in to enable smooth co-working between the roles. These are: Safeguarding: Act as Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) when required, ensuring Routes meets its safeguarding obligations and that staff and volunteers are appropriately supported Finance: Attend and contribute to monthly finance meetings, planned by other Co-CEO, maintaining a clear understanding of the organisation's financial position and flagging any concerns to the Co-CEO and board Person Specification Experience Experience in a senior leadership role within the charity, social enterprise, or public sector Demonstrable experience of managing and developing staff, with a coaching and supportive leadership style Experience of income generation in a charity or social enterprise context, including either grant fundraising, corporate partnerships, or programme sales Experience of designing or overseeing monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks and producing reports that communicate impact clearly Experience of managing operational and governance responsibilities, including policy development and working with a board Experience leading teams in challenging, fast-changing and resource-constrained environments Experience of working with or for communities facing marginalisation, discrimination, or structural disadvantage, and a deep understanding of the barriers refugee and asylum seeking women face in the UK Skills and Knowledge Ability to balance day to day operational oversight with long term strategic planning, ensuring that Routes’ work remains in line with values and objectives whilst responding to the changing needs of participants and the external landscape Strong written communication skills, with the ability to write compellingly for different audiences Financially literate, with the ability to read and engage meaningfully with management accounts and budgets Highly organised, with the ability to manage a broad and varied portfolio without dropping the ball Comfortable working with data, both quantitative and qualitative, and using it to draw meaningful conclusions Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to build trust quickly with a wide range of stakeholders including funders, corporate partners, board members, and colleagues Sound understanding of CIC/charity governance and good practice, and the ability to make confident decisions independently while knowing when to consult Values and Approach Deep personal commitment to gender equality, racial justice, and the rights of refugees and asylum seeking people Understanding of the importance of implementing trauma informed practices and a commitment to accessible working practices for all A collaborative leadership style that builds trust, shares power, and brings out the best in others Comfortable with ambiguity and change, able to hold complexity without becoming overwhelmed by it Honest, transparent, and accountable, someone who says what they mean and follows through on commitments Energised by working in a small, values-led organisation where everyone mucks in Additionally, it would be desirable for you to be trained as a Designated Safeguarding Lead, but training on this can be provided. A Note on Experience We know that leadership experience takes many forms, and that people from marginalised communities, including those with lived experience of the asylum system, are often underrepresented at senior levels in the charity sector despite having exactly the qualities and understanding this role requires. We warmly encourage applications from people who may not follow a conventional career trajectory but who can demonstrate the skills, values, and commitment we are looking for. If you are unsure whether your experience is the right fit, please do get in touch before applying, we would rather have that conversation than miss out on the right person. item.title: Helpline Care Navigator - South and South West Region
item.description: Job Purpose This role offers an opportunity to play a vital part in sustaining our Helpline service, which sits at the heart of the support we provide to people living with PSP & CBD. As Helpline Care Navigator (HCN), you will act as the first point of contact for individuals, families and health professionals across the West and South West. You will deliver compassionate, person-centred support and clear, practical information via telephone and email, ensuring people affected by PSP & CBD feel heard, informed and supported at every stage of their journey. Alongside direct support, you will actively engage with health and social care professionals, neurology clinics and wider partners to strengthen local awareness of PSP & CBD and enhance referral pathways across the region. This is a key role in maintaining continuity, quality and momentum within our Helpline service and you will be reporting to the Helpline and Support Services Manager. Contract Type Full Time – permanent contract (6 month probationary period) Salary £27,500 per annum Hours of Work & Annual Leave 35 hours per week - this may include working some unsociable hours, including evenings and weekends. 28 days plus bank holidays. Pro-rated for part time role. The main office is in Milton Keynes, and we have a hybrid working policy with staff expected to spend one day a week in the office and the remainder can be worked from home. HCN’s currently work from the office on a Wednesday. There is flexibility in the arrangements that need to be agreed upon with the line manager. Key Responsibilities To be ‘first point of call’ for people with PSP & CBD and their families living in the West and South West Region including Shropshire, Herefordshire, Warwickshire, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, Hampshire, West Sussex, East Sussex, Dorset, Somerset, Devon, Cornwall, Avon, Isle of Wight. Providing people with support and information over the phone and via email. To raise awareness of PSP & CBD across all health and social care disciplines in he region by engaging with HSCP’s and neurology clinics. To provide accurate information in all aspects of PSP & CBD in response to enquiries and signpost onto other organisations where appropriate. Ensure a maximum response to all helpline calls, emails and enquires. To keep clear and accurate records and statistics of enquires received and actions taken. To carry out a maximum number of proactive calls to people affected by PSP & CBD within the region as directed by the Helpline Manager. Develop and maintain the existing database of key health and social care professionals and regional services. Attend outreach events to build the profile of PSPA services amongst health and social care professionals. To deliver awareness and learning sessions to HSCP’s within your region Work with the Director of Policy and Influencing to identify ways in which services and care can be improved for families affected by PSP & CBD in the region. To signpost to PSPA Support Groups and services. Liaise with external services to signpost to local support. Take an active part in the delivery and planning of information and support events, which may include the possibility of overnight stays and weekends. Liaise with the fundraising team to signpost to fundraising activities. Liaise with the Volunteer Coordinator to maintain and build volunteering in the region. To attend and contribute constructively to team and other meetings as required. To ensure the implementation of policies, procedures and quality standards as defined by PSPA. Contribute to the development of literature and articles for PSPA Matters. To undertake any other tasks, by agreement as required, in support of the work of PSPA. The duties may be changed and/or varied to meet changing circumstances at the discretion of the CEO and Board of Trustees. Person Specification Essential Criteria: Experience in delivering helpline and/or information and support services Excellent listening and interpersonal skills, with the capacity to listen actively understanding different points of view Ability to keep accurate records Willingness to undertake training and continuing personal development Experience of and sensitivity to communicating with audiences from a range of backgrounds Strong IT skills, with experience in MS Office products and customer relationship management software Flexible and reliable attitude and the ability to self-organise and to work without direct supervision Good communication skills, both oral and written and excellent telephone manner Ability to manage difficulty questions, emotions and situations in a calm and confident way. Desirable Criteria: Knowledge of PSP & CBD or other neurodegenerative diseases and/or experience of working in the NHS An understanding of Safeguarding and an ability to follow relevant policies and procedures Knowledge of healthcare or social care systems. item.title: Legacy and In Memory Manager
item.description: A fantastic opportunity has arisen within our award-winning fundraising team, to join us in an exciting new role of Legacy and In Memory Manager (Lead). At Birmingham Women’s and Children’s Hospital Charity, we believe there’s always more we can do for our sick kids and women, and that’s why we will always strive to do more for our patients and families. It’s our mission to raise the vital funds needed to make a real difference to all who use our hospitals, and to make our hospital feel just like home. This role requires someone with experience in legacy administration and promotion and/or in memory fundraising, as well as excellent communication skills and a strategic mindset. We need someone with previous experience in relationship management and income generation - ideally within a legacy and/or in memory setting - who is able to lead and inspire our supporters and staff in order to generate long term income and awareness for the charity. To be successful in this role you will: Lead the development and delivery of legacy marketing and in-memory fundraising strategies to drive sustained income growth and supporter retention Be self-motivated, independent and target-driven Act as the subject matter expert on legacy administration and in-memory giving, providing guidance, training, and mentoring while promoting a strong culture of philanthropy Manage all aspects of legacy casework, including complex and contentious cases, ensuring effective stakeholder relationships and full compliance with legal, regulatory, and best practice standards Oversee data management, reporting, and analysis to generate insights, improve processes, and support accurate forecasting and long-term financial planning Collaborate across teams to maximise fundraising opportunities, enhance donor engagement across channels, and deliver impactful events and integrated giving initiatives Posses a natural confidence in talking to people with high emotional intelligence and resilience due to the sensitive nature of the role, with excellent communication and relationship building skills. What we offer: Flexible and hybrid working to support work-life balance Generous annual leave entitlement with additional leave for long service Enhanced sick pay Enhanced Maternity and Paternity Pay Employee Assistance Program and Lifestyle Savings Free flu jabs Cycle to work scheme Charity events throughout the year Employer enhanced auto-enrolment pension scheme with 8% employer contribution Ongoing commitment to education and professional development The Charity is committed to equal opportunities and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/belief, sexual orientation or age. Successful candidates will have access to vulnerable beneficiaries therefore the role is subject to Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) clearance. If you think you have the qualities we are looking for and the desire to contribute, please download the Job Vacancy Pack and then send us a CV and covering letter explaining how you meet the criteria for the role and making clear why you would like to be considered for it. PLEASE NOTE: Within our organisation, this role is titled Legacy and In Memory Lead . This reflects our internal structure and does not change the scope or responsibilities described in this advert. We will conduct interviews as suitable candidates apply and we're ready to hire if we find the right person before the job ad closes.
item.dc:creator: Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital Charity

item.title: Community Action Coordinator (Manchester)
item.description: Job description Join a passionate and committed team driving forward social justice through women-led community organising! The successful candidate will support Community Savers groups and networks in North Manchester and Wythenshawe achieve their goals for financial and social inclusion, mental wellbeing, community led development, participatory decision-making, and housing and climate justice. You will work through a community-led process to: build strong community associations develop common visions and area action plans build membership and support capacity building among young women aged 18-30 raise small grants funding identify priorities for skills development and learning exchange help coordinate evidence-based advocacy projects keep appropriate records of meetings and events capture and communicate learning, progress, and impacts. You are: Experienced in working in neighbourhoods with long term health inequalities. Good at building trusting relationships while maintaining boundaries and being mindful of your own levels of resilience. Passionate about social justice and championing community expertise. Compassionate and non-judgemental. Please download the application pack for further information and a full job description. Note that Community Savers is a majority women-led and transinclusive movement that works in alliance with Community Led Action and Savings Support (CLASS). Membership is open to anyone of any gender identity and community action aims to benefit all people in the areas where we work. Leadership and governance structures seek to celebrate and amplify the voices of working class women as those most disadvantaged by the intersecting cost of living, housing and climate crises. item.title: Operations Coordinator
item.description: Job Purpose: Still in its original Fleet Street location, our historic building retains much of its 1890s character, reflecting over a hundred years of history while providing 21st century facilities. With six floors, St Bride Foundation is a unique and memorable setting for a range of events - lectures, workshops, board meetings, conferences, weddings and other celebrations. The Operations Coordinator plays a key role in supporting the day-to-day operation of St Bride Foundation, helping to ensure our historic building is safe, compliant, well maintained and welcoming. Working closely with the Operations Manager and Facilities Coordinator, you'll provide support across facilities management while also acting as a welcoming first point of contact for visitors, tenants and contractors. We're looking for an organised, approachable and proactive individual who enjoys a varied role and is equally comfortable managing administrative tasks behind the scenes as delivering excellent front of house service. Key Responsibilities: Operational Administration Provide administrative support to the Operations Manager and Facilities Coordinator across all aspects of facilities management including planned preventative maintenance programmes and reactive maintenance requests. Liaise with Facilities Coordinator to ascertain what jobs can be completed in-house and what needs an external contractor. Obtain quotations for maintenance, repairs and improvement works from contractors and suppliers. Arrange contractor visits, coordinate access and ensure works are completed to the required standard. Ensure contractors provide appropriate documentation, including risk assessments, method statements and insurance certificates where required. Maintain records of maintenance schedules, servicing, warranties and contractor documentation. Check and process invoices relating to facilities expenditure. Maintain accurate records of maintenance logs and supplier information. Health & Safety Administration Support the Facilities Coordinator and Operations Manager in maintaining Health & Safety records and ensure documentation is up to date. Support Health & Safety compliance appropriate to a Grade II listed heritage building and its public, commercial and performance spaces. Support the administration of statutory inspections, testing and servicing, including fire safety systems, emergency lighting, lifts, electrical testing and water hygiene. Assist with the administration of risk assessments, inspections and audits. Monitor compliance dates and ensure inspections and certifications are completed on time. Assist with emergency procedures, fire safety administration and business continuity documentation. Front of House & Building Support Provide Front of House support, covering reception desk during core hours, welcoming visitors and providing excellent customer service. Assist with general queries on email and drop-in enquiries. Receive deliveries, distribute post and manage courier collections. Act as a point of contact for building tenants, responding to queries and coordinating facilities requests. Assist with room access, keys and general building administration. Help ensure shared spaces remain safe, presentable and welcoming. Digital & Administrative Support Support the Learning team with updating of event listings across ticketing platforms and the organisation's website as required. Manage the administration of the organisation's online bookshop, including processing orders, maintaining stock records and liaising with customers where required. General Act as an ambassador for St Bride Foundation, upholding its mission to preserve and promote print and design heritage. Engage with stakeholders, including donors, volunteers, and beneficiaries, to strengthen community and fundraising efforts. Support and contribute to initiatives that enhance the Foundation’s impact, such as public engagement events, educational programmes, and collaborative partnerships. Complete ongoing staff training to include Health & Safety, compliance and other related topics as required by the organisation. Contribute to the smooth running of the organisation by supporting colleagues across departments. Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role. Essential Qualifications & Experience: Excellent administrative and organisational skills with strong attention to detail. Experience coordinating contractors, suppliers or facilities-related services. Confident obtaining quotations, scheduling works and maintaining accurate records. Good understanding of Health & Safety administration within a workplace environment. Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office 365 and experience using databases or online management systems. Experience in the charitable, cultural, or heritage sector preferred. Key Skills & Competencies: Good team-working and interpersonal skills, with ability to build effective relationships with a wide range of people. Good time-management and organisational skills, with ability to multitask, prioritise and problem-solve. Good written and verbal communication skills, with ability to present well in person and on the phone with a polite, professional and approachable manner, and an outgoing approach to customer service. Ability to self-motivate, use own initiative and maintain attention to detail while working under pressure. A positive, proactive and professional attitude, with a willingness to adopt a flexible and adaptable approach to day-to-day workload. A passion for the arts, heritage, and education, with a strong commitment to the Foundation’s vision and values. Organisational Values & Expectations: Promote and uphold St Bride Foundation’s commitment to cultural preservation, lifelong learning, and community engagement. Work collaboratively with colleagues, volunteers, and external partners to support the Foundation’s charitable objectives. Uphold ethical standards and best practices in charity governance and operations. Health & Safety Responsibilities: Promote a safe and inclusive environment for colleagues, volunteers, and visitors. Act as a Fire Marshal and Emergency First Aider. Terms & Conditions: Working Hours: 8 hours per day (including one hour unpaid lunchbreak), five days per week. The role requires you to work at Front of House reception during core hours.

item.title: Business Development and Events Manager
item.description: Job description Job Purpose: To oversee the management and growth of Venue Hire for our historic spaces covering meetings, conferences, talks, weddings and community activities. This is our primary source of income and key to supporting our library and learning programme, alongside our theatre income and fundraising. The role will also lead on identifying and developing new business opportunities for other commercial income streams, building relationships with clients and partners, and ensuring that commercial activity supports the Foundation’s charitable purpose and long-term sustainability. Optimising the use of space to ensure that St Bride Foundation (SBF) operates profitably as well as meeting the needs of our communities is a key part of the role. The Business Development and Events Manager will oversee the Venue Hire activity and promote the venue’s room resources, as well as supporting the Library and Workshop in the organisation of in-house courses, seminars and events. Key Responsibilities: Events Management Manage the Events Team activity of promoting and selling the venue’s event spaces, ensuring SBF has good visibility on all relevant venue hire websites. Responding to and converting enquiries and monitoring conversion effectiveness. Managing clients’ needs for booked events. Negotiating contracts for both short and long-term use; and ensuring that all aspects of the venue are fit for purpose. Identify new networks and online promotions to promote the SBF offer Be responsible, along with the Operations Manager and Foundation Manager, to the Board for: Setting and achieving yearly and monthly income budgets, including quarterly forecasting and planning. All aspects of pricing and contract negotiation for areas of responsibility including catering, furniture hire, keyholding and cleaning. Ensure service, pricing and contracts are regularly reviewed. Working “hands-on” within a small team, getting involved in all aspects of delivering a quality service, monitoring and reviewing customer experience and satisfaction. Assisting the Operations Manager with Health & Safety and compliance issues relating to your area of responsibility. Line management responsibility for Event Coordinators and Venue Assistant. Overseeing and supporting the Events Team with smooth running of SBF and external events. Ensure time management and priorities are managed for line reports. Support SBF marketing efforts working with the Events team on social media content and website updates. Act as an ambassador for St Bride Foundation, upholding its mission to preserve and promote print and design heritage. Actively contribute to SBF redevelopment plans in terms of future planning for events and building operations. Engage with stakeholders, including donors, volunteers, and beneficiaries, to strengthen community and fundraising efforts. Support and contribute to initiatives that enhance the Foundation’s impact, such as public engagement events, educational programmes, and collaborative partnerships. Complete ongoing staff training to include Health & Safety, compliance and other related topics as required by the organisation. Business Development & Commercial Growth Develop and implement a proactive business development strategy for Venue Hire, identifying new clients, partners and commercial opportunities, as well as additional marketing/outreach activities to boost income during quieter periods. Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective clients and strategic partners, converting opportunities into new and repeat business. Develop relationships with event agencies, corporate organisations, professional bodies, cultural and educational organisations and other relevant networks. Identify opportunities to increase revenue through repeat bookings, new event formats, longer-term agreements, partnerships and additional services. Monitor market trends, competitor activity, customer feedback and venue performance to inform pricing, product development and sales activity. Establish and report on business development KPIs, including pipeline value, enquiry-to-booking conversion, repeat business, occupancy, average booking value and revenue growth. Work collaboratively with Marketing, Fundraising, Learning, Library and Workshop teams to develop opportunities that support both the Foundation's commercial and charitable objectives. Work with fundraising to develop incentives and cross promotions between sponsorship/membership and venue hire and identify other synergies between the physical SBF assets and the fundraising function Essential Qualifications & Experience: Proven experience of business development, sales, partnership-building or income generation, ideally within a venue, cultural, charitable or heritage setting. Proven experience of planning and delivering events end-to-end, on time and within budget. Working with teams on a varied programme of activities for a diverse mix of audiences. Experience of working with volunteers running workshops and events, overseeing all aspects of delivery. Experience working with external partners, including community groups, local authorities and sponsors. Line management experience of an events team, including support with managing workload and personal development objectives. Experience of identifying new clients, generating leads, converting enquiries and developing repeat business or longer-term client relationships. Experience of using data, customer insight or market research to inform sales activity, pricing, service development or income targets. Experience in the charitable, cultural, or heritage sector preferred. Key Skills & Competencies: Highly organised, able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to troubleshoot issues arising during events including those relating to AV, catering and general experience of attendees to ensure seamless delivery. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Confidence in briefing and managing event speakers including volunteers and SBF Trustees to ensure smooth running of events. Confident relationship-builder, able to develop networks with corporate clients, event agencies, cultural partners, community organisations and other stakeholders. Able to set, monitor and report on business development activity and income-related KPIs, including enquiry conversion, occupancy, repeat business and revenue growth. Risk assessment and mitigation in event spaces and knowledge of licensing, insurance, accessibility and inclusion requirements. Financial management and budgeting, including forecasting and reporting of our events revenue. Strong IT skills, including CRM systems, ticketing platforms and newsletters. A passion for the arts, heritage, and education, with a strong commitment to the Foundation’s vision and values. Organisational Values & Expectations: Promote and uphold St Bride Foundation’s commitment to cultural preservation, lifelong learning, and community engagement. Work collaboratively with colleagues, volunteers, and external partners to support the Foundation’s charitable objectives. Uphold ethical standards and best practices in charity governance and operations. Health & Safety Responsibilities: Ensure compliance with all relevant Health & Safety policies and charitable sector guidelines. Promote a safe and inclusive environment for colleagues, volunteers, and visitors. Act as a Fire Marshal and Emergency First Aider. Terms & Conditions: Working Hours: 8 hours per day (including one-hour unpaid lunchbreak), five days per week. You will work on rotation with other members of the Events Team, on one of the following core hour slots: 08:30–16.30, 10:00–18:00, 12:00–20:00 or 14:00–22:00 with one hour lunch. Due to the flexible nature of the work you may be required to work outside of these times. Shifts will be planned and agreed in advance with the other members of the Events team. Ad hoc weekend work will be required from time to time. item.title: Community Action Lead - Manchester
item.description: Job description Join a passionate committed team with a lead role in driving forward social justice through community-led action and partnership development! You will work in alliance with the Community Savers Leadership and key partners to support creative organising for gender, housing, climate, and economic justice across Manchester neighbourhoods. This role is funded by the National Lottery Community Fund (Reaching Communities). You will need: A deep understanding of the context for facilitating community action and community-led development projects in areas experiencing long term and intersecting inequalities. The ability to maintain a positive ‘can do’ attitude while negotiating complex and potentially obstructive political or relational dynamics. Skills & experience in the following areas: community-led action; advocacy; campaigns, fundraising, communications, leadership development, brokering partnerships, equality diversity and inclusion, conflict resolution, safeguarding. Role summary: You will work with the Community Savers Leadership and key partners on the strategic development of community action, projects, and partnerships that reduce health inequalities and promote social justice. This will include networking and building relationships with existing and potential statutory and non-statutory partners; bringing in appropriate expertise to achieve community-led development projects; direct support for community action such as community-led research projects and partnerships; community mapping, visioning and action planning; supporting reflection and evaluation; and sharing learning widely. You will also supervise the coordination support provided to affiliated groups and leaders by our Community Action Coordinator (Manchester); ensuring a community-led process underpins leadership and associational development. Please download the application pack for further information and a full job description noting that this is a 0.6% FTE 3-year fixed term contract (actual salary pro rata). Note that Community Savers is a majority women-led and transinclusive movement. Membership is open to anyone of any gender identity and community action aims to benefit all people in the areas where we work. Leadership and governance structures seek to celebrate and amplify the voices of working class women. item.title: Domestic Violence and Abuse Coordinator (part-time)
item.description: Job Role: Domestic Violence and Abuse Co-ordinator Salary: £15,720 per year (based on an FTE of £26,200 per year) Hours: 22.5 hours per week (3 days across Monday to Friday) Contract type: Permanent Location: BANES Additional information: A valid driving licence and access to own vehicle Participation in an on-call out-of-hours rota Regular travel across the BANES area (travel across the South West for training and events may also be required) Alongside is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. However, this is restricted to women due to the nature of the role. The Occupational Requirement under Schedule 9 (part 1) of the Equality Act 2010 applies. About Alongside: Alongside is a charity dedicated to making a difference to the lives of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged people in society. We run several projects and every year we help thousands of people out of homelessness, into employment, away from domestic abuse, and more. If you’d like a real sense of job satisfaction, great career prospects and a competitive benefits package, you could be who we’re looking for! About the Role: As a Domestic Violence and Abuse Co-ordinator , you’ll play a vital role in supporting victims and survivors of domestic abuse to rebuild their lives. Working holistically, you’ll carry out in‑depth needs assessments and develop tailored support plans that reflect each individual’s circumstances, strengths, and goals. You’ll provide compassionate, trauma‑informed case management, advocacy, and resettlement support for people with a wide range of complex social and housing needs. From navigating services and securing safe accommodation to monitoring progress and celebrating milestones, you’ll walk alongside survivors every step of the way — empowering them to move forward with safety, dignity, and confidence. This is a deeply rewarding role where your work will make a meaningful, lasting difference every single day. What you’ll be doing: Conduct key works sessions on a regular basis whilst developing individual support and risk management plans. Establish the risks and needs of survivors and their children through assessing their practical and emotional support needs. Champion safeguarding by following policies and procedures to keep everyone safe, and that any concerns are brought to immediate attention of a manager. Collaborative multi-agency working to advocate for survivors ensuring their needs are met. Maintain accurate client records using our system, INFORM. Please note: Job descriptions are not exhaustive, and the successful candidate may occasionally be asked to take on other duties that align with the key responsibilities outlined. You can view the full job description by clicking here . What we’re looking for: Understanding of domestic abuse including the impact this has on victims and their children. Experience working in a housing, social or health care setting. There are many great reasons to join our team! Access to our Rewards Platform, which includes an Employee Assistance Programme and Health Cash Plan 27 days annual leave , including an extra day off for your birthday, plus bank holidays - increasing up to 30 days after 4 years of continuous employment (pro rata for part-time staff) 30% staff discount at Alongside charity shop A generous and competitive pension scheme A supportive culture where staff feedback is highly valued and regular supervisions with line managers are conducted Great opportunities for career development and free monthly training sessions from experienced facilitators For all the fantastic and valuable work, you’ll be doing, you’ll be eligible for the Blue Light Card which offers amazing discounts on thousands of brands Reflective Practice sessions from objective, external facilitators Our Ethos As an Equal Opportunities employer, we have an Equality and Diversity Action plan in place showing our commitment in ensuring continuous improvement in creating an inclusive culture. We also have a committed group of Inclusion & Diversity champions who meet monthly to ensure progress is being made. We invite applications from people from all backgrounds and cultures, especially minority groups that are underrepresented in the workplace. We also welcome applications from those with lived experience. We embrace flexibility and are proud to be a Disability Confident and Mindful employer, as well as an Armed Forces Covenant Supporter. If you have any special access requirements or other support needs throughout the application process (including interview), please contact us so that we can let you know how we can support you. We accept CVs and applications in all formats. DBS Checks We welcome applications from people with lived experience. All applicants working with our clients will be expected to undertake an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check. A criminal conviction will not necessarily prevent you from becoming an employee, the decision will depend on the type of offence and its relevance to the role. If you would like to discuss any convictions you may have, please contact the person named in the advert. All information will be dealt with according to our Data Protection Policy.

item.title: Oxford & Thames Valley Peer Support Lead
item.description: Are you passionate about reducing health inequalities and supporting some of the most marginalised people in our communities? We are recruiting for a compassionate, organised, and proactive Peer Support Lead to support our hepatitis C peer project in the Oxford & Thames Valley area. Peers use their lived experience to raise awareness of hepatitis C, reduce stigma, and help people access testing and treatment. Working alongside healthcare professionals, drug and alcohol services, homelessness services, and community organisations, you will recruit, train and support volunteer peers to deliver hepatitis C awareness raising, practical and emotional support. This is a varied and rewarding community-based position involving travel across the Oxford and Thames Valley region. About you We are looking for someone who can build trust and engage people with complex needs in a respectful, non-judgemental way. You’ll be a good communicator, confident working with partner services and supporting volunteers, with good organisational skills and an understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries and managing risk. We welcome applications from people with either lived experience or professional experience relevant to the role. This may include hepatitis C, drug or alcohol use, homelessness, the criminal justice system, or supporting people facing similar challenges. Why join us? The Hepatitis C Trust is a national, patient-led charity committed to eliminating hepatitis C and improving access to harm reduction services across the UK. We are proud to be a Living Wage Employer and are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. How to apply The closing date for applications is midnight, Sunday 27th September 2026 .

item.title: Digital Innovation and Development Manager
item.description: Are you excited by the potential of digital technology and data to make a real difference in people's lives? Community Action Redbridge is looking for a creative, forward-thinking Digital Innovation and Development Manager to lead the next stage of our digital journey and help shape how technology supports communities across one of London's most diverse boroughs. Redbridge is home to vibrant communities and a dynamic voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) sector. We want to harness the power of digital technology and data to strengthen communities, support local VCSE organisations and help create a fairer Redbridge. Working across the organisation, you'll lead the implementation of our ambitious Digital Innovation and Development Strategy. You'll help create more consistent and effective systems that reduce duplication, improve collaboration and enable our team to focus on what matters most: supporting our communities and member organisations. You'll champion a data-driven culture, helping us turn information into insight, better understand our impact, and make informed decisions that respond to emerging needs. You'll play a key role in building digital confidence across the organisation, empowering staff to embrace new technologies, develop their skills and use digital tools effectively in their everyday work. Beyond Community Action Redbridge, you'll work directly with local charities and community groups to strengthen their digital capacity, improve access to data and insight, and foster stronger connections across Redbridge's VCSE sector. If you're excited by the power of digital technology to connect people, improve services and create lasting social impact, we'd love to hear from you. About Community Action Redbridge Community Action Redbridge is a local infrastructure organisation dedicated to building a fairer Redbridge where everyone and every community has an equal opportunity to thrive. Our work supports the development of strong and resilient communities where people lead happy, healthy, and fulfilling lives. At the heart of our work is a commitment to social justice and to tackling the root causes of inequality. We’re passionate about shifting power, amplifying community voices and working collaboratively to create social change. We do this by: What it’s like to work at Community Action Redbridge We’re committed to creating a truly inclusive workplace culture that embraces and celebrates difference. Building a team that reflects the diversity of our communities and brings together a range of experiences, backgrounds and perspectives is essential to the work we do. We want Community Action Redbridge to be a safe space for everyone to bring their whole selves to work, where all our employees have the opportunity to thrive and feel recognised and valued for the work they do. We offer some great benefits including 28 days’ annual leave (including the festive closure period) plus public holidays, a free and confidential employee helpline, face-to-face and telephone counselling, and a travel loan and cycle to work scheme. How to apply Please submit your CV and a covering letter answering the following 4 questions (no more than 500 words each): Describe a digital transformation, systems improvement or innovation project that you have led. What was the challenge, what approach did you take, and what impact did it have on the organisation, team or service users? Why do you want to join Community Action Redbridge, and how do your values, skills and experience equip you to help us use digital technology to strengthen communities and create positive social change? Please apply directly through the CharityJob website by midnight on Monday 28th September 2026. First-stage interviews will take place online on Tuesday 6th October 2026. Candidates successfully shortlisted from the first stage will be invited to attend a second-stage interview in person, which is expected to take place on Tuesday 13th October 2026. If you would like an informal conversation about the role before applying, please email us directly to arrange a suitable time.

item.title: Side-by-Side Community Engagement Worker
item.description: About the role The Side-by-Side project supports children in care and care leavers to have the same opportunities as those who have not experienced care. For many young people, navigating the care system and especially the transition to leaving care can be complex, isolating, and overwhelming. Too often, care-experienced young people are expected to face adulthood before they are ready, without the safety nets of family, friends, and community networks that many of us take for granted. The project provides a mentoring and befriending service, offering consistent, trusted relationships that help young people feel less alone, build confidence and life skills, and navigate key life changes as they move towards independence. Side-by-Side supports young people with a range of needs, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. The project is guided by strong safeguarding practice, built on trust, and delivered through trauma-informed, person-centred approaches. Working 18 hours per week, you will work directly with young people through engagement sessions, group activities and co-designed initiatives. You will also work alongside volunteers, supporting them to safely and effectively engage with young people. This role does not involve acting as a young person’s key worker or holding a caseload. Instead your focus is on enabling connections, strengthening community networks and creating opportunities for young people to thrive across Solihull. Please note this is a fixed term contract position for 12 months. About you We are looking for a compassionate and motivated individual with strong local knowledge and a commitment to community-based support. You will be confident working directly with care-experienced young people, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. Your key responsibilities will include: Build community links: develop relationships with local venues, services, and partners to support young people and Side-by-Side activities. Support volunteers: recruit, train, and guide volunteers, helping them signpost young people to relevant services. Engage young people: deliver activities, gather feedback, and support co-designed initiatives to ensure young people shape the services they receive. Live our values: all work is guided by trust, reducing loneliness, providing practical and emotional support, and delivering person-centred approaches. Employee benefits We offer the following employee benefits: 26 days, increasing to 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata for part time) Occupational sick pay (subject to completion of qualifying period) Enhanced pay for family friendly leave Free parking at some of our offices Employee assistance programme Group stakeholder pension scheme Access to BHSF health cash plan Cycle to work scheme Support and supervision from your line manager Learning and Development opportunities How to apply Please visit our website for the job description and to apply. In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the job description attached. The interview date will be confirmed and are expected to take place in person in Solihull Safeguarding and Compliance NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy, candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the advert early should the right candidate be found before the closing date. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change young lives.

item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Help lead the next chapter of an award-winning, volunteer-powered environmental charity As we celebrate our 10-year anniversary, Shrewsbury Food Hub is looking for an inclusive, practical and strategically minded Executive Director to lead us through the next phase of our development. We have a simple vision: a community where food is valued and not wasted. Founded in 2016, we rescue surplus food seven days a week from local suppliers and redistribute it through charities, community groups, schools and Foodshares. In the year to March 2026 alone, we rescued more than 270 tonnes of food, with our work reaching an estimated 4,000 people every week across Shrewsbury and the surrounding area. We have also developed a growing programme of community cooking, bringing people together to build skills and confidence, share food and strengthen community – while ensuring that good food does not go to waste. The opportunity Shrewsbury Food Hub has grown significantly over the past decade. Our next Executive Director will help us build on that success while strengthening the foundations beneath it. This is an exciting opportunity to lead an established and much-loved local charity through a period of organisational development: bringing greater clarity, focus, structure and resilience while protecting the energy, relationships and community spirit that make the Hub special. The Board is committed to focusing increasingly on governance and delegating day-to-day leadership and management to the Executive Director. You will have the authority and responsibility to lead the organisation, work closely with our Senior Leadership Team and create the conditions in which staff and volunteers can perform at their best. This is not a figurehead role. We need an Executive Director who can see the bigger picture, make difficult choices and turn strategy into practical action – someone equally comfortable around the Board table and spending time with the staff, volunteers and partners who make our work possible. This role is largely based in Shrewsbury, with some home working possible. This is a strongly place-based role requiring a regular and visible on-site presence. What you will lead Working with the Board, staff, volunteers and partners, you will: Lead the development and delivery of a clear, focused and financially sustainable strategy. Strengthen our structures, systems, processes and ways of working, leading organisational change with clarity and sensitivity. Provide overall leadership for safe, reliable and effective operations and organisational risk. Build an inclusive, enabling and accountable culture, supporting and developing our Senior Leadership Team and wider community of staff and volunteers. Oversee financial sustainability and the development of a strong, balanced income base. Build trusted relationships with funders, suppliers, businesses, local authorities and community partners, acting as a visible and credible ambassador for the Hub. Please see the full Job Description and Person Specification for further details. Who are we looking for? You will bring successful senior leadership experience from a charity, social enterprise, public service or other purpose-led organisation, together with experience of shaping strategy, leading change and turning plans into results. You will be financially astute, pragmatic and comfortable creating clarity in a busy organisation. Above all, you will be a genuine people leader : emotionally intelligent, approachable and able to build trust across a diverse community of staff, volunteers, trustees, founders and partners. We don't expect our new Executive Director to be a specialist in everything. You may bring particular depth in operational and organisational leadership or in income generation, fundraising and external development . What matters is that you have credible experience of the other and the leadership ability to bring different expertise together. Previous Executive Director experience is welcome, but is not essential. Our values We want our new Executive Director to share our commitment to reducing food waste and strengthening our community, and to lead in a way that reflects our values: Passion – Accountability – Inclusiveness – Integrity – Caring – Resilience These values shape not only what we do, but how we work together. We are looking for a leader who enables others to succeed, listens to different perspectives, acts with integrity and empathy, and remains purposeful and constructive through change. Our ambitions remain firmly rooted in place. We believe there is significant potential to deepen our environmental and social impact across Shrewsbury and Shropshire , rather than becoming a national organisation. How to apply: Please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than three pages , outlining your suitability for the role, by 5pm on Friday 25 September 2026 . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to visit Shrewsbury Food Hub on Monday 5 October 2026 , providing an opportunity to meet the team, see the Hub in action and gain a deeper understanding of the organisation ahead of formal interviews. Shrewsbury Food Hub values the strength that comes from different experiences and perspectives. We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds and are committed to a fair and accessible recruitment process. #Executive Director #Executive Director Jobs #Executive Director Charity #Executive Director Non Profit #Executive Director Third Sector #Executive Director Voluntary Sector #Charity Executive Director #Executive Leadership #Senior Leadership #Strategic Leadership #Charity Leadership #Charity Leader #Charity Director #Director Charity #Director Jobs #Chief Executive #Chief Executive Officer #Charity CEO #Non Profit Leadership #Third Sector Leadership #EnvironmentalCharity #ShrewsburyFoodHub #Shropshire

item.title: Bid Writer
item.description: Job description The postholder will be responsible for identifying, writing, and submitting compelling, well-researched and tailored funding applications to relevant grant-giving bodies. The post holder will work closely with the LDHAS management team to gather information, write bids, and track progress of submissions, ensuring LDHAS meets income targets as agreed by the Trustees. The postholder will: Proactively research, navigate the system and identify suitable grant and funding opportunities from charitable trusts, foundations, and statutory bodies. Write and submit high-quality funding applications and proposals in line with LDHAS's strategic priorities working closely with the Manager and in their collaboration with key partners. Work collaboratively with the LDHAS Manager and colleagues to gather accurate, up-to-date data and service information for applications. Tailor applications to funder requirements and priorities, ensuring persuasive storytelling and alignment with LDHAS 's mission. Manage a pipeline of applications and submissions, ensuring deadlines are met and income targets are tracked. Ability to turn service data and case studies into powerful narratives that align with funder priorities. Act as an ambassador for vulnerable people. Maintain effective communication with the Board Analytical and judgement skills Research and identify suitable grant and funding opportunities from charitable trusts, foundations, and statutory bodies. Work collaboratively with LDHAS Manager and colleagues to gather accurate, up-to-date data and service information for applications. Planning and organisation skills Contributes to LDHAS's long-term income generation plans. Support development of strong internal bid and grant management systems, including templates, case studies, and project reporting tools. Provide general advice tomembers of public contacting LDHAS. Responsibilities for policy and service development Lead on Bid writing policy and procedure development. item.title: Youth Volunteer Officer
item.description: Youth Volunteering Officer 35 hours per week, temporary contract until December 2028. We are Chester Zoo We're not just an award-winning visitor attraction that's home to 30,000 incredible animals within 128 acres of stunning gardens. We're a major conservation charity committed to preventing extinction and restoring nature, both locally and globally. As the world faces an extinction crisis, we're making a significant contribution to conservation when it's needed most. We are Chester Zoo and we prevent extinction. The Role We have an exciting opportunity for a Youth Volunteering Officer to join our Volunteering Team within the Conservation Education and Engagement Directorate. As a Youth Volunteering Officer, you will work closely with the Volunteer Manager and the Networks for Nature project staff to deliver an inclusive volunteering programme for young people aged 14-25. The role focuses on creating meaningful opportunities that connect young people with conservation and social action, whilst supporting their personal development and wellbeing. The Youth Volunteering Officer will recruit, train and mentor young volunteers, ensuring high-quality experiences that are inclusive, safe and impactful. The Youth Volunteering Officer will also recruit, train and support adult Youth Champion Volunteers who will be empower and support the youth volunteers to participate and engage in the volunteer programme. As Youth Volunteer Officer, you will co-ordinate a supported programme for young people that will include practical conservation, visitor engagement and the Conservation Changemakers programme, designing and delivering their own projects while recognising and evidencing the skills they gain. The role will also support the delivery of our wider youth programmes including our Environmental Leadership courses, and Youth Network events supporting pathways for young people to access training, events, and volunteer experiences. We're looking for someone who can: Programme Delivery With guidance from the Volunteer Manager, coordinate and deliver youth volunteering opportunities for young people aged 14-25, including practical conservation activities, visitor engagement opportunities and social action projects. Support young people to develop skills, confidence and experience through meaningful volunteering. Volunteer Recruitment and Support Recruit, induct, train and support youth volunteers, ensuring they receive a positive and rewarding volunteering experience. Support young people to access pathways into conservation, community action and the wider youth programme. Recruit, train and support Youth Champion Volunteers who play a key role in encouraging and facilitating youth participation within the programme. Inclusive Participation Work proactively to reduce barriers to participation and provide tailored support for young people from diverse backgrounds, including those with disabilities, neurodiversity, mental health challenges or socio-economic disadvantage. Youth-led Projects and Co-production Coordinate and facilitate youth-led conservation and community action projects through the Conservation Changemakers programme. Enable young people to generate ideas, plan activities, take ownership of projects and evidence their learning and achievements. Events, Training and Activities Planning and Delivery With support from the Volunteer Manager, deliver volunteer events, training sessions, workshops and networking opportunities for youth volunteers, working with colleagues and partners to provide engaging and high-quality experiences. Support the delivery of youth programme events, including Environmental Leadership courses. Participant Engagement Monitoring Monitor participation through surveys, feedback mechanisms and regular check-ins. Collate engagement and outcome data, contributing to project evaluation and reporting for internal stakeholders and funders. Daily Volunteer Engagement Manage day-to-day communication with youth volunteers and Youth Champion Volunteers, including responding to enquiries, processing applications, maintaining records, organising rotas and training bookings, and providing ongoing support. Safeguarding, Safety and Risk Assessments Work with the Volunteer Manager to ensure all youth volunteering activities operate within safeguarding policies and procedures. Assist with risk assessments and ensure that appropriate welfare, wellbeing and safety measures are embedded throughout all activities. Partnership Working Work with the Volunteer Manager to develop effective working relationships with schools, colleges, youth organisations, community groups and relevant internal departments to increase participation, reduce barriers to engagement and strengthen programme delivery. What makes Chester Zoo a great place to work? Well, where do we start? Here goes… We’re a huge team of conservationists, scientists, educators, animal welfare experts, marketeers, visitor experience professionals, environmental policy influencers; the list goes on. Each and every one of us is on a mission to make Chester Zoo the best in the world, and our planet a better place. As the UK’s biggest and best zoo, we have ambitious goals, exciting plans, and there’s always lots going on here. We’re an inclusive and diverse organisation, made up of over 600 permanent and 500 temporary team members, and we know how important it is to invest in our colleagues to help boost their career development. We have ambitious goals, and we want you to be with us for the long term on our exciting journey. Our working environment could not be more different from a typical office – where else can you see critically endangered orangutans from your office window, or stroll among rare giraffes and tigers on your lunch break? The Package • Fixed term contract until December 2028 • 35 hours per week • Salary £24,062.50 per annum (pro rata based on 35 hours per week) • The postholder will work 5 days out of 7 including a regular weekend day • 33 days annual leave plus the option to buy or sell up to 5 days (pro rota) • Staff pass so you can visit the zoo during your time off, plus multiple complimentary tickets for your friends and family • Cycle to work scheme • Healthcare plan • Discounted gym membership • Discounts on cinema tickets, restaurants, high street shops and more via Perks • Pension scheme with generous employer contributions Our Requirements • An understanding of and commitment to Chester Zoo's mission, vision and values. • Experience of working with young people. • Experience of coordinating, supporting or working with volunteers. • Experience of delivering training, workshops or activities with a range of audiences. • Knowledge of inclusive practice and supporting young people with diverse needs. • Strong organisational, administrative and planning skills. • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. • Excellent communication and literacy skills including by phone, face to face and via email/online discussion boards • Ability to build positive relationships with young people, colleagues and partner organisations. • Sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and digital communication tools. • Experience of working in a busy office environment as part of a team & on own initiative • Full UK driving licence. Although not essential, the following would be desirable: • Knowledge of youth work/ youth engagement which could be demonstrated by a relevant qualification in youth work, education, community development, related field or relevant experience • Experience of delivering conservation, environmental or outdoor learning activities. • Experience of supporting young people facing barriers to participation. • Working knowledge of volunteer management systems. • Knowledge of safeguarding legislation and best practice. • Experience of monitoring and evaluating volunteering activities Additional Information • Due to the nature of the role, this post is subject to an enhanced DBS check. • The closing date for applications is 27/09/2026. Networks for Nature is made possible with The National Lottery Heritage Fund, thanks to National Lottery players.
