item.title: Advise and Navigation Manager
item.description: Advice & Navigation Manager 6-Month Fixed-Term Contract (potential to extend) 28 hours per week (4 days) Hybrid Working | North London £30,310 per annum (pro rata salary based on £37,887 FTE) ASAP Start Subject to an Enhanced DBS check A community-focused charity is seeking an experienced Advice & Navigation Manager to lead and develop a busy frontline service supporting individuals experiencing poverty, health inequalities, social isolation, housing challenges and other forms of disadvantage. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced service manager with a strong background in casework oversight, safeguarding, service quality and team leadership . Managing a team delivering advice, navigation and social prescribing support, you will ensure residents receive high-quality, person-centred services that make a genuine difference to their lives. The Role A key focus of this position is the oversight and management of complex casework. You will ensure effective triage, caseload allocation, case progression and closure, supporting staff to deliver safe, timely and impactful interventions. Alongside day-to-day service management, you will provide leadership to a team of advice workers, social prescribing practitioners and volunteers, ensuring high standards of practice, compliance and safeguarding. You will also work closely with health partners, statutory agencies and community organisations to strengthen referral pathways and improve outcomes for residents. Key Responsibilities Lead the delivery of advice, navigation and social prescribing services. Oversee casework management, including referrals, triage, caseload allocation, quality assurance and case progression. Support staff with complex cases, safeguarding concerns and complaints. Line manage and develop a team of frontline staff and volunteers through supervision, coaching and performance management. Ensure compliance with safeguarding, data protection, health and safety and organisational policies. Monitor service performance, outcomes and impact, using data and insight to support continuous improvement. Build and maintain effective partnerships across health, local authority and voluntary sector organisations. Contribute to reporting, service planning and the delivery of contractual and funding requirements. About You We are looking for someone who can demonstrate: Significant experience managing advice, navigation, support, advocacy or community-based services. Strong experience overseeing complex casework involving vulnerable or disadvantaged individuals. Experience managing or supporting social prescribing, community health or welfare advice services. A thorough understanding of safeguarding, risk management and professional boundaries. Experience leading, supporting and developing teams through effective supervision and performance management. A track record of working in partnership with health, statutory and voluntary sector organisations. Experience using data and service insight to improve performance and demonstrate impact. Excellent communication, organisational and stakeholder management skills. Desirable Experience Social prescribing within primary care or community settings. Service development, improvement or change management. Leading hybrid or community-based teams. A relevant qualification in advice, health, social care or management. We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you.

item.title: Service Manager - LBN Support Service
item.description: REPORTING TO: Head of Services RESPONSIBLE FOR: Team Leaders and other service-based roles as required PURPOSE OF POSITION The Service Manager will have overall responsibility for the operational leadership, quality, performance and contract delivery of both the LB Newham Core and the Intensive Support Accommodation contracts. The role will ensure a joined-up support pathway for residents with low, medium, high and complex support needs, promoting safety, stabilisation, independence, move-on and long-term tenancy sustainment. The post-holder will lead staff teams to deliver high-quality, trauma-informed, strengths-based and person-centred support for vulnerable single homeless adults, including residents with multiple disadvantage, high levels of risk and complex support needs. The role will set, monitor and embed clear resettlement and support standards, ensuring residents receive consistent assessment, support planning, risk management, move-on preparation and tenancy sustainment support. The role will be accountable for safeguarding, housing management, performance reporting, quality assurance, partnership working, commissioner confidence and continuous service improvement. What makes this role different • Lead the full move-on journey, from pre-tenancy preparation to sustaining community accommodation, ensuring residents receive timely, effective support. • Combine trauma informed support, tenancy sustainment, homelessness prevention, partnership working and values-led leadership to help residents build independence. • Work with Resident Services, Intensive Housing Management team. landlords, commissioners and agencies to prevent repeat homelessness and improve outcomes. • Lead with purpose, strengthen practice and model a learning culture rooted in Growth, Inclusion, Collaboration and Compassion. The role will require participation in the on-call rota and occasional evening and weekend work in line with service needs. RESPONSIBILITIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES Key Responsibilities • Lead the delivery supported accommodation contracts in line with commissioner expectations, contract requirements, organisational policies and agreed performance standards. • Provide clear management oversight of service quality, safety, safeguarding, risk, incidents, complex cases and escalation. • Ensure residents receive effective assessments, risk management, support planning, move-on planning and outcome-focused reviews. • Set and maintain clear resettlement standards across the service, ensuring residents are supported to develop independent living skills, secure appropriate move-on options and sustain accommodation after leaving the service. • Ensure support standards are consistently applied, including timely assessments, person-centred support plans, regular key work, outcome-focused reviews, accurate case recording and clear escalation of risk or non-engagement. • Promote trauma-informed, strengths-based and psychologically informed practice across the service. • Work closely with the Intensive Housing Management team to oversee housing-related support, including referrals, placements, rent accounts, Housing Benefit claims, arrears prevention, voids, licence or tenancy obligations, move-on and tenancy sustainment. • Ensure the intensive supported accommodation service provides safe, responsive and proportionate support for residents with complex needs and high levels of risk. • Monitor performance against contract indicators, including outcomes, safeguarding, engagement, rent accounts, move-on, tenancy sustainment, voids and resident feedback. • Prepare accurate reports, evidence and performance commentary for commissioner monitoring, audits, inspections and service reviews. • Lead, develop and support staff to work as one team while maintaining service-specific boundaries, contractual standards, professional accountability and Your Place values. • Maintain effective staffing arrangements, including cover for key working, weekend, out-of-hours and intensive provision requirements. • Build strong partnerships with commissioners, Adult Social Care, health services, substance misuse services, criminal justice partners, housing providers and community agencies. • Use service data, resident feedback and quality assurance activity to drive improvement, demonstrate impact and evidence value for money. • Work closely with the Quality Assurance Manager and Impact Manager to use performance data, quality assurance findings, resident feedback and outcome measures to identify trends, strengthen practice and drive continuous service improvement. • Work flexibly to respond to urgent operational issues, safeguarding concerns, incidents, commissioner requests and service pressures. • Embed person-centred practice and meaningful co-production with residents, ensuring services are shaped by lived experience and aligned with Your Place values of Growth, Inclusion, Collaboration and Compassion PERSON SPECIFICATION The successful candidate will bring the experience, knowledge, leadership skills and values needed to manage high-quality supported accommodation services and contribute effectively to the wider Your Place team. Essential Criteria • Experience managing or supervising staff in supported housing, homelessness, social care, community support or a similar setting. • Ability to lead change, improve practice and support staff through service development. • Experience supporting vulnerable homeless adults, rough sleepers or people facing multiple disadvantage. • Strong understanding of risk, safeguarding, trauma, mental health, substance misuse, tenancy sustainment and move-on barriers. • Experience leading services that manage challenging behaviour, anti-social behaviour, safeguarding concerns, tenancy breaches, arrears or complex risk. • Experience of contract management, performance monitoring, quality assurance, reporting and service improvement. • Good understanding of housing management, including arrears, voids, tenancy or licence breaches, maintenance, health and safety, and property-related risk. • Ability to analyse performance information, identify risks and trends, produce clear reports and use data to drive improvement. • Experience building constructive relationships with commissioners, statutory services, voluntary sector partners and internal stakeholders. • Knowledge of person-centred, strengths-based, trauma-informed and psychologically informed support. • Knowledge of safeguarding adults, mental capacity, confidentiality, professional boundaries, data protection, equality and diversity, and complaints handling. • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear reports, briefings and monitoring returns. • Commitment to resident involvement, co-production, equality, diversity, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice. Desirable Criteria • Experience managing commissioned homelessness or supported accommodation contract. • Experience working within or alongside London local authority homelessness pathways. • Experience of managing voids, referrals, move-ins, move-outs and partnership-based accommodation arrangements. • Experience of using Home Star, In-Form, Pyramid or equivalent systems to monitor support, tenancy sustainment, risk, outcomes and case recording. • Experience preparing for audits, inspections, commissioner reviews or contract monitoring meetings. • Experience leading services through mobilisation, remodelling, restructure or improvement planning. Aptitude and Behaviours confidently use performance data, resident feedback and quality assurance learning to improve outcomes and value for money. Provides values-led leadership and communicates clearly with staff, residents, commissioners and partners. Use written, numerical and performance information to make sound, accountable and compliant decisions. Involving and Including Embeds resident involvement and promotes dignity, choice, equality, inclusion and cultural competence. Build and develop a high-performing team through clear direction, supervision, support and accountability. Appointment is subject to an enhanced DBS check, satisfactory references and the right to work in the UK

item.title: Quality Assurance Manager - Maternity Cover
item.description: REPORTING TO: Director of Front-line Services PURPOSE OF POSITION The Quality Assurance Manager is a blended leadership role combining strategic quality assurance, performance oversight, service management and practice development. The role is split broadly between focused on quality assurance, data-led improvement and performance oversight, and two days focused on service management, practice leadership and frontline improvement activity. The postholder will lead the development and delivery of a strong quality assurance framework across support services, ensuring that practice, performance and service delivery are safe, effective, person-centred and aligned with contractual, regulatory and organisational standards. Alongside this, the postholder will remain closely connected to frontline delivery through service management responsibilities and practice development leadership, particularly within Housing First and complex-needs services. This makes the role ideal for someone who enjoys combining strategic oversight, data insight, operational leadership and the development of high-quality, trauma-informed support practice. What makes this role different A distinctive role for someone who wants strategic influence while staying close to frontline practice. You will help shape quality, use evidence, support staff, strengthen resident outcomes and join an organisation committed to compassion, collaboration, inclusion, growth, learning and resident voice. Enjoy variety and influence work across performance oversight, service management and practice development, with scope to shape systems, standards and ways of working. RESPONSIBILITIES & ACCOUNTABILITIES Key Responsibilities Quality assurance and improvement: Lead the quality assurance function across support services, coordinating audits, quality checks, case file reviews, service reviews and improvement plans. Turn findings into practical actions that strengthen safety, consistency, resident experience, safeguarding, support planning and trauma-informed practice. Work with managers to embed learning, monitor progress and evidence improvement against internal and external standards. Performance oversight and reporting: Monitor performance against contractual, regulatory and organisational standards, including service outcomes, compliance requirements, safeguarding expectations and commissioner reporting. Identify risks, gaps, trends and good practice, escalating concerns and supporting corrective action where needed. Produce clear, evidence-based reports and briefings for senior leaders, governance meetings, commissioners and external stakeholders. Data, insight and systems: Use performance, safeguarding, complaints, incidents, resident feedback, outcomes and quality data to identify service strengths, pressures and improvement priorities. Maintain and improve reporting systems, including InForm, so information is accurate, consistent and useful. Analyse patterns, support decision-making and make practical recommendations that improve quality, accountability and resident outcomes. Information retrieval and STAIRs requests: Act as QA Manager lead for information retrieval relating to STAIRs requests, including triaging scope, gathering internal and contractor records, coordinating redaction and drafting responses within regulatory timeframes. Service and support management: Provide hands-on support management across frontline services, including Housing First improvement activity, Hope Street and St Mungo’s contracts, team rota management and the Support Manager on-call rota. Support managers and teams to manage risk, strengthen case accountability and recording, and deliver consistent, high-quality support to residents with complex needs. Practice development: Embed person-centred, trauma-informed and psychologically informed practice across support services. Develop practical tools, guidance, quality forums, workshops and reflective learning that help staff apply policy, improve support planning, strengthen safeguarding and promote consistent resident-centred practice. Resident voice and accountability: Strengthen resident engagement, feedback and involvement so resident experience informs service design, quality assurance, learning and improvement. People management and collaboration: Line manage agreed roles, including the Impact Specialist and Resident Engagement Specialist, supporting clear objectives, accountability, development and collaborative working across services. General duties: Attend key directorate, management, planning, quality and performance meetings; work flexibly across organisational priorities; and undertake other reasonable duties within the scope of the role. PERSON SPECIFICATION Assessment will be through application, interview and, where relevant, a practical assessment Quality assurance: Experience delivering quality frameworks, audits, case file reviews, standards and improvement plans that strengthen safe, consistent, person-centred and trauma-informed practice. Able to lead improvement activity, influence managers and turn findings into sustained service change. Performance and reporting: Able to monitor contractual, regulatory and organisational standards; identify risks, gaps, trends and good practice; and produce clear reports for leaders, governance forums and commissioners. Data, insight and systems: Strong analytical skills and confidence using performance, safeguarding, complaints, incidents, outcomes and resident feedback data to identify patterns, support decisions and improve services. Experience using resident feedback, consultation or involvement activity to inform quality assurance, service design and improvement, including through InForm or similar systems. Information governance: Understands confidentiality, record handling and information governance. Able to triage STAIRs requests, gather internal/contractor records, support redaction and draft timely responses. Support management and practice: Experience supporting people experiencing homelessness or rough sleeping with complex needs. Able to support managers, manage risk, strengthen recording and embed person-centred, trauma-informed, psychologically informed and anti-discriminatory practice. Safeguarding and risk: Sound knowledge of adult safeguarding, risk assessment, MARAC processes and safe information sharing with vulnerable adults. Communication and values: Strong written, verbal and facilitation skills; collaborative, organised, accurate and resilient, with commitment to compassion, collaboration, inclusion and growth. Appointment is subject to DBS check and right to work in the UK

item.title: Head of Services (Female Applicants Only)
item.description: About the role This is an exciting opportunity to join Women and Girls Network's Senior Leadership Team and lead two of our most impactful service areas: the Intersectional and Anti-Oppressive (IOS) Team and the Criminal Justice and Violence Against Women & Girls (CJS, VAWG) Team. As Head of Services, you will play a vital role in shaping and driving services that support women and girls affected by gender-based violence, ensuring they receive empowering, trauma-informed and culturally responsive support. You will lead with a strong commitment to feminist, anti-racist and anti-oppressive values, ensuring that the voices and experiences of survivors remain at the heart of everything we do. Working closely with the Director of Services and senior colleagues, you will provide strategic leadership across a diverse portfolio of services, strengthening partnerships, influencing systems and championing innovative approaches that remove barriers and improve outcomes for women facing multiple disadvantages. This is a unique opportunity for an experienced leader to make a lasting impact, both within our organisation and across the wider VAWG sector. Job description As the Head of Services, you will: Lead and inspire the IOS and CJS, VAWG teams, providing strategic direction and oversight to ensure services are accessible, high-quality, survivor-centred and aligned with WGN's feminist values and vision. Champion intersectional and anti-oppressive practice, ensuring services are responsive to the diverse experiences of women and girls, particularly those from Black and Global Majority communities and others facing systemic barriers. Drive excellence in service delivery, safeguarding and quality assurance, ensuring robust risk management and compliance while creating environments where survivors can heal, recover and thrive. Lead, support and develop Service Managers, fostering a culture of collaboration, wellbeing, accountability and continuous learning that enables staff to deliver their best work. Build influential partnerships across statutory, voluntary and community sectors, strengthening pathways for survivors and ensuring WGN's expertise informs local, regional and national responses to violence against women and girls. Use insight, evidence and survivor feedback to evaluate impact, drive innovation and shape the future development of services, ensuring they continue to meet emerging need and deliver meaningful change. Represent WGN as a sector leader, advocating for systemic change and helping to create a society where all women and girls can live free from violence, inequality and discrimination. Supporting Statement Guidance Your supporting statement should clearly demonstrate how your experience, knowledge, skills, and qualifications meet the requirements of the role. Please address the key criteria outlined in the Job Description and Person Specification, providing specific examples of achievements and responsibilities that evidence your suitability for the position. Focus on relevant professional experience, transferable skills, and the impact of your work. Where possible, use concise examples to illustrate how you have successfully applied these skills in practice. The supporting statement should be no more than 500 words and should complement, rather than repeat, the information contained in your CV or application form. Closing date and interviews This vacancy will close at 9am on Monday 28 September 2026 . Interviews will take place shortly thereafter, and shortlisted candidates will be notified of the arrangements. We encourage early applications, as we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive a high volume of applications or identify a suitable candidate. The selection process will consist of two interview stages and a role-related assessment task. Interviews may be conducted either in person or remotely, depending on panel availability and logistical requirements, and may involve a combination of both formats throughout the process. Candidates invited to participate will receive full details of each stage, including the assessment task and interview arrangements, in advance. About us Women and Girls Network (WGN) is a pan-London organisation that supports women and girls affected by all forms of gendered-based violence. Our overall aim is to promote, preserve and restore the mental health and well-being of women and girls who have experienced, or are at risk of, gendered-based violence, whilst working towards a society free of gendered-based violence. We do this by: Providing women-only holistic and seamless therapeutic services, which meet women and girls’ needs and contribute to total and sustainable recovery from the experiences of violence. Evidencing the impact of gendered-based violence and presenting this information in appropriate forums to affect social change in attitudes towards, and responses to, gendered-based violence. Developing good practice in the sector by providing training and guidance on specialist service provision and the development of culturally appropriate service delivery. WGN is proud to be an accredited Living Wage Employer and a member of The London VAWG Consortium, Halo Code, and Helplines Partnership. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion We are deeply committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity, resilience and strength of the women and girls we serve. We strongly encourage applications from Black and Global Majority women and applicants with Lived Experience, including those who may not meet every criterion. WGN is an equal opportunities employer. Exemption This post is exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1 , and is open to female applicants only , due to the nature of the role.

item.title: Director of Finance
item.description: Noah's Ark Children's Hospice is partnering with Robertson Bell on a retained basis to recruit a Director of Finance on a permanent basis. This is an exciting opportunity to join a highly regarded children's hospice at a pivotal stage of its development, taking a leading role in strengthening financial performance, improving organisational effectiveness and helping shape the charity's next phase of growth. This is more than a traditional Finance Director role. Noah's Ark has undergone significant transformation in recent years, moving from a predominantly community-based service to operating a 24/7 hospice facility at The Ark. The successful candidate will join at a critical point in this journey, with the opportunity to strengthen the finance function whilst working closely with the wider Senior Leadership Team to ensure the charity is making the best possible use of its resources and delivering maximum value for children and families. For an ambitious, commercially minded finance leader, this is an opportunity to combine strong financial leadership with genuine organisational impact, helping to shape a more effective operating model and contributing directly to the future direction of the charity. The role Partner with the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board of Trustees to shape the charity's financial and strategic direction during a period of organisational change. Stabilise and strengthen the finance function, ensuring high-quality financial management, robust controls and accurate, insightful reporting. Lead the budgeting, forecasting and financial planning process, including modelling different care delivery approaches, investment decisions and longer-term strategic scenarios. Support the charity to improve its financial position, identifying opportunities to increase efficiency and ensure resources are being deployed to maximum effect. Oversee statutory accounts, external reporting, audit and regulatory requirements, ensuring the charity maintains strong financial governance and compliance. Ensure effective management of reserves, investments, cash flow, liquidity, insurance and restricted funds. Contribute to the development of the charity's next multi-year strategic plan, bringing commercial discipline, financial insight and a practical focus on delivery. Identify opportunities for cost efficiency and productivity improvements across the organisation, working collaboratively with colleagues to turn insight into action. Support the design and implementation of new IT and financial systems, ensuring they provide the information and controls required to support an effective organisation. Lead and develop a small finance team, setting clear expectations, building capability and creating a culture of accountability and high performance. Play an active role in wider organisational leadership, bringing constructive challenge and financial insight to decisions beyond the traditional finance remit. The organisation Noah's Ark Children's Hospice provides specialist care and support to babies, children and young people with life-limiting or life-threatening conditions, alongside their families. Its purpose-built hospice, The Ark, opened in 2019 and provides a unique environment where children can receive specialist care, therapy, bereavement support and family services in a safe and welcoming setting. Rated 'Outstanding' by the Care Quality Commission, Noah's Ark supports families across North and Central London and Hertsmere, delivering care wherever it is needed - in the family home, within the community or at The Ark. This is an organisation with a warm, supportive culture and a strong commitment to its values of Kindness, Excellence and Courage. It is now looking for a finance leader who can combine that collaborative approach with the confidence to challenge constructively, make difficult decisions and drive meaningful improvement. Essential criteria Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent). Strong experience leading a finance function. Strong understanding of financial controls, governance, audit and statutory reporting. Demonstrable experience producing and interpreting high-quality financial information that supports effective decision-making. Experience leading and developing teams, with the confidence to set expectations, address underperformance and hold colleagues accountable. Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders and non-finance colleagues. A proactive, hands-on and self-starting appr

item.title: Concierge
item.description: Concierge When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Job Title: Concierge Location: Based in Croydon. Step free access is available at this service. Salary: £28,000 Shift Pattern: 37.5 hours per week Monday to Sunday on a night rota between 20:00 - 08:30. You may be required to work outside these hours including day shifts, and bank holidays as per service and resident requirements About the Role An internal opportunity for a Night Concierge to join our team based in Croydon. In this role, you will provide concierge services within our service which provides 24/7 support to residents with forensic mental health needs. As a Concierge, you will help create a safe, welcoming and well run environment, offering reassurance and practical support to residents when they need it the most. This role is key to keeping our building, residents, and service secure and responsive. You will conduct regular safety checks, monitor access, respond to emergencies, support residents with queries, and keeping records. You will be key to creating and maintaining a clean and safe environment. You will be expected to remain awake, alert, accessible, and actively engaged throughout the shift. There is a focus on welfare checks, providing resident support, and completing administration tasks, ensuring clear handovers are prepared for the day staff and managers. Some Key Responsibilities Include: Ensuring our buildings are safe by monitoring, completing welfare checks and responding affectively and appropriately to emergencies Maintaining professionalism and kindness with residents and visitors, attending to calls, managing deliveries and ensuring great communication with the team in line with policies and procedures Provide a daily report on resident activity, AINMs, safeguarding and concerns for handovers. Working with the wider team to make sure any urgent issues are picked up and followed through Remain alert and monitor CCTV throughout the shift Adapting to service needs to support risk assessments, safeguarding checks, and service standards Supporting residents to build confidence and independence, contributing to a psychologically informed space where everyone is treated with respect and dignity Noticing when someone might be struggling with their physical or mental health, and taking prompt action to prevent escalation Helping to keep the environment clean and welcoming from tidying communal spaces to reporting repairs and completing admin tasks accurately and sensitively Be a valued and reliable member of the team, completing handovers for colleagues for a seamless service Other duties include maintaining cleanliness, removing rubbish, reporting repairs, ordering supplies, and general tasks About You We’re looking for someone who understands the importance of compassion, routine and safety who’s ready to make a difference in a calm, consistent way. Whether you’ve worked in supported housing before or bring transferable skills from another role, what matters most is if you’re dependable, care about people, and want to make a difference during quieter hours. Furthermore we look for: Experience in providing high quality customer service Ability to work independently and taking responsibility for the service You will require excellent communication skills with residents, colleagues and external partners to build positive and respectful relationships Understanding the importance of diversity, equity and inclusion in everything you do You have the ability to stay calm and supportive in a fast paced and constantly changing environment Ability to take a compassionate, non judgmental approach when helping others You share our values of Ambition, Empowerment, Inclusivity, and Transparency in your everyday work Please refer to the JDPS attached for more details on the vacancy and our requirements/key criteria. What we Offer 25 days (Full time equivalent) annual leave, increasing with the length of service Employer Pension Contribution Eligibility to register with Blue Light Discount Card Access to discounted tickets for music events, shows, sports and more Reflective Practice regular sessions with a therapist provided by an external provider to support Mental Health and Wellbeing at work Training and Development, including access to courses, upskilling, and progression plans Employee Assistance Programme, including counselling Life Assurance Scheme Cycle-to-work scheme Annual Staff Awards EDI Ambassador programme About Social Interest Group (SIG) SIG is a not-for-profit organisation providing thousands of people with good-quality support and care in residential, drop-in centres, community floating support settings, probation settings, and hospitals. We do so across London, Brighton, Bedfordshire, Luton, Kent and Liverpool. Our goal is to transform lives through empowering change. We believe good care and support improves lives with the vision to create healthier, safer, and more inclusive communities. Join us on our mission to empower independence through trauma-informed solutions and dynamic partnerships that keep people out of prison, out of hospital, and off the streets. Want to know how we work? Watch our short Theory of Change video to see how we support people towards a brighter future: Theory of Change Further details can be found on our website here: Theory of Change - Social Interest Group - Social Interest Group. Additional Information Please note that this job advert may close early due to screening applications on an ongoing basis. We advise applying as soon as possible for your application to be taken into consideration at the early stages. Please note that as part of our process, we complete an enhanced DBS check, some roles may require further vetting. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds. Unfortunately, we are unable to provide sponsorship, please ensure you have full right to work in the UK prior to applying to our positions.

item.title: Executive Support Team Lead - Thomson Reuters Foundation
item.description: The Thomson Reuters Foundation is the corporate foundation of Thomson Reuters and an independent charitable organisation dedicated to advancing free, fair and informed societies worldwide. Through the combined power of journalism, legal expertise and data intelligence, the Foundation works to strengthen independent media, improve access to justice, and promote responsible business practices to address some of the world's most pressing challenges. We are seeking an experienced and proactive Executive Support Team Lead to lead the evolution of our newly centralised Business Support function. This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in shaping a centre of excellence that provides high-quality administrative, financial and operational support across the Foundation. Leading a small but impactful team, you will drive service excellence, strengthen governance and controls, and deliver efficient, customer-focused support to colleagues across the organisation. You will oversee complex invoicing and billing processes, manage key systems and vendor relationships, and identify opportunities to streamline and improve the way we work. As we transition from a decentralised administrative model to a more strategic and centralised approach, you will have the opportunity to design and embed best practices, build organisational capability, and help create a scalable support function that enables our teams to maximise their impact around the world. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys combining operational leadership with hands-on problem solving and is excited by the opportunity to build and shape a function for the future. About the Role As a Executive Support Team Lead at the Thomson Reuters Foundation, you will: Lead, coach and develop the Business Support Coordinator and Invoicing & Billing Analyst, overseeing workload planning, performance management, recruitment, onboarding and ensuring effective service coverage across the organisation. Act as a senior subject matter expert for the Foundation's core business systems (including SAP, Ariba and Convera), overseeing training, licensing, user support and escalation management while maintaining appropriate team resilience and back-up coverage. Oversee invoicing, billing, payment processing, sales order administration, vendor onboarding and procurement compliance, ensuring accuracy, strong financial controls and adherence to organisational policies. Manage organisational subscriptions, approved travel provider relationships, purchasing support and the resolution of financial administration queries, including expense investigations and budget coding issues. Lead the continuous improvement of business support processes, systems and documentation, driving greater efficiency, consistency, automation and service excellence across the Foundation. Develop and deliver guidance, training and performance reporting for business support services, identifying opportunities for further centralisation and supporting wider Operations objectives. Oversee delivery of core administrative services, including executive diary management, travel and event coordination, onboarding and offboarding administration, facilities support, shared inbox management, organisational records and contingent worker administration. Provide hands-on support for complex travel arrangements, staff induction activities, organisational website updates and logistics for Foundation-wide events, ensuring a seamless experience for colleagues and stakeholders. About You To be a Executive Support Team Lead at the Thomson Reuters Foundation, you will likely have: Proven experience in business operations, office management, business support or financial administration, including responsibility for leading and developing teams. Strong understanding of invoicing, procurement and financial administration processes, with a track record of ensuring accuracy, compliance and effective controls. Experience using ERP and financial management systems, such as SAP, alongside invoicing and payment platforms (e.g. Convera); familiarity with system administration and user support is advantageous. Previous experience within a charity, NGO or purpose-led organisation would be beneficial. Demonstrated people leadership skills, with the ability to coach, motivate and develop high-performing teams while fostering a collaborative and customer-focused culture. Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple activities, balance competing demands and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, coupled with sound judgement and a continuous improvement mindset focused on enhancing processes, efficiency and service delivery. Confident communicator and relationship builder, capable of working effectively with senior stakeholders, programme teams and external suppliers, while handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion and professionalism. What’s in it For You? Global Perspective and Impact: Interested in working for a dynamic global organization with a focus on social impact? With hubs all over the world from Bangkok to Madrid to Rio de Janeiro, join a truly international team with a shared goal of helping to build societies around the world that are free, fair, and informed. Unique Approach: Our expertise in media and the law is world class. We combine the power of both to address the critical issues faced by humanity. Our Relevance: With a focus on advancing media freedom, fostering more inclusive economies and promoting human rights, our work has never been more needed than right now. Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer competitive salary packages and market-leading benefits. Learning & Development: We are dedicated to the continual professional development of our employees and offer access to both in-house and external training opportunities. About Thomson Reuters Foundation TheThomson Reuters Foundationisthe corporatefoundation of Thomson Reuters, the global news and information services company. As an independent charity, registered in the UK and USA, we leverage our media, legal and data driven expertise to strengthen independent journalism, enable access to the law and promote responsible business. Through news, media development, free legal assistance and data intelligence, we aim to build free, fair and informed societies.

item.title: Data, Insight and Development Lead
item.description: Hours: 37 per week (part timemin 25 hours considered) Bradford and Airedale Citizens Advice & Law Centre is a leading provider of legal advice and information, supporting thousands of clients every year. We are a busy, client focused and dynamic service with a track record of delivering high-quality advice face to face and over the phone. Our communities are facing unprecedented challenges with rising costs. The rising cost-of-living continues to directly impact individuals and families, with more people than ever in negative budgets and experiencing personal debt. Our teams provide support and empower vulnerable clients to manage their income, maximise income and assess their best strategies and options to address debt issues long-term. Join our Team! We're looking for a curious and analytical Business Analyst to join our team and help us understand how our services work, where they can work better, and how technology and data can support the tens of thousands of people who come to us for help each year. About the Role To lead the development and continuous improvement of the organisation’s data, insight and reporting systems, ensuring that information is used effectively to improve services, demonstrate impact and support strategic decision-making. As our Data, Insight and Development Lead, you will work alongside operational colleagues, management and development teams, the postholder will combine data analysis with business analysis and service improvement. They will work with colleagues, partners and other stakeholders to understand needs, map processes, identify problems and opportunities, and define practical requirements before new systems, tools or ways of working are developed. The role will turn information from case management, telephony, digital and other systems into clear, accessible reports, dashboards and insights. These will help staff, managers, trustees, funders, commissioners, Citizens Advice and external partners understand service performance, client outcomes, emerging needs, risks, gaps and opportunities. The postholder will act as a bridge between operational teams and developers, ensuring that technology and data solutions address genuine user and organisational needs. They will support improvement projects from discovery through to delivery, including consultation, requirements gathering, testing, documentation, implementation and evaluation, helping new ways of working become embedded and effective. Other organisations may call this role Business Analyst, Business Improvement Officer, Insight & Improvement Analyst, Service Design Analyst, or Systems Analyst. The role will also strengthen the organisation’s Research and Campaigns work by identifying emerging issues affecting clients and producing robust evidence to influence local and national policy. Through this work, the postholder will help establish data as a strategic organisational asset and promote a culture of curiosity, collaboration, continuous improvement, evidence-based decision-making and organisational learning. Closing date:- 9.00 am 5th October 2026 Interview date:- Monday 19th October 2026 (in person)

item.title: Director of Finance and Resources
item.description: The British Academy is the UK’s national academy for the humanities and social sciences. We support outstanding research and researchers, bring new ideas into public debate and help ensure that evidence and expertise inform some of the biggest questions facing society. We are looking for a new Director of Finance & Resources to help us build on that work and plan confidently for the future. This is an important appointment at an exciting point in the Academy’s development. We will celebrate our 125th anniversary in 2027, following a period in which we have grown our policy work, transformed our building to create more opportunities for public engagement and developed a national network for early career researchers. As Director of Finance & Resources, you will make sure we have the resources, systems and organisational capacity to deliver our ambitions. You will lead our finance function and have overall responsibility for HR, IT & AV, Estates & Facilities, and Venue Sales & Marketing, working with experienced Heads of Department across each area. Finance will be central to the role. You will lead our financial strategy and planning, oversee our financial controls and reporting, and provide clear advice to the Chief Executive, Senior Management Team, Council and its committees. You will also help us think longer term about our financial sustainability, including our plans to diversify income through philanthropy and commercial activity. But we are looking for more than a strong Finance Director. You will be part of a close-knit Senior Management Team which works collectively to lead the Academy. We want someone who is interested in the organisation as a whole, who enjoys working across boundaries and who can help colleagues make good decisions about where we put our people, money and attention. You will also have responsibility for some important assets. These include our historic home at 10–11 Carlton House Terrace, our technology and infrastructure, and our trading subsidiary. Ultimately, your job will be to make sure these resources are working as hard as possible in support of the Academy’s purpose. About you You will be a CCAB-qualified accountant with substantial and senior finance experience, gained in a complex organisation. You will have led finance teams and significant budgets and be comfortable advising senior leaders, Boards or Trustees. You will also bring broader leadership experience. You may already have responsibility beyond finance, or have worked closely with areas such as people, operations, estates or technology. We are looking for someone who can combine sound financial judgement with a practical, collaborative approach. You will be able to deal with complexity without making things unnecessarily complicated, communicate clearly with people who are not finance specialists, and provide constructive challenge when it is needed. You should also be someone who enjoys leading through others. There are strong Heads of Department across the Resources portfolio, so this isn't about being the expert in every area. It is about setting direction, asking good questions, supporting people to succeed and bringing the different parts of the portfolio together. Why join us? The British Academy has a distinctive role in national life. In 2025/26 we awarded around £63 million in research funding. Alongside funding research, we convene academics, policymakers, businesses and civil society, engage the public with new ideas and use research to inform policy. The Director of Finance & Resources helps make all of that possible. For someone who wants to use their financial and leadership experience in an organisation with a clear public purpose, this is an opportunity to make a real contribution to the Academy’s next chapter. Recruitment Timetable Application deadline: Sunday 27th September, midnight Shortlisting: Thursday 8th October Fireside chats with CEO: week of 12th October Panel Interviews: 20th / 23rd October To apply, please send your CV, along with a supporting statement (no more than 2 pages) via the link by Sunday 27th September. For an informal conversation about the role please contact our exclusive partner, Bryony Thomas via the Allen Lane agency website.

item.title: Fundraising and Communications Officer
item.description: Fundraising and Communications Officer We are seeking an experienced and proactive fundraiser who can build relationships, grow community support and create engaging communications that make a difference. Salary: £30,000 – £34,000 Location: Hybrid – home and Loughborough, with occasional travel across Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland Hours: 37 hours per week Closing Date: 25th September 2026. Interviews will take place during week commencing 28th September About the role This is an exciting opportunity to join a small, committed fundraising team within a charity working to prevent homelessness and support people at risk. Working closely with the Fundraising and Partnerships Manager, you will help deliver an ambitious fundraising and communications strategy, increasing voluntary income, raising the charity’s profile and developing lasting relationships with supporters, businesses and local communities. It is a varied role combining community fundraising, supporter engagement, events, digital fundraising and communications. Key responsibilities will include: Developing community fundraising opportunities that increase income and awareness. Building relationships with schools, universities, businesses, community groups and individual supporters. Representing the charity at community events, talks and networking opportunities. Helping to create and deliver fundraising events, campaigns and challenge events. Creating engaging social media and website content, including case studies and video. Supporting digital fundraising campaigns, online giving and e-newsletters. Stewarding supporters and fundraisers, helping them feel valued and connected to the charity. Monitoring fundraising activity, budgets and campaign performance. About you You will be a confident relationship-builder who enjoys getting out into the community, meeting people and turning conversations into meaningful support. You will ideally have at least two years’ experience within charity fundraising, with experience across one or more areas such as community fundraising, corporate partnerships, major donors, digital fundraising or social media. You will be comfortable making the ask for support, developing fundraising ideas and creating engaging communications. Strong written and verbal communication skills are important, alongside the ability to manage competing priorities and work collaboratively as part of a small team. You will need to be able to travel across the local area, and some occasional evening and weekend working will be required. A DBS check is also required. About the organisation You will be joining a values-led charity working to prevent homelessness and respond to increasing demand from people who need support. This is an exciting time to join, with a new fundraising strategy focused on growing voluntary income year on year and reaching more people at risk of homelessness. You will have the opportunity to bring ideas, develop new relationships and play a visible part in growing the charity’s community presence. Other roles you may have experience of could include: Community Fundraiser, Fundraising Officer, Communications Officer, Community Engagement Officer, Corporate Fundraiser, Fundraising and Marketing Officer, Supporter Engagement Officer, Community and Events Fundraiser, Fundraising and Communications Executive.

item.title: Director of Fundraising and Communications
item.description: LCH Charity is one of the East Midlands' fastest-growing children's charities. In just five years, we have grown from an annual income of £70,000 to a forecast £1.2 million by August 2027. We have expanded our reach across the East Midlands, built strong partnerships with schools, businesses and communities, and supported tens of thousands of children and families experiencing poverty. Our growth has been driven by innovation, ambition and a relentless focus on meeting the needs of children and young people. Through close collaboration with our school partners, we deliver practical support where it is needed most, helping children to thrive regardless of their circumstances. While our impact within schools continues to grow, we know there is still enormous potential ahead. Awareness of our work beyond the education sector remains relatively low, and the opportunity to engage businesses, philanthropists, individual supporters, trusts and foundations across the region is significant. We are now seeking an exceptional Director of Fundraising and Communications to help unlock that potential and lead the next phase of our journey. The Opportunity This is not a role focused on maintaining the status quo. This is an opportunity to build on a proven success story and help shape the future of a charity with ambitious plans for growth. This is a genuinely exciting opportunity that offers the freedom to be creative and ambitious, with the autonomy to shape, lead and deliver your own strategy. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the growing Executive Leadership Team, you will lead the creation, development and delivery of an ambitious fundraising and communications strategy that diversifies income, elevates our profile and strengthens our reputation across the East Midlands. You will inherit an organisation with strong foundations, a compelling story and a highly successful fundraising model. Our flagship School Colour Dash programme currently generates approximately 70% of our income and has become a powerful platform for both fundraising and engagement. The challenge, and opportunity, is clear. We are looking for a dynamic and entrepreneurial leader who can develop sustainable income streams capable of matching, and ultimately exceeding, the success of our flagship event. This is a rare opportunity to help create the next £1 million of income growth. About the Role As Director of Fundraising and Communications, you will: Lead the creation, development and delivery of a bold and ambitious fundraising and communications strategy. Diversify income across corporate partnerships, major donors, trusts and foundations, community fundraising, individual giving and philanthropy. Develop compelling propositions that inspire investment in our mission. Increase awareness, visibility and understanding of LCH Charity across the East Midlands. Strengthen and protect the charity's brand and reputation. Build strategic relationships with senior business leaders, philanthropists, partners and stakeholders. Identify and develop innovative new income opportunities. Lead and inspire a talented, committed and growing fundraising and communications team. Use insight, data and market intelligence to drive decision-making and growth. Act as a passionate ambassador and advocate for children, young people and families. Use systems to increase engagement across all supporters. Contribute to organisational leadership and strategic development as a member of the Executive Leadership Team. Who We Are Looking For We are seeking an ambitious, strategic and inspirational leader with a proven ability to deliver significant growth. You will be someone who combines vision with action, enjoys building relationships, and thrives in environments where there is genuine opportunity to innovate and make a lasting impact. You will bring: A successful track record of securing substantial fundraising growth. Experience working across a range of income streams, including corporate partnerships, trusts and foundations, philanthropy and individual giving. Strong commercial awareness and an entrepreneurial mindset. Exceptional communication, influencing and relationship-building skills. Experience of developing successful communications, marketing or brand strategies. Strong leadership experience and the ability to motivate and develop teams. The confidence to identify new opportunities and convert them into sustainable income. A genuine passion for improving outcomes for children, young people and families. Most importantly, you will be excited by the opportunity to take an already successful charity to the next level. Why Join LCH Charity? This is a unique opportunity to join a charity that has already demonstrated what can be achieved through ambition, innovation and determination. Over the last four years, we have transformed our income from £70,000 to a forecast £1.2 million, expanded our reach across the East Midlands and built a model that is changing lives every day. Yet we believe we are only at the beginning of our journey. We are looking for a leader who shares our ambition, who sees opportunity rather than limitation, and who wants to play a defining role in shaping the future of a growing and impactful organisation. What Success Will Look Like In this role, you will: Build income streams capable of matching the success of our flagship School Colour Dash programme. Secure transformational corporate, philanthropic and strategic partnerships. Significantly increase awareness and recognition of LCH Charity. Strengthen our influence across the East Midlands. Position LCH Charity as a charity of choice for businesses, donors and supporters. Help drive the organisation through its next phase of transformational growth. Enable thousands more children and families to access the support they need. Join Us We have grown from £70,000 to a forecast £1.2 million in just five years. Now we are looking for an exceptional fundraising and communications leader who can help us do it again. If you are ambitious, entrepreneurial and motivated by the opportunity to create lasting change for children and families, we would love to hear from you. Join us and help build the future of LCH Charity. We are looking for ideas as well as experience. Please submit your CV together with a supporting statement (maximum two pages) outlining: Why this opportunity interests you. Why this role is the right next step in your career. What excites you most about the growth opportunity at LCH Charity. Informal and confidential conversations with our Chief Executive Officer are welcomed and encouraged.

item.title: Mental Health and Homelessness Outreach Worker
item.description: Do you want to support people with mental health issues in a moment of crisis? Are you calm, non-judgemental and able to work effectively with people experiencing distress? If you can embody our values of Hope, Courage, Togetherness , and Responsiveness , and want to help others build resilience and manage their wellbeing, we’d love to hear from you. Mental Health and Homelessness Outreach Worker (Single Homeless Support Pathway) x2 Reference: 368 Salary: £26,000 – £27,000 per annum, depending on skills and experience inclusive of Outer London Weighting (OLW) Hours: 37.5 hours per week (Monday – Friday, 9am – 5pm) Contract: Fixed term 1 Year Working base(s): 1 person to be based in St Albans Wellbeing Centre 1 person to be based in Watford Wellbeing Centre About the Service The Complex Needs Housing Service works as a multi-disciplinary team with housing teams and Drug and Alcohol Services across District and Borough councils. These teams will be working with individuals who are presenting as homeless and have a number of Complex Needs. The service has been running since 2022 with a dual-district model, however, is now expanding to offer a single district outreach service. We have roles available in the service in the following areas: St. Albans – supporting individuals who are homeless, in temporary accommodation or hostels in the district with their mental health South & West Hertfordshire – supporting women who have fled domestic abuse and currently residing in refuge/safe accommodation in the area with their mental health N.B. Only female applicants will be considered for this role. The objectives of the Single Homeless Support Pathway are: To improve the mental wellbeing of people experiencing mental ill health. To increase early access to help for people experiencing mental ill health in, by providing a clear and effective pathway to services provided by Herts Mind Network and other third sector and statutory providers. To contribute to an improvement in individual mental wellbeing. To remain a source of independent support for all clients. To reduce the use of police, ASB, tenancy enforcement, housing needs and environmental health services by clients whose primary need is related to mental ill health. To reduce the use of crisis services by people experiencing mental ill health without positive outcomes for the individual. To provide an assertive outreach approach for clients who are in crisis and/ or those that may have complex or multiple needs. To work collaboratively within a multi-disciplinary team consisting of District and Borough council’s housing teams, drug and alcohol services and other professionals. About the Role The purpose of the Hertfordshire Mind Network Community Outreach Worker role is to: To provide advice, information, onward referral and holistic support to clients who are experiencing mental ill health or need support with their mental wellbeing. These will be clients who are presenting to District and Borough councils as homeless and need intervention and support with their mental health and housing. To ensure that the safety and wellbeing of the client is monitored and reviewed regularly. To remain a source of independent support for all clients. Embed a person-centred recovery orientated and trauma informed approach in all aspects of the roles. We offer: Annual leave entitlement of 25 days per year pro rata, rising in increments to a max. of 29 days after 5 years employment (plus 8 days Bank Holidays) An additional day of leave each year for your birthday following completion of probation period. Ongoing training relevant to your role. An Employee Assistance Programme. Eligibility for blue light card. Health cover (after 6 months employment) – compensation payment for Optical, Dental, Chiropody and Therapy Treatments. Being able to drive and having access to your own vehicle (or equivalent) is essential for this role. Closing date for receipt of applications is Monday 28th September at 5pm. Interviews will be held on a rolling basis. Please note we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. We encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. N.B. Please quote reference number 368 when completing your application for this role. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We welcome applications from all suitably-qualified candidates, irrespective of gender, disability, marital or parental status, racial, ethnic or social origin, colour, religion, belief, or sexual orientation. In addition, during the various stages of recruitment, specific measures can be taken to ensure equal opportunities for candidates with disabilities or special needs. Hertfordshire Mind Network is committed to the Disability Confident and Mindful Employer charters. We actively recruit staff who have a lived experience of mental ill health. Our inclusive approach recognises the unique skills, knowledge, and perspectives that lived experience brings to our team. No agencies please.

item.title: Supporter Services Executive, UK (Deadline:13th September 2026)
item.description: You will be the main person responsible for our UK phone line and be the first point of contact for our many supporters. You will be working closely with the rest of the Supporter Care Team to ensure every interaction supporters have with our charity is a positive one and that they understand how integral they are to our mission. You will communicate with supporters on our progress and ensure we utilise every opportunity for positive engagement. You’ll work with a wide range of people, efficiently gathering and providing information as well responding to whatever queries or situations may arise. As a Supporter Services Executive, you will be working closely with our external fulfilment partners, ensuring that they deliver the high standard of service that we and our supporters expect. With them, you will provide a seamless, first-class end-to-end donor experience. You’ll be well-organised, self-motivated and display a high level of accuracy, consistency and attention to detail and be comfortable working with supporters and colleagues across all of our markets and teams. Supporter Care and Communications Work collaboratively across a global Supporter Experience team to ensure supporter enquiries are handled to the highest standard, providing prompt, efficient, accurate responses in line with the charity’s messaging and service level expectations Keep up to date with programme activities and news from across the organisation to ensure you can provide informed supporter communications and deal with supporter enquiries confidently, efficiently and consistently Handle difficult or distressed supporters in a sensitive and skilled manner, displaying empathy and establishing rapport whilst balancing the needs of Animals Asia Use agreed letter templates and produce bespoke responses as required Coach and co-ordinate with external colleagues to deliver the Animals Asia magic through their work for us Gift Processing & fulfilment coordination Work closely and coordinate with colleagues in the Gift Processing team to ensure that donations are processed in a timely and efficient manner Liaise with external partners to ensure that our gift processing is delivered to the highest and most efficient standards Work with internal colleagues and external partners to ensure supporter queries are managed effectively and requests for materials to be mailed are fulfilled promptly Generate ad hoc acknowledgements and receipts for all offline payment channels, including annual statements to regular donors Process donations, online and offline, across all fundraising products Administer the end-to-end recurring gift process Ensure donations are processed on time and with accurate coding to track the source of fundraising income Assist where required in the review and implementation of new payment channels to ensure smooth and accurate gift processing Develop and maintain a good understanding of local payment channels and processes Administration and financials Ensure procedure manuals are updated in line with changes Occasionally help to organise postal mailings Proactively liaise with supporters to capture missing / incomplete donation and supporter information Legal and compliance Keep abreast of GDPR (UK and EU) Ensure full participation in training when provided Ensure that all processes are carried out in line with the mandatory regulations relevant to each country that we operate in and in line with training protocols Database Management Help to maintain donor records & data integrity Accurately enter new data and amend existing data on the fundraising database following contact from supporters, and in line with Animals Asia’s policies and procedures Ensure supporter interactions are recorded accurately and consistently Ensure recurring gifts records are clear and neat on the fundraising database Fundraising Support and Supporter Journey Assist with the delivery of fundraising materials to supporters Assist in acquiring and managing UK Gift Aid declaration from the donors to maximise income from Gift Aid Train & supervise volunteers as required Miscellaneous Promote and advocate AAF to the general public Actively participate in team meetings Always keep the supporters and interests of Animals Asia at heart when dealing with supporters so as to develop and maintain positive long-lasting relationships Person Specification Qualifications, knowledge & skills required: Excellent written and oral communication skills, with extensive experience communicating with a broad range of people Demonstrable experience in a customer service role responding to a high level of enquiries via telephone and email with excellent interpersonal skills and telephone manner Experience of working on a customer relationship database (experience with Blackbaud CRM - a NFP database - is highly valuable, but not essential) Ability to understand and streamline processes and procedures Proven high level organisational and time management skills, including ability to manage workflows and balance competing priorities Understanding of working in a fundraising environment Accuracy and excellent attention to detail Demonstrable ability to respond effectively to challenges, to work effectively in a small, diverse and busy cross-functional team environment with minimal supervision Highly organised, able to prioritise varied workloads and meet deadlines Understanding of Data Protection (GDPR in UK & EU) Understanding of animal welfare issues and conservation is desirable but not essential Personal attributes required: Innovative, flexible and resilient Always acts professionally, with integrity and discretion Excellent attention to detail Well presented, articulate and polite Genuine enjoyment of meeting and interacting with people and building relationships Strong people skills with a high level of organisational awareness and ability to liaise with a broad and diverse range of stakeholders Commitment to professionalism, discretion and confidentiality Solution-focused with a creative approach to issues and a “can do” attitude Be able to take on accountability and to take the lead while being a strong team player Ability to display initiative, common sense and diplomacy Thoughtful and considerate Passionate about animals and animal welfare Circumstances (essential): Able to work efficiently and effectively from home without disruption Able to connect to sustained, high quality internet connection from home Able to be work occasional extended hours and weekends as required Able to accommodate global meetings in the early morning or late evening (flexible working hours) Conditions and Benefits Place of work : Home based – anywhere in the United Kingdom. Working hours : Full time – standard hours are 37.5 hours per week. You will be required to work such additional hours as are necessary to fulfill your role which may include evenings and weekends. You will be expected to manage your hours, responsibilities and workload accordingly. Reports to : Global Head of Supporter Care. Manages : n/a. Budget responsibility : n/a. Probation : The appointment will be subject to the satisfactory completion of a 3 month probationary period. Annual leave : Annual paid vacation entitlement of 32 in each holiday year, this entitlement includes the eight bank and public holidays. Other benefits : Training will be provided as required. Flexible working conditions. How to apply Applications should be in the form of a CV with a covering letter explaining your interest in and suitability for the role. Please provide both email and telephone contact information for yourself. . Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK. Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Applications should be received by 11:59pm on Sunday 13th September 2026 at the latest.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: We’re looking for someone inspirational, approachable, open-minded, with great communication skills and a genuine passion for supporting people experiencing mental health difficulties, their families, friends and their carers to live their best lives. If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. As our current CEO prepares for retirement, we are looking for someone new to lead our organisation with the kindness and professionalism we’re known for. For more than 30 years, Pembrokeshire and Carmarthen Mind has supported people across the Pembrokeshire and Carmarthen Local Authority areas and the Hywel Dda University Health Board region. Mental health challenges affect people from all walks of life, and the need for accessible, person-centred support continues to grow. Conditions such as anxiety, depression, and other long-term mental health difficulties remain some of the most common health issues faced by individuals, families, and communities. Compassionate, local mental health support can make a meaningful difference, we help people build resilience, maintain independence, and find hope during difficult times. Across the UK, many people experience significant impacts on their daily lives, relationships, and wellbeing because of mental health problems. The wider effects on families, carers, and support networks can also be profound, highlighting the importance of early help, ongoing support, and community-based services. Who we’re looking for: We’re looking for an experienced, confident and compassionate leader who can balance people, purpose and performance. You will be responsible for implementing the organisation’s strategy, as set by the Board of Trustees, leading staff and volunteers, overseeing services and finances, and ensuring strong governance and compliance. You’ll need strong knowledge and understanding of NHS and Local Authority structures, as well as health and social care legislation in Wales. You will maintain our welcoming, inclusive culture while planning for the future by identifying opportunities, building new partnerships and income streams, managing risk, and ensuring the charity’s financial sustainability. You will be a great listener, ensuring that our community feels heard. You will amplify their voices locally, regionally and nationally. These views will also inform the design, development and delivery of all our high-quality services Application Resources For Job Role specifics and more about us please see our CEO Recruitment Pack Application Instructions Ready to lead? If you are interested in becoming Pembrokeshire and Carmarthen Mind’s next permanent Chief Executive Officer, please complete our application form and attach your CV. The application form can be found on our website. For Full Application Instructions and more about us please see our CEO Recruitment Pack Closing date for this role will be at 12:00 midday on 30/09/26 Interviews for this role will be held on week commencing 19/10/26

item.title: Connect To Work Triage Co-ordinator
item.description: An exciting full time opportunity has opened up at CPSL Mind. CPSL Mind is a vibrant, values-led charity that supports local people in their recovery from mental health issues, promotes wellbeing and campaigns against stigma and discrimination. Connect To Work Triage Co-ordinator Salary: £27,113.00 per annum Salary Scale Point: 15 Hours: 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday Based: Peterborough with hybrid working option About CPSL Mind Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and South Lincolnshire (CPSL) Mind is a progressive and expanding mental health charity. Our vision is a society in which everyone has positive mental health and feels part of a connected community. Our work ranges from prevention and early intervention to award-winning crisis support. We also seek to influence positive change through our training services and ground-breaking campaigns activity. About the Service The Connect to Work Triage Coordinator is a key role, coordinating activity between referrers and partner providers to ensure individuals receive support and guidance to support them to enter, return to, or stay in work. This role is responsible for triaging Expressions of Interest for the Connect to Work programme, delivered in partnership with Cambridgeshire County Council and other specialist providers. This role will: Provide the first point of contact and support for individuals referring in Oversee completion of pre-assessment of eligibility against defined criteria Ensure the smooth handover of eligible referrals through to specialist employment services Connect ineligible referrals with an appropriate local service, maintaining a strong understanding of CPSL Mind services, local groups and other local service providers Support the collection of data and impact stories required for reporting against key performance indicators. Taking general enquiries Key criteria: You should have demonstrable ability to connect with individuals and staff with empathy, compassion and understanding in relation to their unique challenges and needs. Strong verbal and written communications skills are essential, with the ability to clearly articulate ideas and instructions. Proven ability to work collaboratively and build strong professional relationships with a diverse range or stakeholders, including individuals, employers and healthcare providers Closing date: 28th September 2026 Interview Date: To be advised Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. CPSL Mind is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. We actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills and potential and welcome applications from a wide range of candidates, including those with criminal records. Having a criminal record will not necessarily bar you from working with us. This will depend on the nature of the position and the circumstances and background of your offences. No agencies please.
