item.title: Corporate Partnerships Manager
item.description: Purpose of the role The Literacy Pirates is an educational charity working across the UK to develop the literacy, confidence and perseverance of children who are falling behind in school and have fewer opportunities in their personal lives. We offer in-person and online literacy programmes that support children to meet age-related expectations in reading and writing, succeed in school, and thrive beyond the classroom. Literacy Pirates is at an incredibly exciting point in its 15-year journey, as we embark on year two of our five-year national expansion plan, with a target to quadruple the number of young people we support over the next four years and double our fundraised income. About the Fundraising & Communications Department The Corporate Partnerships Manager reports to the Head of Development and is part of the broader fundraising and communications team along with the Trusts & Foundation Manager and Communications Manager. Corporate partnerships revenue accounts for 40% of our fundraised income and is a key strategic target for growth. The Corporate Partnerships Manager role is therefore critical to achieving our national expansion ambitions. This role is office-based in London, with the option to work from remotely two days a week. Key Purpose Duties and Responsibilities General A commitment to high standards of service delivery and customer care Regularly monitor and update all financial and KPI data on departmental reporting documents Participate actively in regular departmental meetings and support colleagues on broader fundraising and communications work. Person Specification Interest in, and enthusiasm to, identify and develop new corporate fundraising strategies and initiatives. Proven track record of securing income and managing partnerships and sponsorships within a target driven environment Experience of delivering events, both standalone and as a part of a wider partnership. Salary: £40,000 - 42,000 (incl. London Weighting) Contract: Full time, permanent Location: London based, three days in the office, with the option to work remotely two days.

item.title: Content Coordinator
item.description: We're looking for an organised and creative Content Coordinator to join our Communications team and help bring IHP's work, impact and stories to life. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys creating engaging content, managing digital communications and ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. IHP’s vision is to see a world in which all suffering due to lack of healthcare is eradicated. Our Christian faith underpins all that we do. It motivates us to care for those in need, and give our best in all circumstances, as an expression of God's love. We serve the poor in health without regard for ethnic or religious background, focusing on where the need is greatest. About the role This is a varied and hands-on role where you'll help ensure our communications are engaging, consistent and effectively showcase the impact of our work. Working closely with the Communications Manager and Senior Communications Officer, you'll play a key role in delivering day-to-day communications activity across IHP's channels. You'll be responsible for: Creating and scheduling engaging social media content Helping to tell the stories of the people and communities we support Managing and maintaining digital content and image libraries Supporting communications campaigns and partnership activities Maintaining content calendars, records and communications systems Identifying opportunities to improve audience engagement and content effectiveness About you We're looking for someone who has experience creating content for social media and digital channels, understands how to create content that engages different audiences across social media platforms, and is comfortable using analytics or communications data to understand what is working. Experience managing digital content, images or other communications assets would also be valuable. You will be: ✅ Highly organised, with excellent attention to detail ✅ Confident and engaging in both written and verbal communication ✅ Comfortable planning and scheduling regular content ✅ Able to work independently and use initiative ✅ Collaborative and approachable, with strong interpersonal skills ✅ Confident maintaining accurate records and systems ✅ Passionate about finding practical ways to improve processes and ways of working Experience in a small charity, not-for-profit or other purpose-driven organisation would be desirable, as would an interest in using communications to demonstrate organisational impact. For further details regarding responsibilities and person specification, please see the job description. Why join IHP? This is more than a communications role. Every piece of content you create will help raise awareness of our work, strengthen partnerships and support our mission to improve access to essential medicines worldwide. You'll join a supportive, values-driven organisation where your contribution will have a direct impact on the lives of vulnerable communities across the globe. Staff regularly spend time together praying for IHP’s work and there is an occupational requirement for the post holder to have a personal commitment to the Christian faith. Employee Benefits include: 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro-rate for part-time hours) Health and wellbeing support through Unum help@hand Life Insurance and Critical Illness Cover Hybrid and flexible working options in a modern office near Chancery Lane Tube Station IHP is an Equal Opportunities Employer and is committed to working and embedding diversity and inclusion in all aspects of our work, including recruitment and selection. We actively encourage applicants to inform us of any specific support or reasonable adjustments we can make in the recruitment process (eg for disability or neurodivergence) and will continue this conversation into employment, as appropriate. Applicants must have the legal right to work in the UK. Join a supportive and inclusive team where your skills are valued, your voice is heard, and you have the space to work independently and develop.

item.title: Senior Communications Officer
item.description: We are seeking an experienced and proactive Senior Communications Officer to help raise the profile of International Health Partners and showcase the life-changing impact of our work around the world. Working closely with colleagues, partners and stakeholders, you will lead the development of compelling communications, build strong partnership stories and support the growth of an organisation dedicated to improving access to essential medicines for vulnerable communities. IHP’s vision is to see a world in which all suffering due to lack of healthcare is eradicated. Our Christian faith underpins all that we do. It motivates us to care for those in need, and give our best in all circumstances, as an expression of God's love. We serve the poor in health without regard for ethnic or religious background, focusing on where the need is greatest. About the role This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced communications professional who thrives on storytelling, stakeholder engagement and strategic communications. You'll collaborate across IHP to identify and develop powerful stories, create engaging content across multiple channels and lead communications activity that supports organisational priorities and partnership growth. From developing partnership campaigns and impact stories to creating digital content and communications materials, you will help increase awareness of IHP's work, demonstrate the value of our partnerships and support our mission of improving access to essential medicines worldwide. For further details regarding responsibilities and person specification, please see the job description. About you We're looking for someone who combines excellent communications expertise with creativity, initiative and strong relationship-building skills. You will have: ✅ Excellent writing, editing and storytelling skills ✅ Experience developing communications for different audiences and channels ✅ Strong project management and organisational skills ✅ The ability to influence and advise stakeholders with confidence ✅ A keen eye for detail and commitment to producing high-quality content ✅ A proactive, solutions-focused mindset ✅ Experience evaluating communications activity and using insight to improve performance Experience working within a charity, not-for-profit or purpose driven-organisation is desirable. item.title: Education Programme Lead
item.description: For over 60 years the National Children’s Bureau (NCB) has been building a better childhood for all. We are currently recruiting an Education Programme Lead to join us on a fixed-term contract until March 2027. Education Programme Lead Contract: Fixed term until March 2027 Work Pattern: 35 hours per week. (1 FTE). We are open to flexible hours and working patterns, including accommodating part-time and compressed hours where possible Salary: £51,349 (£55,512 if based in London) Location: London E8 / Belfast, Northern Ireland / Newton Abbot, Devon / Sheffield / Remote within the UK. NCB promotes a hybrid, flexible way of working with 1 day working in the office if based in London. The Vacancy This role will lead key programmes of work related to education and equalities and will work to influence legislation, policy and practice to secure system improvement, more inclusive opportunities and better outcomes for children and young people, with a particular focus on disabled children and young people and those with special educational needs. This role will also be involved in developing opportunities for work on education and equalities to improve access and inclusion in schools, and early years and post-16 settings. They will also develop and hold relationships with partner organisations, local and national agencies, to influence and respond to national education policy affecting wellbeing and disabled children and young people and those with SEN. About NCB For more than 60 years, the National Children’s Bureau has championed the rights and amplified the voice of children and young people in the UK. We interrogate policy and uncover evidence, blending in lived and learnt experience to shape future legislation and develop more effective ways of supporting children and families. Bringing people and organisations together is fundamental to how we improve the systems that babies, children, young people and their families rely on to thrive. We push boundaries, even looking beyond childhood itself to consider transitions into adulthood and the impact of childhood issues on an entire lifespan. We are united for better childhoods and brighter futures. The Benefits 30 Days Annual Leave Generous Pension Scheme Cycle to work scheme Flexible Working Winter Holiday Closure & Break Employee Assistance Programme Applications close at 08:00am on Friday 25th September 2026 . Assessment and interviews to be conducted on Thursday 15th October 2026 . Please note that we reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a high volume of applications. We encourage interested candidates to submit their applications as soon as possible. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We are actively seeking to broaden the diversity of our staff group and warmly welcome applications from candidates underrepresented in the charity sector, including those from Black and Global Majority communities, disabled people, LGBTQ+ individuals, and people with lived experience of the issues NCB works on. No agencies please.

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Communications Officer Job Description About Emergency Nutrition Network (ENN) Emergency Nutrition Network (ENN) works to reduce undernutrition globally. We enhance the effectiveness of nutrition policy and programming by improving knowledge, stimulating learning and building evidence. We are passionate about being network-driven, independent and evidence-based. Our vision is that every individual caught up in a nutritional emergency, or suffering from malnutrition anywhere in the world, gets the most effective help possible. Through our work and collaborations, we support agencies and individuals to implement evidence-based nutrition programming, predominantly in low- and middle-income countries and in fragile and conflict-affected states. ENN’s portfolio includes projects specialising in Infant Feeding in Emergencies, Wasting, Adolescent Nutrition and Management of small & nutritionally At-risk Infants under six months & their Mothers (MAMI), as well as our highly regarded global nutrition publication, Field Exchange. For more information about ENN’s work see our website. Our People ENN’s team is made up of a range of technical experts in nutrition, with decades of collective experience, and a small, experienced operational team. ENN is highly committed to diversity and inclusion, to enabling and promoting flexible working for our staff, and to supporting continued professional development . Terms and Conditions Hours of work : Full time (37.5 hours per week) Type of contract: 12-month fixed term contract, with potential to be made permanent. Location: Hybrid or UK-based homeworking with occasional travel to meetings, training events and organisational activities, primarily in Oxford/Oxfordshire . ENN may operate hybrid working arrangements and reserves the right to review working arrangements in the future following consultation. Applicants must have and maintain a valid right to work in the United Kingdom throughout their employment with ENN. Holidays: 25 days plus UK public holidays, increasing by one day per annum after two complete years of service to a maximum of 27 days per annum.ENN also provides additional paid office closure days between Christmas and New Year. Pro-rata for part-time staff. Pension: Auto-Enrolment to ENN scheme with a generous Employer contribution of 5%. · Additional Benefits include Dental cover, Life cover, Employee Assistance Programme and Wellbeing contribution. · Salary: £28,000 to £29,000 per annum, dependent on experience and suitability for the role. · Purpose of the role and Reporting Lines The Communications Officer will report to the Communications and Digital Manager. The role works closely with our Project Managers, and technical project leads. The Communications Officer will facilitate effective and engaging communications across the organisation (internal and external) with particular emphasis on enabling effective communication of our project’s work/outputs, demonstrating impact, and enhancing dissemination to a wider and more diverse audience. We are looking for someone with a passion for translating technical nutrition/public health content and communicating it to a broad array of stakeholders, ensuring it is widely accessible, to drive effective and positive change in nutrition policy, practice and research at global, regional and national levels. Key Responsibilities: Support the Communications and Digital Manager in executing ENN’s communication strategies (both internal and external) by: Project Communications, Publication and Dissemination · Plan and execute a communication and dissemination plan for each project/output, working alongside the technical project lead, project manager and communication and digital manager, within budget/resourcing. · Produce an array of professional dissemination resources (e.g. social media content, brochures, posters, visual abstracts etc) to effectively communicate our work to different audiences (both technical and non-technical) · Create engaging visual multimedia content for use on ENN websites, social media channels and online events, under the support and direction of the Communications and Digital Manager. · Manage an image bank, ensuring that it is refreshed, and that all imagery has been appropriately licensed/credited. Identifying suitable imagery for use in various contexts. · Support with procurement, coordination and briefing of copyeditors, designers, videographers, translators, printers and other external communication service providers as needed. Review and check proofs and coordinate feedback/revisions. · Assist with the production and dissemination of ENN’s flagship publication Field Exchange (both print and digital in English and French). · Set up and administer online meetings, launch webinars, and in-person dissemination events e.g., conference side events etc. · Create and administer surveys seeking feedback on our work including collation and formatting of results. Website and social media · Online content production and day-to-day updating and uploading of content on ENN’s website, and YouTube channel. · Manage social media campaigns for projects/outputs/events, including drafting and posting content across platforms (LinkedIn, Facebook, WhatsApp Community, en-net forum) · Plan and manage a social media calendar, scheduling posts and aligning content with relevant days/upcoming events in the sector relevant to ENN’s work. · Support with delivering training/instruction, producing guidance, for staff on use of social media, comms/website, AI etc. · Maintain the CRM system (network signups through the website), and communication to our networks via newsletters, ensuring that data protection procedures are adhered to. Communication Monitoring and Analysis · Monitor and analyse communications data and produce reports to improve performance and grow our audience and reach · Ensure that monitoring sources (including Google Analytics/DOIs) are up to date and collection of website monitoring data is functioning properly. · Support with data visualisation Digital Fundraising · Undertake research on potential funding opportunities/sources, and support with developing funding proposal with a focus on digital fundraising Person Specification Essential · Knowledge or strong interest in communication in nutrition, global public health, and / or the humanitarian/development sector. · Excellent communication (in both English and French): writing, editing, presenting and proof-reading skills; the ability to write content for websites/social media including adapting technical language and content to appeal to a wide and diverse audience. · Experience producing high-quality communication and dissemination products using a variety of digital tools/software. · Creative vision to help develop appealing content that is accessible, with an eye for detail and design. Able to innovate and problem-solve. Open to learn new skills. · Experience in organising high level dissemination events e.g. launch webinars/ conference events, online and in-person. · Strong organisational skills, with experience of prioritising a varied workload and meeting deadlines using own initiative and with minimal supervision. · Excellent attention to detail and ability to consolidate data and information with a high degree of accuracy. · Strong interpersonal skills, able to work both autonomously and as a member of a dispersed and diverse team. · Good cross-cultural communication skills with an understanding of, and commitment to, equal opportunities and diversity. · Experience in creating /uploading website content and working with online content management systems. · Proficiency with mainstream social media platforms (e.g., YouTube, Threads, LinkedIn, Instagram) and experience using social media effectively for business purposes. · Ability to use Adobe Suite, Canva and video/podcast editing software e.g. Riverside. · Strong technical skills including fluency in Microsoft Office Desirable · Practical experience in web design and functionality · Experience in filming interviews/producing podcasts · Experience working with CRMs web and email management platforms (e.g., Brevo, Salesforce, HubSpot, Drupal, Mailchimp) · Experience with Google Analytics and/or other website data analytics and data visualisation tools. · Other Language skills (e.g. Spanish, Arabic) are not essential but will be a plus as we also produce content in these languages Eligibility to work: The successful applicant will be required to demonstrate that they have and can maintain the Right to Work in the United Kingdom throughout their employment with ENN. This includes evidencing a UK National Insurance number and UK tax residency. A Certificate of Sponsorship, visa sponsorship and relocation package are not available for this position. ENN is committed to diversity and inclusion, and to building a culture where every staff member and volunteer is recognised and valued as an individual. We actively encourage applications from a broad range of experiences and backgrounds. Application Process Please submit a Cover Letter (no more than 1 page) and CV no later than 23:59 on Tursday 1 October 2026.

This is an exciting time to join us. HMP Channings Wood is preparing for a significant prison expansion, creating opportunities for development, progression, and future career growth within a growing service. item.title: Fundraising Manager
item.description: Community Volunteers Enabling You (COVEY) has been a lifeline for children, young people and families across Lanarkshire since 1992. We provide one-to-one and group-based befriending, mentoring and family support services tailored to those who need it most. Our mission is to help children, young people and families become more resilient, safe and better equipped to reach their full potential. As Fundraising Manager, you will lead the development of community fundraising, corporate fundraising and fundraising events (either held by us or undertaken by members of the public such as the Kiltwalk), helping COVEY grow sustainable unrestricted income and build long-term relationships with supporters. This is a brand new role with real scope to build on COVEY’s trusted place in the local community, developing new fundraising opportunities and partnerships, as well as building on our existing relationships with volunteers, staff, trustees, supporters, funders, schools, employers, community partners and local networks. You will also help shape fundraising activity linked to COVEY’s 35th anniversary in 2027, using this milestone to celebrate the children, young people and families we have supported over this time (and the volunteers and staff that made it happen), in turn raising our profile and build long-term supporter relationships beyond the anniversary year. This role would suit someone who is confident, proactive and relationship-focused, with the ability to engage people, spot opportunities, make compelling asks, build partnerships and turn interest into meaningful support for COVEY. What we’re looking for: A successful track record of generating income, developing partnerships, identifying new leads and converting opportunities into active support Previous experience of fundraising, which could include community fundraising, corporate fundraising, supporter stewardship, sponsorship, challenge events, employee fundraising, Charity of the Year partnerships, etc Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, including confidence in networking, presenting and making fundraising asks Strong planning and organisational skills, with the ability to manage fundraising activity, events, budgets, supporter communications and CRM records A collaborative, supporter-focused approach and a strong commitment to COVEY’s mission, values and outcomes COVEY is entering an important period of growth. Our 2025-28 Strategy sets out ambitious plans to increase income, grow unrestricted funding, strengthen our external profile and develop wider community support for the charity. The Fundraising Manager will play a key role in achieving this, and will be able to shape exactly how we do this from the ground up. What We Offer We offer a rewarding and fulfilling role with the opportunity to develop your skills and career in an enriching environment. Our benefits package includes: 6% employer pension contribution 22 days annual leave (rising to up to 27 days) and 10 public holidays One special leave day to celebrate your birthday Flexible working HSF Health plan (including dental, optical, physio claim back, personal accident coverage, GP, mental health counselling, legal support, and discounts for gym, cinema, and shopping) Quarterly staff wellbeing activities Access to ScotWest Credit Union (loans, mortgages, and savings accounts) Access to learning and development opportunities

item.title: Recovery Coordinator
item.description: Overview Looking for a rewarding career where you can make a real difference? Join our team at HMP Channings Wood as a Recovery Coordinator and help people overcome challenges, reduce the impact of drug and alcohol use, and take positive steps towards recovery. You'll work closely with individuals throughout their recovery journey, providing tailored support, delivering interventions, facilitating group sessions, and helping people access the services they need to achieve lasting change. Experience in substance misuse, criminal justice, mental health, social care, or a related field is beneficial, but we're equally interested in people with strong transferable skills, a passion for supporting others, and a commitment to making a difference. This is an exciting time to join us. HMP Channings Wood is preparing for a significant prison expansion, creating opportunities for development, progression, and future career growth within a growing service. If you're looking for a role with purpose, where you can empower people to build healthier, more positive futures, we'd love to hear from you. Where: HMP Channings Wood Ho urs: 37.5 per week Contract Type: Permanent Full-time hours at Change Grow Live are 37.5 hours per week. For part-time roles, the salary and payments will be pro rata based on contracted hours. This is a rolling recruitment campaign and applications will be reviewed as they are received. The vacancy will close once a suitable candidate has been appointed, so early applications are encouraged. Responsibilities Looking for a Rewarding Career Where You Can Make a Real Difference? As a Recovery Coordinator at HMP Channings Wood, you'll support people to overcome challenges, reduce the impact of drug and alcohol use, and take positive steps towards recovery. You'll work closely with individuals throughout their recovery journey, helping them identify goals, access support, build resilience, and make sustainable changes that improve their health and wellbeing. Experience in substance misuse, criminal justice, mental health, social care, or a related field can be beneficial, but we're equally interested in people with strong transferable skills, a passion for supporting others, and a commitment to making a difference. Why Join Us? This is an exciting time to join our team. HMP Channings Wood is preparing for a significant prison expansion, and our service will grow alongside it to support an increasing prison population. Joining us now means becoming part of a growing team with exciting opportunities for development, progression, and future career growth. What You'll Do Carry out assessments and develop personalised recovery plans. Support individuals throughout their recovery journey. Deliver one-to-one interventions and facilitate group sessions. Help reduce drug and alcohol-related harm and promote healthier lifestyles. Signpost and refer individuals to appropriate support services. Advocate on behalf of service users to improve access to support. Work collaboratively with prison staff, healthcare teams, and partner organisations. Support people to build confidence, resilience, and independence. Monitor progress and review outcomes to support positive change. What We're Looking For You might be a great fit if you: Enjoy helping and supporting others. Communicate effectively and build positive relationships. Can motivate and engage people who may be reluctant to access support. Are organised and able to manage competing priorities. Work well independently and as part of a team. Have a proactive, solution-focused approach. Are committed to learning and developing your skills. Experience in substance misuse, criminal justice, mental health, social care, healthcare, community work, counselling, coaching, mentoring, or related services is welcomed but not essential. We value attitude, motivation, and transferable skills and will provide support to help you develop in the role. What We Offer 25 days annual leave capped at 30 days. Paid weekly Wellbeing Hour. Pension scheme and employee wellbeing support. Discounts on shopping, travel, and entertainment. Ongoing training and career development opportunities. Join Us At Change Grow Live, we believe everyone deserves the opportunity to change, grow, and live life to its full potential. Apply today and help people take positive steps towards recovery, wellbeing, and a brighter future. This is a rolling recruitment campaign and applications will be reviewed as they are received. The vacancy will close once a suitable candidate has been appointed, so early applications are encouraged. Please ensure that when completing your application form and supporting statement, you reflect on the details outlined in the job description. This will help us understand how your skills and experiences align with the requirements of the role. A note about using AI in your application AI can be a really helpful tool when putting together your application, and we're happy for you to use it. However, what we're most interested in is you. We want to understand your experiences, achievements and strengths, so please make sure your application reflects your own story and clearly shows how you meet the essential criteria and the impact you've made in previous roles. There's no need to write in a particular style. The strongest applications are those that are authentic, specific and clearly demonstrate your skills, experience and potential. We look forward to learning more about you . Direct applications only — we will not be engaging agencies for this vacancy. Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK at the time of application. For applicants with time-limited visas, unfortunately, we are unable to support new visa applications or extensions. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Salary Range (pro rata if part time) CGL points 23 to 28 (£28,557.79 - £32,802.41) Closing Date 25/11/2026 This post is subject to a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check at an enhanced level.

item.title: Residential & Commercial Property Manager
item.description: Residential & Commercial Property Manager Hours: Minimum of 37.5 hours per week, normally Monday to Friday. Due to the nature of the role the working pattern may occasionally change to include evenings, weekends and Public Holidays, with reasonable notice provided or by prior agreement. This may be to support property inspections, tenant matters, or other operational requirements for example. TOIL will be provided for additional planned evening or weekend working in accordance with departmental arrangements. Normal start and finish times may be reasonably adjusted with reasonable notice to meet operational requirements. The role requires regular travel across the property portfolio and occasional travel to St James's Place, London, and other locations as required. The Role The Property Department is responsible for the facilities management and maintenance of the historic, residential and commercial properties belonging to the Rothschild Foundation and National Trust, including Waddesdon Manor, The Stables, Windmill Hill, the Five Arrows Hotel, The Bow, The Dairy, commercial and residential properties and various other smaller outbuildings, staff houses and general infrastructure. The department is led by the Head of Property & Facilities Management, supported by the Facilities & Maintenance Manager, Residential & Commercial Property Manager and a team of skilled trade technicians, general facilities & maintenance operatives, grounds assistants and administrative and data support staff. The Residential & Commercial Property Manager is responsible for the effective management, performance and development of the Rothschild Foundation's residential and commercial property portfolio, working within the strategic direction set by the Head of Property & Facilities Management. What you will do The role is responsible for maintaining high standards of landlord and property management, supporting optimal occupancy and rental income, ensuring appropriate legal and regulatory compliance, and providing a professional and responsive service to tenants and internal stakeholders. The postholder line manages the Lettings Administrator and works closely with the Facilities & Maintenance Manager, Facilities & Maintenance Administrator, Property & Systems Data Lead, Finance and HR to ensure the effective management of the portfolio. Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Portfolio Management & Strategy Work with the Head of Property & Facilities Management to develop and deliver the long-term strategy for the residential and commercial property portfolio. Manage the day-to-day performance of the residential and commercial portfolio, ensuring properties are managed effectively, professionally and in accordance with organisational objectives. Maintain oversight of occupancy, voids, rental performance and emerging portfolio risks, providing regular information and recommendations to the Head of Property & Facilities Management. Identify opportunities to improve the performance, condition, use and value of the portfolio and make recommendations for investment or improvement. Support property acquisitions, disposals, lease renewals and other portfolio changes as required, working with appropriate professional advisers. Prepare and contribute to relevant budgets, forecasts and longer-term property plans and monitor expenditure and income against agreed targets. Residential Lettings & Tenancy Management Provide management oversight of the full residential lettings and tenancy lifecycle, ensuring properties are marketed, let and managed efficiently and in accordance with organisational policy and legal requirements. Line manage the Lettings Administrator, providing clear direction, regular one-to-one meetings, performance management, development support and appropriate oversight of workload and priorities. Ensure appropriate processes are in place for marketing, viewings, referencing, tenancy documentation, inventories, rent reviews, renewals, tenancy changes and check-out arrangements. Review recommendations relating to prospective tenants, rental values and tenancy arrangements and approve or escalate decisions in accordance with delegated authority. Maintain oversight of rent collection and arrears, working closely with Finance and ensuring concerns are identified and escalated promptly. Ensure tenant queries, complaints and tenancy-management matters are handled promptly, professionally and consistently. Maintain appropriate oversight of void properties and coordinate with Facilities & Maintenance colleagues to agree required works and support timely re-letting. Staff Accommodation Provide property-management oversight of the organisation's staff accommodation portfolio, working closely with the Director of People and HR Department. Ensure the Lettings Administrator provides effective administration of staff accommodation, including Manor flats, National Trust Key Representative housing, Pathways Programme accommodation and other short-term or emergency accommodation. Ensure property, landlord, occupancy and compliance requirements relating to staff accommodation are appropriately managed. Work with the Director of People and/or Head of Property & Facilities Management on staff accommodation matters, recognising that employment-related eligibility, approvals, rental concessions and associated policy decisions sit outside the Lettings Administrator role and are determined in accordance with organisational policy. Commercial Property Management Manage the day-to-day administration and performance of the commercial property portfolio, maintaining appropriate records of leases, licences, rent reviews, renewals and other key dates. Build and maintain effective relationships with commercial tenants and occupiers and act as a key point of contact for property-management matters. Coordinate lease events, rent reviews and other commercial property matters with external agents, valuers, solicitors and other professional advisers as required. Monitor rental performance, arrears, lease compliance and emerging risks and make recommendations to the Head of Property & Facilities Management. Support the effective management of commercial properties including the Five Arrows Hotel and The Bow where relevant to the landlord/property-management responsibilities of the Foundation. Property Maintenance & Condition Work in close partnership with the Facilities & Maintenance Manager to agree priorities, capacity and workflows for planned and reactive works across the residential and commercial portfolio, balancing property and tenant requirements with available Facilities & Maintenance resources and wider departmental priorities. Agree appropriate timescales for works with the Facilities & Maintenance Manager before commitments are made to tenants or other stakeholders, and ensure priorities are reviewed where operational demands or available capacity change. Provide the Facilities & Maintenance Manager with relevant property, tenancy and access information to support effective planning and allocation of work. Maintain appropriate oversight of outstanding residential and commercial property works, working with the Facilities & Maintenance Manager and Facilities & Maintenance Administrator to ensure progress is communicated effectively to tenants and other stakeholders. Monitor property condition and identify emerging repair, investment or compliance requirements, escalating significant issues to the Head of Property & Facilities Management. Support property inspections, condition reviews and programmes of improvement as required. Escalate competing priorities, significant capacity constraints or unresolved issues to the Head of Property & Facilities Management where agreement cannot reasonably be reached. Compliance & Risk Ensure the residential and commercial portfolio is managed in accordance with applicable landlord, property, housing and tenancy legislation and regulatory requirements. Maintain oversight of relevant property and tenancy compliance records, working closely with the Property & Systems Data Lead and Facilities & Maintenance colleagues to ensure information is accurate and up to date. Ensure appropriate processes are maintained for statutory and landlord requirements, including relevant safety certification, tenancy documentation, deposit and occupancy requirements where applicable. Keep abreast of changes in residential and commercial property legislation and good practice and advise the Head of Property & Facilities Management on implications for the portfolio. Identify, assess and escalate property-management risks and support the implementation of appropriate controls and mitigations. Work with the Facilities & Maintenance Manager and Health & Safety Manager to ensure responsibilities for property compliance, maintenance compliance and health and safety are clearly coordinated. Stakeholder & Professional Relationships Develop and maintain positive and professional relationships with residential and commercial tenants, prospective tenants and occupiers. Work collaboratively with the Head of Property & Facilities Management, Facilities & Maintenance Manager, Facilities & Maintenance Administrator, Property & Systems Data Lead, Finance, HR and other internal stakeholders. Build and maintain effective relationships with external agents, valuers, solicitors, local authorities, contractors and other professional advisers. Represent the Rothschild Foundation professionally in property-management discussions and negotiations within the authority delegated to the role. Prepare reports, updates and property information for the Head of Property & Facilities Management and other stakeholders as required. Undertake occasional travel to St James's Place, London, and other locations as required in connection with the responsibilities of the role. You will be a great fit if: You’re a confident communicator and supportive manager who us

item.title: Hertfordshire Project Assistant
item.description: Job Title: Hertfordshire Project Assistant Salary: £27,980 (London Fringe weighting) Position Type: Full time/Fixed term (until December 2028) Reports to: Scaling Manager Based at: Remote, with travel to schools in Hertfordshire Working Hours: 5 days a week, 9am-5pm (flexible) Pension: School Food Matters matches pension contributions at 7% of pensionable earnings Holiday: 31 days including bank holidays that fall on working days. Holidays must be taken during the school holidays This role requires occasional work outside of core hours (for example, if visiting a school breakfast club). It also requires travel to schools across Hertfordshire, so access to a car would be desirable. Training for delivery of the programme will be provided online and in person, and you will be expected to travel outside of Hertfordshire for some of these sessions. Background to School Food Matters At School Food Matters we believe that school food can unlock a happier, healthier, more sustainable future for every child. We want a school food system that delivers for all children, so they can enjoy nutritious, delicious and sustainable school food and leave school with an informed and positive relationship with food. To achieve this, we campaign for a better school food system, bringing the voices of children, parents, and teachers to government policy, and deliver fully funded food education programmes in schools across the country. Background to Nourish Our Nourish programme supports schools to create a food environment that puts children and young people's nutrition first. The evidence-based, multi-component programme helps schools to develop action plans and policies to cover the food served across the whole school day. Nourish uses a collaborative whole school approach to food involving everyone across the school community to create lasting positive change. Job purpose · To support two Project Officers with the delivery of Nourish in 30 schools in Hertfordshire (primary, secondary and SEND settings) over 2 years Key tasks include · Recruit schools to take part in Nourish · Shadow and support project team to deliver in person food audits in schools · Build relationships and work closely with teachers, teaching assistants, cooks, kitchen teams and senior leaders in schools in Hertfordshire to improve the food they offer their students · Provide practical support to the project team with setting up workshops including paperwork and food shopping · Provide admin support to the project team · Tailor Nourish resources for Hertfordshire schools where required · Collect data and maintain accurate records relating to the project · Gather content for our comms team, website and social media platforms · Keep project team fully updated on progress · Keep up to date with safeguarding requirements and reporting procedures · Maintaining the ethos of the charity and positively promoting our work at all times · You will also be expected to undertake any other tasks relevant to the affairs of SFM that may arise from time to time. Therefore, being flexible and approaching the job with an open and positive mindset is essential. Person Specification Essential · Excellent administrative and organisational skills with great attention to detail · Excellent IT skills including excel, word and email · Ability to work in a team, and seek help when needed · Comfortable engaging with variety of audiences (students, school staff and parents), incl. writing and responding to email, conducting telephone, virtual and face to face meetings, and running workshops · Self-motivated and optimistic with a can-do attitude Desirable · Experience of working for a charity or not for profit organisation · Experience of working in schools · An interest in food education and children’s health · Access to a car

It also requires travel to schools across Hertfordshire, so access to a car would be desirable. Training for delivery of the programme will be provided online and in person, and you will be expected to travel outside of Hertfordshire for some of these sessions. Background to School Food Matters At School Food Matters we believe that school food can unlock a happier, healthier, more sustainable future for every child. Key tasks include · Support with recruitment of schools to take part in Nourish · Complete in person food audits in schools looking across the whole school day · Support schools to create and deliver a food improvement plan (action plan) · Develop and deliver workshops in schools to staff, parents and students based on their action plan (e.g. assemblies, cooking sessions, school food standards training, packed lunch advice, food ed/sensory tasting sessions) · Support schools to write a school food policy · Build relationships and work closely with teachers, teaching assistants, cooks, kitchen teams and senior leaders in schools to improve the food they offer their students · Collect data and maintain accurate records relating to the project · Work closely with University of Hertfordshire and our Evaluation team to complete all monitoring and evaluation · Work in collaboration with Hertfordshire project delivery team · Gather content for our comms team (website and social media platforms) · Keep Scaling Manager fully updated on progress · Keep up to date with safeguarding requirements and reporting procedures · Maintaining the ethos of the charity and positively promoting our work at all times · You will also be expected to undertake any other tasks relevant to the affairs of SFM that may arise from time to time. item.title: Fundraising Manager
item.description: Job description Music as Therapy International is looking for an ambitious, creative and relationship-focused Fundraising Manager to lead our fundraising as we enter an exciting new phase of our development. Registered in 1998 and recently converted to a CIO, we are a small, established charity with a big ambition: To inspire, guide and champion caregivers to use music to strengthen care. Our work equips caregivers with practical skills and approaches that use music to improve the lives of people in vulnerable situations around the world. As our Fundraising Manager , you will have a genuinely influential role in making that ambition possible. Working closely with our Director and wider team, you will take the lead on developing and delivering our fundraising strategy across trusts and foundations, major donors, regular giving, community fundraising, corporate partnerships and legacies. This is not a role where you will be one small part of a large fundraising machine. You will have the opportunity to shape our approach, develop meaningful relationships with supporters and funders, identify new opportunities and turn our impact into compelling propositions that inspire people to give. We have entered a new strategic period focused on extending our reach, evolving our training and securing the future of music in care. In 2025 we operated with an income of c.£225k. We are now looking for someone to build on this, bringing fundraising expertise, initiative and curiosity to help us turn our strategic ambitions into sustainable growth. If you are an experienced fundraiser who enjoys having responsibility, building relationships and seeing the direct results of your work, we would like to hear from you. Refreshed on: 01 September 2026 Closing date: 02 October 2026 at 17:30 Tags: Campaigns, Communications, Fundraising, International Development, Content Writing / Copywriting, Design, Partnerships, Research, Strategy, Community Fundraising, Corporate Fundraising, Individual Giving, Legacy, Major Donor, Trusts / Foundations, Grants The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Trainee Wellbeing Practitioners x 5
item.description: Please note: In accordance with our Safer Recruitment Policy, we are unable to accept CV's and ask that you complete the application form instead This can be found to download further down this page. Application deadline: Wednesday 30th September 2026 (5:00 pm) Proposed Interview Date(s): Tuesday 27th and Thursday 28th of October 2026 ** Please make sure you can be available on the proposed interview date as it is very difficult to offer an alternative ** About The Role Are you an experienced Youth Worker? Are you passionate about improving wellbeing outcomes for young people? Are you looking to develop your practice and training around young people’s mental health? We are currently seeking five Trainee Wellbeing Practitioner’s to join our Youth Services team based in Bristol and South Gloucestershire. You will work within Creative Youth Network as part of the Youth Services team, delivering, high-quality, evidence-based interventions for children and young people experiencing, mild to moderate anxiety, low mood and behavioural difficulties. This is a 1 year training role within the Children and Young People’ Improving Access to Psychological Therapies programme (CYP IAPT). You will attend Exeter University for all university based taught and self-study days required by the education provider, and work in the service for the remaining days of the week using your newly developed skills. Your travel and accommodation to Exeter University will be provided for you as part of the trainee programme. You will then be based at The Station (BS1) or Kingswood Estate (BS15) sites with up to two evening open access sessions per week. The training and service experience will equip you with the necessary knowledge, attitude and capabilities to operate effectively within the wider service. Please note - One of the five Trainee Wellbeing Practitioner roles is LGBTQ+ focused and is in partnership with Diversity Trust. For that role we recognise the value of lived experience and encourage applications from members of LGBTQ+ communities. Please apply via the other listed vacancy (Trainee Wellbeing Practitioner LGBTQ+) for that specific role. About Us Creative Youth Network is an award-winning charity with a mission to enable young people to reach their potential, no matter what their background or circumstances. Operating across Bristol and South Gloucestershire, we offer a range of services ranging from our 9 local youth clubs, to targeted support for young people with specific needs, work within schools (in particular for young people at risk of disengaging from education), and an exciting range of creative courses, programmes and activities, including early career support for young people embarking on careers in the creative sector. Our services are rated “Outstanding” by the National Youth Agency. This role is subject to a satisfactory enhanced DBS check . To Apply A full Job Description and Application form are available to download below and via our website where you can also apply. The Benefits • 33 days annual leave (inc. bank holidays) per year pro rata • Excellent family friendly policies • A generous pension scheme • A cycle to work scheme • Paid breaks • Fantastic development opportunities • Employee Assistance Program • Virtual GP consultation and medical advice service Equity, diversity and inclusion Creative Youth Network is committed to inclusivity, equality, and equity. We pride ourselves on giving opportunities to people of all walks of life and all class backgrounds. This includes people who identify as D/deaf, disabled or neurodivergent, LGBTQIA+, are early in their careers or come from groups who experience racial inequality. We therefore particularly encourage applications from candidates who are likely to be underrepresented, including people from Global Majority backgrounds (often referred to as BAME – Black, Asian or Minority Ethnic). As an employer we are committed to promoting and protecting the physical and mental health and wellbeing of all our staff. Adjustments We want to ensure our recruitment process is accessible to everyone. If you require any reasonable adjustments or support to attend an interview — for example, wheelchair access, extra time for assessments etc. - please let us know.

item.title: VCSE Development Lead
item.description: VCSE Development Lead Wiltshire Wide | 30 hours per week (4 days) | Fixed-term 3 year contract Salary: £32,000 FTE (pro rata) Help Wiltshire's community organisations grow, thrive and make a bigger difference Community groups and charities are at the heart of stronger, healthier communities. They bring people together, tackle local challenges and create opportunities for those who need them most. At Wessex Community Action, we're looking for a passionate and proactive VCSE Development Lead to work alongside voluntary organisations, charities and grassroots groups across Wiltshire, helping them develop the skills, confidence and resilience they need to flourish. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys building relationships, supporting others to succeed and making a tangible difference in communities. What you'll be doing As our VCSE Development Lead, you'll be out in communities across Wiltshire, working directly with organisations at every stage of their journey. Whether it's helping a new community group put the right foundations in place, supporting a charity to strengthen its governance, or helping an organisation become funding-ready, you'll provide practical advice, tailored support and encouragement that enables local organisations to thrive. You'll also develop and deliver training, facilitate networking opportunities and connect organisations with partners, funders and wider support networks. Most importantly, you'll help community organisations become stronger, more sustainable and better equipped to meet local needs. Who we're looking for We're looking for someone who: Has experience working with charities, voluntary organisations or community groups Understands organisational development, governance and community capacity building Can support organisations to improve their sustainability and funding readiness Is confident facilitating workshops, training sessions and group discussions Builds trusted relationships with a wide range of people and organisations Is passionate about empowering communities and reducing inequalities Enjoys working independently while being part of a supportive team What we offer A rewarding role where you can make a real difference in local communities. Flexible and supportive working arrangements. The opportunity to work alongside inspiring community organisations, volunteers and local leaders. A friendly, values-driven team committed to strengthening communities. 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata). Additional leave between Christmas and New Year (subject to organisational arrangements). Contributory pension scheme. Health plan. Annual volunteering day. Training and professional development opportunities. Dedicated external training budget. Join us If you're passionate about helping community organisations develop, grow and create lasting impact, we'd love to hear from you. Please send your CV and a covering letter (maximum two sides of A4) outlining: Your interest in the role Your experience of working with and supporting charities and community groups Closing date: Sunday 4 October Interviews: 12 and 13 October

item.title: Housing Officer - CAS3
item.description: Job Role: Housing Officer Salary: £28,935 per year Hours: 37.5 hours per week Contract type: Permanent Location: Covering Somerset, B&NES and North Somerset Additional information: Participation in an on-call, out-of-hours rota Valid driver's license and access to own vehicle – business insurance will be required for roles involving travel for work. Flexibility to work until 8:00 PM according to the project needs. Please note, this role involves travel across the South West, including Somerset, B&NES, and North Somerset. As travel is a regular part of the role, please note that mileage and other travel expenses can be claimed back. About Alongside: Alongside is the new name for Julian House. We work with people experiencing social exclusion across the South and West of England, providing outreach, accommodation and support. Our clients may be sleeping rough, fleeing abuse, rebuilding after trauma, leaving prison, recovering from addiction, or trying to settle safely in a new community. Whatever their starting point, we work alongside people to help build safety, stability and independence. If you’d like a real sense of job satisfaction, great career prospects and a competitive benefits package, you could be who we’re looking for! About the Role: As a Housing Officer within our CAS3 (Community Accommodation Service Tier 3) project, you’ll be at the heart of supporting individuals leaving prison who might otherwise have nowhere to go. This is your chance to change lives every single day by providing safe, stable temporary accommodation at a crucial turning point in someone’s journey. You’ll manage a dynamic caseload across the Southwest, working directly with people on probation as they transition back into the community. From helping someone settle into their temporary home to empowering them to build the skills and confidence they need to move on successfully; your support will be essential. No two days are the same — and every day is an opportunity to make a meaningful difference. Responsibilities include: Collaborative Working: Build strong relationships with partner agencies, keeping them informed of any issues that may affect clients or their accommodation placements. Together, you’ll create a safer, more supportive environment for every individual . Welcoming New Clients: Be the first point of support for new arrivals — introducing them to their accommodation, helping them settle in, and clearly outlining expectations so they feel confident and supported from day one. Housing Management: Take pride in maintaining high-quality living environments. You’ll ensure properties are safe, secure, and well-kept, promptly identifying and reporting any repairs or maintenance needs to keep homes in top condition. Delivering Outstanding Support: Provide person-centred, strengths-based, and trauma-informed support that empowers clients, builds resilience, and helps them take positive steps toward independence. Please note: Job descriptions are not exhaustive, and the successful candidate may occasionally be asked to take on other duties that align with the key responsibilities outlined. You can view the full job description by clicking here. Qualifications / Requirements: Experience working with people who may have complex needs and/or challenging behaviours. Knowledge around the supported housing sector, ideally having worked with people on probation. Driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes. Willingness to work flexibly until 8pm, as needed, to support new arrivals into properties. There are many great reasons to join our team! Access to our Rewards Platform, which includes an Employee Assistance Programme and Health Cash Plan 27 days annual leave , including an extra day off for your birthday, plus bank holidays - increasing up to 30 days after 4 years of continuous employment (pro rata for part-time staff) 30% staff discount at our charity shops A generous and competitive pension scheme A supportive culture where staff feedback is highly valued and regular supervisions with line managers are conducted Great opportunities for career development and free monthly training sessions from experienced facilitators For all the fantastic and valuable work you’ll be doing, you’ll be eligible for the Blue Light Card which offers amazing discounts on thousands of brands Reflective Practice sessions from objective, external facilitators Our Ethos As an Equal Opportunities employer, we have an Equality and Diversity Action plan in place showing our commitment in ensuring continuous improvement in creating an inclusive culture. We also have a committed group of Inclusion & Diversity champions who meet monthly to ensure progress is being made. We invite applications from people from all backgrounds and cultures, especially minority groups that are underrepresented in the workplace. We also welcome applications from those with lived experience. We embrace flexibility and are proud to be a Disability Confident and Mindful employer, as well as an Armed Forces Covenant Supporter. If you have any special access requirements or other support needs throughout the application process (including interview), please contact us so that we can let you know how we can support you. We accept CVs and applications in all formats. DBS Checks We welcome applications from people with lived experience. All applicants working with our clients will be expected to undertake an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check. A criminal conviction will not necessarily prevent you from becoming an employee, the decision will depend on the type of offence and its relevance to the role. If you would like to discuss any convictions you may have, please contact the person named in the advert. All information will be dealt with according to our Data Protection Policy.

item.title: Mass Participation Event Manager
item.description: Job Title: Mass Participation Event Manager Location: Hybrid, minimum 1 day per week in our London Bridge office Contract: Permanent Working Pattern : Full-time role based on a 32-hour working week across four days Reporting to: Head of Fundraising (Community & Events) Salary: £35,000 – £37,000 per annum About Spinal Research Every two hours, someone in the UK becomes paralysed. Globally, more than 15 million people live with paralysis. At Spinal Research, our vision is a world where paralysis can be cured. We fund groundbreaking research to deliver life-changing treatments for people with spinal cord injuries. By backing the brightest minds and fostering innovation, we are driving progress towards what could be the medical breakthrough of the 21st century: curing paralysis. We will not stop until that future is achieved. The Role This is an exciting opportunity to join our Events team in a newly created management role, building on four years of significant growth and success across our mass participation programme. As Mass Participation Event Manager, you will play a key role in shaping the future direction of the programme while driving continued growth in income, participation and supporter engagement. You will have responsibility for the development, performance and delivery of the mass participation portfolio, working closely with the Head of Fundraising (Community & Events) to grow income, participation and engagement. Alongside this overall responsibility, you will have direct ownership of your own area of the portfolio, including the Great North Run, Berlin Marathon, Chicago Marathon, Cape Town Marathon and our wider challenges programme. You will manage these events from recruitment and participant onboarding through to fundraising, event-day delivery and post-event stewardship, while supporting the Head of Fundraising (C&E) with our flagship London Marathon. You will also line manage the Events Junior Officer, who will have direct responsibility for their own allocated events. You will provide leadership, direction and support to ensure their events are delivered successfully and contribute to the wider mass participation goals. This is a senior, hands-on role. You will be expected to lead the development of the overall programme while remaining directly involved in the day-to-day delivery of your own events. This includes recruiting and stewarding participants, developing campaigns, managing budgets and suppliers, speaking directly with supporters and being hands-on at events. Key Responsibilities · Strategy & Growth: Grow the mass participation portfolio, increasing income, participation and engagement through insight-led planning. · Supporter Recruitment & Stewardship: Lead recruitment campaigns and deliver excellent supporter journeys from sign-up to post-event stewardship. · Event & Portfolio Management: Manage allocated events end to end, including budgets, logistics, suppliers, event-day delivery and major event support. · Team Management: Line manage the Events Junior Officer, providing direction, support and oversight across their events. · Systems, Insights & Reporting: Use CRM and performance data to monitor KPIs, report on progress and inform future activity. · Collaboration: Work across the Community & Events team and wider organisation to deliver a strong, aligned mass participation programme. About you · Proven experience growing mass participation fundraising, with a track record of increasing income, participation and supporter engagement. · A track record of increasing income, participation and supporter engagement. · Experience leading recruitment campaigns and managing supporter journeys. · Confident managing event budgets, suppliers, CRM systems and performance data. · A strong communicator who builds great relationships with supporters, colleagues and partners. · Highly organised, proactive and able to manage multiple priorities. · Experience leading, supporting or developing others. · Comfortable balancing strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. Why Join Us? Full-time role based on a 32-hour working week across four days, with Fridays as a non-working day. 8% pension contribution. Flexible, hybrid working environment split between home and our London Bridge office. Opportunity to play a key role in a growing fundraising programme. Join a supportive, values-driven team built around commitment, integrity, collaboration and innovation. Occasional evening or weekend working may be required to meet organisational needs, with time off in lieu provided. Ready to help us deliver life-changing impact? Apply now to join Spinal Research and play a key role in our mission to cure paralysis. Spinal Research is a Disability Confident Committed employer and welcomes applications from all candidates. We are committed to making our recruitment process inclusive and accessible and will provide reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process where required.

item.title: Head of Philanthropy
item.description: Prospectus is delighted to be supporting a national countryside conservation charity in the search for a new Head of Philanthropy at this crucial time during their centenary year, ahead of the launch of a new 10-year strategy in December. The charity is a campaigning organisation that believes in having accessible countryside and green spaces for all. They supports the protection and regeneration of countryside spaces rich in nature and believe this plays a crucial role in responding to the climate emergency. With a local office in every county in England, they are passionate about working with communities and creating better places for everyone to enjoy. This role is offered on a permanent full-time contract basis paying a salary of circa £61,000 per annum to work in a hybrid and flexible working model from their London Office. The post holder will proactively lead and implement strategies for maximising funding through significant support from trusts & foundations, statutory & institutional funders, high net worth individuals and corporate partners. They will develop and steward key relationships and identify new funding and partnership opportunities that support the charity's campaigning priorities. The post holder will provide strategic direction and hands-on support to a team of two officers, fostering a collaborative, ambitious and effective approach to income generation. They are looking for a candidate with demonstrable experience of identifying, securing and developing relationships with potential for significant funding particularly through partnerships, along with trusts, foundations and high net worth individuals. They are looking for someone with demonstrable experience of securing 5 and 6 figure philanthropic and trust & foundation funding and meeting targets. The ideal candidate will have demonstrable experience of creating sponsorship, engagement and cultivation opportunities to secure long-term funding. At Prospectus we invest in your journey as a candidate and are committed to supporting you with your application. We welcome all candidates to apply, regardless of age, sex/gender, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, marital status or pregnancy/maternity. If you have any disability and require reasonable adjustment/s to any part of the process, then please contact Firas El Dib at Prospectus. If you feel you meet some of the criteria but not all, we really hope you'll enquire and learn more. Prospectus can advise and support on each part of the role and hopefully your application, so we look forward to hearing from you. In order to apply please submit your CV in the first instance. Should your experience be suitable, we will arrange for a meeting to brief you on the role. You'll then have all the information you need to formally apply. We are looking forward to connecting with you soon.

item.title: Children’s Domestic Violence Advocate
item.description: Children’s Domestic Violence Advocate (CHIDVA) Women only occupational requirement : This role is restricted to women under Schedule 9 (Part 1) of the Equality Act 2010. The nature of the work involves providing support to women who have experienced domestic abuse, and Safenet considers it a genuine occupational requirement that the post-holder is a woman. About Safenet Safenet delivers domestic abuse services across the North West of England, including refuges for women and children, safe houses for men, and community-based support. We provide trauma-informed, survivor-led services and work with partners to help people stay safe and rebuild their lives. About the role We are looking for a compassionate, skilled and trauma-informed practitioner who can provide high-quality support to children and young people affected by domestic abuse. The successful candidate will have strong safeguarding knowledge, experience of working with children, young people and families, and the confidence to manage risk, complete assessments and work effectively with partner agencies. They will be child-centred, inclusive and reflective in their practice, with the ability to build trust, advocate for children’s voices and support safe, positive outcomes for children, young people and non-abusive parents/carers. As a Children’s Domestic Violence Advocate (CHIDVA), you will safeguard and support children and young people affected by domestic abuse across the Continuum of Need, including Child Protection. You will deliver child-centred 1:1 and group interventions, complete child-focused risk assessments and safety plans, and ensure children and young people’s voices shape the support they receive. Working with partner agencies (including through MARAC), you will contribute to coordinated responses that improve safety, wellbeing and long-term resilience. Key responsibilities Provide emotional and practical support through 1:1 sessions and groupwork using trauma-informed approaches. Complete child-focused risk assessments (including SafeLives DASH RIC) and contribute to dynamic safety planning. Represent children and young people’s needs in MARAC and other multi-agency forums, ensuring their voice informs decisions. Work with social care, education, health and criminal justice partners to coordinate support and reduce barriers to access. Help children and young people understand the impact of abuse, build resilience and develop age-appropriate healthy relationships. Work with non-abusive parents/carers to strengthen safe relationships, attachment and recovery. Identify and act on safeguarding concerns, including self-harm or suicidal ideation, and refer via appropriate pathways. Maintain accurate, confidential case records and monitoring information in line with organisational and funder requirements. Model inclusive, culturally sensitive, anti-discriminatory and anti-racist practice in all work. What we’re looking for Essential SafeLives CHIDVA qualification (or working towards) and/or a relevant children and young people qualification (or working towards). Experience supporting children and young people affected by domestic abuse, trauma or adversity. Experience managing a caseload and delivering consistent, high-quality support to children, young people and families. Experience working in multi-agency settings (e.g., social care, education, health, criminal justice). Strong safeguarding knowledge (including Children Acts 1989/2004 and Domestic Abuse Act 2021) and confidence escalating concerns. Ability to build trust and communicate effectively with children/young people and professionals, adapting to age and need. Strong record-keeping skills and a commitment to confidentiality and data protection. Commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion, including anti-racist and intersectional practice. Desirable Women’s Aid or Respect accredited training (e.g., DAPA) and/or Paladin Independent Stalking Advocacy Caseworker (ISAC). Level 4 Diploma in Domestic Abuse; DASH risk assessment; trauma-informed care training. Experience supporting children and young people with complex needs (including self-harm or suicidal ideation) and knowledge of referral pathways. Knowledge of culturally specific forms of abuse and barriers to access for ethnic minority and migrant survivors (e.g., HBV, FGM). We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of adults, children and young people. Appointment will be subject to appropriate safer recruitment checks. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are committed to inclusive, anti-discriminatory and anti-racist practice.

item.title: Financial Wellbeing Adviser (Seaview Partnership)
item.description: Location: St Leonards-on-Sea and outreach venues Closing: Friday 16th October, or earlier if a suitable candidate is found Join Citizens Advice 1066 to help people build a more secure future Citizens Advice 1066 is looking for a compassionate and motivated Financial Wellbeing Adviser to work in partnership with Seaview Project , supporting people who are experiencing homelessness, at risk of homelessness, or moving into settled accommodation. This is an opportunity to join two well-established local organisations working together to help some of the most vulnerable people in our community. By providing practical advice, support and advocacy, you'll help clients improve their financial wellbeing, maximise their income, manage debt and develop the skills needed to maintain independent living. About the role Working closely with Seaview staff, housing providers and partner agencies, you'll deliver specialist financial inclusion support using a person-centred and trauma-informed approach. You'll build trusted relationships with clients facing a range of challenges, including homelessness, poor mental health, substance misuse, social exclusion and financial hardship What you'll be doing ● Providing advice and casework on welfare benefits, debt, budgeting and financial capability. ● Supporting clients to maximise income through benefits, grants and other financial assistance. ● Helping people manage rent, household bills and debts to maintain stable housing. ● Carrying out holistic assessments and developing support plans. ● Working collaboratively with Seaview, housing providers and other local services. ● Advocating on behalf of clients and helping them access specialist support. ● Maintaining accurate records and contributing to high-quality service delivery. We're looking for someone who: ● Has knowledge of welfare benefits, debt and financial inclusion. ● Has experience supporting vulnerable adults through advice, support or casework. ● Understands the challenges associated with homelessness, poverty and social exclusion. ● Can build trust and engage effectively with people who may be reluctant to access support. ● Has strong communication, organisational and advocacy skills. ● Is committed to delivering person-centred, non-judgemental support. What we offer ● 31 days annual leave including bank holidays (rising with service). Pro rata for part-time. ● Employer pension contribution ● Employee wellbeing support ● TOIL scheme ● Training and development opportunities ● A supportive and inclusive workplace This role is subject to an Enhanced DBS check.
