item.title: Learning Manager
item.description: Salary: £39.326 Contract: Permanent, full time We also offer: 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) and a discretionary Christmas closure Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay policy Private GP Service Salary sacrifice schemes for gym, bicycles, annual leave buying, and nursery/childcare Free Premium Headspace membership Financial, life and leadership coaching Life Assurance policy of 3x annual salary Access to free online, in-person or telephone therapy Location: Head office (8-10 Grosvenor Gardens) and Grosvenor Square, with time at Camley St Natural Park, Woodberry Wetlands, Walthamstow Wetlands, Centre for Wildlife Gardening, Gunnersbury Triangle, and Sydenham Hill Wood Hours: 35 hours per week, typically 9:00am – 5:00pm. We welcome flexible working requests from day one. Role & Responsibilities As wildlife faces unprecedented challenges, inspiring the next generation to care for and champion the natural world has never been more important. We're looking for a passionate and experienced Learning Manager to lead and develop our thriving learning programmes, which currently engage over 10,000 school children and 12,000 family learning participants every year. This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of environmental education across London, building on our successful primary school offer while expanding opportunities for secondary-aged young people and ensuring our programmes are inclusive and accessible to all. Working as part of our ambitious Learning & Engagement team, you'll oversee learning delivery across multiple sites, manage a team of Learning Officers, and play a key role in developing innovative programmes that deepen people's connection with nature. You'll balance strategic leadership with hands-on delivery, helping ensure our learning programmes are high-quality, impactful and responsive to the needs of London's diverse communities. You'll be involved in: Leading the delivery and continuous development of our formal learning programmes for schools and families across the Trust. Expanding our offer for 11-16-year-olds, helping to address the "high school gap" through engaging nature connection activities, curriculum-linked programmes and green careers initiatives. Developing inclusive learning opportunities that meet the needs of children, young people and families from a wide range of backgrounds, including those with additional needs. Building strong relationships with schools, teachers and community partners to increase participation and maximise impact. Managing and supporting a team of Learning Officers, creating a positive culture of development, collaboration and high performance. Overseeing learning budgets, resources and programme planning to ensure effective and sustainable delivery. Monitoring, evaluating and reporting on programme outcomes, helping demonstrate the impact of our work and secure future investment. Representing London Wildlife Trust with funders, schools, local authorities, community organisations and other external partners. Our Ideal Learning Manager An experienced education professional with a passion for connecting people to nature. Experience designing, delivering and evaluating learning programmes for children, young people and/or families. Strong leadership skills with experience managing, motivating and developing staff An excellent communicator who can build positive relationships with schools, funders, community organisations and colleagues. Experience developing inclusive programmes that engage diverse audiences and remove barriers to participation. Organised and proactive, with the ability to manage multiple projects, priorities and budgets effectively. Comfortable balancing strategic thinking with practical, hands-on delivery when needed. Committed to London Wildlife Trust's mission, values and approach to equality, diversity and inclusion. (Please see the job description for the full list of responsibilities and person specification.) Does this sound like you? We’d love to hear from you! Closing date: Monday 21st September at 9am Our vision is a London alive with wildlife, with nature in everyone's neighbourhood. To achieve our goal of inspiring everyone to help restore London’s wildlife, we recognise that our team must better reflect and represent all of London’s diverse communities. We are also committed to ensuring that the safety and wellbeing of children, young people and adults at risk is at the heart of our engagement with people

item.title: Marketing and Communications Manager
item.description: Marketing and Communications Manager Up to £40,000 + benefits (including 25 days annual leave and pension) Leatherhead, Surrey About the role: We are looking to appoint an experienced Marketing and Communications Manager to lead and deliver marketing campaigns that will drive awareness of Rainbow Trust and support fundraising activity to strengthen our position as experts in children’s palliative care. This is a broad and exciting role which includes creating, developing and delivering the brand campaigns and communication strategies. Reporting to the Head of Marketing and Communications, you will take the lead on generating creative, engaging content and ideas for fundraising and brand awareness campaigns that drive increased targeted engagement to showcase our work, build on our organisational strategy and deliver our fundraising ambition. What we’re looking for: An experienced marketing and communications manager – you have a motivational engaging style, who can draw out information and ideas of others Lively and enthusiastic – you are outgoing, with a collaborative approach to achieving goals through knowledge-sharing and effective delegation. You are excellent at building rapport and developing good working relationships A multi-tasker with a sense of urgency for goal achievement – you work at a faster than average pace, delegating effectively with thorough follow-up, and are quick to learn An innovative, practical and creative problem-solver – you are a big picture thinker that responds quickly to varied activities and changing conditions. You will have experience in developing and delivering communication and media strategy Applications will be particularly welcome from those in the charity/not-for-profit sector with a marketing, PR and communications background. What we offer: We’re proud to be a Two-Star Best Companies Top 50 mid-sized organisation and a Top 10 Charity, and we’re committed to creating a great place to work. You will benefit from: · Pension scheme where we contribute 5% of your salary and you contribute at least 3%. · A life assurance scheme for all employees which provides a death in service benefit of three times’ basic pay. · Flexible working hours to balance home and working life. · 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays – rising to 26 days after 1 year, 27 days after 5 years and 30 days after 11 years, with an additional 5 days to use in your 10th or 20th year of service (pro rata for part time). · The option to buy/sell annual leave, as well as additional leave for your birthday, wedding/civil ceremony and an extra half day off for Christmas shopping. · Time off in Lieu. · Employee Assistance Programme with access to remote GP, counselling, physiotherapy, resources to support your mental health and financial wellbeing, as well as a 24/7 helpline via Help@Hand. · Family friendly policies, focused on employee wellbeing, and an active cross-organisational wellbeing group running a number of initiatives throughout the year. · Access to the Blue Light Card Scheme, and other rewards and discounts. · Bike to work, season ticket loan and payroll giving schemes. · A recommend a friend recruitment bonus scheme. · Robust training and development programmes to support your learning and growth. If you’d like to find out more about these benefits and working with us, please visit our why work with us page. More information about us and our recruitment process can be found in our Candidate Pack online. About us: Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity enables families who have a child with a life-threatening or terminal illness to make the most of time together, providing expert, practical and emotional support, where they need it for as long as it is needed. For families living with childhood illness, time is everything. Right now, there are too many families coping alone with no support, no time to think, no time to make memories and no time for each other. We believe that no family should go through this alone, so we are here to change that. How to apply: To apply please send your CV and Covering letter to us via the link. Closing date: - 02 October 2026 Your covering letter should highlight why your application should be considered above others and clearly state how your experience matches the essential criteria outlined in the Person Specification. Please disclose in your covering letter if you have used AI for any part of your job application. For a detailed job description visit our website Interviews will take place at our Head Office in Leatherhead. We will only contact those applicants who have been successful. If you require any adjustments during the interview process, please let us know. Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early. An enhanced DBS disclosure will be required for this post. Rainbow Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all employees to share this commitment. Rainbow Trust is an equal opportunities employer and we welcome applications from all backgrounds.

item.title: Mental Health Carers Peer Support and Development Worker
item.description: This peer support project is delivered in partnership with South West London and St George’s Mental Health NHS Trust to support Carers of people with mental health conditions. This project will work to support Carers through one-to-one support, outreach, training and peer support groups. About The Role: Using your lived experience of caring for someone with a mental health condition, and a strengths-based approach, you will support mental health Carers in their caring role. You will provide person centred one-to-one- support, information, signposting, and advocacy, develop, and facilitate peer support groups and deliver training and outreach sessions at different locations across the borough. Key Requirements of the role Include: Please see the job description and person specification for the full list of requirements and specifications. Our Charity: We are a busy, ambitious charity operating at the heart of the Wandsworth community since 1995, helping thousands of people across the borough in unpaid Caring roles. We give information and advice, organise respite, offer complementary therapies, deliver training, provide peer support, arrange fun events and much more. In short, we are the Carer's friend and advocate, often helping Carers through difficult times. Benefits of working for Wandsworth Carers’ Centre: If you're committed to working in the voluntary sector and want to be part of a diverse team that makes a real difference to people’s lives, this role is for you! Wandsworth Carers’ Centre is an inclusive employer, committed to the continued development of a diverse workforce.

item.title: Community Fundraiser
item.description: Since 1892, Birmingham Dogs Home has been rescuing, rehabilitating and rehoming dogs across the West Midlands. Each year, thousands of dogs receive the second chance they deserve because of the generosity of our supporters. As we prepare to celebrate our 135th anniversary, we're investing in our income generation team and are now looking for an experienced Community Fundraiser to help shape the next stage of its development. You will take the lead role in growing community fundraising across the West Midlands, building strong relationships with local groups, schools, clubs, small businesses and individuals. You will inspire people to fundraise in their own communities by developing new opportunities and will help to turn local support into sustainable income for Birmingham Dogs Home. Working closely with the Events & Community Fundraising Manager, you will develop our community fundraising programme, enhance our volunteer led supporter base and play a key role in developing one of our charity's key income streams. About You We're looking for someone with previous community fundraising experience, or relevant experience in a similar relationship-building or business development role. You will be confident in developing new relationships, identifying opportunities and turning ideas into successful fundraising activity. You will be organised, self-motivated and comfortable managing a varied workload across a wide geographical area. You will enjoy building lasting relationships with supporters and local organisations, providing the encouragement and practical support they need to raise funds successfully. You will understand what makes a positive supporter experience and know how thoughtful stewardship can turn a one-off donation into long-term support. Above all, you will be a confident ambassador for Birmingham Dogs Home, with the ability to inspire others to support dogs in need across our region. In return, we offer: Two weeks' free dog boarding 25% discount on veterinary treatment Free on-site parking Life assurance BHSF Health Plan Employee Assistance Programme Pension contribution Ongoing CPD and development opportunities If you're looking for a role where you can make a genuine difference, we'd love to hear from you.

item.title: Interim Public Affairs and Media Manager
item.description: This is a fantastic opportunity to lead a team working for democracy, peace and climate justice. We’re looking for someone to manage our Advocacy and Media team for a year. The team covers public affairs, media, social media, and relationships with other churches and faiths. We need someone with the relevant skills and experience, who can also learn fast and start leading the team’s work quickly. You will have a background in policy, public affairs and/or campaigning work, and experience of line-management. You will need excellent interpersonal, communication and organisation skills. We have our own advocacy projects on democracy and human rights in Westminster and Holyrood, as well as working in coalition with other organisations on issues such as climate justice and peace. You will have the opportunity to work within a friendly and collaborative team for an organisation striving for peace, truth, equality and sustainability. Contract: Fixed term for 13 months, maternity leave cover. Hours: Full-time, 35 hours per week. Location: Based at our offices in London (NW1) or at home nationally, but must be within 2 hours’ travel of London and willing to travel regularly and sometimes at short notice. Office-based staff can work at home some of the time by agreement. For details of how to apply, please visit our website. Closing date: 8.00am on Monday, 5 October 2026. Interviews: Wednesday, 21 October 2026 (Friends House, London). Quakers are committed to equality and welcome applicants from all identities and backgrounds. Selection is based solely on skills, experience, qualifications, and abilities. We aim to prevent age, belief, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender reassignment, marital status, nationality, neurodivergence, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation or social class from being a barrier to employment. We aim for an equitable, user-friendly application process, and reasonable adjustments can be made if needed. As a Quaker organisation we expect all applicants and employees to uphold our values. We are committed to safeguarding children, young people and vulnerable adults. All candidates will undergo pre-employment checks in line with our Safer Recruitment guidelines.

item.title: Community & Individual Giving Fundraiser
item.description: Community & Individual Giving Fundraiser Bethlehem Care & Hospice Trust Salary: £34,000-£40,000 FTE, pro rata depending on experience | Hours: 14.8-22.2 hours per week (0.4-0.6 FTE) | Location: Home-based; applicants must be based in Yorkshire | Contract: 12 months initially, with a view to extension subject to funding and performance Build the community of supporters who will sustain Palestine's first and only licensed palliative care service Bethlehem Care & Hospice Trust (BCHT) is a small UK charity supporting the development of specialist palliative and hospice care in Palestine. In August 2023, the service we support became the first licensed palliative care service in Palestine. Since then, its specialist nurses have cared for more than 350 patients and their families and delivered more than 5,000 home visits. We now need to build the community of supporters who will help secure that service for the future. We are investing in professional fundraising for the first time and are looking for an enthusiastic, relationship-focused Community & Individual Giving Fundraiser to help grow our supporter base, develop community fundraising and increase regular giving. The opportunity This is a new role with considerable freedom to shape how BCHT develops community and individual giving. Working closely with Trustees, patrons, volunteers and existing supporters, you will initially focus on Yorkshire and northern England, where BCHT already has networks on which to build. You will develop relationships with churches, schools, universities, Rotary clubs, community organisations, businesses and individual supporters; help people fundraise for BCHT; develop regular giving; and ensure that our supporters feel connected to the extraordinary work they make possible. You will also help us develop a more systematic approach to supporter communications, digital fundraising, stewardship and volunteer engagement. This role could be for you if you have experience of community fundraising, individual giving, supporter engagement, marketing or relationship management; are an excellent communicator and natural relationship-builder; enjoy meeting people and are confident speaking to groups; can develop ideas and turn them into practical fundraising activity; can work independently; and want the opportunity to build something rather than simply inherit an established fundraising programme. Experience of community or individual fundraising, regular giving, working with volunteers, CRM systems, or church, school or faith-community fundraising would be particularly valuable. You will need to be based in Yorkshire and able and willing to travel regularly throughout the region. BCHT is inspired by Christian values of compassion, dignity and service. Applicants should be sympathetic to the values and mission of the charity. The palliative care service we support is provided to people regardless of faith, ethnicity, background or ability to pay. What we offer: flexible home-based working; 25 days' annual leave plus UK public/bank holidays, pro rata; and a workplace pension scheme with a 5% employer contribution, subject to scheme rules. You will have considerable scope to shape BCHT's community fundraising programme from the outset and direct access to Trustees and supporters. To apply, please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than two pages explaining why you are interested in the role and how your experience meets its requirements. Please download the Recruitment Pack for further information. Closing date: Friday 25 September 2026 | Interviews: Week commencing 5 October 2026 | Start: As soon as possible by agreement

item.title: Community Organiser
item.description: Sheffield Cathedral is inviting applications for the role of Community Organiser, a new post within the Cathedral Resourcing Project, at an exciting moment in the Cathedral’s mission, civic life and partnership with communities across Sheffield. At the heart of a changing and creative city, Sheffield Cathedral is both an ancient holy place and a living centre of worship, welcome, culture and public engagement. We are seeking to grow as a civic, relational and faith-rooted institution: not acting for communities from a distance, but acting with communities through trust, shared leadership and common action. This new role is for a relational, disciplined and justice-minded organiser who can listen deeply, build trust across difference, identify and develop local leaders, and help people move from shared concern to collective action. Working in the Citizens UK tradition of broad-based community organising, the Community Organiser will help embed organising across the Cathedral, its parish partnerships and its civic relationships, contributing to the co-creation of Sheffield Citizens Alliance. We are looking for someone who understands that lasting change is built through relationships, local leadership, patient listening, strategic action and negotiated public wins. The successful candidate will work confidently within the life and values of Sheffield Cathedral, while helping churches, communities and civic institutions build the power to act together for justice and the common good. This post is open to people of all faiths and of none. There is no requirement to be a practising Christian, but the postholder will need to work sympathetically within the public mission and inclusive Christian values of Sheffield Cathedral. Salary: £36,000 p.a. plus pension Contract & Working Pattern 37.5 hours per week, with some evening and weekend work Fixed-term until 31 December 2028, starting as soon as possible Working at Sheffield Cathedral, partner parishes and civic institutions across Sheffield, with some hybrid working possible by agreement Final application closing date: Wednesday 7 October 2026, 2.00pm Shortlisting: Thursday 8 October 2026 Interviews/Tasks: Thursday 15 October 2026 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We reserve the right to close this vacancy before the advertised closing date if a sufficient number of suitable applications are received. We therefore encourage interested applicants to apply as early as possible. For more information, or to download an application form, please visit the vacancy page on Sheffield Cathedral's website.

item.title: Recovery Officer at Yeldall Manor
item.description: At Yeldall Manor , we have been helping men overcome drug and alcohol addiction for over 50 years through our residential rehabilitation programme and Christian recovery community. We believe that lasting recovery is possible and are committed to supporting individuals to rebuild their lives, restore relationships and discover renewed hope and purpose. We are looking for a committed Christian to join our Recovery Coordination Team as a Recovery Officer . This is a rewarding and varied role at the heart of our recovery programme, providing practical, emotional and spiritual support to men seeking freedom from addiction. As a Recovery Officer, you will act as a keyworker for residents, helping them navigate their recovery journey, achieve personal goals and overcome challenges along the way. You will work closely with residents, colleagues, families, commissioners and external agencies to coordinate support and ensure each individual receives the care they need to thrive. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about recovery, enjoys building meaningful relationships and wants to make a genuine difference in people's lives every day. Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays, rising to 30 days after 3 years' service. Company pension. Employee Assistance Programme (EAP). Death in service benefit. Meals provided whilst on site. Ongoing training and development opportunities. Supportive supervision and appraisal process. What will you do? Act as a keyworker, providing personalised support to assigned residents. Develop, monitor and review care plans and risk assessments. Support residents in achieving programme goals and progressing through the stages of recovery. Conduct resident inductions and provide ongoing guidance and encouragement. Coordinate move-on planning and support residents to prepare for independent living. Liaise with families, support networks and partner agencies. Work closely with healthcare professionals, probation services, local authorities and other stakeholders. Monitor resident wellbeing, behaviour and engagement with the programme. Carry out drug and alcohol testing, room searches and other safeguarding responsibilities in line with policy. Dispense medication following training and competency assessment. Contribute to resident reviews, reports and multi-agency meetings. Support admissions by conducting assessments and interviews with prospective residents. Maintain accurate records and ensure compliance with data protection requirements. Participate in the Christian life of the organisation, including prayer meetings, fellowship gatherings and celebrations. What are we looking for? Experience working with vulnerable adults, addiction recovery, rehabilitation, social care, housing or related services. Understanding of the challenges faced by people recovering from addiction. Strong organisational, administration and record-keeping skills. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Ability to build positive, professional relationships with residents and external agencies. Experience of care planning, risk assessment or keyworking is desirable. Ability to work both independently and as part of a team. Good boundaries, conflict management and problem-solving skills. Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and case management systems. Full UK driving licence. Demonstrated commitment to the Christian faith, ability to encourage others in their faith and able to support the Yeldall Basis of Faith, Ethos Statement and values. About You You will be someone who genuinely enjoys helping people grow, overcome challenges and achieve lasting change. You will be compassionate and resilient, able to support residents through difficult situations while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries. You will be organised, adaptable and comfortable working in a dynamic residential environment where no two days are the same. Most importantly, you will be passionate about seeing lives transformed and committed to supporting men as they rebuild their lives free from addiction. We welcome applications from people in recovery who can demonstrate appropriate stability and readiness for the responsibilities of the role. As a Christian charity, we bring our faith to the work we do and the men we work with, so you will be someone with a deep-rooted Christian faith, able to inspire others in their faith journeys, seeking the guidance of the Holy Spirit in all key decisions. Our Christian Ethos Yeldall Manor is a Christian faith-based charity and recovery community. We welcome applications from people who are committed to our Christian ethos and values and who are willing to actively contribute to the Christian life of the organisation. Safeguarding Yeldall Manor is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable adults. The successful applicant will be required to undergo an Enhanced DBS check including a check against the Adults' Barred List due to the nature of the role. About Yeldall Manor For over five decades, Yeldall Manor has supported men seeking freedom from addiction through a structured residential rehabilitation programme, therapeutic support, work-based activities and Christian community life. We are passionate about seeing lives transformed and are looking for people who share our commitment to recovery, compassion and hope. This is more than a job. It's an opportunity to walk alongside people at one of the most important moments of their lives and help them discover a future filled with hope, purpose and lasting recovery.
item.dc:creator: Yeldall Manor, Reading

item.title: Recovery in Community Worker (Referrals and Assessments)
item.description: Role Context Recovery in Community is a successful partnership between Manchester Mind and Gaddum. We support people to manage and live with their mental health in their community. Staff are employed by both organisations but work together collaboratively and as a team. As the Recovery in Community Worker (Referral and Assessment) you will be supporting people in who have been referred into Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) services but may not meet the threshold for secondary or specialist mental health services. The aim of this work is to ensure that people referred receive the right support at the right time. You will work closely with the Referral and Assessment team at Greater Manchester Mental Health Trust (GMMH) to take referrals and ensure people get access to the mental health and social support they need. Role Purpose You will be building trusting and kind relationships with the understanding that they enable people to be listened to and heard and that this makes a difference. You will be part of a team providing effective person-centred support to people who come through the referral and assessment hub – many of whom often have tried many times to get the help they need. We want to enable people to feel connected within their communities – to services, friends and family. You will also be building relationships with NHS and statutory services. The structure of the service is brief intervention (working with people for a short period of time) with a focus on supporting people to connect to community services and resources effectively. You will be well supported in this role. The service takes a team-based approach, and you will be joining a team of five and you will be supported directly by a Team Coordinator as well as being part of the wider Recovery in Community Service. We share skills, experience and learning across the teams so that everyone benefits and we can make a meaningful difference. Main Duties and Responsibilities · Take referrals from the GMMH (Greater Manchester Mental Health) Referral and Assessment Hub and build trusting relationships with people so that they receive the support they need to recover and stay well. · Build relationships with other key professionals to ensure individuals achieve their goals (e.g. GPs, social care, community services etc). · Support the development of a supportive and productive referral route into and out of the service, managing exit from the service safely. · Support the development of this new service, responding professionally to changes as we improve and evolve our working practice collaboratively. · Provide a trauma-informed service to people: listening, offering safety, choice and empowerment to the people you support so they can effectively engage with services and make sustainable links in with their communities. · Identify and deliver appropriate interventions. · Identify when people need referrals to secondary services or specialist mental health services and make appropriate referrals. · Independently travel to visit people in a range of settings across in Manchester and across Greater Manchester, adhering to lone working and risk management procedures. · To integrate effectively with colleagues at Manchester Mind, taking a “one team approach” to deliver a seamless service, understanding the different roles in the Recovery in Community team and recognising each other's strengths. · Maintain accurate and up-to-date case notes and records using agreed case management systems, following standard operating procedures. · Support people to engage in our service through coproduction, engagement events and feedback forms. · Contribute to service reporting, monitoring and evaluation as required. · Identify additional needs that people have and highlight them to Manchester Mind with a view to sharing them with Greater Manchester Mental Health Trust and commissioners. All staff are expected to work within all Gaddum policies and procedures. This role is subject to an enhanced DBS check.
item.dc:creator: Gaddum

item.title: Grants Lead
item.description: To successfully lead the Grants team and raise voluntary income from a range of Grantmakers including Trusts, Foundations and local Government grant funders contributing to an overall team target of £1-million +. Working effectively with a grants team of three, and across the organisation, you will meet team annual targets of circa £675,000 through finding new opportunities, building excellent relationships with funders and managing the team effectively. This will lead to more young people reached by Eikon’s services. Responsibilities Income generation · Lead responsibility for raising current annual team target of £675,000 for restricted and unrestricted income · Work to agreed metrices including an annual target of £220,000 - £250,000/year with a pipeline including statutory, national & regional grant funders (some being invite only). · Develop and lead networking plan (internal/external) to secure long-term grant and statutory funding opportunities to help increase financial income year on year. Account Management · Lead a stewardship framework, ensuring excellent account management of funders across the team (including own portfolio) · Lead plans for the year, thinking creatively to develop new engagement opportunities such as panels, breakfast meetings and other events · Collaborate with other leads and managers in the team to maximise opportunities through relationships, for example Major Donors, Corporate partnerships and Individual Givers. Management · Line management two staff members (Senior Grants Fundraiser and Trust Fundraiser), creating a positive and supportive working culture supporting them to meet their targets · Lead on managing pipeline information on Donorfy, being able to pull reports for information and analysis including: o Provision of data and narrative for monthly team meetings o Contribution to Board reporting with narrative and pipeline information o Analysis for annual planning sessions Quality and standards · Ensure all staff and volunteers understand and deliver within Eikon’s safeguarding policies and practices when taking part in fundraising activities. · Ensure all activities follow the relevant Fundraising Codes of Practice and Eikon’s Ethical Fundraising Policy. · Prepare relevant Grant Agreements and contractual information. · Carry out risk assessments for all activities for which you are responsible. · Carry out required basic due diligence on new funders. Finance and resources · Budget responsibility with authorisation up to agreed limits · Operate within organisational approved budgets, policies and procedures. Communications and relationships · Work collaboratively with the Communications Lead to devise annual communications and marketing plans, ensuring Eikon is strategically positioned externally. · Work collaboratively with service leads ensure new services developed meet funder needs and requirements Strategy/transformation work · Lead on developing and delivering annual grants plan · Participating in a Leads network, contribute regularly to organisation matters including strategies, annual plans and budgeting. Organisational requirements · Work within Eikon’s equal opportunities, health & safety, and safeguarding policies at all times · Understand and act when safeguarding issues need to be escalated · · This is hybrid role. You must be available to attend regular external meetings across Surrey and occasional meetings at Eikon’s New Haw office. Some meetings may take place outside normal working hours or at weekends. · Work co-operatively and under the management of The Eikon Charity staff to ensure the highest quality of delivery and support · Work within Eikon’s internal policies, safeguarding and data protection regulations · Be responsible for equipment/resources · To promote, monitor and maintain health, safety and security in the working environment

item.title: Head of Policy and Communications
item.description: Head of Policy and Communications When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Head of Policy and Communications Location England £58,212 per annum (pro rata for part time) Ref: 114REC Part Time - 21 hours per week – we are happy to talk flexible working Base: Home based/hybrid, in or commutable to London Contract: Maternity Cover Disclosure: Basic/Enhanced/ DBS is not required for this position as the post holder will not be working with school and community groups in the region. ABOUT THE ROLE Team: Strategy and Engagement/ Policy and Communications As the Head of Policy and Communications you will lead our policy, communications and influencing work in England, helping to increase support for walking, wheeling and cycling. As a key member of the Policy and Communications leadership team, you will raise the profile of Walk Wheel Cycle Trust, strengthen engagement with supporters and influence decision-makers to create positive change. Working closely with senior leaders, you will shape political strategy, develop clear and compelling messages, and build strong relationships with policymakers, partners and stakeholders. You will use evidence, insight and collaboration to influence national policy and help deliver our UK-wide goals. This is an exciting opportunity to drive real change by championing healthier, greener and more accessible journeys for everyone. What You’ll Be Doing This role is ideal for someone who enjoys leading both communications and public affairs for a cause, working with others internally and externally to achieve positive change. ABOUT YOU We’re looking for someone who has experience and understanding in the areas listed below. You don’t need to meet every requirement — if you feel you’d be a good fit, we encourage you to apply. LIVING OUR VALUES At the Walk Wheel Cycle Trust, we’re a values‑driven organisation. We’re looking for people who are: Always Learning – curious, open‑minded and committed to continuous improvement. Championing Equity – inclusive, respectful and focused on ensuring everyone has a voice and fair opportunity to succeed. Taking Ownership – proactive, responsible and empowered to make things better. Delivering Together – collaborative, transparent and motivated by shared success. Through our values we make it possible for more people to walk, wheel and cycle safely, healthily and joyfully. WHAT WE OFFER We want you to feel supported, valued, and empowered in your role. That’s why we offer flexible working, a positive team environment, and benefits designed to support your wellbeing, finances, and family life. WellbeingSupport FinancialBenefits Family FriendlyPolicies ADDITIONAL INFORMATION We actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, particularly those underrepresented in our workforce, including people of colour and candidates with disabilities. Adjustments are available throughout the recruitment process.
item.dc:creator: Walk Wheel Cycle Trust

item.title: Activity Centre Manager
item.description: You’ll be at the helm of a busy, welcoming centre that brings residential stays, day visits, camping and outdoor activities to guiding groups, schools, youth groups, corporate teams, families and friends. That variety is part of what makes the role so rewarding. No two days look the same, and that’s exactly the point. This is a senior role with real scope and real responsibility. You’ll lead a team, set the tone for high standards across the site, manage the practical realities of running a working centre, and help shape its future direction in line with Girlguiding Anglia’s values and ambitions. You’ll have the chance to think strategically about where the centre goes next while staying hands on with the day to day running that keeps a place like Hautbois thriving. We’re after someone positive, proactive and organised, who leads with warmth as much as with structure. You’ll need to be comfortable holding multiple priorities at once, calm under pressure, and genuinely motivated by creating great experiences for the people who come through the centre’s doors. If you enjoy variety, thrive on responsibility and want your work to have a visible, lasting impact, this role offers all of that in abundance. The role is based at Hautbois, right in the Norfolk countryside. Flexible working may be possible where it suits the business, though some evenings and weekends will be part of the job given the nature of a residential site. The centre isn’t easily reached by public transport, so a car and full driving licence are essential for commuting and the occasional meeting further afield. In return, you’ll get free parking, office drinks and snacks, a holiday allowance that grows with your length of service, and modern IT and working facilities to support you in the role. This role might also suit candidates with backgrounds as an activities manager, camp manager, adventure manager, outdoor learning manager or residential centre manager.
item.dc:creator: Girlguiding Anglia, Norwich

item.title: Data, Risk and Compliance Officer
item.description: Who we are: Muslim Aid is a UK faith-based international development organisation that provides support to communities around the world affected by disasters, conflict, or endemic poverty without regard to their social, religious, or ethnic background. Established in 1985, Muslim Aid has facilitated the engagement of the British Muslim and non-Muslim community in support of its work in a variety of ways. Over the years, its humanitarian work has included responses to major crises around the world including, famine in East Africa, earthquakes and flooding in Pakistan and Bangladesh as well as conflicts in Syria and Yemen. We place strong emphasis on long-term development projects that build the capacity of local people to help themselves. In addition to the 5 country offices worldwide we also work with multiple partner offices focusing on sustainable Development Programmes and providing humanitarian relief during times of crisis. Summary of the role: The Data, Risk and Compliance Officer will manage Muslim Aid’s organisational approach to data protection, risk management, compliance and assurance coordination. The role will provide oversight of key registers, trackers, records, reports and action plans, including the corporate risk register, compliance obligations register, policy review schedule, data protection records, information-rights requests, breach records, audit action trackers and assurance follow-up. The postholder will work directly with the COO, leadership team and functional owners across the organisation to strengthen governance, ensure risks and compliance actions are actively managed, support timely escalation and drive continuous improvement in organisational controls and accountability. The postholder will own coordination, tracking, records, follow-up and administrative support for these areas, while supporting senior colleagues with design, judgement, quality assurance and insight. About the Role: Maintain the corporate risk register and ensure risks, controls, actions, owners and deadlines are kept up to date. Gather regular updates from functional owners and support teams to describe risks clearly and consistently. Maintain the compliance obligations register, policy review schedule and evidence of compliance activity. Work with departments to record legal, regulatory, donor, funding agreement, data protection and internal policy requirements. Maintain data protection policies, procedures, templates, records of processing activities, data flows and information asset records. Prepare regular reports, exception reports, committee updates, action summaries and briefing notes on risk, compliance, data protection, audit actions and overdue matters. About You: You must currently hold the right to work in the UK. Muslim Aid is not offering sponsorship for this role. This role operates on a hybrid working basis, with a requirement to work from the office for a minimum of two/three days per week, and additional days where required to meet organisational needs. TWOTo be successful in this role, you will need: Law degree, equivalent legal qualification or equivalent experience in legal, compliance or regulatory matters. Significant experience in data protection, risk, compliance, governance, assurance or a related area, including responsibility for improving organisational processes and controls. Experience managing risk registers, compliance trackers, policy schedules, action logs and organisational records, with responsibility for quality, timeliness and escalation. Strong organisational and management skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands, oversee several trackers, manage deadlines and deliver high-quality reports. Ability to influence and follow up actions firmly and professionally, make sound judgements, identify issues requiring escalation and handle sensitive information with discretion. Ability to write clear reports, updates, guidance, action summaries and recommendations for managers, leadership team, committees and the Board. Why you should apply: Join Muslim Aid as our Data, Risk & Compliance Officer and play a key role in strengthening our approach to data protection, risk management, compliance and organisational assurance. Working closely with the COO, Leadership Team and colleagues across the organisation, you’ll help ensure key risks, compliance obligations and data protection responsibilities are effectively monitored, managed and addressed. You’ll oversee essential registers, records and action plans, support audit and assurance activity, and help strengthen organisational controls and accountability. If you’re passionate about good governance, effective risk management and using robust processes to drive continuous improvement, we would love to hear from you. Benefits you will enjoy working for us: 25 days annual leave + 4 Privilege days Hybrid working – minimum of 2/3 days per week in the office Paid time off for medical appointments 2 hours lunch break on Fridays Time off in Lieu (TOIL) Pension Scheme How to apply: To apply please submit your cover letter (no more than 1 page) and CV. Pre-employment Checks: Due to the nature of our work with children & vulnerable communities, Muslim Aid operates rigorous safeguarding and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) procedures in our recruitment process. We are committed to the prevention of sexual abuse, exploitation and adopt a zero-tolerance approach to SEA, as a result, any employment with Muslim Aid is subject to the following checks prior to your start date: Satisfactory professional references, including safeguarding specific-enquiries. A Basic level Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and/or an International Criminal Record Check where applicable. Right to work documentation review in the country this role is located. We will do everything possible to ensure that only those who are suitable to work with children and vulnerable people are recruited to work for us. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all suitably qualified persons regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/belief, or age. Only Shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Applications will be accepted until closing date, however, Muslim Aid reserves the right to initiate interviews and the selection process on a rolling basis with the aim of identifying an appropriate candidate as quickly as possible.
item.dc:creator: Muslim Aid

item.title: Volunteer Coordinator
item.description: We're looking for a Volunteer Coordinator who's good with people and good at organising them - someone who can recruit, train and keep in touch with the volunteers who make FFLAG's support possible. Are you someone who enjoys building relationships and helping people do their best work? This role is about making sure FFLAG's volunteers - most of them parents of LGBT+ children themselves - feel properly recruited, trained and supported. About FFLAG FFLAG is a national voluntary organisation and registered charity and is the UK's longest established parent support charity in the LGBT+ sector. Our history began in the grassroots parent helplines of the 1960s, grew through the 1980's and 90's as we supported anxious parents and fought against the discrimination of Section 28, becoming a formally registered charity in 2000. Our work sounds simple, but it is life changing. We help parents and families understand, accept and support their lesbian, gay, bisexual, non-binary and transgender family members with love and pride. We offer a range of support options spanning 1-2-1 online and helpline support services to a UK-wide monthly group Zoom meeting and face to face local groups. We also have an extensive collection of online resources and guides. We attend as many Pride events as we can and our work supports thousands of people every year. This support is provided by an active base of FFLAG volunteers who are parents of LGBT+ children themselves, supported by other volunteers and allies. What this job is all about As Volunteer Coordinator, you'll make sure FFLAG's volunteers are properly recruited, trained and supported, so they can continue doing this work well. Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will: Identify what volunteers FFLAG needs, then recruit, induct and train them, including DBS checks and references Maintain training, the volunteer handbook and the Code of Conduct up to date Maintain regular contact with volunteers, so they stay engaged, safe and supported Act as FFLAG's Safeguarding Lead, providing regular supervision to support volunteers Keep accurate records, liaise with Trustees, and report on volunteer activity to the Board Be a member of the Services and Support Committee Provide support to the Operations Manager with events, as required What are the skills and attributes you will need? This role needs someone who's organised, approachable, and motivated by helping people do well - but it also needs real, hands-on experience of volunteer coordination from day one, since it's a small, part-time role with no one else to lean on for this work. We're specifically looking for candidates who can point to evidence of previous experience in: Recruiting, training and supporting volunteers in a paid or voluntary role Keeping volunteers engaged and retained over time Handling safeguarding matters sensitively and appropriately Working independently and comfortably in a remote-working setup A genuine interest in equality, diversity, and the LGBT+ community Please note: this role isn't suitable as a first step into volunteer management - we're looking for candidates who already have relevant, demonstrable experience in this area. Why join us? It's a chance to play a hands-on role at a charity with a long history of supporting parents and families, helping the volunteers who in turn support thousands of people every year. It's part-time, flexible and home-based, with 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays (both pro rata), and a pension in place. How to apply Click the CharityJob Apply button below. You'll be asked to submit a CV and answer a few screening questions about your experience. Closing date for applications is Friday 25th September.
item.dc:creator: FFLAG

item.title: Head of External Relations
item.description: Role: Head of External Relations Salary Band: £40,000 - £65,945 gross per annum Contract: Permanent Hours: Full Time Location: Woodstock, Oxfordshire. We value in-person collaboration and this role is primarily office based, with flexibility available where appropriate and regular travel across the UK. About Us Plunkett UK is a national charity supporting people in rural areas to set up and run successful community-owned businesses. These businesses, from shops and pubs to woodlands and farms, provide vital services, create local jobs, strengthen rural economies and bring people together. We've championed community ownership for over 100 years because it delivers thriving, inclusive and resilient places. About the Role We're looking for an ambitious and strategic Head of External Relations to lead delivery of Plunkett UK's Stronger Movement strategic priority, helping to grow our visibility, influence, membership and external relationships. This is a senior leadership role with a particular focus on strengthening our communications and marketing. You'll help ensure Plunkett's impact, expertise and role within the rural community business movement are better understood by community businesses, funders, policymakers, corporate partners and other key stakeholders. Working closely with the Chief Executive and leading a multidisciplinary team, you'll develop compelling communications, build our profile and ensure our voice is heard where it matters most. You'll also lead the development of our membership strategy, helping us strengthen and grow the rural community business movement, while providing strategic oversight of our policy, public affairs and research work. The role offers an exciting opportunity to shape how Plunkett is perceived externally, build influential relationships and contribute directly to the organisation's long-term sustainability and impact. The successful candidate should have the following skills and attributes: A strategic communicator – able to turn complex ideas into clear, persuasive and memorable messages. Marketing-minded – focused on audiences, positioning, reach and converting awareness into action. Creative and proactive – bringing ideas, energy and momentum rather than waiting for direction. A strong leader and coach – able to inspire colleagues, build confidence and create ownership. Collaborative – comfortable working across teams and through other managers to achieve shared goals. Commercially aware – able to connect external relations activity with membership growth, partnerships, fundraising and wider organisational sustainability. Politically astute – confident operating with senior stakeholders while maintaining Plunkett’s independence and apolitical stance. A relationship builder – able to develop trusted relationships with members, funders, policymakers, partners and suppliers. Accountable – committed to Plunkett’s principle of listening first and acting second, using evidence and insight to guide decisions. Closing date for applications: 9am on Monday 28 September Interview date: In person w/c 5 October Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We are committed to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) and our approach goes beyond ‘protected characteristics’ to thinking more broadly about inclusion. Every individual will think and feel differently and we believe that these differences should be embraced, and individual needs taken into account. Additionally, the makeup of the rural communities we work with leads to their own particular diversity and exclusion challenges and opportunities compared to urban areas. Our commitment to EDI, both internally and externally, has been tailored to Plunkett and the communities we serve. No agencies please. Registered Charity: 313743
item.dc:creator: Plunkett UK

item.title: Senior People Business Partner
item.description: Senior People Business Partner – 6 Month Maternity Cover We are seeking an experienced Senior People Business Partner to provide strategic HR leadership, expert advice and support across a complex organisation. Salary: £60,000 pro rata Contract: 6-month maternity cover Hours: Full time, 36 hours per week with flexible core working hours Location: London – hybrid working, with Wednesdays in the office Closing date: Applications and CVs will be reviewed on a rolling basis, with interviews taking place as suitable candidates are identified. About the role This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Senior People Business Partner to join a high-profile organisation and work closely with senior leaders across a varied and complex environment. You will provide a proactive, strategic people partnering service, supporting leaders and managers with organisational priorities while ensuring effective people management and a positive employee experience. Key responsibilities will include: Partnering senior leaders and managers on strategic and operational people matters Leading and supporting organisational development, change and restructuring programmes Managing complex and high-level employee relations cases, including dismissal and appeal Building constructive relationships with trade union representatives Coaching and challenging managers to strengthen leadership and people management capability Identifying workforce trends, risks and opportunities and providing pragmatic solutions Supporting workforce planning, talent management and succession planning Using people data and management information to inform decision-making Developing and reviewing people policies, procedures and working practices Line managing and supporting colleagues within the People team About you You will be an experienced HR/People professional with a strong track record of operating at Senior Business Partner level within a large or complex organisation. You will bring substantial generalist HR experience, including managing complex employee relations matters and advising senior stakeholders on sensitive people issues. Experience within a unionised environment is highly desirable , and candidates with experience of working within the public sector or a similarly complex, highly governed organisation would be particularly well suited. You will also have: CIPD Level 5 or equivalent relevant experience Strong knowledge of UK employment law and HR best practice Experience of organisational change, restructuring and people projects Excellent influencing, coaching and relationship-building skills The confidence to challenge constructively at senior level Strong analytical and organisational skills A collaborative, pragmatic and people-focused approach About the organisation You will be joining a nationally recognised organisation with a strong public purpose and commitment to creating an inclusive, welcoming and high-performing workplace. The organisation employs a diverse workforce and offers an interesting and complex People environment, making this an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys combining strategic business partnering with hands-on senior HR support. Other roles you may have experience of could include: Senior HR Business Partner, HR Business Partner, People Business Partner, Senior People Partner, HR Manager, Senior HR Manager, Employee Relations Manager, People and Culture Business Partner, Strategic HR Business Partner or HR Consultant.

item.title: Membership Services Director
item.description: Our mission at York SU is simple - we provide representation, opportunities and run services for all 22,000+ students at the University of York. Following an ambitious period of growth, we are now entering the next chapter for York SU. As our Membership Services Director you will join our Senior Leadership Team, shaping the Union’s student experience offer and leading strategic development, operational management and evaluation of the Union’s membership activities across three core teams: student voice and representation, communities and opportunities, fostering an empowering and high-performing culture. Reporting to the Co CEO (Membership Services and Charity Affairs), we are looking for a strategic leader that can balance a robust approach and day to day operational excellence with big-picture thinking; helping us navigate an increasingly complex regulatory landscape while keeping our members at the heart of everything we do. You will be expected to contribute to excellent operational delivery that is inclusive by design and creates an offer that is reflective of our student communities to grow engagement, impactful representation and satisfaction. You will serve as the senior point of escalation for high-risk operations, ensuring that student activity operates within safe, legal, and inclusive frameworks. And you will champion a data-driven approach, using research and insight to influence policy and practice, and demonstrate our impact. York SU is unashamedly ambitious, innovative, and value-led. We actively invest in our people and pride ourselves on a deeply collaborative and sector-leading working culture. If you’re excited by the opportunity to harness the voices of students, and want to contribute to a sustainable and enterprising Union that’s working hard to empower, support and challenge to ensure that student life at York is the best that it can be, now and in the future, then we would love to hear from you.
item.dc:creator: University of York Students Union (York SU), York

item.title: Head of Community Research & Impact
item.description: High Trees Community Development Trust is seeking an ambitious Head of Community Research & Impact to join our senior management team and lead one of our core service areas. Community-led research sits at the heart of how High Trees works. Our approach aims to rebalance the role and power that communities have in deciding how research is informed, delivered and used to improve lives for Lambeth residents. Over recent years we have built a strong foundation for this work and developed two flagship community research partnerships — the Lambeth Peer Action Collective and the Lambeth Community Research Network. We are now looking for someone to significantly expand this work: building local evidence of community need, working with communities to identify solutions and appropriate responses to local challenges, and advocating for change to policy and practice where needed. This is a broad and varied leadership role . Alongside our direct research programmes, you will lead the development of infrastructure around community-led research in Lambeth, so that voluntary and community sector (VCS) organisations can access the training, resources and networks they need to design and deliver their own research. You will also lead our Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning and Communications functions , ensuring the impact of everything we do is understood, evidenced and communicated well. As part of High Trees’ senior management team, the Head of Community Research & Impact will not only oversee delivery in their service area, but also help shape organisational strategy , grow partnerships and income, and ensure we work as one High Trees — keeping our practice responsive, collaborative and always led by community need. About High Trees Based in Tulse Hill, High Trees has been rooted in the local community for nearly 30 years. We deliver community action, employment, education, youth services and community research, working in partnership with local people and local organisations to build stronger communities and create meaningful change. We are recognised for our collaborative, long-term approach and our ability to adapt and respond to the issues that matter most to local people. About the role As Head of Community Research & Impact, you will: Lead and inspire our Research & Impact team to deliver high-quality, community-led research that drives change. Shape and deliver High Trees’ strategic vision for community-led research, championing collaborative research practice across Lambeth. Take the lead on designing new research programmes, support with sourcing the funding to run them, and ensuring projects are completed to a high standard with high-quality outputs. Grow the infrastructure for community-led research locally, including through the Lambeth Community Research Network and the Lambeth Peer Action Collective. Support VCS organisations with community research training, resources and capacity building support. Lead and embed Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) and Communications across High Trees and our partnership work. Contribute as a member of High Trees’ senior management team, ensuring a joined-up approach across all our services. About you We are looking for someone who brings: Significant professional experience in research and/or community settings, with a track record of leading research projects. Experience of qualitative and mixed methods research and a working knowledge of participatory research approaches. A proven track record of leading teams and managing multiple projects and programmes at once. The ability to build trust and long-lasting relationships across community, academic, public sector and voluntary sector organisations. A strategic mindset, balancing day-to-day delivery with long-term vision. A solid understanding of the context in which High Trees delivers its work Why join us? This is a rare opportunity to take a senior leadership role in a values-led organisation at a time of growth and ambition. You will help set the standard for community-led research and system change, creating tools, resources and practices that benefit the wider sector — and be part of a collaborative team dedicated to creating lasting change.
item.dc:creator: High Trees Community Development Trust

item.title: Fundraising & Income Generation Manager
item.description: Job Title: Fundraising & Income Generation Manager Reporting to: Head of Trent Bridge Community Trust Contract type: Fulltime 35 hours/week Salary: £35,000 - £40,000 per annum plus bonus Start date: 1st November 2026 Trent Bridge Community Trust is the charitable arm of Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club. Since 2008, we’ve used the power of cricket to connect communities, improve wellbeing, and create life-changing opportunities across Nottinghamshire. Following our transition to charitable status, we are entering an exciting phase of growth and ambition. Our new Fundraising Strategy (2027–2030) sets a bold target to diversify income, increase sustainability, and expand our impact—especially for disadvantaged communities. To help us achieve this, we are now looking for a Fundraising & Income Generation Manager to lead our income growth. This is a new and pivotal role within the Trust, responsible for delivering an ambitious fundraising strategy to secure over £545,000 across three years, contributing to a wider £800,000 long term income vision. You will lead on building diverse and sustainable income streams, helping us: Expand community and cricket programmes across the county Increase participation, especially among underrepresented groups Sustain vital health and wellbeing projects Strengthen our long-term financial resilience If you have a proven track record in fundraising and income generation, have experience across multiple streams (grants, corporate, events or individual giving), skilled in developing pipelines and achieving financial targets, this is the challenge you are looking for! If you are committed to making a difference in communities, are motivated by impact, inclusion and opportunity and excited about the power of sport in transforming lives then we want you on our team! Why should you join us? Be part of an organisation with strong community impact and heritage, help shape and lead a new fundraising function from the ground up and play a key role in building long – term sustainability and growth. ROLE PROFILE 1. RELEVANT GENERAL OBJECTIVES The Fundraising & Income Generation Manager will lead the delivery of the Trent Bridge Community Trust’s three-year Fundraising Strategy (2027-2030), securing a minimum of £545,000 (within a wider £800,000 long term ambition). The roles aim is to: · Build financial sustainability and resilience · Reduce reliance on restricted and short-term funding · Increase unrestricted income and diversified revenue streams · Enable delivery of key programmes that improve health, wellbeing, and community participation through cricket 2. SPECIFIC ROLE RESPONSIBILITY A. STRATEGIC FUNDRAISING LEADERSHIP Lead the implementation and delivery of the fundraising strategy and income action plan. Develop and manage a rolling 12–24 month fundraising pipeline. Set and monitor annual and quarterly income targets. Establish systems, processes and KPI dashboards to track performance. Identify new income opportunities aligned to Trust priorities. B. INCOME GENERATION Corporate Partnerships & Sponsorship Design and deliver tiered corporate partnership packages. Identify and secure new business partnerships across Nottinghamshire and the region. Develop programme, event and apprenticeship sponsorship opportunities Steward and grow existing partners (e.g. Tweezerman, Vertu, Russell Scanlan) Work closely with the club’s Commercial team to identify potential corporate/commercial partnerships. Grants & Trusts Develop and manage a structured grant pipeline calendar. Write high-quality funding applications to Local Authorities, Charitable Trusts & Foundations, Government and statutory funders. Prioritise multi-year and unrestricted funding bids. Maintain and grow relationships with existing funders. Donations & Individual Giving Develop a regular giving programme (yearly, multi years, monthly donors) Launch and manage digital fundraising campaigns (e.g. JustGiving) Grow and segment the supporter/membership database. Introduce targeted community appeals linked to community programmes. Establish a Patron’s programmes targeting high net worth members. Fundraising Events Lead delivery of flagship events such as Charity Zipwire, Golf Day and Charity Auction. Develop and deliver new fundraising events. Maximise income through sponsorship and participation growth. C. PROGRAMME & IMPACT ALIGNMENT Work with Managers to ensure all funding aligns to: Volunteer growth (diverse and female volunteers) Expansion of programmes into North Nottinghamshire Apprenticeships and employability pathways Health & wellbeing programmes Translate programme outcomes into compelling funding cases, social impact stories and social return on investment. D. FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY & PLANNING Increase proportion of unrestricted income and multi-year funding agreements. Support annual budget planning and income forecasting. Monitor income vs expenditure alongside Managers and Trust Board. Contribute to achieving £300,000 reserves target. E. STAKEHOLDER & RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT Build strong relationships with Funders and partners, corporate sponsors, Donors and supporters. Develop structured stewardship plans. Support the production of an impact report, case studies and funder updates. Support Trustees in fundraising activity and engagement. F. PERFORMANCE & REPORTING Track and report on KPIs, including income secured vs targets, Application success rates, donor and partner growth. Provide quarterly reports to the Trust Board. Contribute to the annual review in February. Continuously refine approaches based on performance data. G. SYSTEMS & INFRASTRUCTURE Lead the development and implementation of a CRM/fundraising database, Income tracking systems, fundraising processes and policies. Maintain a risk register of funding opportunities and contracts. 3. KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS Minimum of £545,000 secured over three years Annual income targets achieved (Breakdown shown in table below) Year 1: £154,000 Year 2: £167,000 Year 3: £222,000 Generate an increase in the proportion of unrestricted income Growth in corporate partnerships and individual donors Strong, active fundraising pipeline (12–24 months ahead) Measurable contribution to volunteer growth, programme expansion and new apprenticeship roles through the income generated. Improved financial resilience and reduced dependency on NCCC and ECB funding PERSON SPECIFICATION ESSENTIAL • 3-5 years proven track record in fundraising and income generation • Success in securing funding from multiple streams: o Grants & trusts o Corporate partnerships o Events and individual giving • Experience managing fundraising pipelines and targets • Experience of developing and managing strategic partnerships that deliver measurable outcomes • Exceptional skills in bid writing and grant applications • Strong understanding of funding landscapes • Excellent relationship management and networking skills, with the ability to influence and engage a wide range of stakeholders • Strategic thinking with strong delivery focus • Strong competency in budgeting, forecasting and reporting • Ability to analyse data and drive performance • Knowledge of fundraising compliance and best practice • Commercial awareness • Degree or equivalent in business, marketing or communications • Ability to think strategically • Passion for community impact and social change • Passion for community sport and increasing participation, particularly underrepresented groups • Entrepreneurial and proactive mindset • Highly organised and results-driven • Collaborative team player • Resilient and adaptable in a changing funding environment • Collaborative mindset with ability to work across teams and organisations • Ability to travel independently between sites DESIRABLE • Experience in charity, sport, or community sector • Good at building long-lasting relationships with key stakeholders • Knowledge of non-profit governance and structure • Introductory Certificate in Fundraising • Certified Fund-Raising Executive (CFRE) • Specialized training from the Chartered Institute of Fundraising
