item.title: Operations Support Assistant
item.description: Job description Join the London District and become part of a collaborative, supportive team. As our Operations Support Assistant, you will be a key member of the team, contributing to the many workstreams that support the life of Methodism across London. We are looking for an excellent organiser who can manage their own workload, support others and provide first-rate administrative assistance. You will also be confident using a range of IT applications. We value people who think independently, take initiative and work collaboratively - sharing ideas and helping to turn them into action. You will work closely with the existing Operations Support Assistant in a job-share like partnership, keeping in touch and sharing information to support one another. This part of the job-share partnership will focus on managing the District Chairs diaries, coordinating room bookings and leading support for the Justice and Mission Group. Why work with us? You will enjoy a central office in Westminster, the flexibility to work remotely and the support of welcoming colleagues. We also offer flexible working arrangements, learning and development opportunities, competitive pay, a pension and generous annual leave. We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion - and to creating a workplace where everyone can contribute and thrive. Take a look at the job description to find out more. If the role sounds right for you, complete the application form. If you have any questions, please get in touch - we would be happy to hear from you. item.title: Sales Executive
item.description: Job description Role Overview: The Talent Set are delighted to partner with the client on a fantastic Sales Executive role. This position involves driving membership growth for a prominent industry organisation through proactive outreach, relationship building, and sales activity, all supported by comprehensive training within a collaborative environment. Key Responsibilities: Identify and qualify potential membership prospects through inbound and outbound communication. Manage sales enquiries, nurture leads, and guide applicants through the membership application process. Develop and deliver tailored proposals to meet individual customer needs. Maintain accurate CRM records, tracking all sales activities and customer interactions. Meet or exceed individual sales targets by converting interest into memberships. Represent the organisation at industry events, exhibitions, and networking opportunities. Keep informed about the full range of membership products and industry competitors. Provide exceptional customer experience throughout the sales journey. Prepare regular sales reports and updates in accordance with organizational procedures. Ensure compliance with data protection policies and relevant legislation. Collaborate with colleagues and participate in ongoing training to enhance sales skills and product knowledge. Person Specification: Proven experience in sales, particularly with membership or service subscriptions, ideally with CRM systems such as Microsoft Dynamics. Skilled in initiating cold calls and following up on warm leads with a customer-focused approach. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a friendly and professional telephone manner. Ability to build strong relationships and demonstrate good questioning and listening skills. Organised, with effective time management and prioritisation capabilities in a fast-paced environment. Self-motivated, results-oriented, and comfortable working both independently and within a team. A keen willingness to learn about industry products, market trends, and the organisation’s services. item.title: Finance Officer
item.description: We are looking for an experienced and organised Finance Officer to join our team and take responsibility for the day-to-day financial management of our charity. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working with numbers but also understands that good charity finance is about much more than processing transactions. You will help us understand our financial position, make informed decisions about our resources and ensure that our funding is managed responsibly. You will be responsible for the day-to-day running of our finances, including bookkeeping, payments and receipts, reconciliations, payroll liaison, budgeting, grant monitoring and producing regular management information. You will also support the preparation of year-end information and work with our external auditor as required. We are a placed based health and wellbeing charity working to improve the lives of people in our communities. We are committed to making a meaningful difference and ensuring that our resources are used effectively and responsibly. This is an opportunity to join an organisation where your work will have a direct impact. Good financial management enables us to deliver our work, meet our commitments to funders and make sustainable decisions about our future. If you are looking for a role where you can use your financial skills in a supportive, purposeful organisation — and where your contribution will genuinely matter — we would love to hear from you.

item.title: Interim Head of Communications and Marketing
item.description: Charity People is delighted to be working with Florence Nightingale Foundation to recruit for an interim Head of Communications and Marketing to join their talented and passionate team. Working across the UK and globally, Florence Nightingale Foundation is dedicated to supporting nurses and midwives to improve care and save lives. Through innovative leadership development programmes, scholarships, research, and professional networks, the organisation empowers nursing and midwifery professionals at every stage of their careers to lead, influence healthcare policy, and drive positive change across health and care systems. Inspired by Florence Nightingale's legacy, the organisation champions excellence, inclusion, and compassionate leadership to improve patient outcomes and strengthen the future of healthcare. Interim Head of Communications and Marketing Contract: Interim seven month contract, working on a full time basis Salary: £52,840 per annum Location: Hybrid role working between home and Florence Nightingale Foundation's Head Office in London Bridge at least two days per week Closing date for applications: 9am on Friday 25th September Interviews: week commencing 5th October As interim Head of Communications and Marketing you will be hands-on and delivery focused and will play a key role in strengthening the Foundation's profile, reach and influence during a critical period for the organisation. You'll line manage a Communications and Marketing Officer and work as part of a small team to ensure that communications and marketing activity supports the organisation's programmes, membership, fundraising, policy and stakeholder engagement objectives. Core responsibilities within the role will include: Lead and manage a clear communications channels strategy ensuring that all audiences are defined and that channels are maximised for the optimal outcome. Increase reach by identifying and targeting new and existing audiences and growing brand awareness, strength and perception Oversight and responsibility for all FNF official social media channels and content management, including supporting the Communications & Marketing Officer with posting and content creation Lead on managing and maintaining FNF's website, ensuring it is up-to-date, user-friendly, and aligned with branding and messaging guidelines Develop and oversee multi-channel digital marketing and stakeholder engagement campaigns and projects, working closely with colleagues across the organisation Oversee the writing and delivery of promotional materials and publications including newsletters to key stakeholders, as well as impact and annual reports Lead on media opportunities and relationship management with the press, proactively seeking new PR opportunities and preparing and disseminating press releases Oversee a continuous record of Florence Nightingale Foundation media and social media activity Ensure consistency across FNF brand and all communications; helping to cement the Foundation as the 'go to' organisation for the nursing and midwifery professions Support fundraising team by leading on key donor stakeholder communications Monitor the external environment to develop a good understanding of the political landscape, emerging trends in health and social care and the ambitions of other nursing and midwifery charities Coordinate and attend relevant external sector events to support marketing activity, raise the profile of the Florence Nightingale Foundation, and identify opportunities for stakeholder engagement and content generation Work with the Head of People and Operations to lead internal communications support and messaging Ownership of the marketing and communications budget, including inputting into setting the annual budget and quarterly re-forecasts, and tracking monthly expenditure Offer advice and guidance to the wider team on communications and marketing, encouraging content gathering and building storytelling skills We'd love to hear from individuals with the following skills and experience: Previous communications and marketing experience with responsibility for leading strategy and content planning and delivery Experience of, or demonstrable evidence of the capacity to, manage a small team Demonstrable experience of using digital channels, analytics and audience insight to plan, deliver and improve communications and marketing activity Experience using email, web content, CMS, CRM tools and creative software to produce engaging multimedia and visual content Copywriting and editing skills, desirably within communications or marketing in a charity, health or an educational context Experience of applying and advising on brand identity Excellent communication skills, able to develop engaging stories using a range of communications channels Highly organised with ability to prioritise effectively and complete work on time. Sound judgement and confidence in advising senior leaders on communications, reputation, media handling and stakeholder engagement If you have the following skills and experience we'd love to hear from you! Please reach out to Alice Wood at Charity People today with a copy of your CV to get the process started. If your experience matches what we're looking for, we'll be in touch to arrange a phone call. Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

item.title: Methodist Heritage Officer
item.description: The Vacancy This exciting role combines supporting the management of Methodist historic places of worship and other spaces across Britain with interpretation and audience development. The Methodist Heritage Officer will advocate for Methodist Heritage, contribute to delivering the Methodist Heritage Strategy 2026-2032 and work towards our historic spaces being sustainable, welcoming and engaging. For example, you will aim to develop and promote a compelling and integrated missional visitor offer with our museums, and resource the pilgrimage opportunities offered by our historic chapels. About You We are seeking an experienced Christian heritage professional, who is passionate about the development of Methodist Heritage and its use as a tool to deliver contemporary Christian mission. You will work with our four nationally accredited museums, but also with our many other heritage sites and historic chapels. Working with the expert volunteers in the Methodist Heritage Committee and teams at our heritage sites, as well as Connexional (national) staff team colleagues in archives, property and communications, for example, you will be someone who can ensure coordinated best practice for the Church in heritage management in relation to historic properties, advise on collection care and develop engaging interpretation and outreach. This role has an occupational requirement to be a practicing Christian in accordance with the Equality Act 2010. If you meet most of the requirements, we encourage you to apply; transferable skills and experience will also be taken into consideration. Disclosure and Barring Service An enhanced DBS disclosure is required for this position. The Methodist Church will cover the associated costs. Informal Enquiries For an informal conversation about the role, please contact Jo Hibbard, Director of Heritage & Art . For questions or reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, please email HR Team. Key Dates Closing Date for Applications : 1 October 2026 Interviews (on-site in London): 12 October 2026 Please note: We reserve the right to close this advert early if sufficient applications are received.

item.title: Volunteer Manager
item.description: Job description Help shape the UK’s dedicated Muslim Cancer Support Network. Lead, inspire and support volunteers delivering faith‑sensitive cancer support across the country. Safeena is the UK’s dedicated Muslim Cancer Support Network, created to ensure no Muslim facing cancer feels alone. As we grow into a professionally governed national charity, we are recruiting a Volunteer Manager to lead, develop and support our expanding volunteer workforce. The Volunteer Manager will oversee Safeena’s national volunteer programme including Befrienders, Community Champions, Bereavement Volunteers and operational volunteers, ensuring high‑quality recruitment, training, safeguarding, supervision and ongoing support. This role is central to Safeena’s transformation programme, helping build a credible, compliant and compassionate volunteer service that reflects the needs of Muslim communities affected by cancer. Key Responsibilities Recruit, onboard and train volunteers Deliver induction and ongoing training programmes Provide supervision, wellbeing support and reflective practice Coordinate rotas, assignments and community outreach activity Maintain volunteer records, policies and compliance Promote Safeena’s volunteer opportunities across communities and mosques Person Requirements Essential Experience managing or coordinating volunteers Strong organisational and communication skills Ability to support volunteers in emotionally sensitive roles Knowledge of safeguarding and confidentiality Confident delivering training or group sessions Desirable Experience in charity, community or health settings Understanding of Muslim communities and culturally sensitive support Training in safeguarding, bereavement or cancer awareness Posted on: 04 September 2026 Closing date: 25 September 2026 at 14:55 Tags: Administration, Campaigns, Volunteering Management, Operations, Cancer, Compliance / Quality, Engagement / Outreach, Ethnic Minority / BAME, Faith-Based, Mentoring / Coaching, Muslim, Safeguarding, Talent Acquisition / Retention, Governance / Management The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Direct Marketing Manager
item.description: The Christie Charity is a vibrant, fast moving, energetic organisation with a passionate team and a fantastic reputation. Everything we do is geared to supporting the renowned Christie hospital ensuring cancer patients receive the highest level of treatment and care and have access to world leading research and technology. We provide funding over and above what the NHS provides. We are currently entering a particularly exciting period of growth and expansion as we fundraise for a number of major projects. We are looking for a dynamic, enthusiastic and proactive individual to play a key role in shaping and enhancing our direct marketing programme. Working closely with the Supporter Experience Manager you will be responsible for the achievement and development of direct marketing income at The Christie Charity and will support on the development of our supporter experience programme. The Charity team is responsible for raising millions of pounds each year to ensure Christie patients receive the very best care and treatment. This includes everything from access to world first clinical trials and receiving radiotherapy in state-of-the-art treatment centres, to young adults being cared for in a bespoke age-appropriate centre and being able to offer patients anxiety reducing complementary therapy, or even creative sessions in our art room. If you want to make a real difference to cancer patients and are ready to rise to the challenge of working for one of the most successful charities in the North-West, then this exciting opportunity could be the role for you.

item.title: People Manager
item.description: Job description As People Manager, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality HR and people support across the organisation. You will manage the day-to-day employee lifecycle, providing practical advice and guidance to managers and employees while ensuring compliance with employment legislation, regulatory requirements, and organisational policies. This is a hands-on role focused on recruitment, employee relations, learning and development, performance management, and people administration. You will work closely with managers to help them build and maintain skilled, engaged teams that deliver excellent support to people with disabilities. You will promote and uphold the values and culture of Lisieux Trust, ensuring that people remain at the heart of everything we do. Key Responsibilities Recruitment and Onboarding Coordinate and manage end-to-end recruitment activities. Prepare and place job advertisements across relevant platforms. Arrange interviews and support managers throughout the recruitment process. Complete all pre-employment checks including references, right-to-work checks, DBS applications and onboarding documentation. Ensure recruitment practices follow safer recruitment principles and employment legislation. Coordinate induction programmes for all new employees. Employee Relations Provide first-line HR advice and guidance to managers and employees on people-related matters. Support managers with absence management, probation reviews, performance management and capability concerns. Coordinate disciplinary, grievance and investigation processes in line with organisational policies. Liaise with external HR and employment law advisors where appropriate. Maintain accurate and confidential employee records. Learning and Development Coordinate mandatory and statutory training programmes. Monitor training compliance and produce reports for managers. Support the administration and monitoring of the Care Certificate process. Identify development needs and arrange learning opportunities for employees. Work with managers to support employee growth and career development. Performance and Wellbeing Support managers in delivering effective probation reviews, supervision sessions and annual appraisals. Promote employee wellbeing initiatives across the organisation. Monitor absence trends and support managers in implementing appropriate actions. Encourage a positive, inclusive and supportive workplace culture. HR Administration Prepare contracts of employment, contract amendments and employment-related documentation. Ensure HR systems and personnel records remain accurate and up to date. Produce regular workforce reports and people-related data as required. Support payroll administration by providing accurate employee information. Ensure compliance with GDPR and data protection requirements. Compliance Ensure employment practices comply with current employment legislation and best practice. Maintain awareness of changes in employment law and support implementation of required updates. Support compliance with Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements relating to workforce management. Assist with internal audits and quality assurance processes as required. General Responsibilities Act as a role model for the values and behaviours of Lisieux Trust. Build positive and effective working relationships across the organisation. Maintain confidentiality and professionalism at all times. Participate in training and development activities relevant to the role. Undertake any other duties reasonably required and appropriate to the position. item.title: Legacy and In Memory Officer
item.description: Would you like to join our caring and ambitious team, using your strong communication and organisational skills to provide an excellent supporter journey, underpinned by positivity and empathy? Macular disease is the biggest cause of sight loss in the UK, with around 300 people diagnosed every day. The Macular Society is the only charity determined to beat the fear and isolation of macular disease with world class research, and the best advice and support. To support people affected by macular disease now, the Macular Society provides a range of support, information and services. Our research programme is focused on finding new treatments and a cure to beat macular disease forever. We are undergoing significant changes, with a transformational new strategy to multiply our income, ultimately funding research that will find a cure. What we’re looking for We’re looking for an organised, proactive and people-focused person who enjoys getting things right, communicating with others and making a positive difference to the supporter experience. This is an Officer-level role, ideal for someone with experience in administration, supporter care, fundraising, marketing or a similar role who is looking to develop their skills and build a career in charity fundraising and marketing. You don’t need to be an expert in legacy or In Memory fundraising - what matters most is that you’re curious, willing to learn and confident working with both people and processes. As part of our Legacy and In Memory team, you’ll play an important role in delivering excellent supporter care. You’ll have a varied mix of responsibilities, from processing donations and correspondence and responding to enquiries from existing and future supporters, to supporting marketing campaigns, identifying and supporting the production of marketing materials and helping us build strong, lasting relationships with our supporters. You’ll be someone who takes pride in providing a high standard of stewardship, is comfortable managing administrative tasks and can communicate with warmth, sensitivity and empathy - particularly when supporting people who are remembering someone they have lost. Our team is ambitious and curious, and we’re always looking for new ways to grow income and supporter engagement through legacies and In Memory giving. You’ll be encouraged to bring your ideas, learn from others and contribute to a positive team culture where we support and challenge each other to do our best work. If you’re looking for a role where you can combine organisation, communication, creativity and purpose, while developing your fundraising and marketing experience and helping the Macular Society make a lasting difference, we’d love to hear from you. What we provide in return In return we provide a great working culture and offer flexible working options, 27 days annual leave, the ability to buy or sell annual leave, supportive family policies, and 6% pension contribution. Macular Society is proud to be a Disability Confident Employer. A guaranteed interview will be offered to all disabled applicants where: • The candidate has evidenced the minimum criteria for the role through their application • The candidate has chosen to share that they have a disability in the covering letter/application email • Where the minimum (essential) criteria have been met, we will provide an opportunity to request any reasonable adjustments for the interview and/or the role. We want to be an inclusive and diverse employer reflecting the community we serve and welcome applications from all parts of the community, in particular people with lived experience of sight loss. We offer a flexible approach to working in this role, including the potential opportunity to work compressed hours over fewer days, or spreading out the hours out across the working week. It is important that you can work from our Andover office for all, or some, of your hours, in order to process and fulfil postal correspondence and donations. To apply: Please email your CV and a covering letter explaining how you meet the job description and person specification In line with our value of “Showing we care”, we ask that the covering letter is written in your own words and not heavily reliant on AI-generated content. Closing date: 23.59, Monday 28 September 2026 Please apply early, as we’ll be reviewing candidates throughout. We reserve the right to close the advert in advance of the published date. Interviews: Week commencing 5 October 2026

item.title: Head of Improving Rivers
item.description: Job Title: Salary: £55,000 to £60,000 per annum Band: Senior Leadership Team Contract length: Permanent - 35 hours per week, full time. Hybrid working Location: London-based, primarily Guildhall (EC2V 7HH) and Bow Lock (E3 3JY), with work across Thames21 project locations. Responsible to: Chief Executive Responsible for : Improving Rivers Managers and associated staff. About Thames21: Thames21 is an environmental charity which works across London and the Thames Basin to deliver high-impact nature-based solutions to the climate and biodiversity crisis by restoring rivers, whilst also connecting communities to their local green-blue spaces and inspiring long-term stewardship of them. Diversity at Thames21 Thames21 is committed to building a diverse and inclusive organisation that reflects the communities we serve across London and the Thames Basin. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, and lived experiences. Purpose of the role Lead and grow Thames21’s Improving Rivers Team to deliver high-quality river restoration, catchment management and environmental evidence programmes, while contributing to organisational growth and strategic partnerships. Key relationships Chief Executive and Senior Management Team, Improving Rivers Managers, Finance, Fundraising/Partnerships, external partners including the Environment Agency, water companies, local authorities, GLA and mayoral bodies, academic partners, environmental NGOs and funders. Main duties and responsibilities 1) Strategic leadership & portfolio growth · Lead the strategic development of the Improving Rivers portfolio, setting clear objectives and outcomes aligned to Thames21’s plan (2023–2028). · As a member of the Senior Management Team, contribute to organisational strategy, financial sustainability, risk management and culture across Thames21. · Translate strategy into actionable delivery plans with measurable targets and milestones. · Embed effective monitoring & evaluation across projects and programmes to evidence impact and inform decision‑making. · Contributing to organisational risk management and business planning. · Champion innovation and the use of environmental/nature finance mechanisms where appropriate to scale delivery. 2) Programme oversight, quality & compliance · Direct and support Improving Rivers Managers to deliver a coherent programme of work across river restoration, evidence, and catchment partnerships. · Enable cross‑team collaboration (with the Engagement & Learning Team and others) to maximise multiple benefits for people and nature. · Ensure robust project governance, risk management and reporting. Oversee Health & Safety and CDM compliance and safe systems of work. · Act as one of the Duty Senior Managers in the weekend cover rota · Establish and maintain portfolio measurement indices and ensure timely data entry into Thames21 platforms. 3) People leadership & culture · Lead, motivate and develop Improving Rivers Managers; set clear objectives, undertake regular 1:1s, appraisals and PDPs. · Foster an inclusive, collaborative and high‑performance culture. Ensure staff wellbeing and professional development. · Plan and chair IR team and managers’ meetings. Maintain effective internal communications and knowledge‑sharing (e.g., SharePoint). 4) Finance, funding & organisational development · Hold delegated authority for budget setting and expenditure sign‑off within the portfolio. Ensure accurate financial planning, management and reporting. · Support development of high‑quality bids and funding agreements (statutory, partnership and philanthropic), including large strategic bids and environmental market opportunities by providing technical expertise, programme design and partner engagement. · Work with Finance and Fundraising to strengthen controls, update relevant policies/processes, and ensure audit‑ready documentation. · Contribute to whole‑organisation systems, policies and processes that support effective delivery and financial resilience. 6) External relations & advocacy · Represent Thames21 with senior stakeholders (e.g., Environment Agency, water companies, GLA/mayoral teams, local authorities, eNGOs, funders, corporate partners and the Rivers Trust). · Build and steward strategic partnerships and alliances that enable delivery at scale and unlock new funding and policy influence. · Act as a confident spokesperson for Thames21 when required. 7) Reporting, governance & data · Ensure timely and accurate portfolio reporting for SMT and Board, including dashboards/infographics and risk register updates. · Promote effective use of organisational systems and data within the team to improve efficiency and data quality. Key performance indicators (portfolio ‑ level) · Water quality - monitoring & investigation: improved evidence base and prioritisation of pollution sources for resolution. · Improving water quality - implementation of evidence‑based actions at catchment scale. · Flows - natural flood management outcomes and strengthened drought/low‑flow resilience. · River/wetland enhancement, restoration & connectivity - ecological condition and connectivity improved. · Catchment‑based approach - strengthened hosting and partnership effectiveness. Other Duties This job description cannot cover every issue or task that may arise within Thames21. At various times the post-holder will be directed to carry out other reasonable duties in support of other Thames21 activities that are consistent with those in this Job Description. For more information and how to apply Additional Information · The role may require occasional evening and weekend work. Travel across London and the Thames Basin as needed. · 25 days annual leave (plus public holidays) and office closure between Christmas and New Year; flexitime/TOIL. · Auto‑enrolment workplace pension with NEST with 8% employer contribution · Laptop and mobile phone for company use; season‑ticket/bike loan (interest‑free). · 24/7 access to our employee assistance programme. Please follow thw application instructions later on in the Charity Job application process 5pm on Friday 2 October 2026 . Please mark the reference of your application ( HIR0926 ). We appreciate the time you will have taken to apply to this role, and we do appreciate that it is disconcerting when you don’t hear back from a role you have applied for. However, due to the high number of applications we expect to receive,we are unable respond to or give feedback on individual applications, but we do want to be able manage expectations. Therefore, if you do not hear from us within 4 weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has not been successful on this occasion.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Lead the next chapter for liver health in the UK This is a unique opportunity to lead a respected and financially stable health charity at a pivotal moment of transformation. Following a successful merger, the organisation has proudly just completed a full rebrand to Liver UK, bringing together services, information and advocacy across all ages. With a clear, trustee-approved strategy for 2026–2032 already in place, the next Chief Executive will focus on delivery, growth and national influence. A strong platform and a planned transition This role comes at a natural and positive point within a planned leadership transition. Our current Chief Executive has provided long-standing, successful leadership and is excited to hand over the rebranded charity for it to be led into its next phase of strategic development, sustainability and growth. The incoming CEO will inherit a well-led organisation with strong governance, a clear strategic direction, and real momentum. About the role As Chief Executive, you will lead delivery of an established strategy, ensuring the organisation continues to grow its reach, impact and income. You will work closely with an engaged and supportive Board of Trustees to maintain high standards of governance, regulatory compliance and risk management, while strengthening the charity’s voice in national policy and public affairs. This is a role that balances external influence with internal leadership, ensuring both impact and organisational resilience. Key responsibilities Deliver a trustee-approved long-term strategy, refining priorities as needed Ensure robust governance, legal and regulatory compliance Lead policy, public affairs and national influencing activity Maintain financial sustainability and drive income growth Lead and develop a high-performing Senior Management Team Oversee delivery of high-quality services and information About you You are a credible and values-driven leader with senior experience in the charity, health or related sectors. You will bring: Proven senior leadership experience at Director or Chief Executive Officer level Strong understanding of governance, finance and regulatory compliance Experience influencing policy and working with senior stakeholders A track record of delivering organisational growth and impact Excellent communication and relationship-building skills You will be confident working with a Board of Trustees, able to build strong relationships, provide clear advice, and operate effectively in a governance-led environment. You will be motivated by improving health outcomes and confident leading an organisation with both national influence and strong operational delivery. Why join us? A clear, trustee-approved strategy ready for delivery Strong governance, financial stability and organisational foundations A positive and well-managed leadership transition The opportunity to shape a newly unified, UK-wide charity A chance to make a meaningful difference in an under-recognised area of health A strong, engaged and motivated Board A competitive salary will be offered, reflecting the experience, skills and leadership qualities of the successful candidate. #CEO #Chief Executive #Chief Executive Officer #Charity CEO #Chief Executive Charity #Health Charity CEO #Healthcare CEO #Nonprofit CEO #Charity Leadership #Executive Leadership #Senior Leadership #Chief Executive Jobs #CEO Jobs
item.dc:creator: Liver UK

item.title: Research and Impact Manager
item.description: To identify new prospects (trusts, foundations, philanthropists, corporates) to support the development and strategic objectives of The Christie Charity. To manage post-award impact and reporting requirements of The Christie Charity and work closely with the Grants Manager, who will focus primarily on the pre-award stage of the grant life cycle. To source and share industry information across the Charity. The role will be instrumental in both developing and expanding our prospect pipeline, identifying new opportunities and providing high-quality research materials to support our fundraising efforts. WHY THE CHRISTIE CHARITY? If you want to make a real difference to cancer patients and are ready to rise to the challenge of working for one of the most successful charities in the Northwest, this role could be for you. The Christie Charity is a vibrant, fast moving, energetic organisation with a passionate team and a fantastic reputation. This is an exciting time to join The Christie Charity as we embark on a period of transformational growth with the launch of key capital appeals enabling us to see a real step change in our income. We are looking for dynamic individuals to join our successful fundraising team at this exciting time. We are an independent charity and everything we do is geared to supporting the renowned Christie hospital to ensure that cancer patients receive the highest level of treatment and care and have access to world leading research and technology. We provide enhanced services over and above what the NHS funds. The Christie Charity operates from the same campus as The Christie NHS Foundation Trust.
item.dc:creator: The Christie Charity

item.title: Grants Manager
item.description: This is an exciting new role which will be integral to the organisation. Working closely with grant applicants, being primarily NHS Trust teams, the role will oversee and take ownership of the Charity’s grant-making process. The role will have responsibility for ensuring a robust grant management framework is set up and enforced across the organisation. The role will primarily focus on the pre-award stage of the grant life cycle, and work closely with the Charity’s Research and Impact Manager who will focus on the post-award stage of the grant life cycle. This role requires a proactive individual with excellent communication and organisational skills, who thrives in a fast-paced environment and can manage multiple priorities at once. The postholder will be expected to build effective relationships with clinical, research and corporate teams across the Trust and develop a strong understanding of the projects and services for which charitable funding is sought. The individual will need strong relationship building skills and the ability to work effectively with teams under pressure. The role would suit an experienced grants professional who can help set up future-proofed systems and processes with potential scope for expansion in the future. WHY THE CHRISTIE CHARITY? If you want to make a real difference to cancer patients and are ready to rise to the challenge of working for one of the most successful charities in the Northwest, this role could be for you. The Christie Charity is a vibrant, fast moving, energetic organisation with a passionate team and a fantastic reputation. This is an exciting time to join The Christie Charity as we embark on a period of transformational growth with the launch of key capital appeals enabling us to see a real step change in our income. We are looking for dynamic individuals to join our successful fundraising team at this exciting time. We are an independent charity and everything we do is geared to supporting the renowned Christie hospital to ensure that cancer patients receive the highest level of treatment and care and have access to world leading research and technology. We provide enhanced services over and above what the NHS funds. The Christie Charity operates from the same campus as The Christie NHS Foundation Trust.

item.title: Welfare Benefits Advisor
item.description: Hours: 21 hours per week. All hours to be worked between 9 – 5 Monday – Friday. We will consider full days or shorter days to meet personal commitments. Contract: Permanent Responsible to: Information & Advice Manager Location: White House Community Centre, Hampton and at community locations / homes across the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames . Some home working is also possible in line with Hybrid Working Policy. Salary: £30 – 32,000 FTE DOE plus 5% pension contribution pension contribution. Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Blue Light card and Age UK discount schemes. Work as part of a team giving great support to local older people Age UK Richmond upon Thames is a local independent charity supporting older people across the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames. We provide a wide range of useful and well utilised local services in Richmond upon Thames designed to improve wellbeing and enhance independence – including information & advice; a wide range of social & wellbeing centres and sessions; support after hospital discharge; digital skills development; Dementia Friendly Richmond; mental health peer support and home services such as handyperson, housekeeping and gardening. Partnership is a core part of our work – we work in close collaboration with other voluntary sector partners and wider organisations to maximise our impact and reach. Our friendly and committed team of 50 staff and 100+ volunteers support over 4,000 local older people each year. Our Information & Advice service is a central part of our organisation. Our small team of staff supported by excellent volunteers provide free and confidential Information & Advice to older people across the borough on a range of topics. The main area of support is to claim welfare benefits and other forms of financial support – but also includes a range of other topics such as accessing care & support; independent living; sorting out paperwork and housing. We currently have an excellent opportunity for a Welfare Benefits Advisor to join the team. The role will include: · Providing welfare benefits & financial advice, including advising older people on the financial support available, making applications on their behalf and following through applications to result. · Providing Information & Advice on other topics older people require support with. · Providing support via home visits, over the phone and in community settings. We are looking for: - Experience of giving information & advice. - Experience of welfare benefits advice work and completing benefit forms. - Good understanding of the welfare benefits system for older people. Access to a car is required. Click on apply to be taken to our website for full information, and how to apply. We are interviewing as suitable applications are received.

item.title: Domestic Abuse HUB Worker
item.description: About Us Birmingham and Solihull Women’s Aid have for over 45 years supported women and children with services around domestic violence and abuse. Could you be a part of our team as we continue our mission to end domestic violence and abuse? The region’s leading charity in tackling violence against women and girls, BSWA offers a helpline, webchat, drop in and and community support as well as emergency accommodation in six refuges across the area. Projects supports women in the criminal justice system, in healthcare settings, and throughout the community, offering support to women and children experiencing domestic violence. Alongside this, we also have staff offering training and consultancy to businesses and health and social care professionals alike, raising awareness on gender based violence issues. We seek like-minded women to join our enthusiastic team of workers, all of us passionate about the vital and valuable work we do to support women and children who have experienced domestic abuse, and tackling the wider issues of violence against women and girls. Key Responsibilities To work as part of a team to provide emotional and practical support to women and children affected by violence and abuse through our Early Intervention hub and helpline service. Experience Required - Of providing practical and emotional support to women and children affected by domestic violence Of offering advice and information and advocating for service users on a range of issues including homelessness, benefits, legal, social welfare issues etc. Of developing and maintaining effective working relationships with external agencies Of working within safeguarding guidelines to protect and promote the well-being of children and vulnerable adults Benefits 31 days annual leave (excluding bank holidays) Up to 6% matched pension contribution Free access to Employee Assistance Programme Life Assurance scheme while in employment (a lump sum of 4 times salary) Cycle to Work scheme Health Cash Plan scheme available to all employees from day one Successful candidates may have the opportunity to work under hybrid working arrangements, subject to the role and to the terms of our Hybrid Working Policy BSWA is a Disability Confident Employer. We want everyone to have equal chance at being considered for our jobs. Should you be unable to submit your application online and would prefer an alternative method, or you are experiencing another barrier to completing your application, please contact our recruitment team via our website. These posts are covered by a Genuine Occupational Requirement (Schedule 9; Equality Act 2010) and women only need apply. The closing date for receipt of completed applications is at 12 noon on Friday 2nd October. Interviews will take place weeks commencing 19th October. Apply via our website.

item.title: Fundraising Director
item.description: About Animal Defenders International London – Los Angles – Bogota – South Africa. Animal Defenders International (ADI) is a UK non-profit; ADI Foundation is a UK registered charity (inc. Lord Dowding Fund for Humane Research); Animal Defenders International Inc.US (nonprofit). Animal Defenders International South Africa, PBO (charity), funding the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary, South Africa. ADI works to protect wildlife, our environment; to end suffering of animals in entertainment (circuses, movies, shows, sports); replacement of animals in research & testing with advanced technology. When governments ban the use of all, or wild animals in entertainment, or wildlife pets, ADI supports with relocation of the animals, emptying all circus cages in Bolivia, Peru, Colombia, Guatemala. The ADI Wildlife Sanctuary (ADIWS), South Africa, is home to over 30 rescued big cats from circuses, illegal pet trade, zoos. Location: London (hybrid/remote; 3 days office, 2 days remote) Terms: Permanent, full time. Benefits: 20 days annual leave; national holidays; 5 days office closure Christmas–New Year; Stakeholder pension. Reports to: ADI President and Vice President Position objective: Ensures every aspect of ADI’s work is fully funded. Planned growth of ADI income from general public, marketing, special projects and appeals, foundations and corporate support. Implements fundraising appeals; marketing strategies; major gifts, foundations, corporate support; promotions of legacies; estates. Obtains funding for special projects, e.g., science research, ADIWS support, capital projects. Annual and quarterly plans, strategies, alliances, growth of ADI income through marketing, social media, legacy media, donor relationships, corporate support. Effective management of fundraising and development teams. Duties: Production of quarterly and annual fundraising, marketing corporate and media plan: targets – quarterly, annual; schedules, outlines, incorporating senior management team objectives (media, science projects, campaigns, education, rescues, ADIWS). Outreach – corporate, foundations, major donors, other. Donor base: sustained giving; digital and postal direct response; increasing donor engagement and retention; planned giving; special events/calendar dates; major gifts; grants; corporate; legacies, trusts, estates; new income research. Manages fundraising calendar , mailings, events, targets, tracking; includes social media. Grant Applications, foundations, corporate: Identify, plan, approach, draft grant applications/letters of inquiry and collateral for foundations, trusts, corporate partnerships and gifts, major donor gifts. Donor liaison, relationships: high donors, foundations, estates, corporate, sponsors. Reporting – weekly, monthly, quarter, annual: income tracking, supervise production of data for quarterly reports, annual. Liaison with senior directors: Weekly. Publications, Social, Websites, Online & Print Weekly Social media posts – contribute copy, graphics Weekly E-News alerts to supporters (with public relations director) Contributes fundraising and development section to Annual Report Contributes copy for quarterly Rescuer magazines Other contributions to publications as needed General: Drafting copy, editing, production; collaborates with public relations/senior directors on various publications Oversees production of print and online publications – liaison with external graphic designers (collaboration with public relations director) Websites – contribute content, collaborate with public relations on structure. Advertising, marketing, ADI YouTube channel – develop fundraising, marketing. Management, data, oversight, reporting: Management of UK supporter engagement, fundraising team. Oversight of Raiser’s Edge NXT, Engaging Networks, interface with financial database and records; liaison with Chief Financial Officer. Monitor, manage, daily: data entry, gifts, acknowledgements, income tracking, donor communications; distribution of newsletters; calls to action; appeals. Reporting. Monitor, manage reconciliations, data manipulation, data-integrity projects, audits, segmentation, quarterly and other reports. Oversee planning, mailings, responses, data management. Monthly and quarterly reports: income, mailings, gifts, trusts, estates, corporate, other. Who should apply: You have the necessary skills and experience, with at least 4 years’ experience in fundraising planning and management for charities, including: Educated to degree level in a related field (or equivalent experience) (required). A successful track record in direct response campaign fundraising and marketing. Excellent written English, you can demonstrate impactful and persuasive content for high donors, foundations, corporate support, supporters, social media, marketing and legacy promotion (required). Strong technical skills, data management, manipulation; MS Office suite, Excel/Google, etc; competent with digital research (NB: ChatGPT not permitted for ADI product) (required). Strong Raiser’s Edge NXT and Engaging Networks skills (or similar); segmentation, creating lists and reports, data hygiene, audits (required). Some knowledge of social media tools, e.g. Canva, Photoshop, or other. You can plan and deliver programs for regular and planned giving, major gifts, estates, support from foundations, corporate support (required). Management of external vendors for direct response campaigns, production of merchandise catalogue and other sales, marketing, collateral. Ensures compliance with ADI’s language, policies, communications style guidelines, editing and publications authorization process (required). Skilled at organization and multitasking, you can successfully handle competing priorities and deadlines (required). Supporter Engagement culture: strong verbal and written communication skills, you can create a friendly, welcoming approach, for supporters with their donations and advocacy. Oversight and Management of staff and supporter relations (required): - Create friendly, positive, service-oriented approach to help supporters donate and advocate for animals. - Diligent processing/handling of donations, acknowledgements, correspondence, phone calls. - Integrity and confidentiality in the handling of sensitive and confidential information - Integrity of financial records with finance database; liaison with CFO. You are reliable, able to work both independently and collaboratively. About Us: ADI is Great Nonprofits Top-rated; Charity Navigator 4-star. Operating from London, Los Angeles, Bogota and South Africa. Exposes animal suffering and works for legal protection; replacement of animals used in research; ending the suffering of animals in entertainment; movies, advertising, circuses, sport. Wildlife trade, environment. Once animal circuses are banned ADI helps governments with implementation and relocation of the survivors to ADI Wildlife Sanctuary, South Africa: ADI has featured in CBS 60 Minutes, Animal Planet Discovery features and made award-winning documentary, Lion Ark (broadcast in over 40 countries). Our internal policies: ADI is dedicated to ending the suffering of animals and works for their legal protection. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment, and a plant-based lifestyle is preferred. ADI is also committed to equal opportunities and welcomes applications from all, regardless of background, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, physical ability or other. How to apply: Apply early – no closing date – applications and interviews on rolling programme. Send email detailing how you meet our criteria, together with your CV. A formal application form will be sent if you have been selected for interview. Interviews online and in person – once your application form has been reviewed. In-person interviews arranged following virtual interviews. If you have been selected for interview we will send you an application form to complete beforehand; this is an essential part of our recruitment process. Virtual interviews will be arranged once your application form has been reviewed. In-person interviews will be arranged following virtual interviews.

item.title: Domestic Abuse Services Manager
item.description: Lead a service that changes lives Do you want your leadership to have a direct and lasting impact on people affected by domestic abuse? We are looking for an experienced, compassionate and motivated Domestic Abuse Service Manager to lead and develop our specialist services across Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland. This is much more than an operational management role. You will lead a committed team delivering support through safe accommodation, community and outreach services , helping ensure adults and children affected by domestic abuse receive safe, high-quality and empowering support when they need it most. You’ll have the opportunity to shape services, strengthen partnerships and help define what excellent domestic abuse support looks like . The opportunity Reporting to the CEO, you will provide confident leadership across our domestic abuse services, managing a diverse team of practitioners, outreach workers, project staff, volunteers and others. You’ll create a positive culture where staff feel valued, supported and able to deliver their best work, while maintaining high standards of safeguarding, quality and practice. You’ll build strong relationships with police, housing, health, children’s services, courts, commissioners and voluntary sector partners, ensuring the voice, rights and safety of victim-survivors remain central. As our Designated Safeguarding Lead , you’ll play a key role in developing a strong safeguarding culture across the organisation, ensuring concerns are managed effectively and learning leads to meaningful improvement. You’ll also use data, outcomes and feedback to understand what is working, identify emerging needs and drive service development. You will: Lead, support and develop a dedicated domestic abuse team. Oversee safe and effective delivery across refuge, community and outreach services. Champion trauma-informed, strengths-based and person-centred practice. Lead safeguarding for adults and children and contribute to multi-agency processes. Develop and deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, risk and trauma-informed practice. Build effective relationships with commissioners and partner agencies. Monitor performance, analyse data and evidence the impact of our work. Contribute to service development, funding applications, tenders, policy and organisational learning. Ensure contractual, quality, health and safety and financial requirements are met. Promote equality, diversity, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice. About you You’ll have experience of managing people and services, together with a strong understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on adults and children. Experience within domestic abuse, safeguarding, housing, social care, family support or a similar specialist service would be highly relevant. You’ll combine strong leadership with genuine compassion . You’ll be confident managing risk and complex situations, able to challenge poor practice when necessary, and committed to developing others. We’re looking for someone who is: An inspiring and supportive people manager. Experienced in trauma-informed, person-centred
item.dc:creator: Women's Aid Leicestershire Ltd, Leicester

item.title: Youth Work Manager
item.description: At One YMCA, we work alongside young people to help them develop confidence, skills, resilience, and positive futures. We are looking for an inspiring, experienced and motivated Youth Work Manager to lead and develop our local youth work provision, ensuring that high-quality, impactful services reach young people across our communities. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering our Youth Work Strategy, managing a dedicated team, driving quality and developing services that make a real difference in the lives of young people. About the role: Reporting to the Head of Youth Work, you will take operational responsibility for the delivery, development, monitoring, and quality assurance of our youth work services. You will lead and support Youth Work Coordinators and wider youth work staff, ensuring services are safe, effective, youth-centred, and aligned with One YMCA's strategic priorities. Key responsibilities include: Leading the development and delivery of youth work programmes, specialist support services, mentoring initiatives, life skills courses, and large-scale youth events. Managing and supporting staff through recruitment, induction, supervision, training, and performance development. Monitoring contract performance, outcomes, impact data, and key performance indicators to demonstrate the difference our services make. Building strong relationships with schools, local authorities, partner agencies, and community stakeholders. Leading quality assurance, compliance, safeguarding, and continuous improvement across the service. Acting as Designated Safeguarding Lead and participating in the safeguarding on-call rota. Working with young people and teams to ensure youth voice is at the heart of everything we do. We're looking for someone who combines strong operational leadership, experience in managing contractual compliance, with a genuine commitment to young people. You will bring: Significant experience delivering and managing youth work programmes, projects, or contracts. A strong understanding of issues affecting young people's lives and a passion for helping them achieve positive outcomes. Experience leading, motivating, and developing staff teams. Excellent communication, relationship-building, and partnership-working skills. The ability to analyse data, monitor impact, and use insight to improve services. A youth work or related community-focused qualification at degree level, or significant equivalent experience. A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle for work purposes. Location: Home-based role but with regular travel to YMCA youth work delivery sites across Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, as well as to support the broader youth work within One YMCA. Driving licence and access to a car is essential for this role. If you are an experienced youth work leader ready for your next challenge, we would love to hear from you! Important: Please include a supporting statement with your application/CV. We do not provide visa sponsorship; you must be eligible to work in the UK. You must reside in the UK for the duration of your employment and provide Right to Work evidence. As some of our roles involve working with vulnerable members of society, this position may require a Basic or Enhanced Criminal Disclosure, which will be conducted once a conditional offer is made Previous Applications: We welcome applications from all qualified candidates. However, if you have applied for a similar role within the last 6 months and were not successful, please consider whether your experience has developed further before reapplying Accessibility & Adjustments: We are committed to making reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process and will strive to be as accommodating as possible. Please inform us in advance of any arrangements you may need to fully participate in the process. At One YMCA we are an inclusive organisation and actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills, and potential. We do not discriminate on the basis of Age, Disability, Gender Reassignment, Marriage/Civil Partnership, Pregnancy/Maternity, Race, Religion/Belief, Sex and/or Sexual Orientation. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities, and industries, and are committed to having a team that is made up of diverse skills, experiences, and abilities. Working hours: 37.5 hours per week, generally Monday to Friday but with flexibility of working pattern to support both the ideal candidate and business need. Some evening work expected, and occasional weekend, overnight stays or residential work.

item.title: Communications & Marketing Lead
item.description: We’re hiring: Communications and Marketing Lead We’re looking for a creative and enthusiastic Communications and Marketing Lead to join the Youth Focus North West team. This is a great opportunity for someone who loves creating engaging content, telling stories and finding different ways to connect with people. You’ll help us share the impact of our work with young people and the youth sector across the North West, developing campaigns, creating content for social media, websites and publications, producing graphics and video, ensuring our communications are clear and engaging. You’ll also help us understand what’s working by using insight and analytics to improve our communications and reach more of the people we want to connect with. item.title: Independent Domestic Violence Advisor
item.description: £30552.00 - £32383.00 per annum Contract (BBTECH_RESERVED:Text100) Justice Job description We have an exciting opportunity for an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate (IDVA) to join the team in Merton. This role involves both face to face and virtual support in a hybrid model of working, you will work from home and Victim Support Office at Merton Civic Centre. This role is offered on a fixed term contract basis until June 2027 with the possibility of this being longer subject to funding. Do you want to make a difference every day? Do you want to contribute to change & improvement for those who need it? Do you have resilience & adaptability? Can you work effectively with a focus on customer service and care? What we offer At Victim Support we believe in attracting & retaining the best people and offer a competitive rewards & benefits package including: Flexible working options including hybrid working 28 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, rising to 33 days plus Bank Holidays An extra day off for your birthday & options to buy or sell annual leave Pension with 5% employer contribution Enhanced sick pay allowances, maternity & paternity payments High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment & leisure discounts Access to our financial wellbeing hub & salary deducted finance Employee assistance programme & wellbeing support Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes Cycle to work scheme & season ticket loans Ongoing training & support with opportunities for career development & progression About the Role This role is based in the London borough of Merton. As an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate you will: Implement effective ways of working with victims and those supporting them to increase safety and reduce harm. Provide a high-quality, front-line service to victims of domestic abuse, delivering a premium service prioritised according to risk, primarily focusing on victim/survivors aged 16+ Work within a multi-agency framework consisting of the MARAC and local partnership responses to domestic abuse to keep safety central to all services for victims of domestic abuse. Knowledge of help-seeking barriers and support needs of victims of domestic abuse (in heterosexual or same-sex relationships). An understanding of domestic abuse including the impact of domestic abuse on victims and their children. To understand the principles of risk assessment, safety planning and risk management for victims of domestic abuse and their children Knowledge of safeguarding issues, and the legal responsibilities surrounding these issues. Previous experience of direct service delivery to victims of domestic abuse or other vulnerable people. Strong communication, negotiation and advocacy skills, both written and verbal when interacting with a range of agencies and individuals. Understand and be committed to equal opportunities and diversity issues in policy and practice. Good crisis management skills and the ability to deal with stressful and difficult situations. Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details. About Us Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required. At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minoritised communities. As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process. How to apply To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible. item.title: Fundraising Manager – Major Giving
item.description: PWSA UK is looking for a relationship-focused fundraiser to grow income from major donors, corporates, trusts and foundations, including pharmaceutical companies. This new role will help build lasting supporter relationships and secure significant gifts that make a meaningful difference for people with Prader-Willi syndrome and their families. About the role This is a new role and you will identify, cultivate, solicit and steward prospective and existing supporters, developing tailored communications, proposals and engagement opportunities that connect donors’ interests with PWSA UK’s mission. Working with colleagues, trustees and volunteers, you will manage relationships, support donor meetings and events, and maintain accurate donor records and pipeline information. • Build and manage a portfolio of prospective and existing major donors. • Research and identify new supporters and relationship opportunities. • Develop persuasive proposals, cases for support and donor communications. • Support cultivation, stewardship, meetings, visits and events. • Keep accurate records, forecasts and pipeline reports. About you You will be an excellent communicator, careful researcher and organised relationship manager, with experience in major giving, corporate fundraising, or trusts and foundations. You will be confident working with donors and senior stakeholders, handle sensitive information with discretion, and share PWSA UK’s commitment to supporting people with Prader-Willi syndrome. Why join us? This is an opportunity to shape a new fundraising role within a specialist charity and help grow high-value support for PWSA UK’s work.

item.title: Fundraising Manager – Individual Supporters
item.description: PWSA UK is looking for an individual who is experienced in individual supporter fundraising, capable of growing our income from our community network, individual givers including seasonal and capital campaigns. You will have the drive to make a difference for our stakeholders, be able to build strong supporter relationships at a distance and create compelling proposals that connect donors with PWSA UK’s mission and will enjoy working independently in a small team. About the role This is a new role and you will manage and maintain a regular giving programme for new and existing supporters, developing tailored communications, proposals and engagement opportunities for the community that connect donors’ interests with PWSA UK’s mission. Working with colleagues, trustees and volunteers, you will support community fundraising, establish an effective individual giving programme using the CRM and increase the number of legacy pledges achieved over time • Build and manage an individual giving programme. • Support and build upon the community fundraising activity • Develop persuasive campaigns, cases for support and donor communications. • Maintain the CRM and utlise it to its full potential • Keep accurate records, forecasts and pipeline reports. About you You will be an excellent communicator, careful researcher and organised fundraising manager, with experience in individual giving and community fundraising. You will be confident communicating with donors and senior stakeholders, handle sensitive information with discretion, and share PWSA UK’s commitment to supporting people with Prader-Willi syndrome. Why join us? This is an opportunity to shape a new fundraising role within a specialist charity and help grow high-value support for PWSA UK’s work.

item.title: Specialist Independent Sexual Violence Advocate (ISVA)
item.description: We are seeking a qualified Specialist ISVA (Independent Sexual Violence Advocate) to join our Advocacy team at Respond. The role includes providing pro-active emotional, practical and advocacy support for adults with learning disabilities and autistic people with complex or multiple needs who have experienced any form of sexual violence and are engaging, (or considering engaging) with the criminal justice system. The ISVA will work across London to provide non-judgmental, trauma-informed emotional support, working in partnership with other London sexual violence support services. Our ideal candidate will have experience in the ISVA role as well as a friendly and relational approach to working with clients. You will have the ability to build trusting relationships, work in an empowering and inclusive way and support clients to heal following sexual abuse and develop coping capacity. You will be a self-motivated individual who will engage with a wider range of people who have experience sexual violence, and other barriers to justice. This is an exciting opportunity to join an inclusive and passionate team, and you will be supported by the ISVA Service Manager in your ongoing development. Respond values and encourages working in a collaborative and compassionate way, as we support each other to address one of the most enduring injustices; of the experience of trauma to autistic people and people with learning disabilities and their families. Background information about Respond Respond started in 1991 and has grown from a small London based charity to a medium sized national charity in recent years. Our mission is to reduce the impact of trauma in the lives of people with learning disabilities and autistic people, by developing trusting relationships, through psychotherapeutically informed services. An important part of our work at Respond is working in a trauma-informed way. What this means for us is that we hold in mind the impact of trauma at all levels of the organisation, and all staff take part in reflective practice or team dynamics. We are keen to encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates including people with lived experience, who are both interested in working in partnership to provide advocacy support, as well as supporting people with learning disabilities and autistic people who have experienced trauma. We are committed to the furthering of human rights, equality, and positive social change through our therapeutic and advocacy work and are committed to anti-racism and other forms of anti-discriminatory practice. We recognise that we need to continually keep this as a focus in our work and as an integral part of our organisational strategy. We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every requirement in the person specification, we encourage you to apply anyway and demonstrate how your experience is transferrable for this role. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles within the organisation. Respond Benefits package (all per financial year) We offer a generous and comprehensive package of flexible benefits to all of our staff. Hybrid working model, which means that if you’re full time you make a commitment to be working in the office at least two days a week, with the remainder working from home. Part time hours are altered accordingly. Generous paid leave benefits including 28.5 days holiday (plus Bank Holidays), with some to be taken between Christmas and New year. Up to 4 weeks paid sickness leave at full pay and a further 4 weeks at half pay, Discretionary study leave to support training relevant to your role. Paid leave to employees who may need to take one day off a year when a religious festival falls on a workday. Up to 5 days paid time off for dependents per financial year. Opportunity to apply for up to 2 days (14 hours) paid leave per year to participate in volunteering activities relevant to the role. Access to a workplace pension scheme, administered by NEST, with a minimum 5% employee contribution and 3% employer contribution from commencement of employment. Access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) which includes 24/7 telephone service and counselling. Note all of the above days per annum stated are pro rata’d for part time employees. If you’d like to find out more about this role , please read through the job description and our person specification. When you apply, please send a CV and address the points in the person specification in an accompanying supporting statement.Your statement should be no more than 2 sides of A4. Closing date for applications: 5th October 2026
