item.title: Communications Manager
item.description: The Role This is a hands-on communications role sitting at the centre of a small, ambitious and growing charity. The Communications Manager will take responsibility for planning, coordinating and delivering communications across Not A Phase. You will bring together communications from across our services, campaigns, fundraising, partnerships and events, ensuring that what we communicate is engaging, accessible, consistent and recognisably Not A Phase. This is not simply a social media role. We are looking for someone who can see the bigger picture of the charity's communications while also being comfortable doing the work themselves - writing copy, developing campaigns, briefing creatives, producing content, updating the website, coordinating photography and filming, creating newsletters and making sure projects actually get delivered. You will work closely with colleagues across the organisation to understand what is happening within our services and turn that activity into compelling communications for our community, supporters, partners, funders and the wider public. You will also play an important role in protecting and developing the voice of Not A Phase: positive, confident, human, community-led and grounded in the lived experiences of trans+ people. What We Offer 26 days annual leave + bank holidays (33 days total) Festive Period break (avg 7-10 working days) Flexible working hours Mostly remote working with in-person attendance for relevant events Travel expenses covered Key Responsibilities 1. Strategy, Planning & Coordination Own and deliver an organisation-wide communications plan aligned with Not A Phase’s strategy and priorities. Maintain a forward calendar covering services, campaigns, events, partnerships, fundraising and key dates. Work across teams to identify opportunities, coordinate activity and ensure projects are supported from launch through to impact. 2. Content, Storytelling & Brand Lead on writing and editing clear, accessible content for web, email, campaigns, reports, fundraising, partnerships and organisational updates. Tell compelling stories that reflect the breadth of our work and celebrate trans+ community, creativity, achievement and joy. Protect and develop the Not A Phase brand, messaging and tone of voice, helping colleagues and partners communicate consistently. 3. Digital, Social & Campaigns Lead our digital and social media communications, representing our programmes, locations, communities and partnerships. Plan joined-up campaigns across social media, email, web and partner channels, including relevant LGBTQIA+ and diversity calendar moments. Keep our website and email communications current, grow audiences and use performance data to improve activity. 4. Content Capture & Creative Production Plan photography, video, testimonials and other content across services and events. Attend selected activities to capture or coordinate content, managing external creatives where needed. Maintain an organised asset library and ensure consent, safeguarding and privacy processes are followed. 5. Community Reach & Service Communications Clearly communicate our services, who they are for and how to access them. Develop targeted communications to increase participation and reach new and underrepresented audiences, including people outside major cities. Use feedback to make communications clearer, more accessible and effective. 6. Partnerships, Fundraising & Impact Support fundraising and partnership communications, clearly showing the value and impact of support. Create materials, stories and case studies using service data, feedback and testimonials. Work collaboratively with external partners on developing and promoting partnership communications. Help communicate organisational progress and strengthen relationships with supporters, funders and partners. 7. Media & Responsive Communications Support our external profile through press releases, statements, briefings, media relationships and spokesperson preparation. Work with the CEO and Senior Leadership Team on sensitive or fast-moving communications, using sound judgement and keeping responses grounded in our mission. Prepare appropriate messaging where public or reputational issues arise. 8. Insight & Improvement Monitor performance, set practical communications KPIs and report useful insight to the CEO and Senior Leadership Team. Use audience data to improve communications, systems and processes, while keeping up with relevant charity and digital communications practice. Person Specification Essential Experience in a charity, community or purpose-led organisation. Excellent writing, editing and proofreading skills, with the ability to make complex information clear and engaging. Strong communications, marketing or content experience, including multi-channel campaigns. Strong digital and social media experience, including websites, email, audience growth and performance insight. Excellent organisation and project-management skills, with the ability to plan ahead and manage competing deadlines. A strong understanding of brand, tone of voice, accessibility and inclusive communications. Sound judgement when communicating about sensitive or contentious subjects. A collaborative approach, with the confidence to work independently and own projects from idea to delivery. Experience managing external creatives, freelancers or agencies. A hands-on approach and willingness to personally produce much of the charity’s communications. Desirable Experience communicating with LGBTQIA+ communities and an understanding of issues affecting trans+ and gender-diverse people in the UK. Media relations or PR experience. Experience producing or commissioning photography and video. Experience supporting fundraising, partnerships or impact communications. Experience managing staff, freelancers or volunteers. The Person We are a small team delivering a growing UK-wide programme, so we need someone comfortable taking ownership. The role is varied: you might plan a national campaign, update a Trans+Connect webpage, coordinate content at a Misfits session or prepare communications for a new partnership. You will spot strong stories across the charity and turn them into effective communications. You will understand that good communications are about reaching the right people, telling meaningful stories, building trust and demonstrating impact. You will bring structure and forward planning while retaining the personality, creativity and community-led approach that makes Not A Phase distinctive. What You'll Help Us Achieve Over the next five years, Not A Phase aims to deepen its impact and reach more trans+ adults across the UK. Reach more trans+ people who could benefit from our services. Tell our story and demonstrate impact. Strengthen relationships with supporters, funders and partners. Grow national recognition of Not A Phase. Improve communications across the organisation. Celebrate trans+ diversity, creativity and achievement. Ensure our work is seen, understood and valued. Please be aware that we use AI detection software will not be moving ahead with applcations or CV's that are written by AI.

item.title: Independent Advocate (BSL)
item.description: Are you qualified for BSL Level 6? Do you thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment? Are you ready to take on a role that impacts your community? An exciting opportunity has arisen for a part time Independent Advocate to join our Birmingham team. This role covers statutory advocacy services including Independent Mental Capacity Advocacy, Independent Mental Health Advocacy and Care Act Advocacy. The post will be home based working across Birmingham including providing advocacy support for the Deaf and hard of hearing people in care homes and on secure mental health hospital wards in our area. As an Independent Advocate, you will provide crucial support to vulnerable adults facing significant health and social care challenges. Your role involves delivering persuasive verbal and written representations on behalf of clients, collaborating with public and voluntary organisations, and taking directed actions to address client issues. This role demands flexibility, excellent communication, and the ability to handle sensitive information confidently. You will need to have experience of working with Deaf people and providing BSL communication support. Due to this specific element of this role, a minimum proficiency of level 6 British Sign Language (BSL) is required. Hours of Work: Part Time: hours to be agreed working between Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm Location: Home based with travel across Birmingham and the surrounding area(Applicants should live within the Birmingham area/within reasonable travelling distance; have a full driver’s licence and access to their own transport, travel expenses will only be paid within the Birmingham border area.) Salary: Starting salary to be agreed dependent on hours (£25,877.80 pro-rata) Contract Type: Permanent Independent Advocate Requirements: Strong communication and time management skills to successfully work remotely. Excellent IT skills, including the use of Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel, and the ability to learn software packages such as client management databases. Attention to detail to ensure accurate recording of records and reporting to meet tight deadlines. Desirable: Previous experience in advocacy, information and advice, or a similar role within health, social care, or the voluntary sector. Demonstrable experience working with vulnerable adults in the Community and also within secure Mental Health settings. Working knowledge of public and voluntary organisations. Benefits: 25 days annual leave (pro-rata)+ Bank holiday (Rising to 30 days (pro-rata) after 5 years’ service) with the option to buy or sell up to 5 days leave + your birthday off as an additional holiday day after 1 years’ service! Discretionary shutdown days at Christmas with up to 4 additional days leave. 1 Community Leave Day per annum. Cash Wellbeing Healthcare Plan which covers Optical/dental/alternative therapy and more! Auto enrolment Pension plan Death in service cover. Bike to work scheme. Meet the Organisation: Who We Are and What We Do At POhWER, we are committed to empowering individuals and enabling their voices to be heard. We provide advocacy and information services to support people in making effective decisions about their health and social care. Our team is dedicated to listening, exploring options, and taking action to meet our clients' best interests. We provide a full induction, training and equipment including a laptop and mobile phone. It is a contractual requirement that all advocates hold or are working towards an advocacy qualification. The most recognised qualification is the City and Guilds Level 4 Independent Advocacy Practice Qualification (IAP) for practising advocates, previously completed City and Guilds Level 3 National Advocacy Qualification (NAQ). If you do not already hold an NAQ certificate or diploma or IAP qualification or equivalent, the expectation will be that you will gain the City and Guilds IAP qualification following successful completion of probation and pre-enrolment process. POhWER will fully sponsor this and provide a reasonable amount of study time and in return expect advocates to manage their time and complete within 12 months of registration. Think you are the perfect fit for this Independent Advocate role? Don't wait! Apply Now with your CV and Cover letter! Interview Date: To be confirmed An enhanced DBS check and National Offender Management Service vetting will be conducted for this position. We're proud to support our colleagues from the armed forces signing the Armed Forces Covenant in August 2024. POhWER is committed to equality, diversity, and inclusion. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, cultures, and abilities, and particularly welcome candidates from groups currently underrepresented in our workforce. Our goal is to foster an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute. This includes, but is not limited to, people with disabilities, women, men, Black, Asian and other racially minoritised people, LGBTQ+ who are currently under-represented in our workforce. To help embed inclusion for all, from day one, we offer a range of family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements and employee networks to support people from different backgrounds. POhWER is an equal opportunities employer, holder of the Investors in People Silver award, and a member of the MINDFUL EMPLOYER scheme. We are a member of the Disability confidence scheme, and disabled applicants who meet all the essential criteria will be guaranteed an interview.

item.title: Solicitor (Support Through Court Advice Clinic)
item.description: Who we are Every year, thousands of people in the UK face court alone. Often through no choice of their own, people must represent themselves at a moment that could have life-changing outcomes. This includes loss of access to children or homelessness. At the same time, people facing court alone may find themselves up against a party with legal representation. They are instantly at a disadvantage and overwhelmed by the enormity of the challenges they are up against. We supported unrepresented litigants in the civil and family courts in England and Wales over 45,000 times last year. We provide a safe space with volunteers who listen to each client’s individual story. Last year, over 1000 volunteers helped people to get their thoughts in order, problem-solve and decide next steps, source relevant and reliable legal information, explain complex procedures, complete court forms, and clearly present statements. At a time when legal support is increasingly limited, we have a vision that no one should have to face court alone. The role Support Through Court is establishing a legal advice clinic for money claim matters under £10,000, for a one-year pilot. Advice will be given to clients across the national service network who have been internally triaged to the clinic. The role involves day-to day management of the clinic and supervising law students as they facilitate client appointments, conduct research and draft letters of advice. Clients will predominantly be supported remotely with occasional in-person appointments and advice “drop-ins” in the local area. You will train and supervise students to help them gain practical legal skills in a clinic setting, having final sign-off of completed letters of advice/oral advice to ensure clients receive an excellent service. You will embed the legal advice offering of the clinic into the organisation, increasing and developing referrals from our national service network and supporting staff understanding of referral ability. Who we are looking for Ambitious, professional, committed and friendly. That describes us. If it also describes you and you have a passion for access to justice, then we’re keen to hear from you. You will be a qualified solicitor with at least 3 years PQE (ideally 5+) with an active practicing certificate. You will have experience managing students and/or volunteers and a commitment to supporting Litigants in Person. We are open to applicants wishing to take the role either on a full-time basis, or on a part-time basis as a job share. Please make it clear in your application whether you are applying for a full-time or part-time role. Interviews will be taking place on a rolling basis as applications are received.

item.title: Head of Church Buildings
item.description: Head of Church Buildings Are you looking for an exciting opportunity to help shape the future of one of the largest church buildings portfolios in the country? We are seeking an inspiring leader to head the Church Buildings Team, overseeing the care, conservation and suitable use of 808 churches across Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire. This is a unique opportunity to influence strategy, lead a talented team, and help ensure these historic buildings continue to serve communities for generations to come. Position: Head of Church Buildings Location: Kidlington, Oxford/hybrid Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week Salary: £58,133.82 - £62,605.56 per annum Contract: Permanent Closing Date: Tuesday 6 October 2026, at midnight Interviews: Monday 26 October 2026 and may be combined with both an off-site visit and on-site interview located at Church House Oxford, Langford Locks, Kidlington, OX5 1GF. Transport will be provided for any element of the off-site visit. The Role This is a unique opportunity to lead the largest and one of the most significant church buildings portfolios in the country, helping to secure the future of 808 churches across Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire. As Head of Church Buildings, you will: Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Diocese Church Buildings Team Oversee the care, conservation, adaptation and sustainable use of church buildings and churchyards Lead an excellent team of specialist staff Manage key relationships with bishops, archdeacons, parishes and national church bodies Ensure the effective operation of the Diocese's statutory responsibilities relating to church buildings. Act as Secretary to the Diocesan Advisory Committee (DAC) Oversee the faculty system across the Diocese Oversee pastoral reorganisations and initiatives that help churches meet contemporary challenges, including sustainability, community use and Net Zero ambitions. The role also includes responsibility for church closure schemes and closed churches, working with a wide range of stakeholders to secure sustainable futures for historic church buildings no longer required for worship. This is a high-profile leadership role requiring strategic vision, excellent people management skills and a passion for conserving and sustaining some of England's most important heritage assets. It will require someone comfortable working autonomously and to bring their own ideas and enthusiasm to the transformation work, successfully put in train by the previous post-holder. It provides a fantastic opportunity for a senior leader to influence and mould the future operating model of the Church Buildings’ Team. About You We are looking for an experienced and inspiring leader with a strong background in historic building conservation, heritage management, property, architecture or a related field. You will have: Experience of managing complex projects, leading professional teams and working with multiple stakeholders in often sensitive and politically nuanced environments. Experience of operating at both strategic and operational levels, with excellent communication skills and the ability to influence, negotiate and build effective partnerships. A deep understanding of conservation principles and the management of historic buildings, together with the ability to balance heritage considerations with the mission, worship and community needs of today's churches. Significant experience of leading and developing professional staff and teams. Experience of strategic planning and delivering programmes that support the care and sustainability of historic buildings. Strong project, governance and budget management skills. The ability to work confidently with senior leaders, committees and external partners. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the preparation of reports and presentations. An understanding of, and sympathy with, the mission and work of the Church of England. Knowledge of the Church of England's faculty jurisdiction, ecclesiastical legislation and church closure processes would be advantageous, although applications are welcome from professionals with transferable experience from related sectors. You do not need to be a practising Christian to work with us. Around half of our staff are not practising Christians, but all are comfortable working within the Christian ethos and values that underpin our work. The successful candidate must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews. If you do not hear from us, your application has not been successful. We are particularly keen to receive applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority heritage and disabled candidates, who are currently underrepresented. Our client is committed to the safeguarding, care, and nurture of everyone within the church community. They follow and are committed to their Safeguarding Policies and the relevant statutory legislation and guidance, "Working together" to ensure the welfare of children and young people is paramount. You may have experience in other areas such as Facilities, Heritage, Conservation, Buildings, Estate, Historic Buildings, Property, Head of Facilities, Head of Heritage and Conservation, Head of Buildings, Head of Estate, Head of Historic Buildings, Head of Property. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People. #INDNFP

item.title: Project Coordinator
item.description: We are looking for a highly organised and proactive Project Coordinator to support the effective delivery of our assessment, onboarding, grants administration and event activities. This role is central to ensuring a positive experience for applicants and participants throughout their journey, providing excellent customer service, coordinating key processes, and maintaining accurate records across multiple platforms. The successful candidate will be confident managing competing priorities, have exceptional attention to detail, and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same. The role involves coordinating assessment and recruitment activities from initial enquiries through to final decisions, ensuring applicants receive a professional and positive experience throughout the process. Responsibilities include managing applications, coordinating interviews and selection panels, preparing panel documentation, communicating outcomes, and supporting assessment activities. Working closely with programme and grants colleagues, you will ensure processes run smoothly, deadlines are met, and accurate records are maintained. In addition, you will support participant onboarding, grants administration, and event delivery. This includes maintaining participant records across multiple systems, carrying out verification checks, processing grant payments, and supporting the logistics of in-person events. We are looking for someone with excellent organisational and administrative skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities. The successful candidate will also contribute to improving team processes and developing specialist knowledge in key areas of programme delivery, helping to ensure the efficient and effective operation of our programmes.

item.title: HR & Office Manager

The Manager, HR and Office Management will translate our new organisational strategy into forward-looking people practices, while ensuring that colleagues are supported by the policies, systems, resources and working environment they need to thrive. Working closely with directors, the leadership team, line managers and two HR Coordinators, the postholder will shape the employee experience across the full journey—from recruitment and induction to development, progression and exit. The role will also oversee workplace services, internal communications, budgets and legal compliance across multiple jurisdictions (UK, Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, Belgium, and Canada), helping a hybrid and remote workforce stay connected, informed and confident. As an additional resource, an experienced HR consultant delivers recruitment campaigns and other special projects. We are looking for an experienced generalist HR professional, who combines strategic insight with practical delivery and sound judgement. You will bring current employment law knowledge, strong influencing and coaching skills, a genuine commitment to inclusion and wellbeing, and the confidence to improve policies, systems and ways of working in an international, values-led organisation. Above all, you will be collaborative, resilient and motivated by ISEAL’s mission to accelerate positive change for people and the planet. The key responsibilities we entrust you with: HR Management Develop and deliver a HR strategy aligned with the organisation’s new strategic direction, translating priorities into sustained impact In collaboration with Leadership team, advise on and implement resource and overhead planning to support strategic objectives Shape, continuously improve and communicate ISEAL’s HR policies, procedures and processes, enabling colleagues in a hybrid/remote setting to understand them easily and apply them confidently Deliver a proactive approach to employment compliance, anticipating legislative developments across 6 jurisdictions with ISEAL staff and translating them into clear, timely organisational actions Champion a thriving organisational culture, empowering colleagues at every level to bring ISEAL’s values to life in their decisions, behaviours and ways of working Cultivate a workplace where wellbeing is embedded in everyday practice and open, constructive dialogue flows well between employees, line managers and across the organisation Foster and continually enhance an inclusive employee experience across the full journey—from recruitment and induction to performance, HR situations Serve as a trusted strategic adviser to directors and the leadership team, bringing forward progressive HR practices that strengthen organisational effectiveness and employee engagement Coordinate support of a dedicated external HR consultant for recruitment and special projects Oversee maintenance of all personnel and HR records in appropriate systems Office Management Lead on maintaining a comfortable and well-functioning workplace, including continuous review of the overall physical infrastructure needs and provision Shape and communicate forward-looking workplace policies and practices, pioneering flexible approaches to space, collaboration and ways of working. Create a safe, welcoming workplace by leading the effective delivery and continuous improvement of office services, facilities, IT equipment and resources Act as first point of contact for any issues raised by staff relating to the office Other Lead and continually strengthen internal communications that connect colleagues, reinforce shared purpose and encourage meaningful participation, including monthly staff meetings, the quarterly support staff newsletter and organisation-wide communications. Lead and empower two HR Coordinators, creating the conditions for them to grow, develop and deliver excellent support across the organisation Steward the HR and premises budgets with foresight and accountability, directing resources towards the organisation’s people, workplace and strategic priorities. Build own capacity and knowledge on all matters related to organisational legal compliance Essential attributes / skills / knowledge Substantial generalist HR management experience, combining strategic understanding with confident delivery of day-to-day people operations Demonstrable experience of developing and implementing HR strategies aligned with organisational priorities Strong track record of designing, reviewing and embedding accessible HR policies, procedures and processes Proven experience of managing diverse employee relations matters with sound judgement, fairness, discretion and appropriate confidentiality Current, practical knowledge of UK employment law and the ability to translate legislative change into clear, compliant policies and advice Excellent and, ideally, with the implementation of new systems to enhance HR operations Experience working in an international setting covering a variety of jurisdictions and employee locations Proven people-management capability, including coaching, developing and empowering team members to work to the best of their ability Strong planning, prioritisation and budget-management skills, with the ability to balance strategic projects and operational demands High levels of integrity, initiative and resilience, with a collaborative, solutions-focused approach to organisational change and continuous improvement A personal commitment to and interest in creating a more sustainable world Desirable Oversight of international payrolls CIPD Level 5 qualified ISEAL´s culture and how we will help you thrive Our values are Connection, Empowerment, Inspiration, Wellbeing, Effective Working and Creativity. item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Gendered Intelligence is seeking an exceptional leader to serve as its next Chief Executive. This is a rare opportunity to lead a nationally respected, trans-led organisation with real influence on policy, professional practice and the lives of trans, non-binary and gender exploring people across the UK. The next Chief Executive will inherit strong foundations: an experienced and committed team of just under 40 people, a distinctive and trusted public profile, and a range of services that reach communities, professionals and institutions across the country. With income of around £1.5–2m, the next Chief Executive will lead the organisation through its next phase of development at a time when that leadership matters enormously. The role offers the chance to shape strategic direction, open new partnerships and income streams, and contribute to national conversations on trans equality and human rights, while working alongside people who are deeply committed to the mission and to each other. We are looking for someone who combines strategic clarity with operational grounding, who leads with calm and consistency, and who understands both the privilege and the responsibility of this role. We will be honest with candidates about what the role involves, and we expect the same in return. Full details of the role can be found on our website and in the attached recruitment pack.

item.title: Assistant Headteacher of Inclusion, Safeguarding and Designated Safeguarding Lead
item.description: Assistant Headteacher – Inclusion, Safeguarding and DSL Location: TreeHouse School, Woodside Ave, London, N10 3JA Hours: Permanent, full time (37.3 hours per week) Salary: £62,541 to £66,744 per annum Start date: January 2027 About TreeHouse School: TreeHouse School, part of Ambitious about Autism , is an Ofsted outstanding specialist school supporting children and young people aged 4–19 with autism and complex learning needs. We are committed to providing an exceptional learning environment where every pupil can thrive and achieve their full potential. About the role: We are looking for a resilient and values led Assistant Headteacher of Inclusion, Safeguarding and DSL to join our Senior Leadership Team. This is a pivotal role with responsibility for safeguarding, inclusion and pupil welfare for autistic children and young people with complex needs. You will lead on child protection and safeguarding, working closely with our team of deputy and assistant DSLs and with external partners including Social Care, Health, Police, LADO and Prevent. You will also provide strategic oversight of inclusion, behaviour, wellbeing, healthcare, therapeutic support, Positive Behaviour Support (PBS) and least restrictive practice, working collaboratively with education, nursing and wider multidisciplinary teams. This is not an office based role. You will need to have a strong presence across the school, supporting pupils, families and staff, providing visible leadership and responding calmly and effectively when complex situations arise. What we are looking for: Has strong safeguarding experience and ideally experience as a DSL or Deputy DSL. Has a good understanding of autism, SEND and complex needs, with experience in an education or specialist setting preferred. Could be an experienced education professional, SEN specialist or social worker with substantial relevant experience and a strong understanding of education. Is confident making difficult safeguarding decisions, managing referrals and escalating concerns when necessary. Is resilient, persistent and able to manage complex cases involving vulnerable children. Can build strong relationships with pupils, families, staff and external agencies. Can lead and develop staff, ensuring safeguarding training, recording and procedures are consistently followed. What we offer: You will be well supported by an experienced safeguarding team, Senior Leadership Team and receive regular supervision and mentoring. There will also be opportunities to develop your expertise through DSL, trauma informed, autism and CALM training. This is an opportunity to make a significant difference to the lives of autistic children and young people, while leading a team and helping shape excellent safeguarding and inclusive practice across the school. If you are a confident safeguarding professional who combines expertise with compassion, resilience and determination, we would love to hear from you. Shortlisting date: Friday 2nd of October Outcome of application: Friday 2nd/Monday 5th of October Interview date: Friday 9th and Tuesday 13th of October Ambitious About Autism is committed to fostering equity, diversity, and inclusion at every level of our organisation. We warmly welcome applications from all qualified candidates, valuing the diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives they bring. We encourage applications from individuals regardless of race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origins, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or parental status, disability, or age. Our recruitment process promotes equal opportunities, and we are committed to providing reasonable adjustments for candidates with disabilities or additional needs throughout the recruitment process. Please contact our Recruitment Team for accommodations. We recognise disability as a physical or mental impairment that significantly and long-term affects a person's ability to perform day-to-day activities, as defined by the UK Equality Act 2010. All applications will be considered solely on merit, aligned with our mission to support autistic children and young people. Ambitious About Autism is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and successful candidates will be subject to an Enhanced DBS check. As part of our Safer Recruitment checks, an online search may be carried out in line with Keeping Children Safe in Education. The safeguarding responsibilities of the post are as per the job description and person specification. Whether the post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975, 2013 and 2021. This means that when applying for certain jobs and activities, certain spent convictions and cautions are ‘protected', so they do not need to be disclosed to employers, and if they are disclosed, employers cannot take them into account. item.title: Database and Research Lead – Development
item.description: Database and Research Lead – Development Hours: Full-Time, 36.25 per week (0.8 FTE may be considered) Contract: Permanent Salary: £35,000 - £40,000 depending on experience, with the possibility of further flexibility for an exceptional candidate (pro rata for a 0.8 FTE position). Location: Trinity Lane, Cambridge, CB2 1TL The Role This is an exciting opportunity to join one of the most successful college development programmes. Clare College is celebrating its 700th anniversary this year. Accompanied by a new strategic vision for the College’s eighth century, the anniversary provides an opportunity to launch Clare’s next fundraising campaign. The Database and Research Lead will play a key role in the overall success of the Development Office and the new campaign. The successful applicant will ensure the integrity, accuracy, and effective use of the College’s Development database and will provide comprehensive gift administration and data services. Responsibilities include the overseeing of constituent data with other College and University systems, providing general administrative support for the office and preparing briefings for the Master, other senior College Officers and fundraisers for use on visits and at events. The hours of work will be 36.25 per week with the specific hours to be agreed with the successful candidate. The success of the Development Office depends on the flexibility and ethos of its staff. The role holder will be required to participate in activities outside the core job description that are important to the overall development programme and the College. About Us Clare College is the second oldest of the 31 Colleges in the University of Cambridge. Regarded as one of the most progressive and informal, Clare is renowned as a College that achieves academically at the highest levels, whilst also being welcoming, forward-thinking, and inclusive. Located in the heart of Cambridge city centre, the College is extraordinarily beautiful and famed for its gardens on “the Backs” (the famous backs of the Colleges that overlook the River Cam). item.title: Head of Marketing
item.description: Work where it matters most, achieve what matters more Be part of a team where passion meets purpose, as we work together where the challenge is greatest to change the lives and build the futures of children and young people. We are excited to share an opportunity to join our central Transformation team as our Head of Marketing. In this role you will lead strategic marketing and brand development across the Trust, raising the profile and appeal of our schools to drive pupil numbers and attract brilliant candidates to work at Ormiston. You will lead the marketing team to support schools to develop and deliver marketing campaigns, manage their websites, and engage different audiences on social media. You will also act as a strategic advisor to senior leaders across the Trust, and lead marketing for special projects such as new schools joining the trust and key trust-wide initiatives. This is a home based, national role with regular travel to the Birmingham office, OAT academies and other locations as required. About Ormiston Academies Trust Our vision is to create a school system where every child thrives, regardless of background. Our people are at the heart of our approach – they are our greatest asset. We exist to provide the best learning opportunities every day, in every school for every child. It is the people and teams in our Trust who make this a reality and ensure we have the greatest impact. If you join us at Ormiston, whatever your role, you can be sure of a role with purpose and meaning. Ormiston, where every member of staff enjoys… The opportunity to build on the legacy of those who came before – being part of one of the longest standing Trusts, created with the sole purpose of enabling children and young people to thrive Working for a Trust nationally recognised for its impact on disadvantaged children – a rewarding, stimulating career where staff are challenged to be the best they can be, for the pupils we are proud to serve Being part of a team and community where you belong – receiving bespoke and holistic support from a well-resourced and ambitious network of experts and professionals that work at the heart of communities A supportive environment to grow your career – an extensive professional development programme, alongside flexible working arrangements and generous benefits About you You'll bring strong experience leading and managing a marketing team, with a proven track record of developing and delivering multi-channel marketing strategies and campaigns across digital, print and out-of-home. You'll be confident acting as a trusted adviser to senior leaders, including the CEO, Executive Office and Principals, translating organisational goals into effective marketing plans. The ability to manage priorities in a busy, complex environment, working across multiple stakeholders, is critical to this role. If you are passionate about making a difference and are ready to work in a challenging yet rewarding environment, we would love to hear from you. Benefits that care for you We value your hard work and dedication, and we're committed to ensuring you feel supported, both professionally and personally so that you are in the best position to make the most impact for the children and young people in our schools. When you join us at Ormiston, you can be certain that your work will have purpose and meaning. You can also expect robust and holistic support from us to enable you to excel in your role. You will have access to an attractive benefits package including: 30 days annual leave (rising to 32 days after 5 years' service) Generous pension and life cover Access to health and well-being programmes, including counselling service. Discounts on retail, travel, and leisure through our benefits platform. Free and confidential legal, tax and health 24/7 helpline. Cycle to work scheme. Automatic pay progression. Flexible working arrangements. And much more as part of a leading multi-academy trust. If you have any questions about the role please contact our recruitment team. The closing date for applications is 25 September with interviews due to take place the week commencing 5 October 2026. Early applications are encouraged as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early should a suitable candidate be found.

item.title: Children & Young People's Independent Sexual Violence Advocate (ChISVA)
item.description: Job description We are recruiting for a Children and Young People’s Independent Sexual Violence Advocate (ChISVA) to support and empower young survivors of sexual violence and abuse. The ChISVA will provide information, support, advice and advocacy to children and young people who have experienced sexual assault or sexual abuse in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The post holder will deliver child-centred support to young survivors and non-abusing care givers around criminal justice processes, wellbeing, education and safety, while ensuring child protection procedures are followed at all times. The post holder will work closely with other agencies such as Social Care, the Police, Education, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) and voluntary sector organisations to ensure that children and young people are kept safe and are well supported. They will prioritise, assess, plan, evaluate and deliver all relevant aspects of support to an agreed and expected high standard. This post is part of a countywide ISVA team providing a pro-active service to children, young people and adult survivors of sexual violence and abuse, within and outside of the criminal justice system. For more information and to apply for the role, please click on the 'Redirect to Recruiter' button to visit our website where you will find all the documents and details required. item.title: Partnerships Manager
item.description: Every grant you win becomes someone's first conversation in English, their first step into a job interview, their first time speaking up at a housing tribunal. English for Action (EFA) is looking for a Partnerships Manager to grow the funding that powers our free, participatory ESOL classes for around 400 migrants across London. Our classes don't just teach English, they build the confidence and collective power people need to organise around housing and employment rights. About the role Working closely with our Fundraising Lead, you'll take real ownership of relationships with trusts, foundations and corporate funders, while helping shape how we diversify our income going forward. This is a role with genuine scope to bring your own ideas and see them through, not just execute someone else's plan. You will: - Write compelling grant applications, funding proposals and reports that win and retain funding - Research and build a realistic pipeline of trusts, liveries and corporate foundations - Develop and maintain strong relationships with existing donors and prospects - Contribute to EFA's fundraising strategy, including newer income streams such as statutory, corporate, individual giving, membership and events - Liaise with our Executive Team, Hub Leads and Project Managers so funding proposals stay grounded in what's actually happening in our classrooms and communities - Maintain accurate donor and grant records on Donorfy, and support monitoring and evaluation of project outcomes About you You don't need a degree, and you're not expected to tick every box, nobody does. We're looking for someone with a track record of successful grant writing, strong research and relationship-building skills, and the organisation to manage multiple funding deadlines at once. Knowledge of the UK charity sector and UK trusts and foundations is essential; experience with public sector or EU education funding is a bonus. If you have lived experience of migration and/or learning English as an additional language, we'd love to hear from you and how you'd like to draw on it in this role. About EFA English for Action provides free, participatory, empowering ESOL classes for migrants in London, spaces where students build community and organise collectively around issues like employment and housing rights. We're a national centre of good practice for a radical, participatory approach to ESOL, and we share this approach through training, research and partnerships. We're a team of 11 staff, a wider team of volunteers, and 7 trustees, run through shared leadership rather than a CEO, decisions are made collaboratively, and we aim for our structure to reflect that. What we offer - 22.5 hours (3 days) a week, mostly remote, with just monthly in-person meetings in London - 28 days' annual leave (pro rata) after probation, plus bank holidays, plus a full week's paid closure over Christmas - 6% matched pension contribution - Enhanced sick pay, and enhanced maternity/paternity/adoption/shared parental leave - Wellbeing allowance and full entitlement to leave for sickness, including mental ill-health - A genuinely flat, non-hierarchical culture with collaborative decision-making on strategy and practice - Tech and cycle scheme, and actively encouraged continuous personal development Equal opportunities EFA particularly encourages applications from people of colour, who are currently underrepresented at EFA and across the charity sector, and from people who have experienced moving to the UK or have English as an additional language. Where two or more candidates are of equal merit, priority may be given to a candidate from a less well-represented group. Please let us know about any access or other requirements we can accommodate. Closing date: 11.59pm, Wednesday 30th September 2026 Skills test: w/c 5th October 2026 (writing and budgeting) Interviews: Friday 9th / 16th October 2026 Questions before applying? Email Gina Rodriguez (HR Lead)

item.title: Health Coordinator
item.description: About WSUP Woolwich Service Users Project is a charity based in central Woolwich, supporting people experiencing homelessness, poverty, poor mental health, addiction, social isolation and multiple disadvantage. WSUP provides a welcoming, non-judgemental, open-access community space where guests can access practical support, health and wellbeing services, specialist advice, and trusted relationships. Our work is rooted in lived experience, dignity and relational support. We meet people where they are, offering both immediate relief and pathways into longer-term stability, recovery and community connection. WSUP works closely with local and national partners across health, housing, recovery, advice and community wellbeing to reduce health inequalities and improve outcomes for people who often face barriers to mainstream services. Purpose of the Role The Health Coordinator will lead and develop WSUP’s health coordination offer, ensuring that guests can access timely, appropriate and compassionate support around physical health, mental health, addiction, sexual health, primary care, housing-related health needs and wider wellbeing. The postholder will provide structured triage, one-to-one support, casework, referrals and follow-up for guests experiencing complex needs. A key part of the role will be helping people who are not currently engaged with statutory or mainstream services to reconnect with healthcare, housing, welfare and specialist support. The Health Coordinator will also play a key role in developing and overseeing WSUP’s women’s service provision, including Women’s Wednesday. This will include coordinating health and wellbeing support, strengthening referral pathways for women, supporting peer-led activity, promoting safety and inclusion, and ensuring the service responds to the needs of women experiencing homelessness, domestic abuse, poor mental health, addiction, temporary accommodation, poverty, social isolation or resettlement barriers. The postholder will also support female residents linked to women’s accommodation and community-based support pathways in Greenwich, helping them access WSUP’s trusted community hub, women-only provision, health coordination, practical support, peer connection and specialist referrals at a pace that feels safe and appropriate. Key Responsibilities 1. Health Coordination and Casework · Provide a welcoming, trauma-informed and non-judgemental first point of contact for guests seeking health and wellbeing support. · Carry out structured triage conversations to identify health, housing, safety, safeguarding, mental health, addiction, income, resettlement and practical support needs. · Support guests to register with GPs, attend appointments, understand health information and navigate primary care services. · Coordinate access to health interventions delivered through WSUP and partner agencies, including Hepatitis C testing, TB screening, dental support, eye care, sexual health services, mental health outreach and addiction recovery pathways. · Support guests to access sexual health testing and referrals, mental health referrals, substance misuse support, welfare advice navigation and warm referrals into appropriate specialist services. · Make appropriate referrals to statutory, voluntary and specialist services, including housing, mental health, substance misuse, domestic abuse, welfare advice, safeguarding and emergency support. · Maintain regular follow-up with guests who may miss appointments, disengage or require repeated encouragement to access support. · Maintain accurate, confidential and GDPR-compliant records using WSUP’s case management systems. 2. Development of Women’s Service Provision · Lead the development and day-to-day oversight of WSUP’s women’s service provision, including Women’s Wednesday. · Ensure Women’s Wednesday provides a safe, welcoming, women-only, low-barrier community support space offering peer support, health coordination, wellbeing activities, welfare advice and community connection. · Work with women using WSUP services to co-produce activities and shape the ongoing development of the women’s programme. · Identify and respond to the specific needs of women experiencing homelessness, domestic abuse, unsafe housing, temporary accommodation, poor mental health, substance misuse, poverty, trauma, isolation or resettlement barriers. · Develop clear pathways into specialist support for women, including domestic abuse services, sexual health services, mental health support, substance misuse services, housing advice, welfare advice, safeguarding provision and emergency support. · Provide a trusted community hub for women who may not yet feel ready to engage with formal casework or statutory services. · Help women reduce isolation, build confidence, sustain community connections and gradually move towards more formal support where appropriate. · Monitor attendance, outcomes, feedback and emerging needs within the women’s service and report learning to WSUP’s leadership team. · Promote a psychologically safer environment for women who may have experienced trauma, stigma, exploitation, violence, exclusion or previous negative experiences of services. 3. Partnership Working · Build and maintain effective working relationships with local health, housing, recovery, advice, mental health, domestic abuse, women’s services and community partners. · Act as a key link between WSUP guests and external services, helping partners deliver support in a trusted community setting. · Support partner clinics, drop-ins and outreach sessions hosted at WSUP. · Coordinate warm referrals into specialist services and follow up with guests and partners where appropriate. · Attend relevant meetings, case discussions and multi-agency forums where appropriate. · Represent WSUP professionally and promote the organisation’s relational, dignity-led and trauma-informed approach. · Identify gaps in provision and work with WSUP leadership to develop new partnerships that respond to guest needs, including the needs of women accessing WSUP’s women-only provision. 4. Peer Support and Co-production · Work alongside volunteers with lived experience to provide safe, relational and purposeful support. · Help ensure peer volunteers understand safeguarding, boundaries, confidentiality, lone-working and referral procedures. · Contribute to volunteer briefings, debriefs and reflective practice where relevant. · Support quarterly co-production sessions with women using WSUP’s provision, enabling them to shape activities, share feedback and identify gaps in support. · Ensure feedback from guests and women using the service informs programme development, partnership working and service improvement. · Promote lived experience as a valued part of WSUP’s approach while ensuring appropriate support, supervision and boundaries are in place. 5. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting · Record triage, referrals, casework activity, attendance, outcomes and follow-up actions accurately. · Monitor attendance, health and welfare triage, referrals, partner services accessed, peer-support activity, safeguarding concerns, guest feedback and outcomes. · Collect feedback from guests, including women using Women’s Wednesday, to inform service development. · Contribute to internal reporting, case studies, impact evidence and partnership updates. · Use data and lived experience feedback to identify trends, unmet needs and service improvement opportunities. · Support WSUP’s Community Pulse approach by ensuring guest voice and co-production are embedded in health and women’s service development. Person Specification Essential Experience · Experience of working with people facing homelessness, rough sleeping, poverty, mental health challenges, addiction, trauma, domestic abuse, migration issues, social exclusion or multiple disadvantage. · Experience of providing one-to-one support, triage, casework, advocacy, signposting or referral support. · Experience of working with health, housing, mental health, substance misuse, domestic abuse, welfare or community support services. · Experience of managing risk, safeguarding concerns and sensitive personal information. · Experience of working in a person-centred, strengths-based and non-judgemental way. · Experience of supporting or developing services for women, particularly women affected by trauma, homelessness, domestic abuse, poor mental health or complex needs. · Experience of working with volunteers, peer supporters or people with lived experience is desirable but not essential. Essential Knowledge and Skills · Good understanding of health inequalities and the barriers faced by people experiencing homelessness or multiple disadvantage. · Ability to build trust with people who may have had poor experiences of statutory or mainstream services. · Strong communication, listening and interpersonal skills. · Ability to work calmly and confidently with people in distress or crisis. · Good understanding of safeguarding adults, confidentiality, professional boundaries and GDPR. · Ability to coordinate referrals and liaise effectively with external agencies. · Good organisational skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities and maintain accurate records. · Commitment to equality, diversity, inclusion and anti-discriminatory practice. · Understanding of trauma-informed practice and psychologically informed environments, or willingness to undertake training. · Understanding of the importance of women-only spaces, safety, choice and trust when working with women affected by trauma or multiple disadvantage. Desirable Experience, Knowledge and Qualifications · Experience of working in a women-only or gender-responsive service. · Experience of co-production, peer support or lived experience-led service design. · Experience of using case management systems · Knowledge of services and referral pathways in Greenwich and South East London. · Lived experience relevant to

item.title: Employment Advisor – Connect To Work
item.description: Do you want to support people with mental health issues in a moment of crisis? Are you calm, non-judgemental and able to work effectively with people experiencing distress? If you can embody our values of Hope , Courage , Togetherness , and Responsiveness , and want to help others build resilience and manage their wellbeing, we’d love to hear from you. Employment Advisor – Connect To Work (IPS Employment Advice) Reference: 350 Salary: £29,400 per annum (pro-rata for part time) Hours: 15 hours - 37.5 hours per week Contract: Permanent Working base(s): Watford, Hemel Hempstead or St. Albans with Herts countywide travel required. About the Service Herts Mind Network is a new delivery partner of Hertfordshire’s ‘Connect To Work’ programme, overseen by Step2Skills, Hertfordshire County Council. The Connect to Work programme has launched in Hertfordshire in August 2025 and is designed to support residents with disabilities, health conditions, or complex barriers into meaningful employment. This UK Government-funded programme is part of a nationwide effort to reduce economic inactivity and promote inclusive workplaces. Connect to Work is a personalised Supported Employment programme that pairs eligible individuals with dedicated Employment Advisors. About the Role We are seeking four highly motivated, organised and compassionate Employment Advisors, to deliver the countywide Connect To Work programme in our new Employment workstream. In this highly rewarding role, you will be responsible supporting individuals experiencing mental health problems, and those facing complex barriers, to secure and sustain meaningful paid employment. This position is part of the Connect to Work programme — a voluntary Supported Employment initiative funded by the Department for Work and Pensions. You will deliver the Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model, offering tailored advice and guidance to individuals, while also building strong partnerships with local employers to create opportunities aligned with individuals’ skills and aspirations. As an Employment Advisor you will deliver the Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model to meet individuals regularly to understand an individual’s skills, strengths and goals; developing clear action plans; provide practical support; and co-create personalised action plans. The programme provides structured, 1:1 and group based person centred support to build confidence, motivation and resilience, to help individuals work towards clear, work related goals. You will also engage with employers to identify suitable opportunities, arrange interviews, and offer ongoing support to both individuals and employers to promote successful job retention; whilst advocating for individuals to de-stigmatise mental health. You may also work with a small number of individuals who are already in work to sustain and thrive in their employment. As an Employment Advisor you will be responsible for: Delivering effective 1:1 and group person centred employment support to individuals looking for work Delivering effective 1:1 and group person centred employment support to individuals looking to continue with work Liaising with employers to seek opportunities for individuals Accurate and timely record keeping to demonstrate activity and impact Ensuring high-quality support is delivered at all times, aligned with HMN values We offer: Annual leave entitlement of 25 days per year pro rata, rising in increments to a max. of 29 days after 5 years employment (plus 8 days Bank Holidays) An additional day of leave each year for your birthday following completion of probation period. Ongoing training relevant to your role. An Employee Assistance Programme. Eligibility for blue light card. Health cover (after 6 months employment) - compensation payment for Optical, Dental, Chiropody and Therapy Treatments. Being able to drive and having access to your own vehicle (or equivalent) is essential for this role. Closing date for receipt of applications is Sunday 27th September 2026. Interviews to be held on Friday 9th October. You will be asked to prepare a 5 - 10 minute presentation to be submitted ahead of time. N.B . Please quote reference number 350 when completing your application for this role. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We want people from all backgrounds to apply, no matter your gender, disability, marital or parental status, race, colour, religion, or sexual orientation. We make sure everyone has a fair chance, especially those with disabilities or special needs. Hertfordshire Mind Network is committed to the Disability Confident and Mindful Employer charters. We actively recruit staff who have a lived experience of mental ill health. Our inclusive approach recognises the unique skills, knowledge, and perspectives that lived experience brings to our team. No agencies please.

item.title: Head of Network Development
item.description: UK Youth has launched an ambitious new strategy to widen the reach and deepen the impact of youth work and outdoor learning. At the heart of that strategy is a clear commitment: We Back Youth Work Leaders. As our new Head of Network Development, you will turn that commitment into action. You will lead the development and delivery of a powerful national offer that equips youth work leaders with the investment, support, relationships and connections they need to thrive. This includes leading our Grants+ approach—combining significant, multi-year grant funding with tailored organisational-development support—and developing partnerships that strengthen youth sector infrastructure locally, regionally and across the UK nations. This role is about much more than managing a network. We are evolving towards a more relational way of working: listening deeply to youth-work leaders, understanding the realities they face, involving them in shaping our work and building relationships founded on trust, respect and shared purpose. You will ensure organisations can access the right support, expertise and opportunities—and that their insight continually shapes UK Youth’s work. You will have the opportunity to lead the delivery of the £13 million UK Youth Fund, strengthen the resilience and effectiveness of grassroots youth organisations, and help create a more connected and equitable system of support for the wider sector. We are looking for someone with deep knowledge and experience of youth work and the youth sector—someone who can talk the talk and walk the walk with youth organisation leaders. You will bring substantial experience of the youth work sector and infrastructure, organisational development and capacity building, alongside the strategic and operational leadership needed to deliver significant grant-making activity and complex partnerships. You will be an inclusive and credible leader who can turn ambitious strategy into excellent delivery, bring people and organisations together, and remain focused on what youth work leaders need to succeed. Across the country, youth workers are changing—and often saving—young lives. This is your opportunity to ensure the people and organisations doing that vital work have the investment, infrastructure and support they deserve. Purpose of the job The Head of Network Development will lead the operationalisation of UK Youth’s new We Back Youth Work Leaders strategic pillar. The role will turn our ambition to equip youth-work leaders with the skills, networks and confidence to deliver exceptional support into a coherent network development offer—leading our Grants+ approach of multi-year funding alongside tailored organisational development, and strengthening youth-sector infrastructure locally, regionally and across the UK nations. Central to the role will be embedding UK Youth’s increasingly relational approach to its network: building trusted, mutually beneficial relationships with youth-work leaders; listening to and understanding their needs; involving them in shaping our support and connecting organisations to the right opportunities, expertise and infrastructure. Reporting to the Director of Network Delivery, the postholder will be responsible for translating this strategic ambition into high-quality, well-governed delivery, while ensuring that learning and insight from the network continually improve our work and contribute to securing sustainable investment in youth work and outdoor learning. Why work at UK Youth? Every young person deserves a youth worker. UK Youth exists to make that a reality. Our vision is a society that backs every young person - through each spark, struggle and success. As the UK’s national infrastructure body for youth work, we strengthen and champion a diverse network of youth organisations, unlock investment, shape policy and build the evidence base for what works. At a time of growing need and inequality of access, our work has never been more important. We are entering an exciting new phase of our strategy - focused on long-term resilience, income diversification and a transformational Capital Appeal to develop Avon Tyrrell as a national centre of excellence for outdoor learning. Joining UK Youth means being part of an ambitious, impact-driven organisation committed to strengthening youth work for generations to come. Key responsibilities Portfolio leadership and delivery Lead the strategic and operational delivery of UK Youth’s network development portfolio, translating organisational strategy and funded commitments into clear plans, outcomes, budgets, milestones and accountabilities. Ensure programmes and services are delivered to a high standard, on time and within budget, with effective governance, performance management, risk control and escalation to the Director of Network Delivery. Mobilise new initiatives and partnerships, establishing proportionate delivery models, systems, teams and governance arrangements. Lead continuous improvement across the portfolio, responding effectively to evidence, partner feedback, changing needs and the external environment. Be a champion of UK Youth’s network across all of UK Youth’s work. Grant making and organisational development Lead the delivery of UK Youth’s significant, multi-year grant-making portfolio, including the £13 million UK Youth Fund, ensuring responsible stewardship of charitable and restricted funds. Ensure effective management of the full grant lifecycle, including programme design, application and assessment, due diligence, decision-making, contracting, payments, monitoring, reporting, complaints and closure. Maintain robust and proportionate grant governance, financial controls, safeguarding assurance, risk management, data quality and compliance with funder and regulatory requirements. Lead an integrated organisational development offer alongside grant funding, enabling smaller youth and outdoor learning organisations to strengthen their financial sustainability, leadership, governance, workforce and resilience. Embed open, trusting, accessible and equitable grant-making practice, reducing unnecessary barriers while maintaining appropriate accountability. Network and sector infrastructure support Develop and deliver UK Youth’s approach to engaging, connecting and supporting our national network, informed by the needs and experiences of youth work leaders and organisations. Create opportunities for peer learning, collaboration, knowledge exchange and access to relevant support across the network. Lead major initiatives that strengthen youth sector infrastructure locally, regionally and nationally, working with partners to improve the consistency, coordination and accessibility of support. Support regional and national partners to understand need, develop shared plans and approaches, and deliver locally relevant infrastructure and organisational support. Work with the Communications Team and relevant colleagues to ensure network communications are timely, accessible, coordinated and purposeful. Experience we're after Substantial leadership experience within the youth sector, grounded in an in-depth understanding of youth work practice, youth work leadership and the realities facing youth organisations and their leaders. Experience of leading a complex, multi-year network development or comparable portfolio, translating strategy and funded commitments into successful delivery and managing significant budgets and risks. Experience of leading substantial grant making or onward funding activity, including governance, due diligence, financial oversight, risk and accountability. Substantial organisational development and capacity building experience, including diagnosing organisational needs and designing practical support that strengthens leadership, governance, financial sustainability, workforce and resilience. Experience of developing networks, partnerships or infrastructure across multiple organisations, regions or systems, with demonstrable credibility among youth organisation leaders. What we can offer you We offer a competitive range of benefits, good work/life balance, excellent learning and development opportunities and vibrant organisational culture: Flexible/Agile Working 27 days annual leave (24 days + 3 days winter closure) plus bank holidays (pro rata for part time employees) Funded training provided in; Safeguarding, GDPR, Information and Cyber Security & Equality & Diversity Other training available in support of your personal and professional development Pension scheme (currently UK Youth match employee contributions up to 5%) Membership of our life insurance scheme which would pay-out up to 4 times your salary Employee Assistance Programme to support employees both professionally and personally 20% discount off bookings at Avon Tyrrell, our New Forest Outdoor Centre, including camping, lodges and outdoor activities. IT equipment provided for the duration of contract CycleScheme and TechScheme How to apply If you would like to be considered for this fantastic opportunity, please complete an application via our completely anonymised recruitment system provided by Applied which looks to create a fair and unbiased application process for all. Scroll to the top of the page and start your application. Closing date: 29th September 2026 at 09:00 Provisional First Stage Interview Dates: 5th & 6th October 2026 Provisional Final Stage Interview Dates (in person): 9th October 2026 As this role involves working in a regulated environment with young people, any offer will be conditional to satisfactory background checks, which include criminal record check and employment reference. Please note CVs will be reviewed as the first stage of the recruitment process. Candidates who are shortlisted following the CV review will then have their sift questions assessed. Only candidates who meet the requirements at both stages will progress further in the recruitment process.

item.title: Music & Culture Manager
item.description: If you have spent years in the creative industries building capital and are looking for somewhere to bring that expertise to bear, this is a route into the NGO world that does not ask you to leave your sector behind. This role is for someone working anywhere across the creative industries - music, film, art, gaming, sport, literature - who wants to put their skills and connections to work for the planet, and to develop a specialism at the intersection of culture and environmental advocacy. The legal work is at the centre of what ClientEarth does. The cultural work builds the understanding, the pressure and the relationships that help it land. This role sits in that space. There is real ownership here: your own projects, your own relationships, your own contributions. The work will regularly take you to events, evenings, industry forums and there is a generous time off in lieu policy to reflect that. Office attendance in our London office is 20% of the month. Full time preferred but we may consider 4 days a week, with salary adjusted on a pro rata basis. Important dates to note: Deadline to submit an initial application: 27th of September If your profile passes initial screening, you will be asked to submit additional information in the form of three additional questions. The deadline to submit your answers is the 29th of September If we do not receive a response to these questions by the deadline we will assume you are no longer interested in the role. Interviews will take place on the 17th, 19th and 20th of October. Please also review the "Our Hiring Process" section at the bottom of this advert to learn more about the stages involved for this specific role. Key Responsibilities Identify and develop a broad portfolio of cultural relationships and supporters across music, arts, film, TV, gaming, literature, books and sport, drawing on your own network and ClientEarth's existing relationships, working in close collaboration with the team lead Project manage the Music & Culture team's contribution to major international advocacy and campaigning moments across the year (e.g. COP, Climate Week NYC, London Climate Action Week, individual and innovative campaigning moments around case launches and similar) Collaborate with colleagues across the organisation to identify how cultural engagement, partnerships and influential voices can help advance advocacy, communications, fundraising and programme objectives, agreeing priorities with the team lead. Represent ClientEarth in discussions with senior cultural leaders, talent representatives, institutions and strategic partners, consulting the team lead before significant negotiations or commitments and exercising judgement and diplomacy in managing sensitive stakeholder relationships See the job description for a full list of duties for this role. Skills, Knowledge & Expertise A career background in the creative industries with your own established network and contacts in the sector Strong written communication skills: experience producing clear, compelling copy for a range of audiences and formats, whether internal reports, external communications, brochures, proposals or editorial content Proven track record of building and managing relationships with senior or influential figures in the creative industries An understanding of how creative industries work from the inside and knowing how to make the right people feel this organisation is worth their time See the job description for a full list of requirements for this role. Job Benefits Flexible working : We are proud to be a Flexa accredited Employer. Visit our Flexa Employer page for more information on our approach to flexible working. Our flexible working policy allows our people the choice to decide to work from home/another location in the country where their contract of employment is issued for 80% of their month, with the other 20% of their month being office-based. See our benefits page for more: Benefits | ClientEarth Careers as well as our flexible working FAQ. ClientEarth values diversity and inclusion and the benefits this brings. We aim to appoint the most suitable candidate at all times and welcome applications from people from all different backgrounds. See our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) at ClientEarth | ClientEarth journey page for more. Please note that ClientEarth is only able to employ those who have the pre-existing legal right to work in the UK. ClientEarth is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice or legal services to third parties.
