item.title: Head of Executive Office and Communications
item.description: Work where it matters most, achieve what matters more Be part of a team where passion meets purpose, as we work together where the challenge is greatest to change the lives and build the futures of children and young people. Ormiston Academies Trust is looking for an exceptional Head of Executive Office and Communications to sit at the heart of our organisation — running our Executive Office and shaping how we communicate with 45 schools, our staff, and the wider world. In this dual role, you'll act as trusted adviser to our CEO and Deputy CEO, managing correspondence, priorities and special projects across the Trust. You'll lead our entire communications agenda including internal, external, press and public affairs, building a strategy that helps every one of our schools feel connected to our mission, and that raises Ormiston's voice and influence across the education sector. You'll work closely with our National Leadership Group, Principals and senior leaders, and you'll have real scope to shape how a large, multi-layered organisation talks to itself and to the outside world. About you You'll bring senior leadership experience, ideally gained managing a press office or public affairs function, and you'll be confident operating as a trusted adviser to CEO-level and Principal-level stakeholders. You'll have a track record managing communications across multiple channels in a large, complex organisation, and be a confident user of technology and AI, with a clear view of how AI will change communications and administration. Experience in education, the public sector, or working with ministers, regulators or national media would be an advantage, but isn't essential. Strong writing and interpersonal skills are essential, along with the ability to distil complex information for different audiences and communicate it clearly and simply. You'll bring calm, decisive leadership under pressure, including experience managing high-profile issues or reputational risk. This role requires you to combine excellent project management with the ability to build and sustain relationships across an organisation and beyond it. Above all, you'll bring a genuine commitment to Ormiston's mission and values, and the creativity and critical thinking to solve problems in a fast-paced, changing environment. About Ormiston Academies Trust Our vision is to create a school system where every child thrives, regardless of background. Our people are at the heart of our approach – they are our greatest asset. We exist to provide the best learning opportunities every day, in every school for every child. It is the people and teams in our Trust who make this a reality and ensure we have the greatest impact. If you join us at Ormiston, whatever your role, you can be sure of a role with purpose and meaning. Ormiston, where every member of staff enjoys… The opportunity to build on the legacy of those who came before – being part of one of the longest standing Trusts, created with the sole purpose of enabling children and young people to thrive Working for a Trust nationally recognised for its impact on disadvantaged children – a rewarding, stimulating career where staff are challenged to be the best they can be, for the pupils we are proud to serve Being part of a team and community where you belong – receiving bespoke and holistic support from a well-resourced and ambitious network of experts and professionals that work at the heart of communities A supportive environment to grow your career – an extensive professional development programme, alongside flexible working arrangements and generous benefits Benefits that care for you We value your hard work and dedication, and we're committed to ensuring you feel supported, both professionally and personally so that you are in the best position to make the most impact for the children and young people in our schools. When you join us at Ormiston, you can be certain that your work will have purpose and meaning. You can also expect robust and holistic support from us to enable you to excel in your role. You will have access to an attractive benefits package including: 30 days annual leave (rising to 32 days after 5 years' service) Generous pension and life cover Access to health and well-being programmes, including a counselling service. Discounts on retail, travel, and leisure through our benefits platform. Free and confidential legal, tax and health 24/7 helpline. Cycle to work scheme. Automatic pay progression. Flexible working arrangements. And much more as part of a leading multi-academy trust. If you have any questions about the role please contact our recruitment team. The closing date for applications is 25 September 2026 with interviews due to take place the week commencing 5 October 2026. Early applications are encouraged as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early should a suitable candidate be found.
item.dc:creator: Ormiston Academies Trust

item.title: Administration, Governance and Facilities Officer
item.description: As the Administration, Governance & Facilities Officer , you will play a pivotal role in supporting the effective operation of the Joseph Levy Foundation. Working closely with the Executive Director, you will provide high-quality administrative, governance and facilities support, ensuring the Foundation operates efficiently and meets its governance and operational responsibilities. This is a varied and hands-on role in a small, values-led organisation, offering the opportunity to work across board and committee administration, governance support, office and facilities management, organisational administration and stakeholder coordination. You will act as the primary point of contact for governance administration, supporting Trustees and the Executive Director by coordinating meetings, preparing board papers, producing accurate minutes and maintaining governance records. Alongside governance responsibilities, you will oversee the day-to-day administration and facilities functions of the Foundation, ensuring the office operates smoothly and systems and records are maintained. You will also contribute to improving administrative processes and embedding efficient ways of working across the organisation. Key Responsibilities Administration Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Executive Director and, where required, the Chair and Trustees. Prepare letters, reports, presentations and other documents. Manage the Foundation's shared email inbox and correspondence. Update and maintain electronic filing systems, including SharePoint. Maintain accurate organisational, governance and grant records. Support the Foundation's governance administration. Meetings & Coordination Organise meetings, including Board and Trustee meetings, and prepare agendas and meeting papers. Attend Board meetings, producing accurate minutes and action logs. Support the organisation of Foundation events, workshops and meetings. Office & Facilities Maintain a safe, organised and welcoming office environment. Order and monitor office supplies and equipment. Welcome visitors and assist with the day-to-day running of the office. Open and close the office on your working days. Liaise with suppliers and contractors to support the smooth operation of the office. General Responsibilities Build positive working relationships with colleagues, trustees, suppliers and external stakeholders. Maintain confidentiality and handle information appropriately. Work in accordance with the Foundation's values, policies and procedures. Contribute to improving administrative processes and ways of working. Carry out any other duties appropriate to the role. Person Specification We recognise that people develop their skills and experience through many different pathways and do not expect applicants to meet every area listed below. We are particularly interested in people who bring experience of administration, governance and office operations, together with the ability to build positive relationships, manage competing priorities and support the effective running of a small, values-led organisation. Experience Experience of providing administrative support to senior leaders, Boards or Trustees. Experience of coordinating meetings, including preparing agendas, meeting papers and supporting documentation. Experience of producing accurate minutes and maintaining action logs. Experience of coordinating office administration and facilities. Experience of maintaining accurate records and using digital systems to support administration. Skills Able to organise and prioritise a varied workload. Able to communicate effectively with a range of stakeholders. Able to produce accurate work with attention to detail. Able to build positive working relationships with colleagues, Trustees, suppliers and external stakeholders. Able to work independently, use initiative and exercise sound judgement. Able to identify and escalate issues appropriately. Able to contribute to improving administrative processes and ways of working. Knowledge Knowledge of governance processes and Board or Trustee administration. Knowledge of office administration and facilities management. Knowledge of digital systems used to support administration and collaboration. Knowledge of the importance of handling confidential information appropriately. Personal Attributes Proactive and adaptable in your approach to work. Willing to learn and develop new skills. Committed to the Foundation's values. Other Requirements Able to work 2.5 days per week from the Foundation's office in Edgware Road, London, starting at 9am on working days. Legal right to work in the UK. Willing to complete an Enhanced DBS check before appointment. Recruitment Timeline Applications open: Wednesday 9th September Applications close: Sunday 27th September Interviews (in person at our office in Marylebone, London): w/c 5th October Job details Salary: £35 - £37k FTE (£17,500 - £18,750 pro rata) Contract: Part-time, 18.75 hours (2.5 days per week) Location: Office based, Edgware Road, London Reports to: Executive Director Equity and Inclusion The Joseph Levy Foundation is committed to building an inclusive and equitable workplace where everyone feels welcomed, valued and able to thrive. We actively encourage applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives, particularly those who are underrepresented in the charity sector. We recognise that people develop their skills through many different pathways and welcome applications from candidates whose experience has been gained through employment, volunteering, education or lived experience. About us The Joseph Levy Foundation is an independent grant-making charitable organisation with a long-standing commitment to funding smaller, grassroots organisations. With an endowment of around £23m, our annual commitment in grants in recent years has averaged £500,000. We have recently embedded an ambitious strategy which aims to find, fund and support organisations and individuals who have ambitious ideas to help young people experiencing disadvantage. In tandem with our strategy review, we have undergone a comprehensive change process, which includes refreshing our processes and embedding an equitable grant making procedure. As we enter the midpoint of the new strategy we will continue to be ambitious by introducing a Young Advisory Board to guide our work and to coach and support charity leaders of the future. This continued commitment will see the Foundation lead with its values which are: Connectivity and collaboration Innovation and imagination Engagement and Joy for life
item.dc:creator: Joseph Levy Foundation

item.title: Resourcing Coordinator (Maternity Cover)
item.description: Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF) is seeking an organised and creative MAF in the Community (MiC) Resourcing Coordinator to support our vital resourcing and community fundraising work across the UK. This is a rewarding opportunity for a dedicated administrator to use their skills to equip our staff, volunteers and church representatives, helping them inspire new donors and supporters to get behind our life-changing work. Location: Folkestone or Glasgow (with hybrid working) Contract: 12 month, fixed-term maternity contract As an MAF in the Community (MiC) Resourcing Coordinator, you will support the day-to-day delivery of MiC UK’s resourcing and community fundraising activities. Working under the direction of the MiC Resourcing Lead, you will help develop and maintain engaging resources for churches, volunteers and other stakeholders, ensuring they have the materials and information they need to promote MAF and attract new donors and supporters. You will also support the development of community fundraising plans, campaigns and supporter engagement, providing groups and individuals with resources and advice to help maximise fundraising income and attract new supporters. Additionally, you will: - Gather content for quarterly MiC Church newsletters - Update volunteer, website, e-news and social media content - Help develop new church and audience engagement resources - Assist with the planning and delivery of MiC UK events - Manage queries and meeting and speaking engagement paperwork About You To be considered as an MAF in the Community (MiC) Resourcing Coordinator, you will need: - Experience in an administrative role - Experience of working in an office environment - Proficiency in Microsoft applications - The ability to communicate positively, assertively and sensitively within a cross-functional team environment - An efficient and organised approach - The ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities - Excellent attention to detail - The ability to work on your own initiative - Creativity and innovation - At a minimum, A-levels or equivalent experience About Us Mission Aviation Fellowship (MAF) is a Christian organisation that uses light aircraft to deliver practical help, physical healing and spiritual hope to some of the world’s most remote and inaccessible communities. For 80 years, MAF has been working in partnership with hundreds of other organisations to enable access to medical care, education, livelihood training and long-term support in over 24 low-income countries. They believe that every community, however remote, should have access to the essentials of life – that’s why MAF’s flights are a lifeline, not a luxury. The Benefits - Salary of £28,701.28 per annum - Annual leave entitlement of 22 days per year plus 8 paid public holidays per year - Non-contributory pension scheme (10% of salary); employees may make voluntary additional contributions - Death in service payment - Flexible working policy - Access to our Employee Assistance Programme This is a rewarding opportunity for an organised administrator with experience to join our purpose-driven Christian organisation. You’ll enjoy a varied role spanning resourcing, community fundraising, events and communications, giving you the chance to broaden your experience, put your creativity to great use and develop a diverse range of skills. Perhaps most rewarding of all, your work will help equip the people who champion MAF across the UK, supporting them to reach new audiences and inspire more people to get behind our life-changing work around the world.
item.dc:creator: Mission Aviation Fellowship UK

item.title: Learning Disability & Neurodiversity Carers Service Coordinator
item.description: Job description Are you passionate about making a difference to the lives of unpaid carers? Join the Carers’ Hub team and help create lasting, positive change for carers across Lambeth. In this rewarding role, you will lead our Learning Disability & Neurodiversity Carers Service . You’ll have the freedom to be creative, working directly with carers to co-design and deliver a vibrant programme of 1-to-1 support, peer groups, and social activities. What you’ll be doing: Shape & Deliver Support: Build a trusted programme of 1-to-1 advice, peer support, and social events for adults caring for someone with a learning disability and/or neurodiversity. Collaborate: Listen to carers' ideas and turn them into practical, impactful activities. Empower Communities: Motivate and inspire carers to connect, facilitating group discussions and building a welcoming environment. What we are looking for: A Champion for Carers: A genuine passion for supporting unpaid carers and improving their wellbeing. A People Person: Confidence in facilitating group discussions and the ability to connect comfortably with a diverse range of people. Organised & Autonomous: Exceptional organisational skills, with the confidence to make decisions, solve problems, and use your initiative within a small, friendly team. About Carers' Hub Lambeth Unpaid carers often make huge sacrifices to look after loved ones, frequently at the expense of their own wellbeing. At Carers' Hub, we work to limit these financial, emotional, and educational challenges. We achieve this through four core workstreams: Raising awareness of the vital role carers play. Influencing local policy through community engagement. Improving carer wellbeing directly. Connecting carers to each other, support networks, and training. Ready to apply? Please download our Job Pack for the full person specification and details on how to apply. We look forward to hearing from you! Closing date: 9am Wednesday 7th October Interviews will take place on Wednesday 14th October at 336 Brixton Road Posted on: 09 September 2026 Closing date: 07 October 2026 at 09:00 Tags: Advice / Information, Autism, Engagement / Outreach, Learning Disability, Social / Support Work The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Sanctuary Operations Manager
item.description: Dean Farm Trust is seeking an experienced and compassionate Sanctuary Operations Manager to take responsibility for the day-to-day leadership and operational management of our 32-acre animal sanctuary near Chepstow. Home to 200 rescued animals, including pigs, cows, sheep, goats, equines and birds, Dean Farm Trust provides a home for life to animals in need. This is a senior, hands-on leadership role with animal welfare at its heart. The Sanctuary Operations Manager will lead our on-site team, working through our Team Leaders to ensure the Sanctuary operates safely, effectively and to the highest standards of animal welfare. The role will oversee staffing and rotas, volunteer development, recruitment and training, budgets and resources, facilities and maintenance, land and pasture management, health and safety, compliance, contractors, projects and the operational delivery of Sanctuary events and activities. We are looking for someone with strong leadership and people-management experience who is confident managing a busy operational environment and developing both staff and volunteers. You will need to be organised, practical and able to balance the immediate demands of running a sanctuary with longer-term planning and improvement. This is an important appointment for Dean Farm Trust as we strengthen our operational structure and build a sustainable future for the Sanctuary. The successful candidate will work closely with the Director and Trustees while taking real ownership of Sanctuary operations and providing strong, consistent on-site leadership. A genuine commitment to animal welfare and to the values of Dean Farm Trust is essential. Please read our full Candidate Pack before applying. It includes the complete Job Description, information about Dean Farm Trust and further background on why we are recruiting for this role now.
item.dc:creator: Dean Farm Trust

item.title: Monitoring and Data Officer
item.description: For over 20 years, Village Water has been committed to transforming lives in Africa by delivering vital support in safe water, sanitation and hygiene education (WASH) to rural communities in Zambia and Mozambique. Collaborating with local partners, we reach the most marginalised populations in villages, schools, and health centres improving health and empowering communities with opportunities to thrive. The Role As the Monitoring & Data Officer, you’ll support the Monitoring & Data Manager and Coordinator to validate, clean, and manage programme data. You’ll review submissions for accuracy and completeness, resolve discrepancies, and help ensure the integrity of the data that underpins our impact. Your work will support evidence-based decision-making. Collaboration and attention to detail are key, as is a passion for improving lives in rural Zambia and Mozambique. Your Responsibilities: Validate and clean incoming data from local partners, identifying and flagging any errors or inconsistencies using tools such as Excel and Salesforce. Conduct regular (weekly and monthly) checks on submitted data to ensure accuracy and assess progress against set targets. Maintain and update all impact data, ensuring all records are accurate and complete. Assist in testing and reviewing both new and existing data systems to ensure proper functionality, support the addition of new fields and adjustments as needed. Support data validation during data collection rounds by reviewing data collection tools. Liaise with local partners and internal teams to clarify discrepancies or follow up on incomplete submissions. Be proactive in helping strengthen the monitoring systems. About You We're looking for someone who is passionate about the cause and excited to make a meaningful impact. Your experience will include: Work collaboratively with staff & volunteers supporting them to achieve Village Water's goals. Support other fundraising initiatives, as required. Sharing skills and knowledge with colleagues All staff have a responsibility for safeguarding and must undergo the required training to ensure compliance with the organisation's safeguarding policies. Interest in and commitment to Village Water’s mission and the vital role of overseas aid. Comfortable managing a diverse workload with minimum supervision. Flexible and supportive Excellent Excel & IT skills Excellent attention to detail Why Village Water: We are a small, dynamic team that values our personal touch, collaborative approach, and unwavering commitment to driving positive change. You'll work alongside passionate individuals who are making a tangible difference in people's lives every day. Equality and Diversity Village Water is dedicated to promoting a workplace that embraces inclusivity, values diversity, and honours the unique contributions of its employees and partners. It ensures equal treatment for all individuals and encourages everyone to reach their full potential. Village Water is an advocate for disability inclusion, so if you require alternative application methods, please get in touch with us for further assistance. Closing date: 4th October 2026 17:00
item.dc:creator: Village Water

item.title: Self-Employed Mental Health Advocate
item.description: Are you passionate about people’s rights?! We are looking to recruit Self-Employed Mental Health Advocates to work in the following areas: - Gloucester (GL2 9EE) - Birmingham (B13 8QE) - Northamptonshire (NN5 6UD) - Cambridge (CB21 5EE) - Luton (LU4 0LU) - Kent (TN12 0ER) - Greater Manchester (M46 9NT & M6 7DU) - Warrington (WA2 8TR) - Huyton (L36 5SA) -West Yorkshire (BD20 6TU) - Wrexham (LL11 1BU) - Aberbeeg (NP13 2DA) This is a self-employed position and you will be paid a sessional rate. Our Service NYAS provides mental health advocacy to individuals within mental health settings throughout the UK. Our service provides independent advocacy to people within mental health hospitals and community-based settings. We support individuals to ensure their voice is heard regarding their care and treatment and that they are aware of their rights. This also includes representing them during various meetings such as ward rounds and at multi-disciplinary team meetings. This role requires you to produce written reports to ensure that the views of patients are fully represented. We work with adults and children and young people. DO YOU HAVE: Direct experience of working with children/young people or vulnerable adults in a social care or mental health setting. Experience and understanding of child protection/vulnerable adult safeguarding procedures Ability to maintain professionalism at all times An understanding of the importance of listening to children/young people and vulnerable adults without bias or prejudice. Ability to communicate in an effective way. Ability to record concise case notes and produce good quality reports You will need to evidence your skills using specific examples in your application meeting the criteria in the person specification. Safeguarding and Training You will be required to complete annual safeguarding and compliance training including, Personal Safety, Data Protection, Information Security, Safeguarding and Equality and Diversity. You will be able to subscribe to an e-learning platform provided by NYAS. The platform will provide you with the opportunity to undertake a number of other professional courses that you can complete in your own time to maintain your own CPD. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early once we receive a high number of applications. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer, and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. item.title: Self-Employed Independent Mental Health Advocate
item.description: Are you passionate about the rights of people with mental health problems in inpatient and residential settings? Are you able to challenge others on their behalf? Do you want to make a difference to their lives? About the Service NYAS provides mental health advocacy to patients at hospitals throughout the UK. Our service provides independent advocacy to patients within locked secure hospitals and community-based settings where we ensure that patients who are admitted are given a voice to make sure their rights are upheld. We provide advocacy support for patients with mental health issues and learning disabilities at times when it is important for their wishes and opinions to be heard and their feelings expressed, for instance, representing them during discharge meetings, ward rounds and at multi-disciplinary team meetings. The primary users of our services are vulnerable adults however some settings do include working with children and young people. The Vacancy We are looking to recruit a Self-Employed Independent Mental Health Advocate to work in the following areas: - Birmingham (B13 8QE) - Northamptonshire (NN5 6UD) - Luton (LU4 0LU) - Kent (TN12 0ER) - Greater Manchester (M46 9NT) - Warrington (WA2 8TR) We are looking to recruit Self-employed Independent Mental health advocates to provide independent and confidential mental health advocacy to qualifying patients and work to agreed outcomes with the patients promoting an understanding of outcomes and options available to them. You will be expected to work in line with Mental Health Act 1983 code of practice and will be required to produce written reports with the purpose of ensuring the views of the patient is fully represented. For more information, please view the attached contract delivery specification. Please note: In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the contract delivery specification below. Requirements include: Proven practice experience in delivering direct work to children, young people and vulnerable adults in a social care or mental health setting Experience and understanding of child protection/vulnerable adult safeguarding procedures Ability to maintain professionalism at all times An understanding of the importance of listening to children, young people and vulnerable adults without bias or prejudice with a strong commitment to support and develop and opportunities for children, young people and vulnerable adults to engage with the service. If you do not hold the IMHA Qualificaton City and Guilds 3614, we would expect the successful candidate to commit to undertaking the training after being in the role for 6 months, with the expectation of completing this within 12 months after starting the course' You will be required to complete annual safeguarding and compliance including, Personal Safety, Data Protection, Information Security, Safeguarding and Equality and Diversity. You will be able to subscribe to an e-learning platform provided by NYAS. The platform will provide you with the opportunity to undertake a number of other professional courses that you can complete in your own time to maintain your own CPD. You can do this on the e-learning platform at a significantly reduced cost compared to undertaking each course individually with different providers. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early once we receive a high number of applications. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change lives.

item.title: Philanthropy and Partnerships Manager (Maternity cover)
item.description: About the Role Our small Fundraising team has benefitted from significant investment in recent years and this maternity cover role will provide vital continuity as EIA develops and expands its network of philanthropic supporters and strategic partners. You will be joining EIA at a pivotal time, working closely with the Head of Fundraising to sustain momentum across philanthropy, support the launch of our giving circle, Nature Network, and help strengthen selected partnership opportunities that contribute to our fundraising ambitions. The fundraising team at EIA, is responsible for raising income across trusts and statutory funders, as well as raising funds from individuals. The income raised from individuals has increased in recent years and we are investing further in this area so that we can conduct even more investigative and campaigning work to protect our planet. The role will focus on developing and strengthening relationships with High Net Worth Individuals (HNWIs), inspiring supporters to give generously, and stewarding donors so they feel closely connected to EIA’s work to combat environmental crime and abuse around the world, as well as supporting partnership activity where it aligns with philanthropic giving, cultivation and long-term relationship development. The Philanthropy and Partnerships Manager (Maternity cover) will lead the day-to-day delivery of EIA’s philanthropy programme during the maternity cover period. This will include tailored stewardship for HNWIs, prospecting and cultivation, donor funding propositions, implementing and growing the Nature Network giving circle following its launch in September, engaging our network of ambassadors, Future Stewards, and maintaining effective systems to support growth in philanthropy. The role will also contribute to a focused partnerships pipeline, ensuring partnership activity supports philanthropic income growth and deepens engagement with EIA’s mission. Key areas of responsibility Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following: Development of the existing supporter base: Develop and deliver a tailored stewardship programme for higher level donors. Establish appropriate KPIs to track progress and measure success. Expand the donor base by acquiring new high value prospects: Conduct regular prospecting and cultivation to identify new potential supporters. Use network mapping to identify potential connections with existing stakeholders. Lead the development and delivery of cultivation events and exploratory meetings. Develop donor funding propositions: Work with campaign teams and the wider fundraising team to develop funding propositions for HNWI and a Case for Support for the different areas of our work. Launch and develop Nature Network and associated stewardship: Following the September launch of Nature Network, EIA’s giving circle, recruit new members and provide a compelling stewardship journey for supporters giving at this level. Support aligned partnerships activity: Maintain and develop a focused pipeline of prospective partners where there is clear alignment with EIA’s campaigns, values and philanthropic priorities. Work with the Head of Fundraising and colleagues to support partnership cultivation, proposal development and stewardship. Lead the prospecting and stewardship of our brand ambassador programme, Future Stewards, including developing a social media communications plan with the Social Media and Digital Engagement Manager Strategy development, budgeting and campaign reporting: Work with the Head of Fundraising to deliver philanthropy plans during the maternity cover period and contribute to wider fundraising strategy where relevant. Monitor income and expenditure across philanthropy, Nature Network and relevant partnership activity to ensure they meet budget and contribute to the mid-year reforecast process. Produce regular income reports that monitor performance against KPIs and feed back to the Head of Fundraising and wider organisation to share successes with the EIA team. Person Specification Essential Significant experience of identifying, cultivating and stewarding relationships with high value supporters and securing significant gifts. Considerable experience of developing and communicating high value funding propositions and writing compelling cases for support and applications. Strong verbal communication skills, confident in communicating effectively and passionately with supporters, team members across EIA and senior stakeholders. Excellent networking and presentation skills. Experience of planning and delivering stewardship events for HNWIs. Experience of managing or supporting giving circles, membership-style donor programmes or structured supporter journeys would be advantageous. Experience of partnership development, corporate relationships or cross-sector collaboration, with the ability to identify opportunities that support philanthropic income growth. Driven to provide the very best supporter experience. Energetic self-starter able to work on own initiative with attention to detail. Dynamic and positive attitude. Creative and innovative thinker. Well-organised, able to prioritise work and meet deadlines. Fully proficient in Microsoft SharePoint and Office 365. Fully proficient in Fundraising databases (CharityCRM would be an advantage but not essential) Solid knowledge of Charity Law and Fundraising regulations Strong interest in or knowledge of wildlife trade and environmental issues Flexibility to work out of hours at a few events through the year.

Our community of volunteer engineers design and create equipment when no commercial alternative exists – at no charge to the individuals we help. We are looking for an experienced Fundraising Manager to focus on leading and developing a diverse programme of fundraising activities that will generate sustainable income and support the organisation’s very compelling cause. REMAP is unique. item.title: Individual Giving and Legacies Manager
item.description: This role is based at the National Greyhound Centre, Horley, Surrey, RH6 9SX, with a minimum of three days in the office and the option to work two days from home. Job role: Each year, thousands of greyhounds across the UK rely on the generosity of supporters of the Greyhound Trust to find safe, loving homes. With an annual income of around £4.5 million, individual giving and gifts in Wills is central to our income generation strategy and this role lead its growth and development. This role is perfect for an experienced fundraiser ready to own the individual giving and gift in Wills strategy end to end. You will set the direction for donor communications, appeals and the legacy pipeline, taking responsibility for income from individual donors and KPIs while working closely with the Head of Income Generation and Engagement to contribute to the overall income generation and engagement strategy. You will take the lead in developing, testing, learning and growing the direct marketing programme and developing supporter journeys both online and offline. You’ll develop our email marketing and online supporter journeys for now and the future. This is a broad, varied role, for a senior fundraiser. Whether your background is strongest in individual giving, community fundraising, legacies, digital or data, if you are a confident communicator with proven experience of owning fundraising strategy, income and supplier relationships ready to take your next step in animal welfare, this is the role for you. Key responsibilities: Lead the development of the individual giving and legacies strategy and annual planning, budgeting and KPIs, reporting performance to the Head of Income Generation. Set the direction for a sustainable individual giving programme, growing the supporter base across all channels and developing strategies to engage and motivate supporters. Own the planning and delivery of engaging, multi-channel fundraising campaigns and appeals. Provide advice and support to branches for one-off lottery or other individual giving initiatives; ensuring compliance with our gambling commission licence nationally and through branches. Lead the ongoing development of the charity’s programme of appeals, regular giving and sponsorship products, lottery and donor development programmes. Maximise digital fundraising opportunities whilst recognising the contribution of non-digital approaches for certain audiences and product types. Own email marketing and online supporter journeys. Lead the legacy giving and in-memory fundraising strategy. Own monthly analysis of income and expenditure against KPIs, reporting on progress and forecasting future results. Design and implement a stewardship programme with particular attention to supporter journeys for new and existing supporters that increase average values and long-term support. Own compliance of the individual giving programme, identifying and managing risk and escalating to the Head of Income Generation and Engagement where necessary. Ensure data collection, management, use, storage and destruction comply with data protection law and best practice. Work closely with other members of staff and senior managment to ensure individual giving products and initiatives are integrated with other areas of the charity, such as brand and marketing programmes, retail development and homing campaigns. Own direct relationships with external suppliers, agencies and freelancers, setting briefs, managing budgets and holding them to account. Act as the organisation’s senior specialist on individual giving and legacies, advising and influencing colleagues, volunteers and homing centres on how their roles can support fundraising opportunities, without formal line authority. Essential skills and experience: Experience of working in a senior individual giving, direct marketing, community, or general fundraising role. Demonstrable track record of delivering sustained income growth and establishing new programmes of activity. Experience owning a budget and KPI set, forecasting, reporting to senior management and adjusting plans in response to performance. Proven ability to get the best out of external suppliers and agencies (copywriters, designers, mailing houses, platform developers, etc.) to maximise outcomes, setting budgets and holding suppliers to account for results. Demonstrable experience of donor development, journeys and stewardship at a strategic level. Proficient written and verbal communicator with the ability to adapt tone to engage and inspire different audiences and write compelling fundraising copy. Excellenet relationship and influencing skills with the ability to gain buy in and shape the approach of colleagues without formal authority over them. Excellent stewardship skills with the ability to communicate with supporters via letter, email, telephone and face to face with care and compassion. Able to plan and prioritise independently across several income streams. Track record of writing clear, engaging supporter communications (appeals, newsletters, thank you journeys). Confident using data to select, segment, or report on supporter groups. Experience managing ongoing relationships with individuals (donors, supporters or clients). Experience of legacy marketing. Proficiency in using a CRM to manage donor relationships and supporter journeys. Strong working knowledge of charity law, GDPR and the Fundraising Code of Practice with experience of ensuring organisational compliance. A collaborative approach and willingness to develop new areas of fundraising. Desirable experience and qualifications: Relevant fundraising or marketing qualification (e.g. Institute of Fundraising / CIOF certificate, CIM), or evidence of ongoing professional development. Experience of legacy marketing, legacy administration, or legacy pipeline management. Experience of writing or approving legacy-specific communications (in-memory, will-writing campaigns, pledger updates). Experience designing and evaluating acquisition or retention campaigns and activity across a variety of offline and digital channels. Experience of building or improving email marketing programmes or automated supporter journeys. Experience of working with fundraising databases (e.g. Raiser's Edge, Donorfy, Beacon) and GDPR-compliant data handling. Experience of liaising with solicitors, executors, or handling sensitive/bereavement-related conversations. Experience of managing a pipeline or CRM-tracked process from enquiry through to completion. Have empathy and enthusiasm for the mission of the Greyhound Trust. You will be required to work or provide support outside of standard working hours for events and operational needs, so flexibility is key. This post and its role requirement will develop with the needs of the charity.

item.title: Senior Principal Gifts Manager
item.description: Senior Principal Gifts Manager – The British Museum – Location: London – Salary: £54,000 Help shape one of the most ambitious cultural transformation projects of our generation. The British Museum is embarking on a landmark £1.3 billion Masterplan, reimagining one of the world's most iconic cultural institutions for the 21st century while preserving its unique role as a museum for everyone. To support this vision, we are launching a major philanthropic campaign with a target of raising £500 million+. We are seeking an exceptional Senior Principal Gifts Manager to secure transformational philanthropic support from leading UK and international donors. Working closely with senior leadership, trustees and campaign volunteers, you will develop and manage relationships with principal-level philanthropists, guiding complex donor journeys and securing significant multi-year gifts. Key Responsibilities ▪ Manage a portfolio of principal gift prospects and donors. ▪ Develop and deliver strategies to secure transformational philanthropic commitments. ▪ Lead peer-to-peer fundraising activity with senior stakeholders and volunteers. ▪ Establish and manage the Masterplan Campaign Board. ▪ Coordinate complex fundraising projects across the Museum and wider stakeholder network. ▪ Build compelling cases for support aligned to the Museum's strategic priorities. About You You will be an accomplished fundraising professional with a proven track record of securing major gifts, ideally within the arts, culture, heritage, charity or higher education sectors. You will combine exceptional relationship-building and influencing skills with strong project management expertise, strategic thinking and the confidence to engage high-profile donors and senior stakeholders. Why Join Us? This is a rare opportunity to play a leading role in one of the most significant fundraising campaigns in the cultural sector, helping secure the future of a world-renowned institution that cares for over eight million objects spanning human history. For an informal and confidential discussion, please speak with our advisors at Berwick Partners: William Pringle Partner, Head of Charity, Arts, Culture & Heritage Practice Berwick Partners +44 (0) 207 518 2635 / +44 (0) 7515 919 648 Closing date for applications: Thursday 15th October 2026

item.title: Admin and Grants Officer
item.description: Could you play a crucial role within our busy and friendly team and take responsibility for managing our benevolent fund? We are looking to recruit an Administration and Grants Officer to support the output of our HQ, including benevolent fund caseload management, member support, and general Association output. Some travel is expected to support membership events inc. evenings & weekends, with occasional overnight stays. We offer generous holiday entitlement, 6% employer pension contribution, free parking, access to gym/swimming pool, canteen, café and shop. We are the UK’s largest membership organisation of female veterans and serving women - a financially sustainable £8m charity which aims to provide camaraderie, benevolence and support to women who have served in the Army. Additionally, we aim to exert influence within the military charity sector to broaden support for all female veterans of the UK Armed Forces. Our benevolent fund awards over £200k in grants per year to an average of 120 applicants, from minor requests to major grants, and annual maintenance. We organise both national and local events for our members to attend where they meet up with old friends, remember those we have lost, support each other, have fun and make new and lasting memories. We have approaching 5000 active members which we hope to grow as we reach out to many more female veterans eligible to join our Association. You will: have experience of working in a member or public-facing organisation, supporting and liaising with a diverse cohort of individuals in a wide variety of interests and needs have experience of managing caseloads and carrying out detailed casework have a sound knowledge of how individual grants are awarded have a strong understanding of the work of SSAFA, TRBL & other caseworking and almonising agencies understand the value of strong communication and be experienced in engaging people from many walks of life, tailoring your communication style to a variety of audiences be skilled at building positive working relationships, with a friendly and engaging manner be highly organised with great attention to detail, and work well within a small staff team where each team member is expected to pitch in and work collaboratively Be engaging and welcoming, able to attend events and interact with members of the public The charity is governed by a Board of Trustees with a number of sub-committees, all volunteers. We are a small staff team of 5, led by a CEO, who are motivated by the good work we do to support some amazing, brave and pioneering women. We are proud of the work we do to support female veterans, many of whom are now well into retirement. Some have fallen on hard times and need our financial support, whilst others may be lonely or have reduced mobility, and rely on our association to keep them in touch with like-minded comrades. We are an inclusive employer seeking to attract and employ the best people from the widest talent pool, committed to supporting our staff and the female veterans we serve. All applicants must be able to demonstrate current eligibility to work in the UK. If you are a motivated, self-starting and engaging individual with a passion for working with people and supporting their needs, then we look forward to receiving your application by way of a CV and a detailed supporting statement demonstrating your suitability for the role with regard to the above person specification.

item.title: North-West GCSE Resits Senior Programme Coordinator
item.description: Our charity delivers a series of interventions that help disadvantaged learners in Further Education to secure gateway English and maths qualifications that unlock opportunities. These interventions include our award-winning GCSE Resit Tuition Programme, for those resitting GCSEs, our Functional Skills Tuition Programme, supporting those on or aspiring to undertake apprenticeship programmes, and training and resources to support teachers and leaders of English and maths in Further Education. Our benefits include: About the role As a Senior Programme Coordinator, you will lead the day-to-day delivery across a portfolio of partner colleges. Acting as the main point of contact for students, tutors and college staff, you will build strong working relationships, maintain a consistent on-site presence and ensure programmes are delivered smoothly, professionally and in line with agreed standards and KPIs. You will take ownership of programme performance across your portfolio, with a particular focus on student enrolment, attendance, and session dosage targets. You will oversee programme logistics, monitor delivery quality, and work proactively to maximise student participation and tutor effectiveness. This role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to operational challenges. You will also play an important role in maintaining high-quality partnerships with colleges, ensuring stakeholders receive clear communication, accurate reporting and responsive support throughout programme delivery. Alongside this, you will contribute to wider organisational priorities, including safeguarding, tutor development, programme improvement and initiatives that strengthen student outcomes. As a Senior Programme Coordinator, you will be expected to role model best practice to the wider Programme Coordinator team, working collaboratively to problem solve, and work with your Programme Manager to ensure strategic approaches to meeting KPIs. This is a highly collaborative, delivery-focused role suited to someone who enjoys a challenge, is confident managing relationships. MAIN DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES See recruitment pack ABOUT YOU You will: Thrive in a busy, fast-paced environment and enjoy managing multiple priorities effectively. Be passionate about improving outcomes for young people, with a genuine commitment to tackling educational inequality. Enjoy working collaboratively with colleagues, tutors and college partners to achieve shared goals. Be comfortable working independently, taking ownership of your workload and delivering results with minimal supervision. Demonstrate initiative and a proactive approach, identifying opportunities and resolving challenges effectively. Be highly organised, detail-oriented and able to manage competing demands without compromising quality. Take accountability for your work and be confident making decisions and driving progress. Be resilient, adaptable and solutions-focused when responding to challenges. Be motivated by working in a mission-driven organisation where your contribution has a direct impact on learners' success and future opportunities. The closing date for applications is 9:00am on Monday 28 September. Applications received after this time will not be considered. NEXT STEPS Suitable candidates will be contacted after the closing date. Screening calls will take place on the Thursday 1st & Friday 2nd October. These will take place online. The first-round interviews will be held online on Tuesday 6th October & Wednesday 7th October , followed by a second in-person interview Thursday 15th October (London). You will be able to expense your travel for this interview. We value diversity and actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, particularly individuals from ethnically diverse communities who are currently underrepresented in our sector. We are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels they belong. For full details on responsibilities please see the recruitment pack.

item.title: Senior Legacy Marketing Manager
item.description: Compassion in World Farming International is a global movement transforming the future of food and farming. Lead our UK and international legacy marketing programme and help inspire supporters to leave a lasting gift for farm animals, people and the planet. Senior Legacy Marketing Manager (UK and International) Role type: Full time; Permanent Location: Godalming, Surrey - HQ. Hybrid working pattern 2x days per week in the office: Tuesdays & Thursdays. The office is located close to Godalming station, with direct trains from/to London Waterloo in approximately 45 minutes. Salary: £45,000 to £50,000 per annum (depending upon skills and experience) About the role As our Senior Legacy Marketing Manager (UK and International), you’ll lead the strategic development and delivery of Compassion in World Farming’s legacy marketing programme across the UK and internationally. This is a vital role within our Global Fundraising team, helping to shape a sector leading legacy strategy that inspires supporters to leave a lasting gift for farm animals and the planet. As part of this exciting role, you’ll be responsible for: Legacy strategy and coordination – Leading the development of Compassion’s UK and international legacy marketing strategy, reporting on KPIs and identifying opportunities to strengthen engagement and investment. UK legacy marketing delivery – Overseeing and delivering legacy communications across direct mail, email, social media, website content, events, supporter engagement and promotional campaigns. International legacy delivery – Supporting fundraising teams in France, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, the USA and Poland to deliver locally relevant legacy campaigns, content, training and enquiry handling. Supporter care – Responding sensitively and efficiently to legacy enquiries and helping colleagues feel confident talking to supporters about gifts in wills. About you To succeed as our Senior Legacy Marketing Manager (UK and International), you’ll be a confident and strategic legacy marketing professional with a strong track record of delivering impactful campaigns that inspire supporters to leave a very special gift. You’ll bring a deep understanding of legacy fundraising, ideally gained within the charity or NGO sector, and feel comfortable working across both UK and international markets. You’ll be highly organised, proactive and detail-oriented, with the ability to craft compelling messages for direct response and manage multi-channel campaigns. Skills and experience you’ll need to bring as part of this role: Track record and knowledge of legacy marketing and legacy strategy, ideally as a practitioner. Strong understanding of direct marketing, digital marketing or supporter fundraising, with excellent copywriting and creative skills. Proven strategic planning skills, with the ability to manage budgets, suppliers, data and reporting. Experience of working collaboratively with international teams across multiple countries and time zones. Ability to engage supporters with sensitivity, care and confidence, including through legacy events and enquiry handling. Proficiency in relevant fundraising or database systems, ideally Salesforce CRM. A demonstrable interest in farm animal welfare issues and Compassion’s mission. If you don’t meet every requirement but believe you could thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply. Why join us This is a rare opportunity to lead a global legacy marketing programme that directly supports a mission to end factory farming. We offer a supportive, flexible workplace with a strong focus on wellbeing and development, including: 25 days annual leave + bank holidays Health Cash Back Plan and 24/7 GP access Employee Assistance Programme and MHFA support Premium Calm App subscription Electric car scheme available Defined contribution pension scheme Enhanced discretionary sick pay Hybrid working model (role and location dependent) Free onsite parking and office next to mainline station Cycle Benefit scheme and other savings options Ongoing learning and development opportunities How to apply and key dates If you’re ready to make a global impact, we’d love to hear from you. Please submit your CV and a cover letter outlining how you meet the Person Specification. To support a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly ask that you do not include a photo in your CV. Please note that we may begin interviews on a rolling basis, so early applications are encouraged. Closing date: 29 September 2026 1stStage (Teams) Interview 2ndStage (Face to Face at HQ) Interview, with task “ Join us in building a more compassionate future for animals, people, and the planet.” As part of Stage 1 interviews, shortlisted candidates may, for some roles, receive pre‑shared, values‑based interview questions to support a positive candidate experience. If you require any adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know, we’re always happy to support candidates. About Compassion Compassion in World Farming International is a leading global organisation working to end factory farming. Founded in 1967 by British farmer Peter Roberts, we’ve spent over 50 years driving change, successfully campaigning to ban cruel practices such as barren battery cages, veal crates, and sow stalls across the UK and Europe. Our work combines advocacy, campaigning, and collaboration with policymakers and businesses to promote animal welfare and sustainable food systems. We envision a future where animals are treated with compassion, and farming supports both people and the planet. To learn more about our mission, culture, and opportunities, please explore our Candidate Pack, and Careers Page on our website. To comply with legal requirements in the UK and internationally, all applicants must be able to demonstrate their right to work in the country where the role is based. Compassion in World Farming is absolutely committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone regardless of their background. We value diversity and live experience and acknowledge the underrepresentation of people from certain backgrounds, both within our organisation and across the sector. We welcome applications from underrepresented groups, whether these be of ethnicity, gender, identity, religion, physical ability, sexual orientation or other.

item.description: Head of Earned, Shared and Paid Digital (2666) Location: Oxford UK/ (with the ability to work from home under Oxfam GB's hybrid working arrangements) Workplace Type: Hybrid Hours: 36 hours per week Salary: £49,601 with a discretionary range up to £56,518 depending on experience Job Family: Communications Division: CEO Office Grade: B Job Type: Open ended Closing Date: 30 September 2026 Country: United Kingdom Oxfam is a global movement of people working together to end the injustice of poverty. The Role: As Oxfam's Head of Earned, Shared and Paid Digital, you will work collaboratively across teams to shape the strategic direction for how Oxfam earns attention, engages audiences, and grows its reach across organic social, paid digital and channels beyond our own. Together, you'll ensure that this engagement translates into income, influence and long-term support for our mission. You will lead and empower our organic social and paid digital teams, holding oversight of day-to-day activity while focusing on elevating and optimising our channel, platform, targeting and digital marketing strategies. You will support your teams to deliver brilliantly by setting a clear creative direction, providing strong editorial and brand stewardship, and embedding a data-led approach to performance and learning. You'll create the space, confidence and connections that enable teams to think beyond individual channels and deliver integrated, audience-focused work. Working closely with the Head of Digital and Head of Owned Digital, you will help shape Oxfam's wider digital strategy and strengthen our impact across the organisation. By building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, you will bring audience insight into campaigning, fundraising and public engagement activity, ensuring digital expertise informs decision-making and positioning the team as a trusted strategic partner. If you have any questions about the role, we'd love to hear from you.Please e-mail us at , making sure you include the job title and reference number of the role you're asking about.Please be aware we are unable to accept CVs or applications via e-mail.To apply, please use the "apply now" button on the right hand side of this advertisement. What we are looking for: We’re looking for a candidate who cares about Oxfam's mission to end poverty and is personally aligned to our feminist principles and values of empowerment, accountability and inclusion in all you do. An ideal candidate for the role will also have: Experience of managing a multi-disciplinary team and the performance of others Lived experience (s) or evidence of learning/taking action on anti-racism and inequalities. Strong knowledge of digital platforms, marketing technologies and industry trends. A proven track record of growing income, influence and audience engagement through digital channels, ideally within the charity, campaigning or wider social impact sector. Proven experience of crisis and reputation management within digital channels. Proven success in developing audience-led digital strategies and integrated campaigns across earned, shared and paid channels that deliver measurable impact. Excellent stakeholder management skills, experienced in proactive collaboration across organisations. Outstanding communication skills, with the ability to engage, inspire and influence a wide range of audiences. A strong commitment to Oxfam's values. We offer: We offer a competitive salary and a range of additional benefits to staff including flexible working options, generous pension scheme, annual leave, additional leave allowances, company sick pay, life assurance and a range of other benefits. From the day you join Oxfam we invite you to stretch and learn in your role. Our wide range of Learning & Development opportunities includes in-house courses, e-learning modules, on-the job learning opportunities, coaching and mentoring, and much more. You can read more about all Oxfam has to offer Flexfam: We believe flexible working is key to building the Oxfam of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you. How to apply: As part of your online application, please upload your up to date CV and Cover Letter explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile. Our values and commitment to safeguarding Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Oxfam GB engages. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our are recruited to work for us. The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Oxfam GB also participates in the .In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures. We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organisation and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply. About us Oxfam is a global community who believe poverty isn’t inevitable. It’s an injustice that can be overcome. We are shop volunteers, women’s right activists, marathon runners, aid workers, coffee farmers, street fundraisers, goat herders, policy experts, campaigners, water engineers and more. And we won’t stop until everyone can live life without poverty for good. is a member of of 21 organisations working together with partners and local communities in the areas of humanitarian, development and campaigning, in more than 90 countries. A thriving diverse Oxfam: It’s people power that brings about change. To play our part as a global organisation working to overcome poverty and inequality, we need equality, diversity and inclusion across our community of staff, partners and volunteers. Together, we’re committed to becoming a more diverse workforce, better able to tackle the global challenges that face our world today. To do that: We need to dismantle the unequal power structures that exist everywhere, this including Oxfam and the wider development and charity sectors. We need an inclusive Oxfam where everyone can bring who they are to our work and feels celebrated for the differences they bring. We want and need everyone, and that means we need you .

item.title: Policy Officer
item.description: Job description About the British Society for Heart Failure The British Society for Heart Failure (BSH) is the UK's leading charity and membership organisation dedicated to improving care for people living with heart failure. We bring together healthcare professionals, researchers and decision-makers to improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment and long-term outcomes through education, awareness, research and policy influence. This is an exciting time to join BSH as we deliver our ambitious new strategy and continue to drive forward our national 25in25 campaign to reduce mortality from heart failure and improve outcomes for patients across the UK. About the Role This is a high-profile opportunity to shape and deliver BSH's policy agenda and strengthen its influence across the healthcare sector. Reporting to the Chief Executive, you will work with clinical leaders, parliamentarians, NHS stakeholders and partner organisations to ensure BSH remains a credible and influential voice on heart failure policy. You will help develop evidence-based policy positions, influence decision-makers and support improvements in heart failure prevention, diagnosis and care across the UK. Key Responsibilities Lead the delivery and development of BSH's policy framework and priorities. Develop policy papers, briefings, consultation responses and stakeholder communications. Build relationships with parliamentarians, NHS leaders, policymakers and healthcare organisations. Represent BSH at meetings, consultations, forums and policy discussions. Identify opportunities to influence policy and improve outcomes for people living with heart failure. Work collaboratively with partner organisations on advocacy, campaigns and policy development. Monitor the healthcare and policy landscape, identifying emerging issues and opportunities. Support wider organisational activity including communications, events and strategic initiatives. Our Commitment to Inclusion We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. If you're excited by this opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still encourage you to apply. As this role is primarily remote we also encourage applicants from any location in the UK that enables occassional travel into London and elsewhere in the UK. item.title: Head of Marketing & Communications
item.description: ABOUT THE ROLE The Head of Marketing and Communications will strategically lead Trees for Cities’ marketing and communications to grow reach, influence and engagement, delivering agreed organisational objectives, OKRs and KPIs. This role leads the strategic direction and delivery of Trees for Cities’ marketing and communications function, ensuring campaigns, communications and audience engagement activities support organisational objectives and deliver measurable growth. The postholder oversees team performance, external partners, media relations, fundraising communications and marketing for the Trees for Streets programme, while driving audience development, supporter stewardship and digital innovation. As a senior leader, they contribute to organisational strategy, provide expert communications counsel, manage budgets and resources, and foster a high-performing, inclusive team culture that strengthens the organisation’s profile, reputation and long-term impact. ABOUT TREES FOR CITIES Trees for Cities is an ambitious, far-reaching organisation. Trees for Cities is the only charity that focuses on planting, protecting and promoting urban trees across the UK. We are a rapidly growing and developing organisation that suits ambitious, dedicated and passionate staff. ABOUT YOU This is an exciting opportunity for a strategic, creative and purpose-driven marketing and communications leader who wants to use their skills to help our vital work to plant and establish urban trees where they are needed the most. As our Head of Marketing and Communications, you'll be a confident and inspiring leader with a proven track record of growing audiences, building influential brands and delivering impactful multi-channel campaigns. You'll be equally comfortable shaping long-term strategy as rolling up your sleeves to make things happen, bringing energy, creativity and commercial awareness to everything you do. We're looking for someone who can spot opportunities, tell compelling stories and build meaningful engagement with supporters, partners, policymakers and the public. You'll have strong experience across marketing, communications, PR, digital engagement and brand management, alongside excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to lead and develop a high-performing team. Most importantly, you'll be motivated by our mission. As the climate and biodiversity crisis intensifies, urban trees have never been more important. They help cool our cities, improve health and wellbeing, support biodiversity and create greener, more resilient communities. We need an ambitious communications leader who can raise our profile, inspire action and help grow a movement that puts trees at the heart of healthier cities for everyone. Key skills and experience: Strategic marketing and communications leadership Audience growth, brand development and campaign delivery Media relations, PR, thought leadership and reputation management Digital marketing, audience insight and data-led decision making Team leadership, coaching and people development Stakeholder, partner and agency management Budget and project management A passion for creating positive environmental and social impact Trees for Cities is committed to the principles of equal opportunity. We value diversity and are committed to promoting diversity within the workplace. We aim to ensure that our employees achieve their full potential and that all employment decisions, including recruitment, are taken without reference to irrelevant or discriminatory criteria. A full copy of our Equal Opportunities Policy can be provided on request. HOW TO APPLY Please visit our website to view full job description. To apply, use the application link on our website to submit your CV and supporting statement (no more than 2 sides of A4) outlining why you are interested in the role and your fit with the Person Specification. Please note we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role, you must therefore have a valid right to work in the UK to apply. item.title: Independent Visitor
item.description: Do you believe that all children should receive consistently high-quality care in environments that strive to improve outcomes for each child? Do you have experience in social work, education, inspection, advocacy or residential childcare management? Then we have an exciting opportunity for a professional like you. The Vacancy An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Independent Visitor to join NYAS Independent Monitoring Service. This is a full-time permanent role, working 35 hours per week across Scotland. As an Independent Visitor you will be required to complete and report on settings via independent visits The purpose of this role is to ensure that judgements are consistent with evidence provided and that the feedback given is an element of continuous improvement. While the role is home-based, where travel is required, it may include public transport. About You We are looking for a self-starter who prides themselves in professionalism and accuracy. You must have a relevant professional qualification and proven extensive experience in working with children and young people or adults at risk in a social care setting. For more information, please view the attached job description. In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the job description attached. Requirements include: Professional qualification in a relevant field. Proven extensive experience in working with children and young people or adults at risk in a social care setting. Experience and an understanding of child and adult safeguarding procedures. Experience of quality assuring reports for regulatory bodies. Ability to analyse a range of information to assess effective evidence-based judgements of reports. Proven experience of using QA to improve report writing. Ability to communicate effectively and to a high standard both orally and in writing to a wide range of people. Please note that as this role is based in Scotland, Scottish bank holidays will apply. NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references, Digital Risk Assessment and Right to Work check. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early once we receive a high number of applications. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change young lives.
