item.description: Job Title: Shop Manager Salary: c. £29,000 per annum Team: Godalming Hours: Full Time, 37.5 per week Contract Type: Permanent Location: Godalming Shop, 1DW GU7 About the role Your key purpose will be to lead the day to day operation of our Godalming charity shop, maximising income and delivering an excellent experience for our customers, volunteers and supporters while helping to raise vital funds for Shooting Star Children's Hospices. You will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of shop performance, including customer service, stock management, donation processing, merchandising and financial administration. You will ensure donations are processed efficiently, Gift Aid opportunities are maximised, and stock is presented to a high standard through attractive displays and effective merchandising. Working closely with Assistant Shop Managers and volunteers, you will create a positive and inclusive environment, providing training, support and direction to ensure the shop is fully staffed and operating effectively. You will be responsible for driving sales performance, maintaining accurate financial records, ensuring compliance with policies, procedures and relevant legislation, and identifying opportunities to maximise income from donated goods. You will also support fundraising initiatives, charity campaigns and special events, while ensuring the shop remains safe, welcoming, clean and well-presented at all times. Flexibility is essential, as you may be required to provide support and cover across other shop locations when needed. About you This role requires experience of managing a retail environment, including responsibility for sales performance, customer service, cash handling and ensuring compliance with relevant policies and procedures. You will have experience of motivating and supporting staff, with the ability to build strong relationships and create a positive and inclusive team culture. Strong organisational skills, the ability to prioritise competing demands and confidence in making day to day operational decisions are essential. You will be able to manage stock effectively, maintain high merchandising standards and identify opportunities to maximise income through donations, Gift Aid and retail sales. Experience of recruiting, training and coordinating volunteers would be advantageous, as would experience of charity retail, financial reporting and stock management. Above all, you will be proactive, adaptable and passionate about delivering excellent customer service while supporting the vital work of Shooting Star Children's Hospices. Please see the attached job description for more information about this opportunity at Shooting Star Children’s Hospices. What we offer In return you will receive a competitive salary along with a range of benefits, which include: Pension scheme NHS Pension Scheme (for eligible employees) or our stakeholder pension scheme, with up to 7% employer contributions Annual leave 27 days plus Bank Holidays rising with length of service 2 weeks paid sabbatical leave after 5, 10 and 15 years’ service Contractual benefits Generous sick pay scheme Enhanced maternity, adoption, and paternity leave pay Flexible working arrangements Death in service benefits Reimbursed professional membership fees Eye care Employee referral scheme Blue Light discount card Health and wellbeing Employee Assistance Programme Occupational Health Mindfulness sessions Mental Health First Aiders Safeguarding We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expect all our staff to share this commitment. Also, we are committed to equal opportunities and consider all applicants to be in line with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. Employment is subject to receipt of satisfactory references and a DBS check. Equality, diversity and inclusion Shooting Star Children’s Hospices is committed to inclusion and diversity in everything we do. We know that getting things right is critical for us to live our organisation’s values: Professionalism, Respect, Integrity, Diversity and Excellence. We are always trying to improve our way of working to be more inclusive and equal. Our vision is for Shooting Star Children’s Hospices to be a place where people of all backgrounds, groups and communities feel welcomed to work and volunteer. Anticipated closing date : 25/09/2026

item.title: Children and Young People's Independent Sexual Violence Advisor (ISVA)
item.description: Job description Yellow Door is an amazing charity that is quite literally changing lives for the better across the Hampshire area, with a team of around 100 staff and volunteers, working together to prevent and respond to domestic and sexual abuse. We provide a diverse and innovative range of services to local people of all ages and genders. Last year we engaged with over 4,500 clients to provide crucial support, information, and in some cases a lifeline. Right now, our services have never been more in demand, so our volunteers and supporters are absolutely critical to us. Would you like to be part of our amazing team that is changing lives for the better in the Southampton area? We are looking for highly motivated individuals to provide proactive advocacy and support services to people who have experienced sexual violence/ abuse. The CYP ISVA provides practical and emotional support to children and young people who have experienced sexual violence or abuse. The role focuses on delivering age-appropriate, trauma-informed support that reduces distress and supports informed decision-making. You will work with children and young people who may not be ready for counselling, offering accessible support while guiding them through the criminal justice process and advocating on their behalf. The role also involves supporting parents and carers, ensuring the young person’s voice is heard and their needs are met. We are looking for individuals who have experience of working within an advocacy role, preferably within domestic or sexual abuse or related fields such as mental health/social care/justice roles. You will have a sound understanding of risk assessment alongside experience of managing diverse caseloads and working pro-actively within multi-agency partnerships to support victim-focused outcomes. The successful applicants will have effective communication and advocacy skills and knowledge of the impact of sexual violence/abuse. For further information and to apply for the role, please visit our website. item.title: Regular Giving and Legacies Coordinator
item.description: About the role: Imperial’s Regular Giving and Legacy team is seeking a coordinator to support their fundraising programme. Are you interested in a varied and interesting role within a high performing team at a university which is not only world leading, but also world changing? Are you a talented administrator looking to get started in fundraising? Then this could be the role for you. For this role you will need to demonstrate outstanding organisational skills, be process-led and have excellent communications skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to work with a wide range of individuals. What you would be doing: Imperial’s Regular and Mid-Level Giving programme raises funds to advance the work of the University. The programme focuses on using direct marketing such as direct mail, email and telephone campaigns to solicit support from alumni through regular donations, mid value gifts and gifts in wills. The team coordinator is the lynchpin of the programme and supports the team in all aspects of direct marketing fundraising and administration. Duties and responsibilities Your responsibilities will be wide-ranging, but the key duties are: • Support the telethon fundraising campaigns, direct marketing fundraising appeals, and managing your own fundraising projects such as emails and social media. • Act as first contact for all fundraising related queries (by telephone, email, post and in person); liaise across the team to draft and send appropriate responses. • Collect, collate and manage case studies, including building relationships with students. • Support the team with general administrative and office duties such as booking meeting rooms. • Provide diary management and PA support to the Head of Regular Giving and Legacy Giving. • Support with the team with budgets including raising PO’s and tracking invoices. What we are looking for: In order to hit the ground running, you will need to possess the following required skills: • Experience of working in a customer, alumni or donor focused environment. • Excellent organisational skills, ability to manage a varied workload and a process led approach. • Outstanding communications (both written and oral) and interpersonal skills • Ability to communicate effectively and concisely with a range of internal and external stakeholders, at all levels. • A proven track record of outstanding attention to detail and methodical approach to work. • A sound understanding of customer relations databases (CRM) to manage customer/donor data. What we can offer you: • The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to use science for humanity. • Benefit from a sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 41 days’ annual leave and generous pension schemes). • Access to a range of workplace benefits including a flexible working policy from day one, generous family leave packages, on-site leisure facilities and cycle-to-work scheme. • Interest-free season ticket loan schemes for travel. • Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further Information This is a full-time open-ended post (not less than 35 hours per week). For your reference, the following text will appear on all adverts on our jobs website and doesn’t need to be included in other sections of the job advert. Please note that job descriptions are not exhaustive, and you may be asked to take on additional duties that align with the key responsibilities mentioned above. If you experience any technical issues while applying online, please don't hesitate to email us. We're here to help. Closing date: 30th September 2026 About Imperial Welcome to Imperial, a global top ten university where scientific imagination leads to world-changing impact. Join us and be part of something bigger. From global health to climate change, AI to business leadership, we navigate some of the world’s toughest challenges. Whatever your role, your contribution will have a lasting impact. As a member of our vibrant community of 22,000 students and 8,000 staff, you’ll collaborate with passionate minds across nine London campuses and a global network. This is your chance to help shape the future. We hope you’ll join us at Imperial. Our culture We work towards equality of opportunity, eliminating discrimination and creating an inclusive working environment. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities and industries, and are committed to employing a team that has diverse skills, experiences and abilities. You can read more about our commitment on our webpages. Our values are at the heart of everything we do and everyone in our community is expected to demonstrate respect, collaboration, excellence, integrity and innovation.

item.title: Senior Administration Officer
item.description: Join Liver UK at an exciting point in our development. Liver UK is the national charity for people affected by liver disease and liver cancer. We provide expert information and support, raise awareness, promote prevention and earlier diagnosis, influence policy and ensure the voices of people affected by liver disease are heard. Following the coming together of the British Liver Trust and Children’s Liver Disease Foundation, we are now Liver UK: one charity supporting people of all ages and with all types of liver disease. We have strong foundations, an ambitious strategy for 2026–2032 and a clear goal to make liver health a national priority. We are now moving from a period of transformation into one focused on delivery, growth and impact. We are looking for an experienced, highly organised and confident Senior Administrator to play a central role in helping our organisation run effectively. The role This is much more than a traditional administration role. You will be at the heart of our day-to-day operations, providing high-quality administrative and operational support across Liver UK and working with colleagues at all levels, including our Senior Management Team. We are looking for someone who enjoys creating structure, improving processes and finding ways to make how we work more efficient and effective. You will manage a varied workload, keep important actions moving, coordinate organisational processes and help ensure agreed deadlines are met. You will need to be confident and appropriately persistent. You’ll build good relationships with colleagues, while also being comfortable following things up, challenging constructively and having clear and confident conversations about deadlines, priorities and standards. You will also provide day-to-day supervision and support to our office-based Apprentice, helping them to organise their workload, develop their skills and build confidence in their role. What you’ll be doing · Providing senior administrative and operational support across the charity. · Coordinating meetings, diaries, travel, events and other organisational activity. · Managing central telephone and shared email services. · Proactively following up actions, information and approvals across teams. · Supervising and supporting our Apprentice and overseeing office-based volunteers. · Maintaining accurate information within Raiser’s Edge and other organisational systems. · Supporting data quality, GDPR and records management. · Managing routine supplier arrangements and office contracts, obtaining good value and negotiating where appropriate. · Supporting staff technology and systems, including laptops and telephony administration. · Coordinating our monthly all-staff Touchpoints. · Supporting office facilities, health and safety, publications and stock. · Helping improve systems, processes and ways of working across Liver UK. About you You will already have significant experience in a busy administration, office operations or organisational support role. You’ll be exceptionally organised, reliable and comfortable taking ownership rather than waiting to be directed. You’ll be able to manage competing priorities, spot what needs to happen next and see tasks through to completion. Just as importantly, you’ll have the confidence and interpersonal skills to work effectively with colleagues at all levels, combining diplomacy and positive working relationships with appropriate challenge. You’ll have strong written and verbal communication skills, excellent attention to detail and good IT skills. Experience of databases, CRM systems or similar organisational systems is important, while experience of Raiser’s Edge, the charity sector or a health environment would be an advantage. Experience of supervising, coaching or supporting another member of staff, apprentice or volunteer would also be valuable. You’ll enjoy supporting someone early in their career, providing encouragement, clear expectations and constructive feedback to help them build confidence, develop their skills and succeed in their role. Why Liver UK? Liver disease and liver cancer are among the UK’s fastest-growing and most under-recognised health challenges. They affect people of all ages, and the need for earlier diagnosis, better treatment, prevention and support has never been greater. This is an opportunity to join a committed national charity at an important point in its development and to take on a role where strong organisation behind the scenes has a real impact on what the wider charity can achieve. Please apply through CharityJob with your CV and a covering letter explaining why you are interested in the role and how your experience meets the requirements set out in the Job & Person Specification. We will review applications and interview suitable candidates as they are received, so we may close the vacancy early. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from candidates with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. We offer a range of benefits for our employees: 25 days elective annual leave (FTE), plus bank holidays. Life assurance 4x your salary starting from date of employment. 5% employer pension contribution, rising to 7.5% at 15 months and 10% at 27 months service (optional on contribution increase). BUPA Wellbeing Health Expenses plan; including dental, prescriptions and optical cover. And many more…

item.title: Executive Projects Manager - 1 year fixed-term contract
item.description: Role Overview You will be a strategic partner to the CEO and Senior Leadership Team, operating at the heart of the organisation to enable effective leadership, decision-making and delivery. This role requires strategic project management, stakeholder engagement and organisational coordination. Acting as an extension of the CEO, you will help ensure priorities remain aligned, actions are delivered and the leadership team operates effectively in pursuit of Greenhouse's mission. Additionally, you will provide senior level executive support to the CEO. You will be passionate about our purpose and committed to making a meaningful difference for young people. As a trusted representative of the organisation, you will build strong relationships with colleagues, partners, donors and other key stakeholders. The role could be done full time, or 0.8 FTE spread across five days. Job Description Senior Leadership Team Support & Coordination Serve as a key point of coordination for the Senior Leadership Team, driving alignment, communication and accountability across the organisation. Organise and facilitate SLT meetings, including agenda planning, preparation of papers, minute-taking, action tracking and follow-up. Ensure actions arising from SLT meetings are clearly assigned, monitored and progressed to completion. Support the CEO and SLT in translating strategic objectives into actionable plans and tracking delivery against agreed priorities. Coordinate leadership away days, strategic reviews, planning cycles and organisational planning activities. Build effective working relationships with department leads to support collaboration and alignment across functions. Strategic Planning & Business Operations Lead and coordinate projects and strategic initiatives on behalf of the CEO, ensuring delivery against agreed objectives, timescales and outcomes. Track progress against organisational objectives, providing oversight of actions, risks, dependencies and deadlines. Produce executive reports, dashboards and briefing papers to support strategic decision-making. Support governance activities where required, including preparation of papers, actions and documentation for Board, Committee and Trustee meetings. Drive business improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, consistency and effectiveness across executive and organisational processes. Stakeholder & Relationship Management Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including partners, funders, trustees and senior leaders. Act as a professional representative of the CEO and SLT in meetings, correspondence and stakeholder interactions where appropriate. Facilitate effective communication between the CEO, SLT and wider organisation, ensuring key messages and priorities are clearly communicated and understood. Organisational Effectiveness & Change Support Identify risks, bottlenecks and competing priorities, escalating issues and recommending solutions where appropriate. Continuously review and improve executive and organisational processes to increase efficiency and effectiveness. Support change initiatives and organisational development activities aligned to Greenhouse's strategic objectives. Support the planning and delivery of organisation-wide events, staff engagement initiatives and cultural activities. Mentor and support junior colleagues, sharing knowledge and promoting best practice across the organisation. Contribute positively to leadership discussions and demonstrate a collaborative, solutions-focused approach to challenges and opportunities. Executive Support to the CEO Act as a trusted partner to the CEO, providing proactive, high-level support to maximise effectiveness and focus on strategic priorities. Manage and prioritise the CEO's complex and dynamic diary, inbox and commitments, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities. Exercise sound judgement in managing competing demands, anticipating needs, risks and opportunities while acting as an effective gatekeeper and maintaining strong stakeholder relationships. Coordinate all travel, accommodation, expenses and logistics for the CEO. Prepare executive briefings, correspondence, presentations, reports and meeting materials to support informed decision-making. Proofread and quality assure high-profile communications, proposals, reports and presentations, ensuring consistency, accuracy and professionalism. Provide executive support to other members of the SLT as required. Experience & Skills Proven experience leading and delivering cross-functional projects involving multiple stakeholders, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and drive successful outcomes. Strong business acumen with the ability to understand organisational priorities, identify risks and recommend solutions. Experience drafting, reviewing and implementing organisational policies, procedures and governance documentation. Demonstrable experience managing competing priorities, exercising sound judgement and operating effectively within a highly confidential environment. Exceptional written communication skills, with experience preparing reports, executive briefings, presentations, policies and stakeholder communications. Proven ability to build trusted relationships and influence effectively at all levels of an organisation, including senior leaders, trustees, funders and external partners. Significant experience providing executive-level support to a CEO, Executive Director, Board or Senior Leadership Team within a complex and fast-paced environment. Highly proficient in Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, with confidence using project management, collaboration and reporting tools. A track record of improving processes, systems and ways of working to increase organisational effectiveness. Experience working across multiple functions, building alignment and enabling effective communication between teams. Passion for Greenhouse's mission and commitment to making a positive difference for young people. Who You Are A trusted and highly professional executive who operates with discretion, integrity and confidentiality. Strategic and commercially aware, able to understand the wider organisational context while maintaining excellent attention to detail. Proactive and forward-thinking, anticipating needs and taking action before issues arise. An exceptional organiser who thrives in a fast-paced environment and remains calm, resilient and solution-focused under pressure. A confident relationship-builder who quickly establishes credibility and trust with colleagues, senior leaders and external stakeholders. Comfortable working independently, exercising sound judgement and making decisions within agreed parameters. Skilled at navigating ambiguity, managing competing priorities and adapting to changing organisational needs. Confident providing constructive challenge, driving accountability and ensuring commitments are delivered. Passionate about Greenhouse's purpose, values and culture, acting as a positive ambassador for the organisation.

item.title: Learning and Communities Officer
item.description: The Learning and Communities Officer will help bring AmplifyChange's community of Grantee Partners together, creating opportunities for organisations and activists working on sexual and reproductive health and rights to connect, share their expertise and learn from one another. You'll play a hands-on role in shaping and delivering AmplifyChange's learning and community offer. From building an active online community and hosting engaging digital learning sessions to supporting in-country convenings and developing accessible learning resources, you'll help create spaces where Grantee Partners can exchange ideas, build relationships and share what works. You'll have the opportunity to connect with a diverse network of Grantee Partners, facilitators and technical experts across Africa, South Asia and the Middle East, helping people share their knowledge and learn from one another. You'll also work closely with colleagues across AmplifyChange to bring partner experience and learning into the organisation through Grantee Partner showcases, case studies, impact briefs and other engaging content. This is a varied and creative role for someone who enjoys bringing people together and turning ideas and experience into engaging learning opportunities. You'll have the chance to experiment with different approaches to digital learning and community engagement, including the responsible use of AI-enabled tools, while helping us continually improve how we connect with and learn alongside our Grantee Partners. AmplifyChange is a bilingual fund working in English and French, so professional-level written French and confidence speaking French are essential for this role. MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES Learning and Community Engagement Create opportunities for Grantee Partners to connect, share their expertise and learn from one another, building an active and welcoming community across AmplifyChange's network. Develop and coordinate an annual learning and ommunity engagement plan in collaboration with AmplifyChange colleagues and partners, ensuring activities align with organisational priorities and Grantee Partner needs. Build an active and welcoming online community on Circle, creating opportunities for peer learning, collaboration, knowledge sharing and sustained engagement. Work with the Learning, Monitoring and Evaluation Manager, Grant Managers and other colleagues to ensure learning activities are shaped by Grantee Partner priorities, experience and expertise. Coordinate Grantee Partner showcases and internal learning sessions that strengthen staff understanding of the grant portfolio and partner organisations. Learning Events and Programmes Bring learning to life through engaging, inclusive and well-run online, in-person and hybrid experiences that enable Grantee Partners to connect, participate and learn together. Plan, coordinate, host and deliver high-quality online, in-person, and hybrid learning events, programmes, workshops dialogues and convenings. Coordinate event logistics, including scheduling, registration, speaker and facilitator liaison, accessibility, technology, and participant communications. Support the delivery of multi-day dialogues and convenings by managing behind-the-scenes operations, technical delivery, and participant support to create a positive and inclusive experience. Support the development of longer participatory learning programmes and, over time , their transformation into accessible digital learning courses Facilitate and host learning activities using Zoom, Microsoft Teams, livestreaming and other digital engagement platforms. Anticipate and manage? risks, contingencies and changing requirements to ensure effective and inclusive delivery Communications, Content and Knowledge Management Turn learning and partner experience into engaging, accessible content and resources that can be shared across AmplifyChange and its community. Work closely with the Communications team to promote learning activities and maintain consistent branding and messaging across learning and community channels. Coordinate the development of promotional materials, case studies, impact briefs and other learning resources, working with external designers and suppliers where required. Coordinate event reports, notes, recordings, and other learning outputs, ensuring they are accurate, accessible, appropriately edited and shared. Manage communications with Grantee Partners and other audiences through CRM systems including Constant Contact, Circle, and other digital channels. Use AI assisted tools appropriately to support drafting, translation and content repurposing, ensuring outputs are reviewed for accuracy, inclusivity, and quality. Contribute to the development of AmplifyChange’s Learn and other digital learning resources. Work with colleagues, Grantee Partners facilitators, technical experts and external providers to develop high-quality learning materials, case studies, and knowledge products rooted in partner experience and evidence. Capture, organise and share learning from events, programmes and community activities to support organisational learning and knowledge management. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Use feedback, evidence and reflection to understand what's working and continually improve the learning and community experience for Grantee Partners. Work closely with the Learning, Monitoring and Evaluation Manager to collect, analyse, and report on participant feedback and learning outcomes. Monitor participant experience and engagement across learning events, programmes and digital platforms, identifying opportunities to strengthen participation and engagement. Lead reflection and continuous improvement activities. ensuring learning from evaluations and community engagement to shape future events, programmes and resources Safeguarding, Data Protection and Security Help create safe, inclusive and accessible learning and community spaces, ensuring activities are delivered in line with AmplifyChange's safeguarding, data protection and information security requirements. Ensure all learning and community activities comply with GDPR and AmplifyChange's data protection policies, working with the Operations team and Data Protection advisers as required. Maintain secure digital filing systems and follow organisational information security procedures. Support the development and implementation of appropriate safeguarding, vetting, and event security measures to create safe and inclusive learning environments where required. Organisational Contribution Contribute positively to the wider work and culture of AmplifyChange, collaborating with colleagues and responding flexibly to changing priorities. Work collaboratively across teams, sharing learning and contributing to wider organisational priorities. Contribute flexibly in response to emerging needs and opportunities within a fast-paced environment. You'll undertake any other duties reasonably required that are consistent with the scope and level of the role. Please be aware that some of the SRHR material you will be engage with as part of your role may be of a distressing and sensitive nature. Relevant support is available in this regard. PERSON SPECIFICATION We're looking for an organised, creative and collaborative person who enjoys bringing people together and creating engaging learning experiences. You'll be confident building relationships across cultures and communities, comfortable using digital tools and able to manage multiple activities while keeping people and their experience at the heart of your work. You'll bring strong communication skills, curiosity and a proactive approach, with an interest in finding new ways for people to connect, share knowledge and learn from one another. The candidate should possess the following: Essential A commitment to AmplifyChange's vision, mission and values, including support for sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender equality, LGBTQI+ rights and diverse and inclusive social movements. Professional-level written French and confidence speaking French, alongside excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Experience of coordinating and delivering engaging learning activities, events or programmes across online, in-person and/or hybrid formats. Experience of building and supporting engagement within online communities or networks. Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and coordinate activities involving a range of internal and external stakeholders. Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and sensitively with people from different countries, cultures and backgrounds. Confident using digital collaboration and engagement platforms, with the ability and willingness to learn new technologies. Strong facilitation, presentation and communication skills, with the confidence to engage different audiences and support inclusive participation. Ability to develop clear, engaging and accessible content and learning materials for different audiences. Good judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to ensure content and activities are accurate, inclusive and appropriate, particularly when working with sensitive topics. A proactive, collaborative and adaptable approach, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment. Desirable Experience of developing digital learning content, including using Canva, Learning Management Systems, video or similar tools. Experience of working with external facilitators, technical experts, designers or other suppliers. Experience of using AI-enabled tools to support learning, communications or knowledge management, with an awareness of responsible and ethical use. Experience of working with geographically dispersed communities or networks. Experience of working within international development, sexual and reproductive health and rights, gen

item.title: Night Support Assistant
item.description: About the role: Feeling safe shouldn’t stop mattering when the day team goes home. At St John’s Mansions in Islington, you’ll provide a calm, consistent and reassuring presence throughout the night, helping to make sure clients feel safe, respected and supported in their home. You’ll often be the first person someone turns to if something goes wrong overnight, so the way you respond can make a real difference. As a Night Support Assistant, you’ll take responsibility for the safe and secure running of the service during your shift. You’ll manage access to the building, complete regular patrols and health and safety checks, monitor security, respond to safeguarding concerns and emergencies, and provide a first response to clients who need help. You’ll also support emergency placements where required and make sure significant incidents, concerns and actions are recorded clearly and handed over to the day team. This is a role that calls for sound judgement, resilience and the confidence to stay calm when situations become challenging. At times you may be lone working, with buddy arrangements and SHP’s out-of-hours management support in place. Throughout your work, you’ll take a person-centred, psychologically informed and strengths-based approach, balancing safety and appropriate boundaries with dignity, choice and independence. We have two Night Support Assistant opportunities available: one working four nights per week, Monday to Thursday , and one working three nights per week, Friday to Sunday, night shifts are 10pm - 08.15am . Whichever pattern you join, you’ll be part of the wider St John’s Mansions team, with regular supervision, training and opportunities to continue developing your knowledge and practice. About you: Can build positive, respectful relationships with people from a wide range of backgrounds while maintaining clear and professional boundaries. Is calm, resilient and confident under pressure, able to assess what is happening, prioritise effectively and respond appropriately to incidents or concerns. Understands the importance of safeguarding, health and safety and recovery-focused support, including the ways substance use may affect people’s wellbeing and safety. Can work in a person-centred, strengths-based and psychologically informed way, supporting people to have choice and control wherever possible. Is comfortable working independently, staying alert throughout a night shift and communicating clearly through accurate records and effective handovers. About us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important info: Closing date: Sunday 27th September at midnight Interview date: Tuesday 6th and Wednesday 7th October online via Microsoft Teams Please note there will be a second stage interview in service in Islington for suitable candidates. This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed (by SHP) for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.title: Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator
item.description: About the role: Recovery is about more than addressing immediate needs. It is also about having somewhere to belong, opportunities to build confidence and skills, meaningful connections with other people, and the chance to take part in the community around you. As our Recovery and Opportunities Co-ordinator, you’ll help make those opportunities a reality for people experiencing homelessness and multiple disadvantage in our St John's Mansions service. You’ll develop and coordinate our Recovery and Opportunities programme, creating activities and opportunities that reflect what clients actually want from their services and communities. You’ll work alongside clients, colleagues, volunteers and peer supporters to co-produce activities, build participation and make sure people are supported to get involved in ways that feel meaningful to them. You’ll also help equip others with the confidence, training and resources they need to deliver opportunities effectively. A big part of the role happens beyond our services. You’ll build strong relationships with community organisations, local residents, statutory and voluntary-sector partners and other opportunities across Islington, opening doors for clients to access volunteering, education, cultural activities and wider community life. You’ll represent Single Homeless Project (SHP) at local forums and events, champion social value across our services and look for creative ways we can contribute positively to the communities our clients are part of. You’ll also help us understand what is making a difference, monitoring participation and outcomes and using what we learn to strengthen the programme over time. It’s a role with plenty of scope for creativity and initiative, where you can turn relationships, ideas and client feedback into opportunities that reduce isolation, strengthen belonging and help people move forward with greater confidence, independence and purpose. About you: You have experience engaging and motivating people experiencing multiple disadvantage, including people who may have previously found it difficult to engage with services or opportunities. You can develop, coordinate and facilitate engaging groups, activities or programmes, and understand how to encourage meaningful participation from different people. You’re confident building relationships with community organisations, residents, colleagues and external partners, and can turn those relationships into practical opportunities for clients. You understand the importance of social value and social impact and can think creatively about how services can contribute positively to their local communities. You’re an engaging communicator who can work collaboratively across different teams, represent a service externally and bring people together around a shared goal. About us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. item.title: Charitable Service Lead
item.description: Support, Guide and Lead Services That Change Lives This is your opportunity to provide leadership to services that make a real difference to people, families and communities across Lancashire. Join a values-led organisation where your leadership will help shape services, support talented teams, and create positive, lasting change. At New Era North West, we believe everyone deserves the opportunity to thrive. For over 40 years, we have worked alongside children, young people, adults and families to reduce inequality, improve wellbeing, increase opportunities and build stronger communities. Through our work in employment, skills and education, health and wellbeing, and family and community services, we help people overcome challenges, build resilience and achieve their potential. As our Charitable Service Lead, you will provide strategic and operational leadership across our charitable services, ensuring they remain high quality, responsive and focused on delivering meaningful outcomes. Working closely with the CEO, Operations Manager and Leadership Team, you will provide direction, guidance and support to service managers and practitioners, enabling them to deliver high-quality services that achieve positive outcomes for the people and communities we serve. You'll play a key role in developing confident, capable teams, fostering a positive and supportive culture, and ensuring our services continue to make a lasting difference across Lancashire. This role offers the opportunity to influence the future direction of a respected and growing organisation. You'll lead and support passionate teams, develop strong partnerships, and help create a positive workplace culture where people feel valued, supported and empowered to do their best work. We're looking for someone who can inspire others, bring people together, and balance strategic thinking with a practical approach to leadership. What We Offer Salary: £38,428.46 per annum Contract: Permanent, full-time (37 hours per week) Location: Burnley, Lancashire, with travel across service areas required (essential car user) Annual Leave: 32 days per year The opportunity to shape and influence services that improve lives and strengthen communities. A supportive, values-driven culture built on Care, Support and Belief. The chance to work alongside committed colleagues who are passionate about making a difference. A senior leadership role where your ideas, experience and vision can have a genuine impact. If you are passionate about creating opportunities, supporting communities and leading services that deliver real social impact, we'd love to hear from you. Join us and help challenge inequality, strengthen communities and transform lives.

item.title: Safeguarding Case Officer
item.description: About This Job You will form part of a small satellite team of Safeguarding Case Support Officers (SCSOs). Overseen by a Senior Caseworker Manager, you will assess and decide on safeguarding allegations and concerns within the Army Cadets across Scotland and Northern Ireland. You must be an appropriately qualified and experienced safeguarding professional, capable of conducting child safeguarding investigations and adept at collaborating with multiple agencies. Essential Skills · Diploma or Degree in a relevant subject area. · Evidence of continuing personal and professional development · Front-line safeguarding interventions and/ or risk assessment of perpetrators of abuse. · Sound knowledge of safeguarding interventions. · Understand legislative requirements for safeguarding young people. · Please refer to the attached Job Description for further information. Our charity ACCT UK is a national youth charity dedicated to improving the life chances of young people. The Combined Cadet Force Association (CCFA) is a charity dedicated to the promotion of the ideals and activities of the Combined Cadet Force in schools. Together we want to ensure that every young person has the opportunity to learn new skills, build confidence and be inspired through their cadet experience. We want to develop the youth leadership and training abilities of adult volunteers whilst also helping young people to access cadet activities through fundraising, grant-making, developing new resources and direct support. We strongly believe that everyone benefits when you help young people to develop their character and values through activities that stretch and mature them. We also know that when young people engage with others at a range of levels in their communities it builds confidence and improves empathy for other’s lives. Who we are By joining the charities, you will help us to reach more young people and make a greater difference and we look forward to working with you. We actively promote and encourage you to explore ideas that improve all aspects of the charity’s work in pursuit of its charitable aims. The charities are proud of our diverse teams, with people on different working patterns, from different backgrounds and at different life-stages. Our experience has taught us that having people with different perspectives and different lived experiences leads to better outcomes for our beneficiaries. If you are wondering if our organisation is for someone like you, the answer is yes! Please apply and explain how you, your experience, your talent and your potential are the right fit for this role. What we can offer you In addition to your salary, we offer all staff: · Flexible working arrangements (you agree a working pattern with your line manager). · The ability to work both from home and from our London office. · Personal Accident Insurance, including loss of earnings cover and death benefit. · 15 days of sick pay in any 12-month period (after 12 months employment - pro-rata for part time staff). · A contributory pension scheme (you contribute at least 5% and we will contribute 10%). · Good leave allowances (which are offered pro-rata for part time staff): o 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays. o Additional privilege leave, on set days each year, such as between Christmas and New Year. o An additional five days of volunteering leave. · Support for qualifications and personal development. · Employee Assistance Programme. · Season ticket loan. · Railcard (if you are eligible). · A caring and supportive team environment. How to apply Please send a CV and Cover letter that details how you meet the requirements of the job description by 2359hrs by Sunday 11th October 2026. Interviews will be held shortly after the closing date, in person/virtually TBC – we will let you know if you have progressed. While AI tools can be beneficial, we value the personal touch and authenticity in job applications. We encourage you to highlight your unique experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, ensuring all information is accurate. Please use AI tools responsibly and with integrity throughout the application and selection process. Please note that as a charity dedicated to improving the lives of young people, we require staff to make a declaration about any relevant convictions, undergo a Disclosure and Barring Service check. In addition, we will follow up with references. Please be advised that this position may close earlier than the stated deadline if a sufficient number of high-quality applications are received. To ensure your application is considered, we strongly recommend submitting it as soon as possible. Candidates will be notified of the next stage in the recruitment process if they are shortlisted.

item.title: Digital Analytics Coordinator
item.description: Central London, Greater London (Hybrid) Covent Garden, Greater London £23,055 per year Part-time (21 hours per week ) Permanent Health Job description Are you curious about what digital data can tell us about how people find and engage with content? We’re looking for a Digital Analytics Coordinator to join the Communications Directorate at the Royal College of Radiologists. In this role, you’ll analyse performance across our website, email and social channels, turning complex data into clear insight that helps shape how we plan and evaluate content and campaigns. You’ll also help ensure we’re measuring digital activity effectively, using tools including GA4 and Google Tag Manager to implement and maintain tracking. Working closely with colleagues across the Content and Brand teams, you’ll help us understand what’s working, how our members are engaging with our content and where we can improve. Your insight will help us make evidence-based decisions, test and learn from what we do, and improve the digital experience we provide for our members. What you’ll do: Gather, analyse and present performance data across the College’s digital channels, including website, email and social media Maintain analytics dashboards and produce regular insight highlighting trends, changes in performance and opportunities to improve engagement. Implement, test and maintain tracking through GA4 and Google Tag Manager, ensuring digital activity is measured accurately and consistently. Work with Content and Brand colleagues to establish appropriate measures for campaigns and evaluate performance against agreed objectives and KPIs. Analyse campaign and audience behaviour across digital channels, identifying the content, channels and approaches driving engagement. Use email performance data, segmentation and A/B testing to identify opportunities to improve targeting and engagement. What you’ll need: Experience analysing and interpreting data from digital platforms such as GA4, Search Console, social media and email marketing platforms, and using insight to inform content and marketing decisions. Practical experience of GA4 and Google Tag Manager, including implementing, testing and troubleshooting tracking. Experience creating dashboards, automated reports or data visualisations and measuring performance against objectives and KPIs. Experience using segmentation, A/B testing or dynamic content within an email marketing platform to evaluate and improve performance. Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn complex data into clear, practical recommendations for non-specialist colleagues. Excellent attention to detail, with a strong commitment to data quality and accuracy. A collaborative and organised approach, with the ability to work across teams and manage multiple priorities. Experience in a membership organisation, charity or not-for-profit environment would be beneficial but is not essential. Why work with us? The RCR is a membership organisation and charity that works with our Fellows and members to improve the standard of medical practice across the fields of clinical radiology and clinical oncology. You’ll join a friendly and ambitious organisation with a clear sense of purpose – and a team that’s proud to support doctors working at the heart of cancer and imaging services. When you join us: Make a difference to the lives of Doctors and medical specialties Hybrid working – up to 60% remote Modern working environment with home‑working equipment provided Generous annual leave, plus the option to buy up to 5 extra days Enhanced family‑friendly leave (maternity, paternity and adoption) for those with 2+ years continuous service Excellent pension scheme Sabbaticals (5+ years’ service) and secondment opportunities Interest‑free season ticket loan and cycle to work scheme Employee Assistance Programme Long service recognition awards Posted on: 11 September 2026 Closing date: 28 September 2026 at 00:00 Tags: Communications, Marketing, Digital, Brand, Content Writing / Copywriting

item.title: Head of Service (City Services)
item.description: It is an occupational requirement that applications are open to WOMEN ONLY , as permitted under Schedule 9, Part 1, of the Equality Act 2010. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and actively encourage applications from individuals who are disabled, neurodivergent, or from minoritised ethnic backgrounds. Juno Women’s Aid are a growing organisation with an exciting pipeline of innovative projects and ambitious plans for the future. This is a unique opportunity to join a forward-thinking team and play a key role in driving new ideas and initiatives from concept to delivery. Who We're Looking For We are seeking an experienced operations professional who combines strategic thinking with strong planning, implementation, and project management capabilities. The successful candidate will be an excellent communicator, confident in engaging with a wide range of stakeholders and comfortable with public speaking. You will thrive in a fast-paced, survivor-focused environment, demonstrating the ability to remain calm under pressure while managing a varied and demanding workload. item.title: People Manager
item.description: Harris Hill is delighted to be working on behalf of National Parks Partnerships (NPP) to recruit a People Manager. NPP is a small and entrepreneurial organisation that identifies, secures and manages commercial and strategic partnerships for the UK’s 15 National Parks, helping to grow their impact, resources and influence while supporting action on the climate and biodiversity crises. As NPP continues to grow, this is an exciting opportunity to take ownership of its people function and play a key role in supporting the organisation’s development. The role is offered on a salary of £40,135 FTE ( non-negotiable ) and is available on a full-time basis, with the possibility of working four days per week. This is a one-year fixed-term contract, with the possibility of extension, and is fully remote, with occasional UK travel required. Sitting within the Operations team and reporting to the Head of Operations, the People Manager will lead NPP’s day-to-day HR function as a largely standalone HR professional. You will develop and implement HR strategies, policies and processes across the employee lifecycle, providing trusted advice to the CEO, Head of Operations, SLT and line managers. You will lead recruitment activity, support managers with performance, probation and employee relations processes, oversee annual leave and absence, payroll administration and pay awards, and ensure NPP continues to meet its employment, health and safety and data protection obligations. You will also play an important role in developing organisational culture, embedding NPP’s Manifesto, competency framework and behaviours, and ensuring equality, diversity and inclusion remain central to its people practices. Alongside the core HR remit, you will support the wider Operations team with external agencies, suppliers and procurement activity, including maintaining supplier relationships, supporting purchasing processes and ensuring compliance with relevant procurement requirements. We are looking for an experienced People & Culture professional with a strong track record of developing and implementing HR policies and strategies, managing HR projects, and supporting organisational change, as well as experience leading recruitment processes from job design through to shortlisting and interviewing. You will be a clear thinker, confident decision-maker and excellent communicator who can build strong relationships across an organisation and with external partners. Experience of payroll, EDI, health and safety, procurement or working within a purpose-led organisation or public authority would be advantageous. To apply, please submit your up-to-date CV by 27 September at 23:59. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to submit a tailored cover letter after reviewing the full job description. Please note that only applicants with an unrestricted right to work in the UK will be considered for this position. Please note, only successful applicants will be contacted with further information. As a leading charity recruitment specialist and a certified B Corp™, Harris Hill is committed to high and ever-improving standards of equitable and inclusive recruitment. We actively welcome applications from all sections of the community regardless of age, disability, gender, race, religion, sexuality and other protected characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Harris Hill Charity Recruitment Specialists

item.title: IDVA
item.description: Are you looking for a dynamic and rewarding role working for an organisation with the feminist agenda at the core of its ethos? Then Advance Charity could be the career choice for you! We are looking for a Peripatetic IDVA to join our team in London. In this role you will move between teams supporting different domestic abuse services dependent on need. This is a great opportunity to develop varied experience within a supportive and collaborative team environment. Job Title: Peripatetic IDVA Salary: £28,000 - £35,000 per annum. The salary offered will be dependant on your level of experience and whether you hold an IDVA qualification Hours: 35 hours (1-2 days per week working from home depending on placement) Location: Various locations across London; including some time spent in Hammersmith Contract Type: Permanent This post is open to female applicants only as this is deemed a genuine occupational requirement under Schedule 9, Paragraph 1 of the Equality Act 2010. Please note : Any offer of employment will be made subject to references, confirmation of the right to work in the UK, and satisfactory enhanced DBS check. In the future, this role may be subject to Police Vetting but this check will not delay your start in the role. Job Summary Advance delivers nationally accredited, high quality domestic abuse services across London. Advance's domestic abuse services are community based and include local authority commissioned advocacy services, co-located projects in a range of settings such as housing and children’s social care, and specialist projects for victim/survivors with different intersecting needs including children and young people. As a Peripatetic Independent Domestic Violence Advocate (IDVA), you will provide front line support across Advance’s domestic abuse services, covering vacancies across teams to ensure service delivery remains effective and consistent. You will cover a range of roles all involving advocacy and support of people experiencing domestic abuse; some roles may also involve co-locating with partner agencies, delivering training or undertaking triage and assessment work. Your office location and pattern of work will change depending on your placement however all roles offer the opportunity for some hybrid working. This role is an excellent opportunity to develop skills, knowledge and experience in a range of settings and would suit someone who is passionate about advocating for victim/survivors of domestic abuse. You will thrive in fast-paced environments and enjoy the diversity of working across a range of roles within different teams. An excellent understanding of domestic violence and its effects on women and children is essential, alongside some past experience working directly with victim/survivors of domestic abuse. About You To be successful as the Peripatetic IDVA you will need the below experience and skills: Youwill have an excellent understanding of domestic violence and its effects on women and children and of best practice within the domestic abuse in various areas of need, with particular knowledge of safeguarding and legislation. As an experienced domestic violence advocate who has worked with complex and multiple needs, the post holder will be skilled in risk management and safety planning, remaining calm in a crisis and in handling sensitive information on a daily basis. Experience of direct work with female survivors of domestic violence, of supporting women with child safeguarding, needs, and of working within safeguarding procedures is essential for this post, as is the need to adopt and promote a strong partnership approach to service provision. How to apply: Please submit your up-to-date CV with a supporting statement. Please note that only applications made via the job advert on the Advance careers page, and those that include a cover letter will be considered. Closing Date for Applications: Sunday 27th September 2026* Interviews are taking place on a rolling basis *Advance reserves the right to close the advert early, or on the appointment of a candidate What we can offer you - Employee Benefits: An exceptional 30 days of paid holiday per year (pro rata for part time), PLUS public holidays on top (that's nearly 40 days paid holiday per year!) Additional days off to celebrate International Women’s Day, and for religious observance and moving home Perkbox - an employee discount platform where you can receive free rewards as well as take advantage of savings on clothes, groceries, travel, leisure and more Pension scheme Enhanced maternity/adoption provision Access to our Employee Assistance Programme Employee eye-care scheme Clinical supervision for front line staff and first line management roles Refer a Friend Scheme - £250 for each referral who passes probation Organisation wide away days Thorough induction and training Career development pathways ************************************************************** Under the Equality Act 2010, we are required to make any reasonable adjustments. If you have a disability as defined under this act and/or have special needs, please email the Talent Acquisition Team via the Advance website and will aim to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate your needs. Diversity, Inclusion and Equal Opportunities We are committed to providing equality of opportunity and actively seek to recruit people from groups underrepresented in our current team. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay and benefits. Safeguarding Advance is committed to safeguarding and creating a culture of zero-tolerance of harm and expects all staff, including volunteers to share this commitment. We believe all individuals have the right to live their life free from violence and abuse and the right to feel and be safe. We have a suite of safeguarding policies, procedures and practice guidance, accessible to all staff, which promotes safeguarding and safer working practices across all our services and activities. When we recruit staff, we follow rigorous safer recruitment practices, this involves carrying out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks, and identity checks. We ensure all staff undertake mandatory safeguarding training relevant to their role and responsibilities, to empower them to be competent and feel confident in recognising and responding appropriately to safeguarding issues and promote wellbeing.

item.title: Community Hub Activities Coordinator
item.description: Join the Renewal Programme as our Community Hub Activities Coordinator and help bring people aged 55+ together through guided walks, social activities and our Community Connection Café. We’re looking for a warm, organised and community-focused person who can build trusted relationships and help residents feel welcomed, connected and supported. The Community Hub Activities Coordinator will lead the day-to-day coordination of a one-year walking, wellbeing and social connection programme for Newham residents aged 55 and over. The programme combines a weekly accessible guided walk, delivered in partnership with other external partners with a weekly Community Connection Café facilitated by the postholder. The postholder will build trusted relationships with residents who may be isolated, inactive, recently bereaved, living with long-term health conditions or lacking confidence to join community activities. They will coordinate outreach, referrals, venues, volunteers, safeguarding, signposting and monitoring so that participants receive a safe, welcoming and inclusive experience. The role will ensure that walking is a gateway to friendship, confidence, healthier ageing and wider practical support. How to apply Please submit your CV and a cover letter addressing each of the points in the person specification. Submissions without a cover letter will not be considered. We aim to interview candidates on a rolling basis until the post is filled. We may close the ad sooner than initially advertised if a successful appointment is made. The selection process will consist of Shortlisting based on competences matched to the person specification and the JD Competence based interview and work-based test Provisional job offers are conditional upon receipt of satisfactory references, one of which must be from current or most recent employer, and a DBS check.

item.title: Head of Finance and Sustainability
item.description: An exciting full time opportunity has opened up at CPSL Mind. CPSL Mind is a vibrant, values-led charity that supports local people in their recovery from mental health issues, promotes wellbeing and campaigns against stigma and discrimination. Head of Finance and Sustainability Hours: Full Time, 37.5 hours per week Salary Scale Point: 33 Salary: £42,525.00 per annum Based: in Cambridge or Peterborough with hybrid working options. About CPSL Mind Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and South Lincolnshire (CPSL) Mind is a progressive and expanding mental health charity. Our vision is a society in which everyone has positive mental health and feels part of a connected community. Our work ranges from prevention and early intervention to award-winning crisis support. We also seek to influence positive change through our training services and ground-breaking campaigns activity. About the Role As a key part of CPSL Mind’s Senior Leadership Team, this role will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization financial management, ensuring robust governance, financial sustainability and informed decision making across the charity. You will lead the finance function, ensuring the highest standards of financial control, compliance, reporting and operational efficiency, while driving a culture of financial accountability throughout the organization. Alongside this, you will oversee our income generation portfolio, including fundraising, training and events, ensuring these functions contribute to a diversified and sustainable income base. You will also lead our broader approach to financial sustainability, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, strengthen commercial decision making, maximise value for money and ensure every pound delivers the greatest possible impact for the communities we serve. Key Criteria You must have: a relevant accounting qualification, e.g. ACA, CIMA, ACCA experience of managing budgets and detailed reporting on financial performance/forecasting experience of working with and presenting to Trustees, Directors and Senior Leaders Closing date: 11th October 2026 Interview Date: 22nd October 2026 in Cambridge Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. CPSL Mind is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. We actively promote equality of opportunity for all with the right mix of talent, skills and potential and welcome applications from a wide range of candidates, including those with criminal records. Having a criminal record will not necessarily bar you from working with us. This will depend on the nature of the position and the circumstances and background of your offences. CPSL Mind is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults at risk. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment and work in accordance with our safeguarding policies and procedures. No agencies please.

item.title: Senior Care Coordinator
item.description: Contract: Permanent Hours: Part time (21 hours per week) Location: London Centre Starting salary: £29,004 to £33,645 (FTE £48,340 - £56,075) Closing date: 12/10/2026 Expected date of interviews: 22/10/2026 Freedom from Torture is the Winner of the Overall Award for Excellence and the top prize for Campaigns and Advocacy at the 2023 Charity Awards. We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Care Coordinator to support in our clinical service delivery. Many of our clients have complex needs and this role ensures that clients acquire the support they need to receive multi-agency services. Would you like to join our award-winning organisation? About the role The role involves managing the care coordination service area assessment and organising the allocation of care-coordination tasks, working alongside the Adult Team Manager and Clinical Services Manager as part of the intake panel and holding a caseload offering care coordination to survivors of torture. This role ensures that service users at Freedom from Torture have a central role in planning their care planning and are supported to access the most appropriate support for their needs. Working together with our therapists, and legal and welfare staff as part of a multi-disciplinary team, the ideal candidate will be a Registered Mental Health Nurse, Social Worker or Occupational Therapist with significant experience of working in the mental health sector with complex mental health presentations and will have a passion for working with asylum seekers, refugees and survivors of torture. The role will include delivering line management and supervision to care co-ordinators within the team and may at times include delivering supervision to social work students, lived experience support workers as well as other clinical staff and approved volunteers. The Senior Care coordinator also works closely with the national pain lead in support of pain management for our clients, which involves linking with, GPs, community physio services and at times the role may include running and facilitating 1:1 and group psychological pain management interventions or stabilisation strategies alongside clinical colleagues. The role will also involve providing clinical manager cover – i.e. on-site managerial cover and duty cover in line with the clinical cover procedure, and to provide guidance for clinicians with urgent queries. The Senior Care coordinator will work alongside the National safeguarding leads to support clients and colleagues by attending internal and external safeguarding/ child protection meetings and provide consultation to line reports and other colleagues around managing safeguarding concerns and regularly updating and reviewing our internal safeguarding tracker. About you In return, we offer a competitive package, with a generous 30-day annual leave entitlement, and 6% employer pension contribution (minimum 1% employee contribution). Freedom from Torture is committed to showing the salary for all advertised roles and not negotiating salaries for roles, in light of evidence that this contributes to structural inequality. Our policy is that all appointments will be at the start of the salary range but successful candidates will have the opportunity to move up the scale over time. The progression up the salary range is reviewed on an annual basis and subject to affordability. For this role, the salary range is £29,004 to £33,645 (FTE £48,340 - £56,075). Please note a CV and a cover letter addressing the job description and person specification of the role are mandatory to be considered for the position. Freedom from Torture is dedicated to healing and protecting people who have survived torture. We provide therapies to improve physical and mental health, we medically document torture, and we provide legal and welfare help. We expose torture globally, we fight to hold torturing states to account and we campaign for fairer treatment of torture survivors in the UK. We campaign for national and global change, using evidence from our services and survivor voices to protect and promote survivors' rights and hold torturing states to account. We are proud to play a significant role in the global anti-torture movement. Survivors, active and empowered, are at the centre of all of our work. Freedom from Torture is committed to its responsibilities under safeguarding, and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. This post is subject to a satisfactory enhanced DBS disclosure, as well as a need for full employment history and up to date employment references. This post is subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (Exceptions Order) 1975 and as such it will be necessary for a submission for Disclosure to be made to the Disclosure and Barring Service (formerly known as CRB) to check for any previous criminal convictions.) Freedom from Torture is an equal opportunity employer. People with lived experience of torture or asylum, from Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds, LGBTQIA+ individuals and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. No agencies please.
item.dc:creator: Freedom from Torture

item.title: Fundraising Manager
item.description: Job description Role Purpose The Fundraising Manager will drive fundraising growth for YMCA Lincolnshire, a well-established charity working to improve the lives of children and young people, families, local communities and those at risk of homelessness. Reporting to the Head of Income Generation, you will lead the delivery of YMCA Lincolnshire's Fundraising Strategy and be responsible for achieving agreed income targets across a diverse range of income streams. You will grow income through individual giving, corporate partnerships, trusts and foundations, community fundraising, events and campaigns, while strengthening donor stewardship, supporter journeys and the effective use of our Beacon CRM. Working collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation, you will translate service delivery outcomes into compelling cases for support and build meaningful relationships with supporters, funders, businesses and community groups. You will ensure all fundraising activity is compliant, insight-led and aligned with YMCA Lincolnshire's mission, values and strategic objectives. The closing date is Friday 25th September 2026 at 5pm. Applications will be shortlisted as they are submitted, so this position may close early should the right candidate be found.
