item.title: Area Teams Manager
item.description: Hope Nottingham's vision is to inspire and grow communities of hope across Nottingham where local people are enabled to volunteer to support those in need, addressing poverty of resources, reducing loneliness and providing spiritual support. We are rooted in our Christian faith and currently have a staff team of 9 and support over 320 volunteers in teams across Nottingham. We are looking for an energetic, compassionate, highly organised and values-led Charity Area Teams Manager to lead and inspire our staff, volunteers, and service delivery teams, as they deliver practical help, community connection and Christian care across our food banks, hubs and community activities. In this pivotal role, you will oversee the effective management of team operations, ensuring that service standards are consistently met and that our charitable initiatives reach those in need. You will ensure activities are safe, welcoming, well-planned and aligned with Hope Nottingham's vision, mission, values and Theory of Change. Responsibilities Lead and support staff through objectives, reviews, training and wellbeing conversations Recruit, induct, develop and engage volunteers and volunteer leaders Oversee service delivery across multiple locations, maintaining safe, inclusive and welcoming standards, focused on making a real difference in our communities Act as Safeguarding Coordinator and escalate concerns appropriately Use feedback and impact information to improve support, training and delivery Uphold and promote Hope Nottingham's Christian ethos while welcoming people of all faiths and none Ensure compliance with organisational policies, safety standards, and legal requirements across all service activities. Foster strong relationships with community partners, stakeholders, and local organisations to enhance outreach efforts. Monitor operational metrics and prepare reports to evaluate team performance, identify areas for improvement, and celebrate successes. Skills Proven team management, volunteering and service delivery experience in a charity, community, church or social action setting. Approachable and confident communication skills both verbally and in writing to represent the organisation both compassionately and professionally Ability to lead diverse teams effectively in a fast-paced environment, balancing compassion with accountability Strong organisational skills with the capacity to manage multiple priorities simultaneously Ability to adapt quickly to changing circumstances while maintaining focus on service quality Demonstrable commitment to community service and organisational values. Proficiency in using office 365 and service related software A full driving license and access to a car are essential. 28 days holiday per year (includes 3 days between Christmas and New Year) + bank holidays, Life Assurance, 3.5% employer pension contribution, wellbeing scheme including access to counselling and bi-annual staff team retreat days. There is a genuine occupational requirement under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, for the postholder to be a practising Christian because the role supports Hope Nottingham's Christian ethos, prayer, chaplaincy and faith-based activities. If you are passionate about developing people, volunteering and community transformation, we would love to hear from you.
item.dc:creator: Hope Nottingham CIO

item.title: Operations and Membership Lead
item.description: About us The Alliance for Youth Justice is an alliance of more than 70 non-profit organisations advocating with and for children to drive positive change in youth justice across England and Wales. We mobilise our members’ frontline expertise, children’s lived experience, and evidence from research to champion a child-centred, rights-based and trauma-informed system that treats contact with the justice system as a sign of unmet need and systemic failure, prioritises support over criminalisation and gives every child the opportunity to thrive. We're widely recognised as the most influential group campaigning for improvements to the system, with trusted access to decision makers, working towards three goals: keeping children safe from the youth justice system through prevention and diversion; racial justice across the system; and custody as a last resort for children. About the role Following the launch of our new strategic approach, our Operations and Membership Lead will provide the operational, financial and administrative backbone of the organisation — keeping our finances and governance on track, and coordinating our network of over 70 member organisations. Finance, operations and governance (70%) — manage bookkeeping in QuickBooks, coordinate banking, prepare management accounts, support grant financial reporting, maintain internal systems (SharePoint, IT), lead on policy compliance (safeguarding, GDPR, health and safety), and support Board governance and statutory filings. Membership coordination (30%) — manage the end-to-end membership process from enquiries to renewals, coordinate member surveys and data, and organise our events — quarterly member meetings, roundtables and webinars. Anti-racist, anti-oppressive practice runs through how we work with our Board, staff, members and stakeholders. About you You have experience in an operations, finance or administrative coordination role within a non-profit or membership organisation, including managing the full financial cycle within a charity and a working knowledge of charity fund accounting. You're practically experienced with QuickBooks (or equivalent), highly proficient in Microsoft 365, SharePoint and Excel-based tracking systems or CRMs, and bring exceptional organisational skills, discretion and a proactive, self-motivated approach. You have a personal commitment to anti-racism, social justice and child rights. Why join us We're a small team of three punching well above our weight, with real scope to shape how we work and few layers of hierarchy. We offer flexible, trust-based home working (within core hours), plus 25 days' leave (pro rata), Christmas office closure, and a 5% employer pension contribution. We encourage applications from historically marginalised groups even if you don't meet every requirement, and we do not use criminal records to exclude candidates. Please download the reruitment pack to find out more and read the full job description and person specification.
item.dc:creator: Alliance for Youth Justice

item.title: Head of Digital
item.description: Ready to transform how supporters connect with women’s health? Harris Hill is supporting Wellbeing of Women to find their new Head of Digital. This is an opportunity for a digital expert to put digital at the heart of a charity’s growth — helping Wellbeing of Women reach more people, deepen supporter engagement and drive fundraising and advocacy. We’re looking for an experienced, strategic and hands-on digital leader to lead the digital function within the Income and Engagement team. You’ll shape and deliver an ambitious digital strategy, mapping and improving the supporter journey to turn audiences into engaged supporters, donors and advocates. From website, email and social media to PPC, paid social and digital analytics, you’ll bring insight and innovation to every channel — using data to understand what’s working, optimise performance and increase engagement and conversion. You’ll work closely with colleagues across income generation, research, education and external affairs, as well as leading agency relationships, to make sure digital is fully integrated across the organisation and firmly focused on delivering fundraising and engagement objectives. You will also line manage the Social Media Coordinator. If you’re a digital leader who combines strategic thinking with a love of data, optimisation and getting things done, this could be your next big move. I’m especially keen to hear from individuals with knowledge of the women’s health landscape, but it’s not a pre-requisite. Salary £50,000- £55,000 Full-time, permanent position. Hybrid working between London Bridge office (minimum 2 days per week) and remote working Attractive benefits package including private health care, employee discount scheme and cycle to work scheme Interested? We’d love to hear from you. Closing date: 9am Monday 28 th September, however please apply early to receive the full job pack. As leading charity recruitment specialists and a certified B Corp™, Harris Hill is committed to high and ever-improving standards of equitable and inclusive recruitment. We actively welcome applications from all sections of the community regardless of age, disability, gender, race, religion, sexuality and other protected characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Harris Hill Charity Recruitment Specialists

item.title: Senior Programme Coordinator
item.description: North-West GCSE Resits Senior Programme Coordinator Our charity delivers a series of interventions that help disadvantaged learners in Further Education to secure gateway English and maths qualifications that unlock opportunities. These interventions include our award-winning GCSE Resit Tuition Programme, for those resitting GCSEs, our Functional Skills Tuition Programme, supporting those on or aspiring to undertake apprenticeship programmes, and training and resources to support teachers and leaders of English and maths in Further Education. Our benefits include: About the role As a Senior Programme Coordinator, you will lead the day-to-day delivery across a portfolio of partner colleges. Acting as the main point of contact for students, tutors and college staff, you will build strong working relationships, maintain a consistent on-site presence and ensure programmes are delivered smoothly, professionally and in line with agreed standards and KPIs. You will take ownership of programme performance across your portfolio, with a particular focus on student enrolment, attendance, and session dosage targets. You will oversee programme logistics, monitor delivery quality, and work proactively to maximise student participation and tutor effectiveness. This role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to operational challenges. You will also play an important role in maintaining high-quality partnerships with colleges, ensuring stakeholders receive clear communication, accurate reporting and responsive support throughout programme delivery. Alongside this, you will contribute to wider organisational priorities, including safeguarding, tutor development, programme improvement and initiatives that strengthen student outcomes. As a Senior Programme Coordinator, you will be expected to role model best practice to the wider Programme Coordinator team, working collaboratively to problem solve, and work with your Programme Manager to ensure strategic approaches to meeting KPIs. This is a highly collaborative, delivery-focused role suited to someone who enjoys a challenge, is confident managing relationships. MAIN DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES See recruitment pack ABOUT YOU You will: Thrive in a busy, fast-paced environment and enjoy managing multiple priorities effectively. Be passionate about improving outcomes for young people, with a genuine commitment to tackling educational inequality. Enjoy working collaboratively with colleagues, tutors and college partners to achieve shared goals. Be comfortable working independently, taking ownership of your workload and delivering results with minimal supervision. Demonstrate initiative and a proactive approach, identifying opportunities and resolving challenges effectively. Be highly organised, detail-oriented and able to manage competing demands without compromising quality. Take accountability for your work and be confident making decisions and driving progress. Be resilient, adaptable and solutions-focused when responding to challenges. Be motivated by working in a mission-driven organisation where your contribution has a direct impact on learners' success and future opportunities. The closing date for applications is 9:00am on Monday 28 September. Applications received after this time will not be considered. NEXT STEPS Suitable candidates will be contacted after the closing date. Screening calls will take place on the Thursday 1st & Friday 2nd October. These will take place online. The first-round interviews will be held online on Tuesday 6th October & Wednesday 7th October , followed by a second in-person interview Thursday 15th October (London). You will be able to expense your travel for this interview. We value diversity and actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, particularly individuals from ethnically diverse communities who are currently underrepresented in our sector. We are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels they belong. For full details on responsibilities please see the recruitment pack.
item.dc:creator: Get Further

item.title: Engagement Officer
item.description: Job title: Engagement Officer Department: External Relations Responsible to: External Relations and Communications Manager Location: London (UK) - Hybrid working Salary: £32,500 gross per annum Working pattern: Full-time, 38.5 hours per week Duration of contract: Permanent Start date: As soon as possible Do you enjoy creating connections and turning them into opportunities? Join our dynamic team as an Engagement Officer at UWC International, where you will play a crucial role in the External Relations team. With over 90,000 alumni worldwide, you'll collaborate with colleagues from our 18 schools across four continents and UWC International to connect alumni who are making a difference at local, national, and international levels. We are seeking someone with experience in alumni engagement who is eager to grow and develop with us. This role is central to identifying and connecting with the alumni community, creating opportunities for collaboration, sharing impactful stories, and expanding our reach. With the support of senior colleagues your work will involve key areas, including the UWC hub and events such as our Impact Forums and UWC Day. You will work closely with the External Relations and Communications Manager, the Head of External Relations, and the Chief of Staff, as well as colleagues in the Development, Funded Programmes, and Education teams. The ideal candidate should be a people person who is passionate about helping talented young people access education, regardless of their background, and be committed to bringing together changemakers from around the world. You will also be a self-starter, innovative and curious who can support the growth and expansion of our engagement activities. If this is you, please do not hesitate to apply. About us Changing the world takes passion and dedication UWC is a global movement of 18 schools across four continents with a shared mission: to make education a force for peace and a sustainable future. Each year, we bring together young people from over 150 countries and diverse backgrounds to live and learn together in richly diverse, international settings – developing not only academic excellence, but cross-cultural understanding and a drive for social impact. UWC students don’t just prepare for exams, they prepare to lead change. Through real-world challenges, they build the skills, compassion and courage to make a difference. Our students go on to become leaders in politics, NGOs, business, education and grassroots movements – people shaping a more just and sustainable world. Today, our global network includes more than 85,000 changemakers united by the values they lived at UWC. About UWC International UWC International is the operational arm of UWC, a UK-registered and Germany-registered charity at the heart of the global UWC movement. Based in London and Berlin, our team works closely with stakeholders across the UWC network and supports a global alumni community of over 85,000 changemakers. Our work includes global fundraising, communications, promotion and support for the network of more than 150 UWC national committees. We also lead on global strategy and provide key services to UWC schools and colleges. We are proud to reflect the diversity we champion. Our international team represents over 25 nationalities, bringing a wide range of perspectives and lived experiences. We are committed to anti-racism, diversity, equity and inclusion (ARDEI) across all aspects of our work – ensuring our organisational culture reflects the values we promote across the UWC movement. What we offer As part of a commitment to our employees, we offer the following: UWC International London Hybrid working - we operate hybrid working arrangements, with at least 20% of the week in the office and up to 80% working from home . Flexible working hours - our standard working hours are 38.5 per week. We support flexible working and are happy to discuss different working patterns. Generous annual leave allowance – we offer 28 days holiday per year plus 8 public holidays (pro rata for part-time or fixed-term contracts). Paid leave for personal growth - up to 2 days per year for volunteering or up to 2 days per year for study leave. Learning & development opportunities – we have access to various learning and development platforms to support your professional growth, as well as a budget set aside for professional development. Enhanced sick pay In-person meetings : Yearly Staff Away Days, team retreats and travel to our international schools and international events as needed to create connected teams. Income Protection & well-being support - We offer income protection to all employees, an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) with access to a legal support helpline, remote GP appointments, medical second opinions, mental health support, physiotherapy, lifestyle coaching, personal trainer and nutritionist sessions, and a well-being calendar featuring podcasts and webinars. Exclusive discounts & perks - with access to a range of discounts across shopping, dining, lifestyle and entertainment, with thousands of offers on hundreds of top retailers. Cycle scheme and eyecare vouchers Enhanced maternity and enhanced paternity leave Higher-than-standard pension contribution scheme - UWC International will contribute up to 8% of the employee’s gross salary toward their Pension scheme with NEST in the UK. Visa requirements Anyone who applies to work at UWC International in London must have a work visa before starting employment, in compliance with the relevant immigration rules. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Please provide confirmation of your eligibility to indefinitely work or reside in the UK in your application. If you are planning to be USA based, please make this known in your application. Any offers of employment made by UWC International will be subject to a right-to-work check on your immigration status. Application Process Do you want to be part of our team? To apply, please submit an up-to-date copy of your CV along with a cover letter in English (each a maximum of 2 pages): Your cover letter must: Outline your experience, skills and competencies against the Person specification section in the attached Job Description . Explain why you want to join UWC International. Confirm your eligibility to work or reside in the UK. Provide the name and contact details of two professional referees , including their job title, email address and the capacity in which you are known to them. References are taken up prior to the second round interviews. We will not contact your referees without first letting you know. Please note that CVs received without a cover letter, including the information requested above will not be considered. Deadline for application: 10:00 AM UK time, Monday 5 October 2026 Interview and/or assessment dates: First round interviews week commencing 12 October (remote) Second round interviews week commencing 19 October (remote) Safeguarding Statement The job holder might have to travel to UWC schools and colleges. Therefore, a Basic DBS check (Disclosure and Barring Service) or international equivalent will be required before any job offer is made. We will also take up references before the second stage of the interview process. Referees will not be contacted without your consent. Diversity Statement UWC places deliberate diversity at the heart of our educational model because of its critical importance in our mission ‘to unite people, nations and cultures for peace and a sustainable future’. At the UWC International Office, we believe this commitment to deliberate diversity must be reflected within our team, organisational practices, policies and culture. We recognise people with different backgrounds, skills, attitudes and experiences bring fresh ideas and perceptions, and we encourage and leverage these differences to make our work more relevant and accessible. We will not discriminate or tolerate discriminatory behaviour on any grounds such as, but not limited to, race, gender, disability, nationality, national or ethnic origin, religion or belief, marital/partnership or family status, sexual orientation, age or socioeconomic background. We strive to be an inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging, has a voice, can raise concerns, and feels comfortable and confident. We expect everyone who works with us to share this commitment and to act accordingly as we aspire best to serve the UWC mission and our global community. It is an ongoing journey and we welcome all those ready to travel with us.

item.title: Active Essex Foundation Impact Lead
item.description: You will have autonomy and will need to help guide the team, shape priorities, and will be working closely with Foundation colleagues delivery partners, funders and communities, the postholder will lead on the collection, analysis and communication of evidence to demonstrate impact, improve delivery and inform future investment decisions. This role will work closely with the Impact Manager and Sport for Development Officer. The role will support a range of programmes including: The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring that learning and evidence are translated into action, helping Active Essex Foundation maximise its impact and continuously improve its programmes. You will be a self starter with strong motivation to drive the work. Active Essex Foundation is a successful and growing charity dedicated to creating the conditions for young people and communities across Essex to thrive. Our work focuses on three core areas: improving young people’s mental health, reducing vulnerabilities to youth crime and exploitation, and strengthening communities through trusted relationships and positive engagement. We collaborate with a network of over 100 community organisations and local partners to design and deliver programmes that use physical activity, mentoring and community support as tools to build resilience, improve wellbeing and reduce inequalities. Active Essex Foundation is a successful and growing charity dedicated to creating the conditions for young people and communities across Essex to thrive. Our work focuses on three core areas: improving young people’s mental health, reducing vulnerabilities to youth crime and exploitation, and strengthening communities through trusted relationships and positive engagement. We collaborate with a network of over 100 community organisations and local partners to design and deliver programmes that use physical activity, mentoring and community support as tools to build resilience, improve wellbeing and reduce inequalities. item.title: PR and Media Officer
item.description: About Scotland's Charity Air Ambulance Scotland’s Charity Air Ambulance (SCAA) exists so nobody in Scotland suffers or dies because medical help cannot get there in time. People can get sick or have accidents anywhere and anytime. But in Scotland there are places where urgent medical help cannot reach people. Or help gets there too late. And when lives are at risk every minute matters. As a charity we rely on donations from the Scottish public, companies and communities to ensure that urgent medical help gets to the patient when it is needed, wherever they are and at whatever time of day. The Role We are seeking a confident media and communications professional to join our Marketing and Communications team and lead PR and media activity across SCAA. Reporting to the Marketing and Communications Manager, the successful candidate will secure impactful media coverage, manage press enquiries, build relationships with journalists and stakeholders, support and brief spokespeople, and develop compelling stories that showcase the charity's impact. Working collaboratively across the organisation, they will play a key role in delivering our communications strategy and increasing awareness, engagement and support for SCAA’s mission. This role will be based in Perth, at Scone Airport. SCAA supports flexible and hybrid working arrangements—our current approach typically includes two office days per week for those working on a hybrid basis. The usual hours of work will be Monday—Friday, 9am—5pm but it should be noted that this role will require the successful candidate to occasionally work at weekends and during the evenings. This role will also require the successful candidate to travel regularly to operational locations and media opportunities within Scotland, sometimes at short notice, and to undertake media on-call duties as part of a rotational rota. About You Essential Experience working in journalism, public relations, communications or a press office environment. A strong track record of securing positive media coverage and developing relationships with journalists and media outlets. Excellent writing and storytelling skills, with experience creating engaging content for print, digital and broadcast channels. Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to work with senior leaders, spokespeople and external partners. Sound editorial judgement and the ability to communicate sensitive stories with empathy, professionalism and discretion. Highly organised, able to manage multiple projects and deadlines, and remain calm under pressure. A collaborative approach, with excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build effective relationships across teams. Commitment to the values and mission of Scotland's Charity Air Ambulance, with the flexibility to travel across Scotland as required. Please refer to the full person specification and job description for more information. Our Benefits Pension: 12% employer’s & 5% employee’s contribution (after 3 months’ service) Annual Leave: 36 days (incl. public holidays) + an extra day for your birthday (and additional days with long service) Death in Service benefit: 4 times annual salary Optional Private Medical Insurance plan and Cashplan Employee Assistance Programme Enhanced Maternity/Adoption/Paternity Pay Access to Blue Light Card Learning and Development Opportunities Selection Process Interviews will take place at our base at Perth Airport in Scone during the week commencing the 12 October 2026. How to apply Please refer to the full job pack on our website. Application deadline is 5pm on Sunday 4 October 2026.

item.title: Sport for Development Officer
item.description: Active Essex Foundation is a successful and growing charity dedicated to creating the conditions for young people and communities across Essex to thrive. Our work focuses on three core areas: improving young people’s mental health, reducing vulnerabilities to youth crime and exploitation, and strengthening communities through trusted relationships and positive engagement. A defining feature of our approach is our network of more than 100 Locally Trusted Organisations (LTOs) across Essex. These community-based organisations are at the heart of our delivery model, providing trusted relationships, local insight and direct support within the communities they serve. Working closely with our LTO network enables us to reach those who may be least likely to engage with traditional services and ensure support is tailored to local needs. Through partnerships with our LTOs, we deliver programmes that use physical activity, mentoring and community support to build resilience, improve wellbeing and reduce inequalities. This role will play a key part in developing and strengthening these relationships, helping our LTO network to maximise its impact and deliver positive outcomes for young people and communities across Essex. Everything we do is shaped by the real experiences of the people we serve, ensuring our interventions are meaningful, accessible and rooted in what communities tell us they need. Active Essex Foundation works to improve life chances for young people and communities across Essex by focusing on three core areas: mental health , youth crime prevention , and strengthening communities . Through our programme structure, we co-design community-led initiatives that use physical activity and positive engagement as tools to build resilience, improve wellbeing and reduce inequalities. The Sport for Development Officer will play a key role in supporting the delivery and growth of these programmes. Working closely with our programme leads, locally trusted organisations (LTOs), and community stakeholders, the postholder will help strengthen organisational capability, and ensure high-quality delivery across our mental health, youth crime prevention and community strengthening work. The role will also contribute to the leadership of workstreams aligned with our strategic Outcomes, supporting the Foundation’s mission. The ideal candidate will bring strong relationship-building skills and experience of working collaboratively with a diverse range of stakeholders. They should demonstrate a track record of delivering impactful projects or initiatives at local or county level, applying a systems approach to complex community issues, and using strengths-based methods to build resilience and capacity within local organisations. The post holder will work with AEF staff across the business to deliver the duties and responsibilities set out below.

We’re looking for a strategic, creative and hands-on communications leader to join Wellbeing of Women’s Senior Management Team and lead its Education and External Affairs teams. You’ll shape and deliver an ambitious multi-channel communications, campaigns, marketing and external affairs strategy — raising the charity’s profile, influencing public debate and engaging the audiences and stakeholders who matter most. item.title: Marketing & Content Manager
item.description: Great marketing connects organisational priorities with the people we need to reach. This 9-month maternity-cover role will lead integrated campaigns and high-quality content that build awareness, strengthen trust and support the impact of Southern Hospice Group across our communities. You will take ownership of campaign planning and delivery across digital, print, events and media, translating priorities from Fundraising, Retail, Clinical Services, the People Team and Corporate Partnerships into audience-led marketing activity. You will balance planned campaigns with emerging organisational needs, making clear choices about where time and resource will have the greatest impact. Alongside campaign leadership, you will help shape editorial and content planning, developing compelling, accessible content that communicates our impact and supports engagement. You will work closely with Brand, Digital and Creative colleagues to ensure campaigns are joined up, consistent and effective across channels. You will be a trusted marketing partner to senior and operational stakeholders, using insight and performance data to improve activity and provide clear recommendations. You will also provide day-to-day leadership, coaching and direction to Marketing and Communications Officers and apprentices. This is a fixed-term role where pace matters. Success will mean quickly building strong relationships, maintaining continuity through maternity cover and delivering measurable campaigns without losing quality, brand discipline or audience focus. You'll be You do not need to come from a hospice or charity background. What matters is that you can bring relevant expertise, understand the responsibility attached to our work and use your skills to deliver meaningful, measurable impact. Significant experience delivering integrated marketing campaigns from planning through to evaluation. Experience developing marketing plans and managing multiple campaigns, stakeholders and deadlines at the same time. Strong campaign management and project management skills, with evidence of delivering on time and within budget. Excellent copywriting and editing skills, with the ability to turn organisational priorities into clear, compelling audience-focused content. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including confidence advising senior colleagues and constructively challenging briefs. Experience using audience insight, segmentation and performance data to improve marketing activity and make recommendations. A strong understanding of digital marketing, brand management, accessibility and inclusive communications. Experience coaching, mentoring or supervising colleagues and creating clear priorities for delivery. A practical, collaborative and solutions-focused approach, with the confidence to make sound decisions in a fast-moving environment. Alignment with our values: Caring, Connected and Courageous.

item.title: Lived Experience Facilitator
item.description: Mind BLMK works across our communities to support positive mental health and wellbeing. Working closely with a range of partners, we offer a number of activities from our wellbeing centres and local venues to make a difference to the mental health and wellbeing of people in Bedfordshire , Luton and Milton Keynes , and our aim is to make sure that no-one has to face a mental health problem alone. Job title: Lived Experience Facilitator – Peer Support Post no: 669 Area covered: Central Bedfordshire and Bedford (Dunstable, Biggleswade, Leighton Buzzard and Ampthill and Bedford) Hours: 15 hours per week. Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday Working pattern: Tuesday – (HQ Flitwick 10am to 12pm) and (Ampthill) 12pm to 3pm, Wednesday – HQ (Flitwick) 10am to 3pm, Friday – 10am to 3pm (Biggleswade) OR (10am to 3pm) Leighton Buzzard Contract: Permanent Salary: £24,454.04 per annum FTE (£9,913.80 per annum actual for 15 hours per week) About the Role and the Service This role offers an exciting opportunity to join our Peer Support service for Central Bedfordshire and Bedford. As a Lived Experience Facilitator, you will be at the heart of the service, using your lived experience of mental health difficulties and recovery to facilitate and guide peer support group sessions. You will also hold a one to one mentoring caseload, using your lived experience to empower people to take meaningful, practical steps in their recovery, supporting them to building confidence, resilience and independence within their communities. In addition, you will assess individuals’ suitability for the service and signpost to wider services where necessary. There will also be opportunity to support events in the community to raise awareness of Mind BLMK services and build professional relationships with local organisations. About You You will need to be empathetic, energetic and deliver a person-centred approach in a non-judgemental way, collaborating with people to empower and engage them. The successful candidate will work with the Bedfordshire Wellbeing Hub Service Manager to ensure that the Peer Support service is delivered effectively in line with best practice. You have an understanding of Peer Support, a minimum of 2 years’ experience working with people with mental health needs and supporting recovery as well as personal lived experience of mental health challenges and recovery You can build constructive working relationships with a wide range of people, including those from culturally diverse communities. A strong communicator, you are able to build positive peer relationships, maintain professional boundaries, manage challenging situations calmly, and work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team. You are committed to empowering others, embracing lived experience as a valuable asset, and are comfortable using IT systems and travelling across Bedfordshire to deliver services. Entitlements/benefits: 25 days (pro rata) Annual Leave plus Bank Holidays (pro rata) Auto-enrolment NEST pension scheme (employer contributes 3%, employee contributes 5%) Optional Health Plan Discounts available through Blue Light Card & Tickets for Good In-house and external Learning and Development as appropriate for the role. Flexible Working On request (in line with Mind BLMK policy on Right to Request Flexible Working) If you have a passion for working in mental health and possess the required skills, we would love to hear from you. Closedown: Monday 28th September 2026 at 5pm Please note: We reserve the right to close this advert early if enough suitable applicants apply Start date: ASAP Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. Mind BLMK has been committed to the Mindful Employer charter and the Disability Confident Employer Scheme since 2008. item.title: Influencing Manager
item.description: About us The Alliance for Youth Justice is an alliance of more than 70 non-profit organisations advocating with and for children to drive positive change in youth justice across England and Wales. We mobilise our members’ frontline expertise, children’s lived experience, and evidence from research to champion a child-centred, rights-based and trauma-informed system that treats contact with the justice system as a sign of unmet need and systemic failure, prioritises support over criminalisation and gives every child the opportunity to thrive. We're widely recognised as the most influential group campaigning for improvements to the system, with trusted access to decision makers, working towards three goals: keeping children safe from the youth justice system through prevention and diversion; racial justice across the system; and custody as a last resort for children. About the role Following the launch of our new strategic approach, our Influencing Manager will lead the development and delivery of AYJ's influencing, policy, public affairs and campaigning work to shift policy, legislation, practice and public narratives. Campaigning, policy and public affairs (70%) — lead our influencing strategy alongside the CEO, spot opportunities for systemic change, develop evidence-driven policy positions and briefings, and build relationships with members, politicians, civil servants and stakeholders. Strategic communications (30%) — ensure the reach of our influencing, write high-impact influencing content for our digital channels, and act as first point of contact for media enquiries. Anti-opressive, anti-racist practice and youth voice run through everything, including involving children and young people with lived experience safely and meaningfully in our work. About you You have a proven track record of influencing for systemic change through policy, public affairs, communications or campaigning within a voluntary sector organisation or coalition, and know how to turn complex policy and research into compelling written communications for varied audiences. You have a thorough understanding of the political environment and Parliament, strong relationship-building skills, and excellent project management. You bring a genuine interest in youth justice and the issues facing children in England and Wales, alongside a personal commitment to anti-racism, social justice and child rights. Why join us We're a small team of three punching well above our weight, with real scope to shape how we work and few layers of hierarchy. We offer flexible, trust-based home working (within core hours), plus 25 days' leave (pro rata), Christmas office closure, and a 5% employer pension contribution. We encourage applications from historically marginalised groups even if you don't meet every requirement, and we do not use criminal records to exclude candidates. Please download the reruitment pack to find out more and read the full job description and person specification.
item.dc:creator: Alliance for Youth Justice

item.title: Events & Community Fundraising Manager
item.description: About Arthritis Action Arthritis Action is the UK charity giving hands-on, practical help to improve the quality of life of people affected by arthritis. We offer an integrated self-management approach, which looks at both the physical and mental health impact of living with arthritis. We support people living with musculoskeletal conditions through healthy eating advice, mental health resources, pain management techniques, Online Groups, employment support, and exercise advice and resources. We are looking for a Community and Events Fundraising Manager to lead Arthritis Action’s community and events fundraising programme, growing income and supporter engagement through innovative campaigns, challenge events, community partnerships and excellent stewardship. The role will identify new opportunities, build long-term relationships with supporters and community groups, and use data and insight to maximise participation, income and impact. Purpose This is a varied and rewarding fundraising management role, focused on developing and delivering an ambitious community and events fundraising programme that generates sustainable income, increases awareness of our work and builds long-term supporter relationships. You will lead the development of community fundraising, supporting and inspiring individuals, families and community groups to raise funds for Arthritis Action. Working collaboratively with colleagues across the Fundraising, Communications and Services Teams, you will help maximise fundraising income, increase engagement and ensure our supporters receive outstanding stewardship. Key Responsibilities – the role will include but not be limited to: Lead the community and events fundraising programme, developing and delivering an ambitious annual programme that grows income, participation and supporter engagement. Develop and diversify income streams across community fundraising, challenge events, sponsored activities, individual fundraising and third-party events. Build strong relationships with community fundraisers and supporters, providing excellent stewardship, motivation and ongoing engagement to maximise lifetime value. Identify and develop new fundraising opportunities, including local community groups, schools, clubs, businesses and networks aligned with Arthritis Action’s mission. Develop compelling fundraising propositions and supporter materials that inspire individuals and communities to raise funds and champion Arthritis Action. Work closely with the Communications Team to promote events, tell powerful supporter stories and increase awareness, engagement and fundraising reach. Develop excellent supporter journeys, from initial recruitment and onboarding through to stewardship, recognition and re-engagement, using data and insight to improve retention. Measure and evaluate fundraising activity, reporting on income, participation, return on investment and supporter engagement, and using insights to continually improve performance. Collaborate across the organisation to ensure community and events fundraising supports Arthritis Action’s wider strategic objectives and increases engagement with people affected by arthritis. Representing the Charity at networking events to promote fundraising and meet contacts, travelling as appropriate within London and the rest of the UK. Other Activities Ensure all fundraising activity complies with relevant legislation, regulations, safeguarding requirements and Arthritis Action policies. Keeping up to date the parts of the CRM and website relevant to community and events fundraising. Undertake other tasks relevant to the level of this position within the organisation. PERSON SPECIFICATION EXPERIENCE & SKILLS A track record in community and events fundraising - Essential Experience of building strong relationships and engaging supporters from a wide range of backgrounds - Essential Excellent oral and written communication skills including the ability to write in Plain English for a range of audiences - Essential Experience of balancing multiple priorities while maintaining excellent attention to detail - Essential Experience of monitoring and evaluating fundraising activity, and managing budgets - Essential An understanding of, and commitment to, Arthritis Action’s vision, mission, equal opportunities and diversity - Essential Database experience - Desirable ATTRIBUTES Excellent interpersonal skills - Essential A self-starter, able to work on own initiative where required - Essential Enthusiastic team-player with a can-do attitude - Essential Able and willing to travel within the UK - Essential How to apply Applications should be in the form of a CV with a covering letter explaining your interest in and suitability for the role. Please provide both email and telephone contact information for yourself. Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK. Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Applications should be received by 11:59pm on Monday 28 September 2026 at the latest. Interviews will take place in the London office on Monday 5 October 2026. Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert ahead of the deadline should we receive a sufficient number of applications. Arthritis Action is an equal opportunities employer. We treat employees and job applicants in the same way regardless of age, disability, marital status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, religion or belief.

item.title: Homelessness Caseworker
item.description: Location: Waltham Forest Salary: £32500 Hours: 37.5 Contract Type: Permanent Closing Date : Oct 2nd 5pm Reports To: Operations Manager We are a small, person-centred homelessness charity committed to supporting people experiencing homelessness, housing insecurity, and social exclusion. We work alongside individuals to help them overcome barriers, improve wellbeing, access accommodation, and achieve greater independence. We are seeking an enthusiastic, compassionate, and motivated Homeless Caseworker to join our growing team. Forest Churches Emergency Night Shelter employs and works with all faiths and none, candidates would be expected to be comfortable with the Christian ethos underpinning the charities work. This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people's lives while helping shape and develop a responsive and innovative service. Job Description Job Title Homeless Caseworker Responsible To Operations Manager Job Purpose To provide high-quality assessments, advice, and ongoing support to individuals experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. The post holder will act as a first point of contact for service users, undertaking assessments, identifying support needs, developing support plans, managing a caseload, and working collaboratively with partner organisations to achieve positive client outcomes. Key Responsibilities Assessment and Engagement ● Conduct comprehensive assessments with new clients accessing the service. ● Identify housing, welfare, health, safeguarding, immigration, employment, and support needs. ● Complete risk assessments and safeguarding referrals where necessary. ● Develop person-centred support plans. ● Support clients to access appropriate services and resources. ● Provide information, advice, and guidance tailored to individual circumstances. Case Management ● Manage an allocated caseload. ● Maintain accurate and timely case records. ● Record all interventions and outcomes on the case management system. ● Ensure compliance with GDPR and confidentiality requirements. ● Review client progress and update support plans regularly. Housing and Homelessness Support ● Support individuals to access accommodation pathways. ● Assist with housing applications and referrals. ● Liaise with local authorities and housing providers. ● Advocate on behalf of clients where appropriate. Outreach Responsibilities ● Participate in community outreach activity. ● Engage rough sleepers and vulnerable individuals. ● Support clients who are reluctant or unable to access office-based services. ● Facilitate access to emergency accommodation and support services. Partnership Working ● Build positive relationships with local agencies and stakeholders. ● Attend multi-agency meetings where appropriate. ● Make referrals and coordinate support plans with external partners. Safeguarding and Risk Management ● Promote the safety and wellbeing of all service users. ● Identify and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns. ● Maintain professional boundaries. ● Follow all safeguarding policies and procedures. ● Participate in safeguarding training and reflective practice. Team Responsibilities ● Attend team meetings and supervision sessions. ● Contribute to service development and continuous improvement. ● Support volunteers and placement students where appropriate. ● Undertake training relevant to the role. General Responsibilities ● Promote equality, diversity, and inclusion. ● Maintain confidentiality and professionalism. ● Adhere to organisational policies and procedures. ● Act as an ambassador for the charity. ● Undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. Essential Qualifications ● GCSE (or equivalent) in English and Mathematics. ● Relevant training or willingness to undertake training in homelessness, safeguarding, housing, mental health, or related areas. Essential Experience ● Experience supporting vulnerable adults and/or young people. ● Experience carrying out assessments and support planning. ● Experience working within homelessness, housing, support services, social care, or community settings. ● Experience maintaining accurate records and case notes. Essential Knowledge ● Understanding of homelessness and housing-related challenges. ● Knowledge of safeguarding adults and young people. ● Understanding of GDPR and confidentiality requirements. ● Knowledge of trauma-informed approaches. ● Understanding of professional boundaries. ● Awareness of equality and diversity principles. Essential Skills Communication ● Excellent verbal and written communication skills. ● Ability to build rapport with a wide range of individuals. ● Ability to communicate effectively with partner organisations. Assessment ● Ability to undertake comprehensive client assessments. ● Ability to identify support needs and develop action plans. ● Ability to manage risk appropriately. Organisation ● Strong organisational skills. ● Ability to manage competing priorities. ● Ability to maintain accurate case records. IT Skills ● Competent in Microsoft Office. ● Ability to use databases and case management systems. ● Confidence using digital systems and maintaining electronic records. Personal Qualities ● Compassionate and non-judgemental. ● Reliable and professional. ● Resilient and adaptable. ● Motivated to improve outcomes for vulnerable people. ● Able to work independently and as part of a team. ● Committed to learning and development. Desirable Criteria ● Experience working with people with complex needs. ● Experience working within homelessness services. ● Experience of working with clients with multiple disadvantages ● Knowledge of housing legislation and homelessness pathways. ● Experience conducting outreach work. ● Relevant qualification in housing, Substance Misuse Mental Health, social care, counselling, or related field. What We Offer ● Flexible and supportive working environment. ● Regular supervision and reflective practice. ● Ongoing training and professional development. ● Opportunity to influence and shape service delivery. ● Employee wellbeing support. ● Meaningful work that changes lives. item.title: Hull and East Riding - Family Engagement Officer
item.description: WHO WE ARE We are Zarach, the children’s bed charity, and we’re on a mission to end child bed poverty, helping children get a good night's sleep, and the chance to thrive at school. In our eight years as a registered charity, we’ve captured the hearts and attention of many individuals, community groups, businesses and funders who want to support us on our mission. We’ve also been given an incredible media platform from which we have raised awareness of child bed poverty at local, regional and national levels. This support and awareness has seen us deliver over 18,000 bed bundles to children to date! WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR Zarach is well established in West Yorkshire and Doncaster. We are now continuing to grow across the Yorkshire region, with a launch in Hull, Bridlington and Goole in October. We are looking to recruit a Family Engagement Officer to join our dedicated Yorkshire team. This is a unique opportunity to play a key part in the growth and development of our vital service as we expand into the East Riding. As our ideal candidate you will be happy to travel in and around Hull and the East Riding. You will be able to travel regularly to meet with the team and conduct home visits across the region. You will also need to be able to attend our Leeds Warehouse, or other areas in Yorkshire when required. You will be confident to work autonomously in your area while being supported remotely by a wider regional team. You will be someone who has good experience of the broad range of day-to-day case management, working with external partners, volunteer support, and administrative activities that working in a dynamic charity brings, and someone who enjoys the busyness and variety of this. While not essential, as training will be provided, experience working alongside schools will help you hit the ground running as you build relationships and support local families. Alongside your family support and engagement-related skills and experience, we’ll be looking to see that you have a genuine care for our mission and, as such, are self-motivated to do a great job and be a values-led member of our team. Ideally, you’ll have experience of working with vulnerable families and managing volunteers in the charity sector, due to some of the specialties that come with this, such as safeguarding and partnership working. But charity experience is not essential if you can demonstrate an appetite and track record for continual learning and development across your working life to date. WHAT WE OFFER Starting at £26,000 with progression up to £30,000 p/a Full time hours (35 hours per week) 28 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) Healthcare Cash Plan Quarterly Staff Recognition Award A great working environment! One of our colleagues described us as- “Zarach is a wonderful place to work with the mission at the core of all that we do” To decide if you’d like to bring your skills and experience to bear in the pursuit of our mission, please have a look at the job description, our website and the coverage of us across social media. Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. Therefore, we encourage you to submit your CV and cover letter as soon as possible.

item.title: People & Culture Coordinator
item.description: Are you looking for a rewarding role within an intersectional feminist organisation? We have an incredible opportunity for a People & Culture Coordinator to join Solace Women’s Aid. Solace exists to end the harm done through gender-based violence. We work to prevent violence and abuse and provide services to meet the individual needs of survivors, particularly women and children. Our core values reflect our history and were developed in consultation with staff and service users. Feminism and intersectionality are key to our work, and we are committed to the principles of being survivor-led, trauma-informed, empowering, diverse, anti-racist and anti-discriminatory. About the Service We are on an ambitious journey to strengthen and modernise our People & Culture function, moving beyond traditional HR support to build a proactive, inclusive and high-performing culture across the organisation. Alongside supporting the day-to-day realities of a complex frontline charity, we are leading a broad programme of improvement and transformation across people systems, workforce planning, leadership capability, employee experience, organisational development and service delivery. About the Role The People & Culture Coordinator provides high-quality administrative and coordination support across core People & Culture processes, ensuring that employee lifecycle activities, documentation and systems are delivered accurately and efficiently. The role focuses on the operational delivery of people processes and supports compliance through accurate record-keeping, timely processing, and effective use of P&C systems. About You You'll bring solid experience of providing excellent HR support within a busy People and Culture team, and you'll know first hand what it takes to keep things running smoothly under pressure. You're flexible and responsive by nature, comfortable using your own initiative and exercising good judgement. You can manage a busy and varied workload without losing sight of deadlines, and you understand that getting the basics right consistently and accurately. Additional Information This is a hybrid role, with a minimum requirement to work two days per week at our Head Office in Camden and the remainder working remotely. This is a 12 month fixed term contract to cover maternity leave. What we can offer you We provide a comprehensive benefits package to all our employees, including: Flexible working Focus on learning and development (internal career progression and training) Generous holiday entitlement Employer pension contribution Family-friendly leave and enhanced maternity pay Access to Inclusion Networks Daily clinical debriefing Two paid wellbeing days Employee Assistance Programme providing free 24/7 support and advice Employee Benefits Platform offering staff discounts, benefits, and savings Flow & Restore yoga classes Meditation sessions Cycle to Work Scheme How to apply Please submit your CV and Supporting Statement through the recruitment portal. When applying for this role, kindly highlight in your Supporting Statement how your values, knowledge, transferable skills, and experience align with each point within the following sections of the Job Profile Document: Values, Behaviours & Competencies Knowledge, Experience and Skills Solace Women's Aid values diversity, promotes equity, and challenges discrimination. We encourage and welcome applications from candidates of diverse cultures, abilities, perspectives, and lived experiences. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay, and benefits. Our Inclusion Networks support staff with protected characteristics and offer inclusive spaces to connect. We anticipate and provide reasonable adjustments as needed and support employees who acquire a disability or long-term health condition, enabling them to stay in work. This service is run by women for women and is therefore restricted to female applicants under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1. Section 7(2)(e) of the Sex Discrimination Act 1975 applies. The post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act. As part of safer recruitment practices, we carry out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) and right to work in the UK checks. No agencies

item.title: Supporter Care Manager
item.description: " Package Description: The National Autistic Society is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and adults who use our services. Successful applicants will be required to complete the relevant safeguarding checks if relevant to their role. Join Us as a Supporter Care Manager The National Autistic Society helps create a world that works for autistic people and within National Programmes wechampion the rights and interests of autistic people and their families, making sure national policies and legislation reflect their needs.We have a rewarding opportunity for a Supporter Care Manager within the Fundraising Operations Team. If you share our values and want to make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. Visit our website to find out more about who we are: About the Team The Fundraising Operations Team plays a vital role in supporting the National Autistic Society's fundraising activities and supporter engagement. Working closely with fundraising, data services and operational teams, we ensure supporters, donors and members receive an excellent experience while maintaining the highest standards of compliance, governance and operational effectiveness. The team champions a supporter-focused culture and continuously seeks opportunities to improve supporter journeys, engagement and retention. About the Role We are looking for an experienced and proactive Supporter Care Manager to lead our Supporter Care function and deliver an exceptional supporter experience. You will oversee the day-to-day operation of the Supporter Care team, ensuring supporters, donors, members and enquirers receive high-quality and timely responses across all interactions. You will also provide strategic leadership on fundraising compliance, supporter experience and continuous improvement, helping to strengthen supporter relationships, maximise engagement and support long-term income generation. What You’ll Do Lead and develop the Supporter Care team, ensuring high performance and excellent service delivery. Champion a supporter-centred approach, using feedback and insight to improve supporter journeys and engagement. Oversee fundraising compliance activities, ensuring adherence to fundraising regulations, GDPR and internal policies. Manage supporter feedback and complaints, including regulatory reporting requirements. What We’re Looking For Experience leading supporter care, customer service or contact centre operations. Proven experience managing and developing teams and improving operational processes. Knowledge of fundraising regulations, the Code of Fundraising Practice and UK GDPR requirements. Strong leadership, stakeholder management and communication skills. This advert is for a Permanent, Full Time position at 35 hours per week . Occasional flexibility may be required to support organisational priorities. This role is Hybrid. We are flexible regarding work location and support hybrid working arrangements. The role is primarily office and home based with occasional travel for meetings, training and events as required. What we can offer you Pension – Auto-enrolled pension scheme. Annual Leave – 33 days (including public holidays). You can buy or sell leave each year. Training – Great induction and training, including autism training. Discounts – Online staff discount scheme for shopping, cycling, tech, and more (e.g., Asda, Tesco, Nike, Apple). Healthcare – Cash plan for permanent staff. Life Assurance – 2x your base salary. Flexible Benefits – Options like private health, dental insurance, holiday trading, enhanced pension. Support – 24-hour Employee Assistance Programme and counselling. Mindfulness – Free Headspace app for you and up to 3 family/friends. Blue Light Card – Eligibility for discounts. About our application process You will be required to upload your CV. If you are providing a supporting statement, please consider the following: Look at the job description and person specification. Tell us how your skills and experience match the role. Give examples if you can. We might close this job advert early if we get lots of suitable applications. To protect our autistic adults & children at the National Autistic Society, some roles require employees to have a criminal background check. Possession of an Enhanced DBS Check either on the Update Service or conducted within the last 12 months would be preferable but not essential if its applicable to your role. Applications for this job are sought from anyone who is suitably qualified and experienced for the role but particularly welcome from autistic people. We are an equal opportunities employer and part of the Disability Confident Employer scheme. Important Information Agencies need not apply. Please note the National Autistic Society are unable to provide sponsorship for Visas. All application decisions are made by people and are not determined automatically by AI. "

item.title: Senior Advocacy Advisor – Climate
item.description: Starting Salary: £44,766 - £48,225 (including London weighting) Contract: Permanent Location: UK, Hybrid working with a minimum of 40% of your time in theLondon Office Job Profile This role will lead CAFOD’s policy and advocacy work aimed at tackling the global climate crisis. The post holder will have a solid understanding of debates around climate change, in particular how it impacts climate-vulnerable countries in the Global South. You will bring knowledge of the causes of the climate crisis, and its solutions, particularly global financing needs. Working closely with CAFOD’s overseas partners, and within UK and global networks, this role will hold policy expertise on behalf of the organisation. This will involve developing policy positions and representing the organisation externally. The role will work closely with CAFOD’s government relations and campaigns colleagues to lobby decision-makers and mobilise supporters as part of our climate justice work. Sitting within the Advocacy, Policy & Campaigns team, the role is managed by the head of department. Key Responsibilities Person Specification Strong background working in climate policy and/or international development policy Excellent analytical and research skills and an understanding of how to form strategic policy positions Experience of developing strategic advocacy plans Experience of lobbying decision makers Background working with partners and coalitions, both in the UK and overseas Excellent written and verbal communication skills CAFOD is a welcoming, supportive workplace committed to a safe, inclusive culture where everyone is respected.CAFODwill make reasonable adjustments at every stage of the recruitment process to ensure candidates with disabilities or individual needs are fully supported. Safeguarding for Children and Vulnerable Adults CAFOD recognises the personal dignity and rights of children and vulnerable adults, towards whom it has a special responsibility and a duty of care and respect. CAFOD, and all its staff and volunteers, undertake to do all in our power to create a safe environment for children, young people and vulnerable adults and to prevent their physical, sexual or emotional abuse. CAFOD is committed to acting at all times in the best interests of children and vulnerable adults, seeing these interests as paramount. Any candidate offered a job with CAFOD will be expected to adhere to CAFOD’s Safeguarding policy and sign CAFOD’s Code of Behaviour as an appendix to their contract of employment and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these documents. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references, and appropriate screening checks can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. CAFOD also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

item.title: Senior Quantitative Policy and Research Officer
item.description: Contract: Permanent, Full-Time (37.5 hours per week) Salary: £37,221.19 - £39,500 per annum Closing Date: Monday 28 September 2026 Interviews will be held w/c 12th October 2026 Please note, we may close this advert early if we receive a high volume of applications. About us Centrepoint, the UK’s leading youth homelessness charity, is looking for a Senior Quantitative Policy and Research Officer to join our Policy and Research team based in London. We help vulnerable young people by giving them the practical and emotional support they need to find a job and live independently. Centrepoint provides homeless young people with accommodation, health support and life skills in order to get them back into education, training and employment. We want to end youth homelessness by 2037 . Together with our partners, we support over 15,000 young people each year. The Policy and Research team at Centrepoint provides the evidence base for the organisation’s policy and influencing work, using research, data and the experiences of young people to understand the causes and scale of youth homelessness and identify effective solutions. The team leads research across a range of policy areas, produces Centrepoint’s Youth Homelessness Databank, analyses national and local data, and translates findings into clear policy recommendations. It also supports external influencing, engaging with Government, Parliament, local authorities and other organisations to ensure evidence is used to shape policy and improve outcomes for young people. Hybrid Working Centrepoint operates a hybrid working model. The requirement is a minimum of 50% of your working week. For most full-time colleagues, this means attending the office for five days over a two-week period (e.g., two days one week and three days the next). For colleagues on different contracts (including part-time or compressed contracts) this will be adjusted accordingly. About you Effective communicator with natural ability to facilitate open and honest conversations. Able decision maker with a can do attitude. Respectful and empathetic, always considering the impact on our young people. Flexible, always adapting to changing needs. Engaging, committed to self-development by engaging with training and continuous learning. Proactive, always looking for creative ways of working. What you’ll be doing Lead on the development and delivery of research projects, with a particular focus on the quantitative data analysis required to create a robust evidence base needed for Centrepoint’s policy and research work. This includes managing the Youth Homelessness Databank project, ensuring it remains the most comprehensive source of youth homelessness data in the UK and continues to meet the strategic needs of the organisation. To work with Centrepoint staff and young people to shape Centrepoint’s policy messages and further Centrepoint’s mission to end youth homelessness. To build strategic relationships with key policy makers and relevant voluntary organisations needed to influence government policy. Why join Centrepoint? In return for your efforts, you’ll receive a competitive salary, excellent training and development, and a host of staff benefits including: 25 days of annual leave per year, rising by one day per year to a maximum of 27 days Healthcare cash plan (Cover the costs of a wide range of medical treatment including Dental, Optical, Complementary and Alternative therapies). Private Medical insurance Income protection Employer pension contributions of 5% Access to Cycle 2 Work loan scheme An interest-free travel loan At Centrepoint we challenge the discrimination within society that contributes to youth homelessness, and we are just as committed to fairness and equality within Centrepoint itself. We are passionate about ensuring all of our colleagues are made to feel included in the work we do and that we value the rich diversity within the organization. We are an equal opportunities employer and we welcome applications regardless of sex, gender, race, age, belief in any religion and none, gender identity, ethnic origin, class, sexuality, nationality, appearance, unrelated criminal activities, disability, responsibility for dependents, part time or shift workers, being HIV positive or living with AIDS, lived experience of homelessness or using young people’s services and any other matter which causes a person to be treated with injustice. Centrepoint’s policy is to recruit, employ and promote people on the basis of their suitability for the work to be performed, and to this end, our aim is to ensure that all applicants, employees and volunteers receive equal treatment. Our approach to applications We recognise that candidates may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support their applications. While this is absolutely fine, all examples and statements included must be truthful, accurate and based on your own experience. We’re keen to understand your individual skills, experience and motivations, so please ensure your application reflects your own voice . Don’t miss out on this fantastic opportunity to join our team as a Senior Quantitative Policy and Research Officer click ‘Apply’ now!

item.title: Supporter Journey Executive - CRM
item.description: The Woodland Trust is looking for a Supporter Journey Executive to provide technical support, deliver and optimise supporter journeys. Head office attendance would be required once a month on average. • This is a fixed term contract for 9 months. The Candidate: • Experience building and delivering supporter/customer journeys or campaigns. • Strong collaboration skills with the ability to communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders. • Knowledge of marketing automation and customer lifecycle journeys. • Experience conducting A/B testing and optimisation. • Experience working with CRM systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365. • Strong prioritisation skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines. • Knowledge of data selection, segmentation and marketing operations. Benefits and Wellbeing: Joining our team means you’ll be part of our fight for a greener, healthier planet for people and wildlife. We take good care of our staff, offering support and training opportunities. We also offer: • Enhanced Employer Pension • Life Assurance • Flexible and hybrid working options (7am - 7pm) • Generous annual leave - 25 Days plus Bank Holidays (pro rata for part-time) • Buy and sell holiday scheme • Enhanced parental pay • Employee assistance programme To support inclusivity and remove barriers for candidates, we publish all salaries upfront and proudly follow the We Show the Salary pledge. The salary listed is the set salary for this role, and we don’t ask applicants to state their current pay or expectations. If you choose to apply, we’ll take that as confirmation that the advertised salary meets your expectations. About Us: The Woodland Trust is the UK’s largest woodland conservation charity. We want to see a world where woods and trees thrive for people and nature. The Trust engages and inspires people to make a difference by protecting, restoring and creating woodland and getting more trees in the ground. Our commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: To achieve our mission, we need to better reflect society and the communities we work in. People of colour and disabled people are currently under-represented across the environment and conservation sector. If you identify as a person of colour and/or disabled, we particularly encourage you to apply. Application information and advice: For fairness we keep our candidates’ personal details hidden from the hiring managers, and CVs are redacted until after shortlisting is complete. Make sure that your personal statement clearly shows how your skills and knowledge link to the specifications in the job description and you share with us your passion for the role. Completed applications will be reviewed by a hiring manager and/or a member of the recruitment team, and you will receive an update on the outcome of your application via email. Acceptable Use - Artificial Intelligence (AI): We understand that candidates may choose to use AI tools to support their job applications. However, we ask that any information submitted reflects your own experience, skills and understanding. During interviews, candidates are expected to respond independently without the use of AI tools. Apply now: If you're ready to make a difference and grow with us, apply today. We might close advertising early if we get a lot of applications, so it's a good idea to apply soon. If we do close the advert early, and you have an application in progress, we will email you prior to closing to give you time to complete. Interviews will take place via Microsoft Teams on the 14th October 2026.
