item.title: Specialist Housing First Worker
item.description: About the role: Housing First changes what is possible for people who have been shut out, moved on and let down for too long. Single Homeless Project's (SHP’s) Camden Housing First service is expanding, and we’re looking for a passionate and skilled worker to join an innovative team supporting people with long histories of rough sleeping, multiple exclusion and co-occurring needs. This includes a new and important focus on supporting couples who have been rough sleeping and will be accommodated separately in their own self-contained flats, while receiving intensive, relational and trauma-informed support. Based from King’s Cross, you’ll work across the community and in people’s homes, carrying a small caseload so you can offer flexible, persistent and person-centred support that is shaped around each person’s strengths, safety, needs and goals. You’ll build trust with people who may have had difficult experiences of services, working at their pace while keeping a strong focus on housing sustainment, wellbeing, risk, choice and recovery. You won’t be doing this work alone. You’ll be part of a multidisciplinary team and will work closely with statutory services, housing partners and specialist colleagues including health, psychology, Solace, occupational therapy and perpetrator support. With safety at the heart of the work, you’ll play a key role in supporting people where relationships, trauma, exploitation, abuse or external risk may be part of their lives. At SHP, you’ll also have access to learning, reflective practice and development opportunities that help you keep growing your skills while doing meaningful, complex and life-changing work. About you: You have experience supporting people facing multiple disadvantage, including homelessness, trauma, mental ill health, substance use, contact with the criminal justice system or long-term exclusion from services. You know how to build trust with people who may be wary of services, using patience, consistency and creativity to keep people engaged without forcing change before they are ready. You understand the links between severe and multiple disadvantage, VAWG, coercion, abuse, exploitation and safety, and you can respond in a way that is trauma-informed, boundaried and safeguarding-focused. You are a confident advocate and communicator, able to work with partners, negotiate well, challenge when needed and keep the person’s voice at the centre. You are organised and self-sufficient in your day-to-day work, with the written, IT and recording skills needed to manage a caseload, update systems clearly and keep support plans moving. About us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important info: Closing Date: Monday 28th September at Midnight Interview Date: Wednesday 7th October online via Microsoft Teams Please note shortlisted candidates will be required to complete a short psychometric test before being confirmed for interview. This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed (by SHP) for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted or progressed.

item.title: Chief Operating Officer
item.description: Help strengthen the organisation behind the UK’s professional voice and trade union for midwives and maternity support workers. Location: Hybrid, with travel to London and across the UK as required Applications close: 9 a.m. Monday 12th October 2026 Who we are The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) is the membership organisation, professional association and trade union for midwives and maternity support workers across the UK. We support our members throughout their careers, from education and training through to the day they leave the profession. Our work is guided by members and focused on improving their working lives, amplifying their voices and building our midwifery community. The RCM plays an important role in maternity services, workforce issues, professional leadership, campaigning and public policy. Our members need an organisation that is influential, responsive and trusted, with the systems, insight and confidence to support them well. About the role The Chief Operating Officer will help the RCM turn its strategy into disciplined, inclusive and member-focused delivery. Working closely with the Chief Executive, Board, Executive Team and colleagues across the four nations, you will strengthen the business engine behind the RCM’s purpose. This includes financial planning, governance, risk, compliance, digital, data, CRM, operational performance, supplier management and organisational improvement. The role comes at an important stage in the RCM’s development. We have made significant progress in working as One RCM, bringing together our professional association, trade union, membership and business functions around a shared commitment to members. The next COO will build on that work by improving financial grip, strengthening data and insight, developing clearer systems and helping teams work with greater confidence and accountability. What we are looking for You will bring significant senior leadership experience in a broad organisational role, such as COO, Deputy CEO, Chief Executive, Director of Corporate Services, Director of Resources or a comparable position. You will understand how to build strong business infrastructure, improve systems and lead change through people. An accounting qualification is not required; however, you will have experience delivering strategic financial management. Importantly, we need someone confident with governance and risk, who is interested in how data, CRM and insight can improve member experience and decision-making. You do not need to have worked in an organisation exactly like the RCM. Experience in a membership organisation, professional body, trade union, charity or values-led organisation would be helpful, but we are also interested in leaders from other settings who bring the judgement, curiosity and humility to understand our distinctive role. If you connect with the RCM’s purpose and can help strengthen the organisation that supports midwives and maternity support workers across the UK, we would be pleased to hear from you. Please click on the link to be redirected to the Peridot Partners website, where you can find full details of the role and how to apply. Applications for this role close at 9 a.m. Monday 12th October 2026.

item.title: Trusts and Foundations Manager
item.description: The Urology Foundation is looking for a Trusts and Foundation Manager, to develop and grow income from charitable trusts, foundations, grant giving bodies and public funders. This will include identifying opportunities, developing persuasive cases for support, cultivating meaningful relationships and securing significant grants including multi-year grants for both core work and project-based activities. TUF has a well-established and growing Trusts and Foundations portfolio. It is an important fundraising stream, raising between £600,000 to £1,000,000 annually supporting the delivery of The Urology Foundation’s strategy. As Trusts and Foundations Manager, you will build and manage a grant giving programme, securing significant gifts from trusts, foundations and other grant-making bodies to support The Urology Foundation’s strategic objectives and £5 million Research Appeal. You will manage existing funder relationships and develop new opportunities while delivering excellent stewardship. A central aspect of this role will involve gathering knowledge and data from a range of sources to identify compelling funding packages in order to create strong cases for support and funding applications. Therefore, an entrepreneurial, pro-active attitude, strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach are essential. The role will suit an experienced fundraiser with a proven track record in growing grant income, successfully managing and delivering grant fundraising programmes and securing five and six figure gifts. A self-starter with an interest in research and / or urology, the ideal candidate will use initiative and work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation and stakeholders to secure income and support the delivery of TUF’s work.

item.title: Executive Assistant to the CEO
item.description: We Are Survivors is a survivor-focused voluntary sector organisation that aims to create and facilitate safe spaces for male (including trans and non-binary individuals) survivors of sexual harms across Greater Manchester, providing access to quality-assured support. Our work is focused on developing ways for individuals to empower themselves to work through personal and sometimes painful issues, guided and supported by our trauma-informed team, following the trauma and recovery model. Our vision is to have “A society where NO male survivor is left behind” We are looking for an Executive Assistant who can work closely with our CEO and help them make the best use of their time, relationships and influence. At the heart of this role is our ambition that no male survivor is left behind. You will support the CEO to keep that ambition visible in their day-to-day work, helping them stay focused on the conversations and opportunities that can create meaningful change for male survivors. This is more than an administrative role. You will help the CEO manage their priorities and prepare for important meetings. You will keep track of commitments, follow up on agreed actions, and ensure the right information is available when needed. There will be times when plans change quickly, so you will need to be comfortable using your judgement and adapting your approach. You will also help We Are Survivors engage and influence at the local, regional, and national levels. This could involve supporting contact with commissioners or government departments, preparing briefings for meetings, coordinating events and helping the CEO maintain strong relationships across the sector. Your work will help ensure that the experiences of male survivors are heard in the places where decisions are made. As someone working closely with the CEO, you will often be a first point of contact for people inside and outside the organisation. You will need to be approachable while understanding the importance of confidentiality. You should feel confident managing sensitive information and recognising when something needs the CEO’s immediate attention. We are looking for someone who is organised and able to take initiative. You will share our commitment to male survivors and understand the difference that thoughtful executive support can make. You do not need to know everything from day one, but you should be curious about our work and motivated by the opportunity to help We Are Survivors extend its reach and impact.

item.title: Senior Safeguarding Specialist
item.description: Senior Safeguarding Specialist When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Role Title: Senior Safeguarding Specialist Salary: £49,370 to £50,797 Location: Hybrid: London Tenure: Permanent Part time, 28 hours ActionAid UK is a member of the ActionAid Federation, an international charity that works with women and girls living in poverty. We work with our partners and dedicated staff in 43 countries to end violence and fight poverty so that all women, everywhere, can create the future they want Are you a keen advocate of women and girls’ rights in emergencies? Do you have the expertise to lead safeguarding strategy, strengthen organisational culture, and ensure robust protection from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment? Then we'd love to hear from you! Reporting to the Director of People and Organisational Development, the Senior Safeguarding Specialist will provide expert leadership, advice and operational direction for the continuous development and delivery of ActionAid UK's safeguarding strategy, policies, systems and culture. This is a pivotal role that will drive safeguarding excellence across the organisation, ensuring strong safeguarding standards, effective compliance, and a culture where safeguarding is understood as everyone's responsibility. The postholder will lead the implementation and ongoing development of safeguarding policies, processes and standards, supporting the protection of staff, rights holders, partners and the communities with whom ActionAid works. Key Responsibilities: Lead the delivery and ongoing development of ActionAid UK's safeguarding strategy. Provide safeguarding expertise and operational leadership across the organisation. Ensure compliance with all Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) and safeguarding policies, protocols and commitments. Drive the integration of safeguarding principles into all areas of ActionAid UK's work, including new funding initiatives and programmes. Strengthen safeguarding systems, processes, learning and organisational culture. Work closely with senior leaders, trustees and safeguarding stakeholders across the ActionAid Federation to promote best practice and continuous improvement About You We are looking for a safeguarding professional who: Has significant experience of leading safeguarding initiatives, frameworks and investigations within a complex organisation. Possesses strong knowledge of safeguarding, PSEAH and organisational risk management. Can influence and engage senior stakeholders with confidence and credibility. Demonstrates excellent judgement, analytical ability and decision-making skills. Is committed to feminist values, anti-racism, equity and the rights of women and girls. Has a passion for creating safe, inclusive and accountable organisational culture At ActionAid UK, you'll be part of a global movement working to achieve a world free from poverty, injustice and gender inequality. Every day, our staff work alongside women and girls around the world to challenge the systems and structures that perpetuate discrimination and violence. As our Senior Safeguarding Specialist, you will have the opportunity to shape and influence safeguarding practice across the organisation, ensuring that the safety, dignity and rights of staff, partners, rights holders and communities remain at the heart of everything we do. This is a highly visible role with the opportunity to work closely with senior leaders, trustees and safeguarding colleagues across the ActionAid Federation to strengthen safeguarding culture and drive meaningful change. In return, we offer a supportive and collaborative working environment, flexible and hybrid working arrangements, and the opportunity to do impactful work that contributes to lasting change for women and girls worldwide. Additional information Diversity, equality, inclusion and belonging: Diversity, inclusion and belonging are key to our organisational culture. We are on a journey to become not only an anti-racist organisation but one that proudly celebrates the diversity of all applicants and employees. We look forward to you bringing your full self to work, proudly sharing your unique perspective and helping us to shape our combined future. We especially welcome applications from those from under-represented/marginalised communities. AAUK is a Disability Confident Committed organisation and as such any candidate that declares a disability will be shortlisted for interview if they meet the essential criteria for the role. Referencing and safeguarding: All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, safeguarding, criminal records and terrorism finance checks. By submitting an application the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. ActionAid UK is committed to preventing any form of sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse (including child abuse and adult at-risk abuse) and responding robustly when these harms take place. We expect all ActionAid UK staff and ActionAid UK representatives to share this commitment. We will not tolerate our staff or other representatives carrying out any form of sexual harassment, exploitation or abuse towards anyone we come into contact with through our work. Working practices: ActionAid is committed to supporting flexible working. If you would like to discuss flexible working options, including the possibility of a job share for this role, there will be space to do so during the interview process. ActionAid UK has a hybrid working policy for many of our roles. The requirement will vary from team to team and the responsibilities of individual roles. As a minimum, all colleagues are expected to attend the office 12 days per year, plus additional time for induction, training, and company connection days. Some roles may require in-office attendance on all days and if so, these will clearly be marked as in-office roles. Please note that ActionAid UK does not offer fully remote working options. We encourage you to discuss hybrid working expectations at interview. Recruitment processes: Please note that ActionAid UK may review, shortlist and interview candidates prior to the closing date so we encourage all candidates to apply as soon as possible. If we receive a very high response, we may close the vacancy early and will not accept further submissions. Vacancies close at 23:55pm

item.title: Business Development Manager
item.description: You will use a wide range of commercial and interpersonal skills to develop the way our services support children, young people and families. The core area of your work will be working with teams of Barnardo's colleagues to produce compelling proposals to commissioners and partners in Scotland and Northern Ireland. As such, you'll be able to demonstrate: Strong organisational skills Meticulous attention to detail The ability to elicit and articulate great ideas Strong written and spoken communication You will need to be a good writer, communicating ideas effectively on paper with an ability to analyse large volumes of information to develop clear and compelling responses to tenders. It is critical that you can build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to support the development of proposals and service design. You will manage all aspects of proposals and tenders, leading the development and delivery of bids, working to deadlines, ensuring that we present strong business cases and bids that underpin successful outcomes. In addition, there will be the opportunity to help us develop new services and innovations in priority growth areas, monitor market intelligence, assess commercial and contract risks and work alongside operational colleagues in Children's Services. Your project management skills may have been developed in any sector, and may need further development, but your commitment to the work we do will be demonstrated by your enthusiasm and ability to learn. In Business Development we are a supportive team, with stimulating and challenging work and extensive opportunities to learn and to help Barnardo's transform the lives of the UK's most vulnerable children. These roles will operate on a 'Work from Anywhere' basis, meaning that you can work both from home and/or from an office 'hub' that's nearest to where you live. Some travel across Scotland and Northern Ireland may be required. Barnardo's believe in creating equality of opportunity in the workplace and supporting people to manage their work-life balance; we are therefore open to offering flexible working arrangements. Please note due to the high volume of applications for some posts, this advert might close before the displayed closing date. We recommend that you apply for this role as soon as possible

item.title: Facilities and Operations Manager
item.description: AKF(UK) JOB DESCRIPTION 1. JOB TITLE Facilities and Operations Manager 2. REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS JOB TITLE FOR 2.1 REPORTS DIRECTLY TO Head of Kings Cross Properties Strategic direction, measuring performance against targets, regular reviews, role modelling, support, guidance, development and performance management. 2.2 REPORTS INDIRECTLY TO AKF(UK) Property Committee Reporting on financial results, compliance, company law, charities legislation. 2.3 DIRECT REPORTS Facilities and Maintenance Assistant Manager Facilities and Maintenance Officer x 3 Strategic & Operational direction, measuring performance against targets, regular reviews, role modelling, support, guidance, development and performance management. 3. JOB PURPOSE In the heart of London’s Knowledge Quarter, the Aga Khan Centre (AKC) is a place for education, knowledge, cultural exchange and insight into Muslim Civilisations and is home to three organisations founded by His Highness the Aga Khan, The Institute of Ismaili Studies (IIS), the Aga Khan University Institute for the Study of Muslim Civilisations (AKU-ISMC) and the Aga Khan Foundation United Kingdom (AKF(UK)). This role is responsible for managing the effective functioning of the Aga Khan Centre to provide safe, efficient, secure, legally compliant and environmentally friendly spaces for residents, employees, students and visitors. 1. Leading a small team, the Facilities and Operations Manager will be responsible for providing a seamless support service to manage and deliver high quality proactive and reactive maintenance to a standard which is in accordance with the nature of the Aga Khan Centre and provides value for money. The role covers all aspects of repairs & maintenance including plumbing, air conditioning, electrics, building fabric, health & safety and emergency support and requires the postholder to be hands on, supporting the maintenance team with technical support, knowledge & coordination as well as executing PPM plans, managing contractors and overseeing and inspecting works. The Facilities and Operations Manager will be a natural people person who leads with warmth, fairness and consistency, builds strong relationships across the team and the wider building, and is confident in managing day-to-day people situations with empathy, sound judgment and a balanced approach. This is an office-based role, Monday to Friday, 8 hours per day (including a 1-hour unpaid break), to be worked flexibly within the hours of 8am and 6pm. Whilst weekend work is rare, there may be occasional requirements to attend site outside of normal working hours. The postholder will also be required to be on call for out of hours emergencies. 4. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 4.1 AKC Building Operations · Oversee and manage the teams responsible for the reception, security and cleaning. · To prepare and keep up to date the Facilities Management (FM) Plan for AKC and the approach taken for each ‘hard’ and ‘soft’ FM service, including planned preventative maintenance and lifecycle replacements, ensuring that a suitable, safe, high-quality operating environment is provided. · To act as a point of contact for technical support in order to reduce supplier callouts and ensure the correct supplier is allocated to resolve the problem, after issues have been looked at in-house first. · To manage, plan and monitor the day-to-day repairs and maintenance activities of the building management team, ensuring works are completed on time, to the highest quality and in line with the approved FM plan. · To coordinate and manage activities of suppliers working in and around AKC including checking and approving completed work, ensuring it is on budget, within agreed timescales and to the quality required. · To act on defects highlighted in suppliers’ reports and ensure resolution following up on any unresolved issues that could affect plant or equipment performance and safety. · To ensure the AKC maintenance reporting system is updated with work carried out and outstanding tasks. · To ensure maintenance supplies, spares and stock levels are monitored and supplies are always available. · To receive, review, store and respond to suppliers’ reports, i.e. lifts, eye bolts, water sampling, lighting protection, etc. and supply a level of technical advice to ensure compliance with the relevant legislation. · To maintain and review equipment asset registers and update accordingly. · Responsible for the Health and Safety policy for AKC and liaising with outsourced consultants to ensure that AKC is compliant and required checks are carried out. · To maintain all maintenance and H&S documents, registers and systems at all times and act as knowledge-holder on behalf of AKF(UK) for Operation Manuals, as-built drawings, maintenance records, licences and operating certificates related to AKC. · Working in conjunction with the AKC IT team and external providers be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the core building services systems including for FM, Room Booking and Security. · To adhere to the AKC environmental policy promoting and driving energy & water saving initiatives as well as recycling initiatives at all times. · Plan and implement minor projects to optimize space utilisation within AKC. Participate as a key stakeholder in major projects. · Support the relationships with the tenants of the AKC retail units. · Ensure that the gardens embedded within the AKC, and the surrounding grounds and gardens are properly cared for and landscaped. · Liaise with the Estate Landlord and their agents regarding estate management, central services, infrastructure and security issues and maintenance of the public realm around AKC · Liaise with other building managers on the KX Estate and maintain good neighbourly relations. · Respond to emergency situations or other urgent issues involving AKC. 4.2 AKC Building Administration · To prepare an annual operational plan and budget for the AKC building management team. · To provide commentary and analysis for the monthly building management finance report and work with the Property Finance Manager to ensure that there is an up to date forecast at all times. · To lead any supplier procurement processes related to building management. · Monitor and approve all building management supplier invoices and staff expenses for payment in line with approved budgets. Seek additional approvals for unbudgeted or excess expenditure. · To ensure that safeguarding processes are embedded into all building management operations, all building management supplier contracts and the building management policies and processes. · To routinely review standards of service and ensure best practices are being followed and to benchmark the costs of AKC building management against equivalent buildings to assess and demonstrate value for money. · Manage and maintain the SLA standards, KPIs and targets for the AKC building management team. · To own the AKC building management risk register ensuring that it is up to date at all times. · To attend the AKF(UK) Property Committee meetings · Work flexibly in terms of working hours to support and accommodate events and incidents outside of regular working hours. · To ensure all tasks from the Security Audit are completed promptly, while maintaining up to date policies including the Critical Incident Plan and Office Security Plan 4.3 AKC Events · To ensure that the building management team support the events management team with all large and complex events, including organising facilities for car parking, traffic control, security, first aid, and hospitality. · To ensure that the building management team supports the dismantling and removal of the event materials and clearing the venue efficiently. 4.4 People Management · Help the AKF(UK) CEO and Senior Management Team promote an organisational culture of teamwork and service, high-quality, transparency and accountability, innovation, and inclusiveness. · Supervise, coach and mentor building management staff, building a highly skilled and motivated team demonstrating best practice in the sector and exemplifying AKF (UK) values and behaviours. · Oversee and set annual performance objectives and evaluate performance in accordance with the AKF (UK)’s staff performance management procedures. · Identify staff with potential for advancement and, as part of succession planning, contribute to their development. · Build a culture throughout the building management team of continuous improvement, in which staff are cognizant of and influence the broader learning agenda alongside delivery objectives. Carry out any other duties as assigned by the Head of Kings Cross Properties. 5. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, ATTRIBUTES & BEHAVIOURS 5.1 Qualifications · A degree in Facilities Management or similar qualification would be an advantage. 5.2 Experience · Experience of staff management · Experience of managing third-party contractors · Experience in managing complex mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems · Experience of managing planned preventative maintenance for hard and soft services · Experience of working in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment · Experience in planning programmes of work for maintenance in accordance with the buildings requirements and identifying gaps in the maintenance strategy. · Experience of identifying trends and developing/implementing management reports. · Experience in a similar field e.g. school, university or charity. 5.3 Skills · Good interpersonal, customer care and liaison with a wide range of stakeholders · Ability to explain technical issues to non-technical personnel. · Ability to work both strategically and operationally. · Ability to successfully manage time, plans and other related tasks. · Ability to continuously meet targets and surpass expectations. · Ability to lead, inspire and motivate a team to meet objectives. · Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. · Goo

It aims to raise awareness and understanding of all mental health conditions; fight to improve frontline mental health services for individuals and carers; provide support, information and guidance through SANEline, our Call Back service, email and text support; and promote and host research into causes, treatments and therapies through its Prince of Wales International Centre for SANE research. item.title: Young Person's Worker
item.description: About the role: Step into a role where your drive, resilience and belief in young people can truly change lives. As a Young Person’s Worker in Camden, you will be right alongside young people at risk of homelessness, helping them move from uncertainty towards stability and independence. This is hands on, purposeful work where every day matters, and where your determination can unlock real opportunity for those who need it most. In this role, you will manage a caseload of young people, building trusted relationships and empowering them to lead their journey forward. You will create and review personalised support and safety plans, support moves into independent accommodation, and help young people take confident steps into education, training or employment. Working within a trauma informed and strengths based approach, you will champion each young person’s goals while developing practical life skills such as budgeting, self care and cooking. You will also support access to essential services including mental health support, housing advice and employment pathways, motivating and coaching young people to take ownership of their futures. At Single Homeless Project (SHP), you will be part of a tenacious, values driven team that does not shy away from challenge and believes in doing things differently to achieve lasting change. We will support your ambition with ongoing training, development and the chance to grow your career while making a genuine impact. If you are ready to bring your energy, compassion and persistence to a role that truly matters, we would love to hear from you. *This role includes sleep-in shifts as part of the rota at Cecil Court, which are paid at an additional rate on top of your salary. About you: You bring experience working with young people in the community and in accommodation services. Your toolkit includes practical skills in motivation and coaching young people Your approach is creative, analytical, trauma-informed and rooted in a strengths and recovery model. You can creatively inspire opportunities for our young people to thrive and to develop to their highest potential. A non-judgmental approach to working with complex needs young people and to promote a strengths-based approach and an understanding of and commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion. Strong team-working and interpersonal skills, maintaining a collaborative approach to supporting young people achieve the outcomes and goals we support them to set for themselves. About Us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important Info: Closing Date: Sunday 4th October at midnight Interview date: Tuesday 13th, Wednesday 14th and Friday 16th October at SHP Head Office in Kings Cross Please note there will be a second stage interview in service for suitable candidates This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed (by SHP) for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.title: Trainee Energy Advisor
item.description: Location : Bristol Office Salary: £27,950 per annum (Band C), rising to £29,095 per annum after successful completion of a 5-month probationary period Job Type: Fixed Term (12 months, with possibility of extension), Full time (37.5 hours per week), part time considered (minimum 30 hours per week) The role: Working within our Household Energy Services (HES) team, the Trainee Energy Advisor role is for those who would like to learn the skills and gain experience of providing energy advice to households. You’ll be providing energy advice on our advice line and through a range of related projects, supporting low income and vulnerable households with billing queries, applications for grants and referrals to contractors for insulation and heating improvements. There may also be the opportunity to staff events and give advice to clients in person. As part of the role you’ll complete our HES Training Programme, including a City & Guilds qualification in Energy Awareness. Successful completion of your probationary period will lead to a change of role to Energy Advisor for the remainder of the contract. Specific responsibilities An applicant appointed to the role will be expected to: Work on the advice line and other telephone advice projects, making and receiving calls from people who may need help with energy-related issues. Record client details accurately and use your own knowledge to assess the help and support needed. Refer clients to other support organisations in their area as appropriate. Identify energy improvements that can be made to clients’ properties and refer them to installers who can carry out the work. Help vulnerable clients make applications for grants and switch energy tariffs where appropriate. Listen attentively to callers, some of whom may be angry or in distress, and respond to their needs in an empathetic way. Follow advice line processes and procedures. Maintain accurate records on our client database, including handling sensitive data appropriately and in compliance with GDPR guidance. Remain vigilant for safeguarding concerns during client interactions and report promptly to the designated Safeguarding Officer. Undertake the HES Training Programme, including the City & Guilds Level 3 Energy Awareness and Level 2 Fuel Debt Advice in the Community courses. To see a more detailed list of responsibilities please see the supporting documents attached. These documents are also available to download from our website. About you: Essential attributes for this role include: Ability to respond to clients in a respectful and engaging manner. Ability to communicate effectively with people, both verbally and in writing. Ability to work well in a team and identify how your skills complement others. Ability to maintain admin systems independently and accurately. Highly organised, with strong time and workload management. Empathy and compassion, with an awareness of the need to maintain your own wellbeing. A commitment to CSE’s aims and values of collaboration, conscientiousness and initiative. Skilled in the use of MS Office applications including Word, Excel and Outlook. Understanding of safeguarding principles and the importance of protecting vulnerable individuals. Please note, the above is an overview of the skills required for this role. To see the full list of essential and desirable skills please see the attached job description. Benefits: CSE offer a range of other benefits including: Company pension scheme (8% employer, 6% employee contributions) You will be entitled to 25 days' paid holiday, pro rata for part-time hours (plus statutory holidays) Subsidised bike purchase and Tech Scheme Life Assurance Health Cash plan Retail discounts Discounted breakdown cover and many more. We will pay fees and expenses on relevant training courses. We are flexible with the working hours of this role and will discuss this openly if you are invited to interview. How to apply To apply, please download and complete the application form available from our website and send it to our Jobs email. Your application should demonstrate your suitability for the role against the criteria outlined in the person specification and job description. The closing date for applications is 5pm on Wednesday 30 September 2026 . Interviews are expected to take place Tuesday 6 and Wednesday 7 October 2026 (in person at our Bristol office), though this is subject to change. If invited to interview, we will ask you to provide evidence of eligibility to work in the UK. #LI-DNI

item.title: Monitoring & Evaluation Manager
item.description: AllChild is a charity pioneering a new way of working with children and young people at the tipping point of need. Through our two-year, in-school Impact Programme, dedicated Link Workers build trusted relationships and bring together personalised support from families, schools and communities before problems escalate, helping children and young people progress socially, emotionally and academically and flourish in school and beyond. We are seeking a Monitoring & Evaluation Manager to shape how we monitor performance, evaluate our two-year Impact Programme and use evidence to improve support for children and young people. The Monitoring & Evaluation Manager will play a key role in strengthening AllChild’s approach to monitoring and evaluation, ensuring we generate robust evidence about programme implementation and outcomes and use it to improve our work. Reporting to the Head of Monitoring & Evaluation, they will oversee core M&E activity and support programme performance management, organisational decision-making and external reporting. They will work closely with Programme Design, Delivery, Systems and colleagues across AllChild. We are looking for someone with strong analytical skills, excellent project management and communication, and a clear understanding of what robust, high-quality monitoring and evaluation requires. They will be confident working with complex data and solving problems, translating M&E requirements into effective systems and reporting tools, and communicating findings clearly and accurately, including what the evidence can and cannot tell us. They will line manage the M&E Officer and help build a strong M&E function that enables AllChild to understand, improve and demonstrate its impact. For further information and to apply, please download the job pack and visit our dedicated recruitment page via the link below. Closing date: 6 October 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received, so early application is encouraged. We recognise that candidates may use AI tools to support research and check grammar. However, we ask that all supporting statements and application responses reflect your own thoughts and experiences. Over-reliance on AI may limit our ability to assess your individual skills, critical thinking, and personal approach, which are important parts of our selection process.

item.title: National ISVA Coordinator
item.description: Come and join our team! We are looking for an exceptional individual(s) to join our busy team at LimeCulture, the UK’s leading sexual violence training and consultancy organisation. LimeCulture has extensive experience of supporting sexual violence service providers and commissioners to deliver safe, effective, and survivor-centred services. We work collaboratively with organisations to strengthen coordination, address gaps in provision, and embed trauma-informed practices. Our support includes independent service reviews and evaluations, delivery of specialist training, and consultancy support to drive meaningful, sustainable improvements. As the UK’s leading provider of training for Independent Sexual Violence Advisers (ISVAs), we deliver accredited development and continued professional development (CPD) programmes that build confidence, competence, and capability across this specialist workforce. We are seeking a National ISVA Coordinator(s). The postholder(s) will provide an initial point of contact, undertake initial risk and needs assessment, provide trauma-informed information and support, and coordinate onward referral and handover to appropriate local ISVA and specialist services. A key focus of the role will be providing initial support to adult and child survivors affected by group-based child sexual abuse and exploitation (GBCSAE), as well as other forms of sexual violence. The role will involve working effectively with police and other agencies, helping individuals navigate complex review, criminal justice and support pathways, while promoting choice, control and informed decision-making. The role is a national coordination function and is not intended to replace ongoing local ISVA casework where appropriate local provision is available.

item.title: Programme Development Manager
item.description: Saferworld is seeking an experienced Programme Development Manager to join our Funding & Programme Development Team. The Programme Development Manager will support a portfolio of Saferworld’s teams in co-designing and mobilising funding for peace, security and justice programmes alongside Saferworld’s partners. The successful applicant will have a focus of 3-4 countries, which will be decided based on the candidate’s experience and preference. Working closely with Regional Directors, Country Managers, and programme and grant management colleagues, the post-holder will lead on: coordinating and facilitating programme co-design processes (including taking the lead in facilitating co-design, processes, drafting high quality concept notes and proposals, theories of change, logical models, risk matrixes and budgets); developing and supporting the implementation of long-term country funding strategies; and supporting new donor engagement and sustaining relationships with current donors. The post-holder will be responsible for managing funding portfolios across institutional and non-institutional donors in our programmes. The post-holder will have a successful track record in developing programmes and leading new business development efforts with institutional donors such as Global Affairs Canada (GAC), the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), the European Union (EU), UN agencies and European Governments such as Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida). Additional experience in mobilising resource from trusts and foundations and other non-traditional funding mechanisms is desirable. Strong applicants will have proven programme experience, such as in project management or programme support, which equips them to lead and inform high-quality programme design. They will be skilled in coordinating complex processes, facilitating participatory co-creation with partners, and ensuring proposals are robust, contextually relevant, and strategically aligned.

item.title: Project Officer
item.description: About the Role This Project Officer role is part of Bright Futures, our mentoring and employability support programme for young Gypsy and Traveller people aged 15-25. You will keep the programme organised, connected and running smoothly - managing records and systems, building partnerships, and coordinating workshops and activities so that young people can find their way in and get the most out of the support on offer. Many of the young people we work with have faced exclusion or discrimination within mainstream education, employment and other services, and are often not in education, employment or training (NEET). The processes, systems and communications you manage all need to be accessible and responsive to young people who may be wary of formal support. You will coordinate outreach and community engagement to bring young people into the programme, build and maintain relationships with colleges, training providers, employers and community organisations, and manage day-to-day communications with young people, families and partners. You will set up and coordinate a Youth Advisory Group, giving young people a structured way to help shape the programme. You may also be asked to cover for mentee support when a mentor is unavailable or at capacity. This role is funded by The National Lottery Community Fund. About You This role is for someone who enjoys keeping things organised and connected, and who wants that work to make a real, practical difference in young people's lives – someone committed to supporting young people from marginalised and underserved communities to fairly access relevant opportunities. You will be highly organised, with strong admin skills and confidence using digital tools and databases. You will also be a confident communicator, equally comfortable writing a promotional post, following up with a training provider, or having a conversation with a young person or their family. The role is ideal for someone with experience of outreach, building partnerships or community engagement, who can build trusting relationships with a wide range of people – from young people and families to colleges, employers and community organisations. You should be open to providing support to young people when needed. We don't expect you to already have all the answers what matters most is your admin and organisational ability, your commitment to the communities we work with, and your confidence building relationships across a wide range of people and settings. We will support your development through supervision, training and a small, collaborative team environment. We know not everyone will meet every requirement in the job description below, but if you feel you have what it takes, please apply and tell us how your experience and skills make you suitable. If you are not sure what the work looks like or you want to ask questions before applying, we are happy to chat with you about the role. Please contact Mini Ravi (Programme Lead) by calling on our office phone. About LGT and Bright Futures London Gypsies and Travellers (LGT) challenges social exclusion and discrimination, working for change in partnership with Gypsy and Traveller communities living on council caravan sites, roadside camps, in flats and houses, and those experiencing homelessness. Bright Futures supports Gypsy and Traveller young men and women aged 15–25 through mentoring, skills development, employability and wellbeing support. The programme helps young people build confidence, develop practical skills and identify realistic pathways into training and employment, working at their own pace and around their needs and interests. The programme is shaped by a deep understanding of the Gypsy and Traveller culture, and designed to empower young people to engage with wider society with pride, motivation and confidence. Our services also include accommodation advice and advocacy, family support, community development, research, policy work and campaigns, and we support hundreds of individuals and families each year. We are a small, committed and supportive team who seek to live our organisational values throughout our work: Collaboration, Courage, Empowerment, Inclusivity, Equity, Community. We are committed to equal opportunities and workforce diversity. We strongly encourage applications from Gypsy and Traveller communities. To Apply Review the responsibilities and person specification in the job description enclosed. Using the ‘Apply Now’ button, please submit your CV Instead of a cover letter, please submit answers to the following 3 questions in the space provided when you apply. 1. Briefly tell us about your experience of providing admin and coordination work. What exactly did you do and what tools or systems did you use? 2. What is one of the barriers that young people from vulnerable or marginalised backgrounds face around education, training and work? Why? 3. Why are you interested in this role and working with London Gypsies & Travellers? 250-300 word answers for each question is enough, but you are welcome to write more. There is no right answer and we are not interested in perfect responses. We want to know about you and the knowledge, skills, and experience your will bring to the role. Closing date: Wednesday 30th September 2026 Interviews: Thursday 22nd October (in person), Tuesday 27th October (potential stage 2, online) Please check you are available on these dates before applying, in case you are shortlisted for interviews. Please note: An enhanced DBS check is required for the role . Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

item.title: Youth Mentor
item.description: About the Role This Youth Development Mentor for young men is part of Bright Futures, our mentoring and employability support programme for young Gypsy and Traveller people aged 15-25. You will build trusted, consistent 1-1 mentoring relationships with young men, supporting them to grow in confidence, work out what they want, and build the skills to get there. You will deliver the programme's set mentoring offer, adapting your approach to individuals as needed, alongside group sessions on skills and personal development. Many of the young men we work with have had negative experiences of school or other services and are often not in education, employment or training (NEET). The role is about helping the young men move forward at a pace that works for them, towards something they've chosen and can stick with, rather than pushing them down a set route. You will keep detailed records of progress and milestones reached. You will also play a role in outreach and community engagement – building relationships with families and community members. This includes keeping up good working relationships with colleges, training providers and employers, and making sure young people's voices are heard, both within Bright Futures and externally. This role is funded by The National Lottery Community Fund. About You This role is for someone who wants to make a real difference in young people's lives – someone committed to supporting young men from marginalised and underserved communities to get equitable access to opportunities, and to helping bring about wider change for those communities. You will enjoy the challenge of working with young men who may take time to trust and engage, and see that as part of what makes the role rewarding. The role is ideal for someone with experience of mentoring, youth work or a similar community-based role working with young men (paid or voluntary). Someone patient, non-judgemental and comfortable adapting support to suit the person in front of you. You will be just as comfortable speaking to family members as with college staff or social services. We don't expect you to already have all the answers – what matters most is your commitment and ability to build genuine, trusting relationships and to keep going with young people who may take time to open up. We will support your development through supervision, training and a small, collaborative team environment. We know not everyone will meet every requirement in the job description below, but if you feel you have what it takes, please apply and tell us how your experience and skills make you suitable. If you are not sure what the work looks like or you want to ask questions before applying, we are happy to chat with you about the role. Please contact Mini Ravi (Programme Lead) by calling our office phone. About LGT and Bright Futures London Gypsies and Travellers (LGT) challenges social exclusion and discrimination, working for change in partnership with Gypsy and Traveller communities living on council caravan sites, roadside camps, in flats and houses, and those experiencing homelessness. Bright Futures supports Gypsy and Traveller young men and women aged 15–25 through mentoring, skills development, employability and wellbeing support. The programme helps young people build confidence, develop practical skills and identify realistic pathways into training and employment, working at their own pace and around their needs and interests. The programme is shaped by a deep understanding of the Gypsy and Traveller culture, and designed to empower young people to engage with wider society with pride, motivation and confidence. Our services also include accommodation advice and advocacy, family support, community development, research, policy work and campaigns, and we support hundreds of individuals and families each year. We are a small, committed and supportive team who seek to live our organisational values throughout our work: Collaboration, Courage, Empowerment, Inclusivity, Equity, Community. We are committed to equal opportunities and workforce diversity. We strongly encourage applications from Gypsy and Traveller communities. To Apply Review the responsibilities and person specification in the job description enclosed. Using the ‘Apply Now’ button, please submit your CV Instead of a cover letter, please submit answers to the following 3 questions in the space provided when you apply. 1. Briefly tell us about your experience of working with young men/people. What did you do and what kind of support did you provide? 2. What is one of the barriers young men from vulnerable or marginalised backgrounds face around education, training and work? Why? 3. Why are you interested in this role and working with London Gypsies & Travellers? 250-300 word answers for each question is enough, but you are welcome to write more. There is no right answer and we are not interested in perfect responses. We want to know about you and the knowledge, skills, and experience your will bring to the role. Closing date: Wednesday 30th September 2026 Interviews: Thursday 15th October (stage 1, in person), Tuesday 20th October (stage 2, online) Please check you are available on these dates before applying, in case you are shortlisted for interviews. Please note: An enhanced DBS check is required for the role . Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

item.title: Needle Exchange & Harm Reduction Coordinator
item.description: Job description Providence Row is recruiting for a Needle Exchange & Harm Reduction Coordinator . Founded in 1860, we are an established charity that delivers support for individuals who are homeless and rough sleepers. This is a fixed term contract until 23 October 2027 (35 hours per week) with a salary of £35,020. Job located at The Dellow Centre, London E1 7SA. Auto enrolment from day one into the People’s Pension. The role will support individuals to reduce the risks associated with drug and alcohol use and to connect with treatment, recovery and wider support. Also to deliver a person-centred and strengths-based approach while building relationships and creating opportunities for people to access wider health and support services. Closing date is Monday 05 October 2026. To apply, please upload your CV with a covering letter detailing how you meet the person specification. Posted on: 15 September 2026 Closing date: 05 October 2026 at 23:30 Job ref: Needle Exchange & Harm Reduction Coordinator Tags: Health / Medical, Homelessness The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Senior Direct Marketing Executive (Creative Lead)
item.description: Location: Homebased with travel to London, fundraising and industry events required occasionally Contract type: Fixed term contract (May 2027) Salary: £35,581 per annum pro-rated plus £5023.71 London weighting pro-rated if applicable Hours: 35 hours per week Closing date: Tuesday 29th September 2026 at 11:30pm Do you want to bring your creative flair and digital expertise to a cause that matters? Join Shelter as our Senior Direct Marketing Executive (Creative Lead) and play a vital role in delivering our key campaigns. About the role Our Senior Direct Marketing Executive (Creative Lead) will play an important role in delivering our multi-million-pound campaign at winter and work across Shelter’s individual supporter digital recruitment channels, propositions and products. You’ll be working alongside an ambitious team delivering the individual giving programme & strategy. You’ll bring digital fundraising (or marketing) expertise, an audience understanding and your creative flair to develop standout digital campaigns. Role specifics You’ll develop and deliver audience-led and creatively inspired Individual Giving campaigns that attract, convert and retain cash, regular giving and lottery supporters. Managing projects from planning and creative development through to evaluation, you’ll create compelling multi-channel campaigns, oversee budgets and performance targets, and use testing and insight to optimise results and supporter lifetime value. You’ll collaborate with internal teams, agencies and suppliers, champion an inclusive and positive team culture, and ensure all fundraising activity meets relevant regulatory and data protection requirements. Apply to be part of our team and be the change you want to see in society. Benefits We offer a wide range of benefits, including 30 days of annual leave, enhanced family friendly policies, pension and interest free travel loans. Our employees also have access to a tenancy deposit loan, payroll giving, cycle to work scheme and an employee assistance programme. We are happy to talk about flexible working, personal growth, and to promote a workplace where you can be yourself and achieve success based only on your merit. About the team This post sits within the Individual Giving Team, which is responsible for delivering a diverse programme of work with ambitious income targets that support our organisational strategy, across cash, regular giving and lottery products. How to Apply Please click ‘Apply for Job’ below . You are required to submit your work history and a supporting statement. The supporting statement should include your responses to the points in the ‘About You’ section of the job description of no more than 1500 words in total. Please provide specific examples following the STAR format and ensure you demonstrate how you address the behaviours below in your responses: We prioritise diversity and have an inclusive and open mindset Any applications submitted without a supporting statement will not be considered. About Shelter Home is a human right. It’s our foundation and where we thrive. Yet everyday millions of people are being devastated by the housing emergency. We exist to defend the right to a safe home. Because home is everything. We need ambitious, passionate people to join us. This is your chance to play a part in the fundamental change we are striving to achieve. Our enemy is the social injustice at the core of the escalating housing emergency. To win this fight, we must be representative of the people we are here to help and those who support our movement. In all our people decisions, we take pride in being inclusive, equitable and transparent. We are committed to combating racism both within and outside Shelter. We welcome you on our journey to becoming truly anti-racist. Safeguarding statement Safeguarding is everyone's business. Shelter is committed to protecting the health, wellbeing and human rights of those we support, and enabling them to live free from harm, abuse and neglect. All our staff will be expected to observe professional standards of behaviour and conduct their work in line with our Safeguarding Policies. Shelter does not accept unsolicited CVs from external recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them.

item.title: Philanthropy Manager
item.description: Are you a relational leader passionate about Christian mission? Church Mission Society (CMS) seeks a dynamic Philanthropy Manager to shape our strategy and unlock growth at a pivotal moment. You will build generous high-net-worth pipelines, leading significant income opportunities to fuel Jesus-centred mission across the UK and globally. Join our team and bring Christ’s love and hope to the edges. Ø Permanent, 35 hours per week. Ø Hybrid working – approximately two days a week at CMS House, Oxford. Ø Starting salary of £42,840 per annum with a generous pension contribution: up to 10 per cent employer contribution on annual salary. Incremental increases to salaries are applied annually. Ø CMS offers 36 days of annual and bank holiday leave as well as enhanced paid sickness, maternity, paternity and adoption leave. Ø CMS supports the mental wellbeing of its employees and offers a generous rewards and wellbeing package, including: · Access to 24/7 employee assistance programme with qualified counsellors. · Up to three volunteer days per annum. · Up to three family emergency leave days per annum. · Retreats and resources for prayer life. We welcome applications from everyone. We particularly welcome applications from individuals from minority groups as they are currently underrepresented within our organisation at this level. All appointments are made on merit of skill, experience and potential as set out in the job description and person specification. Your role Church Mission Society (CMS) is a dynamic global community with a 227-year history of making disciples of Jesus at the edges of societies. To support an ambitious three-year plan to see communities transformed and local leaders empowered, we are appointing a Philanthropy Manager to establish a sustainable income strategy. Reporting directly to the Fundraising and Communications Director, you will line manage a dedicated four-person philanthropy team. You will own the strategic direction of our high-net-worth individual programme, as well as our trust and foundations income portfolios. Key responsibilities include network mapping, cultivating robust prospect pipelines, and embedding a best-in-class donor stewardship framework. Additionally, you will equip senior stakeholders to secure high-value major gifts. We are seeking a proactive, values-led Christian leader who excels at translating complex contextual mission work into compelling funding proposals. The ideal candidate brings a proven record of major donor fundraising, team management expertise, and an analytical approach to CRM-driven donor pipelines. Based at CMS House with hybrid working, this role offers a rare opportunity to pioneer growth that empowers marginalised communities worldwide. The organisation you’ll be joining Church Mission Society is comprised of people who are passionate about mission and fired up about helping people follow Jesus. For over 200 years CMS has been at the forefront of global mission, living out the gospel of Jesus, seeing lives changed and communities transformed. If you join CMS, you will find an organisation that has been reinvigorated with a fresh vision to make disciples of Jesus among people at the edges, both in the UK and around the world. What you’ll need to succeed The successful candidate will be a self-starter with high levels of motivation and the ability to develop and deliver strategy the leader of the team. You will have a track record in successfully initiating, managing and developing relationships with high-net-worth individuals securing six/seven figure donations and grants, via proposals or through face-to-face meetings as required. It is a requirement for this post holder to be a committed and practising Christian as well as committed to CMS’s values and aims. Further details can be found in the job description and person specification available to download on the CMS website. Our commitment to you Our core values of being pioneering, relational, faithful and evangelistic are integral to everything we do, and we work hard to ensure that every member of staff is valued, supported and encouraged to continually learn and develop their skills. We are committed to the safeguarding and protection of the people we serve, our partners, our volunteers, and our staff. We believe that every child or adult we come into contact with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm and abuse. Our recruitment and selection processes are in line with our Safeguarding Policy Closing date We must get your application by midnight on Sunday 4th October 2026 Interviews are planned to be held on Wednesday 13th October 2026 in CMS House, Oxford. To apply Please send your application form and CV via our website or by post to HR Team, Church Mission Society, Watlington Road, Oxford OX4 6BZ. CVs will only be considered when sent with a completed application form, which is available to download from our website. Candidates for all UK roles must already be eligible to work in the UK, with a valid visa and work permit if required. As a member of the Inter-agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, CMS has committed to systematically check with previous employers from the last five years for any ‘SEAH’ (Sexual Exploitation, Abuse or Harassment) issues relating to all potential new hires.

item.title: Direct Marketing Officer - Regular Giving (Lottery & Lead Generation)
item.description: Battersea is entering an exciting phase of innovation and transformation as we continue into the second year of our new five-year strategy. Our fundraising team bridges the journey of the animals in our care with the wider public, demonstrating how their contributions enable us to support every dog and cat. We currently have a permanent opportunity for someone to join us as a Direct Marketing Officer - Regular Giving (Lottery & Lead Generation). As part of this role, you will manage and deliver a series of high standard direct marketing campaigns across our Regular Giving programme. You will be recruiting, retaining and upgrading regular donors to generate agreed income through a variety of direct marketing methods such as direct dialogue, DRTV, digital, and direct mail. You’ll also be encouraging regular monthly gifts or support via one of our main products such as general Regular Giving and Sponsorship, our Lottery, Value Exchange programme and other methods of committed giving as they arise. What we can offer you: In return for your commitment to our cause and to recognise the value of our employees, Battersea offers a range of benefits to support the wellbeing of our employees. These include: • 28 days of annual leave (plus 8 days paid public holidays) per year. • Discounted gym memberships and cycle to work schemes. • Employee Assistance Programme and access to Wellbeing Resources. • Generous pension contributions - up to 10% employer contribution. • Free healthcare cash plan, where you can claim for a range of treatment including dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropody and acupuncture every year. • Annual interest-free season ticket loans. We are also committed to providing learning and development to our employees. During your time with us, we provide support for your professional and career development, including access to digital and in-person training programmes, leadership and management training, mentoring and much more. Our hybrid working model: We operate a 50% onsite hybrid working model, with our office-based staff splitting their time between site based and home working. This enables our office-based staff to balance the benefits of home working with onsite collaboration and maintaining a connection to our cause. Diversity and inclusion: We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive experience for all staff, volunteers and trustees and those hoping to join us. We operate an anonymised shortlisting process and actively seek to ensure our process is fair and equitable for all. We understand the value of diverse voices, perspectives, and experiences to help us deliver even more for our dogs and cats, and we welcome applicants from all sections of the community. As a Disability Confident Committed Employer we will ask about any adjustments you may need at application and/or interview stage, and if you are offered a role with us, we’ll talk to you about any workplace adjustments you may need to help you perform at your best. If you would like to talk more about this, please contact us. Greyscale copies of the recruitment pack are also available on request. More about us: At Battersea, we aim to never turn away a dog or cat in need of help. We give each one lots of love, expert care and get to know their characters and quirks so we can find them a new home that’s just right for them. Join us and help us be here for every dog and cat, wherever they are, for as long as they need us. Acceptable use of AI: At Battersea, we value expertise. We recognise each candidate that applies to us will have a range of expertise they can offer us, so we want to hear about this in your own words. We understand the support that generative artificial intelligence (AI) software can offer but it can also lead to numerous applications presenting as generic and impersonal. This makes it difficult to gain understanding of your unique experience. To best showcase yourself, we encourage you to write your responses without the assistance of AI. If you require the use of AI software to aid in completing your application, we ask you use the generative responses as a prompt for writing your answers and avoid copying and pasting. You must also ensure the information presented in your application accurately reflects your experience. Closing date : 28th September 2026 All applications must be submitted before the closing date advertised. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Interview date(s): First Round (questions format): w/c 5th October 2026 Second Round (in person, task and further questions): w/c 12th October 2026 For more information about the role, please download our Recruitment pack. To apply for the role, please click the "Apply" button.

item.title: Marketing Content Executive
item.description: The Marketing Content Executive is responsible for creating engaging, audience-focused content that supports fundraising, supporter engagement and brand objectives across digital and offline channels. The role plays a key part in bringing MAF's mission and impact to life through compelling storytelling, effective marketing copywriting and content that inspires supporters to engage, give and advocate. Working closely with colleagues across Marketing, Fundraising and Donor Experience, the role develops and adapts content for campaigns, supporter journeys, email communications, web pages, social media and printed materials, ensuring communications are creative, consistent and aligned with organisational priorities. The role also provides support for the development of supporter engagement activities and selected events, helping to create meaningful experiences that strengthen supporter relationships. Salary: £32,510.27 Location: This role will be based at our Folkestone office, operating on a hybrid working arrangement with 2 days a week in the office. Working Hours: Office open officially from 9am to 5.30pm (Mon-Fri) and 9am-4pm on Fridays. Closing date: 7 October 2026 Responsibilities Campaigns and content Write, edit and proof high-quality copy tailored to channel and audience ensuring clarity, consistency and alignment with brand tone and messaging; brief designers and videographers as needed. Support in the maintenance of MAFs asset register and ensure brand consistency across the relevant touchpoints. Support the creation of case studies and story gathering in collaboration with programme, communications and fundraising colleagues. Create, update and maintain copy for content across multiple marketing channels, including website pages, email communications and campaign assets. Digital marketing and analytics Set up campaign tracking (e.g. UTM parameters, QR codes, short links) and ensure accurate tagging across channels. Supporter journeys and fundraising collaboration Work collaboratively with donor experience and supporter engagement colleagues to develop content that supports supporter journeys, appeals and stewardship, and improves engagement outcomes. Help segment audiences and tailor content to increase engagement and Donor Income – one-off, regular and monthly. Ensure supporter-facing content reflects organisational purpose, values and safeguarding standards. Events Support the Marketing & Events Coordinator in delivering supporter and fundraising events, including assisting with event preparation, materials, creative content and on-the-day delivery. Contribute creative storytelling ideas and engagement concepts for supporter experiences and engagement tools, including the MAF Cube and future event activities. Project management and ways of working Champion cross-team collaboration and clear communication; develop simple checklists and templates to aid consistency. Maintain orderly files and version control for campaign materials and approvals. Brand, compliance and risk Uphold brand, tone of voice and accessibility standards across all outputs. Comply with GDPR, PECR and fundraising regulations; handle personal data securely and ethically. Follow organisational policies, including safeguarding, health and safety, and inclusion. Any other responsibilities as requested by your line manager. This job description reflects the current requirements of the role. As duties and responsibilities change and develop, this will be reviewed and will be subject to amendment in consultation with the post-holder. Tasks common to all staff: Role modelling of organisational values and beliefs - to contribute to the shared spiritual life of the MAF UK team as a unique Christian charity. This will include attendance and participation in corporate times of biblical reflection and corporate prayer. To participate in appropriate matrix programme and project teams, contributing skills and expertise to required timescales from the appropriate programme leader. To keep line manager informed of all relevant and timely information. At all times comply with statutory requirements for handling personal and sensitive data in a confidential manner. To abide by MAF UK’s Safeguarding and Conduct Policies, and all other organisational policies provided on the Intranet. Terms : At least 36 hours with 1 hour for lunch daily unpaid per week. Hours should be agreed with line manager according to the flexible working policy. Flexibility will be required for working additional hours and travel to meet business needs or for travel or meetings etc. on weekends. Annual leave entitlement of 22 days (158.4 hours) per year and 8 days (58.5 hours) paid public holidays per year. Non-contributory pension scheme (10%) salary.
