item.title: Stewardship Manager
item.description: Crisis is the national charity for people experiencing homelessness. We believe everyone should have the foundation of a safe, affordable home. Location: Hybrid from our London office, E1, with the requirement to travel as needed. We are open to a range of flexible working options, in line with Crisis' Hybrid Working Policy. Contract: Permanent About the role This is an exciting opportunity to lead the delivery of high-quality stewardship and donor engagement for some of Crisis' most committed supporters. As Stewardship Manager, you will ensure high-value donors receive meaningful, timely and supporter-centred communications and experiences that build trust, confidence and long-term support for our mission. You will also lead and develop a small stewardship team, driving excellent delivery, strong processes and effective use of CRM and engagement systems. This is a highly collaborative role that combines people management, project delivery and supporter-focused thinking. Your experience We are very open to hearing from a range of candidates with different backgrounds. You may be: A Stewardship Manager, Donor Relations Manager or Donor Experience Manager, leading supporter engagement, reporting and stewardship programmes for major donors, trusts or corporate partners. A Major Giving, Philanthropy or Trusts fundraiser who enjoys donor engagement who wants to specialise in supporter experience. A fundraising operations or supporter engagement professional with experience coordinating communications, events and donor journeys across complex stakeholder groups. About you You have experience delivering donor stewardship, supporter engagement or relationship management activity in a high value fundraising environment, preferably across multiple high value fundraising types such as trusts, philanthropy and partnerships. You are skilled at managing multiple projects and deadlines while maintaining high standards of quality and accuracy. You can translate impact, financial or programme information into engaging communications for external audiences. You have experience managing or supervising staff and supporting teams to deliver excellent results. You are a strong collaborator who can build effective relationships with stakeholders across an organisation. Above all, you are motivated by Crisis' mission and values and want to help end homelessness for good Please see the full Job Pack for a complete list of requirements for this role. We realise that long lists of criteria can be daunting, and you may not want to apply for a role unless you feel 100% qualified. However, if you feel you have relevant examples to answer the screening questions, we encourage you to apply. We believe diversity is a strength, and our aim is to make sure that Crisis truly reflects the communities we serve. We are actively working towards our organisation being a place where everyone can thrive and make their best contribution to our mission of ending homelessness for good. We know that the more perspectives, voices and experiences we can bring to this work, the better. We particularly welcome applications from people who have lived experience of homelessness, and people from all marginalised groups, communities and backgrounds. Working at Crisis Our values, Bold, Impactful, Collaborative and Equitable , are at the heart of everything we do as we continue in our mission to end homelessness. Our staff, members and volunteers are vital to getting the right government policies in place, providing breakthrough services and building a supportive community. We'll lead by example to nurture a positive and ambitious workplace guided by ending homelessness. As a member of the team, you will have access to a wide range of employee benefits including: A competitive salary. Please note our salaries are fixed to counter inequity and we do not negotiate at offer stage. Interest free loans for travel season ticket, cycle to work, and deposit to secure a tenancy. Pension scheme with an employer contribution of 8.5%. 28 days' annual leave (pro rata) which increases with service to 31 days and the option to purchase up to 10 additional days' leave. Enhanced maternity, paternity, shared parental and adoption pay. Flexible working around the core hours 10am to 4pm. Wellbeing Leave to be used flexibly. And more! (Full list of benefits available on the Crisis website.) Alongside our excellent staff benefits, we will support your ongoing development to build your skills, experience and career. When you join us, you will have the opportunity to join our staff diversity networks, which aim to champion issues across the organisation, enable staff to be their authentic and best selves and contribute to making Crisis a truly diverse organisation. How do I apply? Please click on the 'Apply for Job' button below. Our shortlisting process is anonymised as part of our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. We do not ask for CVs. Instead, we ask you to complete the work history section and answer the screening questions so we can assess you fairly and objectively. At least two members of staff score all applications. Closing date: Sunday 25th September at 23:59 Interview process: Two panel interviews with competency and values-based questions. Interview date and location: Teams (online), week commencing 5th October. AI in Job Applications We understand some candidates use AI tools when applying. Whilst we welcome the use of technology to support clear communication and structure, we want to learn more about you, so please ensure that your application reflects your own skills, knowledge and experiences. Accessibility We want our recruitment process to be as accessible as possible. If you need us to make an adjustment or provide additional support as you apply for a role, please contact our Talent Acquisition team via our website and they will be will be happy can help. For more information about our work please visit our website. Registered Charity Numbers: E&W1082947, SC040094.

item.title: Trusts and Grants Manager
item.description: Turn compelling ideas into vital funding for hospice care. We are looking for an experienced and motivated Trusts & Grants Manager to grow sustainable income from trusts, foundations, grant-making bodies and statutory funders. Reporting to the Head of Philanthropy, you will build a strong funding pipeline, create persuasive applications and develop trusted relationships that help local people and their families living with life-limiting illness. What you’ll do Research and prioritise new funding opportunities, including higher-value and multi-year grants. Write compelling applications, proposals, cases for support and impact reports. Manage funder relationships, stewardship, reporting deadlines and grant conditions. Work with colleagues across the Hospice to develop realistic, accurately costed projects. Maintain accurate CRM records and provide clear pipeline and income reporting. About you You will bring proven trusts and foundations fundraising experience, excellent written communication and strong relationship-management skills. Highly organised and collaborative, you will be comfortable balancing multiple deadlines, using insight to shape priorities and representing the Hospice professionally. Experience of CRM systems is essential; knowledge of Donorfy, volunteer management or hospice fundraising would be an advantage. Why join us? Join a compassionate, ambitious organisation where your expertise will directly support high-quality hospice care. We offer a generous holiday allowance, pension options, free on-site parking, flexible working opportunities where appropriate, staff discounts and access to learning and development. Ready to make a measurable difference? Apply with details of how your experience, skills and approach match the requirements of the role.

item.title: Breathing Space Project Coordinator (Wales)
item.description: Position: Breathing Space Coordinator, Wales Hours: 21 hours per week Contract: Fixed term until March 2029 Location: Home-based in Wales Salary: £26,912 per annum FTE, (£16,147 per annum actual for 21 hours per week) plus excellent benefits Salary Band and Job Family: Band 1, Charity You’ll start at our entry point salary of £26,912 per annum FTE (£16,147 actual), increasing to £28,594 per annum FTE (£17,156 actual) after 6 months service and satisfactory performance and to £30,276 per annum FTE (£18,166 actual) after a further 6 months. About us We make sure people living with MS are at the centre of everything we do. And it’s this commitment that unites us across the UK. Our strategy is based on what people affected by MS have told us is important to them. It gives us a clear and determined focus. Our work is based on the hopes and aspirations of our MS community. Together we campaign at all levels, fund ground-breaking research and provide award winning support and information. Our people are our greatest asset and the key to our success. We offer a vibrant, progressive working environment where you'll be able to make a difference. About this job This part-time, fixed-term role (21 hours per week) will coordinate our Breathing Space project in Wales until March 2029. The project enables unpaid carers supporting people with MS and other neurological conditions to take short breaks. We are seeking an enthusiastic, experienced Project Coordinator who enjoys delivering fixed-term funded projects, working directly with the people we support and our volunteers. Excellent communication skills and a proven ability to achieve project objectives are essential. You will work closely with unpaid carers, people affected by MS and other neurological conditions, key external partners, the Service and Support Team, the Director for Wales and teams across the MS Society. Focused on outcomes and tangible results, you will build strong stakeholder partnerships and represent the MS Society at meetings and events promoting the project to unpaid carers. The role can be based anywhere in Wales, but regular travel across Wales is expected. Welsh language skills are desirable Closing date for applications: 9:00 on Monday 28th September 2026. Anticipated interview date: 6th & 7th October. Interested? PLEASE PRESS THE 'HOW TO APPLY' BUTTON FOR MORE INFORMATION. Equal Opportunities We particularly welcome applications from people with disabilities and or from ethnic minority backgrounds. We’d be grateful if you downloaded and completed the equality and diversity monitoring form and submit it with your application. Disability Confident Employer We’re a Disability Confident Employer and we’re committed to promoting equality and diversity. You can ask for reasonable adjustments as part of both our recruitment and new starter on-boarding processes. If you need any help or adjustments to apply for this role, please contact us. You can also ask for the application materials to be sent to you in a different format. Such as for them to be sent to you by email or in a larger word format. More about our employee benefits: We have a wide range of employee benefits including (but not limited to): Encouraging work life balance 38 days paid annual leave (including bank holidays), pro-rata for part-time More annual leave entitlement, based on length of employment Smart working options (with the opportunity to work remotely and find a smart working pattern that suits both you and us) Flexible working options Caring for you and your family Generous sick pay entitlement More sick pay entitlement, based on length of employment Opportunity to buy and sell annual leave in each calendar year Free access to a GP virtually 24 hours a day/7 days a week allowing you unlimited advice, reassurance and where appropriate diagnosis Enhanced leave for new parents Free access to a confidential 24 hours a day/7 days a week helpline service for both you and your family with a specialist range of support and information Special leave options (such as up to 5 days paid leave for domestic or personal emergencies a year) 10 days paid disability leave a year, pro-rata for part-time 10 days paid carers’ leave a year, pro-rata for part-time Cycle to work scheme Death in service scheme New family-friendly benefits, including paid leave: In the event of miscarriage or still birth To support fertility treatments For antenatal appointments for both parents Thinking about your finances Enhanced salary sacrifice pension scheme Discounted season ticket loan and interest-free emergency loans Give as you earn to support other charities of your choice before tax New employee portal item.title: Environmental Officer/ Swyddog Amgylcheddol
item.description: The National Lottery Community Fund is delivering an environmental strategy that will not only help communities we Fund but also identifies us as an exemplar in managing our own environmental impact. It’s an exciting time to join the Fund as the Environmental Officer role will help lead our journey to Net Zero emissions as well as support our Environmental Strategy both internally and externally. An interest in climate change and an understanding of environmental sustainability in the workplace will be a key part to this role as well as the confidence to bring in new ideas and support engagement of staff. The role will sit within the Facilities team which helps support all nine of the Fund’s offices which are based in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. The Environmental Officer role will be varied but some of the key responsibilities are: You will be responsible for facilitating the Fund’s efforts to reduce its environmental impact and move towards being a Net Zero organisation. You will lead best practice around environmental sustainability across sites and engage staff to consider their own impact. You will draw learning and resources from external sources, to develop an array of approaches, with a view to getting all staff to consider the resources they use, irrespective of their motivation You will support the Fund’s established Climate Action Network, ensuring that they all feel connected to and can contribute to energy and resource savings projects/initiatives/themes. You will ensure projects are well planned and progressed and will collate and share environmental measures to demonstrate achievements. You will help with environmental data capture and carbon accounting and reporting on any trends both internally and externally. You will also provide relevant updates to Senior Management Team (SMT) and work closely with the SMT lead on environmental sustainability, highlighting any issues requiring resolution The role will mainly be based in one office, but you’ll be required to engage across the Fund and develop communications that will reach all staff. You may be drawn into any project/team to advise on environmental sustainability. You will engage with internal and external stakeholders and will support the communication of strong external messages declaring our dedication to working sustainably. Key responsibilities may include: Serve as the Fund’s lead contact for environmental matters, providing advice and maintaining oversight of environmental activity. Support the implementation and delivery of the Fund’s Net Zero commitments through effective stakeholder engagement and strategic guidance. Coordinate environmental data collection and reporting processes to track performance and identify opportunities for improvement. Draft and coordinate environmental reports, including following guidance for sustainability returns to DCMS and the sustainability report for inclusion within the Annual Report and Accounts. Skills & Requirements The candidate for this role should have passion, commitment, and enthusiasm to help deliver our Net Zero targets. They should have good communication skills as well as strong analytical and report writing skills. Previous experience of environmental sustainability within the workplace would be beneficial. Interview details: Date: 6th and 7th October Format: Online Location: UK-wide We have a hybrid approach to working and you will likely visit the Fund’s other offices on an ad hoc basis. Work pattern and location will be agreed with the successful candidate. The role can be based at any of our UK offices: Belfast, Birmingham, Cardiff, Exeter, Glasgow, Leeds, London, Manchester and Newcastle. We will be hosting a briefing session on: 16th September, 11:30am , to register or ask any questions please email us. How to apply: Upload your CV in word format and write a supporting statement (1000 words) with the following criteria, we will use this to score your application. Essential: Demonstrable understanding of environmental sustainability in the workplace, and/or working as an organisation toward Net Zero Excellent organisational skills, managing a diverse workload Ability to analyse, synthesise and present complex information in an accessible manner. Ability to work as a key team player, comfortable with liaising with numerous people from across different departments internally. Desirable: Experience with / skills in internal communication Comfortable with carbon scopes and managing a Net Zero pathway Ability to confidently engage with similar ALB’s to understand their Environmental work Ability to confidently engage with internal and external stakeholders in order collect relevant environmental reporting data Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Communities in the UK come in all shapes and sizes. National Lottery funding is for everyone – therefore, we are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion and we work hard to ensure our funding reaches where it is needed. We also believe our people should represent the communities, organisations and individuals we work with. That’s why The National Lottery Community Fund is committed to being an inclusive employer and a great place to work. We recognise and celebrate the fact that our people come from diverse backgrounds. We positively welcome applications from people from ethnic minority backgrounds, people with disabilities or longstanding health conditions, people who are LGBTQ+, and people from different socio-economic and educational backgrounds, as well as people of all ages. As a Disability Confident Employer, we take a proactive approach in making reasonable adjustments, if needed, throughout the recruitment process and during employment. (This can be related to a physical and mental health condition.)

item.title: Senior legacy officer
item.description: Location: Contracted to our Peterborough office with the flexibility for hybrid working Salary: £29,000 – £34,000 FTE depending on experience Hours: Full time, 37.5 hours per week (part time considered, minimum 30 hours per week with office attendance at least every 2 weeks) Contract: Permanent Benefits: We want all our employees to feel valued and engaged and are committed to offering a positive working culture along with a good work-life balance. As well as ensuring we pay our employees fairly, we offer the following benefits: Flexible working, Generous annual leave, Private Medical Insurance, including dental and optical, Pension Scheme, Sick Pay, Death in Service, Employee Assistance Programme, Bike Loan Scheme, Cycle2Work Scheme, Eyecare, Discount Portal. Be a part of an energetic and vibrant team who are driven by the desire to improve the lives of people living with kidney disease. Our vision is the day when everyone lives free from kidney disease. As a senior legacy officer, you will play a key role in delivering our legacy and in-memory programme, helping to amplify this significant area and drive income growth for the charity. The Role Deliver and develop our legacy and in-memory giving programme, helping to grow this significant area of our fundraising income Plan and deliver acquisition and stewardship campaigns for legacy and in-memory supporters across a range of channels Build and maintain strong relationships with supporters, family members and colleagues, handling sensitive and personal conversations with care and professionalism Monitor, analyse and interpret campaign results, using insight to make recommendations for continuous improvement Work closely with colleagues across Individual Giving and the wider organisation to ensure a joined-up approach to legacy and in-memory marketing Ensure all activity is delivered in line with best practice, relevant regulations and Kidney Research UK's values What We're Looking For Proven experience of delivering acquisition and stewardship campaigns across multiple channels within legacy and/or in-memory fundraising Excellent attention to detail, with the ability to interpret data and results to inform decision-making Strong relationship-building skills, both internally and with external supporters and stakeholders Confidence and sensitivity when handling emotive or personal conversations with supporters and their families A collaborative, proactive approach and the ability to manage multiple projects at once A genuine commitment to Kidney Research UK's mission and values About Kidney Research UK: Kidney Research UK is the leading charity in the UK focused on funding research into the prevention, treatment and management of kidney disease. Our vision is the day when everyone lives free from kidney disease and for more than 60 years the research we fund has been making an impact. But kidney disease is increasing, as are the factors contributing to it, such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease and obesity, making our work more essential than ever. At Kidney Research UK we work with clinicians and scientists across the UK, funding and facilitating research into all areas of kidney disease. We collaborate with partners across the public, private and third sectors to prevent kidney disease and drive innovation to transform treatments. Over the last ten years we have invested more than £71 million into research. We lobby governments and decision makers to change policy and practice to ensure that the estimated 7.2 million people living with all stages of kidney disease in the UK have access to the most effective care and treatment, and to make kidney disease a priority. Most importantly, we also work closely with patients, ensuring their voice is heard and is at the centre of everything we do, from deciding which research to invest in to how we plan our priorities and our work across the charity. Those patient contributions are vital, always helping us and our partners to understand what life is like with kidney disease, always ensuring we see the patient behind the treatment and always reminding us that behind every statistic and every number is a person – the patients and the carers who inspire our mission and push us forward to make a difference and change the future of kidney disease. How to Apply Please complete the online application form and submit together with your CV. Closing date: Tuesday 29 September 2026. We may extend the closing date, but please apply as soon as possible. Telephone interviews will be held week commencing 5 October 2026. Interviews will be held week commencing 12 October 2026. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for everyone and encourage applications from all sections of the community. No agencies please. You may have experience in the following: Legacy Officer, Legacy Fundraiser, In Memory Fundraiser, In Memory Giving Officer, Individual Giving Officer, Legacy Marketing Officer, Gifts in Wills Officer, Donor Stewardship Officer, Fundraising Officer, Supporter Relations Officer, Charity Fundraising, Legacy and In Memory Marketing, Not for Profit, NFP, Third Sector, Charities.

item.title: Head of External Affairs (maternity cover)
item.description: CENTRE FOR AGEING BETTER Head of External Affairs (Maternity cover) - January 2027 start · Maternity cover · Salary £62,388 per annum · Full or part time (minimum 4 days a week) · Flexible working options will be supported. · Central London Office and Hybrid working (at least 6 days a month office attendance) We offer a pension scheme with employer contribution up to 10%, in addition you’ll receive 28 days holiday plus bank holidays, 24-hour access to a comprehensive employee assistance programme, cycle to work scheme and season ticket loan scheme and other benefits. Help shape the UK's response to an ageing society The Centre for Ageing Better is looking for an experienced, politically astute and ambitious Head of External Affairs to join us on a maternity cover contract. This is a unique opportunity to lead one of the UK's most influential voices on ageing at a time of significant social, economic and political change. As Head of External Affairs, you will lead our communications, public affairs and campaigning work, helping us secure greater government attention, commitment and action on the opportunities and challenges of our ageing society. Alongside leading a high-performing team, you will personally drive some of our most strategically important influencing priorities. Working closely with senior leaders across the organisation, you will lead high-profile programmes of work across our action areas of Work, Homes & Communities and Ageism & Inequality , helping to ensure that government, parliamentarians, local leaders and other decision-makers take meaningful action to improve the experience of ageing. These programmes will sit at the heart of our efforts to make ageing a mainstream political priority and secure practical policy change. This is an ideal role for someone who combines outstanding strategic leadership with a track record of delivering high-impact public affairs, policy and communications programmes that have achieved real-world change. About you We're looking for someone who brings a blend of strategic leadership, political awareness and hands-on delivery experience. You will have: Significant experience in public affairs, strategic communications, campaigning and policy influencing. A strong track record of securing policy, political or systems change through effective influencing and stakeholder engagement. Experience of working successfully with Westminster, Whitehall and other senior decision-makers. Demonstrable experience of developing policy positions and translating evidence, research and evaluation into compelling content and influencing narratives. Experience of leading high-profile programmes, campaigns or initiatives that have attracted government attention and resulted in action from decision-makers. A track record of developing and delivering integrated communications and influencing strategies that achieve measurable impact. Excellent writing, stakeholder management and political influencing skills. Strong leadership and people management experience, with the ability to motivate and develop high-performing teams. The ability to think strategically while also delivering complex projects and responding to a fast-changing external environment. About us The Centre for Ageing Better is an independent centre of excellence on ageing and demographic change. We work with national and local government, industries, businesses and community organisations to improve how people experience ageing. Our work focuses on creating better workplaces, homes and communities, while tackling ageism and addressing inequality in later life. The Centre for Ageing Better is a charitable foundation funded by The National Lottery Community Fund (NLCF) and part of the government’s What Works Network. We are fortunate to have monies remaining from our endowment from the NLCF to fully fund us until 2029, and we will be looking for new funding opportunities to sustain activity beyond 2029. We are striving to create an organisation that reflects our society and the communities we serve with a workplace where everyone feels empowered and where diversity of background and thought is celebrated. We know there is more work to be done and are committed to continuing to improve our practice around Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion. We very much welcome applications from minority groups and those underrepresented in our workforce. This especially includes people from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic backgrounds, LGBT+ people, and Disabled people. We are a Positive Action employer, therefore in recruitment where two candidates are ‘as qualified as’ each other, we will favour a candidate from any group identified as currently underrepresented in our team based on protected characteristics as outlined in the Equality Act 2010. To Apply To apply, please follow the link to complete an application form and Equality and Diversity form. Please address in your supporting statement how you meet the person specification for the role as fully as possible to demonstrate why you should be shortlisted for an interview for this post. Failure to do so will result in your application being automatically rejected. We understand the benefits of using AI in the workplace and the support that generative AI can offer. However, we would encourage you to write your supporting statement and complete your application without the use of AI and if you do use AI, to avoid copy and pasting and to consider the value it will add. We encourage you to showcase your experience and knowledge using your own unique voice. The closing date for this role is 9am on Monday 28th September, with in- person interviews to take place during the week commencing 26th October with an expected W/C 4th January start date.

item.title: Programme and Partnerships Officer (RTFN)
item.description: Job Title - Programme and Partnerships Officer (RTFN) Contract - Fixed Term for 1 year, with the possibility of extension Hours - 14 hours per week with flexibility across the working week Salary - £12,800 per annum (£32,000 FTE) Location - Home-based, with occasional travel to Coram Campus in London and other locations for meetings and events About Coram Coram is committed to improving the lives of the UK’s most vulnerable children and young people. We support children and young people from birth to independence, creating a change that lasts a lifetime. Coram is the UK’s oldest children’s charity founded by Thomas Coram in London helping vulnerable children and young people since 1739. Today, the Coram group helps more than one million children, young people, families and professionals every year by providing access to the skills and opportunities they need to thrive. Coram is a leader in adoption and fostering, children’s health education, therapy, child and family law, and advocacy for those in and leaving care. The organisation has grown rapidly in recent years, both in terms of income and staffing, making an exciting and interesting place to be. About the role We are looking for an organised, collaborative and proactive Programme & Partnerships Officer to provide the coordination and delivery capacity that will help RJFN strengthen its national network and deliver its programme of work across advocacy, policy and practice development, research, training and member engagement. Working closely with the RJFN Chair, members and partners, you will support member engagement, build and maintain partnerships, organise events and communications, and help monitor the network’s reach and impact. This is a varied role with significant autonomy and an opportunity to help shape a growing national network. We welcome applicants with skills and experience gained through a range of routes, including professional, voluntary, community and lived experience. Knowledge or experience of racial justice, children’s rights, children’s social care, family justice or a related area is desirable, but we are particularly interested in strong organisational, relationship-building and communication skills, and a clear commitment to racial justice and anti-racist practice. If you enjoy bringing people together, building relationships, communicating creatively and helping turn ideas into action, and you share our commitment to racial justice, we would love to hear from you! To apply for this role, please click on the 'apply now' button below to complete the application. Closing Date: Monday 12th October 2026 23.59pm Interview Date: Thursday 22nd October 2026 Coram is an equal opportunities employer and we believe a diverse workforce enables us to improve the services to the children and families we help. We are genuinely committed to encouraging candidates from all sections of the community we seek to support. This includes those from global majority ethnic backgrounds, those that identify as LGBQT+, those with disabilities, those with lived experience of care, those with neuro-diversity, and those from other groups who are underrepresented at Coram. If applicants feel comfortable, we would encourage them to draw on lived experience as well as professional experience in their personal statement as part of their application. We are committed to the safeguarding of children and where appropriate will require the successful applicant to undertake a check from the Disclosure and Barring Service. item.title: Head of Fundraising
item.description: Head of Fundraising Salary range: £58,265 per annum Location: London Hours: 35 per week Contract: Permanent We are Living Streets, the UK charity for everyday walking. We want to create a nation where walking is the natural choice for everyday, local journeys; free from congested roads and pollution, reducing the risk of preventable illnesses and social isolation. We want to achieve a better walking environment and to inspire people of all generations to walk and wheel more. Living Streets has been around for almost a century, but our campaigns and delivery programmes tackle some of the biggest issues our society faces today. More walking improves mental and physical health, community cohesion, local economies and the environment. Our people and our mission are EPIC, as our values state. Come join our growing team to make a big impact to UK streets. We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated individual to join our team as our new Head of Fundraising. In this strategic role you will be responsible for developing and delivering a comprehensive fundraising strategy to secure income from diverse sources. You will lead the small but growing fundraising function, drive income growth, and build strong relationships with donors, partners, and stakeholders to support Living Streets' mission and strategic priorities. What you'll do Develop and deliver an ambitious, multi-year fundraising strategy across major donors, trusts & foundations, corporate partnerships, individual giving and events Own high-value donor relationships and lead on proposals and pitches that secure significant funding Act as a senior ambassador for Living Streets, building relationships with donors, funders, trustees and partners Sit on the senior leadership team, shaping organisational strategy and providing fundraising reporting to the Senior Management Team and Board. What you'll bring A track record of developing fundraising strategy in the third sector, with income generation success across at least two of: major donors, mid-level donors, individual giving, corporates Experience managing a team to hit department and organisational goals Sharp, persuasive writing and communication skills, with the ability to distil complex issues clearly A genuine understanding of funder care and how to build long-term relationships with grant-giving bodies CRM experience is a plus, as is knowledge of the transport, environment or health agenda Why Living Streets Join us and help make streets better places to walk. We have a clear mission and investment in income generation as a strategic priority. This role is what you make of it: the strategy, the team shape, the donor relationships will be yours to build. How to apply Charity People is delighted to be partnering with Living Streets on this appointment. Please send your CV to Philippa Randle at Charity People as a first step. Closing date: midday on Weds 7 October Interview date: Mon 12 October Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

We are looking for a School Partnerships Lead to drive the growth of our school and multi-academy trust (MAT) partnerships. item.description: Team: Individual Giving Location: Homebased with occasional travel for meetings Work pattern: 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday Salary: Up to £36,327.99 per annum Contract: Fixed term until 30th June 2027 We are the UK’s largest cat welfare charity. All over the country, our passionate employees, volunteers and supporters are using their kindness and expertise to make life better for millions of cats and the people who care for them. Will you join us and make life better for cats? Responsibilities of our Individual Giving Officer: The successful candidate will be responsible for leading on projects across multiple communication channels to recruit and steward our wonderful supporters. This includes everything from leading creative development, building engaging and thoughtful supporter journeys, and project managing campaigns – all of which feature cats at the heart, of course! About the Individual Giving Team: We currently have a team of 14 working across Acquisition and Retention on our Cash Appeals and Raffles, Membership, Sponsorship, Lottery and regular giving programs using Mail, Telemarketing, Face to Face, DRTV, email, Digital, Social and other paid media What we’re looking for in our Individual Giving Officer: What we can offer you: Interested? Here’s how to apply: Application closing date: 27th September 2026 Virtual interview date: 5th & 6th October 2026 Applications may close before the deadline, so please apply early to avoid disappointment. Please note, applications received after the closing date may not be responded to. If successful, your recruitment journey will include: 1. Anonymised application form 2. Virtual interview via Microsoft Teams Please email if you require any adjustments to be made for you to complete your application or to participate in the recruitment journey

item.title: Digital Challenge Officer
item.description: Job description We're recruiting an interim Digital Challenges Officer (12m) for a leading national health charity. You will deliver exceptional experience for supporters taking part in online fundraising challenges. The role: You will join a supportive, collaborative team with exciting ambitions. You will keep supporters motivated, confident and well supported throughout their journey, using proactive communication, tailored stewardship and high-quality care to meet or exceed engagement and income targets. Develop insight-led communications and personalised engagement strategies that improve the supporter experience, strengthen loyalty and contribute to sustainable fundraising growth. Analyse campaign and supporter data, optimise supporter journeys, improve campaign performance and maximise income. Deliver day-to-day operational and project work consistently to a high standard Plan and deliver projects within agreed timescales and resources. Work constructively with colleagues and stakeholders to achieve shared goals, address challenges and contribute to well-planned projects and working groups. The Candidate: Experience of managing digital fundraising activity, across multiple channels or products. Knowledge of Meta-led fundraising products and experience of designing, testing and optimising supporter journeys that balance an excellent experience with fundraising objectives. Experience of developing insight-led creative content and communications. Experience of monitoring and reporting on live activity, identifying trends and recommending practical improvements. Experience of multi-channel marketing, including digital, social, influencer, email and offline activity, to drive fundraising and engagement. Working knowledge of fundraising regulation, safeguarding and data protection requirements, including UK GDPR. Posted on: 16 September 2026 Closing date: 14 October 2026 at 08:27 Job ref: eu1-603680-614112 Tags: Digital

item.title: Senior Church Partnerships Manager
item.description: Senior Church Partnerships Manager We are seeking an experienced relationship-focused fundraiser to build church partnerships and inspire Christian audiences to support vulnerable children worldwide. Salary: £45,563 to £48,375 per annum, depending on experience Location: Home-based, with regular travel across the South East and wider UK Hours: Full-time, 36.5 hours per week Contract: Permanent Closing date: 5 October 2026 About the role This is an exciting opportunity to grow engagement and income from churches and Christian audiences for an international children’s charity. As Senior Church Partnerships Manager, you will develop trusted relationships with church leaders, congregations and individual Christians. Through meetings, events, telephone and online engagement, you will inspire people to support the organisation’s mission through giving, advocacy and prayer. Key responsibilities include: Building and managing a portfolio of church relationships Developing tailored engagement plans using existing campaigns and resources Generating income through individual giving and wider church partnerships Providing thoughtful and consistent stewardship to supporters Identifying creative opportunities to reach new Christian audiences Delivering compelling presentations and fundraising asks in churches and at events Leading the organisation’s presence at Christian events, both online and in person Maintaining accurate supporter, activity and income information within the CRM Contributing to the long-term Church and Christian Engagement Strategy Supporting colleagues to strengthen donor care and church engagement You will speak in churches on approximately 18 Sundays each year. Regular travel and occasional overnight stays will be required. **Please note that the internal title for this position is South East Area Manager. About you You will be an experienced and confident relationship builder with a background in fundraising, sales, business development or supporter engagement. Comfortable working towards stretching targets, you will combine strategic thinking with practical delivery. You will bring: Experience of developing relationships that generate income or engagement Strong presentation and public-speaking skills Confidence in making clear and compelling fundraising asks Excellent influencing, negotiation and communication skills Experience of managing a varied portfolio of contacts or supporters Strong organisational, data management and CRM skills An authentic understanding of churches and Christian communities The ability to represent a Christian identity with integrity and conviction A full UK driving licence and the existing right to work in the UK are essential. Sponsorship is not available. About the organisation Join an international children’s charity working with children, communities, supporters and partners in almost 100 countries. Through long-term development projects, emergency responses and advocacy, the organisation has helped bring lasting change to millions of children for more than 60 years. As a Christian charity, everything is motivated by faith and a commitment to reflecting God’s unconditional love. Employment is conditional upon applicable background checks, including a criminal records check. The organisation values diversity and particularly welcomes applications from under-represented communities. It offers flexible working practices and encourages disabled applicants to request reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process. Other roles you may have experience of could include Church Fundraising Manager, Church Partnerships Manager, Regional Fundraising Manager, Christian Partnerships Manager, Community Fundraising Manager, Relationship Fundraising Manager or Church Engagement Manager. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People. #INDNFP

item.title: Digitisation Unit Lead (DiSSCo UK)
item.description: About us We are a world-class visitor attraction and leading science research centre. We use the Museum's unique collections and our unrivalled expertise to tackle the biggest challenges facing the world today. We care for more than 80 million objects spanning billions of years and welcome more than five million visitors annually and 16 million visits to our website. Today the Museum is more relevant and influential than ever. By attracting people from a range of backgrounds to work for us, we can continue to look at the world with fresh eyes and find new ways of doing things. We employ 1100 staff in a variety of roles, all united by our vision of a future where people and planet thrive. We need everyone to have the passion and drive to help us with our mission to create advocates for our planet and inspire millions to care about the natural world. This role is specifically working as part of the Distributed System of Scientific Collections UK programme . UK natural science collections hold more than 140 million items. These are an unrivalled source of data about how the Earth and its natural systems formed over 4.56 billion years, with the potential to support research that addresses some of the critical issues facing the world, including biodiversity and climate change. They contain evidence of the changes in the natural world including the impact of human life on our planet over the past few thousand years. The scientific, commercial, and societal benefits of these collections are currently constrained by the limits of physical access, and by highly fragmented digitisation efforts with less than 10% digitally available. DiSSCo UK is a consortium of UK natural science collections, led by the Natural History Museum in partnership with the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) and UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), who are developing a national infrastructure to support the digitisation and use of the UK’s natural science collections to support this critical research. This will take the form of a 10-year programme focused on digitisation of critical mass of collections as FAIR data, made available through a well-supported backbone of technology infrastructure, with continued development and application of innovative approaches such as greater use of Artificial Intelligence and robotics. Investment of the order of £155m over ten years from 2026-27 is expected to unlock at least a four-fold economic return on investment, as well as efficiency savings for UK and global researchers, and the potential for research innovation and studies that have not previously been possible – underpinning a future in which both people and planet thrive. Diversity and inclusion matter to us. Our vision is of a future where both people and the planet thrive. Diversity is one of our core values and we strive to build a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging. All new staff who join us learn about the importance of diversity and inclusion to the Museum and how to contribute to creating an inclusive environment. We know we have more to do, but we are committed to ensuring that everyone who works at the Museum feels they can thrive and feel valued and respected. About the role DiSSCo UK is seeking an experienced and inspirational Digitisation Team Unit Lead to oversee digitisation operations, deliver strategic objectives, and support the development of a high-performing team contributing to the UK's natural science collections infrastructure. The Unit Lead will provide sectional technical and people leadership for digitisation and collection preparation activities, ensuring projects are delivered efficiently, safely, and to a high standard. You will work across institutional teams and external partners to drive innovation, improve workflows, and deliver impactful outcomes that support research, conservation, and public engagement. This role is based within the Museum’s Digital, Data and Informatics (DDI) Department and reports to the DiSSCo UK Operations Team Lead. This is a fixed term role until 31 March 2028. About you You will be a confident communicator, able to foster strong working relationships both within the DiSSCo UK programme and wider NHM Collection teams. You will thrive in team environments, supporting and driving your teams to success, with excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills. The role will combine technical digitisation expertise and people management. While beneficial, it is not essential that the postholder has previous direct management experience. We welcome applicants who may not have had formal line management experience previously, but are willing to learn and embrace building, developing and motivating a team. This post will lead the Botanical section of Digitisers and Collection Assistants. The postholder will need substantial experience working with natural science collections, with applied botanical expertise and the ability to make informed operational decisions on specimen handling and workflow requirements. Thriving at the Museum: the way we work We are proud to work at the Museum and have identified the qualities we all need to embody to reach our shared ambition. This sits alongside the Museum’s values and forms the framework for the way we work. Find out more on our website. What we offer 27.5 days holiday plus 8 bank holidays (full time equivalent) Generous defined contribution Natural History Museum Pension Scheme (employer contribution 4 - 10%) Season ticket, bicycle and rental loan Life insurance Free admission to our exhibitions and many other paid exhibitions at museums, galleries and institutions across London and the UK. Staff discount at our Museum shops and cafes We offer a wide variety of training initiatives and opportunities to build skills. Investing in staff development is important to us, and we are ambitious about helping staff to grow and fulfil their potential. Affordable membership to the Civil Service Sports Council which offers a range of benefits including an extensive list of special offers and reduced entry fees at a selection of cinema chains, theme parks, theatres, retailers and supermarkets. It also provides entry to up to 300 English Heritage sites and other national treasures. Membership to our Sports and Social Association (for a small fee), which includes access to our in-house gym and clubs such as football, softball, table tennis and tennis and classes in Middle Eastern dance, yoga and Tai Chi Hybrid working We are working towards a vision where both people and planet thrive, and nothing gives a greater connection with this, than seeing first-hand, the visitors, scientific research and collections that all of our work is inspired by and working side by side with the teams delivering the visitor experience and events. We also recognise the benefits and flexibility that hybrid working brings. We operate a hybrid working model that requires regular, weekly attendance for this role, with the precise pattern of days on site and worked from home to be agreed with your manager. Hybrid working is possible, with onsite supervision required during digitisation activity, around 3 days per week on average. This may increase in line with business requirements. Occasional work across other Museum or partner sites around the UK may be required. How to apply If this sounds like you, please apply below by clicking on Apply for job. Please note that as part of our commitment to anonymised shortlisting, panels do not view CVs during the recruitment process. If you choose to upload your CV, our system will automatically pull information from your CV into our application form. We advise you to double-check your application form data before submitting as the tool may interpret CVs differently. Closing date: 23:59 on 29 September Interviews expected: w/c 19 October Please note that this role does not qualify for Museum sponsorship so the successful postholder will need to have a valid right to work in the UK at the point of offer.

item.title: Support Officer (Digital)
item.description: Bliss is the UK’s leading national charity for babies born premature or sick, and we are looking for a Support Officer (Digital) to join our enthusiastic and passionate Information and Support team to help make a real difference to the lives of families and babies in neonatal care. The Support Officer (Digital) plays a vital role in ensuring that every family of a baby born sick or premature can access impactful and personalised support, at their time of need. By supporting the improvement and development of the Bliss digital support services, you will help to ensure that families with babies born premature or sick feel confident, supported, well informed, connected to the help they need, and to be partners in the care of their babies. Terms Title: Support Officer (Digital) Location: Hybrid (3 days per fortnight in the London office, SE1) Salary: £33,464 Terms: Full-time (35 hours per week). Permanent. Regular evening/weekend work (remote) at certain points during the year Role Details This is an excellent opportunity for a creative and productive individual who has experience of offering support across a variety of platforms to make a real difference as part of a small, dynamic and dedicated charity. The ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate the following skills and experience: · Experience of supporting people with emotional and/or practical support needs across digital platforms and digital support services. · Strong people and communication skills, including the ability to support people in distress. · Strong experience and skills for digital support content creation · Skills for the moderation of online platforms · Skills for working in project teams to improve and develop new services based on user needs. · Understanding of service-user involvement and co-creation, and its importance in improving services. · Skills for working in partnership with external organisations and individuals to develop and deliver services · Understanding of equity, diversity and inclusion and health inequality. For more details please view the job description and person specification below. How to apply Interested applicants are requested to submit the following documents Your CV (please ensure this does not include your age, gender or any other personal characteristics) Supporting statement explaining how you meet the criteria in the person specification. This should address the essential points of the person specification and is expected to be no more than 1000-1500 words long This information is used when shortlisting candidates for interview. W e understand AI can be a helpful tool, but please use it with caution and ensure your application is personalised and accurate. It is Bliss’ policy not to contact applicants who have not been invited for an interview so if you have not heard from us three weeks after the closing deadline, you should assume that your application has been unsuccessful. Recruitment Timeline The deadline for applications is 5pm on 16th October First round interviews will be held on w/c 26th October, virtually. Second interviews in person at our London Bridge offices on 4th November 2026.

item.title: Youth Development Mentor
item.description: About the Role This Youth Development Mentor for young men is part of Bright Futures, our mentoring and employability support programme for young Gypsy and Traveller people aged 15-25. You will build trusted, consistent 1-1 mentoring relationships with young men, supporting them to grow in confidence, work out what they want, and build the skills to get there. You will deliver the programme's set mentoring offer, adapting your approach to individuals as needed, alongside group sessions on skills and personal development. Many of the young men we work with have had negative experiences of school or other services and are often not in education, employment or training (NEET). The role is about helping the young men move forward at a pace that works for them, towards something they've chosen and can stick with, rather than pushing them down a set route. You will keep detailed records of progress and milestones reached. You will also play a role in outreach and community engagement – building relationships with families and community members. This includes keeping up good working relationships with colleges, training providers and employers, and making sure young people's voices are heard, both within Bright Futures and externally. This role is funded by The National Lottery Community Fund. About You This role is for someone who wants to make a real difference in young people's lives – someone committed to supporting young men from marginalised and underserved communities to get equitable access to opportunities, and to helping bring about wider change for those communities. You will enjoy the challenge of working with young men who may take time to trust and engage, and see that as part of what makes the role rewarding. The role is ideal for someone with experience of mentoring, youth work or a similar community-based role working with young men (paid or voluntary). Someone patient, non-judgemental and comfortable adapting support to suit the person in front of you. You will be just as comfortable speaking to family members as with college staff or social services. We don't expect you to already have all the answers – what matters most is your commitment and ability to build genuine, trusting relationships and to keep going with young people who may take time to open up. We will support your development through supervision, training and a small, collaborative team environment. We know not everyone will meet every requirement in the job description below, but if you feel you have what it takes, please apply and tell us how your experience and skills make you suitable. If you are not sure what the work looks like or you want to ask questions before applying, we are happy to chat with you about the role. Please contact Mini Ravi (Programme Lead) by calling our office phone. About LGT and Bright Futures London Gypsies and Travellers (LGT) challenges social exclusion and discrimination, working for change in partnership with Gypsy and Traveller communities living on council caravan sites, roadside camps, in flats and houses, and those experiencing homelessness. Bright Futures supports Gypsy and Traveller young men and women aged 15–25 through mentoring, skills development, employability and wellbeing support. The programme helps young people build confidence, develop practical skills and identify realistic pathways into training and employment, working at their own pace and around their needs and interests. The programme is shaped by a deep understanding of the Gypsy and Traveller culture, and designed to empower young people to engage with wider society with pride, motivation and confidence. Our services also include accommodation advice and advocacy, family support, community development, research, policy work and campaigns, and we support hundreds of individuals and families each year. We are a small, committed and supportive team who seek to live our organisational values throughout our work: Collaboration, Courage, Empowerment, Inclusivity, Equity, Community. We are committed to equal opportunities and workforce diversity. We strongly encourage applications from Gypsy and Traveller communities. To Apply Review the responsibilities and person specification in the job description enclosed. Using the ‘Apply Now’ button, please submit your CV Instead of a cover letter, please submit answers to the following 3 questions in the space provided when you apply. 1. Briefly tell us about your experience of working with young men/people. What did you do and what kind of support did you provide? 2. What is one of the barriers young men from vulnerable or marginalised backgrounds face around education, training and work? Why? 3. Why are you interested in this role and working with London Gypsies & Travellers? 250-300 word answers for each question is enough, but you are welcome to write more. There is no right answer and we are not interested in perfect responses. We want to know about you and the knowledge, skills, and experience your will bring to the role. Closing date: Wednesday 30th September 2026 Interviews: Wednesday 14th October (stage 1, in person), Thursday 22nd October (stage 2, online) Please check you are available on these dates before applying, in case you are shortlisted for interviews. Please note: An enhanced DBS check is required for the role . Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.
item.dc:creator: London Gypsies and Travellers, N16

item.title: Lead Worker (Coaching)
item.description: Crisis is the national charity for people experiencing homelessness. We have embarked on our 10-year strategy for ending homelessness. We know it is not inevitable. We know together we can end it. Crisis Skylight Merseyside offer direct services to people who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Alongside our frontline service offer, we develop and lead strategy and partnership projects to deliver positive change for homeless people in Merseyside. Location : Crisis Skylight Merseyside, 96 Kent Street, L1 5BD Hours : 35 per week between the hours of 8.30am – 5pm Contract : Fixed Term - 6 months About the role As a Coach Lead Worker in the Coaching team, you will play a key role in supporting individuals that are homeless or at risk of homelessness. You will work with people who have varying levels of engagement with the service: some will work with you in a more planned and structured way, and some are in more complex situations and will require support from other agencies. As a Lead Worker you will: Support members to develop and follow a personalised plan to end their homelessness sustainably. Empower and upskill members to be proactive in their accommodation search and access other relevant support services to meet their needs. Provide support with practical aspects of their route out of homeless, including access to housing, benefits, and other relevant needs. Lead Work a caseload and provide effective case management in line with the Crisis Case Management Framework. The key to success will be your ability to make collaborative, consistent and psychologically informed relationships with members, services, colleagues, and partner organisations. Skills, knowledge, and experience vital to succeeding in this role: Passionate about and dedicated to ending homelessness sustainably. Comprehensive understanding and experience of accessing housing via private rented sector, local authorities, housing associations, supported providers and others. Good knowledge of issues affecting homeless people, including housing, welfare issues, trauma, substance use, involvement in criminal justice services, and social isolation Proven track record of successfully using coaching, IAG or psychologically informed approaches with people who have experienced homelessness. Ability to manage successful relationships with external agencies and relevant service providers and successfully advocate on members behalf. Excellent verbal and written communication skills used to ensure accurate record keeping on a variety of Case Management Systems/Databases. Flexible and adaptable to change. Strong team player, able to use own initiative and reflect on your own practice. Please see the full Job Pack linked below, for a full list of requirements for this role. We realise that long lists of criteria can be daunting, and you may not want to apply for a role unless you feel 100% qualified. However, if you feel you have relevant examples to answer the screening questions in the application form, we encourage you to apply. We believe diversity is a strength, and our aim is to make sure that Crisis truly reflects the communities we serve. We are actively working towards our organisation being a place where everyone can thrive and make their best contribution to our mission of ending homelessness for good. We know that the more perspectives, voices, and experiences we can bring to this work, the better. We particularly welcome applications from people who have lived experience of homelessness, and people from all marginalised groups, communities, and backgrounds. Working at Crisis Our values, Bold, Impactful, Collaborative and Equitable, are at the heart of everything we do as we continue in our mission to end homelessness. Our staff, members and volunteers are vital to getting the right government policies in place, providing breakthrough services, and building a supportive community. We’ll lead by example to nurture a positive and ambitious workplace guided by ending homelessness. As a member of the team, you will have access to a wide range of employee benefits including: A competitive salary. Please note, our salaries are fixed to counter inequity and we do not negotiate at offer stage Interest free loans for travel season ticket, cycle to work, and deposit to secure a tenancy Pension scheme with an employer contribution of 8.5% 28 days’ annual leave (pro rata) which increases with service to 31 days and the option to purchase up to 10 additional days leave Enhanced maternity, paternity, shared parental, and adoption pay. Wellbeing Leave to be used flexibly And more! (Full list of benefits available on website) Alongside our excellent staff benefits, we will support your ongoing development to build your skills, experience, and career. When you join us, you will have the opportunity to join our staff diversity networks, which aim to champion issues across the organisation, enable staff to be their authentic and best selves and contribute to making Crisis a truly diverse organisation. How do I apply? Please click on the 'Apply for Job' button below.Our shortlisting process is anonymised as part of our commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion. We do not ask for CVs, instead we ask you complete the work history section and answer the screening questions for us to be able to assess you fairly and objectively. At least two members of staff score all applications. Closing date: Thursday 24th September 2026 at 23:59 Interview process: Competency-based interview Interview date and location: Monday 28th September 2026. AI in Job Applications We understand some candidates use AI tools when applying. Whilst we welcome the use of technology to support clear communication and structure, we want to learn more about you, so please ensure that your application reflects your own skills, knowledge and experiences Accessibility We want our recruitment process to be as accessible as possible. If you need us to make an adjustment or provide additional support as you apply for a role, please contact our Talent Acquisition team via our website and we will be happy to discuss how we can help. For more information about our work please visit our website. Registered Charity Numbers: E&W1082947, SC040094

item.title: Regional Partnerships & Fundraising Manager
item.description: As we enter an exciting new phase of growth, we're looking for an ambitious and relationship-driven professional to help us build sustainable, diversified income streams that will enable us to increase our impact and reach even more families facing childhood cancer. We are transforming the way we generate income by focusing on long-term partnerships, smarter use of data and technology, and sustainable fundraising models that maximise impact whilst protecting team capacity. This role will play a key part in helping us achieve that vision. We're looking for someone who can spot opportunities, build meaningful partnerships, develop long-term supporter relationships and help shape the future of income generation across the charity. The Opportunity As our Regional Partnerships & Fundraising Manager, you will be responsible for driving sustainable income growth through: Corporate partnerships and sponsorship opportunities Payroll Giving and employee engagement programmes Strategic trusts and grants oversight Regular Giving growth and supporter development Regional relationship building and network development Pipeline management, forecasting and income planning Lead and develop our Charity Fundraiser, providing coaching, mentoring and support to build a high-performing fundraising function capable of delivering sustainable long-term growth. As a member of our Senior Leadership Team, you will play an active role in the strategic leadership of the charity, helping to shape organisational priorities, champion collaboration and contribute to future growth. About You We would love to hear from you if you have: Experience in business development, account management, fundraising or partnership development A track record of securing income, sponsorship, partnerships or commercial opportunities Strong relationship-building and networking skills Confidence engaging with senior stakeholders and decision makers Experience managing pipelines and using CRM systems effectively A collaborative and proactive approach with a focus on finding solutions The ability to turn opportunities into long-term relationships Whether your background is in charity fundraising, commercial partnerships, sales, account management or business development, we are interested in people who can build relationships, create opportunities and deliver sustainable growth. Why Join Us? This is a unique opportunity to join a purpose-led charity at a pivotal stage in its development. You'll have the opportunity to shape and influence the future direction of fundraising, partnerships and sustainable income growth across the charity. You'll be joining a collaborative and ambitious team that believes in: Working smarter, together Building sustainable growth Developing strong partnerships Using data and insight to make informed decisions Creating a positive and supportive culture Making a meaningful difference to children and families affected by cancer Most importantly, you'll help ensure that no family faces childhood cancer alone. Every partnership secured, supporter retained and income stream developed will help us reach more families affected by childhood cancer.

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: Job description We are seeking an experienced Operations Manager who can balance strategic vision with hands-on execution. As a member of our leadership team they will work cross-functionally, colaborating with other key members of the team. They will provide operational excellence by mapping workflows, and use their data skills to provide insights to refine and support service delivery and demonstrate impact. This is a strategic and hands on role. Ultimately, the ideal candidate is a problem-solver who can elevate the charity's reputation, nurture community relationships, and translate high-level strategy into practical, impactful operations. To apply for this role: Please provide your CV (maximum 2 pages) and supporting statement detailing how you meet the requirements of the role - providing clear examples of experience, skills and knowledge (no more than 1 page). We’re keen to understand your individual experience and voice, so please write your supporting statement without the use of AI-generated content About the Role: The Operations Manager is a senior leadership role, responsible for overseeing the operational effectiveness of the organisation. You will ensure our team has the tools, systems and support they need to deliver life-changing services to families. The role is also pivotal in shaping how we measure and demonstrate the impact of our work. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role at the heart of a growing, values-driven organisation. Demonstrable operations experience is essential. Reports to: Managing Director Responsible for: Business Support Administrator Data Consultant Key Responsibilities: Leadership As a member of the Senior Management Team, you will work collaboratively with the Managing Director and other senior leaders to: Build strong relationships with counterparts within the Home-Start London network and at Home-Start UK. Contribute to strategic planning and collaborate with external advisors on specialist projects as required. Deliver against the organisational priorities and objectives as defined in the business plan. Develop our services and ways of working to ensure the charity’s long term sustainability. Support the team to work efficiently and effectively - according to the strategy policies and commitments we have signed up to. Work closely with the Family Services Manager, to ensure our data needs are aligned with our Impact Measurements. Operations Oversee the implementation and development of operational policies and procedures, including GDPR and H&S, ensuring compliance. Manage the operations budget and ensure efficient use of resources. Maintain and streamline administrative systems (eg: Google drive, Google Forms, Charity Log, telephony/communications systems). Lead key operational projects and oversee all office administration, tech support and premises management. Lead on end to end project management of HSUK Quality Assurance requirements as well as our National Data requirement. Manage data collection and evaluation across multiple platforms including Charity Log. This includes project managing and supporting delivery of our Annual Data review. Support governance processes and liaise with the Board of Trustees when required. Impact and Evaluation Lead the organisation’s impact delivery, through supporting data collection and evaluation across multiple platforms including Charity Log. Work with the Family Services Manager to ensure outcomes of family experiences inform service design and delivery. Produce tailored reports and insights to inform funding applications, Impact Reports and Trustee Reports as required. Collaborate on funding applications with the CEO and Communications Manager. Champion the voices of children and families, using data to support storytelling to demonstrate real-life impact. Team Management Line manage the Operations Team (Business support Administrator, Database Consultant). Provide direction to the Business Support Administrator to enable effective and efficient day to day running of the organisation. Manage team in accordance with the Home-Start Wandsworth procedures, policies and values. Support effective management of any non home-visiting Volunteers supporting the organisation’s work . Essential skills and experience: Strategic thinker with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities Proven experience in operations management, ideally in a charity/not for profit setting Strong knowledge of service evaluation and data analysis Skilled in communicating complex information clearly and accessibly IT confident and adaptable to new systems and tools (Charity Log, Monday CRM, Slack etc) Experience of leadership / managing a small team Excellent written and verbal communication. Excellent organisational and project management skills. Working knowledge of GDPR legislation and implementation of associated policy Experience of Board level reporting against objectives and/or data led reporting. Curious and passionate about using data to tell compelling stories of impact Project management expertise Understanding of local community needs and services Posted on: 15 September 2026 Closing date: 02 October 2026 at 11:26 Job ref: Operations Manager V2 Tags: Administration, Project Management, Operations, Business Intelligence, Compliance / Quality, CRM, Data Analysis, Data Protection, Health and Safety, Information Management, Office Management, Safeguarding The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.
