item.title: Corporate Partnerships Officer
item.description: This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and grow St Luke's corporate partnerships programme. The Corporate Partnerships Officer will play a leading role in generating new income and developing relationships with businesses whose values align with our mission. Working closely with the Head of Corporate Partnerships, this role will identify, cultivate and secure new corporate partnerships that support St Luke's work through sponsorship, charitable giving, employee fundraising, volunteering and wider social value initiatives. This role will focus primarily on new business development and income generation while supporting the development of long-term, mutually beneficial corporate relationships. Key Responsibilities: Corporate Partnership Development · Identify, research and prioritise prospective corporate partners whose values, CSR, ESG and social value objectives align with St Luke's mission · Build and maintain a strong pipeline of corporate prospects using effective prospect research, networking and outreach activities · Develop, cultivate and convert relationships with business decision-makers and corporate stakeholders · Secure new corporate partnerships and sponsorship opportunities that generate sustainable income and community impact · Deliver agreed income targets and partnership KPIs · Generate new opportunities through networking, referrals, events and direct engagement Proposal Development and Income Generation · Develop compelling and tailored partnership proposals, sponsorship packages, presentations and pitches · Create funding opportunities across St Luke's programmes and services including digital inclusion, employment and skills, health and wellbeing, food security and social isolation initiatives · Negotiate partnership agreements and secure financial support from businesses · Work with colleagues to develop innovative and attractive corporate engagement opportunities Relationship Management · Support the successful onboarding of newly secured partners · Work collaboratively with colleagues to ensure partners receive an excellent experience and achieve their partnership objectives · Identify opportunities to increase partner engagement through employee fundraising, events and volunteering · Support partnership renewals and the longer-term development of corporate relationships Marketing and External Engagement · Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of St Luke's corporate partnerships offer · Produce engaging partnership materials, impact reports, case studies and promotional content · Represent St Luke's at networking events, business forums, conferences and stakeholder meetings · Act as an ambassador for St Luke's and promote the organisation's values and impact Monitoring and Reporting · Maintain accurate records of partnerships, prospects, meetings and income activity using CRM and reporting systems · Monitor progress against agreed targets and KPIs · Provide regular reports on pipeline development, income generation and partnership activity · Gather and communicate impact data and stories that demonstrate the value of corporate support General Responsibilities · Promote equity, diversity and inclusion throughout all aspects of the role · Ensure compliance with safeguarding, health and safety, GDPR and organisational policies · Attend meetings, events and occasional evening/weekend engagements as required · Undertake other duties commensurate with the level and responsibilities of the post Person Specification We are looking for an individual who can demonstrate the following competencies to a high level. We will be looking for evidence of all of the following key competencies during the selection process if you are shortlisted. Essential Experience and Skills: · Experience of generating income, securing partnerships, winning new business or delivering against sales targets. · Experience building and managing relationships with external stakeholders. · Experience producing persuasive proposals, funding applications, presentations or business pitches. · Excellent written and verbal communication skills. · Strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities. · Ability to identify opportunities and take initiative. · Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities. · Experience using databases, CRM systems or fundraising platforms. · Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a team. Essential Knowledge and Attributes: · Understanding of, or strong interest in, corporate fundraising, business development, sponsorship or partnerships. · Understanding of, or interest in, CSR, ESG and social value agendas. · Commitment to the values and mission of St Luke's. · Genuine interest in community development and social impact. · Professional, enthusiastic and results-focused approach. Desirable: · Experience within the charity, voluntary or community sector. · Experience of corporate fundraising or sponsorship. · Knowledge of the London business community. · Experience organising networking or stakeholder engagement events. · Experience supporting employee volunteering or community engagement programmes.

item.title: Admissions Avoidance Coordinator
item.description: Admissions Avoidance Coordinator £30,024 per annum Birmingham Full time Permanent 37.5hrs per week Location: Hybrid / CYP Hubs, Birmingham Our client is a leading provider of mental health services in Birmingham and the West Midlands. They offer high quality services that support both recovery and wellbeing, and they actively work with people so that they can be in control of their lives. They now have an opportunity for an Admissions Avoidance Coordinator to join them to work closely with people who have experienced mental health difficulties and are being supported through BSMHFT Children’s and Young People Community Hubs and Crisis services. The main aim of the service is to offer an individualised service with a focus on the prevention of hospital admission and provide support for service users. You will work closely with the other Discharge Coordinators providing support cover when required and you’ll work closely with BSMHFT CYP staff to identify individuals who are at risk of escalation because of hardships including social and environmental factors. These individuals will be supported via the service through a person-centered approach that focuses on maintaining and strengthening the person’s wellbeing and enabling people to build their own resilience reducing crisis escalation. They are looking for someone with experience of working in a paid role in the mental health field, with experience of supporting people age 18 – 25 to be in control of their lives. You’ll have knowledge and experience of carrying out needs & risk assessments and you’ll have a good overall understanding of the social determinants of poor mental health and interventions to effect positive outcomes. A full UK driving licence and use of a vehicle is also desirable but not essential. Benefits include an attractive defined contribution pension scheme, PayCare which offers employees affordable cover for a range of healthcare treatments, an Employee Assistance Programme which includes free counselling and a comprehensive training programme. Candidates must have the right to work in the UK for a minimum of 12 months. They are not a registered sponsor and therefore are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position. Their people are key to the success of the organisation and they are recognised as both a Mindful Employer as well as achieving Gold standard success in Investors in People. They welcome applications from people who have experienced mental health difficulties. The closing date for applications is Sunday 27th September 2026 Interviews will take place on Tuesday 6th October 2026

Our organisation is all about people – the people who live in our homes, the communities we serve, and those we work with. So, it’s no surprise that we recruit for attitude and behaviour which are central to us building relationships and delivering great experiences for these people. We employ colleagues who are passionate about making a difference who will take responsibility to get things done. As a not-for-profit housing association, providing affordable homes and services to more than 20,000 people across Greater Manchester. We have a strong social purpose and make it our mission to enable people to live well in their home and community. This role will help us achieve our ambition by working as part of a team within supported housing and outreach services in Greater Manchester, providing high-quality, personalised housing-related support and enablement support to adult clients. We're looking for someone who can help clients live independently in accommodation suited to their needs and successfully maintain their home. You'll support clients to develop the skills, confidence and resilience needed to access education, training, employment and meaningful community activities. You'll also help clients achieve financial stability, maintain healthy lifestyles and work towards their individual goals. In this role, you will be responsible for Using coaching and strengths-based approaches to help clients develop emotional resilience, overcome barriers and take greater control of their lives. Building positive relationships with clients and supporting them to achieve the outcomes identified within their support plans. Liaising with external agencies and professionals and raising safeguarding concerns appropriately and in a timely manner. Completing and maintaining Support Plans, Positive Behaviour Plans, Essential Profiles and Risk Assessments. Supporting the delivery of high-quality housing management, housing-related support and enablement activities within the service. Working as part of a supported housing team to provide personalised support to young adults, including those with ADHD, ASD and substance misuse support needs. Managing a caseload of clients, with workloads determined by client needs and service demand. We need people who have Knowledge and understanding of the needs of vulnerable adults and individuals with complex support needs. Knowledge of issues affecting clients, including behaviour management, mental health, leaving care and neurodiversity. Understanding of safeguarding, risk management and professional boundaries. Experience of working within a supported housing environment or relevant health and social care setting. Experience of supporting young people and vulnerable adults with complex needs. Experience of working with statutory agencies and voluntary sector organisations. Strong communication, record-keeping, organisational and relationship-building skills. The ability to work independently, use initiative and manage a varied caseload. It would be advantageous if you have: Experience of working within supported housing services. Knowledge of legislation and best practice relating to housing support, safeguarding, ADHD, ASD, learning disabilities and substance misuse. A qualification in Health and Social Care or a related subject. Please note that an Enhanced DBS check is required for this role and you must be able to work shifts, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays where required. The successful candidate will be flexible, reliable, resilient, professional and passionate about making a positive difference to the lives of vulnerable adults and young people. We want to hear from you! You may use AI tools to support your application, but any content submitted must accurately reflect your own skills, experience, qualifications and suitability for the role. During the recruitment process, you may be asked to discuss and provide evidence of the information contained within your application. Everyone’s welcome here. Our culture is inclusive, and we are committed to increasing diversity. We enable everyone to be themselves at work, so that they feel at home with us. And we trust and support people to do their best, in a role that is fulfilling and rewarding because we know that this helps us to deliver better outcomes for our customers and our colleagues. item.title: Victim Focus Officer
item.description: This role covers the Cardiff & Vale area, though we are operating a hybrid working model which involves regular home-based working and other flexible base working. The purpose of this role is to provide on-going support to the victims of crime, ensuring that South Wales Victim Focus realises their aim of helping people cope and recover from the effects of being subjected to, or witnessing criminal activity. South Wales Victim Focus serves diverse communities, many of whom experience a range of barriers that may impact on their ability to cope and recover from what they have experienced. These can include financial distress; social isolation; reduced mobility; mental and physical health issues; substance use and lack of opportunity. South Wales Victim Focus aims to identify what matters to service users and empower them to take control of their journey. This role involves regular travel in and around the Cardiff & Vale area. What we offer At Victim Support, we are committed to attracting and retaining the best talent. Our competitive rewards and benefits package includes: Flexible Working Options : Including hybrid working. Generous Annual Leave : 28 days plus Bank Holidays, increasing to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave. Birthday Leave : An extra day off for your birthday. Pension Plan : 5% employer contribution. Enhanced Allowances : Enhanced sick pay, maternity, and paternity payments. Exclusive Discounts : High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment, and leisure discounts. Financial Wellbeing : Access to our financial wellbeing hub and salary-deducted finance. Wellbeing Support : Employee assistance programme and wellbeing support. Inclusive Networks : Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes. Sustainable Travel : Cycle to work scheme and season ticket loans. Career Development : Ongoing training and support with opportunities for career progression. About the role: As a Multi Crime Caseworker you will: Be the first point of contact for clients from the area, or contract to which you have been allocated Carry a caseload of clients within each allocated area as directed Maintain case management records, developing personal support plans, and referring clients on, as required Work with colleagues in local teams, and as part of a national team, to ensure that all outcomes and KPI measures are met You will need: Strong personal resilience, self-motivation and flexibility to work virtually with different teams, as deployed to do so An understanding of the impact of crime on victims Experience of working with clients to achieve outcomes, based on needs and risk assessments Knowledge and understanding of the requirement for confidentiality and safe working practices Effective verbal and written communication skills The ability to work from home effectively, both on your own and as part of a team Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details. About Us: Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required. At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minority communities. As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process. How to apply: To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible.

item.description: Stewardship helps Christians to be the best stewards of the resources God gives them. Every year we support tens of thousands of people with everyday giving through to strategic philanthropy, and help thousands of churches, charities and Christian workers to strengthen their finance and governance. We operate with the financial scope and technical complexity of a mid-sized financial services institution, but with a clear Christian mission at our heart. Amongst other things, we safely received and granted out over £134m from our Donor Advised Fund in 2025, deliver payroll services to over 900 clients each month, reach thousands with our products and campaigns, and still have ambitious plans to grow. The Chief Digital Officer (CDO) will see digital and technology not simply as a function or infrastructure, but as a ministry enabler: creating the systems, platforms and experiences that enable increased generosity, strengthen churches and charities, and scale Kingdom impact. item.title: Community Activator (x4)
item.description: We are recruiting four Community Activators to work alongside communities across East Staffordshire, primarily in Burton-upon-Trent and Uttoxeter, as part of our Sport England-funded Place-Based work. You’ll spend time understanding local experiences, priorities and the things that can make being active more difficult. What you hear and learn will help shape ideas, opportunities and positive change. Each role will be hosted by a different local organisation, giving you the chance to build strong connections within the communities they support and contribute to the next stage of this work. If you’re a good listener, enjoy building relationships and want to help make sure local voices shape what happens next, this could be the role for you. About the Role As a Community Activator, you’ll work with local people and communities across Burton-upon-Trent and Uttoxeter to understand what matters to them and support more people to be active. You’ll spend time in communities, listening to people’s experiences and ideas, exploring the barriers that can make being active more difficult and helping to support small changes and activities that can make a difference to people’s health and wellbeing. You’ll also help gather and share community insight, build relationships with local organisations and partners, and support the wider Place Partnership to understand what is working, what is getting in the way and what could be done differently. Each day will look different. You’ll shape your work around what you learn from local people and your host organisation, while working alongside the other Community Activators as a supportive group. We’d love to hear from you if you: Are a good listener and respond thoughtfully to others Enjoy building relationships and working with different people and communities Can communicate clearly, both verbally and in writing Are adaptable and comfortable working in different environments Show empathy and understanding of other people’s experiences Can work as part of a team and support others Are willing to speak up for community needs Enjoy solving problems and finding different ways forward You don’t need a specific qualification or background to apply. We welcome experience from any part of your life, including employment, volunteering, parenting or caring responsibilities, community organising or personal experience. If you’re someone who enjoys listening, building trust and helping communities shape what happens next, we’d love to hear from you. How the role works All four Community Activators will be employed by Together Active. Each role will then be seconded to one of four host organisations for the duration of the contract, meaning you will work closely with that organisation and the communities they support while remaining a Together Active employee.

item.title: Financial Wellbeing Adviser
item.description: Ready to use your problem-solving skills to transform lives across Swindon? Whether you are an experienced adviser, a driven career-changer looking for a fresh challenge or you are looking for your first start in your career pathway in the voluntary sector, we want to hear from you. Our team is expanding, we are looking for two Financial Wellbeing Advisers to champion financial wellbeing in our community. What You’ll Be Doing Delivering practical, outcome-focused advice on a range of financial wellbeing and resilience topics, including, debt, income maximisation, budgeting and energy efficiency advice, to support residents navigating cost-of-living challenges. Empowering people via 1-to-1 appointments, phone channels, home visits, and interactive group education sessions in schools, colleges and the community. Championing financial inclusion across Swindon by helping to build and maintain community partnerships and spotlighting unfair social issues through national campaigns. Gaining industry-recognised qualifications and training, including the City & Guilds NEA Level 3 Energy Awareness and the Citizens Advice Adviser Training programme. Who we’re Looking For Advisers & Career-Changers: Backgrounds in advice work, benefits, debt, customer-facing roles, or community engagement looking to make an immediate difference Or Driven Career Starters: Enthusiastic, fast learners with strong digital skills, a positive "can-do" mindset, and a genuine passion for helping others build financial security Resilient Communicators: Strong listening and questioning skills to guide people through emotional or high-pressure situations with care, respect and confidentiality. Self-motivation: Outstanding organisational skills to manage active casework and work independently in dynamic settings. Local Mobility: Willingness to travel across the Swindon borough for outreach and client home visits. A driving licence or access to a vehicle is not required, as the local public transport network provides complete coverage. Why Join us? Competitive Salary: £25,012 - £27,012, based on your experience Work-Life Balance: 37 hours per week, with a flexible hybrid model combining office, outreach, and potential for some home working once you're independently thriving. Generous Leave: 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, and 3 discretionary days between Christmas and New Year; that's 36 days a year!! item.description: Self-Advocacy Team Leader Learning Disability Voices Network (LDVN) 30 hours per week | Permanent Starting salary: £30,258 pro-rata (actual salary: £27,664) Location: Brighthelm Centre, Brighton, with some home working Reporting to: CEO Lead a project that helps people with learning disabilities have a stronger voice and greater influence Brighton & Hove Speak Out is looking for an experienced, passionate and values-driven leader to manage and develop our flagship self-advocacy project, the Learning Disability Voices Network (LDVN) . This is an exciting opportunity to join a respected local advocacy charity at a time of growth and development. Thanks to new National Lottery funding, we are expanding opportunities for people with learning disabilities to build confidence, develop self-advocacy skills, influence decision-making and create positive change in their communities. As Self-Advocacy Team Leader, you will lead the delivery of the LDVN project, support a dedicated team of staff and volunteers, and ensure people with learning disabilities remain at the heart of planning, delivery and decision-making. About the role You will be responsible for leading and coordinating all aspects of the Learning Disability Voices Network, including: Lead a team of 4 part-time project staff and volunteers across Brighton & Hove and West Sussex, supporting people with learning disabilities to identify issues that matter to them and take action to bring about change. Develop partnerships, local and national networks that strengthen self-advocacy opportunities. Support the LDVN steering group to plan and co-deliver self-advocacy events and training activities. Support and develop user-led self-advocacy groups, including support for an established user-led campaign group and the development of a new LGBTQ+ self-advocacy group. Oversee a weekly drop-in service in Brighton and the expansion of self-advocacy activity into West Sussex. Work with self-advocates to plan a learning disability-led regional conference Manage project budgets, monitoring systems, evaluation processes and funder reporting requirements. Work closely with the CEO to develop and strengthen the project's long-term impact and sustainability. Above all, you will ensure people with learning disabilities are supported to gain the skills, confidence and opportunities they need to speak up, influence decisions and lead change. About you We are looking for someone who: Is passionate about the rights, inclusion and empowerment of people with learning disabilities. Has experience leading projects, services, staff or volunteers. Understands the principles and practice of self-advocacy and person-centred support. Has experience of supporting people who may face discrimination, exclusion or barriers to participation. Can inspire and support others to develop confidence, skills and leadership. Has excellent communication, organisational and relationship-building skills. Is confident managing multiple priorities, monitoring outcomes and meeting targets. Can build effective partnerships with professionals, community organisations and stakeholders. Is committed to equality, inclusion, accessibility and safeguarding. Experience of working alongside people with learning disabilities is highly desirable. Why work for Speak Out? As well as the opportunity to lead an innovative and impactful project, we offer: 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata) Flexible working arrangements where operationally possible 3 % Pension contribution Employee Assistance Programme Ongoing training and professional development opportunities A supportive, inclusive and friendly team The opportunity to make a genuine and lasting difference to the lives of people with learning disabilities About Brighton & Hove Speak Out Brighton & Hove Speak Out is an independent advocacy charity supporting adults with learning disabilities. We believe people with learning disabilities should have the same rights, choices and opportunities as everyone else and should be supported to have their voices heard. Our work is built on the principles of self-advocacy, empowerment, inclusion and respect. We work alongside people with learning disabilities to challenge barriers, influence services and bring about positive change. item.title: Designer
item.description: Designer Hours: Full time Contract: Permanent Salary: £37,456 per annum Location: King's Cross, London N1C – Hybrid (Minimum 2 days in office per week) Who are we? Art Fund is the national fundraising charity for art. With over 148,000 members, we are leading the way in pioneering support for an inclusive and welcoming museum and gallery sector across the UK. We work closely with a network of over 1000 museums and respond to their needs and aspirations. We're excited to see how they want to develop: to expand and diversify their collections and workforce, develop curatorial skills, make ambitious acquisitions, and create a welcoming, inclusive space for communities. With the support of over 148,000 members who buy a National Art Pass, patrons, and donors we can provide grants, encourage visiting and advocate for museums' essential role and value. We have diversity, inclusion, and sustainability central to our thinking and the opportunity to be a force for good, galvanise support and help change things for the better inspires our team. The role We’re looking for a Designer who cares about the craft as much as the idea — someone who finds real satisfaction in getting things right, whether that’s a multi‑page publication, a set of digital assets, or a single piece of artwork that needs to be perfect down to the smallest detail. This role sits at the heart of our Creative Team. Most days you’ll be deep in design lead - precision creative artworking: building high‑volume digital and social assets, shaping long‑form documents, preparing print‑ready files, and making sure everything is brand‑consistent, technically robust and ready to go. Alongside that, you’ll take on genuine design work — developing concepts for campaigns, events and digital formats, and bringing ideas to life across multiple channels. You’ll work closely with the rest of the team to translate Art Fund’s visual identity / brand story across print, digital, social, environmental and campaign formats. Some days that means designing stage comps or signage for Museum of the Year, other days it’s delivering a full suite of digital and social assets, each one crafted with the same attention to detail, or building decks and mock-ups that help people see the idea clearly. If you enjoy a balance of design and production (the thinking as much as the making) and you take pride in work that’s accurate, thoughtful and beautifully executed, then this is a lovely role for you. Key Employee Benefits Generous Annual leave – 25 days annual leave and bank holidays, with additional non-contractual office closure dates at Christmas. Free National Art Pass (NAP) – for yourself and another person of your choice. Free Entry to Exhibitions Life Assurance – cover for up to three times your basic salary. Season Ticket Loan Pensions – Eligible employees are enrolled into the scheme with the exception of those who have contracts of three months or less. Art Fund contributes 8% of the basic annual salary during the first six months of employment or until probation is successfully completed, whichever is the later. At that point the contribution is increased to 10%. Closing deadline: 23.59pm on Sunday 11 October 2026 Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We're committed to building our team and trustees from the broad range of backgrounds and experiences across the UK, valuing difference and diversity, and building a workplace based on shared values of equality and mutual respect. We have ambitious plans for the future and will be holding ourselves to account and putting our principles into action, as we all work together to help bring about positive change and a fairer future for everyone. We therefore want to encourage applications from all races, ages, religions and sexual orientations, as well as parents, veterans, people living with any kind of disabilities and any other groups that could bring diverse perspectives to our organisation. Non-UK nationals will require current and valid permission to work in the UK. Please note that any suspected use of AI in relation to answering sift questions will be marked down. No agencies please.

item.title: Community Outreach Worker (CSS Housing)
item.description: Do you want to support people with mental health issues in a moment of crisis? Are you calm, non-judgemental and able to work effectively with people experiencing distress? If you can embody our values of Hope, Courage, Togetherness , and Responsiveness , and want to help others build resilience and manage their wellbeing, we’d love to hear from you. Community Outreach Worker (CSS Housing) Reference: 363 Salary: £26,000 - £26,500 per annum Hours: Full-Time, 37.5 hours per week (5 days per week) Reports to: Senior Lead Complex Needs and Community Working base: West Hertfordshire + possible Herts countywide travel. About the Service Community Outreach Workers support people with complex needs who have Housing issues as a primary need. This includes people who may have drug and alcohol difficulties. Particularly when they are coming into repeat contact with Police, Tenancy Sustainment Services, Housing and Homelessness Services and Environmental Health Services. The five-day post will be delivered in West Hertfordshire. With the flexibility to travel Hertfordshire County. The purpose of the Hertfordshire Mind Network Community Outreach Worker role is to: Provide advice, information, onward referral and holistic support to clients with coexisting drug and alcohol difficulties and mental ill-health. These will be clients who are presenting to the Police, Anti-Social Behaviour, Tenancy Enforcement, Housing and Environmental Health Services within Hertfordshire. Ensure that the safety and wellbeing of the client is monitored and reviewed regularly. Remain a source of independent support for all clients. Embed a person centred and solution focused approach in all aspects of the role. Raise greater awareness of complex needs and the effects of Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) amongst local service providers. Supporting them to gain confidence in working positively and consistently with people who have multiple needs. The Community Outreach Worker will: Receive both self-referrals and those allocated by Police, Borough Council, Housing Providers, and other relevant services. To complete a holistic needs assessment, making use of assertive outreach work to achieve the initial client contact, if required. Assist clients to access appropriate mental health services, drug and alcohol services, housing/tenancy services and other services according to assessed needs. Work with multi agency partners to support the delivery of co-ordinated services for clients. Work with partners both internal and external to ensure that vulnerable person’s cases are monitored and risks evaluated in order to promote community safety. work with the third sector and signpost to other agencies as necessary to improve the health and wellbeing of clients referred to the service. Proactively recognise the indicators of deteriorating mental health and provide crisis/safeguarding intervention support Support clients to build their emotional resilience and crisis planning tools, promoting self-management through building an understanding of their own triggers/coping strategies. We offer: Annual leave entitlement of 25 days per year pro rata, rising in increments to a max. of 29 days after 5 years employment (plus 8 days Bank Holidays) An additional day of leave each year for your birthday following completion of probation period. Ongoing training relevant to your role. An Employee Assistance Programme. Eligibility for blue light card. Health cover (after 6 months employment) - compensation payment for Optical, Dental, Chiropody and Therapy Treatments. Being able to drive and having access to your own vehicle (or equivalent) is essential for this role. Closing date for receipt of applications is 9th October 2026 at 5pm Interviews to be held on a rolling basis at our Watford Wellbeing Centre N.B. Please quote reference number 363 when completing your application for this role. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We welcome applications from all suitably-qualified candidates, irrespective of gender, disability, marital or parental status, racial, ethnic or social origin, colour, religion, belief, or sexual orientation. In addition, during the various stages of recruitment, specific measures can be taken to ensure equal opportunities for candidates with disabilities or special needs. Hertfordshire Mind Network is committed to the Disability Confident and Mindful Employer charters. We actively recruit staff who have a lived experience of mental ill health. Our inclusive approach recognises the unique skills, knowledge, and perspectives that lived experience brings to our team. No agencies please.

item.title: Energy Adviser
item.description: Citizens Advice Hounslow is a well-established charity serving the London Borough of Hounslow. We work to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people who come to us for support. Our high-quality, agile advice service responds to the issues and needs of our community, always putting people first. Thanks to our dedicated team of staff and volunteers, we support over 16,000 clients each year through our face-to-face, telephone and digital services. Citizens Advice Hounslow is looking for two Energy Advisers to join our friendly team. In this rewarding role, you will provide vital face-to-face and remote support to residents across Hounslow. You will empower them to avoid fuel poverty, navigate complex energy bills, access financial grants, and reduce their energy usage. If you don’t already have experience in giving energy advice, we provide comprehensive training to ensure you achieve a formal Energy Awareness Level 3 qualification (NEA). If you have a background in energy advice, other advice giving, customer service or community volunteering, and have a natural knack for empathy and hitting targets, we want to hear from you. What you’ll do: Deliver energy and income-maximisation advice via telephone, video calls, office appointments, and home visits. Help clients understand complex energy bills, resolve meter issues, provide confident switching advice, and educate households on the hidden risks of Carbon Monoxide leaks. Identify client eligibility for vital financial support, including energy grants, emergency rebates, and utility trust fund schemes, while making referrals to our internal benefits and debt teams. Use smart meters and temporarily install simple environmental monitoring equipment in client homes to gather data, using the results to show residents visual proof of how they can adapt their habits to save money. Confidently meet and exceed project targets (KPIs) set by our funders. Collaborate with internal debt, benefits, and campaign teams to offer holistic support. What you'll bring · Experience in advice-giving or customer support (face-to-face and phone-based). Excellent active listening skills and empathy for vulnerable community members. Strong digital skills (e.g. MS Office/Google Workspace, data entry). A positive, resilient attitude toward achieving performance targets. Senior role: The Senior Energy Adviser will lead a small energy advice team, comprising an Energy Adviser and a Community Champion. This dual-responsibility position combines direct energy advice with day-to-day team leadership. The Senior Energy Adviser will give energy advice to residents while ensuring service service delivery runs smoothly and project targets are met. The Senior Energy Adviser will also proactively assist the CA Hounslow’s management team with data collection, monitoring and reporting. We offer a range of employee benefits, including generous annual leave, pension contribution, and training and opportunities to continue your professional development. We consider applications from all applicants who meet the person specification irrespective of sex, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership status, pregnancy and maternity, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief, age, or disability.

item.title: Energy Community Champion
item.description: Citizens Advice Hounslow is launching a vital new energy advice programme that tackles fuel poverty and supports vulnerable communities across Hounslow. We are looking for a dynamic, proactive, and passionate Energy Community Champion to drive our grassroots outreach strategy, build robust partnerships, and create a strong community of energy awareness. Citizens Advice Hounslow is a well-established charity serving the London Borough of Hounslow. We work to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people who come to us for support. Our high-quality, agile advice service responds to the issues and needs of our community, always putting people first. Thanks to our dedicated team of staff and volunteers, we support over 16,000 clients each year through our face-to-face, telephone and digital services. The Role As our Energy Community Champion, you will lead outreach and engagement activities across community hubs, food banks, and local venues, identifying vulnerable residents who face barriers to accessing traditional advice services. Your mission will be split between delivering awareness-raising workshops and pop-up events in the community (covering energy efficiency, financial capability, and carbon monoxide safety) and upskilling local partner organisations . By training frontline workers in "problem noticing" techniques, you will build seamless referral pathways that route complex energy cases directly into our energy casework team. Please Note: Experience in energy advice or holding a City & Guilds Level 3 Energy Awareness qualification is highly desirable but not necessary, as full training will be provided. Key Responsibilities Project Development: Assist with the roll out the Energy Redress project across Hounslow, targeting areas of high deprivation. Build Referral Networks: Establish and maintain strong partnerships with voluntary, community, and statutory organisations. Deliver Dynamic Training & Workshops: Run "pop-up" energy-saving awareness events and financial capability workshops for residents, and deliver energy efficiency training to professional partner staff. Impact Tracking & Administration: Use internal database tools to maintain GDPR-compliant records and contribute data for evaluation reports against fixed KPIs. Professional Standards: Work cooperatively with the broader Energy Team and complete a full Level 3 Energy Awareness qualification during your induction. About You We are looking for a confident communicator who thrives when speaking to groups and building networks. You should be highly organized, self-motivated, and comfortable working in a targeted environment. Essential Requirements: Proven experience in grassroots community engagement, outreach, or partnership working. Strong background in delivering training, presentations, or educational workshops to diverse audiences. Experience delivering programmes focused on financial capability, budgeting, or energy-saving measures. Excellent data and IT skills, with an understanding of the barriers faced by low-income or vulnerable communities. Commitment to the aims and principles of the Citizens Advice service. We offer a range of employee benefits, including generous annual leave, pension contribution, and training and opportunities to continue your professional development. We consider applications from all applicants who meet the person specification irrespective of sex, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership status, pregnancy and maternity, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief, age, or disability.

item.description: Global Head of Communications and Marketing We are seeking a strategic and hands-on communications leader to shape the global profile of an international heritage charity and its commercial work. Position: Global Head of Communications and Marketing Location: Home-based in the UK, with frequent travel to London and international travel as required Salary: £52,000 to £65,000 per annum, depending on experience Hours: Full-time Closing Date: 4 October 2026 The closing date may be brought forward if a high volume of applications is received. About the Role This is an influential leadership role responsible for developing and delivering a global communications and marketing strategy across multiple countries, audiences and channels. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you will help position the organisation as a leading heritage charity, a trusted partner for commercial collaborations and a powerful advocate for artisans and cultural heritage. Combining strategic leadership with practical delivery, you will oversee brand, marketing, media relations, digital communications, thought leadership and internal communications. You will also lead a fully remote communications team and work closely with creative, commercial, fundraising and country teams. Key responsibilities include: Developing and delivering a multi-year global communications and marketing strategy Strengthening the organisation’s brand and reputation across commercial, philanthropic and public audiences Leading global media relations, public affairs and crisis communications Overseeing digital channels, content, newsletters and audience engagement Supporting the promotion of artisan collections, exhibitions and commercial partnerships Developing communications that support fundraising, philanthropy and donor engagement Creating consistent global messaging, brand standards and approval processes Supporting major events, launches and external speaking opportunities Leading, developing and setting clear expectations for the communications team Managing budgets, performance measures and communications reporting About You You will be a highly capable and collaborative communications leader who can combine strategic judgement with creativity, organisation and attention to detail. You will bring: Significant senior-level communications, marketing or corporate affairs experience Experience developing organisation-wide communications strategies A strong background in brand, reputation and media relations Digital communications, content and audience engagement expertise Experience leading and developing communications teams Exceptional writing, editing and storytelling skills Confidence advising senior leaders and supporting high-profile stakeholders Experience working across multiple countries, regions or cultures Experience within cultural heritage, arts, luxury, creative industries or international development would be particularly valuable. About the Organisation The organisation is an international charity supporting artisans and communities to protect and revitalise cultural heritage. item.title: Finance Manager
item.description: Finance Manager We are seeking an experienced charity finance professional to support the financial health and sustainability of an international organisation. Position: Finance Manager Salary: £42,000 to £45,000 per annum, depending on experience and qualifications Location: Remote, with occasional travel Hours: Full time, 35 hours per week Contract: Permanent Closing Date: 9 October 2026 About the Role This is an exciting opportunity to oversee the finance function of an international charity working alongside Indigenous and local communities to sustain biocultural diversity, strengthen traditional knowledge and cultivate justice, healing and belonging. Supported by a Finance Officer and working closely with colleagues across the Leadership Team, you will oversee financial planning, management, reporting and compliance. You will help ensure that financial information and processes support effective decision-making and the long-term sustainability of the organisation. Key responsibilities will include: Overseeing daily financial operations, payments, payroll and tax processes Coordinating the preparation of SORP-compliant financial statements Leading annual budgeting, forecasting, cash flow monitoring and management reporting Preparing financial reports for trustees, donors and internal stakeholders Supporting programme teams with budgets and monitoring expenditure Ensuring funding is used in accordance with donor and grant conditions Overseeing multi-currency transactions and international financial processes Managing the annual audit and working with external auditors Maintaining effective financial controls, policies and procedures Contributing financial insight to organisational planning, fundraising and risk management Supporting and developing the Finance Officer About You You may hold a recognised professional accountancy qualification or have developed substantial equivalent experience within a senior charity finance role. For more than two decades, it has worked alongside Indigenous and local communities to strengthen traditional knowledge systems and develop locally rooted responses to ecological and social challenges. Its international network connects changemakers across different regions through mentoring, shared learning and collaborative action. item.title: Head of Housing Development
item.description: Head of Housing Development Location: London/Hybrid Salary: £80,000.00 per annum Weekly Hours: 35 Reference: YMC1237090 About YMCA Founded in England in 1844, YMCA today is a global Movement and the world's largest youth-focused charity, reaching more than 58 million people across 119 countries. In England & Wales, we are a federation of 80 local YMCAs, based in over 700 communities across 168 local authorities, supporting young people and communities to reach their potential. We are also the largest provider of supported accommodation in the country — a role that puts housing at the heart of our mission. YMCA England & Wales is a £23 million organisation of more than 400 colleagues, supporting the wider Federation. Combined, the Movement's turnover across England & Wales reached £386 million in 2025–26. As we grow our income and impact, housing is one of our clearest opportunities for scale: through our 10,000 Homes ambition, we are building a national platform that will let local YMCAs deliver affordable and supported housing faster, at lower risk, and with a unified voice. As we take this ambition forward, we are seeking an established and inspirational Head of Housing Development to lead one of the most pivotal roles in our organisation. About The Opportunity This is a brand-new role. Our Head of Housing Development will establish and lead our national Housing Centre of Expertise: the capacity- and capability-building engine behind our 10,000 Homes ambition. This is not a scheme-delivery role — local YMCAs build, own and operate their own homes. Instead, you will mobilise the talent and resources of the Federation around a shared platform for scale: guiding local YMCAs from feasibility through to investment-readiness, brokering the partnerships and expertise no single YMCA could assemble alone, and leading a single national conversation with strategic partners including Homes England, the Greater London Authority and Welsh Government. You will establish a panel of preferred development partners, support funding bids, and help YMCAs learn from one another rather than rebuilding expertise scheme by scheme. Success will be measured by the pipeline and capability you build across the movement, not by any single project. About You You bring real knowledge of social and affordable housing development, including structuring significant financing models, grant regimes and the regulatory landscape, alongside hands-on experience of property development projects and securing private and public-sector funding. You know how to build strategic partnerships, convene and influence people you do not manage, and translate strategy into coordinated action across independent partners. Experience mobilising change across a federated, membership or infrastructure organisation would be a strong advantage, combined with an in-depth knowledge of Homes England, Greater London Authority and Welsh Government or similar agencies. Above all, you are a natural relationship-builder who can represent YMCA with confidence at a senior, national level, while helping local YMCAs move further and faster together than they could alone.
item.dc:creator: YMCA England and Wales

item.title: Service Transformation and Innovation
item.description: Lead transformation that changes lives. Are you a strategic thinker who can bring people together to turn complex challenges into practical change? Do you have the experience and influence to turn ambitious ideas into practical, sustainable transformation? If so, this could be the opportunity for you. At Together Trust, everything we do is about creating opportunities for the people we support to thrive. As we deliver our ambitious five-year strategy , we are looking for a talented Service Transformation & Innovation Lead to help turn our vision into reality. item.title: Anti-Racism Strategic Lead - Bradford Health Inequities Programme (Bhip)
item.description: The Opportunity This is an opportunity to take a leading role in an ambitious five-year programme working to address how structural racism and discrimination contribute to health across Bradford District. You will provide specialist leadership on structural racism, policy and system influence, working alongside communities and partners to turn lived and community insight into credible structural analysis, practical action and demonstrable system change. From early in the programme, you will build the relationships and routes into health, care and wider systems needed to ensure emerging evidence reaches the places where decisions are made and, creates opportunities to test and evaluate change that is translated into opportunities to test, evaluate and embed change. You will also shape Bhip’s anti-racism and structural discrimination learning, strengthen community leadership and influence, and generate evidence and learning that can inform policy and practice in Bradford and contribute to the National Lottery Community Fund’s National Collective. About You/ The Role You will be an experienced and credible leader with significant expertise in anti-racism, structural discrimination, policy and system change, and an understanding of how these contribute to health inequities. This is not a generic EDI, policy or anti-racism role. It is Bhip’s specialist lead for racism and structural discrimination, responsible for applying structural analysis to community insight and evidence, building structural literacy and anti-racist capability, and working with communities and system partners to translate that learning into accountable changes in policy, practice, commissioning, governance and decision-making that drive demonstrable system change and improvement. You will be equally comfortable working alongside Global Majority communities and community leaders, white allies, VCSE organisations, practitioners, commissioners, senior system leaders and change makers. You will combine strong analytical and policy skills with the ability to build trusted relationships, influence and constructively challenge, navigating complexity and resistance while maintaining a clear focus on shared power and institutional accountability. Working closely with the Programme Lead and wider Bhip team, you will play a key role in turning community insight into defined system action and demonstrable, evaluated system change, generating evidence and learning that can be shared locally and nationally to influence wider policy and practice. You will understand why organisations and systems can resist change and have the interpersonal, political and influencing skills to move people towards action, without diluting evidence or avoiding difficult challenge simply to maintain relationships. The Bradford Health Inequities Programme (Bhip) The Bradford Health Inequities Programme (Bhip) is a five-year programme funded by the National Lottery Community Fund and delivered jointly in partnership by Race Equality Network (REN) and Happy Healthy You (HHU). As part of the National Lottery Community Fund’s National Collective, Bhip is one of nine health inequities programmes established nationally to address health inequities caused by structural racism and discrimination. Working alongside communities, voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) organisations, the NHS, public services and other partners across Bradford District, Bhip will co-design, test and evaluate community-led approaches that address health inequities driven by structural racism and discrimination, influence policy and practice, drive system change, and generate evidence and learning for Bradford while contributing to the National Lottery Community Fund’s National Collective. As an innovative five-year programme, Bhip is expected to evolve through community engagement, co-design, learning and evaluation. The Bhip team members should therefore expect their roles to develop over time in response to programme learning, funding and organisational requirements to achieve its aims.

item.title: Our Place and Our Voice Manager
item.description: Manager – Our Place and Our Voice Pay: £37,650 - £41,250 per annum Hours: Full-time. 35 hours per week Work Pattern: Spread across Monday to Saturday (mostly Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm, with occasional Saturday work to support events and projects) Contract Period: Permanent Location: AoD Our Place Project, Normand Croft Community School, Lillie Road, London SW6 7SR About Action on Disability Action on Disability (AoD), founded in 1979, is one of London’s leading Disabled People’s Organisations (DPOs). Guided by the Social Model of Disability, we work to remove barriers and promote equality, inclusion and choice for all Disabled people. AoD is a medium-sized charity with a Board of Trustees, 27 staff, and a strong pool of casual staff and volunteers. Many of whom have lived experience of disability. We are proud that 100% of our Board and 54% of our staff identify as Disabled. We deliver four key services: Youth, Employment, Welfare Benefits, and Independent Living. Purpose of the Role The Manager for Our Place and Our Voice leads AoD’s work on co-production, peer support, campaigning and community engagement. The postholder ensures Disabled people are actively involved in shaping services, influencing policy and strengthening their voice within the local community and beyond. The role coordinates peer-led programmes, develops accessible training and events, and builds partnerships that promote inclusion and representation. Working closely with the Chief Operating Officer, the postholder ensures that AoD’s values of co-production and Disabled leadership are embedded throughout the organisation. Main Responsibilities 1. Lead, plan and coordinate AoD’s Our Place and Our Voice programmes, including co-production, peer support and community engagement initiatives. 2. Develop and deliver accessible training, workshops and events that build confidence, skills and leadership among Disabled people. 3. Recruit, supervise and support volunteers, peer facilitators and freelancers to deliver activities safely and effectively. 4. Build and maintain positive partnerships with local authorities, VCSE organisations, health services and community networks to promote the voice of Disabled people. 5. Promote co-production practice across AoD’s services, working with other managers to embed user involvement in service design and review. 6. Ensure all activities are inclusive, accessible and aligned with the Social Model of Disability. 7. Monitor and evaluate project performance, including collecting data, feedback and case studies to evidence impact. 8. Manage budgets within agreed limits and support financial planning and reporting to the CEO. 9. Prepare and submit funding applications and tender bids (in conjunction with the CEO) to support programme sustainability and growth. 10. Ensure compliance with AoD policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health & safety and data protection. 11. Represent AoD positively at external meetings, forums and events, promoting our work and values. 12. Work collaboratively with other AoD departments to promote shared learning and inclusive practice. General Responsibilities Work in line with AoD’s aims, values and the Social Model of Disability. Follow AoD’s policies on Equality, Safeguarding, Health & Safety, Confidentiality and Data Protection. Actively contribute to team meetings, supervision and training. Promote AoD’s services and values to partners, employers and the wider community. Be flexible and willing to carry out other tasks that support the smooth running of the service. Organisational responsibilities All staff share responsibility for upholding AoD’s values and ensuring that our work reflects the principles of the Social Model of Disability. In this role you will: Work in line with AoD’s aims, values and strategic priorities , promoting equality, inclusion and co-production in all aspects of your work. Follow AoD’s policies and procedures , including those covering Equality, Safeguarding, Health & Safety, Data Protection and Confidentiality. Promote and represent AoD positively to partners, employers, funders and members of the public. Contribute to organisational development , suggesting improvements and sharing ideas to strengthen our services. Participate fully in supervision, training, team and organisational meetings, and support colleagues to achieve shared goals. Maintain accurate records and monitoring data , contributing to reports for funders, commissioners and internal use. Work flexibly across projects and departments when needed, supporting colleagues and adapting to new priorities. Ensure safe and responsible working practices in all aspects of your role, including the wellbeing of yourself and others. Uphold AoD’s commitment to being a DPO led by and for Disabled people. In return we offer 25 days annual leave (pro rata), rising to 30 days after 5 years’ service Life Assurance (1x salary if enrolled in the auto-enrolment pension) Company sick pay (2 weeks after 6 months’ service; 1 month after 12 months) 2 weeks Disability Leave pay Employee Assistance Programme Additional Information You do not need to meet every point to apply. We welcome applications from Disabled people and value a wide range of experience, including lived experience of disability. Some evening or weekend work may occasionally be required. An enhanced DBS check will be required. Travel across Greater London will be required; travel expenses reimbursed according to policy. Managers are expected to work on-site for at least four days per week (full-time equivalent); for part-time staff this will be proportionate to their hours. Closing Date: Friday 9th October 2026 (3pm) Interview Dates: Thursday 15th October 2026 N.B. We reserve the right to interview and close the deadline early should a suitable applicant apply Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website where you can complete your application for this position. We particularly welcome applications from Disabled people, as they are currently under-represented in leadership roles across the wider voluntary and community sector. As a Disabled People’s Organisation, we believe lived experience brings valuable insight and leadership to this role. We will provide reasonable adjustments at all stages of recruitment and employment. No agencies please.

item.title: Head of Practice
item.description: About the role We’re looking for an experienced and values-led Head of Practice to provide strategic and professional leadership for practice across Hft. This is a key national leadership role, responsible for shaping our approach to Positive Behaviour Support (PBS), restrictive practice reduction, PROACT-SCIPr-UK, practice standards, workforce capability and coaching, and rights-based and trauma-informed practice. A key priority will be leading Hft’s transition to PROACT-SCIPr-UK, ensuring this is embedded within our wider PBS and restrictive practice reduction approach and translates into meaningful improvements in frontline practice and the quality of life of the people we support. You’ll lead our PBS / Practice Team, provide expert oversight of complex situations and act as a trusted professional adviser to senior leaders on practice quality, risk, outcomes and improvement. What you’ll be doing You’ll: Develop and lead an organisation-wide Practice Strategy and Practice Standards Framework. Provide professional leadership, advice and constructive challenge to senior and operational leaders. Lead and develop the PBS / Practice Team and build sustainable specialist capability. Lead the implementation of PROACT-SCIPr-UK across the organisation. Drive our restrictive practice reduction strategy, using data and evidence to identify opportunities for improvement. Provide specialist leadership around complex and high-risk practice situations. Develop workforce capability through training, coaching, observation, modelling and reflective practice. Embed rights-based, person-centred and trauma-informed approaches across Hft. Lead or contribute to practice-related policies and professional guidance. Provide senior leadership with clear evidence of practice quality, risk, outcomes and improvement. What you’ll bring We’re looking for someone with: Significant senior experience within learning disability and/or autism services. Strong professional expertise in Positive Behaviour Support. Significant knowledge and practical experience of PROACT-SCIPr-UK, with the ability to lead organisational implementation. Experience of restrictive practice reduction and least restrictive approaches. Experience leading specialist practice or PBS teams. A strong track record of developing practice standards, frameworks and guidance. Experience building workforce capability through coaching, training and practice leadership. Strong knowledge of safeguarding, Mental Capacity Act principles and relevant health and social care requirements. The confidence to influence, advise and constructively challenge senior leaders. A relevant professional qualification and evidence of continued specialist development. A postgraduate qualification in PBS, Applied Behaviour Analysis, Psychology or a related discipline, relevant professional registration and PROACT-SCIPr-UK instructor or advanced implementation experience would be desirable. What success looks like Success in this role will mean better outcomes and quality of life for the people we support. You’ll help ensure that PBS is embedded in everyday practice, restrictive practices are reduced wherever safely possible, PROACT-SCIPr-UK is successfully implemented, and managers and frontline teams have the confidence and capability to deliver consistently excellent, rights-based support. Working arrangements This is a national hybrid role with regular travel to Hft services and other locations across the organisation. Why Hft? At Hft, our mission is simple: the best life possible. We believe people with learning disabilities should be able to live within their communities, with all the choice and support they need to live the best life possible. This is an exciting opportunity to influence practice at a national level and make a genuine difference to the lives of the people we support. Recruitment process Applications close on 11 October 2026. Interviews will take place on 27 October 2026 and will be held via Microsoft Teams.

item.title: Senior Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods Advocacy Advisor
item.description: Closing Date: 27 September 2026 Ref 7405 Save the Children UK is looking for an experienced policy and advocacy professional to join our Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods team as a Senior Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods Advocacy Advisor on a maternity cover basis, working three days per week. This is a unique opportunity to lead and shape Save the Children's global advocacy on child wasting and malnutrition, helping to drive progress on one of the most critical challenges facing children worldwide. You will strengthen our global leadership and visibility, influence policy and decision-makers, and build strategic relationships with partners including government, multilateral organisations, donors and civil society. You will also coordinate and influence key coalition activities, represent Save the Children in high-profile external forums and help strengthen policy and advocacy capability across the team. This role would suit someone with strong knowledge of the global nutrition policy landscape, particularly child wasting, together with experience of leading coalitions, building partnerships and delivering effective influencing strategies. About Us Save the Children UK believes every child deserves a future. In the UK and around the world, we work every day to give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. When crisis strikes, and children are most vulnerable, we are always among the first to respond and the last to leave. We ensure children's unique needs are met and their voices are heard. We deliver lasting results for millions of children, including those hardest to reach. About the Team Working as part of the Global Impact group, our Global Outcomes function catalyses positive change for children by driving influencing agendas and bringing knowledge, evidence, analysis and expertise to our partnerships, programmes and advocacy work. The Hunger, Nutrition & Livelihoods Team works as part of the Global Save the Children movement and the wider sector to drive long lasting systems changes at the global and country levels. We are committed to promoting inclusive and equitable solutions, amplifying the voices of children most affected by inequality, and prioritising locally led efforts for lasting change. About the role As Senior Hunger, Nutrition and Livelihoods Advocacy Advisor, you will provide global leadership in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods policy and advocacy, with a particular focus on child wasting and malnutritionto shape and drive shared advocacy and impact agendas across Save the Children and the wider sector. You will develop and deliver high-quality policy and influencing strategies, fostering innovation and inclusivity and contributing to systemic change. In this role, you will build strategic relationships with key decision-makers, lead capacity strengthening for colleagues and partners, and champion equality, inclusion and the shifting power agenda. Additionally, you will contribute to multi-disciplinary teams and drive thought leadership. In this role, you will: Provide global leadership in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods policy and advocacy, with a particular focus on child wasting and malnutrition, to shape and drive shared influencing and impact agendas within the Save the Children movement and the wider sector, maintaining up-to-date expertise and monitoring relevant external trends. Set and deliver outcome goals for your area of specialism by working collaboratively to implement strategies that contribute to systemic change, incorporating power analysis, policy, advocacy, research, partnerships and programme portfolios as relevant. Develop and deliver very high-quality policy, research and advocacy outputs with minimal supervision, ensuring inclusivity and excellence in implementation. Contribute to a strong learning culture through leading or supporting research, evaluation, innovation and knowledge sharing. Provide thought leadership in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods, particularly child wasting and malnutrition, including engaging in external debate and producing technical guidance, research briefs and analytical outputs to identify barriers and pragmatic but ambitious solutions for transformative change. Facilitate capacity strengthening through mentoring, coaching and training, providing formal and informal support to colleagues and partners to build expertise and effectiveness. Build and maintain strategic relationships with key high-level decision-makers and opinion leaders, including senior civil servants, academics, leaders in international organisations and civil society partners, to amplify the impact of our advocacy and programmes. Lead and coordinate coalition engagement and partnership working to advance shared advocacy objectives and strengthen collective impact on child wasting and malnutrition. Coordinate and contribute to high-level events, meetings and influencing opportunities, including preparing briefings and materials for senior leaders and representing Save the Children in external forums. Champion and role model equality, inclusion and impact across Save the Children's work and the broader sector, while actively shifting power and resources closer to the communities and children served. Identify and lead strategic partnerships with funders and other organisations in collaboration with partnership colleagues to advance child rights and increase impact. About you To be successful, it is important that you have/are: A strong track-record in designing and implementing successful influencing strategies with minimal supervision, drawing on analytical skills to identify political and other barriers to change and prioritise from a range of possible objectives and approaches. High-level expertise in the global international development and child rights policy landscape and institutions, coupled with deep expertise in hunger, nutrition and livelihoods policy and advocacy, including strong knowledge of the nutrition policy landscape and child wasting. A strong track-record in policy analysis and development, with the ability to draw on different sources of information and ideas from partners and children to generate relevant policy positions and solutions that resonate with target audiences. Experience working in and leading coalitions, partnerships and collaborative initiatives, bringing together diverse stakeholders to drive shared advocacy objectives and impact. Proven ability to build external relationships and partnerships, and to influence decision-makers and policy specialists, including politicians, donors, multilateral organisations, civil society actors and other key stakeholders globally. Very strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to resonate with and influence different audiences. The ability to network and represent Save the Children externally, including facilitating and speaking at high-level events and meetings, engaging with senior stakeholders and acting as a credible organisational representative. Experience coordinating or contributing to high-level events and influencing opportunities, including producing briefings and materials for senior leadership. Strong interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence and authenticity that enable effective communication and relationship-building with a wide range of audiences. Strong convening skills, creating synergy, fostering collaboration and bringing together diverse perspectives to achieve common goals. Experience supporting capacity strengthening through mentoring, coaching, training or knowledge-sharing activities. What we offer you We promote flexibility, inclusion, collaboration, and wellbeing both at work and beyond, and offer a wide range of benefits designed to reward your hard work and inspire you to help improve the lives of children every day. Some of the benefits you can expect include: Generous Annual Leave – Starting at 27 days per year (pro rata for part-time employees) increasing with service up to 32 days, plus public holidays and our annual 'Save the Children Day'. Family Leave – Up to 39 weeks of maternity/adoption pay (including up to 21 weeks full pay) and paternity/adoption leave of 10 weeks full pay (plus statutory entitlement). Special Leave – Up to 10 days paid leave per year (pro rata) for urgent or exceptional personal circumstances, without using annual leave. Volunteer Leave – Up to 3 days paid leave per year to support volunteering and give back. Pension & Life Assurance – Helping you plan for the future with up to 7% employer pension contributions. Employee Discounts – Access thousands of deals across groceries, retail, tech, travel, fitness, and more. Health & Wellbeing Support – Including access to a 24/7 Virtual GP and Employee Assistance Programme and Counselling, eye care support, and seasonal flu vaccinations. Please note: To avoid disappointment, you are advised to submit your application as soon as possible as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications are received. This is to ensure that we can manage application levels whilst maintaining a positive candidate experience. Unfortunately once a vacancy has closed, we are unable to consider further applications. Location & Ways of Working: The majority of our roles can be performed remotely in the UK, but at times you will be required to come to your contracted office (usually between 2–4 days per month, depending on the needs of your role, team, or service). For many roles, this is likely to be the minimum required to deliver impact. This will be discussed and agreed with your manager / team and we encourage candidates to discuss our ways of working in more detail at interview stage. Please note: travel costs to your contracted office will be at your own expense. Flexible Working - We are happy to discuss flexible working options at interview . Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion: Save the Children
