item.description: “Providing free, independent, confidential and impartial advice” Citizens Advice Southwark has a track record of delivering high-quality services from its offices in Peckham and Walworth and outreach locations across Southwark and South East London. We sort out problems together, for good, by providing free, independent, confidential and impartial advice across all areas of social welfare law, and through using the experience of our clients to bring about positive change through research and campaigns. item.title: Christmas Events Assistant
item.description: About Us: Princess Alice Hospice is a charity supporting people in life, death and grief. We’re dedicated to working closely with individuals, communities and organisations in the London Boroughs of Kingston and Richmond and large parts of Surrey, to ensure more people receive the support they need. About the role: We’re thrilled to offer a fantastic opportunity to join our Fundraising Team in a temporary role supporting our Christmas events programme. You’ll help deliver our festive calendar, with a particular focus on our flagship Santa Fun Run, which aims to raise an incredible £66,000. You’ll also support Light Up a Life and our Christmas Tree Collections in January. This is a varied, hands-on role. Key responsibilities include: • Researching and ordering stock and liaising with suppliers • Loading and driving a small van • Putting up banners • Distributing leaflets to businesses and organisations in our care area • Liaising with community fundraisers to promote the event • Engaging with staff across the organisation to promote the event • Updating event briefing documents • Calling supporters to discuss the event, helping them set up fundraising pages and supporting their fundraising • Liaising with the Volunteering team to recruit and brief volunteers • Attending all events is essential. Event dates are 29 November 2026, 4 December 2026, 13 December 2026 and 8–12 January 2027. You'll be there to help set up events and ensure they run smoothly on the day. You’ll also support the wider marketing and administration involved in event management and delivery, including preparing marketing literature and providing administrative support. Who are we looking for? We’re looking for someone who enjoys being part of a lively team, is happy to get stuck into practical tasks and is confident engaging with supporters, volunteers and colleagues. • Ready to unwrap an exciting career in fundraising and make a meaningful difference • Passionate about bringing brilliant events to life and creating a buzz in the community • A super-organised multitasker who keeps the details sparkling and thrives as part of a team • Bursting with energy, can-do enthusiasm and enough festive spirit to rival Santa’s elves! You’ll help bring the Santa Fun Run to life, which may include dressing as Santa or an elf, promoting the event around the Hospice and in the community, and encouraging people to sign up. What you’ll be doing: • Supporting the event lead with planning and logistics • Motivating participants and engaging the community • Assisting with event setup and delivery, including lifting boxes, erecting gazebos and packing vans • Driving a van (so a full UK driving licence is essential) • Working flexibly, including evenings and weekends as needed This role is ideal for someone who wants hands-on experience in the lively world of community fundraising. You’ll build practical skills across charity events and seasonal campaigns while helping create memorable experiences for supporters and the local community. At Princess Alice Hospice we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that values diversity. We are fully committed to equality of opportunity and warmly welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, cultures, and lived experiences. We value the unique perspectives each person brings and strive to create a workplace where everyone feels respected and supported. We are an organisation where you can be you. We are signed up to the Disability Confident scheme and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for the vacancy. Please visit the Join our Team section on our website for tips and guidance on how to complete your application form, and what to expect when interviewing with us. Please visit our Privacy Notices section to understand and be aware of how we use the data you provide to us. All of our vacancies except from retail are subject to a relevant DBS check.

item.title: Individual Giving & Supporter Engagement Manager
item.description: Help grow sustainable income that changes lives across rural Africa. At Ripple Effect, we're empowering farming families across rural Africa to build resilient livelihoods and create lasting change. This is an opportunity for an ambitious, experienced fundraising leader to shape and grow Ripple Effect's supporter income programme, lead a team of specialist fundraisers and play a pivotal role in delivering sustainable unrestricted income growth. Reporting to the Head of Marcomms & Supporter Engagement, you'll lead the development and delivery of our individual giving and supporter engagement programme, playing a pivotal role in growing our supporter base and maximising supporter lifetime value. You'll be responsible for developing and delivering acquisition, retention and stewardship strategies across multiple income streams, ensuring supporters feel connected to the impact of their giving and inspired to continue their journey with us. Using audience insight, data and innovation, you'll identify new opportunities for growth, optimise supporter journeys and improve campaign performance to deliver sustainable income growth. You'll lead and develop a high-performing team, manage income and expenditure budgets, and work collaboratively across fundraising, communications and programme teams to deliver ambitious targets. item.title: Partnership Co-Ordinator
item.description: The Opportunity GOD TV are looking to build our Partnerships call team in the UK. We are looking for dedicated Christians who would like the opportunity tobe part of a dynamictelephone call team committed to sharing the Gospel throughout the globe and serving our viewers both in prayer and creating opportunities for them to partner with us. This is an opportunity to work from home and connect with GOD TV’s viewers via the phone with a variety of calls from across the US, the UK, Europe and the Nordic regions via phone & social media. The Role This role is a telephone based fundraising role. As a Partnership Co-ordinator you will be part of the UK Partnerships team. It will be your job to build mutually beneficial relationships with new and existing contacts over the phone. You will learn all about GOD TV and the powerful testimonies we receive, and will communicate with our partners to encourage them, share these stories and to increase financial support. Responsibilities include making calls to ensure the re-engagement of lapsed donors, increasing regular giving and asking people to give new gifts. This is done from a perspective of creating ‘God’ appropriate opportunities for people to give into and not a sales approach, but as part of your role you will be expected to bring in new income and have an annual target to meet. You will be expected to think of creative ideas to help grow and sustain GOD TV’s donation income alongside your team. Why This Role This is more than a fundraising position; it is a front-line ministry role at a pivotal moment in GOD TV’s history. As a Partnership Co-ordinator you serve as the face of GOD TV, building and maintaining strong relationships with the partners who engage with this ministry. For a professional who excels in communication and finds deep fulfilment in prayer, this role offers the rare chance to use your career to directly advance the Gospel. You will join a high-energy, supportive team where your daily conversations have a tangible, eternal impact on millions of homes worldwide. Please download the full Job Description for more information. Genuine Occupational Requirement Due to the nature and strategic influence of this role, we believe that there is a Genuine Occupational Requirement (GOR) for this role to be fulfilled by a practicing and committed Christian believer.

item.title: DiSSCo UK Digitisation Unit Lead
item.description: About us We are a world-class visitor attraction and leading science research centre. We use the Museum's unique collections and our unrivalled expertise to tackle the biggest challenges facing the world today. We care for more than 80 million objects spanning billions of years and welcome more than five million visitors annually and 16 million visits to our website. Today the Museum is more relevant and influential than ever. By attracting people from a range of backgrounds to work for us, we can continue to look at the world with fresh eyes and find new ways of doing things. We employ 1100 staff in a variety of roles, all united by our vision of a future where people and planet thrive. We need everyone to have the passion and drive to help us with our mission to create advocates for our planet and inspire millions to care about the natural world. This role is specifically working as part of the Distributed System of Scientific Collections UK programme . UK natural science collections hold more than 140 million items. These are an unrivalled source of data about how the Earth and its natural systems formed over 4.56 billion years, with the potential to support research that addresses some of the critical issues facing the world, including biodiversity and climate change. They contain evidence of the changes in the natural world including the impact of human life on our planet over the past few thousand years. The scientific, commercial, and societal benefits of these collections are currently constrained by the limits of physical access, and by highly fragmented digitisation efforts with less than 10% digitally available. DiSSCo UK is a consortium of UK natural science collections, led by the Natural History Museum in partnership with the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) and UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), who are developing a national infrastructure to support the digitisation and use of the UK’s natural science collections to support this critical research. This will take the form of a 10-year programme focused on digitisation of critical mass of collections as FAIR data, made available through a well-supported backbone of technology infrastructure, with continued development and application of innovative approaches such as greater use of Artificial Intelligence and robotics. Investment of the order of £155m over ten years from 2026-27 is expected to unlock at least a four-fold economic return on investment, as well as efficiency savings for UK and global researchers, and the potential for research innovation and studies that have not previously been possible – underpinning a future in which both people and planet thrive. Diversity and inclusion matter to us. Our vision is of a future where both people and the planet thrive. Diversity is one of our core values and we strive to build a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging. All new staff who join us learn about the importance of diversity and inclusion to the Museum and how to contribute to creating an inclusive environment. We know we have more to do, but we are committed to ensuring that everyone who works at the Museum feels they can thrive and feel valued and respected. About the role DiSSCo UK is seeking an experienced and inspirational Digitisation Team Unit Lead to oversee digitisation operations, deliver strategic objectives, and support the development of a high-performing team contributing to the UK's natural science collections infrastructure. The Unit Lead will provide sectional technical and people leadership for digitisation and collection preparation activities, ensuring projects are delivered efficiently, safely, and to a high standard. You will work across institutional teams and external partners to drive innovation, improve workflows, and deliver impactful outcomes that support research, conservation, and public engagement. This role is based within the Museum’s Digital, Data and Informatics (DDI) Department and reports to the DiSSCo UK Operations Team Lead. This is a fixed term role until 31 March 2028. About you You will be a confident communicator, able to foster strong working relationships both within the DiSSCo UK programme and wider NHM Collection teams. You will thrive in team environments, supporting and driving your teams to success, with excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills. The role will combine technical digitisation expertise and people management. While beneficial, it is not essential that the postholder has previous direct management experience. We welcome applicants who may not have had formal line management experience previously, but are willing to learn and embrace building, developing and motivating a team. This post will lead the Botanical section of Digitisers and Collection Assistants. The postholder will need substantial experience working with natural science collections, with applied botanical expertise and the ability to make informed operational decisions on specimen handling and workflow requirements. Thriving at the Museum: the way we work We are proud to work at the Museum and have identified the qualities we all need to embody to reach our shared ambition. This sits alongside the Museum’s values and forms the framework for the way we work. Find out more on our website. What we offer 27.5 days holiday plus 8 bank holidays (full time equivalent) Generous defined contribution Natural History Museum Pension Scheme (employer contribution 4 - 10%) Season ticket, bicycle and rental loan Life insurance Free admission to our exhibitions and many other paid exhibitions at museums, galleries and institutions across London and the UK. Staff discount at our Museum shops and cafes We offer a wide variety of training initiatives and opportunities to build skills. Investing in staff development is important to us, and we are ambitious about helping staff to grow and fulfil their potential. Affordable membership to the Civil Service Sports Council which offers a range of benefits including an extensive list of special offers and reduced entry fees at a selection of cinema chains, theme parks, theatres, retailers and supermarkets. It also provides entry to up to 300 English Heritage sites and other national treasures. Membership to our Sports and Social Association (for a small fee), which includes access to our in-house gym and clubs such as football, softball, table tennis and tennis and classes in Middle Eastern dance, yoga and Tai Chi Hybrid working We are working towards a vision where both people and planet thrive, and nothing gives a greater connection with this, than seeing first-hand, the visitors, scientific research and collections that all of our work is inspired by and working side by side with the teams delivering the visitor experience and events. We also recognise the benefits and flexibility that hybrid working brings. We operate a hybrid working model that requires regular, weekly attendance for this role, with the precise pattern of days on site and worked from home to be agreed with your manager. Hybrid working is possible, with onsite supervision required during digitisation activity, around 3 days per week on average. This may increase in line with business requirements. Occasional work across other Museum or partner sites around the UK may be required. How to apply If this sounds like you, please apply on our website. Please note that as part of our commitment to anonymised shortlisting, panels do not view CVs during the recruitment process. If you choose to upload your CV, our system will automatically pull information from your CV into our application form. We advise you to double-check your application form data before submitting as the tool may interpret CVs differently. Closing date: 23:59 on 29 September Interviews expected: w/c 19 October Please note that this role does not qualify for Museum sponsorship so the successful postholder will need to have a valid right to work in the UK at the point of offer.

The scientific, commercial, and societal benefits of these collections are currently constrained by the limits of physical access, and by highly fragmented digitisation efforts with less than 10% digitally available. DiSSCo UK is a consortium of UK natural science collections, led by the Natural History Museum in partnership with the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) and UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), who are developing a national infrastructure to support the digitisation and use of the UK’s natural science collections to support this critical research. This will take the form of a 10-year programme focused on digitisation of critical mass of collections as FAIR data, made available through a well-supported backbone of technology infrastructure, with continued development and application of innovative approaches such as greater use of Artificial Intelligence and robotics. Investment of the order of £155m over ten years from 2026-27 is expected to unlock at least a four-fold economic return on investment, as well as efficiency savings for UK and global researchers, and the potential for research innovation and studies that have not previously been possible – underpinning a future in which both people and planet thrive. Diversity and inclusion matter to us. Our vision is of a future where both people and the planet thrive. Diversity is one of our core values and we strive to build a workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging. All new staff who join us learn about the importance of diversity and inclusion to the Museum and how to contribute to creating an inclusive environment. We know we have more to do, but we are committed to ensuring that everyone who works at the Museum feels they can thrive and feel valued and respected. About the role We're looking for proactive individuals with a keen eye for detail who can work well within and across teams to deliver agreed digitisation imaging and data outputs within a given collection area (Entomology or Botany). You will have an agile and pragmatic approach to problem solving, seeking advice where necessary and escalating issues in a timely manner. Above all, you are an excellent communicator, thrive in busy target-focused environments and have an enthusiasm for digitisation and the collection areas within which you work. This position is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a nationally significant programme of work during a key phase of DiSSCo UK’s rollout. We encourage applications from candidates (both internal and external) who fulfil most of the key competencies and are willing to engage in training and personal development opportunities to fill any knowledge gaps. This role is based within the Museum’s Digital, Data and Informatics (DDI) Department and reports to the relevant Unit Lead (Entomology or Botany). This is a fixed term role until 31 March 2028. About you Are you passionate about making natural science collections accessible to researchers, policymakers, and the public worldwide? DiSSCo UK is seeking enthusiastic and detail-oriented Digitisers to help transform the Natural History Museum’s physical collections into high-quality digital records. As a Digitiser, you will work initially with Entomological or Botanical collections, capturing specimen data and images to support global research and biodiversity knowledge. Your work will contribute directly to unlocking scientific collections and making them available through both the NHM and national network of DiSSCo UK digital infrastructures. Thriving at the Museum: the way we work We are proud to work at the Museum and have identified the qualities we all need to embody to reach our shared ambition. This sits alongside the Museum’s values and forms the framework for the way we work. Find out more on our website. What we offer 27.5 days holiday plus 8 bank holidays (full time equivalent) Generous defined contribution Natural History Museum Pension Scheme (employer contribution 4 - 10%) Season ticket, bicycle and rental loan Life insurance Free admission to our exhibitions and many other paid exhibitions at museums, galleries and institutions across London and the UK. Staff discount at our Museum shops and cafes We offer a wide variety of training initiatives and opportunities to build skills. Investing in staff development is important to us, and we are ambitious about helping staff to grow and fulfil their potential. Affordable membership to the Civil Service Sports Council which offers a range of benefits including an extensive list of special offers and reduced entry fees at a selection of cinema chains, theme parks, theatres, retailers and supermarkets. It also provides entry to up to 300 English Heritage sites and other national treasures. Membership to our Sports and Social Association (for a small fee), which includes access to our in-house gym and clubs such as football, softball, table tennis and tennis and classes in Middle Eastern dance, yoga and Tai Chi Hybrid working We are working towards a vision where both people and planet thrive, and nothing gives a greater connection with this, than seeing first-hand, the visitors, scientific research and collections that all of our work is inspired by and working side by side with the teams delivering the visitor experience and events. We also recognise the benefits and flexibility that hybrid working brings. We operate a hybrid working model that requires regular, weekly attendance for this role, with the precise pattern of days on site and worked from home to be agreed with your manager. Due to the nature of this role the work pattern will be 100% on site. How to apply If this sounds like you, please apply on our website. item.title: Head of Income Generation
item.description: GLAN’s mission is to use the law to challenge powerful actors and secure justice for people and communities affected by human rights abuses and environmental harm. Through strategic litigation, advocacy and collaboration with partners, we work to hold those responsible to account and contribute to lasting change. The Head of Income Generation is a significant leadership position at GLAN, responsible for leading our small, high-performing fundraising team and driving the organisation’s income generation strategy at an exciting point in its development. The fundraising team comprises three people, including this role. The successful candidate will join GLAN in the final year of our current three-year fundraising strategy, with an exciting opportunity to help shape and lead the development of our next strategy for 2027–30. With a growing portfolio of new projects and opportunities, this is a particularly important moment for GLAN’s development. We have a strong and established pipeline of committed, long-term supporters across trusts, foundations and philanthropy, providing a solid foundation on which to build. At the same time, GLAN is investing in diversifying its income. Our individual giving programme has recently launched, and 2027 is our first year of participation in challenge events, creating new opportunities to grow our supporter base and develop new sources of income. The Head of Income Generation will lead a multi-income-stream fundraising function, balancing the stewardship and growth of established funding relationships with the development of new opportunities. The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on income generation and relationship management, working closely with programme teams and the Senior Leadership Team to ensure that GLAN’s ambitious work is financially sustainable. This is an opportunity for an experienced fundraising leader to play a central role in shaping GLAN’s next phase of growth, strengthening our financial resilience and helping to ensure that our work can continue to deliver meaningful change.

item.title: Mental Health Service Manager
item.description: Mental Health Service Manager If you have lived experience of mental health challenges and the ability to translate your experience into meaningful service improvement, we want to hear from you. We have an exciting opportunity for a Mental Health Service Manager to play a vital role in providing support in Pathfinder West Sussex. This is a new and exciting role in which you will be supporting the Lived Experience workstream within the Pathfinder West Sussex Mental Health Support Service. Position: Mental Health Service Manager (Internal Job Title: Lived Experience Manager) Location: West Sussex/hybrid (with regular travel around West Sussex) Salary: £36,729 per annum Contract: Permanent Hours: 37 hours per week (Monday – Friday) Closing Date: 14 October 2026 at 23:59 Please note the role may close sooner than advertised if a suitable candidate is found, so apply early! About Pathfinder West Sussex As a Mental Health Service Manager, you will be working for a people-led organisation whose mission and values is to inspire change across Sussex. Pathfinder West Sussex is a partnership of mental health, homelessness and employment support organisations working together to improve people’s wellbeing across the county. Co-production is at the heart of everything we do. This role will be instrumental in supporting staff and subcontractors to embed co-production principles and continuously enhance the way we deliver services. Key Responsibilities: Provide leadership and expert guidance on co-production across Pathfinder services, including line management of the Lived Experience Lead and partnership working with lived experience colleagues across West Sussex Mind. Provide lived experience representation on strategic groups and forums. Lead on the collection and analysis of client feedback and outcomes and link with SPFT lived experience groups and the West Sussex LEAG. To support the Senior Manager in delivering the strategic direction of the service, ensuring service development and continuous improvement are informed and shaped by lived experience perspectives. About You To be successful in the role of Mental Health Service Manager, you will need to have great communication skills and be committed to the values of the organisation. Some of the key skills and experience you will need to bring with you include: Lived experience of mental health challenges and a track record of using personal experience to support continuous service improvement. Experience of representing for client views or experience as a group facilitator or Peer Mentor. Experience of establishing, developing and maintaining effective working relationships with voluntary and statutory partners. Knowledge of local agencies that provide services to people experiencing mental health. Knowledge of coproduction involvement and engagement best practice. The role covers the service area of West Sussex and as such we need someone who lives within a commutable distance of the area. In Return The organisation is proud to have Gold Accreditation from Investors in People, be a Disability Confident employer, and part of the Mental Health at Work commitment. You will also receive: 5.5% stakeholder pension scheme and life assurance Medical cash plan with BHSF Access to Learning & Development platform Free and confidential employee assistance helpline Cycle-to-work scheme Free 28-day Network Saver Brighton bus pass (new starters) Generous holiday allowance (starting at 27 days and rising to 32 with service) Opportunities to participate in wellbeing and fundraising activities throughout the year Join an equal opportunities employer, committed to equality, equity, inclusion, and diversity. Applications are welcomed from individuals with lived experience. Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments if invited to interview. Please Note: An Enhanced with Adults DBS check will be required for this role. Lived experience of mental health challenges is an occupational requirement for this role under Schedule 9, Paragraph 1 of the Equality Act 2010. The role requires the postholder to draw upon their personal experience to provide leadership, influence service development, promote co-production, and ensure the voices of people with lived experience are embedded in the design and delivery of services. You may be interested in this role if you have experience in the following areas Mental Health, Mental Health Advocate, Mental Health Service Manager, Mental Health Service, Mental Health Worker, Mental Health Case Worker, Mental Health Outreach. item.title: Senior Homelessness Prevention and Recovery Worker
item.description: Senior Homelessness Prevention and Recovery Worker We are seeking an experienced homelessness professional to provide intensive, trauma-informed support to people facing rough sleeping and housing instability. Position: Senior Homelessness Prevention and Recovery Worker Location: Charnwood, Leicestershire, with remote and community-based working Salary: £27,110 Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week Closing Date: Friday 16th October We reserve the right to close this advert early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. About the Role This is an exciting opportunity to help shape a new service supporting people who are sleeping rough, have experienced repeated or long-term homelessness, or are at immediate risk of returning to the streets. Managing a small caseload of approximately six to eight people, you will provide intensive, flexible and relationship-based support. You will work alongside each person to secure and sustain suitable accommodation, overcome barriers and develop greater confidence, independence and community connections. Key responsibilities include: Completing strengths-based, trauma-informed assessments and personalised support plans Supporting people with housing, benefits, budgeting, household essentials and daily living skills Helping individuals access health, mental health, substance use and other specialist services Working with local authorities, housing providers, landlords and community partners Responding appropriately to safeguarding concerns, risks and crises Undertaking outreach, home visits and community-based appointments Maintaining accurate case records and contributing to service monitoring and evaluation Advocating for clients and coordinating effective multi-agency support Some occasional evening and weekend work may be required. About You You will have experience of supporting adults affected by homelessness, rough sleeping, housing instability or multiple and complex needs. You will understand homelessness legislation, housing options, tenancy sustainment and adult safeguarding. You will be confident completing assessments, developing support plans and working collaboratively with housing, health, social care and other agencies. An understanding of trauma-informed, psychologically informed or recovery-focused practice would be an advantage. Patient, resilient and non-judgemental, you will be able to build trusting relationships with people who may have experienced trauma, exclusion or repeated disengagement from services. You will combine persistence and flexibility with sound professional boundaries and effective risk management. A full driving licence and access to a vehicle, or another reliable means of travelling throughout Charnwood and Leicestershire, is required. This role is subject to an enhanced DBS check. About the Organisation You will join a small, close-knit charity working to tackle homelessness and help local people build safer, more stable lives. The organisation offers a collaborative and supportive working environment, additional holiday, flexible working and training from day one. You will be encouraged to develop your skills while contributing to a service designed to create meaningful and lasting change. Other roles you may have experience of could include Homelessness Support Worker, Senior Support Worker, Housing Support Worker, Rough Sleeper Outreach Worker, Tenancy Sustainment Officer, Recovery Worker, Resettlement Worker or Complex Needs Support Worker. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, NFP People. #INDNFP

item.description: Are you ready to empower young people aged 18–24 to take their first real steps into employment? Job title: Employment Coach – Northern Futures Salary: £26,239 - £28,554 per annum Hours: Full Time – 37 Hours per week Contract: Fixed term – initially until March 2027 Location: Available posts within the North East Combined Authority region (Co Durham, Newcastle, Northumberland, North Tyneside, South Tyneside, Sunderland & Gateshead) About us Groundwork NE & Cumbria is a long‑established environmental and community charity with over 30 years of experience creating greener, healthier and more resilient places across the region. Our mission centres on Creating Better Places, Improving People’s Prospects, and Promoting Greener Living, helping communities thrive no matter the challenges they face. We deliver hundreds of locally‑led projects each year, including initiatives that support young people into education, training and employment, helping them overcome barriers, build life skills, and reach their full potential. About the role You will be responsible for supporting them through every stage of their journey, enabling participants to address their barriers and realise their aspirations. Within this role you will be required to source new referrals who are predominantly economically inactive; complete the enrolment paperwork, including development plans and eligibility checks. You will also be required to attend events and present the delivery model to referral sources to attract additional referrals. Successful employment coaches believe in the potential of every individual they work with. About You We want someone like you with the confidence to positively engage and motivate people from a wide range of backgrounds. We're in search of individuals who have prior experience in employment coaching, case management, or related fields, ideally with a focus on economically inactive individuals. You will have strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport whilst being empathetic, patient, and proficient in communicating with individuals from various backgrounds. You will be passionate about empowering others to recognise their strengths, overcome obstacles, and achieve their goals. Believing that with the right support and guidance, individuals can take control of their own futures and succeed in the labour market Closing date: Wednesday 30th September 2026 Please note , should we receive a high volume of applications, we may look to close the role early, therefore we recommend an early application. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the Apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. This role is subject to an Enhanced Disclosure endorsed by the Disclosure and Barring Service. We want you to be yourself at Groundwork and we value everything that makes you unique. We recognise and celebrate your difference and together we make Groundwork a special and great place to work. As a Disability Confident employer we offer a guaranteed interview to applicants with a disability who meet the essential criteria for the role. item.title: Child and Family Exploitation Practitioners
item.description: Child and Family Exploitation Practitioners Barnardos Warwick, Warwickshire (On-site) £14.91 per hour Part-time (As and when (0 hours)) Temporary (As and when (0 hours)) Youth and Children Job description Warwickshire Base Warwickshire Base aims: To protect children and young people from exploitation To empower children and young people who are abused through exploitation, or vulnerable to such abuse, to develop strategies that will enable them to reduce harm, and to achieve their potential. To reduce the risk of vulnerable children and young people being abused through exploitation, through awareness raising activities with children, young people, parents and professionals working with children and young people. To work directly with children and young people who are abused through child exploitation. To support the work with parents/carers whose child/ young person is abused through exploitation or vulnerable to abuse. You will be required: Deliver best practice in CSE/CCE and keeping children safe. Provide person-centred 1:1 or group work support to children and young people who are victims of exploitation. Demonstrate a working knowledge of Barnardo's '4 A's model' and trauma-informed responses to abuse. Provide guidance to professionals to help and support children and families navigate the complex systems of social care and criminal justice. Work as part of a co-located specialist team, where appropriate supporting Police operations and maintaining robust information sharing pathways to inform multi-agency responses. Attend multi-agency operational meetings -working with local authorities and other statutory partners and contribute towards robust processes and plans to safeguard children. Work as part of the team to enable the voices of children who have experienced CSE/CCE to be heard throughout the sector to encourage and inform best practice. Enable the voices of parents and carers who are affected by exploitation to be heard to inform support services. Providing advocacy, support and strategies to help manage the impact of exploitation on the family unit and to better able support young people. Signpost and assist children and young people to access services that may best meet their needs. Work in partnership with local authority and other statutory and voluntary partners to support children and young people. Ensure cases are reviewed within the 12-week time frame from start of intervention to monitor progress and achievement. Attend Clinical Supervision to support service delivery and personal and professional development. Contribute towards the effective monitoring and evaluation of the service. You may also be required to support with the supervision of staff members. Organisation We're here to help children and young people feel safer, happier, healthier and more hopeful – and have somewhere they feel they belong. item.title: Advocacy and Complex Needs Advisor
item.description: Advocacy and Complex Needs Advisor Royal British Legion Inverness, Highland (On-site) £29,170 per annum Permanent Job description If you are committed to providing holistic and person-centred support to your clients, and making a real difference in people’s lives, we may be the perfect fit for you! We have an exciting opportunity to join our fantastic ACN team, as an Advocacy and Complex Needs Advisor for our Inverness and Highlandsregion. The Royal British Legion’s Advocacy and Complex Needs Service operates across the UK, offering holistic support to veterans facing complex and often isolating challenges. Our Advisors directly support beneficiaries experiencing homelessness, mental health challenges, issues relating to alcohol and substance use, behavioural addictions, domestic abuse, involvement with the criminal justice system, and other circumstances that may affect the safety and wellbeing of adults, children and their families. Your work will empower the Armed Forces community to achieve their potential and lead more fulfilling lives. We have a number of vacancies across our Advisor team as we are delighted to be enhancing our service offering by increasing the size of our team and adding additional Advisor posts to provide more responsive support to our beneficiaries. item.title: Artist Relations and Events Coordinator
item.description: Artist Relations and Events Coordinator We are seeking a highly organised coordinator to support artist engagements, events and Christian partnerships across the UK. Position: Artist Relations and Events Coordinator Location: Milton Keynes/Hybrid Salary: £32,500 to £34,937 per annum, depending on experience Hours: Full-time, 36.5 hours per week Contract: Initial 12-month fixed-term contract Closing Date: 6 October 2026 About the Role This is an exciting opportunity to join a Ministry Development Team and help deliver artist engagements, strategic partnerships and Christian events across the UK. Working closely with the Senior Partnerships Manager, you will provide high-quality administrative, logistical and operational support. You will coordinate UK and international artist visits, tours, workshops, church engagements and partnership events, making sure every detail is carefully planned and delivered. Key responsibilities will include: Coordinating travel, schedules, resources and communications for artist visits, tours and events Supporting partnerships with churches, Christian networks, festivals and other ministry organisations Maintaining calendars, project plans, budgets, records and databases Liaising with artists, agents, event organisers, churches, partners and internal teams Providing practical support before and during events and engagement activities Monitoring deadlines, milestones and changing requirements Helping to improve administrative systems, processes and ways of working Some travel and attendance at events may be required. About You You will be a proactive and dependable coordinator with excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage several priorities at once. You will bring: Experience coordinating events, visits, tours, workshops or partnership activities Strong administrative and logistical planning skills Excellent written and verbal communication Confidence working with a range of internal and external stakeholders Experience using Microsoft 365, Teams, Zoom and other digital tools The ability to remain calm, flexible and solutions-focused when plans change An understanding of artist, events, partnership or ministry environments Knowledge of the UK church and Christian ministry landscape As an active Christian, you will be comfortable integrating your faith into your work and supporting engagement with churches and Christian audiences. Please note the organisation can only consider applicants who presently have the right to work in the UK and all candidates must be personally committed to the Christian faith and be able to respect, uphold and work within our client’s Christian mission, values, culture and faith statements. This individual will represent and speak on behalf of a Christian charity and as such the Occupational Requirement for an active Christian faith is justified under the Equality Act 2010 Schedule 9, Part 1, clause 3. About the Organisation Join an international children’s charity working with children, their communities, supporters and partners in almost 100 countries. Through long-term development projects, emergency responses and advocacy, the organisation has helped bring lasting change to millions of children over more than 75 years. item.title: Service Manager
item.description: We are seeking a Service Manager to lead a high-performing countywide service supporting individuals with multiple and complex needs across Essex. In this key leadership role, you will oversee day-to-day service delivery, support and develop a skilled team, and work closely with commissioners and partners to deliver high-quality, evidence-based services that empower people to make and sustain positive change. Are you looking for an exciting and challenging opportunity that makes a difference? We have an exciting opportunity for a dynamic and motivated Service Manager to lead a team to provide high quality services for individuals with multiple and complex needs. This can include mental health difficulties, problematic substance use, learning difficulties or any other need if left unmet is likely to increase the risk of reoffending. The support offered includes signposting, onward referrals, liaison with other professionals, advocating on people’s behalf as well as accompanying people to services. As a Service Manager you will be responsible for the day to day running of a highly performing, County Wide service that makes a tangible difference to the lives of those it works with. You will lead a team to develop evidence-based services aimed at empowering people to make and sustain positive change. You will have strategic oversight of the service and will liaise directly with the commissioners and partners across Essex to ensure the highest possible standards of services. About you To join us a Service Manager you will need: Experience of managing staff An understanding of the complex issues presented by individuals who use the service. The ability to build effective working relationships with other professionals (health providers, the police, youth services, mental health & substance use organisations) and to maintain the excellent reputation of Phoenix Futures across Essex and beyond. Experience of working with people within a health/criminal justice/substance use or similar field The ability to report performance data and information to managers and commissioners The ability to be innovative and flexible to meet the needs of the service Determined, with a drive to succeed and a willingness to learn Passionate and enthusiastic about making a real difference to the lives of people we support To be proficient in the use of Microsoft Outlook and Word and be familiar with database management systems Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal So, if you’re seeking your next challenge as a Service Manager, please get in touch or apply today. Your Rewards Starting salary of £30,500 per annum, pro rata. with opportunity to access potential yearly salary increments subject to appraisal, meaning potential salary increase up to £36,000 per annum, pro rata. Committed to providing a Real Living Wage for you, through accreditation with the Living Wage Foundation 25 days’ annual leave plus Bank Holidays (increasing each year to a maximum of 30 days) Benefits including season ticket loan, pension scheme and life assurance Support through occupational sick pay, eye-care vouchers and regular wellbeing talks and activities Continuous training and career development via PXL our dedicated learning management system Access to a 24/7 Employee Assistance programme including telephone and online access A rewarding role with the opportunity to help us support people on their journey to recovery and change their lives for the better. We’ll ensure you get all the support you need to thrive and succeed in your role and find your place amongst our incredible and collaborative team. About Phoenix Futures Phoenix Futures Group is a charity with over 50 years’ experience and a leading provider of drug and alcohol treatment. We use our expertise to support people in their personal recovery and to improve their lives. We are dedicated to advocating for people who are often overlooked and stigmatised, to ensure they have a fair chance to lead healthy and fulfilling lives. Our aim is for everyone to be able to achieve their potential for themselves, their families and communities. We encourage and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and believe it is important to include people with lived experience to ensure the needs of the people we support are represented. We are committed to creating an inclusive working environment where everyone is free to be themselves and we ensure equity of opportunity. Our managers and leaders are guided by a shared set of qualities that shape how we work with colleagues, partners and the people we support. These are: BRAVE , HONEST , VISIBLE , VISIONARY , NURTURING and COLLABORATIVE . These qualities underpin our approach to inclusive leadership, accountability and compassionate practice across Phoenix Futures and support the development of a value aligned culture. Interview Process We want you to feel comfortable to be your best during the interview process, so that you can get to know Phoenix and we can get to know you. All details will be provided in advance so that you can feel adequately prepared, and we can support you with reasonable adjustments as required. Please note, we will be assessing applications as they are submitted and may close this role should we find sufficient applicants with which to make our shortlist. As such, we would advise applying as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

item.title: Welfare Officer - RAF Coningsby
item.description: Our Welfare Officers provide direct and impactful welfare support to RAF personnel and their immediate family. As a trusted and confidential source of support, you will assist our service users with challenges they are facing, from mental ill-health, difficult relationships, domestic abuse, financial and cost-of-living concerns, resettlement, housing, childcare, equality issues, bereavement, military discharge or deployment and many more - no day will be the same, as such this is a great opportunity to develop your knowledge and skills within the Welfare sector. Our intervention is provided with consent on a non-statutory basis, and you will work with and engage our service users to develop appropriate interventions for individual outcomes. Our service is transitioning to become more accessible and inclusive, digital technology plays a key role in this, as such you will use digital technologies to complement and enhance processes and service user experience. You will play an active role within the community, promoting the service through the delivery of presentations and representing the service at public engagement events. You will also work closely with RAF welfare teams, local authorities, health, education, civilian agencies, charities and other military organisations to ensure the best outcome for the service user. About the Team 2025 marked 35 years since SSAFA began delivering an independent non-statutory, and confidential service, for the Royal Air Force community across the UK, and this is an exciting time to be joining as we were successful in our bid to continue delivering this service. We are continuously transforming our ways of working to be innovative, to ensure our service is even more inclusive and accessible to meet the needs of a modern RAF. We are a hard-working team from diverse professional backgrounds. Although we all have our own area of responsibility, we support each other in delivering the best possible service to our military community. Find out more about the Personal Support & Social Work Service on our website. About you To thrive in this role you will have relevant experience of supporting adults, families and children/young people. You will be able to take a flexible and creative approach to problem solving. You will have excellent communication skills and be able to deliver presentations with confidence. You will have used Microsoft Office 365 to a high standard. It is important that you have experience of planning and managing your own workload, with minimal supervision. It would be advantageous if you have experience of carrying out assessments, preparing plans, monitoring and reviewing outcomes. There will be some travel required and therefore you will need to be able to drive and have access to your own car. About SSAFA SSAFA, the Armed Forces charity is a trusted source of support for the Armed Forces community in their time of need. In 2024 our trained teams of volunteers and employees helped more than 54,000 people, including veterans, serving personnel (regulars and reserves) and their families. SSAFA understands that behind every uniform is a person. And we are here for that person and their family, any time they need us and in any way they need us. Diversity and Inclusion at SSAFA SSAFA exists to support a diverse range of beneficiaries within the armed forces community, and we believe diversity within our teams is key to ensuring we can deliver our services effectively. We thrive on differences and believe it is critical to our success as a worldwide charity. SSAFA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace that seeks to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people from a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We therefore encourage applications from all genders, races, religions, ages and sexual orientations, as well as parents, veterans, people living with disabilities, and any other groups that could bring diverse perspectives to our business. SSAFA is committed to using the Disclosure & Barring Service to ensure we, as an employer, safeguard those we serve. Closing date: Midnight on Sunday 04 October 2026. SSAFA reserves the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. Interviews: TBC

item.title: Weekend Support Assistant
item.description: About the role: Weekends can be a particularly important time in supported accommodation. With fewer services open and less structure around the day, having a consistent, trusted member of staff available can make a real difference to someone’s wellbeing, confidence and ability to keep moving forward. As a Weekend Support Assistant at St John’s Mansions, you’ll provide practical, person-centred support to residents, helping them build the skills and confidence they need to live more independently. Working from agreed support and risk plans, you might help someone manage their money or accommodation, access appointments and community services, develop everyday living skills or stay engaged with activities and goals that matter to them. You’ll also play an important role in keeping the service safe and well coordinated throughout the weekend. You’ll respond to changing needs, safeguarding concerns and unexpected situations, maintain accurate records and make sure important information is clearly handed over to the wider team. You’ll need to be approachable and compassionate, while also confident in setting boundaries, using your judgement and knowing when concerns need to be escalated. You’ll join an experienced team where you can develop your knowledge of supported housing, safeguarding, recovery-focused practice and working alongside people experiencing multiple disadvantage, with access to training, supervision and ongoing development. We have two roles available, 1x 37.5 hrs per week and 1x 22.5 hrs per week. Exact working patterns will be discussed in interview. About you: You can build positive, respectful relationships with people while maintaining clear professional boundaries. You’re able to encourage and motivate people to build confidence and independence, rather than simply doing things for them. You can stay calm, think clearly and respond appropriately when situations change or become challenging. You’re organised and reliable, with the ability to prioritise work, communicate clearly and keep accurate records. You understand, or are keen to develop your understanding of, homelessness, mental health, trauma, substance use and the barriers people can face when trying to move forward. About us: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important info: Closing Date: Tuesday 6th October at midnight Interview date: Thursday 15th and Friday 16th October online via Microsoft Teams Please note there will be a second stage interview in Islington for suitable candidates This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed (by SHP) for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.title: Research Steering and Involvement Coordinator
item.description: The DRSGs bring together researchers, healthcare professionals, and people living with or affected by diabetes to identify research gaps, shape research priorities, and drive activity that improves the lives of people affected by diabetes. Through workshops, reports, funding recommendations, and collaborative projects, the DRSGs help ensure that diabetes research is both scientifically rigorous and informed by lived experience. The bulk of this role focuses on coordinating the smooth running of the DRSG and related activities, including managing the shared inbox, scheduling meetings, preparing agendas and papers, recording high-quality minutes, and acting as a key point of contact for members. Beyond these core responsibilities, you will play an active role in supporting projects and helping shape member involvement as the DRSG evolves. This includes co-facilitating discussions, tracking qualitative and quantitative insights, helping identify and engage peer reviewers for highlight notice applications, and supporting a range of Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) activities. You will also work closely with the Grants Advisory Panel (GAP), a panel of people affected by diabetes who contribute to funding decisions, and support wider research initiatives, including the Type 2 Prevention Research Challenge. By ensuring our steering groups and PPI panels run efficiently, you enable researchers, healthcare professionals, and people affected by diabetes to collaborate effectively. Success in this role means delivering seamless administrative control, capturing the impact of DRSG outputs, and ensuring patient voices directly influence research priorities. An ideal candidate will combine high-level organisational skills with experience or understanding of biomedical research and the UK research landscape.
item.dc:creator: Diabetes UK

item.title: Research and Outcomes Officer
item.description: Remote/London (must be able to attend the London office at least twice per month if remote working) Permanent | Part-time (4 days / 28 hours per week) £44,358 (London-based) / £39,587 (non-London-based) FTE + excellent benefits Join our Research & Outcomes team at the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists (RCSLT) and help shape the future of speech and language therapy. You’ll plan, deliver and evaluate projects that strengthen research capacity, capability and culture across the profession, champion evidence-based practice, and support members in making the most of outcomes, health informatics and data. Who we are The RCSLT is the professional body for speech and language therapists across the UK. The RCSLT has over 24,000 members and employs around 65 staff predominately based in a London office. The RCSLT also has offices in Belfast, Edinburgh, and Cardiff. Our mission is to improve the lives of people with communication and swallowing needs by facilitating and promoting research, producing guidance, holding events, and influencing government. We aim to promote better education and training for speech and language therapists and provide information to our members and the public about speech and language therapy. The role As a Research & Outcomes Officer, you’ll play a key role in shaping and delivering the RCSLT’s research and outcomes work, helping to strengthen research culture, champion evidence-based practice and support the profession to make better use of evidence and data. You’ll take operational responsibility for a varied portfolio of projects and initiatives, from research priority setting and engagement, to collecting and analysing data, supporting evidence synthesis and monitoring impact. You’ll also help bring this work to life through engaging communications across RCSLT research channels, as well as presentations, webinars, conferences and events. Working closely with RCSLT members, colleagues and external stakeholders, you’ll provide expert, evidence-based advice on research, outcomes, clinical and professional issues, while responding to enquiries and supporting teams across the organisation to identify, understand and apply research evidence. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys combining research, project delivery, data, communication and stakeholder engagement, and who wants to make a tangible difference to the future of speech and language therapy. What we are looking for We’re looking for a qualified Speech and Language Therapist and current RCSLT member with strong clinical and professional knowledge and a passion for research and evidence-based practice. You’ll have experience of literature searching, critical appraisal and evidence synthesis, alongside knowledge of research, evaluation, outcome measures and data analysis. You’ll be confident turning complex evidence and data into clear, accessible insights and communicating these effectively to a range of audiences. You’ll be highly organised, analytical and adaptable, with the ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities. A collaborative approach is essential, as you’ll work with members, colleagues and external stakeholders to provide expert guidance and support. Above all, you’ll be committed to using research and evidence to improve practice and outcomes, championing equality, diversity and inclusion, and contributing positively to the RCSLT’s aims and values. What we can offer you A competitive starting salary Generous annual leave entitlement Excellent staff training and development opportunities Supportive and flexible working environment including, hybrid working arrangements Generous Pension scheme Life insurance cover Season Ticket Loan scheme Eye care voucher scheme Family friendly employer including enhanced maternity and paternity leave Cycle to Work scheme Access to an Employee Assistance Programme and more! How to apply For more information and to apply, please visit our careers portal. Closing date: 9.00am on Monday, 19 October 2026. Interview date: w/c Monday 2 November 2026 (held virtually). There may be a task that will be needed to be completed as part of the interview process. We are committed to a fair, transparent, and inclusive recruitment process. All applications are handled with strict confidentiality to protect your privacy and encourage openness throughout the process. The RCSLT is committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace where everyone feels valued and a sense of belonging. We aim to embed equity, diversity, and belonging practices throughout our recruitment and selection procedures. We strive to ensure everyone is valued equally for their contribution, experience, knowledge, and skills. We welcome applications from candidates of all different backgrounds.

item.title: Head of Influence, Insight and Communications
item.description: The Role This is an exciting time to join Starlight. We already have considerable expertise across influence, insight and communications and a strong platform from which to build. Recent opportunities with broadcasters, parliamentarians and other influential audiences demonstrate the potential to take Starlight's voice further. The Head of Influence, Insight and Communications will bring these strands together, working with talented colleagues to spot, shape and amplify opportunities that advance our ambition to end preventable trauma in children's healthcare. As we enter the next phase of Starlight's development, with our new strategy to end preventable trauma for children in healthcare, our focus is on increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of our influencing work. Our aim is to build on our strong existing capability, bringing together complementary specialist teams to create greater strategic impact, stronger external influence and an even more integrated approach to delivering our mission. This new Influence, Insight and Communications role brings together the existing influencing, insight and communications teams, recognising the significant overlap between strategic communications, public affairs, campaigns, insight and organisational influence. The role will provide strategic leadership across these disciplines, enabling Starlight to connect research, lived experience, policy engagement and communications around organisational priorities, and maximise our external impact. The role will sit within the Play in Healthcare team, reflecting the shift in emphasis of our communications and marketing activity towards influencing, campaigning and systems change. It plays a critical part in making children's experiences visible, amplifying the voices of children and families, and building understanding of why emotionally safe healthcare matters. Reporting to the Director of Play in Healthcare, and working closely with the Director of Income Generation & Engagement, the postholder will bring together Starlight's existing expertise in influence, insight and communications to translate evidence and lived experience into compelling narratives, policy positions, thought leadership and strategic communications that strengthen Starlight's reputation, influence decision-makers and support organisational growth. The postholder will identify, shape and amplify opportunities to position Starlight as a trusted voice on children's healthcare experiences and the role of play in supporting children's wellbeing, development and emotional safety. About Starlight Starlight is the national charity for children's play in healthcare. We believe that healthcare should be a more humane and child-centred experience for every child. We work across the UK to champion the importance of play during treatment, care and recovery, supporting children, parents and carers, and healthcare professionals. Our ambition is to end preventable trauma in children's healthcare.
item.dc:creator: Starlight Children's Foundation

item.title: Social Care IDVA
item.description: Are you looking for a dynamic and rewarding role working for an organisation with the feminist agenda at the core of its ethos? Then Advance Charity could be the career choice for you! We are looking for a Social Care IDVA Salary: £28,000 - £35,000 (salary dependent on skills and experience and whether you are a qualified IDVA) Location: LBHF Children Social Care (Kings Street) and Hammersmith Head Office. You will be in the colocation 3 days per week depending on the service's need, this is subject to change if need in colocation increases. Contract: Permanent Hours: 35 hours per week, 9am-5pm standard hours with occasional duty between 1-9pm done from home This post is open to female applicants only as being female is deemed to be a genuine occupational requirement under Schedule 9, Paragraph 1 of the Equality Act 2010. Please note: Any offer of employment will be made subject to references, confirmation of the right to work in the UK, and satisfactory enhanced DBS check. About us Advance is an award-winning and innovative women-only organisation, established in 1998, providing emotional and practical support to women and girls survivors of domestic abuse and supporting women with short-term sentences to reduce offending. We believe in empowering women and girls to lead safe, non-violent, equal lives so that they can flourish and contribute to the community. We are a community-based organisation who lead in best practice approaches to supporting women in their local community. We achieve this by being available to meet and support women in local settings and at our women’s centres, and by working in close partnership with other agencies. Our values are to listen and support, to empower and respect, collaboration, innovation, and accountability. About the role: You will be co-located at LBHF Children Social Care Offices and will be directly supporting victim/survivors known to children's services. You will manage a caseload, deliver training and consultations to social care professionals and help raise their awareness, identification of and response to those experiencing domestic violence. Working jointly with Social Workers on cases you will support service users and improve partnership responses. You will provide high-quality telephone or face to face crisis intervention, information, advocacy and support to women referred to the service, in respect to risk management and safety planning, criminal and civil remedies, housing, health, welfare rights, and children’s legislation. About You: You will be an experienced IDVA with an excellent understanding of domestic violence and its effects on women and children and of best practice within the domestic abuse in various areas of need, with particular knowledge on children safeguarding/legislation. As an experienced domestic violence advocate who has worked with complex and multiple needs, you will be skilled in risk management and safety planning, remaining calm in a crisis and in handling sensitive information on a daily basis. Experience of direct work with female survivors of domestic violence, of supporting women with child safeguarding, needs, and of working within safeguarding procedures is essential for this post, as is the need to adopt and promote a strong partnership approach to service provision. Your abilities extend to assessing the needs and risks of survivors, carry out short and longer-term risk management, safety planning and support and identify and refer to services appropriate to their needs. Advising women of their rights and options for seeking help and support from other agencies and proactively advocate to ensure barriers to accessing support and protection are reduced. You will work as an advocate and educator to raise awareness and upskill professionals within Children Social Care plus work with colleagues to successfully develop and deliver training. How to apply: Please submit your up-to-date CV with a supporting statement. Please note that only applications made via the job advert on the Advance careers page, and those that include a cover letter will be considered. Closing Date for Applications: Sunday 4th October 2026 @23:59 Interviews are taking place on a rolling basis and we may close the advert early if we identify a suitable candidate so we recommend early application What we can offer you - Employee Benefits: A 35-hour working week An exceptional 30 days of paid holiday per year (pro rata for part time), PLUS public holidays on top (that's nearly 40 days paid holiday per year!) Additional days off to celebrate International Women’s Day, and for religious observance and moving home Perkbox - an employee discount platform where you can receive free rewards as well as take advantage of savings on clothes, groceries, travel, leisure and more Pension scheme Enhanced maternity/adoption provision Access to our Employee Assistance Programme Employee eye-care scheme Clinical supervision for front line staff and first line management roles Refer a Friend Scheme - £250 for each referral who passes probation Organisation wide away days Thorough induction and training Career development pathways ************************************************************** Under the Equality Act 2010, we are required to make any reasonable adjustments. If you have a disability as defined under this act and/or have special needs, please email the Talent Acquisition Team via the Advance website and we will aim to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate your needs. Diversity, Inclusion and Equal Opportunities We are committed to providing equality of opportunity and actively seek to recruit people from groups underrepresented in our current team. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay and benefits. Safeguarding Advance is committed to safeguarding and creating a culture of zero-tolerance of harm and expects all staff, including volunteers to share this commitment. We believe all individuals have the right to live their life free from violence and abuse and the right to feel and be safe. We have a suite of safeguarding policies, procedures and practice guidance, accessible to all staff, which promotes safeguarding and safer working practices across all our services and activities. When we recruit staff, we follow rigorous safer recruitment practices, this involves carrying out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks, and identity checks. We ensure all staff undertake mandatory safeguarding training relevant to their role and responsibilities, to empower them to be competent and feel confident in recognising and responding appropriately to safeguarding issues and promote wellbeing.
item.dc:creator: Advance

item.title: Humanitarian trainee - Communications
item.description: Role: Humanitarian Trainee: Communications Hours: Full-time Pay: £35,000 GBP gross per annum Duration: 18 months (with possible extension dependent on funding) Location: UK-based with international deployment Are you looking to kickstart your career in the humanitarian sector? Is your ambition to develop towards leadership roles in humanitarian work? And are you willing to work hard, learn by doing, and contribute to humanitarian work by doing everything it takes to deliver lifesaving health emergency responses? UK-Med is a frontline medical aid charity. Born of the NHS, we’ve been working for over 30 years towards a world where everyone has the healthcare they need when crises or disasters hit. We are excited to launch our Humanitarian Trainee Scheme, offering three distinct trainee roles in the areas of MEAL, Communications and Human Resources & Membership. The Humanitarian Trainee Scheme presents an unparalleled learning opportunity for early-career professionals who are committed to a career in humanitarian work. It is an opportunity to accelerate your development towards future leadership roles in the humanitarian sector. The Humanitarian Trainee Scheme consists of an 18-month pathway designed to provide in-depth exposure to humanitarian health programming through a structured professional development plan. You will embed within a team, gaining practical experience and contributing actively to its work and priorities and those of the wider organisation, both at Headquarters and in the field. Alongside this, you will undertake formal and informal professional development through training, mentoring, shadowing and on-the-job learning. The traineeship is a structured development opportunity and is not intended to fill an established role within UK-Med’s organisational structure. As a trainee, you will: Embed within a team at UK-Med Headquarters, gaining practical experience while contributing to our wider humanitarian preparedness and activities. Deploy internationally to assist in delivering humanitarian health responses. Participate in tailored training, mentoring, shadowing and on-the-job learning to build your skills, knowledge and experience. You will have relevant qualifications or equivalent professional experience, with an established technical foundation in your chosen field. Some professional and international experience is essential, alongside a strong interest in applying your existing skills and developing your career within the humanitarian sector. How to apply We strongly recommend that you read the Candidate Information Pack - Humanitarian Trainee - Communications - Sept 2026 before applying for this role. To apply, please submit a current CV and answer the application questions : Please apply below, as soon as possible and no later than Thursday 8th October 2026. Our selection process is designed to understand your potential, motivation and suitability for the Humanitarian Trainee Scheme, as well as the skills and experience you would bring to your chosen pathway. Shortlisted candidates will first be invited to an online interview. Following the interview stage, selected candidates will then be invited to attend an in-person assessment in Manchester. The assessment will include a range of individual and/or group activities designed to explore your skills, approach and potential. The in-person assessment is expected to take place on the 19th of November in Manchester. If you progress to this stage, you will be expected to attend in person, so we encourage applicants to keep this date available where possible. UK-Med will provide further information regarding the assessment and associated travel/logistical arrangements to candidates invited to this stage. Please note: Due to the nature of this role, candidates must be deployable without the need for additional visa applications to Schengen countries. This requirement is essential for operational reasons to ensure swift and efficient deployment in humanitarian settings, enabling timely and effective responses to crises. Applications for work in the UK can only be accepted from people with an existing right to work in the UK. UK-Med is committed to safeguarding of our personnel and beneficiaries and has a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse. We conduct thorough vetting before any appointment is confirmed. UK-Med is committed to the principles of diversity, equality, and inclusion. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive environment where employees feel respected and supported to be able to fulfil their potential.
item.dc:creator: UK-Med
