item.title: National Corporate Fundraising Manager
item.description: Purpose of Role - We are seeking a National Corporate Fundraising Managers who as part of our Fundraising Team will be responsible for securing and developing high value, national corporate partnerships to help air ambulance charities save even more lives across the UK. This role is a mix of new business and account management and is designed to give the role the best possible development and growth opportunities. Key Deliverables - Partnership Delivery: Ensure all partnership activities (campaigns, events, employee engagement) are executed effectively and on time. Monitor and report on partnership performance against agreed revenue targets KPIs. Growth & Development: Identify opportunities to extend and deepen partnerships through additional fundraising, sponsorship, or strategic initiatives. Win new national corporate partners with potential of 6 figure donations per annum Work with partners to co-create innovative campaigns that align with their own goals Internal Collaboration: Coordinate with marketing, communications, and program teams to deliver impactful campaigns and activations. Prepare reports and presentations for senior leadership and partners. Financial Management: Track income and expenditure for each account, ensuring accurate forecasting and reporting. Monitoring and Evaluation Monitor, evaluate, and report on partnership development and cultivation. Development of outcomes and impacts reports CRM Maintain an up-to-date CRM and provide revenue forecasts and pipeline reports as and when required Strategy Keep up to date with the latest developments in the charity sector and corporate fundraising identifying key opportunities for AAUK. Other Represent and be an ambassador for AAUK. Work to support AAUK ‘s vision, purpose, values, goals, and priorities. Be flexible and carry out any other associated duties that may arise, develop, or be assigned. Support and promote diversity and equality of opportunity in the workplace. Comply with legal requirements for fundraising and general activities including GDPR, The Fundraising Code of Practice and others. A full, clean driving licence and access to a car is required to fulfil the deliverables of this role. Air Ambulances UK Air Ambulances UK (AAUK) is the national charity supporting the lifesaving work of the UK’s air ambulance charities, enabling them to save even more lives every day. The Air Ambulance community attends 50,000 emergency missions every year, in many cases we are the difference between life and death. We are a dynamic and growing team, and this is a fantastic opportunity to make a massive difference to a much-loved organisation. Application Process If interested, please provide CV and covering letter. Due to the number of applications, we receive for such roles we are unable to respond to unsuccessful applicants. item.title: Campaign Manager, First Light
item.description: About us Royal Museums Greenwich (RMG) is a collection of diverse historical sites. The sites are the National Maritime Museum, Cutty Sark , the Royal Observatory, and the Queen’s House. Each of these sites has a unique identity and a common purpose to serve our communities, through sharing our collections and expertise. We are a place to explore the sea, space, art and history, and our strategy ‘Charting Our Course’ puts people at the core of its success. First Light The Development Team secures vital funding to support core programming and public engagement, exhibitions, collections care and major capital projects at Royal Museums Greenwich. We work with philanthropists, companies and trusts & foundations, building a community of generous and loyal supporters from our Patrons Circle and legacies to major grants and corporate partners. Our current focus is to secure a team target of £2M revenue income in this financial year, and deliver the funding needed to deliver First Light, a landmark capital transformation of the Royal Observatory Greenwich. First Light is an £85M project to deliver an ambitious schedule of much needed repair to the unique built heritage, vital capital improvements to the site plus an embedded programme of activities to build the nation’s science capital. A focus on physical, cultural, intellectual and financial access will ensure that everyone can enjoy, and benefit from, all the Observatory has to offer. Aiming to break ground winter 2025 and reopen in spring 2028, First Light will affirm the Royal Observatory as THE centre for the public understanding and enjoyment of astronomy - a place of awe and wonder. This is an exciting time to join the Development Team as we begin to plan a high-profile public campaign, seek to secure a principal gift to close the campaign and liaise with our ambassadors to build our reach and reputation. The Role Reporting to the Senior Manager: Development Business Operations, the Campaign Manager, First Light will deliver vital fundraising activity in support of this capital campaign - working with colleagues to maximise fundraising opportunities, engage supporters and ensure the successful delivery of campaign events, communications and donor engagement activity. Key responsibilities include to lead delivery of the First Light fundraising campaign to agreed objectives and timescales through the creation of fundraising materials and webpages and the delivery of a successful public fundraising campaign. The role will manage regular campaign communications for all stakeholders, co-lead on the organisation and delivery of a gala fundraising dinner in 2027 and coordinate major donor meetings and events for the campaign. There is also the opportunity to travel through the management of a fundraising visit to the USA in 2027. The successful candidate will have demonstrable experience of planning and delivering events. They will have excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks. They will also have excellent written and verbal communication skills, as well as strong teamworking skills, with the ability to build productive working relationships. This is a full-time, fixed term role until 30 June 2028 in Band 5 - Management and Proficient Specialists. Core hours of work will be 36 hours per week, Monday to Friday between 9am - 5pm, with an additional hour to be agreed upon with management. Occasional evening and weekend working will be required to ensure the successful delivery of First Light campaign events. Salary : £38,568 per annum. Prospective candidates are encouraged to read the attached Job Description and Person Specification before applying. Please be aware that we are unable to sponsor visas. Please also note that due to our commitment to internal opportunities for current staff, internal candidates will be considered first for this role. Interviews are pencilled in for the week commencing Monday 5th October. Benefits We offer: • A generous pension scheme • 22 days annual leave (rising to 25 after 1 year) plus bank holidays • 40% discount in our cafés, 30% in our shops • Interest-free loans (travel, bike, gym, learning) • Free Life Assurance Scheme covering you for 2 times your annual salary • Free entry to exhibitions at partner museums and galleries • Flexible and hybrid working options • A culture that celebrates individuality, collaboration, and innovation To find out more, read a full list of our benefits. EDI Diversity and inclusion are integral to our work at Royal Museums Greenwich, as we are a museum for everyone. We want to foster a spirit of inclusion, collaborative working, innovation, and valuing people as individuals whose lives have been shaped by different experiences. Therefore, we welcome applications from everyone. We actively work with Disability Confident scheme and ask that you let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments you need or things you would like us to know during the interview process, which may include being provided with the interview questions in advance, requiring a step free interview space, that you are eye-contact avoidant, or having the interview questions in a written format or additional time in timed tests, interviews or other assessment activities.

item.title: Community Engagement Practitioner
item.description: At Hestia, we are guided by our core values and are dedicated to fostering an equitable, diverse, and inclusive organisation. Our mission is to empower individuals to rebuild their lives and achieve independence. Right now, we are looking for a Community Engagement Practitioner to play a pivotal role in our Voluntary Community Sector service in Islington, London Sounds great, what will I be doing? You will work as part of a multidisciplinary NHS team alongside clinicians, social workers, and community partners to support adults with moderate to severe mental illness. Holding a caseload of service users, you will act as their key contact, contributing to care planning, monitoring progress, and supporting safe discharge using the RiO clinical records system. Together with service users, you will develop person-centred recovery plans focused on social goals and community integration, building strong therapeutic relationships through trauma-informed and strength-based approaches. You will help individuals access local resources, attend appointments, and engage in wellbeing activities, peer support, and psychoeducational groups. Collaboration is central to the role, as you will liaise with statutory and voluntary organisations, attend clinical meetings and community events, and advocate for recovery-focused, jargon-free communication. You will ensure accurate documentation, uphold safeguarding and health & safety standards, and actively participate in supervision, training, and professional development. What do I need to bring with me? You'll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires as well as match our values and mission. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you're willing to learn. We also value lived experience of the areas we support, so if you feel comfortable, please do mention this on your application. Here's what the team will be looking for We are looking for someone with NVQ Level 4 in Care (or equivalent) or at least two years' experience in a mental health setting. You will bring a strong understanding of mental health issues, recovery, and co-production principles, alongside experience of working collaboratively with professionals, services, and communities. Knowledge of care planning, risk assessment, recovery tools, and the Mental Health Act is essential, as are excellent communication, relationship-building, and group facilitation skills. You should be confident using IT systems, resilient and adaptable, able to work independently or as part of a team, and committed to person-centred, trauma-informed practice. Interview Steps We keep our interview process simple, so you know exactly what to expect. Shortlisting call: We have a team of dedicated recruitment specialists who will speak to you about your experience, motivations and values. They will also tell you about all the great work we do! Face to face interview: Now you will have face to face interview with the hiring manager. Our interviews are value and competency based. Interviews will be held in person on 14th October Don't be alarmed if there are other stages in the process, it's all part of the plan for some of our roles. Our commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion Our services users come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds because it makes us stronger. We are committed to creating and maintaining a diverse and inclusive workforce and value the skills, abilities, talent and experiences, different people and communities bring to our organisation. We are a disability confident employer Hestia is proud to be a disability confident employer, dedicated to the employment and career development of individuals with disabilities. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for all applicants with disabilities who meet the minimum criteria for the role they have applied for. We also provide reasonable adjustments during the selection and interview process, and throughout your employment with us. Safeguarding Statement Hestia is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults, children and young people who are potentially at risk, and we therefore expect all staff and volunteers to do the same. We require all staff to undertake internal and external safeguarding training throughout their employment with Hestia. Important Information for Candidates If your application is successful, please be aware that you will be required to undergo pre-employment checks before a formal offer of employment can be confirmed. We reserve the right to close this job advert early should we receive a high volume of applications or if the position is filled before the closing date. We encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible to ensure their application is considered.

item.title: Triage and Brief Intervention Worker
item.description: Triage and Brief Intervention Worker Galop City Of London, England (Hybrid) £29,453.65 (including London weighting of £4,296.25) per year Contract Human Rights Job description About the role The role will work to assess the needs and eligibility of people referred to the Pan-London LGBT+ Domestic Abuse service, ensuring potential risk or safeguarding issues are identified. The Triage and Brief Intervention Worker will be responsible for completing triage assessments, one-off brief interventions with people who are assessed as low-medium need or referring into Galop’s advocacy services or partner agencies for advocacy and support. The work will involve offering them a conversation to find out about their situation, completing triage assessment paperwork and either referring them into the relevant service that will meet their needs or providing short term support, signposting and safety planning. Your triage work will enable people referred into our service to feel heard, supported and access the advocacy that they require. You will need excellent listening and communication skills, with the ability to obtain the information you need to assess a case while leaving clients feeling supported. Most importantly, you need the capacity and understanding of the broad spectrum of needs that victims and survivors of domestic abuse may present with and be able to provide non-judgemental support at all times. The role is based in Galop’s central London building but hybrid working is available (with an expectation of two days a week in the office). National candidates will be considered on remote contracts, however please note that wherever candidates are based, this role requires some travel to and across London for cross-partnership working and mandatory training opportunities, as well as all-staff days and events. For more information on this role please download the attached job description. Location Galop’s offices are located in London. Hybrid working is available, but the post holder will be expected to be based in the Galop offices 2 days per week if they are on a London contract, Hours Full-Time (35 hours a week) Contract Fixed term until 31 March 2027 (continuation after this point subject to additional funding) Reports to Senior IDVA Salary Starting salary £29,453.65 inclusive of London Weighting Closing Date 11th October 23:59 Questions? If you have any questions or would like to discuss the role further prior to application, please contact [email protected] . item.title: Corporate Partnerships Manager
item.description: Job description About The Role What could you achieve when two organisations with a shared purpose come together? As our Corporate Partnerships Manager, you’ll lead the day-to-day development and delivery of our partnership with The FA. This is a high-profile, high- value partnership. You’ll work across both organisations to build trusted relationships, bring people together and turn ideas into action. The aim? To deliver income, impact and value for everyone involved. Could you take an ambitious idea and turn it into something that works in practice? You’ll bring commercial thinking, project management and a clear external focus to a partnership that reaches audiences across the country. You’ll work with colleagues across Alzheimer’s Society and The FA. This will include operational teams, as well as senior and executive stakeholders. You’ll be based at The FA’s Head Office at Wembley Stadium at least one day a week. You’ll also have regular opportunities to meet partners and colleagues face to face across the UK. Location: This role is contracted as hybrid. You will spend time working from home, at our London office and attending the FA office in Wembley Stadium at least one day a week. You will be regularly meeting partners and stakeholders in person. Occasional UK travel should be expected. Contract: This is a 12-month fixed term contract covering maternity leave Interviews are provisionally scheduled to take place on the week commencing the 12th October via MS Teams. What you’ll do You will take ownership of the partnership’s strategy, relationships and delivery, ensuring it continues to grow in value, profile and impact. - Lead and deliver the partnership plan, objectives, KPIs and measures of success. How will you make sure the partnership continues to grow while delivering what’s already been promised? - Identify opportunities to grow the partnership through income, campaigns, events, employee engagement, advocacy, audience reach and in-kind support. Where could you spot an opportunity that others might not have seen? - Build trusted relationships across The FA and Alzheimer’s Society. Become a credible and solutions-focused point of contact. How will you bring different people and priorities together around a shared goal? - Turn ideas into clear plans. Coordinate multiple teams, deadlines, dependencies and risks. When there are lots of moving parts, how will you keep everything moving in the right direction? - Lead high-profile events, campaigns, communications and other partnership activity. - Use insight, feedback and performance data to understand what’s working and shape next steps. What could the data tell you about where the partnership should go next? - Manage partnership income, budgets and KPIs. Provide accurate forecasts and recommendations. - Create compelling proposals, presentations and impact reports that bring the partnership to life. Can you turn an idea or opportunity into a story that gets people behind it? - Work with specialist teams on contractual, data, brand and compliance requirements. - Share learning across Corporate Partnerships and contribute to our wider approach to purpose-driven partnerships. Could you help turn the reach and influence of football into meaningful action for people affected by dementia? This role gives you the opportunity to help shape what that looks like. About you We are looking for a commercially minded partnership professional who combines excellent relationship management with disciplined delivery. You may have developed your experience in the charity, sport, public or private sectors. You’ll bring: - Strategic project and partnership management skills, with the ability to manage complex activity, multiple workstreams, deadlines, risks, budgets and KPIs. You’ll also keep sight of the bigger picture. - Influencing and relationship management skills, with the confidence to build trust, navigate different perspectives and work credibly with senior and executive stakeholders. Can you build relationships that help people see what’s possible, even when priorities differ? - Experience of strategic partnership growth, with the ability to spot opportunities and connect partner priorities with purpose. You’ll understand how this can create income, impact, reach and shared value. - The ability to work effectively across organisations and teams. You’ll bring people together around shared goals and keep activity moving when priorities, perspectives and dependencies differ. - A proactive and solutions-focused approach. You’ll be comfortable challenging constructively, navigating ambiguity and making sound decisions. - Clear and compelling written and verbal communication skills. You’ll be able to create proposals, presentations, reports and briefings for different audiences. - Financial and organisational skills, including managing budgets, forecasting, tracking KPIs and using CRM systems. - A genuine interest in business, corporate partnerships and creating meaningful change for people affected by dementia. What could you bring to a partnership with the reach of The FA? You might already have experience in corporate partnerships. Or you may have built your career managing complex projects, relationships or commercial opportunities in another setting. Knowledge or an interest in football would be welcome, but it isn’t essential. What matters most is your ability to build relationships, spot opportunities and create strategic partnerships that deliver meaningful results. Could this be the opportunity to use your partnership skills to create change that reaches millions of people? If you’re excited by the potential of this partnership and share our commitment to making a difference, we’d love to hear from you. About Alzheimer's Society Dementia is the UK's biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer's Society, we're the UK's leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding groundbreaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we're working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. Our commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging We need to ensure the voices around our table better reflect and understand the communities we exist to serve. We strongly encourage individuals to apply who have a disability, impairment or health condition or individuals who identify as Black, Asian or from another minority ethnic background, as these groups are currently under-represented at Alzheimer's Society. We want everyone we work with, as a colleague, volunteer, supporter, or someone we support, to feel included and that they belong at Alzheimer's Society. Our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy here along with our internal employee forum and Employee Lived Experience network groups help us promote inclusion and belonging, becoming an engaged and inclusive organisation for all our people. Our hiring process During your recruitment process we want to make sure that you bring your whole self and can be at your best. We are working hard to ensure our recruitment process is as inclusive as possible, so please do inform us of your experience and anything you think we could do better by completing our candidate survey when you apply. Please also contact Alzheimer's Society Talent Acquisition Team via [email protected] for application support or any adjustments you might need. To ensure fairness and consistency to select the best candidate for this role, all our applications are anonymised up until an interview has been confirmed. We recognise the benefits of AI, but if you're considering using it to submit your application, we encourage you to reflect on the value it truly adds. AI tools often lack the personal touch and authenticity that set candidates apart. We want to hear your unique perspective, experiences, and skills, so we encourage you to showcase them in your own voice. We try to avoid closing roles early where possible, however if we receive a high volume of applications, we may close earlier than the advertised closing date. Should this occur, we will aim to provide you with at least 48 hours' notice. We are committed to safer recruitment and ensuring the welfare of those we work with, due to the nature of some of our roles, we might need to carry out a Criminal Record Check at the relevant level. You can read more information via our Website. Giving back to you Our employees work hard every day to make a true difference in people's lives. We are proud to support them with a range of benefits, recognition and many options for working agilely, all contributing to a strong work life balance. We also have various learning programmes to support you in your development and help you grow to realise your potential and shape a career with Alzheimer's Society. You can also visit our Working for Us pages, which give you more information about what it's like to be an employee at the Society. item.title: Advice Casework Manager
item.description: This is an exciting opportunity to lead IRMO’s Advice service. As Advice Casework Manager you will oversee both immigration and welfare & housing casework, managing casework allocation and maintaining rigorous standards across all work. You will provide line management, support staff development and oversee monitoring and evaluation to create accurate reports for funders and senior management. You will also manage a personal caseload, in line with your previous experience. IRMO’s Advice service provides trusted information, resources, advice and casework in Spanish and Portuguese on key areas of need, including immigration, welfare entitlements, housing and homelessness prevention. IRMO is accredited by the Advice Quality Standard (AQS) and the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) at Level 3. We are also members of Advice UK and receive second-tier support from Southwark Law Centre. As part of our Advice for All partnership, you will oversee the delivery of our Advice Workforce Development Programme, working in close collaboration with our partner organisations. This includes supporting the training and development of year-long cohorts of immigration and welfare & housing trainees, as well as strengthening the skills and practice of our existing advice workforce. To succeed in this role, you’ll bring strong experience as a senior caseworker and line manager, with a track record of delivering high-quality advice against targets and communicating impact clearly. You’ll be confident in managing people and priorities, with a leadership style that brings out the best in your team. You’ll also have a strong understanding of the barriers Latin Americans face in accessing immigration, welfare, housing, health and other essential services in the UK, and a genuine passion for advancing the rights and welfare of migrants and refugees.

item.title: Public Affairs and Campaigns Manager
item.description: Shelter Cymru is looking for an individual with experience of working in public affairs and campaigns to join us in the newly created role of Public Affairs and Campaigns Manager. In this role you will lead our engagement work with external stakeholders such as political figures, contribute to the running of campaigns, and line manage two members of staff. At a time when the housing emergency in Wales is negatively impacting people and communities across the whole of the country this is a fantastic opportunity to be at the heart of the Fight for Home, and to be directly involved in securing the changes necessary to ensure everyone in Wales can access a safe, secure, suitable and genuinely affordable home. You will work alongside a range of expert colleagues in Shelter Cymru's Campaigns Team, including those focused on external communications, policy development and lived experience engagement. About you You will be an experienced campaigner who has a track record of delivering impactful campaigns and securing changes to policy and legislation in Wales. Ideally, you will have direct experience of working with the Senedd and the Welsh Government, accompanied by an understanding of the role that public campaigns can play in driving change. Experience of working in campaigns or advocacy for an organisation that offers front line service provision would also be welcomed. While prior experience in housing or another social justice area is desirable it's more important that you share our commitment to ending the housing emergency in Wales. And our belief that change must be focused on achieving outcomes for the people that are currently experiencing the daily realities of Wales' broken housing system. If you are interested in this role and would like to discuss it in more detail then we are happy to arrange a conversation with Robin White, Head of Campaigns.

item.title: Professional Learning Quality Lead - FTC until Dec 2027
item.description: The Chartered College of Teaching is currently working on a number of exciting projects, and is recruiting a Professional Learning Quality Lead to support this work. This is a fixed term position which will focus on supporting the delivery of a key strand of our work relating to teacher development, helping to embed high quality professional development across the sector. By joining our team as a Professional Learning Quality Lead, you’ll be helping us to support teachers, champion great teaching and raise the status of the profession. The role will run until the end of December 2027 in the first instance. Job Title: Professional Learning Quality Lead Reports to: Associate Director, Professional Learning and Accreditation Direct reports: Project Officer (TBC) Salary: £40,000-£45,000 per annum dependent on experience Contract: Fixed term until 31st December 2027 Hours: A full working week is 35 hours and we offer flexible working options. We are open to full-time or part-time candidates (min. 3.5 days/0.7 FTE) Benefits: Flexible working, generous annual leave, 8.5% employer pension contribution, Paycare, individual and team professional development/learning budget. A full list of our benefits can be found here . Based: Home based or office based, with hybrid-working options. Start date: ASAP (by November 2026) Deadline and interview: Applications will close on Sunday 4th October 2026. The interview will consist of a task and competency-based questions. Interviews are currently planned to take place w/c 12th October 2026 but we will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis and may interview and close the role earlier if a suitable applicant is identified. Application: Please apply by uploading your CV and cover letter. Please use the guidance when writing your cover letter. We encourage you to apply promptly as we will be reviewing applications as they are received. The Organisation The Chartered College of Teaching is a charity and the professional body for teachers. We are working to empower a knowledgeable and respected teaching profession through membership and accreditation. We are dedicated to bridging the gap between practice and research and equipping teachers from the moment they enter the classroom with the knowledge and confidence to make the best decisions for their pupils. Our activities mainly focus on four key areas: membership teacher CPD and accreditation research, policy and events online and print resources Since opening membership in 2017, we have grown rapidly. In total our work reaches ~40,000 teachers and more than 3.6 million young people. We are a growing and multi-skilled team of 35 people, supported by a Board with a significant track record and experience in a range of fields. Our business plan focuses on growing membership and Chartered Status, strategic positioning of the College in the education sector, and providing meaningful professional learning opportunities for the teaching profession. The Opportunity The Professional Learning Quality Lead will play a key role in supporting our work around teacher development, helping to embed high quality standards for teacher professional learning across the education sector. Drawing on their deep understanding of teacher development, the Professional Learning Quality Lead will lead on a number of internal and external projects, working with colleagues and sector stakeholders to develop and launch a CPD quality framework. They will deliver training, develop resources and carry out quality assurance activities to support the successful implementation of the framework in schools, colleges and sector organisations. Alongside this, they will support the delivery of the Chartered College of Teaching’s wider professional development offer, developing and reviewing materials and delivering training that is aligned to agreed quality standards, helping to support teacher and school development and career progression. This would be an ideal opportunity for anyone who is passionate about teacher development and who wants to use their knowledge to build expertise and shape quality standards across the sector. Role description Establishing CPD quality standards and quality assurance processes You will lead on the development and implementation of a new CPD quality framework, which will include: Initial development and testing of an evidence-informed framework for CPD quality Seeking input from experts and key stakeholders via a range of consultation activities (e.g. advisory groups, focus groups, surveys) Developing effective processes to quality assure CPD in line with the newly developed framework, underpinned by robust policies and governance processes Developing and delivering training and implementation resources to support the rollout of the framework, helping to ensure the framework is understood and applied consistently Working with partner organisations to quality assure their professional development offer in line with agreed standards Developing training materials You will spend some of your time working on developing and reviewing CPD materials to support the College’s wider CPD offer. This might include: Designing and delivering CPD sessions for teachers and school leaders Designing or contributing to the development of new and existing online courses and content Reviewing and evaluating existing provision, identifying opportunities for further improvement Wider responsibilities You will have the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues from across the organisation, and will champion the framework and the high standards it sets for teacher CPD, within and beyond the College. You will also be expected to: Plan and coordinate work activities for the projects you are responsible for, ensuring that work is completed on time and within budget Provide direct line management for a Project Officer who will support day to day administration of project activity during the project mobilisation period (up to the first 6 months) Engage in CPD, learning activities and training to maintain and develop your knowledge and skills Arrange and participate in meetings, as required Perform other activities as and when required in order to fulfil the purpose and requirements of the role Represent the College at external events (occasional travel may be required) About You We’re looking for someone who is enthusiastic and knowledgeable about teacher and school development; who is motivated by our mission and who is truly passionate about supporting the education sector. The person specification below outlines the essential and desirable knowledge, skills and experience we are looking for in this role. You will need to meet the essential knowledge and experience as a minimum, and at least two of those indicated as being ‘desirable’. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and encourage you to apply. Essential knowledge and experience Educated to at least degree standard, with QTS and experience of teaching in schools in the UK Proven knowledge and understanding of effective professional development methodologies Critical understanding of research and evidence relating to teacher professional development and implementation Experience of designing and/or delivering teacher professional development Able to engage and communicate effectively with a range of stakeholders, including educators, sector leaders, funders and partners Able to organise information and communicate complex ideas in a systematic and coherent way Desirable knowledge and experience Experience leading and/or quality assuring teacher professional development across a school, trust or in a relevant education sector organisation Experience of developing frameworks and/or standards (e.g. quality assurance frameworks, CPD frameworks, assessment frameworks, professional standards, qualifications frameworks) Understanding and/or experience of governance, including developing and monitoring policies and processes Experience of leading or managing projects, including understanding how to manage timelines and budget Have undertaken further study relevant to the role e.g. Masters, Chartered Teacher Status, relevant NPQs, other relevant courses or qualifications As well as the requirements outlined above, we are looking for people who: Believe in the transformative power of education, see teachers as key drivers in achieving improved educational outcomes for all and are motivated to contribute to this change Communicate clearly and effectively, understanding the importance of conveying complex ideas in an easy to understand way and respecting the work schedules and patterns of colleagues Learning and feedback oriented, intellectually curious, and keen to develop their skillset Are committed to equality and diversity, demonstrating these through their work and daily interactions with colleagues, members and other stakeholders. Why Us? As an organisation we care deeply about creating a working environment that supports our people to grow personally and professionally. These are reflected in our organisational values which outline the distinctive working culture we are looking to create. In particular, these values are reflected in our commitment to: Flexible working: responsive management, flexible hours, hybrid or fully remote working Professional development, including formal and informal training and support Transparency and ownership: we have an open culture that ensures all staff guide our strategic direction Mental health and wellbeing: access to health and wellbeing advice and health cash plan. Diversity and inclusion at the Chartered College As a growing organisation we are committed to: Becoming increasingly representative of the sector and geographies that we operate in Providing a positive experience of work as part of an inclusive culture led by our organisational values Maintaining an annual EDI action plan - led by the internal team. item.title: Partnership Advisor (Scotland)
item.description: About Hearing Dogs for Deaf People National charity Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, trains dogs to transform the lives of deaf people and provides hearing loss services – because nobody with hearing loss should feel alone. About the role We are seeking a compassionate, proactive, and organised Interim Partnership Advisor to join our Partnership Support Team on a full-time basis. You’ll manage a defined geographic area covering Borders, East, North East and Highlands. Responsible to: Partnership Support Area Manager. Based: Community based in Scotland (covering Borders, East, North East and Highlands). Contract: Permanent, full-time. Key Responsibilities Companionship – Supporting Thriving Partnerships: Provide long-term, person-centred advice, guidance, and wellbeing planning to partnerships within an allocated regional area. Ensuring all recipients feel they are treated with attention, courtesy and respect. Manage a caseload of partnerships, ensuring regular in-person visits (once per quarter after the first 6 months) and ongoing tailored support via multiple channels. Develop and implement partnership support and wellbeing plans, with robust risk management measures. Support the integration of new partnerships into the local community, delivering monthly support throughout the first 6 months. Lead on retirement and bereavement pathways, offering planning, preparation, emotional support, and signposting to alternative Hearing Link Services (HLS) where appropriate. Provide behavioural guidance and targeted interventions to maintain healthy, successful partnerships. Connection – Building Community and Networks: Organise and attend local community events to strengthen relationships and engagement. Deliver peer-based community programmes that bring together partnerships and Peer Support Volunteers to share experiences, insights, and encouragement. Facilitate support groups for hearing dog partnerships, encouraging shared learning, problem-solving, and mutual encouragement. Work collaboratively with internal teams, volunteers, and external agencies—including support workers, local councils, employers, and veterinary practices—to remove barriers and improve outcomes. Advocate Partnership Volunteer Updates to maintain volunteer engagement and connection. Confidence – Empowering Partnerships to Flourish: Focus on quality of service and partnership outcomes, adapting support levels to meet individual needs. Provide timely emergency cover and practical assistance within the allocated territory, with ad hoc support to neighbouring counties as required. Conduct thorough root cause analysis to identify underlying issues and implement early interventions through targeted coaching and problem-solving. Apply person-centred, evidence-based decision-making to manage partnership breakdowns, returns, cases, and alerts effectively. Conduct annual assessments of each partnerships performance and wellbeing to review ongoing requirements and verify continued compliance with accreditation standards. Keep partnership records accurate, current, and reflective of evolving needs. Capture and share impactful stories to showcase the value and outcomes of our work. Maintain and continually develop expertise in hearing loss, assistive technology, hearing awareness, dog training, and canine wellbeing. Join team events, meetings, and training at regional locations and Hearing Dogs centres, with occasional overnight stays to connect, learn, and collaborate. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise You will need full UK Driving Licence and willingness to travel within and around Borders, East, North East and Highlands, and to our centres. Knowledge: Canine Behaviour & Training: Up-to-date knowledge of canine training practices, behaviour reinforcement, and emotional wellbeing support. Task-Related Assessment: Ability to monitor and evaluate a dog’s task performance, identifying and addressing lapses. Hearing Loss & Deaf Awareness: BSL Level 2 or above with strong Deaf awareness. Partnership Development: Understanding of person-centred support approaches and the user experience throughout the partnership lifecycle. Organisational Policies & Standards: Knowledge of HR policies, GDPR, equality legislation, and Assistance Dogs International (ADI) standards. Skills: Behavioural Guidance: Provide advice on maintaining and reinforcing behaviours, resolving challenges, and refining training plans. Listening & Empathy: Demonstrate strong listening skills, emotional intelligence, and compassion, especially when working with vulnerable people or those experiencing grief. Relationship Building: Establish and maintain trust-based relationships with partnerships, volunteers, and stakeholders. Problem-Solving & Conflict Resolution: Apply solution-focused methods, coaching, and mentoring to resolve partnership or task issues. Root Cause Analysis: Identify and address recurring challenges by working with internal teams on sustainable solutions. Time Management & Organisation: Manage multiple partnerships and initiatives effectively, meeting deadlines and priorities. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work productively with colleagues across different departments and functions. Communication: Adapt communication style for different audiences; communicate clearly across teams, stakeholders, and volunteers. Storytelling: Create engaging communications about partnership journeys for updates and stakeholder engagement. Driving: Hold a valid driving licence and be able to travel within the allocated territory. Behaviours: Self-Conduct: Lead and motivate others, holding self and others accountable while maintaining professionalism. Person-Centred Mindset: Tailor support and training to the unique needs, learning styles, and abilities of each partnership. Community Building: Foster a sense of belonging by creating opportunities for partnerships and volunteers to connect and collaborate. Accountability & Reliability: Deliver on commitments, meeting organisational and partnership expectations. Continuous Learning: Maintain professional development in canine behaviour, hearing loss, and assistive technologies. Professionalism: Act respectfully, reliably, and with integrity in all interactions Benefits: Employee Assistance Programme Death in Service Payment Annual leave enhancements recognising long service Day off for your birthday Defined contribution group personal pension plan Enhanced sick pay Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay Eye care Hearing tests Learning and Development opportunities Discounts on merchandise at Hearing Dog gift shops Pet Dog Policy Closing date: 23rd October 2026. This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 due to its duties involving the protection of children and/or adults at risk. Applicants are therefore required to disclose all spent and unspent convictions, cautions, warnings, and reprimands, as well as any relevant non-conviction information. The successful candidate will be required to undertake a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check in accordance with the Police Act 1997 (Part V).

item.title: People Operations Lead
item.description: Your mission CALM is entering an exciting period of change, with a bold new strategy and big ambitions for the future. As our People Operations Lead, you’ll play a key role in creating the people experience, culture and infrastructure we need to make those ambitions a reality. Your profile About You You are a proactive, detail-obsessed People Ops professional who loves bringing order, structure, and care to people and processes. Highly empathetic yet resilient, you excel at balancing a high volume of operational tasks with sensitive employee relations work. You take pride in being a trusted sounding board for managers, have a natural curiosity for people, data and systems. You are passionate about creating a trusting, inclusive workplace where people feel motivated and supported. Responsibilities Employee Experience Champion CALM’s culture and values, using employee feedback and data to optimise an exceptional employee experience, from recruitment to offboarding. Collaborate with the Operations Team to continuously evolve workplace practices and productivity to meet the changing needs of the organisation and our people. Operational Excellence & Flawless Administration Own end-to-end people operations and systems with meticulous attention to detail. This includes maintaining HR platforms (Personio, Culture Amp, Notion), managing salary benchmarking, keeping policies both compliant and relevant. Ensure flawless, reliable administration across every touchpoint of the employee lifecycle. Manager Empowerment & Employee Relations Work with our HR partners to provide expert guidance on complex employee relations issues, equipping and coaching managers to navigate sensitive people matters confidently, professionally, and with care. Internal Comms Act as an excellent written and verbal communicator across CALM, leading the clear and engaging communication of policies, benefits, and workplace updates, ensuring teams remain informed and connected. Qualification A relevant HR qualification, ideally CIPD Level 5 or equivalent. We would also consider candidates with a Level 3 qualification who can demonstrate exceptional practical experience and expertise in people operations and employee experience, alongside a commitment to continuing their professional development. Experience Experience delivering flawless attention to detail in a fast-paced and busy environment. Strong practical experience across People Operations and the employee lifecycle. Experience providing HR advice and managing employee relations matters, including grievance and disciplinary processes. Experience supporting and coaching managers to confidently handle people-related situations. Experience developing and improving people processes, policies and systems. Experience using data and feedback to identify insights and drive improvements. Experience partnering with Hiring Managers and recruiters to provide an exceptional candidate experience. Experience working with HR systems such as Personio, Culture Amp or similar platforms. Excellent working knowledge of UK employment law and current HR best practice. Competencies People-centred & pragmatic: You genuinely care about people and are motivated by creating an excellent employee experience. You balance empathy with sound judgement and practical action. Inclusive: You actively seek different perspectives and are committed to creating an environment where people feel valued, respected and able to contribute. Organised: You deliver a high standard of work while managing competing priorities. Adaptable: You’re comfortable working in an organisation with evolving needs. Continuous improvement mindset: You naturally look for ways to make things better and more effective, using insight to guide your approach. Why us? Reports to: Operations Director Contract: Permanent Benefits: Unlimited annual leave, Healthcare cash plan, 6% pension contribution, therapeutic services (after completion of probation), hybrid working & nine day fortnight Based: London Waterloo twice a week (Wednesdays and Thursdays) / Remote Working (Mon, Tues & Fri), 9.30am - 5.30pm. Salary: £45k - £52k per annum. We benchmark our salaries to ensure our pay structure remains fair, transparent, and equitable for everyone in our team. Applications will close on Thursday 1st October and are reviewed on a rolling basis; we encourage interested candidates to apply early. About us We’re Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM), and we’re united against suicide. We’re a suicide prevention charity, on a mission to help people end their misery, not their lives. We run stigma-smashing campaigns, offer loads of digital tools and resources, and run a life-saving helpline - all designed to help people find hope and a way forward. We are - united against suicide. Don't meet every requirement? We’re still interested. Research shows that people from marginalised groups – including women, LGBTQ+ people, people from global majority backgrounds, disabled people, and those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds – are less likely to apply for a role unless they meet the full criteria. At CALM, we know that skills and potential come in many forms, and that diverse perspectives and lived experience of mental health or suicide can be just as valuable as formal qualifications. If you're passionate about our mission but your experience doesn't tick every box, we'd still love to hear from you. You could be exactly who we're looking for. Safeguarding We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people, and adults at risk, both offline and online. We recognise that harm can occur in physical, digital, and virtual environments, and we take our safeguarding responsibilities seriously across all areas of our work.

item.title: Mass Participation Coordinator
item.description: Hours: 35 per week Location : London based at our Old Street office with regular office attendance. Travel to fundraising and industry events required Salary: £32,585,37 per annum plus £5023.71 London Weighting Contract: Fixed term until 30th April 2027 Closing Date: Sunday 4th October 2026 at 11:30pm Do you have some experience of working in a charity, fundraising or events environment, plus a real desire to learn more about charity events and develop a career in fundraising? Then join Shelter as a Mass Participation Events Coordinator and you could soon be playing a vital role at the heart of our Community and Events team, helping to deliver our flagship Walk for Home event this winter in London, and supporting Shelter’s participation in some of the UKs leading challenge events. About the role This coordinator role sits within our Mass Participation team in our Income Generation directorate. The role supports participants in mass participation events – both organised by third parties including the London Marathon or bespoke Shelter events that you will have responsibilities for. The main objective of the co-ordinator role will be to deliver challenge and bespoke events, from planning and set up, pulling together financial budgets to meeting supporter recruitment and income targets through to the delivery of event day and evaluating results. This role will give you the exciting opportunity to work on our busy third-party programme, enabling delivery of events including London Marathon, London Landmarks Half Marathon and the Hackney Half and support the development of new bespoke products. This role is a fantastic opportunity to gain experience across a variety of mass participation events with the chance to be involved in event delivery, supporter stewardship and volunteer management for some of the most prestigious events in the charity calendar. About you You will enjoy collaborating and communicating with a wide range of stakeholders, and have experience designing and working across customer journeys with multiple touchpoints. You will bring strong attention to detail and a proactive, solutions-focused approach to your work. You will have a proven track record of delivering against financial targets, with experience in monitoring performance and reporting on progress. Good time management and organisational skills are important for this role as there’s a lot to do, it’s important to be able to manage your time effectively. The team has a great positive attitude in supporting with this and can suggest different tools and methods to help you stay on top of your work. Apply to be part of our team and be the change you want to see in society. Benefits We offer a wide range of benefits, including 30 days of annual leave, enhanced family friendly policies, pension and interest free travel loans. Our employees also have access to a tenancy deposit loan, payroll giving, cycle to work scheme and an employee assistance programme. Shelter helps millions of people every year struggling with bad housing or homelessness through our advice, support and legal services. And we campaign to make sure that, one day, no one will have to turn to us for help. We’re here so no one has to fight bad housing or homelessness on their own. We are happy to talk about flexible working, personal growth, and to promote a workplace where you can be yourself and achieve success based only on your merit. About the team This role sits within our Mass Participation team, which supports participants in challenge events organised by third parties (e.g., the London Marathon) and bespoke Shelter events (e.g., Walk for Home). We’re part of Community and Events, which in turn is part of a wider department - the Income Generation directorate - which focuses on a variety of types of fundraising. The team is welcoming, supportive, and keen to meet you. We work hard but try to have fun as well. How to Apply Please click ‘Apply for Job’ below. You are required to submit your work history and a supporting statement. Please provide specific examples of how you meet the criteria in the 'About you' section of this advert, following the STAR format, and ensure you demonstrate how you address the behaviours below throughout your responses: We work together to achieve our shared purpose We prioritise diversity and have an inclusive and open mindset Any applications submitted without a supporting statement or work history won’t be considered About Shelter Home is a human right. It’s our foundation and where we thrive. Yet everyday millions of people are being devastated by the housing emergency. We exist to defend the right to a safe home. Because home is everything. We need ambitious, passionate people to join us. This is your chance to play a part in the fundamental change we are striving to achieve. Our enemy is the social injustice at the core of the escalating housing emergency. To win this fight, we must be representative of the people we are here to help and those who support our movement. In all our people decisions, we take pride in being inclusive, equitable and transparent. We are committed to combating racism both within and outside Shelter. We welcome you on our journey to becoming truly anti-racist. Safeguarding statement Safeguarding is everyone's business. Shelter is committed to protecting the health, wellbeing and human rights of those we support, and enabling them to live free from harm, abuse and neglect. All our staff will be expected to observe professional standards of behaviour and conduct their work in line with our Safeguarding Policies. Shelter does not accept unsolicited CVs from external recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them. *This role is offered on a fixed-term contract for six months from start date, and is not expected to be extended beyond the initial contract term.

item.title: Area Manager
item.description: We are looking for a dynamic, passionate and performance-driven Area Manager for Staffordshire, to lead and manage commissioned services for all victims of crime, including domestic abuse (all risk levels) and anti-social behaviour. The local services also work with those who harm through both the behaviour change and restorative justice services. All services support both adults and children/young people, and offer professional training, awareness and engagement activity. There are dedicated services to support domestic abuse victims/survivors within Safe Accommodation and at Family Court. This role is full time, regular travel across the area is required and attending Area Manager and other Victim Support events that may be outside of area. A good understanding of domestic abuse, trauma and the Criminal Justice service is essential. What we offer At Victim Support, we are committed to attracting and retaining the best talent. Our competitive rewards and benefits package includes: Flexible Working Options: Including hybrid working. Generous Annual Leave: 28 days plus Bank Holidays, increasing to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave. Birthday Leave: An extra day off for your birthday. Pension Plan: 5% employer contribution. Enhanced Allowances: Enhanced sick pay, maternity, and paternity payments. Exclusive Discounts: High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment, and leisure discounts. Financial Wellbeing: Access to our financial wellbeing hub and salary-deducted finance. Wellbeing Support: Employee assistance programme and wellbeing support. Inclusive Networks: Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes. Sustainable Travel: Cycle to work scheme and season ticket loans. Career Development : Ongoing training and support with opportunities for career progression. About the Role As Area Manager you will oversee delivery of high-quality services across Staffordshire. This includes: Oversight of Operational Managers and the overall performance of the various services commissioned Developing service delivery/improvement plans and social value plans for each of the services Managing service budgets and identifying income generation and/or fundraising opportunities to support business development Driving continuous improvement of performance through use of data and other information to ensure teams perform to the highest standards at all times Building and leading external relationships promoting positive working relationships to ensure joint working and pathways that lead to the best possible standard of support and outcomes for service users Ensuring we listen to and co-design services to meet the needs of our service users, to a standard expected of our commissioners and partners. You will develop and maintain effective relationships and formal partnerships with key stakeholders, attending strategic boards for domestic abuse and community safety. You will strategically lead on local service promotion and development. You will be responsible for service compliance with national Victim Support service delivery standards and best practice guidelines; plus a range of external accreditation standards, such as Safelives Leading Lights. You will represent the charity in an appropriate and professional manner to commissioners, stakeholders, external bodies and the media, whilst acting as a voice for victims to the wider community. Key Responsibilities ensure high quality, efficient and responsive services to service users income growth and partnership opportunities building relationships with commissioning bodies and other stakeholders team development, and the monitoring of performance and quality good understanding of government policy in regard to VAWG, Criminal Justice and community safety Please note that travel across Staffordshire is an essential part of this role and you may be asked to work unsociable hours on occasion. You must be able to attend in person meetings with commissioners and partners as well as attending offices regularly to meet with the local teams. About Us Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required. At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minoritised communities. As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process. How to apply To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible.

item.title: Supported Housing Services Manager (FTC)
item.description: This is a fixed term contract of 3 months, for 21 hours per week. The Supported Housing Service Manager is responsible for leading and managing supported housing services, ensuring high-quality, safe, and person-centred support for residents with diverse needs, including mental health, young people, and LGBTQ+ individuals. Key aspects of the role include: Providing both strategic oversight and operational management to ensure services are compliant, effective, and aligned with organisational objectives and contractual requirements. Embedding trauma-informed and psychologically informed approaches across services, enabling residents to develop independence, improve wellbeing, and achieve goals in employment, training, education, and life skills. Leading service performance, development, and growth while maintaining strong relationships with commissioners, landlords, and other stakeholders. Ensuring financial sustainability, regulatory compliance, and delivery of positive outcomes for residents. The Services Service 1 - Mental health supported housing service: Adults living with moderate to severe mental health conditions, many of whom have experienced trauma, social exclusion, homelessness, substance misuse or other complex needs. Some residents may present with behaviours associated with their mental health, including heightened anxiety, emotional dysregulation, suicidal ideation, self-neglect or periods of crisis. The successful candidate must be comfortable working within these settings. Service 2 - LGBTQ+ supported housing service. We provide both shared and self-contained accommodation, commissioned by LB Haringey, offering housing and tailored support to LGBTQI+ adults aged 25 and over. This service supports individuals who may face challenges within mainstream homelessness provision due to their sexual orientation or gender identity, as well as those who have expressed a preference to live within an LGBTQI+-specific environment. Our Organisation Causeway is a London living wage employer, with a competitive pension scheme. We also offer an employee assistance programme that provides free financial, legal, and mental health advice and support to our employees. We provide core training, and continuous learning and development throughout your career with us.
item.dc:creator: Causeway Irish Housing Association

item.title: Training Manager - Modern Slavery
item.description: At Hestia, we are guided by our core values and are dedicated to fostering an equitable, diverse, and inclusive organisation. Our mission is to empower individuals to rebuild their lives and achieve independence. Right now, we are looking for a Training Manager to play a pivotal role in our Modern Slavery Innovations Team in London Sounds great, what will I be doing? As Training Manager, you will lead the development and delivery of CPD-accredited modern slavery training programmes for corporate partners, frontline professionals, businesses and public sector organisations. Working closely with the Modern Slavery Innovations Manager, Corporate Partnerships team and a Lived Experience Co-Facilitator, you will create impactful, survivor-informed training, guidance and resources that influence policy, strengthen organisational responses and generate sustainable income. This is an exciting opportunity for a confident trainer and relationship-builder to expand Hestia's training offer, develop new business opportunities, manage key stakeholder relationships and ensure survivor voices remain at the heart of everything we do. The role is part time, three days per week hybrid working with travel across London and the UK. What do I need to bring with me? You'll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires as well as match our values and mission. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you're willing to learn. We also value lived experience of the areas we support, so if you feel comfortable, please do mention this on your application. We are looking for an experienced and engaging training professional who is passionate about tackling modern slavery and creating meaningful change. The successful candidate will have a proven track record of designing and delivering high-quality training programmes, both in person and remotely, to diverse and large audiences, with the confidence to engage stakeholders at all levels. You will be skilled at translating complex research, policy and legislation into clear, practical guidance and recommendations, with a strong understanding of modern slavery legislation, including the National Referral Mechanism, Home Office frameworks, and wider compliance requirements. We are seeking someone with excellent project, customer and stakeholder management experience, including managing corporate partnerships, delivering contractual commitments, and meeting challenging timelines. Strong organisational, administrative and budgeting skills are essential. A qualification in Training Delivery and sales or business development experience would be highly advantageous. Most importantly, you will be a collaborative relationship-builder with exceptional communication skills, a high standard of written and spoken English, and a willingness to travel across the UK to deliver impactful training that helps organisations identify, prevent and respond to modern slavery. Interview Steps We keep our interview process simple, so you know exactly what to expect. Don't be alarmed if there are other stages in the process, it's all part of the plan for some of our roles. Our commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion Our services users come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds because it makes us stronger. We are committed to creating and maintaining a diverse and inclusive workforce and value the skills, abilities, talent and experiences, different people and communities bring to our organisation. We are a disability confident employer Hestia is proud to be a disability confident employer, dedicated to the employment and career development of individuals with disabilities. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for all applicants with disabilities who meet the minimum criteria for the role they have applied for. We also provide reasonable adjustments during the selection and interview process, and throughout your employment with us. Safeguarding Statement Hestia is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of adults, children and young people who are potentially at risk, and we therefore expect all staff and volunteers to do the same. We require all staff to undertake internal and external safeguarding training throughout their employment with Hestia. Important Information for Candidates If your application is successful, please be aware that you will be required to undergo pre-employment checks before a formal offer of employment can be confirmed. We reserve the right to close this job advert early should we receive a high volume of applications or if the position is filled before the closing date. We encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible to ensure their application is considered. Shortlisting call: We have a team of dedicated recruitment specialists who will speak to you about your experience, motivations and values. They will also tell you about all the great work we do! Face to face interview: Now you will have face to face interview with the hiring manager. Our interviews are value and competency based.

item.title: Senior Fundraising Officer
item.description: Senior Fundraising Officer (Hybrid) 💰 Salary: £38,057.68 📆 Contract: Permanent We also offer: 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) and a discretionary Christmas closure Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay policy Private GP Service Salary sacrifice schemes for gym, bicycles, annual leave buying, and nursery/childcare Free Premium Headspace membership Financial, life and leadership coaching Life Assurance policy of 3x annual salary Access to free online, in-person or telephone therapy 📍 Location: Head office (Fivefields, 8-10 Grosvenor Gardens, London) with occasional travel to our reserves typically two days per week, the remaining 3 days from home. 🕑 Hours: 9:00am – 5:00pm, with flexibility available from day one. Role & Responsibilities Join us in bringing London’s wildlife back At London Wildlife Trust, we’re working to restore wild places and reconnect people with nature. We need more people to join us, support our work and take action for nature recovery across the capital. This role sits at the heart of that ambition, with a particular focus on growing our membership. You’ll lead the day-to-day delivery of our acquisition programme, working with external agencies and colleagues across the Trust to deliver effective campaigns and hit ambitious targets. You’ll be someone who enjoys looking at the numbers as much as the creative. You’ll use data, audience insight and campaign performance to understand what’s working, spot opportunities and continually improve our approach. You’ll also have the chance to test new channels, develop propositions and explore new ways to recruit members. Alongside acquisition, you’ll contribute to wider membership and individual giving activity, including supporter engagement, fundraising appeals and legacy marketing. If you’re an experienced fundraiser or marketer who enjoys combining creative thinking with analysis and practical delivery, this is an opportunity to make a real difference to how we grow support for nature recovery in London. What you’ll be doing Lead the day-to-day delivery and development of LWT’s membership acquisition programme. Develop our face-to-face recruitment programme, working with external agencies to monitor performance, identify opportunities, improve quality and maximise return on investment. Develop digital acquisition activity, working with the Digital Marketing Lead to plan campaigns, test audiences and creative, monitor performance and identify opportunities to scale. Explore and test new acquisition channels and approaches. Support the planning and delivery of cash fundraising opportunities throughout the year, and legacy marketing activity. Work with colleagues across the team to ensure new supporters have a strong experience from the point of acquisition to welcome, retention and development journeys. What we’re looking for Proven experience delivering successful fundraising, marketing or acquisition campaigns, ideally within a charity, membership or similar organisation. Confidence using data, audience insight and campaign performance to evaluate activity, make recommendations and improve results. Experience working with external agencies or suppliers and building effective relationships with stakeholders. Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple campaigns and priorities and deliver to deadlines. A genuine interest in connecting people with nature and growing support for London Wildlife Trust’s work. (Please see job description for full person specification) Closing Date: Monday 12th October at 9am Interviews: First interviews are scheduled to take place on either Thursday 22 October or Monday 26 October and reasonable adjustments will be offered to all candidates. Does this sound like you? We’d love to hear from you! Our vision is a London alive with wildlife, with nature in everyone's neighbourhood. To achieve our goal of inspiring everyone to help restore London’s wildlife, we recognise that our team must better reflect and represent all of London’s diverse communities. Find out more about London Wildlife Trust’s commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion here: https://www.wildlondon.org.uk/jobs . We are also committed to ensuring that the safety and wellbeing of children, young people and adults at risk is at the heart of our engagement with people. Read about our commitment to safeguarding here: https://www.wildlondon.org.uk/safeguarding . REF-231022
