item.title: Programme Manager: Strengthening Activists and Defenders (STAND)
item.description: ABOUT OUR ORGANISATION Womankind Worldwide is a global women's rights organisation working in partnership with women's rights movements and organisations to transform the lives of women and girls. We strengthen and support women's movements in our focus countries in Africa and Asia, and take collective action at regional and global levels, to ensure women's voices are heard, their rights are realised, and their lives are free from violence. Currently, Womankind has staff based in Kenya and the UK. This position can be based in Kenya or the UK. You must have the right to work in either Kenya or the UK to apply for this role, in line with the laws and regulations of these countries. ABOUT THE STAND PROJECT Strengthening Activists and Defenders: A Global Feminist Initiative to Strengthen Women Human Rights Defenders (STAND) is a Norad-funded, three-year project working across six countries (Afghanistan, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nepal, Uganda and Zimbabwe) to protect and strengthen feminist movements of Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs) in a climate of shrinking civic space and rising anti-rights backlash. Womankind leads the STAND partnership, working with seven implementing partners including AWN (Afghanistan), EWLA (Ethiopia), YWLI (Kenya), WHR (Nepal), WIPC (Uganda) and WCoZ (Zimbabwe). Role Purpose: The STAND Programme Manager leads the day-to-day coordination of the STAND partnership at Womankind, ensuring the project is delivered to a high standard across all six countries, on time, within budget and in line with donor requirements. Working closely with the seven STAND partners and Womankind's Grantmaking and Feminist Partnerships (GFP), Fundraising & Marketing (F&M), Finance, Policy and Advocacy (P&A), and Communications teams, the role holder coordinates, financial monitoring, programme reporting, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) implementation and cross-country learning. Strategic, contractual and high-risk matters are escalated to the Director of Grantmaking and Feminist Partnerships. The role ensures that feminist, safeguarding and risk-aware approaches are embedded throughout the project, working in coordination with relevant Womankind's teams. Areas of responsibility: Programme and Partnership Management Lead day-to-day management and coordination of the STAND project at Womankind, Coordinate the sub-grant lifecycle with STAND partners, Coordinate and deliver the project events, building cross-country solidarity and exchange between partners. Lead the internal coordination and project management of STAND, bringing relevant teams together, clarifying responsibilities, and documenting and communicating progress, risks and learning to colleagues and leadership. Coordinate cross-regional learning with Regional Managers to strengthen Womankind’s grantmaking and partnership practice. Donor Compliance, Finance and Risk Management Coordinate donor reporting and compliance, working with Fundraising and Marketing, Finance and partners to ensure accurate and timely submissions. Oversee programme budgets, expenditure, forecasts and grant amendments, escalating significant financial or compliance issues. Maintain effective project management, risk and audit systems, including risks arising from insecure and restrictive operating contexts. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Coordinate implementation of the project's MEL framework with the MEL Manager, supporting partners to establish baselines, track results and use evidence to strengthen delivery. Coordinate the planning and delivery of STAND shared learning spaces and partner convenings in close collaboration with the MEL Manager and Regional GFP Managers and the Advocacy Manager. Ensure that evidence and learning from STAND contribute to Womankind’s wider organisational knowledge and practice. Partner Institutional Strengthening and Safeguarding Coordinate partner-led organisational strengthening, including safeguarding, governance, financial management, risk management and information security. Work with relevant teams to ensure safeguarding, data protection, wellbeing and protection considerations are embedded across the programme. Advocacy, Communications and Representation Collaborate with the P&A Manager assigned to the project to support partners and WHRDs to engage in regional and international advocacy spaces. Work in conjunction with the P&A Manager assigned to the project to ensure the STAND project and Womankind are represented in relevant external fora, and relationships with peer organisations and networks working on WHRD protection are cultivated Work with the Communications team to coordinate STAND’s internal and external communications to disseminate learning and strengthen the visibility of WHRD’s. Travel and working arrangements: International travel to STAND project countries and other relevant locations will be required, where safe and operationally feasible. All travel will be subject to appropriate risk assessment and security arrangements. Given the six-country, multi-time-zone scope of the role, occasional early-morning or evening meetings should be expected. Key relationships and collaboration: Internally: Grantmaking and Feminist Partnership team, Policy and Advocacy Team, MEL Manager; Finance Team, Fundraising Team & Communications Team. Externally: STAND partners (AWN, EWLA, YWLI, WHR, WIPC, WCoZ); Norad; WHRD networks and coalitions PERSON SPECIFICATION: Qualification and training: A relevant degree or equivalent professional experience in international development, gender studies, human rights, social sciences, or a related field. Training or demonstrated learning in feminist approaches to MEL, programme management and Grantmaking; women's rights, gender equality, or human rights defence (formal or informal). Safeguarding training or demonstrated experience applying survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches. Training or practical experience in programme/project cycle management, ideally with statutory or institutional donors. Essential Experience: Experience managing multi-country, donor-funded programmes or consortia throughout the project cycle, including work planning, partner coordination and reporting against shared outcomes and deadlines. Experience managing substantial multi-partner budgets and forecasts, with a strong understanding of statutory donor compliance and reporting requirements. Experience with Norad or a similar donor would be an advantage. Demonstrable MEL experience, including tracking results, supporting partners to generate and use evidence, and coordinating cross-country learning and exchange. Direct experience working with WRO’s, feminist movements and/or WHRDs. Experience managing programme risk and adapting delivery in politically sensitive, insecure or rapidly changing contexts. Experience applying safeguarding and ethical data-management principles, including the secure handling of sensitive information and survivor-centred responses to risk. Desirable: Experience working with organizations, movements or activists in at least one STAND project country. Knowledge of protection mechanisms for human rights defenders operating in restrictive or shrinking civic space. Experience engaging donors or representing programmes in regional or international advocacy spaces. Knowledge and Skills: Strong commitment to feminist values and women’s rights, with an understanding of intersectional and anti-racist approaches. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to analyze evidence, produce clear reports and communicate complex issues simply. Strong coordination, facilitation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work respectfully across cultures and power dynamics. Sound judgement and integrity, with the ability to navigate sensitive issues and competing donor, organisational and partner priorities while upholding feminist partnership principles. All posts are expected to contribute towards developing a supportive working environment, to demonstrate a commitment to inclusion, professionalism and respect, transparency and accountability and to uphold quality standards as outlined in policies and procedures, and in compliance with Womankind Worldwide's Equal Opportunities Policy. The role also undertakes other responsibilities not outlined above which are commensurate with a role of this nature and which have been discussed an accountability and to uphold quality standards as outlined in policies and procedures, and in compliance with Womankind Worldwide's Equal Opportunities Policy. The role also undertakes other responsibilities not outlined above which are commensurate with a role of this nature and which have been discussed and agreed with the line manager. Working hours: 3 days per week (0.6 FTE) Reporting to: Director of Grantmaking and Feminist Partnership Grade/Level: 3 Contract: 3 year fixed term

item.title: Corporate Partnerships & Sponsorship Executive
item.description: As Corporate Partnerships & Sponsorship Executive, you will play a key role in securing and managing corporate sponsorship for a range of events, including the world-renowned International Symposium on ALS/MND. This brand-new opportunity offers the chance to work across research, fundraising, campaigning and policy, helping to create sustainable income that supports people affected by motor neurone disease (MND). Working with national and international corporate companies and partners, you will develop tailored sponsorship opportunities, deliver excellent stewardship and help create outstanding experiences for sponsors and supporters. This is an exciting opportunity to take ownership of high-profile sponsorship activity, develop strategic partnerships and contribute to the success of internationally recognised events. As Corporate Partnerships & Sponsorship Executive , your work will help generate sustainable income that supports people affected by MND. improve care, fund research and campaign for people affected by MND. Main Responsibilities Secure sponsorship income from national and international corporate organisations, including pharmaceutical and biotech companies Lead sponsorship activity for the International Symposium and other Association-wide events Identify, research and develop new sponsorship opportunities and prospect pipelines Create tailored corporate sponsorship proposals and presentations Build and maintain strong relationships with sponsors, prospects and key stakeholders Deliver excellent sponsor stewardship before, during and after events Plan and coordinate fundraising activity across events to maximise income and engagement Work collaboratively with research, fundraising, events and partnership teams to develop new opportunities Monitor performance, maintain CRM records and provide income and impact reporting About You Essential Experience securing corporate sponsorship, partnership income or significant corporate gifts Experience working with pharmaceutical, biotech or related industry organisations Strong understanding of the ABPI Code of Practice 2024 Excellent communication skills, including proposal, presentation and bid writing Ability to build credible relationships with corporate partners and senior stakeholders Willingness to travel across the UK, with occasional international travel, evening and weekend work as required Desirable Experience engaging corporate partners around scientific research or innovation Experience delivering or supporting fundraising activity at events Experience using CRM systems to manage relationships and income Hybrid working Expectations: One day per week Northampton office attendance required. item.title: Head of Alumni Engagement
item.description: The University of Southampton is a research‑intensive institution and a founding member of the Russell Group. Our aim is to change the world for the better through research, education and knowledge. Our people are at the heart of everything we do, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive. Within the Office of Development & Alumni Relations (ODAR), we build lifelong relationships with our global alumni and supporters, helping them stay connected to Southampton and make a difference through their time, expertise and philanthropy. If you're excited by the idea of shaping and strengthening these communities, this role is for you. About the role This is an opportunity to lead a wide-ranging programme of engagement across our alumni and supporter communities. You will lead and develop a team of four, working across ODAR and the wider University to identify opportunities and deliver impactful programmes. Your portfolio spans engagement and volunteering that advances University priorities – including student recruitment, graduate employability and philanthropy – while strengthening relationships with our international and high‑profile supporters. A central part of the role is leading the volunteering strand of our first University‑wide fundraising and engagement campaign, the £100m Campaign for Southampton. You will also contribute to projects supporting Southampton's brand and reputation, and international engagement in key countries such as China and India. As a member of ODAR's senior team, you will represent alumni and supporter engagement on cross‑University working groups and build relationships with stakeholders across the institution. This role is offered on a hybrid basis, with a minimum of two days a week at Highfield, plus international travel typically once or twice a year. About you You'll bring experience building meaningful relationships with alumni, supporters, volunteers, members or similar stakeholder groups, with a track record of delivering successful engagement programmes – ideally drawing on insight and creativity to reach diverse audiences. An excellent communicator and relationship‑builder, you can influence and work collaboratively with people at all levels. You combine strong organisational and project‑management skills with sound judgement to turn plans into measurable outcomes. You're also an experienced people manager who enjoys developing others. A background in higher education, fundraising, advancement, charity, membership or another relationship‑led environment would be valuable, but transferable experience is equally welcome. About us ODAR has enjoyed an exciting period of growth as we prepare for the Campaign for Southampton. With backing from University leadership, we are investing in the people and programmes needed to deepen alumni and supporter engagement and deliver greater impact for Southampton. We're a friendly, hardworking team with a passion for making a difference, looking for colleagues with intellectual curiosity, fresh ideas and the confidence to shape something ambitious. We welcome applicants with direct experience or transferable skills and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team where everyone can thrive. Apply by uploading your CV and a cover letter of up to two sides of A4, outlining how your skills and experience meet the role's requirements and what attracts you to the opportunity.

item.title: Corporate Partnerships Officer
item.description: Purpose of the job This is an exciting opportunity for those with strong relationship building skills looking to generate partnerships with businesses to deliver better futures for young people. This role focuses on identifying and securing new income generation opportunities with Corporate Partners. You’ll work closely with the Corporate Partnerships Manager in researching and identifying potential new supporters, building our prospect pipeline, making first contact, and helping to develop and present tailored proposals. While you don’t need to be an expert from day one, you will bring energy, curiosity, and great interpersonal skills, along with the ability to think strategically, work well within a team and effectively engage external stakeholders about the importance of UK Youth’s work. Why work at UK Youth? Every young person deserves a youth worker. UK Youth exists to make that a reality. Our vision is a society that backs every young person - through each spark, struggle and success. As the UK’s national infrastructure body for youth work, we strengthen and champion a diverse network of youth organisations, unlock investment, shape policy and build the evidence base for what works. At a time of growing need and inequality of access, our work has never been more important. We are entering an exciting new phase of our strategy - focused on long-term resilience, income diversification and a transformational Capital Appeal to develop Avon Tyrrell as a national centre of excellence for outdoor learning. Joining UK Youth means being part of an ambitious, impact-driven organisation committed to strengthening youth work for generations to come. Key responsibilities Support the Corporate Partnerships team to secure income from new corporate organisations and achieve new business targets, including funding for outdoor learning. Identify new corporate opportunities to add to the new business corporate pipeline Pro-actively engage new businesses using a range of methods: e.g. networking at events, cold calls, emails, LinkedIn Lead on the completion of the due diligence process for new partnership opportunities. Support the development of warm relationships with prospective funders and find opportunities to engage them in the work of UK Youth With the support of the Corporate Partnerships Team, develop corporate bids, budgets and proposals, managing the process across different teams, cultivating strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders Support on the creation and presentation of high quality, persuasive funding bids to C-suite audiences and senior stakeholders Ensure all donations are accurately recorded and recognised, working closely with the finance team Ensure that the CRM is up to date and accurate at all times, including monthly updates of the pipeline report. Support the Corporate team to keep up to date with trends, research and data on fundraising and corporate partnerships, helping to inform long-term strategy. Experience we're after Experience in a sales or corporate fundraising role. Proven track record of corporate partnerships fundraising/ securing sales targets from new organisations Experience of working in a busy and deadline-driven environment and achieving ambitious targets Experience negotiating, pitching and presenting to senior (C-suite) internal and external stakeholders Experience of using a donor database/ CRM system (eg. Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics) What we can offer you We offer a competitive range of benefits, good work/life balance, excellent learning and development opportunities and vibrant organisational culture: Flexible/Agile Working 27 days annual leave (24 days + 3 days winter closure) plus bank holidays (pro rata for part time employees) Funded training provided in; Safeguarding, GDPR, Information and Cyber Security & Equality & Diversity Other training available in support of your personal and professional development Pension scheme (currently UK Youth match employee contributions up to 5%) Membership of our life insurance scheme which would pay-out up to 4 times your salary Employee Assistance Programme to support employees both professionally and personally 20% discount off bookings at Avon Tyrrell, our New Forest Outdoor Centre, including camping, lodges and outdoor activities. IT equipment provided for the duration of contract CycleScheme and TechScheme How to apply If you would like to be considered for this fantastic opportunity, please complete an application via our completely anonymised recruitment system provided by Applied which looks to create a fair and unbiased application process for all. Scroll to the top of the page and start your application. Closing date: 5th October 2026 at 23:59 Interview Dates (In person at London Office): W/C 12th October As this role involves working in a regulated environment with young people, any offer will be conditional to satisfactory background checks, which include criminal record check and employment reference.

item.title: Communications Officer (12-month maternity cover)
item.description: Bible Society believes the Bible is God’s gift for God’s world. We share it because we believe it changes lives for good. We want Christians to be confident in the Bible’s truthfulness and reliability, and we want to change how people talk about it in wider society and invite them to see it as a source of wisdom and joy. We're looking for a creative and highly organised Communications Officer to join our Communications team on a 12-month maternity cover contract. Working closely with the Head of Communications and Social Media and Engagement Lead, you'll create compelling content including digital and social media content that inspires audiences and helps more people engage with the Bible. You'll play a key role in developing content across multiple platforms, supporting our digital content strategy and ensuring all communications are delivered to the highest standard. The ideal candidate will be an excellent copywriter with a strong understanding of social media and digital content, a keen eye for detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities. You'll be a creative thinker, a collaborative team player and a confident communicator who can build strong relationships across the organisation while producing engaging content that connects with a wide range of audiences. You will also be a competent proof reader and editor who can assist others to produce high-quality content. If this sounds like you and you have the legal right to work and remain in the UK, we’d love to hear from you. Please provide your CV and a 250-word statement that sets out your motivation and relevant experience for the job. For the purposes of your cover letter, we ask that you do not use AI-generated content. We would like to hear your own thoughts,experiencesand motivations in your own words. Bible Society is proud to be an Equal Opportunities Employer. We value diversity and aspire to reflect this in our workforce. Second round in-person interviews in Swindon on Tuesday 20 October 2026.

item.title: Individual and Legacy Assistant
item.description: ALDER HEY CHILDRENS CHARITY Job title: Individual and Legacy Assistant Salary: £26,848 - £31,439 Hours: 37.5 hours per week Location: Mix of home working and office based (office is at Alder Hey, Liverpool). Hybrid working available. About us Alder Hey Children’s Charity raises vital funds to help make Alder Hey Children’s Hospital a truly world-class, patient-friendly hospital for the 450,000 patients and families we care for every year. The charity helps to fund a range of activities and projects that are designed to enhance and improve the lives of our amazing young patients. This includes the funding of specialist medical equipment to ensure our brilliant surgeons and clinical staff have the most up to date and cutting edge technology available and funding hi-tech distraction equipment designed and proven to reduce pain and anxiety in our patients. We also fund a range of programmes and special projects such as our ward musicians, our on-site magician and the play specialists we have on every ward. About this role This is an exciting opportunity for an Individual Giving and Legacy Assistant to join the Charity team here at Alder Hey, the UK’s busiest Children’s Hospital. This role sits within the Individual Giving and Legacy team which includes an Individual Giving Fundraiser and a Legacy and In Memory Fundraiser. The role also works closely with colleagues across the community, marketing and finance teams to deliver supporter journeys, website content, and the smooth running of fundraising campaigns. The post-holder supports the generation of income and delivers an excellent supporter experience. They ensure supporters and enquirers receive a prompt, warm, and appropriate response at every stage of their journey with the Alder Hey Children's Charity. The role is responsible for maintaining accurate supporter records on the Charity's CRM system (Salesforce), helping supporter administration (including Gift Aid, tribute pages, and regular giving processes), and assisting with the coordination of legacy enquiries, pledgers, and the free Will Writing service. Key Responsibilities will include: Administration, Processes and Data Stewardship Deal with incoming enquires prioritising, re-directing, or responding in a timely, sensitive and appropriate manner. Help deliver exceptional supporter care, ensuring that everyone who responds to the Charity's campaigns and appeals receives a warm, timely and meaningful thank you, helping to build long-term relationships with Alder Hey Children's Charity. Please see the attached Job Description and Person Specification for more information. Our Values At Alder Hey Children’s Charity, our values guide how we work. Being courageous, working together, showing passion and embracing creativity enables us to support the hospital in delivering the very best care for young patients and their families. Courage We try new things, take risks and innovate. We speak up, take accountability and act with responsibility. Together We work as one team, sharing knowledge and learning. We partner with patients, families, supporters and colleagues. Passion We are passionate about what we do and inspire others. Magic We are creative, fun and child-led, creating special moments and going the extra mile. Additional Information In April 2025, the charity adopted a four-day working week policy. Staff previously working 37.5 hours now work 30 hours across four days, maintaining full pay while supporting a better work-life balance. This job description outlines the general nature of the role and is not exhaustive. It may be subject to change in line with organisational needs. Alder Hey Children’s Charity will make reasonable adjustments where required and is committed to equal opportunities and safeguarding children and vulnerable adults. The post holder will be required to complete an enhanced DBS disclosure check. How to apply You can apply by clicking the link below. Applications must include your CV and a covering letter (no more than one side of A4) which answers the following questions: Additional information is included within the Job Description and Person Specification. item.title: Team Manager
item.description: About the role: For young people who have experienced care, homelessness, trauma or instability, the quality of the adults and services around them can shape what happens next. As a Team Manager in our Young People’s Services, you’ll help create the consistency, safety and skilled support young people need to build confidence, develop independence and move towards adulthood with greater choice over their future. We have two Team Manager opportunities available: one at Cecil House in Camden and one at North Birbeck in Waltham Forest . Working closely with the Service(s), and Regional Services Manager, you’ll provide day-to-day management and practice leadership across the service, supporting and developing frontline staff while maintaining strong oversight of safeguarding, risk, support planning and the quality of practice. You’ll deputise for the Services Manager when required and help make sure young people receive support that is purposeful, individual and rooted in trauma-informed and psychologically informed approaches. Reflective practice will be an important part of how you lead. You’ll create space for staff to think critically about their work, understand the impact of trauma and relationships, learn from challenging situations and strengthen their professional judgement. Alongside this, you’ll help maintain high standards across the service, supporting Ofsted readiness, quality assurance and continuous improvement, and working closely with Children’s Services, Leaving Care teams and other partners to achieve the best possible outcomes for young people. This is an opportunity to take on a significant management role within our Young People’s Services, develop your leadership and regulatory experience and help shape consistently strong practice across the team. You’ll be supported by experienced managers and have access to ongoing learning, development and reflective practice to continue growing as a leader. About you: You know how to lead from alongside a team — giving people clarity, confidence and challenge while creating the kind of environment where strong practice can actually grow. You’re confident in complex situations and don’t lose sight of the young person behind the risk, behaviour or incident. You can help staff stay curious, think clearly and make proportionate safeguarding decisions. You understand trauma-informed and psychologically informed practice, and you can use supervision and reflective practice as real tools for better decision-making, not just as processes to complete. You notice when something in a service is drifting, inconsistent or not good enough, and you’re comfortable asking why, tightening practice and turning feedback, audits and learning into meaningful improvement. You build strong relationships with Children’s Services, Leaving Care teams and other partners, can challenge constructively when needed, and keep young people’s voices, rights and ambitions at the centre of the work. About SHP: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important Info: Closing Date: Sunday 11th October at midnight Interview Date: Tuesday 20th October at SHP Head Office in Kings Cross Please note there will be a second stage interview in service for suitable candidates This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.title: Church & Charity Lawyer (Maternity Cover)
item.description: This is a fixed term maternity cover role for approximately 12months. The fixed term appointment may end earlier or be extended depending on the substantive post-holder’s return date The position is a mixture of office and home-based working for 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday. The usual office days for the Church & Charity team are a Monday and Friday but some flexibility at other times, to accommodate client needs, is an essential part of the role when required. Job Purpose: Reporting to the Head of Department, the principal purpose of the role is to deliver high quality legal services to clients in the ecclesiastical, charity and not for profit sectors, providing advice on governance, regulatory, commercial and property matters. By working collaboratively with all members of the Church & Charity department, the post-holder will provide our clients with a service that is of a high standard, ensures the department works effectively and promotes a professional image of the Firm at all times. The role requires someone familiar with advising clients in a commercial manner, management and control of a caseload, workload, and risk management in relation to the role. It includes helping to develop relationships across departments, as well as interaction with other law firms and professionals. The role also involves working with the management team from time to time, assisting in the design, delivery and implementation of system changes, workflow and process improvements, as well as being involved in training and business development activities to promote the Church and Charity department and the business as a whole. Job Description Principal duties: To operate within a departmental structure delivering a consistent, excellent standard of legal services to our clients. Undertake fee-earning work, working both independently and as a member of the team and provide a profitable contribution to the work of the department. Manage client matters, with a particular focus on: Establishing and registering new charities; Dealing with the Charity Commission and other regulators; Changing legal forms (e.g. incorporating unincorporated charities as a CIO, company limited by guarantee or appointment of corporate trustees); Constitutional reviews and amending governing documentation; Changing charitable objects and advising on public benefit; Mergers, collaborations and restructuring; Trust fund management and complex trust issues; Restrictive funds and permanent endowment; Fundraising; Trading and establishment of subsidiary companies; Donations and legacies; Trustee training; Property matters and Operational issues (e.g. data protection, freedom of information requests, safeguarding, commercial agreements, employment, immigration). Maintain high standards in the processing of client work, both in respect of professional standards and client care. Attending upon clients to take instructions and advising on the most appropriate course of action to meet clients' needs; taking appropriate action in executing clients' instructions in a timely manner. Supervision of the Church & Charity Paralegal as required. Ensure the confidentiality and security of all company and client documentation, information and effects. Maintain good professional working relationships with external institutions and organisations. Comply with the Firm’s policies in the carrying out of duties and assist Partners and other fee earners in achieving a smooth output of work. Liaise with the HOD and other staff to ensure adequate cover within the department at all times, and to attend to clients of other fee earners in their absence, where this is appropriate. Achieve agreed financial targets, in respect of both fee income and the recording of chargeable hours. Financial control of your own matters with particular regard to cash flow through collection of monies on account and billing procedures. Recognise fee-earning opportunities and develop as appropriate. item.title: HR Manager
item.description: Harris Hill is delighted to be partnering with a well-established hospice and family support organisation in the recruitment of an HR Manager. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced HR professional to join an organisation committed to providing exceptional care and support to patients and their families. The role is a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the possibility of an extension. It is a hybrid role, with two days per week working from the hospice’s office in Bromsgrove (near Birmingham). As HR Manager, you will be joining the organisation in a newly created, standalone HR role, providing trusted and proactive HR advice across the organisation. You will support managers and clinical leads across the full employee lifecycle, leading on complex employee relations matters, including disciplinaries, grievances, absence and performance management, while supporting workforce planning, recruitment, safer recruitment and succession planning. You will maintain and develop HR policies and ensure compliance with employment legislation, CQC requirements and safeguarding frameworks. You will also support learning and development, staff wellbeing and engagement, produce workforce reports, and lead HR projects including EDI, change management and wellbeing initiatives. We are looking for an experienced and strategic HR generalist professional with CIPD Level 5 or equivalent, a strong understanding of employment legislation, HR compliance, policies, procedures and best practice, and experience managing HR within a sensitive or regulated environment. As a self-starter, you will be comfortable working independently, establishing and developing an HR function from the ground up, and using your expertise to drive positive cultural change across the organisation. You will be a confident coach and adviser, with excellent communication skills, strong emotional intelligence and the ability to handle sensitive conversations with empathy, discretion and professional judgement. Experience within healthcare, charity, hospice or social care settings would be advantageous. To apply, please submit your up-to-date CV by 4 October at 23:59. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to submit a tailored cover letter after reviewing the full job description. Please note that only applicants with an unrestricted right to work in the UK will be considered for this position. Please note, only successful applicants will be contacted with further information. As a leading charity recruitment specialist and a certified B Corp™, Harris Hill is committed to high and ever-improving standards of equitable and inclusive recruitment. We actively welcome applications from all sections of the community regardless of age, disability, gender, race, religion, sexuality and other protected characteristics.

item.description: Job description Dan Tomlinson is looking for a highly capable and driven leader to join as Head of Office. This person will work closely with Dan to develop and execute a strategy for a better Chipping Barnet as well as being a support to Dan in his role as Growth Minister. We want to go beyond typical MP visits and campaigns and think strategically and creatively about how to make the biggest positive difference we can to the lives of people in Chipping Barnet and beyond. The successful candidate will need to capable of delivering ambitious strategies and leading effective teams, with a deep commitment to serving communities. About Dan Dan has been the Member of Parliament for Chipping Barnet since 2024. He was appointed as a Minister in September 2025, taking the role of Exchequer Secretary to the Treasury. Initially responsible for HMRC and tax policy, his portfolio is currently focused on generating economic growth, working across the Treasury and the Cabinet Office. Dan has previously worked as an economist in the Treasury, at the Resolution Foundation and at the Joseph Rowntree foundation, focusing on improving living standards for all, particularly low- and middle-income families who faced stagnating economic conditions in recent decades. ' I want to work with a Head of Office who shares my values and can put them into practice. We have an opportunity here to build a local movement that makes people's lives better and rebuilds trust in politics – I want to work with a driven, highly capable leader who can help me make that happen .' Job description – Head of Office Manage key team members working across casework, communications, administration, parliamentary and local action roles. item.title: Community Fundraising Manager (Scotland)
item.description: About Hearing Dogs for Deaf People National charity Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, trains dogs to transform the lives of deaf people and provides hearing loss services – because nobody with hearing loss should feel alone. About the role This role will drive income growth and deepen engagement across local communities in the region, play a key role in growing and stewarding supporter-led activity, recruiting and empowering volunteers, and championing legacy giving across the region and deliver an ambitious programme of community and events fundraising, working closely with colleagues across fundraising, communications, and service delivery to maximise reach, impact, and return on investment. Responsible to: North Regional Community and Events Manager. Based: Community based in Scotland. Contract: Permanent, full-time. Key Responsibilities Fundraising: Meet an annual income target for the region. Delivery of existing and new fundraising products. Organising and supporting fundraising events and activities within the region. Ensure participants are stewarded on their supporter journey. Lead where appropriate, project teams on campaigns and product development. Build new relationships with small to medium-sized local businesses, local groups and societies, faith organisations and events and event participants to maximise fundraising in the region. Use fundraising products to secure sponsorship for partnership dogs within the region. Work cooperatively with other fundraising colleagues (Events, Individual Giving and Major Giving, including corporates and trusts and with communications) to jointly further the impact of fundraising regionally. Support and deliver local legacy conversations and the legacy promotion. Resource fundraising volunteers with legacy awareness training or guidance. Contribute to an uplift in legacy pledges or enquirers sourced via community channels. Deliver regional legacy awareness events or campaigns. Support, networks local relationships: Recruit, train, develop, support and motivate community event volunteers and supporters. In collaboration with regional service staff, establish, support and maintain relationships with Hearing Dogs networks of volunteers based around regional projects. Ensure good relations are established and maintained with a variety of media, including local and social to promote the Hearing Dogs brand and develop fundraising and engagement. Represent the Charity at volunteer and sector functions and events. Maximising digital platforms: Use social media platforms, e.g. Facebook, X, to support fundraising initiatives, supporter journey and relationship building. Use digital event and online fundraising platforms to support events, fundraising and engagement. Financial and reporting: Monitor regional income/expenditure monthly against budget. Report on variances and implement appropriate contingency plans. Maintain the charity database with timely and accurate donor, supporter and third-party information ensuring compliance with GDPR. To report back on a regular basis to the Head of Community Fundraising and Events as to activity, progress and achievement against identified financial and soft targets. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Essential: Proactive and confident self-starter with experience of raising funds or from equivalent experience gained either within the voluntary sector or the commercial world. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills coupled with an enthusiastic and positive approach. Ability to work as part of a team and to contribute towards the success of the Community Fundraising team and wider team at Hearing Dogs. Computer literate with MS365 applications and knowledge and experience of databases and an ability to keep accurate records of all contacts and relevant information. Ability to work on own, without close and constant support and supervision and to be able to handle pressure, deadlines and targets. Educated to A Level or equivalent. A full current driving license. Desirable: Experience of the voluntary sector and fundraising. An understanding of charity law and how it relates to community fundraising. Understanding of digital and direct marketing in fundraising Experience of public speaking and presenting to a diverse range of audiences. An understanding and affinity of the challenges faced by the deaf community and the disability marketplace. A significant record of achievement in raising funds either gained within the voluntary sector or within a sales background. A team player with a desire to inspire and motivate others. Benefits: Employee Assistance Programme Death in Service Payment Annual leave enhancements recognising long service Day off for your birthday Defined contribution group personal pension plan Enhanced sick pay Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay Eye care Hearing tests Learning and Development opportunities Discounts on merchandise at Hearing Dog gift shops Pet Dog Policy Closing date: 9th October 2026. This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 due to its duties involving the protection of children and/or adults at risk. Applicants are therefore required to disclose all spent and unspent convictions, cautions, warnings, and reprimands, as well as any relevant non-conviction information. The successful candidate will be required to undertake a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check in accordance with the Police Act 1997 (Part V).

item.title: Community Outreach and Volunteer Manager
item.description: Irish Chaplaincy is seeking an experienced, compassionate and motivated Community Outreach and Volunteer Manager to help us extend our reach, strengthen our volunteer community and provide high-quality support to older and vulnerable Irish people across London. For almost 70 years, Irish Chaplaincy has supported Irish immigrants and people of Irish heritage across England and Wales. Rooted in a Catholic ethos and Catholic social teaching , our work recognises the inherent dignity of every person. We take a holistic and person-centred approach, offering spiritual, emotional and practical support to people who may be isolated, vulnerable or experiencing difficult circumstances. This is an exciting opportunity to play a central role in a respected charity at an important point in its development. As we celebrate our 70th anniversary in 2027, you will help us reach more people in need, build a strong and well-supported volunteer network, and ensure that vulnerable members of the Irish community receive compassionate, practical and pastoral care. This is a varied, hands-on role combining community outreach, face-to-face casework, staff supervision and volunteer management . You will lead efforts to identify and engage people who may benefit from our support, build strong referral relationships across London, and ensure our volunteers are recruited, trained and supported effectively. You will also line manage our Community Outreach Worker and hold a small caseload of your own. This will involve visiting people in their homes, hospitals and care settings and providing pastoral care, advocacy, emotional support and practical help, including support at the end of life. Key responsibilities Proactively reach older Irish people and other vulnerable members of the Irish community, particularly those who are isolated or not currently known to services. Build relationships with parishes, community and faith groups, Irish centres, GP surgeries, social services and other voluntary and statutory organisations. Provide day-to-day line management, supervision and development support to the Community Outreach Worker. Lead the recruitment, induction, training, deployment and ongoing support of volunteers. Develop clear volunteer roles and effective procedures covering safeguarding, safe recruitment and DBS checks. Hold a small caseload and provide face-to-face pastoral, emotional, advocacy and practical support. Represent Irish Chaplaincy at community events, forums and partner meetings. Support community development, fundraising, impact reporting and activity connected with Irish Chaplaincy's 70th anniversary in 2027. About you We are looking for someone with substantial recent experience in: Community outreach, engagement or development , particularly with older people or other vulnerable adults. Face-to-face support and casework , including visits to people's homes, hospitals or care settings. Line managing or supervising paid staff , including supporting performance, wellbeing and professional development. Recruiting, training, supporting and managing volunteers , while creating a positive and inclusive volunteering culture. You will be an excellent relationship-builder with strong communication and organisational skills, a sound understanding of safeguarding, and the ability to balance outreach, management and direct support responsibilities. You will bring a warm, respectful and person-centred approach to your work. You should also have empathy with, and a commitment to, Irish Chaplaincy's Christian ethos and pastoral mission . An understanding of Irish culture and the experiences of the Irish diaspora in Britain would be an advantage. The role requires regular travel across London and occasional evening or weekend work. An enhanced DBS check and the right to work in the UK are required. Irish Chaplaincy is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of older and vulnerable people. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all sections of the community.

item.description: Head of Youth Work and Partnerships This is an exciting role with a significant level of autonomy for an ambitious and experienced youth work professional. Position: Head of Youth Work & Delivery Partnerships Location: White City, West London Salary: £52-58k (dependent on experience) Hours: Full-time 37.5 hours per week. 5 out of 7 days Contract: Permanent Closing Date: 19th October 2026. We’ll review applications and interview candidates as we receive them. We may close the vacancy early if we find the right candidate, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. About the Role The Head of Youth Work & Delivery Partnerships will lead and manage a large team of Youth Workers while taking operational responsibility for the seven-day-a-week universal youth work offer. As the leading provider of universal access youth work in Hammersmith and Fulham, and part of the network, the Youth Zone has a strong reputation and growing impact. You will hold overall responsibility for delivering a vibrant, open access Youth Zone for the young people of West London, welcoming up to 200 young people per session. You will lead the development and delivery of the core youth work provision, including junior, senior and holiday clubs, ensuring high standards of practice and a culture of continuous improvement. You will also ensure the Youth Zone remains a fun, supportive, safe and inclusive environment that attracts and retains young people, helping to raise aspirations and support positive outcomes. You will be a member of the Senior Leadership Team, and will work in tandem with the Chief Executive, the Senior Leadership Team and the Board of Trustees to help achieve its goal of delivering lifechanging youth work to young people in West London. Key responsibilities include: · Staffing · The Offer (programme) · Partnerships and stakeholders · Young people · Leadership · Policy, compliance and quality assurance About You We are looking for someone with experience in youth work, including leading and managing activities, staff and volunteers. You will have: · Experience in safeguarding for example as a DSO, DSL or deputy. · A track record of successful project and budget management · Experience of delivering results through effective team leadership and collaboration · Experience of working with a range of IT systems such as databases, dashboards or CRM · Ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple deadlines while remaining calm under pressure · A degree level qualification in a relevant subject, or equivalent experience · Excellent verbal and written communication, interpersonal, negotiation and relationship building skills · Ability to relate to and engage young people from all backgrounds · Strong people management and coaching skills, with the ability to both lead and work effectively as part of a team · Strong organisational skills, with a structured yet flexible and responsive approach focused on achieving results · A non-judgemental, open-minded and empathetic approach, with sensitivity to individuals and the wider community · Flexibility to meet the needs of young people About the Organisation You will join a vibrant youth charity providing a safe, welcoming and inspiring space for young people across West London. Open seven days a week outside school hours, the organisation offers sports, arts, wellbeing support and employability programmes designed to help young people discover their potential. Benefits include 33 days’ annual leave inclusive of bank holidays, enhanced maternity & paternity leave, Birthday leave, free gym access, a workplace pension and training and development opportunities. Other roles you may have experience of could include Youth Worker, Youth Worker, Youth Work Lead, Head of Youth Work, Head of Youth Partnerships. This is a senior position within the Building and Fire Safety function, with responsibility for providing technical leadership, managing a specialist team and ensuring fire safety arrangements remain robust across a large property portfolio. item.title: Head of Digital and Operations
item.description: Head of Digital & Operations Salary: £62,415 - £64,058. Location: London – Hybrid Working. Contract: Full-time (35 hours/week), Permanent Line Manager: Director of People Operations and Assurance Line Reports: Digital Delivery Lead, Operations Manager, Organisational Strengthening Manager, Data Manager About Start Network Start Network is a global network of over 150 local, national, and international NGOs. We act as a catalyst for system-level change to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and ethics of humanitarian action. By devolving power, resources, and decision-making to locally led networks and hubs, we build early financing systems and community-led solutions that anticipate and respond to crises. The Role We are seeking a strategic, forward-thinking Head of Digital & Operations to lead our operational and digital systems. You will oversee the continuous improvement of our infrastructure, ensuring our programme teams, local hubs, and network members have scalable, compliant, and user-centred support. As Start Network’s senior digital sponsor, you will own our digital and data roadmap, embed cyber security controls, strengthen operational resilience, and drive cross-organisational transformation. Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership: Lead the Digital and Operations function, oversee its budget, sit on the Senior Management Group, and advise the Senior Leadership Team and Board Committees. Digital Strategy & Governance: Own the technology, data, and digital strategy. Provide senior oversight of digital architecture, system integrations, AI/automation ethics, GDPR, and cyber security. Operations & Resilience: Evolve the organisation's operating model. Oversee frameworks for procurement, travel, security, facilities, and business continuity planning. Programme Operations: Oversee the operational support models for key funds and initiatives (Start Fund, Start Ready, anticipatory action). Provide senior decision support on complex issues including hosting, compliance, safeguarding, and donor requirements. Team Management: Line-manage, coach, and develop a high-performing team of specialists while fostering an inclusive, values-driven culture. Rota Responsibilities: Participate in a weekend and holiday rota for smooth programme delivery (Start Fund/Start Ready) and on-call travel/security support. Essential Criteria: Proven experience leading large-scale digital and operational transformations in complex, multi-stakeholder organisations. Expertise in technology strategy development, cyber security, IT service management, and modern digital architecture. Demonstrated ability to build strong data governance, reporting, and insight capabilities. Experience designing multi-geography operational frameworks, policies, and risk mitigation strategies. Strong leadership track record in change management, stakeholder influence, and team coaching. Desirable Criteria: Background in the humanitarian, international development, or charity sectors. Experience working with Board committees, executive teams, and managing complex third-party vendor relationships. Proficiency in Start Network working languages in addition to English. Travel This role involves up to 4 weeks of international travel per year to conferences, Start Network hubs, or countries of operation. Timeline: - Applications close on Monday 5 th October. - 1 st Stage Interviews scheduled for w/c 12 th October. To apply for the role or for an informal discussion, please reach out to Daniel Kelner at Goodman Masson, who are our exclusive recruitment partner for this position:

item.description: We have an exciting opportunity for a Triage and Early Interventions Officer to join the team in Staffordshire, working 37.5 hours per week. Generous Annual Leave : 28 days plus Bank Holidays, increasing to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave. Birthday Leave : An extra day off for your birthday. Pension Plan : 5% employer contribution. Enhanced Allowances : Enhanced sick pay, maternity, and paternity payments. You will conduct comprehensive impact and risk assessments, provide immediate and short-term interventions, and ensure that each client receives tailored support that meets their individual needs. item.title: Fundraising Officer
item.description: Step into a pivotal fundraising role where you’ll drive income growth across regional and community channels, challenge events, and sponsorship, all while delivering excellent supporter care. This is a temporary opportunity offering remote or hybrid working based in Essex, ideal for an experienced fundraiser who can quickly make an impact and build strong donor relationships. About the Role: You will lead on planning and delivering a mix of regional and community fundraising activities, challenge events, and event sponsorship to meet agreed income targets. Working closely with internal teams and supporters, you’ll manage end-to-end campaigns, from prospecting and cultivation through to stewardship and post-event evaluation. Your work will directly enhance supporter experience and strengthen the organisation’s fundraising pipeline. Key Responsibilities: * Plan, deliver and monitor regional and community fundraising activities to achieve agreed income and engagement targets. * Coordinate and manage challenge events and other fundraising events, including logistics, communications, and on-the-day support. * Develop and manage event sponsorship opportunities, including researching prospects, preparing proposals, and securing sponsorship agreements. * Provide high-quality supporter care, ensuring timely, personalised and professional communication with donors, participants and community fundraisers. * Use the Raiser’s Edge database to record and maintain accurate supporter and event data, track income, and produce regular reports. * Implement donor cultivation plans, including follow-up, stewardship journeys and tailored engagement activities to maximise retention and uplift. * Collaborate with colleagues to create compelling fundraising materials and event collateral that support recruitment and income generation. * Monitor performance of fundraising activities, evaluating results and making recommendations to improve future campaigns. Key Requirements: * Proven experience in regional and community fundraising, including planning and delivering income-generating activities. * Track record of managing challenge events and fundraising events from concept through to delivery and evaluation. * Demonstrated ability to provide excellent supporter care and build strong, long-term relationships with donors and participants. * Experience securing and managing event sponsorship, including prospecting and negotiation. * Confident user of fundraising databases, ideally Raiser’s Edge, with strong data management and reporting skills. * Strong organisational skills, able to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a temporary, fast-paced environment. * Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to different supporter audiences. * Ability to work effectively on a remote or hybrid basis, with good self-management and proactive communication. Desirable Skills: * Experience working with charities or non-profit organisations in Essex or the surrounding region. * Knowledge of current community and events fundraising trends and best practice. * Experience developing digital promotion for fundraising and challenge events. * Familiarity with integrating fundraising campaigns across multiple channels (online, community, corporate). Qualifications: * Degree or equivalent experience in fundraising, marketing, communications, or a related field. * Professional fundraising qualification (e.g. IoF/Chartered Institute of Fundraising) is desirable. * Evidence of ongoing professional development in fundraising, supporter care or events management is an advantage. If you’re an experienced fundraiser ready to deliver results in a remote or hybrid role based in Essex, we’d like to hear from you. Apply now to help drive impactful fundraising activities during this key temporary assignment.

item.title: Fundraising Officer
item.description: Join a small charity where your ideas and fundraising work can make a visible difference. We are looking for a Fundraising Officer with strong fundraising fundamentals, curiosity, creativity and a willingness to experiment. At a time when the charity sector and the wider world are changing quickly, we want someone who can look beyond familiar approaches, spot opportunities others might miss and turn new ideas into practical action. ABOUT DISABILITY AFRICA Disability Africa works in partnership with locally led organisations in The Gambia, Kenya, Uganda, Zambia and Eswatini. Together, we create opportunities for disabled children and young people to participate in community life on an equal basis, while working to change attitudes and challenge the exclusion they face. At the heart of this work are community-based play hubs, led by our partners, where disabled children and young people play alongside their peers, build relationships and become more connected to their communities. Our work is grounded in the Social Model of Disability. We focus on removing the social and attitudinal barriers that exclude disabled children and young people, and we reject pity-based approaches to fundraising and communication. We are also conscious of the colonial power structures that continue to shape the international development sector. We work actively to challenge them by building long-term partnerships in which local organisations lead how our approach is shaped and put into practice in their own communities. ABOUT THE ROLE You will help generate the income that sustains and develops our work, joining a small, collaborative team and working closely with the Executive Director, colleagues and volunteers. The role offers considerable variety and the opportunity to develop your fundraising experience across several income streams. You will research opportunities, prepare strong funding applications and donor reports, maintain our fundraising pipeline and CRM, and help build relationships with funders and supporters. You will also contribute to campaigns and help us explore new audiences and fundraising approaches. WHAT YOU WILL DO • Research funding opportunities across trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships, individual giving and other relevant sources. • Prepare and submit clear, persuasive applications, proposals and funding requests. • Maintain an accurate pipeline of prospective and existing funders and manage timely follow-up and repeat applications. • Build positive relationships with donors, funders, corporate partners and prospective supporters. • Produce clear donor reports that demonstrate impact and financial accountability. • Maintain accurate information in our fundraising CRM and use data to help inform priorities. • Contribute to fundraising campaigns, donor communications and materials in collaboration with colleagues and volunteers. • Support the development and testing of new fundraising opportunities and approaches. ABOUT YOU You do not need to have worked across every area listed above. We are looking for someone with a sound grounding in fundraising, strong writing and research skills, and the confidence to develop relationships with different people and organisations. • Experience of fundraising in a charity, non-profit or comparable organisation. • Strong research, writing and proposal-development skills. • The confidence to approach and build relationships with donors and prospective supporters. • Good analytical and numerical skills, with confidence working with data and budgets. • Experience using a CRM or donor database (we use Salesforce). • Strong organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage several priorities. • Curiosity, initiative and a willingness to test new ideas. • Alignment with Disability Africa’s ethos and the Social Model of Disability, including our partnership-based approach, an awareness of the colonial dynamics that continue to shape the sector, and a rejection of pity-based charity narratives. WHAT WE OFFER • A four-day working week, with 28 hours worked from Monday to Thursday. • A 12-month fixed-term contract, with the possibility of extension. • Hybrid working, with two days per week in our Staines office, a three-minute walk from Staines station and less than 30 minutes by train from central London. • Twenty working days of annual leave, equivalent to five full working weeks, plus the Christmas closure period. • The opportunity to shape and develop fundraising work within a small organisation. • A collaborative working environment with close contact across our UK team and African partners. HOW TO APPLY Please submit your CV and a supporting statement of no more than 750 words through CharityJob. Your statement should explain why you are interested in the role, what you believe you would bring to it, and, through relevant examples, how your experience meets the person specification. Applications close at 11.59 pm on Monday 19 October 2026. First interviews are expected to take place on 26 or 27 October, with second interviews during the week beginning 2 November. WHO WE ENCOURAGE TO APPLY We want to hear from people who are excited by this role and share our values, including people who are often excluded from opportunities in the charity sector. We especially encourage applications from disabled people and from people with personal or professional connections to the countries where our partners work. If there is anything we can change in the recruitment process to make it more accessible to you, please let us know. We are sorry that we cannot offer visa sponsorship for this role : the terms of the role do not meet the current sponsorship requirements. Applicants will therefore need to already have the right to work in the UK.

The Role Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you will: Contact and engage people living with HIV by phone, text, email and community outreach. item.title: Team Leader
item.description: We are seeking a dedicated, experienced and compassionate Children and Young People Team Leader to work across Warwickshire, providing effective leadership, guidance and support to a team delivering services to children affected by domestic abuse and other crimes. The service is commissioned by the Warwickshire Police and Crime Commissioner and is a full-time role, working 37.5 hours per week, offering an exciting opportunity to play a key role in the delivery of an essential local service. Are you passionate about supporting children and young people affected by crime and domestic abuse, developing services and teams, and driving continuous improvement within this vital Warwickshire based service. If so, we'd love to hear from you… What we offer At Victim Support we believe in attracting & retaining the best people and offer a competitive rewards & benefits package including: Flexible Working Options: Including hybrid working. Generous Annual Leave : 28 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, rising to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave. Birthday Leave : An extra day off for your birthday. Pension Plan : 5% employer contribution. Enhanced Allowances : Enhanced sick pay allowances, maternity & paternity payments. Exclusive Discounts : High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment & leisure discounts. Financial Wellbeing : Access to our financial wellbeing hub & salary deducted finance. Wellbeing Support : Employee assistance programme & wellbeing support. Inclusive Networks : Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes. Sustainable Travel : Cycle to work scheme & season ticket loans. Career Development : Ongoing training & support with opportunities for career development & progression. About the role As Team Leader you will work closely with the Operations Manager to support the safe, trauma-informed and effective delivery of the service, driving high standards, effective outcomes, and supporting team members' wellbeing and development. You will provide day-to-day leadership, support and guidance to a team of two CYP Case Workers and three CHIDVAs (Children's Independent Domestic Violence Advocate), helping to create a positive, high-performing and learning-focused culture. Key Responsibilites provide leadership and day-to-day support to a team of CYP Case Workers and CHIDVAs, helping to ensure the delivery of high-quality, safe and effective services whilst promoting a positive, confident and resilient team culture. support the Operations Manager with the effective running and development of the service provide advice and guidance to team members and other colleagues around safeguarding, risk and case complexity, ensuring the service prioritises safety and identifies individual needs for tailored support will use data, quality assurance and learning from practice to help identify trends, strengthen service delivery and support continuous improvement This role offers an excellent opportunity for an experienced IDVA, or someone with operational experience working with children and young people, or in the field of Domestic Abuse, looking to take the next step in their leadership journey, or for an existing senior practitioner who is passionate about developing others whilst continuing to make a direct difference to children and young people affected by crime and domestic abuse. This hybrid role requires some working from home, some office-based work (within Warwickshire Justice Centre, Leamington Spa), and regular in-person and online partnership meeting and forum attendance to represent the service and amplify the voices of children and young people affected by crime and Domestic Abuse. The CYP Team Leader will ensure the right support is provided according to individual needs through assessment, safety planning and support. This role involves regular travel and due to the location, a driving license and access to a vehicle is considered an essential requirement. If you are unable to drive because of a disability please indicate this in your application in your personal statement so we can explore the feasibility of alternative arrangements. About Us Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required. At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minoritised communities. As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process. How to apply To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible.

item.title: Marketing and Visitor Experience Lead (Scotland)
item.description: Temporary role for 18 months Home Based with travel (a 50/50 mix of home working and travel) Ref: 22001 About us Our vision is to save every one. It may take us a long time to get there, but drowning is preventable, and we believe that even one drowning is one too many. We are all lifesavers. We are all fundraisers. This is our watch. We’re looking for the best of the best to be part of our RNLI engagement crew. This is an exciting new role for a strategic thinker and creative doer who will support volunteers, create memorable experiences and deliver campaigns that can really make a difference. Your role As Marketing and Visitor Experience Lead you will be audience focused, ensuring our supporters, donors, volunteers and the general public have a great experience and join us, stay with us, advocate for us and feel part of the RNLI family. What you’ll be doing in the role: Although based in Scotland, the role is expected to spend around 50% of its time delivering Scotland-specific activities, with the remaining 50% supporting wider Marketing & Visitor Experience Lead activities across the UK and Ireland, responding to business needs and priorities. Getting to know our audiences and ensuring that RNLI campaigns and experiences are relevant and supporter-centric. Working with staff and volunteers to develop and deliver national, regional and local campaigns and experiences against income, engagement and behaviour change KPIs. Working with staff and volunteers to design and develop inspiring and engaging visitor journeys and experiences within our lifeboat stations, museums and visitor centres. Supporting and feeding into the development of the regional engagement plan. Being an active member of the regional engagement team in the Scotland, demonstrating the highest levels of collaborative working and collective responsibility. Coaching, training and developing our team of Community Managers to deliver against marketing and visitor experience objectives, using your experience to improve their knowledge and skills. Supporting volunteer recruitment, management and training of Lifeboat Visits Teams, Community Presenters and Campaign Ambassadors. About you You’ll have a strong background in either a marketing or visitor experience development role; you’ll get to know your audiences, whether they are supporters, volunteers or supporters of the future and keep them front of mind when developing content across both physical experiences and campaigns. Your energy and creative approach will motivate you to achieve targets and overcome barriers. You’ll be flexible and willing to travel to achieve results and work across the wider engagement team. To be considered as the Marketing and Visitor Experience Lead, you will need: Significant achievements in engaging supporters, volunteers or the public in order to generate funds, increase engagement or change behaviour. A proven track record in the areas of marketing campaign and/or visitor experience. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience of audience insights, brand relevancy and targeted content creation. People leadership skills, including high levels of emotional intelligence and problem-solving skills. Experience of influencing at all levels and working collaboratively with others to lead and embed change and improvements. This role combines home-based working with a significant level of travel across Scotland and to other RNLI locations throughout the UK and Ireland, and occasional travel to our RNLI Support Centre in Poole. This post requires a valid driving licence. For more information and to apply, please visit our jobs page. Closing date: 11 October 2026. Interview date: 20 October 2026. The RNLI is committed to safeguarding; protecting a person’s health, wellbeing, and human rights, enabling them to live free from harm, abuse, and neglect. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment and have a zero-tolerance approach. The suitability of all prospective employees and volunteers will be assessed during the recruitment process in line with this commitment. This will include relevant criminal record checks being carried out dependent on the eligibility of the role. (England & Wales; DBS check, Scotland; Disclosure Scotland PVG, Northern Ireland; Access NI, Republic of Ireland; Garda Vetting; International, International Child Protection Certificate process). Our staff and volunteers have been saving lives at sea without prejudice for 200 years. We respect and value diversity of background, skills and perspectives within our teams, and consider it essential to help us deliver a world-class lifesaving service. We are an inclusive organisation and welcome applications from everyone. In addition to having the skills needed for the role, we also look for applicants who share our commitment to living our RNLI values (trustworthy, courageous, selfless, and dependable), and helping us work towards Our Vision: To save Every One.
