item.title: Deputy Manager
item.description: Summary The Woodfield Project (TWP) is seeking an enthusiastic Deputy Manager to help run our beautifully refurbished community hub on Tooting Bec Common, in SW London. In close collaboration with the TWP Manager, you will coordinate daily operations, deliver a lively programme of events and activities, support members and volunteers and help grow new initiatives. Working closely with the Trustee Board, you’ll also ensure the Pavilion remains sustainable and continues to thrive at the heart of the local community. About us The Woodfield Project is a vibrant, community-focused charity responsible for The Woodfield Pavilion located on Tooting Bec Common, in South-West London. The Pavilion serves as a lively community hub, offering events and activities that: support social wellbeing; bring the local community together; and encourage appreciation and care for the surrounding natural environment. The Pavilion spaces are ideal for meetings, classes, and exhibitions, along with a well-equipped kitchen, toilets and a locker room. As well as hosting its own events and activities, the Pavilion is hired by external organisations for wellbeing classes, workshops and events. Purpose and scope of role We are looking to recruit an enthusiastic and energetic Deputy Manager with the skills and experience to support and drive forward our mission of ensuring that the Pavilion serves as a vital resource for local communities and groups and to actively encourage participation from members and volunteers who share our passion for making a difference. The Trustee Board provides governance and strategic leadership for the charity. The Deputy Manager will work alongside the TWP Manager to coordinate the day-to-day running of the building and plan and deliver an engaging programme of community events and activities, as well as develop new activities. The role includes operational management, future planning and ensuring a sustainable income and membership base. The Deputy Manager will report to the TWP Manager and work collaboratively with the full Board, as well as with individual trustees on specific issues. Key tasks and responsibilities: Delivery Supporting all aspects of the day-to-day management and operation of the Pavilion in line with the Charity’s mission and aims, within the framework set by the trustees. Work with the Manager to coordinate and co-deliver a programme of community and environmental activities and events, including managing events where necessary Oversee (new and existing) workstreams which form part of the TWP vision Manage bookings, hiring, art sales and other Pavilion-related administration Ensure that the building is clean, well-maintained and safe Work with the TWP Manager and Building Management team (trustees and members of the Charity) to ensure the maintenance and development of the physical structure of Pavilion Operational Work with volunteers and members of The Woodfield Project Coordinate and expand the volunteer community Ensure compliance with health and safety, safeguarding and other regulatory requirements Maintain the policies and procedures for operating the Pavilion and ensure that they are followed Work with the TWP Manager and Secretary to organise and support Trustee and Charity meetings Strategic Work alongside the TWP Manager to: Maintain a cycle of events and activities to meet the charity’s aims and running costs Develop, plan and fund future events and projects Develop and manage relationships with stakeholders, partners and users within the community Identify and implement opportunities to develop the activities at the Pavilion and increase funding streams in line with the aims of the Charity Marketing Deliver regular communications to stakeholders about Pavilion news and activities Work with the TWP Manager and Digital Assistant on regular social media, web development and publicity tasks Financial Manage overhead costs within agreed budgets Work with the TWP Manager to identify and develop suitable bids for funding for the Charity, the Pavilion, and its activities Work with the TWP Manager and Treasurer to comply with required internal and external reporting requirements Financial administration including bookkeeping required to support the Charity’s financial policy and procedures PERSON SPECIFICATION Essential Self-reliant, motivated, comfortable with working alone on site and able to work on their own initiative and prioritise work and demands Strong organisational skills with a flexible and resourceful approach Able to work both autonomously and as part of a team Excellent communication and interpersonal skills including the ability to work collaboratively with other teams and with diverse groups of people Strong networking skills and the ability to build partnerships Experience of organising or managing events. Proficiency in using IT for management purposes and social media to promote events and engage with stakeholders. Basic financial management skills, including budgeting and financial reporting. Experience of working with or managing volunteers Willingness to work flexibly, including some weekends and evenings. [Note that most of the building is accessible, but the site is reached on foot down gravel paths, so must be able to navigate these. Desirable Experience in marketing and communications (incl. social media) Experience in business development and identifying potential opportunities Project management skills Experience of community work

item.title: Finance Director
item.description: We are looking for a strategic finance professional to join the senior leadership team of Ark UK Programmes and support the sustainable growth and development of our traded programmes. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with strong commercial experience who is passionate about our mission and motivated by how different funding models and blended finance can enable us to create social impact at scale. Within this role you will work closely with the Group Finance team, which is responsible for all the group financial processing and reporting, and supported by a group financial controller. We are looking for someone who will bring a firm understanding of the drivers of income and expenditure to support effective decision making across our programmes, ensuring that financial sustainability and mission impact are considered together and influence every part of the organisational strategy. The Finance Director will own all the financial modelling underpinning this, managing forecasting and budgeting, and providing rapid and reliable assessments of the financial impact of business decisions. This role requires a curious and commercially minded approach, using a strong grasp of the economics of our ventures to identify risks and opportunities and deepen organisational understanding of key metrics such as subscription renewals. Working closely with the Group Finance team, the Finance Director will ensure management reports provide an accurate view of performance and will oversee spend and income risks, ensuring corrective action is taken where needed. The role will also work closely with the Managing Director to develop new ventures, ensuring their underlying economics are sound. Reporting directly into the Managing Director of Ark UK Programmes, this role will also have dotted line reporting into the Group CFO who oversees all Ark’s financial activity, to ensure consistency and management of risk throughout the Ark Group. The Finance Director will report into Managing Director, Ark UK Programmes. This role is currently operating hybrid working in our West London Office on a permanent basis working full time. 1st round interviews will be taking place in person on Wednesday 21st October 2026 with 2nd round interviews taking place in person w/c 2nd November 2026. Key Responsibilities: Key Requirements: The financial performance of Ark UK Programmes, highlighting risks and issues to the Managing Director to ensure effective commercial decisions are promptly made Developing the strategic plans for Ark UK Programmes including forecasting and budgeting Developing a fully auditable, flexible financial model able to provide rapid and reliable answers about the impact of different decisions on the financial performance Working with the Managing Director and product strategy team on developing new ventures, conducting robust financial analysis to support decision making and fundraising applications Working with the Group Finance Business Partner responsible for Ark UK Programmes to obtain relevant and accurate monthly Management Accounts in a format that supports sound financial management Present Management Accounts to the Ark UK Programmes senior leadership team Responsible for compiling and presenting the quarterly report to the AC+ Programme Board Work with the Group FD, FC and group finance team in making sure financial processes are efficient, processing is accurate, and that we make the most of the use of available technology Work with the Managing Director of Ark UK Programmes to develop a fully auditable flexible financial model able to be interrogated to provide financial insights into the impact of different decisions on the financial performance and long-term sustainability of the ventures, and to use this to advise on proposed changes such as pricing, contractual terms and programme structures As part of the senior leadership team, contribute to organisational direction and priorities that maximise long-term impact, ensuring financial sustainability is central to decision making Right to work in the UK Professional Accounting Qualification, with a preference towards CIMA Educated to degree level or equivalent Minimum of 5 years’ experience in a senior finance role in complex organisations or start ups Understanding the importance of strong financial modelling and experience building and interrogating models Strong commercial management and project experience, including financial management experience in organisations that depend on trading income in highly competitive markets Strong numerical and analytical skills including confidence in analysing large data sets and presenting important findings clearly Experience operating at a leadership level, with the ability to work independently and to structure and lead complex projects Strong relationship skills with enthusiasm for working in an entrepreneurial environment Confident and highly credible with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels Able to juggle multiple priorities and enjoy an environment which is constantly changing Ark Curriculum Plus is a not-for-profit education venture set up by the Ark Multi Academy Trust to improve subject outcomes. We’ve now been going for over ten years, using what we learn in Ark to support over 1,000 schools nationally. Our mission is to empower teachers to give every young person, regardless of their background, the subject knowledge and skills that will allow them to succeed. We now have subject excellence programmes in English, Maths, Science and Geography, at primary and secondary. A team of subject experts work with partner schools to empower teachers to achieve subject excellence using an ambitious curriculum combined with CPD, teaching and assessment resources. Our programmes, including Mathematics Mastery and English Mastery, have been shown to have measurable impact in evaluations by the EEF, FFT and The Brilliant Club. Diversity and inclusion: We aim to build a diverse and inclusive organisation where everyone – staff and students – can do their best work and achieve their full potential. We want to reflect and represent diverse perspectives across our organisation because we know that doing so will make us stronger and more effective. To know more about Ark’s diversity and inclusion commitments, please click on this link. Safeguarding statement: Ark is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people in its academies. In order to meet this responsibility, its academies follow a rigorous selection process to discourage and screen out unsuitable applicants. Ark requires all employees to undertake an enhanced DBS check. You are required, before appointment, to disclose any unspent conviction, cautions, reprimands or warnings under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975. Non-disclosure may lead to termination of employment. However, disclosure of a criminal background will not necessarily debar you from employment - this will depend upon the nature of the offence(s) and when they occurred. To read more about Ark’s safer recruitment process, please click this link. Please note we will be reviewing applications on an on-going basis and this role may close earlier than advertised depending on the level of response. We strongly encourage to submit your application at your earliest convenience.

item.title: Digital Marketing Executive
item.description: Annual leave: 33 days (plus eight bank holidays) Benefits: enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave, and shared parental pay family-friendly policies 8% employer pension contribution (Aviva) life assurance cover at 3 x annual salary health cashback plan (Medicash): employee cover plus up to four dependent children 24/7 virtual GP access (UK registered), plus access to Best Doctors confidential employee assistance programme (Medicash) access to a wellbeing app flexible working options including hybrid working, flexible working patterns such as part-time, compressed hours, and more* learning and development opportunities including bespoke training and access to LinkedIn Learning) commitment to employee health and wellbeing. We have a Menopause Friendly accreditation and are a Disability Confident employer Dementia UK is looking for a Digital Marketing Executive to join our Marketing and Communications team on a 12-month maternity cover. This is an exciting opportunity to help deliver high-performing digital campaigns that raise vital funds, grow our reach and engage supporters with Dementia UK’s work. You will take ownership of paid digital campaigns, from development and launch through to optimisation and reporting. Alongside campaign delivery, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to our evolving digital engagement strategy, helping shape processes, ways of working and how the digital team collaborates with fundraising and other teams across the charity. You will develop and manage paid social campaigns, optimise audience targeting and use performance data to improve results. You’ll produce clear, insightful reporting and recommendations, translating campaign performance for stakeholders and helping teams understand what we can learn and apply to future activity. You’ll have proven experience running paid digital campaigns on Meta, with a good understanding of campaign tracking, optimisation and reporting. You’ll be confident interpreting data and communicating results clearly to non-digital colleagues, with the ability to manage campaigns independently while collaborating effectively across teams. Experience of working within charity fundraising or knowledge of, would be an advantage. Join Dementia UK at an exciting time for our digital engagement work where you will have the autonomy to deliver impactful campaigns and the opportunity to help shape how we use digital to engage supporters and grow our impact. Our culture In addition to offering a competitive salary and a generous benefits package, we truly value our people. It’s important for us to create a workplace culture that looks after our people to support them in achieving their full potential. You will become part of a diverse and dedicated team who are supported to use and develop their skills. We recognise and value the key role you will play in delivering our strategic plans for the benefit of those living with dementia. Our staff have a voice. Representatives from different roles and levels across the organisation lead and positively contribute to our working groups around health and wellbeing, menopause, and equity, diversity and inclusion. Our supportive and nurturing workplace culture has recently earnt us recognition as the Sunday Times Best Place to Work in the non-profit and charities sector 2025 (big organisation). Dementia UK is proud to welcome everyone. We aim for a truly inclusive culture with talented, diverse teams that represent a variety of backgrounds, perspectives and skills. We celebrate differences and individuality and encourage everyone to feel comfortable being themselves at work. Dementia UK is a Disability Confident employer. By applying to join Dementia UK, you acknowledge that in the event you are successful for the role, any offer and your ongoing employment will be conditional on you having or obtaining the right to work in the UK. *Please note that any decision on flexible working is based on business needs

item.title: Service Manager- Domestic Violence and Abuse services
item.description: This is an exciting opportunity to lead and develop services that support people experiencing Domestic Violence and Abuse across Bath and Northeast Somerset. You'll manage and inspire local teams, drive service improvements, and work closely with commissioners and partners to ensure clients are safe and receive high-quality support that enables them to move forward with confidence and independence Job Role: Service Manager- Domestic Violence and Abuse services Salary: £ 34,505 per year Hours: 37.5 hours per week Contract type: Permanent Location: BANES Additional information: Participate in an out-of-hours on-call rota. About Alongside: Alongside is the new name for Julian House. We work with people experiencing social exclusion across the South and West of England, providing outreach, accommodation and support. Our clients may be sleeping rough, fleeing abuse, rebuilding after trauma, leaving prison, recovering from addiction, or trying to settle safely in a new community. Whatever their starting point, we work alongside people to help build safety, stability and independence. If you’d like a real sense of job satisfaction, great career prospects and a competitive benefits package, you could be who we’re looking for! About the Role: We are looking for an experienced and passionate Service Manager to lead our Domestic Abuse Housing services across the BANES (Bath & Northeast Somerset) area. This is an exciting leadership opportunity for someone who is committed to delivering high-quality, trauma-informed support for people experiencing social exclusion, including survivors of domestic abuse. You will be responsible for managing local projects, leading and developing staff teams, driving service improvements, and ensuring contractual, quality, and performance targets are achieved. Working closely with commissioners, partner agencies, and the wider Alongside leadership team, you will ensure services remain person-centred, strength-based, and focused on achieving positive outcomes for clients. You will maintain a visible presence within services, support staff to deliver excellent client support, and help shape service development across the region. What You'll Be Doing Lead, motivate and develop a team delivering high-quality, trauma-informed support services. Ensure clients receive person-centred support that helps them achieve positive outcomes and greater independence. Build strong relationships with commissioners, partner agencies and other stakeholders across the BANES area. Drive service quality, performance and continuous improvement across multiple projects. Oversee housing and operational management, ensuring services remain safe, compliant and effective. Maintain Safelives Leading Lights standards across service delivery What We're Looking For Essential Experience managing teams within housing, domestic abuse, homelessness, social care or support services. Strong leadership skills with the ability to develop and inspire high-performing teams. Knowledge of safeguarding, trauma-informed practice and supporting people experiencing social exclusion. Experience managing service performance and achieving positive outcomes. Excellent communication and partnership-building skills. Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle. Desirable Experience of working in the statutory or voluntary sector. IDVA/ISVA/Safelives Service Manager qualification or equivalent Please note: Job descriptions are not exhaustive, and the successful candidate may occasionally be asked to take on other duties that align with the key responsibilities outlined. You can view the full job description by clicking here . What we’re looking for: Knowledge and understanding of the support needs of people experiencing domestic violence and abuse, facing homelessness, including those with mental health challenges, complex needs and substance misuse issues. Experience working with people who may have multiple and complex needs and/or challenging behaviours due to their experience of trauma and abuse. There are many great reasons to join our team! Access to our Rewards Platform, which includes an Employee Assistance Programme and Health Cash Plan 27 days annual leave , including an extra day off for your birthday, plus bank holidays - increasing up to 30 days after 4 years of continuous employment (pro rata for part-time staff) 30% staff discount at our charity shops A generous and competitive pension scheme A supportive culture where staff feedback is highly valued and regular supervisions with line managers are conducted Great opportunities for career development and free monthly training sessions from experienced facilitators For all the fantastic and valuable work, you’ll be doing, you’ll be eligible for the Blue Light Card which offers amazing discounts on thousands of brands Reflective Practice sessions from objective, external facilitators Our Ethos As an Equal Opportunities employer, we have an Equality and Diversity Action plan in place showing our commitment in ensuring continuous improvement in creating an inclusive culture. We also have a committed group of Inclusion & Diversity champions who meet monthly to ensure progress is being made. We invite applications from people from all backgrounds and cultures, especially minority groups that are underrepresented in the workplace. We also welcome applications from those with lived experience. We embrace flexibility and are proud to be a Disability Confident and Mindful employer, as well as an Armed Forces Covenant Supporter. If you have any special access requirements or other support needs throughout the application process (including interview), please contact us so that we can let you know how we can support you. We accept CVs and applications in all formats. DBS Checks We welcome applications from people with lived experience. All applicants working with our clients will be expected to undertake an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check. A criminal conviction will not necessarily prevent you from becoming an employee, the decision will depend on the type of offence and its relevance to the role. If you would like to discuss any convictions you may have, please contact the person named in the advert. All information will be dealt with according to our Data Protection Policy.

item.title: Community Youth Work Manager, Oasis Community Hub, Waterloo
item.description: Community Youth Work Manager Oasis Community Hub, Waterloo Hours: 40 hours per week Contract type: 1-year fixed term Salary: £34,030 per annum (including London Weighting) Supporting young people to thrive in Waterloo Do you believe in the potential of every young person? Are you an experienced youth practitioner who can combine excellent frontline practice with leadership, strategic thinking and partnership working? Oasis Hub Waterloo is looking for a Community Youth Work Manager to lead and develop our youth services for young people aged 10+ across North Lambeth. Oasis Hub Waterloo has been part of the Waterloo community for more than 20 years. We’re an ambitious, inclusive and Christ-centred organisation working alongside local people to build a community where everyone is included, can contribute and can reach their potential. Our youth service has been working with young people in North Lambeth for more than a decade. We provide accessible, supportive and trauma-responsive services that help young people build confidence, make positive choices and thrive in our community. About the role This is an exciting opportunity to shape and lead our youth work at a time of development You’ll manage a small team of youth practitioners and sessional workers while staying connected to frontline delivery. You’ll oversee and deliver group activities, after-school drop-ins and one-to-one mentoring, as well as developing holiday programmes, youth leadership and social action opportunities. You’ll also help shape the future of our youth provision, working with colleagues across Oasis Hub Waterloo to develop our 0–18 strategy and create new, collaborative services. Partnership working is central to the role. You’ll develop strong relationships with Oasis Academy South Bank , local youth organisations, community partners and statutory services, helping connect education, health and community provision around the needs of young people. About you You’ll bring significant experience of working directly with young people aged 10+, alongside the skills and confidence to lead and develop a youth service. You’ll have: · Strong youth work practice, including group and one-to-one work. · Experience of developing and delivering youth programmes or projects. · Experience of managing or supervising staff, sessional workers or volunteers. · Strong partnership and multi-agency working skills. · A thorough understanding of safeguarding and child protection. · Experience of monitoring, evaluating and improving services. · Creativity, initiative and the ability to develop new opportunities for young people. · A genuine passion for helping young people thrive. Knowledge of youth services in Lambeth or Southwark, and experience of education, youth leadership, social action or statutory services, would be particularly welcome. Join us You’ll join an innovative and supportive charity where you’ll have the opportunity to make a tangible difference to young people and help shape the future of youth work in Waterloo. Oasis is committed to inclusion and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. The role includes regular evening and some weekend work and is subject to an enhanced DBS check. As part of the package, Oasis offers: · A pension scheme, offering 7% employer contribution. · A generous holiday allowance, starting at 25 days per year (plus 8 Bank Holidays). · Policies which promote well-being and are family friendly. To apply, please send your CV and a Supporting Statement (no more than two A4 pages). Please expand on your CV in your cover letter to explain why you would be a good fit for the role. Please include how you would balance frontline youth delivery with leadership and management responsibilities. Please also give an example of a piece of youth work you are particularly proud of, explaining what you did and what difference it made. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Completed applications should be returned by 9am Tuesday 6th October 2026 . Interviews: Date to be confirmed. W e actively encourage applications from people of all ethnic backgrounds and underrepresented groups. If you require any assistance to overcome potential barriers during the recruitment process, please let us know. We appreciate you may wish to use AI to support elements of your application but we strongly encourage all candidates to submit applications that genuinely reflect their own skills, achievements and lived experiences. It's what makes your application stand out! Oasis is committed to making a difference to the lives of the communities it works in, and as such you must show a willingness to demonstrate commitment to the values and behaviours which flow from the Oasis ethos. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. We expect all staff to share this commitment and to undergo appropriate checks, including enhanced DBS checks. The successful candidates must have the right to work in the UK. Oasis cannot assist with sponsorship or visas. Oasis supports Equal Opportunities. Registered Charity No. 1163889

item.title: East Grinstead Foodbank Manager
item.description: Overview The role of Foodbank Manager is to oversee the operations of the East Grinstead Foodbank, with concern for its efficiency and standards within the Trussell franchise. This will include the strategic direction and financial sustainability of the Foodbank and with the wider team the reputation of the Foodbank and its partnerships with other voluntary organisations and governmental organisations. The Foodbank Manager reports to the Trustees, including submitting a report to, and attending Trustee meetings. Responsibilities Strategic Leadership In co-ordination with the Trustees, to shape, implement and review the strategic development of the Foodbank, aligned with its mission, vision and values Management Advocacy and External Relations Fundraising and Financial Management Compliance and reporting Ensure compliance with the relevant statutory obligations of the CIO, including the Charities Commission, food standards, health and safety, safeguarding and the other policies of East Grinstead Foodbank Staff and Volunteers Reporting to Trustees Routine oversight Foodbank Manager - Person Description Essential Working knowledge of statutory compliance in a small organisation, including staff, health and safety, safeguarding and GDPR Desirable Terms This is a permanent post. It is subject to a six-month initial probationary period. The post is part-time, currently at 21 hours per week. Hours may be worked flexibly subject to agreement with the Trustees. The Foodbank is based at Jubilee Community Centre, Charlwoods Road, East Grinstead, West Sussex RH19 2HL. Competitive salary for the charitable sector reviewed annually in January. Benefits: All paid staff are entitled to be part of the NEST pension scheme. Holidays: Paid holiday entitlement of 5.6 working weeks (pro-ratafor part-time hours worked) during a complete holiday year.The Foodbank is closed on bank holidays and these will not count as holidays. Timetable Closing date for applications: 16 October 2026 Interviews: shortly thereafter Start date: Early January 2027, to facilitate a smooth transition from the current manager.

item.title: Catchment Partnership Manager – (Rural/ Thames Valley)
item.description: Role: Catchment Partnerships Manager Salary: £39,890 -£42,544 per annum (depending on experience and skill level) Contract length: Permanent Location: Remote/ Hybrid – Oxfordshire preferable but open to other locations within catchment area, flexible working. Responsible to: Programme Manager Catchment Partnerships, or directly to Head of Improving Rivers About Thames21 Thames21 is an environmental charity which works across London and the Thames Basin to deliver high-impact nature-based solutions to the climate and biodiversity crisis by restoring rivers, whilst also connecting communities to their local green-blue spaces and inspiring long-term stewardship of them. Diversity at Thames21 Equity, Diversity and Inclusion at Thames21 is key to our success and as such we employ staff from a diverse range of backgrounds, this we feel is key in ensuring that everybody has an equal opportunity and is not treated differently or discriminated against because of their characteristics. We value the voices of our individual employees, and we strive to work in a collaborative, innovative balanced way. The postholder must actively support this. Purpose of the job To drive forward Thames21’s ‘Thames Valley’ (broadly Oxfordshire/ Buckinghamshire/ Berkshire) catchment areas programme in line with our 5-year plan and future strategies ensuring appropriate integration across Thames21 and partner organisations. This includes building and sustaining a team to reduce diffuse pollution, increase biodiversity, improve water quality, and support agricultural businesses to deliver environmental improvement works and nature friendly farming practices. The postholder requires operational experience and knowledge at catchment scale as well as project and people management experience. They will take a strategic overview of the programme and guide our growth in the thematical and geographical area, with a particular focus on the following outcomes. Work with 20 farmers each year to reduce diffuse pollution at source and flood risk. Offer advice on nature-based solutions and grant funding to farmers and landowners. Plant 30,000 trees annually. Input and support the achievement of other applicable 5-year plan targets. i.e. River restoration and catchment scale monitoring. Increase Thames21 presence in the Thames Valley, identifying opportunities, supporting, and complimenting the work of other NGOs and regional Rivers Trusts. Developing up bid initiatives to support our work within communities The role is a relatively new area of work for Thames21 and may consist of supporting a range of projects and programmes including Catchment Partnerships, Farm Clusters and Natural Flood Management. Finally, the postholder will take a lead in progressing Thames21’s resilience strategy i.e. working closely with the Fundraising Team, the Catchment Partnership Team, and partner organisations to increase private and public investment to deliver healthy resilient rivers and catchments. Additional requirements may include supporting other Thames21 projects and funding applications, as the need arises. Main Duties and Responsibilities You will oversee and manage the delivery of diverse projects. You will also develop your team’s scope, strategy and action plan in order to grow the team to deliver 5-year plan targets work closely with expert (e.g. statutory bodies, authorities, NGOs and academics) and non-expert (e.g. community groups and volunteers) stakeholders to develop, fund and deliver projects within the catchments, and oversee their management. You will also work closely with the Assistant/ Head of Improving Riversand other members of the Thames21 team to develop funding applications and steer the direction of the catchment areas. Tasks include: · Programme Development & Integration Develop and expand the Thames Valley catchment programme in line with Thames21’s 5-year strategy, ensuring integration with other teams. · Funding & Financial Management Secure diverse funding sources and manage project budgets, including financial reporting and cost tracking to meet objectives. · Project & Risk Management Lead project delivery, monitor progress, and identify risk mitigation strategies to ensure continued success. · Team Leadership & Staff Development Manage and support staff through training, appraisals, workload balancing, and adherence to health and safety requirements. · Stakeholder Engagement Build and maintain relationships with internal teams, funding bodies, landowners and other external stakeholders. · Technical & Farm Advisory Support Provide farm advice, generate reports (including GIS mapping), and maintain a database of visits and environmental opportunities. · Catchment-Based Approach Advocacy Promote and apply catchment-based principles internally and externally in water and land management. · Health, Safety & Compliance Ensure compliance with health and safety policies and broader regulatory requirements across all projects. · Information & Data Management Maintain accurate documentation and project data systems, supporting transparency and accountability. · Promotion & Communications Support production of publicity materials and represent Thames21’s work to broader audiences. Other Duties This job description cannot cover every issue or task that may arise within Thames21. At various times the post-holder will be directed to carry out other reasonable duties in support of other Thames21 activities that are consistent with those in this Job Description. For more information, please see the attached Job Description. This role is ideal for those who: · Enjoy managing people and projects · Enjoy working with project partners and other key stakeholders · Are self-motivated and be happy to research for answers to questions · Are comfortable working in a flexible role, where change happens and being able to flex with change · Are comfortable to work across multiple projects · Are comfortable working at speed · Are happy to work in a role which comprises both desk work and field work · Are happy working outside in a waterside environment in a variety of weathers – alone; and/ or with team members, volunteers and professionals Additional Information · The post holder must be willing to occasionally work in the evening and at weekends. · 25 days paid annual leave plus public holidays. In addition, the Thames21 office is closed between Christmas and New Year. · Thames21 operate a flexitime system of working. · Thames21 have an ‘Auto Enrol’ Workplace Pension Scheme with NEST. · 24/7 access to our employee assistance programme. · Season ticket loan · Laptop & Mobile phone for company use. • Opportunity to join IWGB which is a recognised trade union within Thames21 To apply for this position please, email an up-to-date copy of your CV and a covering letter and apply via the Charity Job button. The closing date for applications is: 5pm, 6 October 2026 Interview dates: Week commencing 19 October 2026 (subject to change) We appreciate the time you will have taken to apply to this role, and we do appreciate that it is disconcerting when you don’t hear back from a role you have applied for. However, due to the high number of applications we expect to receive, we are unable respond to or give feedback on individual applications, but we do want to be able manage expectations. Therefore, if you do not hear from us within 4 weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has not been successful on this occasion. Please advise in your application if you are happy for us to contact you for any future opportunities should they arise, if you are not successful for this position. No agencies please.

item.title: Evaluation and Impact Coordinator
item.description: Evaluation and Impact Coordinator Hours: Full-Time (35 hours per week) Contract(s): 1x Permanent role Salary: £30,500 - £35,500 per annum, plus Into Film Benefits Location: Edinburgh, Belfast, Cardiff, Salford or London. We operate in a hybrid pattern, combining home working with attendance at the office. About Into Film Into Film is the UK’s leading charity for film in education and the community. We provide screen industry careers information and advice, support young filmmakers, and bring the power of moving image storytelling into classroom teaching. We also run the annual Into Film Festival which enables more than 400,000 pupils to visit the cinema for free, and the Into Film Awards - the UK’s leading showcase for young filmmaking talent. The core Into Film programme is free for UK state schools, colleges and other youth settings, thanks to support from the BFI, awarding National Lottery good cause funding, and through other key funders including Cinema First and Northern Ireland Screen. Our vision – Film enriches the life of every child and young person. Our mission – To inspire and support young people to learn, and to realise their creative, cultural and career aspirations, through film and the moving image. Into Film operates a hybrid working policy with offices in London, Cardiff, Belfast, Bristol, Edinburgh and Salford. We are open to flexible working models wherever the role allows, including working compressed hours. We also offer a range of staff benefits and perks which are detailed below. Role Summary This new role is responsible for supporting and developing our research, reporting and evaluation function. Our ambition is to provide accurate reporting to our funders, supporters and education and sector partners and high-quality insights and data about the important role that film and screen culture plays in the educational and personal development and future career aspirations of young people aged 5-19. You will be key to developing and improving our reporting, research and evaluation work at Into Film. In addition, you will support the Head of Impact and Research as well as the Leadership team to ensure the effective reporting and evaluation of the impact of our programmes for our funders and other internal and external stakeholders. Working collaboratively and closely with colleagues across the organisation, this function supports and informs our programme design and development, our income generation and our policy and comms outputs. Main Responsibilities: Support the Head of Impact and Research to grow and develop Into Film's research and evaluation function Support and feed into improvements to and implementation of our organisational theory of change, evaluation framework and impact strategy Under the guidance of the Head of Impact and Research, take the lead on setting and delivering high-quality research and evaluation design, analysis and reporting across the organisation Lead improvements to and implementation of programme-level evaluation frameworks, ensuring input from our programme delivery teams and other key internal stakeholders (e.g. fundraising, marcomms, senior leadership) Provide expert qualitative or mixed-methods research and evaluation support for colleagues, including but not limited to: Providing advice and guidance on research design and methodologies Providing advice and guidance on data collection using focus groups, interviews and case studies Leading and championing best practice for qualitative data collection and analysis as part of monitoring, evaluation, impact and reporting across the organisation Take the lead on implementing improvements to evaluation processes to ensure effective qualitative data management and robust analytical and reporting processes Under the guidance of the Head of Impact and Research, work effectively with the wider Into Film team, including: Keeping colleagues up to date with new research as it is published Working closely with the digital team to understand and develop efficient data capture systems Working closely with internal teams to ensure data is effectively captured and analysed for quarterly and annual reporting Work effectively with external stakeholders to support Into Film’s impact and evaluation work, including: Supporting engagement with our Research and Insight Advisory Group Engaging with partnership research into the impact of using film in education, the benefits of filmmaking and film watching opportunities, and the impact of creative careers guidance and work experience for young people Effectively working with our established Youth Advisory Council and Education Advisory Group, ensuring their expertise informs our research and evaluation work General Responsibilities: Commitment to quality internally and in all dealings with Into Film’s stakeholders including teachers, children and young people, industry partners, funders, supporters, parents and carers, and members of the public Commitment and active participation in helping Into Film live its EEDI values and ethos through everything it does Contribute to long term planning to ensure growth in line with demand and resources Contribute to the regular monitoring and evaluation of Into Film’s work Any other reasonable duties assigned by Into Film Person Specification: Minimum Requirements: Experience in an impact and/or evaluation function Qualitative data analysis expertise, through formal qualification or hands-on experience – must be comfortable with qualitative data management, analysis and reporting Knowledge of the education, skills, creative industries or charity sector space A collaborative colleague who will thrive in a dynamic, responsive cross-organisational role An excellent writer, presenter and communicator who is willing to represent Into Film at in-person meetings and events Experience supporting design and delivery of effective and inclusive evaluation methodologies to demonstrate impact and gather useful learning from programme participants Demonstrable stakeholder management experience, working closely with colleagues and external research partners to support the delivery of multiple high-quality, robust, mixed-method evaluations Experience of supporting colleagues to use evaluation data alongside the wider research and evidence base to shape programme design Experience of providing data and support to external organisations who have been commissioned to provide specialised research Up-to-date knowledge of the formal education sector in England and at least one other devolved nation Desirable: Experience of theory-based evaluation, formative evaluation and implementation and process evaluation approaches Familiarity with the Microsoft Office suite A love and knowledge of film All employees regularly working with children and member data are required to undertake and maintain enhanced DBS clearance (and/or Access NI check or Disclosure Scotland check, depending on working location), acquired at Into Film’s expense; employment is dependent upon this. We also offer a range of staff benefits and perks, including: Annual Leave – 28 days (full time/pro-rata), including 3 days to cover office closure between Christmas and New Year. Pension – matched up to 5% of salary (2% above statutory employer contribution). Flexible working including compressed hours, job share etc. – all applications favourably considered, approval will be at the discretion of Into Film. Enhanced parental/paternity/shared parental leave. Interest-free non-essential study loans. Interest-free bike/scooter/travelcard loan. Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) – 24/7 confidential wellbeing support, advice and guidance. Wisdom health insurance cover – non-contributory (apart from employee tax contribution). BenefitHub portal – offering discounts on healthcare, wellbeing products, and lifestyle products and services. Closing: 12:00am, 14th October 2026 (BST) Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. No agencies please.

item.title: EA to CEO (mat cover)
item.description: Charity People is delighted to be recruiting on behalf of the Florence Nightingale Foundation (FNF) for an experienced Executive Assistant to provide maternity cover for this pivotal role at the heart of the organisation. The Florence Nightingale Foundation develops nursing and midwifery leaders at every stage of their careers, enabling them to stay, thrive, lead and transform health and care. Through leadership programmes, scholarships, policy influence and professional development, the Foundation supports healthcare professionals across the UK and internationally. This is an opportunity to join a highly respected charity at an exciting stage of growth and transformation. Working closely with the CEO, Executive Team and Board, you'll play a central role in ensuring the smooth running of governance, executive support and organisational coordination. Job Details Role: Executive Assistant (Maternity Cover) Salary: £39,898 Contract: Fixed-Term Contract (up to 12 months) Hours: 35 hours per week Location: London SE1 with hybrid working Reports to: Chief Executive Officer Interviews: October 2026 Start Date: November 2026 preferred, allowing for handover with the current postholder About the Role This is a varied and fast-paced Executive Assistant role supporting a busy CEO and Executive Team within a small but ambitious charity. You'll provide high-level executive support while also coordinating Board and Committee activity, helping to ensure effective governance, communication and organisational efficiency. The role suits someone who enjoys taking ownership, thrives on variety and can confidently work with senior stakeholders. Key responsibilities include: Providing proactive support to the CEO, Executive Team and Board Chair Managing complex diaries, meetings and travel arrangements Preparing presentations, reports, board papers and briefing documents Coordinating Board, Committee and AGM meetings Taking accurate minutes and tracking actions Supporting trustee recruitment, induction and development Maintaining governance records and supporting compliance requirements Supporting organisational projects and continuous improvement initiatives Acting as a trusted point of coordination across the Foundation About You We're looking for an experienced Executive Assistant who is highly organised, adaptable and able to work confidently with senior leaders. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change quickly. You'll have excellent judgement, strong attention to detail and the confidence to manage competing demands while maintaining a calm and professional approach. You'll bring: Previous Executive Assistant experience supporting senior executives Experience supporting Boards, Committees or governance processes Strong organisational and prioritisation skills Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities Experience preparing papers, reports and meeting documentation High levels of discretion and professionalism Confidence working independently and using your initiative Strong digital and technology skills Experience working within a charity, membership body, healthcare or public sector environment would be advantageous Why Join the Florence Nightingale Foundation? The Foundation offers a collaborative and supportive working environment where every member of the team contributes to improving health and care outcomes. Benefits include: 27 days annual leave plus festive closure days Hybrid and flexible working Generous pension contributions Employee assistance programme LinkedIn Learning access Ongoing professional development support A friendly and highly committed team culture This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Executive Assistant who enjoys governance, thrives in a collaborative environment and wants to contribute to an organisation making a genuine difference across health and care. If you're an Executive Assistant, Senior Executive Assistant, Governance & Executive Officer, Board Support Officer or EA to a CEO looking for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.

item.title: People Advisor
item.description: People Advisor Salary : From £31,126 per annum (full time equivalent), paid pro rata based on contracted hours Location : Norwich Office (with travel across Charity sites as required) – Hybrid working Hours : Up to 30 hours per week, with a minimum of 22.5 hours per week. Flexible approach to weekly working hours will be considered. Contract : Permanent East Anglian Air Ambulance is a regional charity that provides life-saving care across Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Norfolk, Suffolk and beyond. With two state-of-the-art helicopters and a fleet of critical care vehicles, our expert teams of doctors and paramedics bring advanced pre‑hospital emergency medical care directly to people when they need it most. We have an exciting opportunity for a People Advisor to join our life-saving charity. About the role: People are at the heart of everything we do. As a charity dedicated to delivering life-changing services, we know that supporting our employees to thrive is essential to achieving our mission. We're looking for an experienced, proactive and people focused People Advisor to join our People Team. This is an opportunity to make a real difference, helping shape the experience of employees across the organisation while contributing to a culture where everyone feels valued, supported and able to perform at their best. As a trusted Advisor, you will partner with managers and colleagues across the organisation, providing expert guidance on a wide range of people matters. You will be able to contribute to employee relations matters and organisational change projects, to recruitment, wellbeing and equality, diversity and inclusion initiatives. You will play a key role in helping us create a positive and supportive workplace culture. Reporting to the Head of People, you will: Build strong relationships with managers and teams, supporting them through the full employee lifecycle. Lead recruitment activity and partner with managers to attract and retain talented people. Support organisational development initiatives, restructures and change programmes. Act as a trusted advisor, providing expert guidance on employee relations matters. Contribute to the development and review of people policies and processes. Help shape and deliver wellbeing, engagement and EDI initiatives. Support workforce reporting, analytics and payroll processes, using data to drive continuous improvement. Champion a positive, inclusive and values-led employee experience. You’ll bring: CIPD Level 5 qualification or equivalent experience. Proven experience managing employee relations casework. Up-to-date knowledge of employment legislation and HR best practice. Experience supporting organisational development and people-focused projects. Strong analytical skills and confidence using HR systems and people data. Excellent communication, influencing and problem-solving abilities. The ability to build credibility quickly and work effectively with managers at all levels. A collaborative, solutions-focused approach and a genuine passion for helping people thrive at work. Why join us? This is an opportunity to join a charity that is committed to supporting and developing its people. You'll work alongside dedicated colleagues who are passionate about making a difference and be given the opportunity to contribute to meaningful projects that support employee wellbeing, engagement and inclusion. Most importantly, you'll help create an environment where our colleagues can do their best work and continue delivering outstanding services to the communities we support. N.B. The exact days worked in the office will be agreed with the successful candidate, but you must live within a commutable distance of Norwich. Closing Date: Monday 05 October (9am) First Stage Interview Date: Thursday 08 October (to be held in person at Helimed House, Norwich) Second Stage: date to be confirmed, tentatively Thursday 15 October ( to be held in person at Helimed House, Norwich) Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website where you can complete your application for this position. No agencies please.

item.title: Head of Fundraising (Mat Cover)
item.description: Contract: 12-15 months (Maternity Cover) Salary: £48,250–£51,189 (pro rata where applicable) Hours: 5 days/week, applications from candidates seeking flexible or reduced hours welcome Start date: November/December 2026 We are looking for a capable and innovative Head of Fundraising (Maternity Cover) to join Z2K later this year. Someone who: has a strong track record across fundraising disciplines, ideally including trusts and foundations; can evolve and implement our fundraising strategy; is confident building relationships with funders, donors and senior stakeholders; can spot opportunities to diversify income and turn ideas into action; can make a compelling case for change, using evidence, impact and people’s experiences; enjoys working collaboratively and can bring colleagues with them; is comfortable working in a small organisation where everyone gets involved. Why join us? You’ll have the opportunity to shape fundraising at a pivotal point in Z2K’s development. You’ll work closely with the Chief Executive, Trustees and colleagues with real scope to develop new income streams and relationships. And you’ll be fundraising for a charity where the connection between money, impact and social change is direct and tangible. About Z2K Right now, one in five people in the UK are living in poverty, and the depth of financial hardship is worse than ever. Our vision is of a world where everyone lives a life free from poverty. Founded in 1997, Z2K provides specialist services to help people access the benefits they are entitled to and to prevent homelessness. We challenge the power structures that create poverty in the first place, campaigning for change. And we work alongside experts by experience in everything we do. Our values: Power-sharing, fearless, curious, inclusive, caring. How to apply Please send your CV and a statement (1200 words max.) outlining why you are applying for the role and your relevant skills and experience. Closing Date: 11 October 2026, 5pm First interview: 21/22 October 2026 (online) Final interview: 26 October 2026 (in person) A commitment to the aims and values of Z2K is essential. Z2K is an equal opportunity employer. People with lived experience of poverty, from global majority backgrounds, LGBTQIA+ individuals and disabled people are strongly encouraged to apply. We welcome evidence of experience from both work and non-work settings such as volunteering and personal life.
