item.title: Communications & PR Officer (maternity cover)
item.description: Glaucoma UK is the charity for people with glaucoma. Our vision is to end preventable glaucoma sight loss. We want everyone with glaucoma to be able to live well with the condition, and to make this a reality. More than 10,000 people took part in our National Patient Voices Survey, creating the most powerful picture yet of what it is like to live with glaucoma and receive glaucoma care across the UK. Working closely with our Head of Communications and a specialist public affairs agency, you will help bring those findings to life, secure media attention and make decision-makers listen. Central to this will be finding and sensitively supporting people who are willing to share their experiences, cultivating trusted relationships and helping them tell their stories confidently across print, digital and broadcast media. Alongside this landmark work, you will create engaging content across our magazine, website, email and social media channels, identify opportunities for national coverage and help strengthen and protect Glaucoma UK’s voice and reputation. This is a varied and influential role for an excellent storyteller with strong media instincts who wants their work to make a genuine difference. Position: Communications & PR Officer (maternity cover) Responsible to: Head of Communications Location: Home-based with occasional travel to our head office in Ashford, Kent Hours: 35 per week Contract: 12 months fixed-term (from December 2026) Salary: £34,077 per annum Annual leave and benefits: 25 days holiday per annum (rising by one day per year to 28 days after 3 years’ service), plus Statutory Public Holidays, pro-rated for part-time employees. Up to 5% contributory pension Benenden Healthcare cover including 24/7 Employee Assistance Programme How to apply: Click the CharityJob Apply button below. You’ll be asked to submit a CV and answer a few short screening questions about your relevant skills and motivation. Interviews will take place in the week commencing 21 October. Closing date: Sunday 11 October at 11pm What you’ll be working on: · Proactively creating and delivering high quality, inspiring multi-channel content (including, but not limited to, our quarterly members magazine, awareness campaigns, email marketing schedule, social media and website) to engage key stakeholders and attract new followers to our cause. · Playing a key role in the production of our quarterly member’s magazine; actively contributing to editorial meetings, writing articles, conducting interviews, editing copy, and overseeing timelines through to print and despatch. · Working with the Head of Communications to develop key messages, briefings, and positioning statements to ensure consistency and maximise the impact of our campaigns and manage approval processes internally. · Working alongside the Digital Communications Manager to ensure the website and social media is updated regularly with compelling and quality content. · Providing copywriting and editing support across all internal and external communications for all departments to maintain consistent tone, style and messaging across all outputs and act as a ‘brand guardian’ together with colleagues in the communications team. · Leading on the delivery of an ongoing programme to recruit and develop relationships with patient case studies, celebrity supporters and influencers who can help raise our public profile through the media and other opportunities. This job is for you if… · you have experience of working in a similar role either in-house or in an agency. · you have excellent copywriting and proofreading skills. · you have experience of crisis communications. · you have experience of developing compelling content for print, digital and broadcast communications channels, accurately conveying information and engaging with a wide range of stakeholders. · you have a track record of generating media coverage to deliver messages to a range of audiences. · are a strategic thinker who considers the wider context when planning activity and can sense compelling story opportunities.
item.dc:creator: Glaucoma UK

item.title: People & Culture Advisor
item.description: About The Role Together we can change children’s lives. At Place2Be, we believe every child should have easy access to mental health support whenever they need it. We create a safe place in schools where children and young people can open up without pressure or stigma. Allowing our highly skilled and diverse counsellors to reach children, young people and their families who need us. As People and Culture Advisor, you will play an important role in helping us create a positive colleague experience. Working closely with managers and colleagues across the organisation, you will provide practical, timely and people-centred advice on a wide range of people matters. You will support managers to navigate employee relations matters with confidence, contribute to projects and policy development, and use data and insight to drive continuous improvement. This role is ideal for someone who combines sound people practice knowledge with compassion, curiosity and a genuine commitment to supporting others. As part of a huge community across the United Kingdom you’ll have opportunities to bring your fresh thinking and ideas to the table to help us shape our programmes for today and tomorrow. You’ll have access to an enormous range of training and development and a pathway to develop and grow your career. For a career with purpose, this is your place. Recruitment Process As part of your application you will need to answer some shortlisting questions. Please answer these as fully as you can, we recommend using the STAR model. Situation, Task, Action Result. Your answers will be used in the shortlisting process. Closing date for applications: Midnight on 30 September 2026 Interview date: 07 October 2026 Our Benefits When you work at Place2Be –whether that's in a school, supporting families, providing clinical supervision, or in IT, Finance, or Fundraising –every role can make the difference to a young person. To achieve this, we ask that you bring your best self to your role and our commitment to you, is to welcome you into our community, and help you progress. Because we know that you being at your best, means the best outcomes for the children we support. Here’s just a few things we have on offer: Annual Leave that increases with service Comprehensive learning and development to enable you to progress your career 5% contributory pension scheme Life assurance of four times your annual salary A comprehensive employee assistance programme Mobile Phone Discounts (EE network) Wellbeing days to allow you some ‘you’ time Christmas holidays closure period in addition to your annual leave We welcome applications from everyone regardless of age, gender, gender identity, gender expression, ethnicity, sexual orientation, faith or disability. We are proud to be a disability confident employer and will ask you during your application If you wish to be considered for a guaranteed interview under the disability confident scheme. Under the scheme we commit to offering an interview to disabled applicants that meet the minimum criteria as outlined in the job role. We recognise that AI is becoming part of daily life and you may want to use it to help you format your CV, create responses to application questions or even help you prepare responses. AI can be a powerful enabler and we are open to you using it to apply for roles with us, but we ask you to ensure anything you submit truly represents your capabilities and viewpoint. We value honesty, integrity and creativity and want to understand what you will uniquely bring to our team. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible.
item.dc:creator: Place2Be

item.title: Community Fundraising Officer
item.description: Step into a pivotal fundraising role where you’ll drive income growth across regional and community channels, challenge events, and sponsorship, all while delivering excellent supporter care. This is a temporary opportunity offering remote or hybrid working based in Essex, ideal for an experienced fundraiser who can quickly make an impact and build strong donor relationships. About the Role: You will lead on planning and delivering a mix of regional and community fundraising activities, challenge events, and event sponsorship to meet agreed income targets. Working closely with internal teams and supporters, you’ll manage end-to-end campaigns, from prospecting and cultivation through to stewardship and post-event evaluation. Your work will directly enhance supporter experience and strengthen the organisation’s fundraising pipeline. Key Responsibilities: * Plan, deliver and monitor regional and community fundraising activities to achieve agreed income and engagement targets. * Coordinate and manage challenge events and other fundraising events, including logistics, communications, and on-the-day support. * Develop and manage event sponsorship opportunities, including researching prospects, preparing proposals, and securing sponsorship agreements. * Provide high-quality supporter care, ensuring timely, personalised and professional communication with donors, participants and community fundraisers. * Use the Raiser’s Edge database to record and maintain accurate supporter and event data, track income, and produce regular reports. * Implement donor cultivation plans, including follow-up, stewardship journeys and tailored engagement activities to maximise retention and uplift. * Collaborate with colleagues to create compelling fundraising materials and event collateral that support recruitment and income generation. * Monitor performance of fundraising activities, evaluating results and making recommendations to improve future campaigns. Key Requirements: * Proven experience in regional and community fundraising, including planning and delivering income-generating activities. * Track record of managing challenge events and fundraising events from concept through to delivery and evaluation. * Demonstrated ability to provide excellent supporter care and build strong, long-term relationships with donors and participants. * Experience securing and managing event sponsorship, including prospecting and negotiation. * Confident user of fundraising databases, ideally Raiser’s Edge, with strong data management and reporting skills. * Strong organisational skills, able to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a temporary, fast-paced environment. * Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to different supporter audiences. * Ability to work effectively on a remote or hybrid basis, with good self-management and proactive communication. Desirable Skills: * Experience working with charities or non-profit organisations in Essex or the surrounding region. * Knowledge of current community and events fundraising trends and best practice. * Experience developing digital promotion for fundraising and challenge events. * Familiarity with integrating fundraising campaigns across multiple channels (online, community, corporate). Qualifications: * Degree or equivalent experience in fundraising, marketing, communications, or a related field. * Professional fundraising qualification (e.g. IoF/Chartered Institute of Fundraising) is desirable. * Evidence of ongoing professional development in fundraising, supporter care or events management is an advantage. If you’re an experienced fundraiser ready to deliver results in a remote or hybrid role based in Essex, we’d like to hear from you. Apply now to help drive impactful fundraising activities during this key temporary assignment.
item.dc:creator: Harris Hill Charity Recruitment Specialists

item.title: Charity Accounts Officer
item.description: Job description Global Adventure Challenges are looking for a bright, enthusiastic and effective Charity Accounts Officer to join our award-winning team. We are a Tour Operator based near Chester who specialise in organising worldwide charity and corporate challenge events. The successful person will become an integral team member of the Sales and Marketing Team. You will be working in a fast-paced environment and will possess excellent skills in areas such as organisation, multi-tasking and have the ability to prioritise workloads, along with an excellent eye for attention to detail. We will be looking for somebody with great communication, and customer service skills allowing you and ourselves to maximise relationships with our charity clients. An interest in or experience of working in the charitable sector and/or outdoor activities such as cycling and trekking is desirable, but not essential as training for this office-based role will be given. Key tasks involved in the role are noted below: Ensuring all charity client information is recorded and kept up to date on our Microsoft Dynamics database Maintaining regular contact with our charity clients that are using our Challenges as part of their fundraising calendar Ensuring all charity clients have the appropriate support materials in order to successfully promote and recruit for our Challenges To continuously develop and retain charity clients into promoting further events Ensuring all charity information requests are dealt with on daily basis and ensuring follow up calls are made and regular contact is kept Organising and presenting at information days/nights – out of office hours and weekends. Attending and chairing meetings with charity clients Assisting in the delivery of various charity campaigns through the use of telephone, emails and paper mail shots – for new product launches, reactivation of lapsed clients and sourcing of new business Contribute to the sending of regular charity e-newsletters within the timeframes agreed by Directors and Marketing Manager Developing and suggesting new marketing and client sourcing streams for the business Posted on: 22 September 2026 Closing date: 22 October 2026 at 10:40 Tags: Communications, Business Development, Customer Service, Customer support, Events / Activities The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.
item.dc:creator: Global Adventure Challenges

item.title: Fundraising & Engagement Officer ( Individual Giving)
item.description: Job description About the Charity Our client supports vulnerable individuals and families across Bristol and South Gloucestershire, including young people who take on significant responsibilities well beyond their years. It's a small, close-knit fundraising and communications team looking to grow with the right person alongside them. About the Role This is a genuinely broad, hands-on role — the conduit between fundraising and communications activity. You'll be the first person to own a brand-new fundraising CRM system, and the first to build proper supporter journeys from a base of 600–800 contacts already in place. Two regular newsletters already go out to supporters and the people the charity works with — what's missing is someone to turn that reach into lasting relationships. This October, the charity launches its first-ever integrated fundraising and communications campaign — a Christmas appeal for the young people it supports. Depending on timing, you might join in time to help run it, or join just after and inherit real campaign data to build the next one from. Either way, it's a genuine ground-floor opportunity: no legacy systems, no inherited decisions — what you build is what exists. Key Responsibilities Lead the implementation of a new CRM system, becoming the team's go-to on supporter data Design and build supporter journeys for regular givers and donors from scratch Support delivery of a major Christmas fundraising campaign and future appeals Work closely with the Communications Manager, plugging fundraising into existing newsletters Build authentic case studies and stories with the charity's young people's voice & participation team Help identify new income opportunities alongside the Fundraising Manager once the fundamentals are in place About You Experience of fundraising, supporter care, customer engagement or communications, with excellent written and verbal skills Comfortable owning a CRM yourself — able to run reports and understand segmentation, not just direct someone else in it (specific CRM experience is a bonus, not a requirement) A track record delivering campaigns, appeals or multi-channel engagement activity Strong organisational skills, able to manage several priorities and interpret data to recommend improvements High standards of accuracy and confidentiality, with a sound understanding of data protection and ethical fundraising Desirable: individual giving, regular giving or community fundraising background; experience with Gift Aid and fundraising platforms; charity or social care sector experience. You can read the full brief here https://lnkd.in/p/eDV6sZfR Posted on: 22 September 2026 Closing date: 22 October 2026 at 11:50 Job ref: 3673024 Tags: Campaigns, Communications, Fundraising, Business Development, CRM, Database Management, Engagement / Outreach, Community Fundraising, Direct / Supporters, Individual Giving
item.dc:creator: Raise + Recruit

item.title: Communications and Media Manager
item.description: Teens Unite is leading the way in youth cancer support. We’re an energetic, ambitious and dynamic charity improving the lives of 13-24-year-olds living with, and beyond, cancer. We’re not here to cure cancer. We’re here to empower young people to rebuild their lives and thrive beyond a diagnosis. This is an incredibly exciting time to join the team. We’re growing rapidly, working alongside major brands and global organisations – from YouTube to Warner Bros. - as well as influencers and celebrity ambassadors, from the Sidemen to Grace Andrews. We’re also growing our media presence across everything from podcasts and radio including Capital FM, all to raise awareness of our work and generate the vital support needed to reach more young people. From leading influential campaigns and securing media opportunities, to demonstrating our impact to corporate partners and supporters and acting as a guardian of the Teens Unite brand, this role is about amplifying our voice at every level. You’ll help ensure our message and purpose are clear, our impact is seen and understood, and more people are inspired to support our work. And we’re about to embark on our most ambitious chapter yet. We’re building the first purpose-built retreat in England for young people overcoming cancer. This pioneering, first-of- its-kind development will transform the support available to young people for generations to come. Who you are: You’re creative and proactive, with a talent for compelling storytelling, and a special way with words - whether it’s pitching a media story, keeping supporters updated on the difference they’ve made, or creating a campaign that turns heads, stops scrolling and encourages people to click the donate button. You’ll seek new opportunities, spot potential and think differently about how Teens Unite can continue to grow its voice, influence and reach. You’ll be excited by the opportunity to help take Teens Unite to the next level, finding new and innovative ways to raise awareness, build our profile and ensure more people understand the difference our work makes to young people living with, and beyond, cancer. At the same time, you’ll understand the importance of a strong and consistent brand. You’ll have the confidence to push boundaries and explore new ideas while ensuring everything we communicate remains true to the Teens Unite voice, personality, values and brand guidelines. Driven by purpose, you’ll be excited by the opportunity to use your communications skills to drive real change - ensuring the voices of the young people we support are heard, inspiring more people to support our work, and positioning Teens Unite as a leading charity with influence and recognition far beyond the youth cancer sector. The role: This role is about taking our communications to the next level and ensuring the Teens Unite voice is heard louder than ever. You’ll be our go-to creative for compelling copy and standout design across print, online and digital marketing. From our website and newsletters to campaigns and supporter communications, you’ll bring the Teens Unite voice, purpose and personality to life - creating meaningful, thought-provoking communications that capture attention and inspire action. You’ll keep our supporters motivated, engaged and connected to the difference they make. From demonstrating impact to the major corporate partners we work alongside, to sharing the heartwarming stories our regular donors want to hear, you’ll ensure everyone who makes our support possible feels recognised, valued and connected to our mission. You’ll secure press opportunities through building strong relationships with journalists and media outlets, and understanding what makes a captivating news story, raising awareness of Teens Unite and the issues facing young people living with, and beyond, cancer. You’ll support the delivery of integrated marketing campaigns that support our strategic objectives, from Teenage and Young Adult Cancer Awareness Month to Mental Health Awareness Week - finding creative ways to reach new audiences, start conversations and drive action. And as we embark on our most ambitious chapter yet, you’ll also play an important role in raising the profile of our capital appeal. You’ll help build momentum, generate exposure and increase supporter engagement as we bring England’s first purpose-built retreat for young people overcoming cancer, to life. What we offer: When joining Teens Unite, you can expect: Flexible and hybrid working arrangements 33 days annual leave pro rata (inclusive of Bank Holidays) Christmas office closure Optional company-contributed pension scheme Recently refurbished offices and free on-site parking To be part of an inclusive and dynamic work environment with a dedicated and growing team Support in your personal and professional development, including access to training The opportunity to collaborate with incredible brands and organisations from Tesco to YouTube The chance to make a real-life difference in the lives of young people Essential experience and qualifications: Essential: Experience contributing to or leading multi-channel campaigns Excellent copywriting and storytelling skills Evidence of delivering marketing activity with measurable results Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities A collaborative and confident approach - comfortable contributing ideas and taking ownership of projects Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, forward-thinking organisation and adapt to changing priorities Must be able to commute to Broxbourne, Hertfordshire Desirable: Experience developing media relationships and securing press coverage Experience within the charity or not-for-profit sector Knowledge of Canva or similar design platforms Experience using email marketing platforms (e.g. Mailchimp) Experience updating website CMS systems Summary of Key Milestones The first round of interviews will commence from Monday 5th October Should a suitable candidate be found prior to the closing date, applications will close early.
item.dc:creator: Teens Unite Fighting Cancer

item.title: Legacy & In Memory Fundraiser
item.description: At Claire House, our ambition is to be one of the best places to work in the North West. We have an incredible cause to support, we’ve been offering flexible working for many years and have an awesome team of colleagues who make coming to work fun. We work hard to create a happy workplace where people thrive and feel like they’re making a genuine difference to seriously and terminally ill children in our community. Consequently, staff turnover is low, enjoyment levels are high and there’s always plenty of cake. About the role As Legacy & In Memory Fundraiser, you’ll play a vital part in supporting the Legacy & In Memory Manager to deliver our legacy and in memory fundraising strategy. Your focus will be on day-to day stewardship, engaging with supporters and handling administration. You’ll act as a first point of contact for more complex enquiries, providing excellent service and helping to build meaningful relationships. Working closely with colleagues across Fundraising, Admin and Communications, you’ll help maximise opportunities for legacy and in memory giving, maintain accurate records and ensure supporter journeys are well managed. This is a developmental role for someone looking to build their skills and experience in legacy fundraising, with plenty of scope to learn and progress within the team. The nuts and bolts of the job: • Support the Legacy & In Memory Manager in implementing legacy and in memory activities and campaigns. • Deliver high-quality stewardship and build meaningful relationships with legacy and in memory supporters. • Work with the Admin team to respond promptly and appropriately to supporter enquiries, including acting as a first point of contact for more complex enquiries. • Maximise opportunities to promote will writing and legacy giving by working collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation. • Maintain accurate supporter records and effective systems for legacy and in memory correspondence using our CRM. • Conduct research into legacy and in memory giving trends, and help keep marketing materials and digital platforms relevant and up to date. • Act as an ambassador for legacy and in memory giving, representing Claire House professionally and sensitively. What you’ll need to bring to the role • Experience of managing supporter or customer relationships, ideally within a fundraising environment. • Excellent people skills and the ability to handle sensitive conversations with tact and empathy. • Experience of managing a varied workload and working effectively in a fast-paced environment. • Highly organised, with excellent written communication skills and attention to detail. • Good IT skills and experience of maintaining accurate information on a database or CRM. • Confidence in exploring and presenting insight and data. • A collaborative and motivated approach, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team. • An understanding of fundraising regulation and the Fundraising Code of Practice, or a willingness to develop this knowledge. Closing date: Wednesday 7th October Interviews will take place on: Thursday 15th October
item.dc:creator: Claire House Children's Hospice, Wirral

item.title: Programme Lead (East Midlands)
item.description: Programme Lead - (East Midlands) Salary: £36,409 - £39,191 depending on experience, skills and qualifications* (see below for more details on remuneration) Contract: Fixed term for 12 months. A bout Voice 21 Voice 21 is the national oracy education charity. We exist to empower every child to use their voice for success in school and life. Our work transforms learning and life chances through talk by increasing access to a high-quality oracy education for those that need it most. Follow the links to find out more about why oracy is so vital and the impact Voice 21 has. Your purpose To lead professional development and school improvement programmes facilitating the Voice 21 approach in our Voice 21 Oracy Schools by delivering our high impact learning experiences and materials for teachers and school leaders. To be part of the team, designing and reviewing programme content. Y our opportunity Tackle a vital challenge, with great people. Voice 21 exists to transform children' s learning and life chances through talk and we are currently working with 1100 schools. To reach this goal we recruit great people and give them real responsibility, training and support. Output focused culture, with flexible working opportunities. We have an agile and flexible approach – our team can work when and wherever works best to deliver the requirements of their role. For staff working at home, we support them to create a workspace and provide technology that enables them to work effectively. Real development opportunities. We believe in supporting people to develop the skills they need to be excellent – whether this means funding external training, finding a mentor to support them or giving them the time to learn from others in the organisations through our regular CPD sessions. We also offer paid study leave for team members taking part in formal studies outside of work. Great benefits . 36 days holiday (inclusive of bank holidays and Christmas closure period). Holiday entitlement increases linked to length of service, 5% employer contribution to pension, interest-free season ticket, cycle and technology loans, employee assistance scheme. Remuneration. Our pay is a band and spine point approach where there is up to 6 years progression available (depending on starting point) Your responsibilities Quality programme delivery Lead high-quality professional development and school improvement programmes across our Voice 21 Oracy Schools Membership. These may be delivered in person, online or in school. Deliver transformative consultancy support, working with teachers and school leaders to design and implement bespoke improvement plans for their oracy provision, through in-school and online consultancy support. Build credibility and purposeful relationships with programme participants, both at programme days and touchpoints, and on an ongoing basis to drive impact in our schools. Be responsible for participant learning and experience on your programmes, upholding high standards for all elements such as preparation, adapting to participant needs, content and rigour, ongoing interactions and support, and participant feedback. Learning content & programme development Proactively share insights and learning from the programmes you deliver, proposing and shaping solutions to enable Voice 21 to continually improve its programme offer. Apply and share expertise through varied outputs such as teaching materials, online learning content, resources, written or video outputs. Proactively identify and respond to opportunities or gaps and fulfil briefs or commissions. Contribute to the continual improvement of Voice 21’s programmes through development and review cycles, based on first-hand learning from our schools, content expertise, programme insights and external research and evidence. Team and organisational contribution Act as an ambassador for Voice 21’s national oracy expertise, communicating the value and impact of our approach at conferences, events and through publications. Embody and communicate oracy teaching and learning expertise within the organisation, acting as a resource for the wider team and making contributions to organisational priorities, projects, campaigns and events, outputs and publications etc. Continually and proactively develop your own and others’ expertise in Voice 21’s approach to a high-quality oracy education, and use this to leverage impact for our schools through tangible learning outputs. Identify and carry out other tasks commensurate to the level and spirit of the role as required. Your experience You are an excellent teacher (primary or secondary) You are passionate about teaching and learning, and the role of talk in learning. You have used talk to support learning in your classroom. You have experience leading whole-school change and inspiring teachers to embrace new approaches and ideas. You have a knowledge of a range of speaking and listening techniques and contexts for oracy, these could include: debate, dialogic teaching, storytelling, public speaking or communication and language development. You are a strong communicator both when working in a small team and when facilitating learning for large groups of adults. You are flexible, can think on your feet and can bring your own experiences to the work we do. You are highly-organised, look for solutions and can prioritise and manage a varied workload. You are enthusiastic, willing to learn and feel you would be energised by our mission. If you do not fully meet all the above criteria, but are happy to work towards developing into the role, we would be happy to consider your application. You are willing to travel nationally on a frequent basis (3 days a week) during term time; this will include regular overnight stays. Further details Start date: ASAP Terms: Fixed term for 12 months, subject to successful probation review. Contract: We are open to applicants on a 0.8 or FTE contract Location: Home-based with frequent national travel, including overnight stays, to work with schools and attend meetings. Applicants must hold a valid UK driving licence and have access to a car they can use for work. Application details To apply: Please submit your most recent CV and a document answering the questions below: Tell us why you want to work at Voice 21. What is it about us and our mission that excites you? (Max. 400 words) Making direct reference to the job description, please tell us the three main reasons why you would make an excellent Programme Lead (Max. 400 words). Tell us about something you have achieved recently that you are proud of? (Max 200 words) Please do not apply for this position if you are not based in this area of the UK (East Midlands / London/Hertfordshire/Bedfordshire) Closing date: Friday 9th October, 9am Interview date: Provisional dates for initial phone interviews week commencing 12th October, with second round interviews on Zoom week commencing 19th October. Valuing every voice Voice 21 believes that every voice should be heard and valued. We are committed to the equal treatment of all current and prospective employees and do not condone discrimination on the basis of age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race or ethnicity, religion or belief, gender identity, or marriage and civil partnership. We aspire to have a diverse and inclusive workplace and strongly encourage suitably qualified applicants from a wide range of backgrounds to apply and join Voice 21.

item.title: Community Fundraising Executive
item.description: The Watercress Line is now looking to recruit an experienced Community Fundraising Executive . In this role, you will be responsible for supporting the fundraising strategy with executive action and targeted communications As our Community Fundraising Executive , you will be organised, patient, collaborative and have a passion for making a difference in an exciting and varied role. You will be working as part of a small paid team and a large, dedicated volunteer base. You will have an eye for detail and a flair for getting the best out of people. The Watercress Line works with different communities, each with their distinct motivations for giving. Locomotive, Railway, Local and Regional communities will be the focus of this role. Responsibilities of the Community Fundraising Executive: On site and online fundraising asks – creating and maintaining the solicitation of the public Manage website donation asks and appropriate web pages Promotion at Watercress Line and local events, coordinating the attendance at local and onsite events and the provision of suitable and relevant materials Recruit, train and support volunteers to attend events Coordinating the Membership team, including continuous training and recruitment and retention of the Membership Administration Team and volunteer administrators Coordinating fundraising communications - reviewing and monitoring all communications to ensure that the charity status of the organisation is constantly referenced Generate content and create posts for social media including LinkedIn feed Promote community fundraising events across all channels Managing the donor database Events management Reporting and budget management Required Competencies/Experience: Solid experience in a fundraising role Some experience of being a volunteer Experience of managing small events Ability to communicate effectively to a broad range of people with an understanding of the different communications channels appropriate to different generations and types of people Creative writing skills An aptitude to motivate and manage teams of volunteers The ability to manage information, keeping detailed records and making connections across information sources Excellent prioritisation skills with the ability to meet deadlines We are a heritage steam railway operated by award-winning volunteers and supported by paid staff, bringing smiles to faces through the beautiful Hampshire countryside for 50 years. We are traditional but innovative; respectful but challenging; slow-moving but fast-paced; friendly, intergenerational, real world and hands-on. We deliver social value to our volunteers and visitors; economic value to our region; and cultural value to the nation in the preservation of memories and skills of the heritage steam and diesel.

item.title: Head of Fundraising and Communications
item.description: HEAD OF FUNDRAISING AND COMMUNICATIONS Church Urban Fund (CUF) is a national charity working across England with local churches and faith-based partners who are committed to serving and strengthening the communities where they live, and overcoming poverty in all its forms. Our vision is a future where every neighbourhood across England is able to flourish. We mobilise churches, faith groups and local people to overcome poverty and build stronger, more connected and resilient communities, rooted in an Asset Based Community Development framework that believes local people know their communities best. We're looking for a Head of Fundraising and Communications to lead the team tasked with securing the funding to deliver our mission and communicating the work of CUF in new and exciting ways. Reporting to the Deputy CEO and leading a team of four direct reports, plus one indirect report, you'll shape the strategic direction of fundraising and communications. In this role, you'll have the opportunity to: Lead and inspire CUF's Fundraising and Communications team, building meaningful relationships with supporters, partners and advocates who share our vision of flourishing communities. Play a key role in shaping CUF's future by working with the Senior Leadership Team to develop ambitious plans and turn bold ideas into compelling opportunities for support. Drive income growth across major donors, trusts and foundations, churches and individual supporters, unlocking the resources needed to tackle poverty and strengthen communities. Lead engaging, audience-focused communications that raise awareness of CUF's work, grow support and inspire action through digital channels, marketing campaigns and strategic partnerships. Champion and strengthen the CUF brand, acting as a trusted strategic voice to ensure our mission, values and impact are communicated with clarity, confidence and consistency. If you're an experienced fundraising and communications leader with a talent for building relationships with major donors, trusts and foundations, and a passion for equipping others, we'd love to hear from you. Some knowledge of the different faith communities in England would be an advantage, and the ability to work well with people of different faiths and beliefs is essential. Benefits: 22 days annual leave, plus 3 CUF discretionary days and Bank Holidays 7.5% employer pension contribution, with no minimum employee contribution required Flexible working arrangements considered Employee Assistance Programme The chance to shape strategy at a pivotal moment, as CUF approaches its 40th anniversary For further details please see the candidate pack. Contract & Hours: Permanent, full-time (35 hours per week, flexible working arrangements considered) Location: Hybrid/London (with presence at our London office to be determined with line manager) For an informal chat to ask any questions, please contact Nick Thomas, Senior Consultant, Charisma Charity Recruitment. Please apply through the Charisma Charity Recruitment website with your CV and supporting statement. We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, race, colour, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, age, veteran status or other category protected by law. Key dates: Closing date: Monday 19th October Charisma vetting interviews will be completed on a rolling basis and must be completed by: Friday 23rd October Interviews with Church Urban Fund: 1st stage: Tuesday 3rd November 2nd stage: Monday 9th November

item.title: Head of Supporter Experience: Individual Giving & Fundraising
item.description: The Charity and Our Vision For more than 15 years, Scotty's Little Soldiers has supported children and young people bereaved of a parent who served in the British Armed Forces. We are now on an exciting journey to expand our support to anyone affected by a military-connected bereavement, with the ultimate goal of empowering a community of more than 25,000 bereaved individuals and their families by 2035. Nikki Scott founded the charity in 2010 following the death of her husband, Corporal Lee Scott. Today, Scotty’s provides a unique combination of emotional, practical and educational support to the bereaved military community. Lived experience remains central to our work: we listen continually to families so that we can understand their needs and strengthen our services. Our vibrant, non-traditional culture puts the needs of the bereaved military community at the centre of everything we do. We champion innovative approaches and strive to recognise the strength of community, resilience, and connection. Role Mission To develop and own a best-in-class supporter experience, one that makes every person who chooses to support Scotty’s feel valued and as though they are on the journey with us, not simply funding it. You will own the end-to-end individual supporter journey, whether that is a one-off fundraiser or an ongoing donation. Using insight, the latest technology, and continuous improvement of our processes, you will create experiences that can scale as we grow yet remain personal, and unmistakably Scotty's. You will work with Supporter Care to champion supporter stewardship, fundraising journeys, donation experiences, insight and fundraising technology. Community is one of Scotty's three core fundraising streams, alongside Corporate and Grants, each owned by a dedicated lead within a team supported by the Head of Fundraising. You will own the community income budget and be responsible for protecting and growing it sustainably over time. But income is a consequence of doing the experience well. Many of Scotty's biggest supporters (individuals and corporate) began as individual donors or fundraisers; how we make people feel today shapes what they become tomorrow. Before we look at ways to proactively grow our community income we need the right foundations in place – that’s the primary goal for this role over the next 12-18 months. What you’ll be responsible for: Supporter Experience. Own the end-to-end supporter journey. From someone’s first interaction with Scotty’s right through to a long-term relationship, creating a distinctive Scotty’s experience that works for one person as well as it does for 1,000 people. Own the donation experience across all channels and technology e.g. online, mobile, in-person activities, ensuring it’s slick, safe, and easy. Own the stewardship framework. How do we live our core value of ‘everyone a supporter, every supporter a VIP’ in a manageable and scalable way? How we do recognise and thank supporters, how do we communicate the impact of their support? Systems and Processes. Leadership. What does success look like: 3 months… Onboarding. Completed four weeks of ring-fenced onboarding to ensure understanding of the Scotty’s World (history, brand, values and behaviours, and your role within it), the Military Community, and Military-Connected Bereavement. 6 months… 9 months… A clear evidence-based picture of our supporters. You’re able to present a clear evidence-led view of our supporter base (who they are, what motivates them to support, what is working and what isn’t). What You’ll Need to Succeed Essential Experience growing supporter, donor, customer or community journeys - improving engagement, retention and long-term value. Experience owning data, insight and CRM systems to establish benchmarks, and execute on action to improve supporter journeys, stewardship and results. Desirable Additional Information The Scotty’s Way At Scotty’s, our personal performance is only 50% of what success looks like. Our culture is equally important. When you join our team, you sign up to The Scotty’s Way, rooted in our four core values: Families Come First Everyone a Supporter, Every Supporter a VIP Love What You Do Remember, Every Day Our values are further supported by our four non-negotiable behaviours of Show Respect , Speak Up , Take Ownership and Actively Collaborate . We are looking for an individual who embodies these values and behaviours. Closing date: 21 st October 2026 Important Information Feedback We are unable to provide individual feedback on every application. We will contact candidates who are shortlisted for interviews by email. We will only consider applications from candidates located within 2 hours of central Cambridge. We're a remote-first organisation and our day-to-day work is extremely effective with our team based at home. However, some of the most important work we do, innovation, collaboration, problem-solving, and strategic thinking, benefits hugely from being in the same room, and those moments don't always come with months of notice. That's why we're currently looking for team members who are within a 2-hour travel time of Cambridge. Thank you for your interest in joining our team, we are an equal opportunities employer, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where all employees are treated with respect and given equal opportunities for employment and advancement. We do not discriminate because of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply for employment within our charity, and we provide a fair and inclusive recruitment process for all candidates.

item.title: Programme Design and Development Manager (Bilingual, English and French)
item.description: Prospectus is excited to be working with our client to help them recruit for a Programme Design and Development manager to join their team. The organisation is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. They believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, they are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all. Today, their organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. This role is offered on an a full-time 12-month fixed term contract basis paying a salary of £53,000 per annum with flexible hybrid working arrangements at their London office or any country programme where our client operates. As a part of the organisation's Programme Design and Development team, the post holder will independently lead the development of dynamic and successful programmes and proposals for institutional donors, including bilateral and multilateral donors, private foundations, charitable trusts, and host country governments. Working closely with in-country and technical teams across the organisation, they will confidently handle single- and multi-country proposals processes, including bid writing and coordination. The post holder will also own the country fundraising action plans process, facilitate programme design processes, negotiate partnerships, and building the capacity of the organisation's country programmes to effectively conduct local donor engagement. They are looking for someone with a demonstrable track record of writing and managing complex, high-value, and/or multi-country proposals and securing grants and contracts from donors, foundations, and trusts. They are looking for someone who is bilingual in both English and French . They are looking for a candidate with a demonstrable track record of securing and managing 7 figure funding relationships and be confident of working at a senior level externally. The ideal candidate will have demonstrable experience working in business development in international development or the humanitarian sector Please note that it is vital that every team member believes in and is committed to their organisational mission, vision and values. As a pro-choice advocacy organisation, our client are seeking candidates who are committed to and able to support their mission, values and objectives. At Prospectus we invest in your journey as a candidate and are committed to supporting you with your application. We welcome all candidates to apply, regardless of age, sex/gender, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, marital status, or pregnancy/maternity. If you have any disability and require reasonable adjustment/s to any part of the process, then please contact Firas El Dib at Prospectus. If you feel you meet some of the criteria but not all, we really hope you'll enquire and learn more. Prospectus can advise and support on each part of the role and hopefully your application, so we look forward to hearing from you. In order to apply please submit your CV in the first instance. Should your experience be suitable, we will arrange for a meeting to brief you on the role. You'll then have all the information you need to formally apply. We are looking forward to connecting with you soon.

item.title: Technical Advisor Research - Sierra Leone
item.description: Technical Advisor Research - Sierra Leone Reference: SEP20261127 Location: Based in Sierra Leone, West Africa Contract: 2 years Hours: Full-Time, 37.5 hours per week Salary: £40,381.00 - £43,113.00 Per Annum Benefits: Pension Scheme, Life Assurance Scheme, 26 days' Annual Leave (Pro-Rata) The Greater Gola Landscape, covering approximately 350,000 hectares and straddling the Sierra Leone-Liberia border, is one of the largest remaining blocks of Upper Guinea Forest. It supports exceptional biodiversity and provides critical ecosystem services, including climate regulation, water conservation and resilience for local communities. The Gola Programme is implemented through a partnership between the Conservation Society of Sierra Leone (CSSL), the Gola Rainforest Conservation Leadership Group, the Society for the Conservation of Nature of Liberia (SCNL), the Governments of Sierra Leone and Liberia, local communities and the RSPB. The programme aims to conserve this globally important forest ecosystem and its exceptional biodiversity, while contributing to climate change resilience, water conservation and sustainable livelihoods and resilience for communities living in and around the landscape. About the role and what you will be doing The RSPB is seeking an experienced Technical Advisor - Research and Biodiversity Monitoring to provide scientific and technical leadership across biodiversity research, ecological monitoring and conservation projects within the Greater Gola Landscape. Working closely with the Gola Rainforest Conservation (GRC-LG) Research and Monitoring Department, RSPB teams and programme partners, you will ensure that conservation activities are underpinned by robust scientific evidence and best-practice approaches. You will also play a key role in strengthening local technical capacity, supporting REDD+ monitoring, developing research partnerships and translating evidence into practical conservation action. Key responsibilities Lead and support ecological research and biodiversity monitoring programmes. Develop and oversee robust field survey and monitoring methodologies. Quality-assure, analyse and interpret ecological and REDD+ data. Strengthen the technical capacity of GRC-LG, CSSL, SCNL and other partners through mentoring and training. Provide technical input to conservation planning, species recovery and protected-area management. Support research proposals, new project development and external partnerships. Undertake regular fieldwork in Gola Rainforest National Park and surrounding community lands. Promote the use of scientific evidence to demonstrate conservation impact and inform decision-making. About you You will have an MSc or PhD in ecology, conservation biology, environmental science or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience, together with significant experience in ecological research, biodiversity monitoring or applied conservation. You will have: Experience designing and implementing ecological field surveys and biodiversity monitoring programmes, including selecting survey methodologies and ensuring data quality. Experience analysing and interpreting ecological or environmental data. Experience delivering ecological research, biodiversity monitoring or conservation programmes within tropical forest environments. Experience coordinating field teams and planning, prioritising and delivering multiple projects or workstreams to agreed objectives and timescales. Experience building effective partnerships and delivering training, mentoring or technical support to colleagues, partners or stakeholders. Experience working effectively in remote or challenging field environments and adapting plans to address operational challenges. Experience applying scientific evidence to conservation planning, management or decision-making and supporting the development of local technical capacity. Experience providing technical or scientific advice to conservation programmes, projects or partner organisations. Experience of working in West Africa or the Upper Guinea Forest, REDD+, GIS/spatial analysis, community-based conservation, research partnerships or fundraising would be an advantage Additional Information This is a Fixed-Term (2 years) role for 37.5 hours per week. The candidate will be based in Sierra Leone for the duration of the role. The RSPB reserves the right to extend or make this role permanent without further advertising dependent on business needs at the end of the contract term. Closing date: 23:59, Thursday 8th October 2026 We are looking to conduct interviews for this position W/C 12th October. N.B. This role does not require you to have the right to work in the UK. However, when completing your application, please select ‘ Yes ’ when asked whether you have the right to work in the UK in order to proceed with your application. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. We are committed to developing an inclusive and diverse RSPB, in which everyone feels supported, valued, and able to be their full selves. To achieve our vision of creating a world richer in nature, we need more people, and more diverse people, on nature’s side. People of colour and disabled people are currently underrepresented across the environment, climate, sustainability, and conservation sector. If you identify as a person of colour and/or disabled, we are particularly interested in receiving your application. The RSPB is an equal opportunities employer. This role is covered by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. In order to apply you will be required to upload a CV and complete an application form where you will have the opportunity to explain how you meet the criteria above. Contact us to discuss any additional support you may need to complete your application. No agencies please.

item.title: Look Closer Campaign Manager
item.description: Closing in 4 days Look Closer Campaign Manager The Children's Society Flexible Location (On-site) £35,100 per annum Permanent Job description National Look Closer Campaign Manager Permanent contract with funding until 31st March 2027 35 hours per week £35,100 per annum Location: Home based with the location being flexible within England and Wales. The role includes semi regular travel, usually to London Benefits include but not limited to: -36 days' annual leave, inclusive of flexible bank holidays, increasing with length of service -Enhanced maternity/paternity leave -We match up to 8% pension -Free counselling service -Opportunities to develop and widen your skills -2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us: The Children's Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. Our Youth Impact domain creates impact for children and young people. With highly skilled and experienced staff working across England and Wales, we provide direct support to children, young people, parents and carers, as well as conduct research and influence Government to make changes. We also provide training for professionals. Our value driven team change the lives of children in this country for the better — and with your help and expertise, tomorrow we can support even more. About the role:You'll play a key part in our national exploitation Prevention Programme, leading our award winning Look Closer child exploitation awareness campaign. We are looking an experienced public awareness or behaviour change campaigner, with excellent project management skills who has a passion for championing the views of young people and who wants to drive national improvements to ensure child victims of exploitation are identified earlier and get the right support. Key skills and experience: The required skills and competencies for this role are: -Leading public awareness and/or behaviour change campaigns and supporter mobilisation -Strong project management and evaluation skills. -Excellent networking and stakeholder management skills. -Experience of creative production, including both print and digital resources in a variety of formats. It would also be an advantage if you have any of the following skills and competencies: -Digital campaigning skills and experience of using e-campaigning software -Knowledge of child exploitation and abuse and a commitment to equity and inclusion -Skill in managing competing priorities and balancing proactive and reactive campaigns work -People management skills Closing date: Midnight on 27th September 2026 *Please note if we receive a high volume of applications we reserve the right to close the vacancy early* Interviews are due to take place on 5th and 6th October In this role you will: -Join the award winning Prevention Programme to influence and encourage new and innovative approaches to prevent child exploitation and abuse, working to ensure all child victims of exploitation are recognised and receive the right support. -Lead and develop the Look Closer campaign to ensure it is focusing where it is most effective, to incorporate young people's voices and meet the needs of different audiences including the public, statutory, third and private sectors and ensure it makes a meaningful contribution to improving the lives of children and young people. -Represent and promote the Prevention Programme and The Children's Society more widely and communicate effectively with key audiences and stakeholders both internally and externally, winning support and gathering new ideas to inspire our campaign and the wider activity of the Prevention Programme and The Children's Society as a whole. We view diversity and inclusion as fundamental to achieving social change and recognise that systemic racism, homophobia, transphobia and disability discrimination actively prevent children from being safeguarded and receiving appropriate support. To tackle the complex issues facing young people, we need access to diverse talent, perspectives, experiences and working practices. The Prevention Programme is committed to inclusion, anti-racism and trans allyship. We actively support all LGBTQIA+ people, people with disabilities and those who identify as neurodiverse and are currently engaged in work to address issues of systemic exclusion and discrimination as they relate to exploitation and abuse. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and communities and we have policies to support flexible, inclusive and accessible employment. The Children's Society is committed to safeguarding and protection of the children and young people we work with. As such, our safer recruitment process includes a Basic or Enhanced DBS check, 5 years of references, and additional vetting checks relevant to the role. We have a comprehensive range of policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices across all areas of our organisation.In support of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, shortlisting is carried out on an anonymised basis. Personal details are hidden from the shortlisting panel, and candidates are referenced by a candidate number only. As part of this process, we ask that your CV is anonymised before submission - this means removing personal information such as your name, contact details, age, and any other identifying details. AI tools can support your application but only when used appropriately. You're welcome to use them to improve clarity, structure, and research. However, overuse or misuse (e.g. inventing experience or using AI during assessments) may lead to rejection at any stage. We want to hear the real you - authenticity matters. item.title: Individual Giving Executive (Mid-value)
item.description: Crisis is the national charity for people experiencing homelessness. We have embarked on our 10-year strategy for ending homelessness. We know it is not inevitable. We know together we can end it. Location: London based, with hybrid working in line with Crisis’ Hybrid Working Policy You will be joining a team dedicated to raising vital year-round income and making Crisis supporters feel valued and inspired. This role will support the delivery of our Mid-Value Programme, as we continue to grow this crucial source of sustainable income and inspire more supporters to deepen their commitment to ending homelessness. About the role Mid-value giving sits at the heart of our new Brand, Marketing and Fundraising Strategy as one of our highest-priority income streams. As an Individual Giving Executive, you’ll play a key role in managing one-to-one and one-to-many relationships with Crisis mid-value supporters, delivering excellent supporter care to deepen engagement and build financial commitment, and supporting the multi-channel programme that delivers tangible impact for Crisis and bring people closer to our mission to end homelessness. As we evaluate and refine our Mid-value offer to supporters, you’ll be using creativity and innovation to develop campaigns, communications, and engagement opportunities to inspire people with this way of giving. By collaborating with colleagues from across the organisation and our trusted partners, you’ll be bold in delivering an impactful stewardship programme that nurtures our supporters’ consideration and creates new opportunities for them to feel valued. You’ll take an equitable approach in sharing stories of people experiencing homelessness, to deepen our supporters’ engagement and bring them closer to our mission. About you We’re looking for a fundraiser with experience delivering in-person, one to one stewardship, ideally within a philanthropy or high-value context. You’ll be an organised project manager and excellent communicator across multiple channels and be comfortable having thoughtful and tactful conversations with our supporters. We are a dynamic team that delivers results and are in the process of re-designing our mid-value programme for Crisis. So we’re looking for someone who can learn quickly and happy to get involved with multiple projects straight away. To be successful in this role you will: be a confident communicator, whether writing persuasively for a specific audience, speaking one-to-one with a Crisis supporter, or organising events for Crisis mid-value supporters. have knowledge of higher-value and philanthropy giving programmes. be an effective project manager, with experience working in direct marketing, ideally within a fundraising environment. enjoy thinking creatively and using storytelling to bring complex issues to life. be comfortable using digital platforms and technology, and working with data to improve outcomes. take an organised and proactive approach to managing your workload and balancing different priorities. be a solutions-focused problem solver who is ready to adapt to a changing environment. Previous experience in fundraising or stewardship is essential, ideally within a higher-value/philanthropy context. Most of all we’re looking for a candidate who’s passionate about ending homelessness and can play an active role in a busy, diverse and dynamic team. Please see the full Job Pack linked below, for a full list of requirements for this role. We realise that long lists of criteria can be daunting, and you may not want to apply for a role unless you feel 100% qualified. However, if you feel you have relevant examples to answer the screening questions, we encourage you to apply. We believe diversity is a strength, and our aim is to make sure that Crisis truly reflects the communities we serve. We are actively working towards our organisation being a place where everyone can thrive and make their best contribution to our mission of ending homelessness for good. We know that the more perspectives, voices, and experiences we can bring to this work, the better. We particularly welcome applications from people who have lived experience of homelessness, and people from all marginalised groups, communities, and backgrounds. Working at Crisis Our values, Bold, Impactful, Collaborative and Equitable, are at the heart of everything we do as we continue in our mission to end homelessness. Our staff, members and volunteers are vital to getting the right government policies in place, providing breakthrough services, and building a supportive community. We’ll lead by example to nurture a positive and ambitious workplace guided by ending homelessness. As a member of the team, you will have access to a wide range of employee benefits including: A competitive salary. Please note our salaries are fixed to counter inequity and we do not negotiate at offer stage Interest free loans for travel season ticket, cycle to work, and deposit to secure a tenancy Pension scheme with an employer contribution of 8.5% 28 days’ annual leave (pro rata) which increases with service to 31 days and the option to purchase up to 10 additional days leave Enhanced maternity, paternity, shared parental, and adoption pay Flexible working around the core hours 10am-4pm Wellbeing Leave to be used flexibly And more! (Full list of benefits available on website) Alongside our excellent staff benefits, we will support your ongoing development to build your skills, experience, and career. When you join us, you will have the opportunity to join our staff diversity networks, which aim to champion issues across the organisation, enable staff to be their authentic and best selves and contribute to making Crisis a truly diverse organisation. How do I apply? Please click on the 'Apply for Job' button below. Our shortlisting process is anonymised as part of our commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion. We do not ask for CVs, instead we ask you complete the work history section and answer the screening questions for us to be able to assess you fairly and objectively. At least two members of staff score all applications. Closing date: Sunday 4 October 2026 at23:55 Interview process: Competency based interview Interview date and location: Monday 12 and Tuesday 13 October 2026, online via Teams AI in Job Applications We understand some candidates use AI tools when applying. Whilst we welcome the use of technology to support clear communication and structure, we want to learn more about you, so please ensure that your application reflects your own skills, knowledge and experiences Accessibility We want our recruitment process to be as accessible as possible. If you need us to make an adjustment or provide additional support as you apply for a role, please contact our Talent Acquisition team who will be happy to help. For more information about our work please visitour website. Registered Charity Numbers: E&W1082947, SC040094

item.title: Wellbeing & Volunteer Coordinator
item.description: Wellbeing and Volunteer Coordinator Marauders Men's Health Charity Hours: 20 hours per week (part-time) Salary: £26,520 per annum pro rata Location: Remote Contract: Fixed-term until March 2028 Responsible to: CEO About Marauders Men's Health Charity Marauders Men's Health Charity is committed to improving the health and wellbeing of men and creating opportunities for men to connect, build supportive relationships and access the help they need. We recognise that men can face significant barriers to talking about their mental and physical health. Through our activities, support, volunteering and community engagement, we aim to create welcoming, inclusive spaces where men feel able to participate, connect and thrive. We are looking for a passionate and organised Wellbeing and Volunteer Coordinator to play a key role in supporting our wellbeing activities and developing our volunteer network. The Role The Wellbeing and Volunteer Coordinator will be responsible for coordinating and developing Marauders' wellbeing activities while supporting, recruiting and engaging volunteers across the charity. This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who enjoys working with people, building relationships and creating positive opportunities within the community. You will be an important point of contact for volunteers and participants, helping to ensure that our activities are safe, welcoming, inclusive and responsive to the needs of the men we support. The successful candidate will be confident working independently, but also enjoy being part of a small, committed team. You will need excellent communication and organisational skills, a positive attitude and a genuine commitment to improving men's health and wellbeing. Key Responsibilities Wellbeing Coordination Coordinate and support the delivery of Marauders' wellbeing activities, groups, sessions and events. Help develop activities that encourage men to improve their physical, mental and social wellbeing. Create a welcoming and inclusive environment where participants feel comfortable and valued. Build positive relationships with participants and identify opportunities to improve their experience. Monitor attendance patterns and personally connect with disengaged members to provide targeted encouragement and support. Work with the CEO to develop wellbeing plans for beneficiaries Gather feedback from participants and use this to inform the development of activities and services. Assist with planning, promoting and evaluating wellbeing programmes and events. Volunteer Coordination Recruit, welcome, support and retain volunteers across the charity. Develop positive and supportive relationships with volunteers. Coordinate volunteer rotas, roles and activities. Ensure volunteers receive appropriate induction, guidance, training and ongoing support. Help volunteers understand their roles, responsibilities and boundaries. Recognise and celebrate volunteer contributions. Maintain accurate volunteer records and ensure relevant checks, documentation and training are kept up to date. Identify opportunities for volunteers to develop new skills and take on additional responsibilities. Organise volunteer meetings, briefings and opportunities for feedback. Support the development of a positive, inclusive and rewarding volunteer culture. Community Engagement Build relationships with local organisations, community groups and relevant services. Promote Marauders' activities and volunteering opportunities within the local community. Attend community events and represent the charity in a professional and positive manner. Help identify opportunities to reach men who may benefit from Marauders' support. Support partnership working with organisations involved in men's health, wellbeing and community development. Administration, Monitoring and Safeguarding Maintain accurate records relating to participants, volunteers and activities. Support monitoring and evaluation of projects and services. Contribute to reports, funding applications and evidence of impact where required. Follow Marauders' policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, equality and diversity, confidentiality and data protection. Identify and appropriately report safeguarding or wellbeing concerns in line with organisational procedures. Support risk assessments and ensure activities are delivered safely. Undertake other reasonable duties that support the effective operation and development of the charity. Person Specification Essential Experience of working with people in a community, voluntary, wellbeing, health or support setting. Experience of coordinating volunteers, activities, groups or community projects. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to build trust and positive relationships with people from a wide range of backgrounds. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. Confidence working independently and using initiative. Good written and verbal communication skills. A non-judgemental, empathetic and inclusive approach. An understanding of the importance of men's health and wellbeing. Commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. Good IT and administrative skills. Willingness to work some evenings or weekends when required for events or activities. Desirable Experience of working specifically with men and/or men's health. Experience of supporting people experiencing mental health or wellbeing challenges. Experience of recruiting, training or managing volunteers. Knowledge of local community and voluntary-sector services. Experience of partnership working with health, community or voluntary organisations. Relevant qualifications or training in health, wellbeing, community development, volunteering or a related field. Experience of monitoring outcomes and evaluating community programmes. Personal Qualities The successful candidate will be: Approachable and empathetic Positive and encouraging Organised and reliable Proactive and self-motivated A confident communicator Inclusive and non-judgemental Adaptable and resilient Passionate about improving men's health and wellbeing What We Offer A rewarding opportunity to make a real difference to men's health and wellbeing. A supportive and friendly working environment. The opportunity to develop and shape Marauders' volunteer programme and wellbeing activities. Opportunities for professional development and training. The chance to work closely with volunteers, community organisations and the men we support. 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays! (pro rata) 5% pension employer contribution Flexible hours Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Marauders Men's Health Charity is committed to creating an inclusive organisation where everyone is treated with dignity, respect and fairness. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from groups that are currently underrepresented within our organisation. Safeguarding Marauders Men's Health Charity is committed to safeguarding the welfare of all participants, volunteers and staff. The successful candidate will be required to undertake appropriate safeguarding checks and comply with all relevant organisational policies and procedures. How to Apply To apply, please submit your CV and a supporting statement explaining your interest in the role, relevant experience and what you could bring to Marauders Men's Health Charity. Closing date: October 10th Interview date: TBC Start date: ASAP
