item.title: Head of Finance and Operations
item.description: Kentown Africa Foundation is an ambitious UK grant-making charity with a clear mission: to improve the health and wellbeing of children across Sub-Saharan Africa. Kentown Africa Foundation is looking to recruit a Head of Finance and Operations at an exciting stage in the organisation’s development. About us Every child deserves the opportunity to survive, thrive and reach their full potential. Kentown Africa Foundation is a UK-based grant-making foundation dedicated to making that a reality for children across Sub-Saharan Africa. The Foundation provides funding to organisations, partnerships and innovative programmes that strengthen health systems, improve access to quality healthcare and create sustainable, lasting change. Its approach is deliberately collaborative and locally led, working with trusted partners, healthcare professionals, researchers and community organisations to support evidence-based interventions and stronger healthcare systems for the future. This is a relatively small but ambitious organisation, with a team bringing together expertise across global health, philanthropy, grant-making and programme management. The Foundation is supported by an experienced Board of Trustees and is now building its infrastructure and capacity for its next stage of growth. About you This is a broad and influential finance role, reporting directly to the CEO and forming part of the Senior Management Team. The Head of Finance and Operations will take overall responsibility for the finance function, providing high-quality financial information, strong financial controls and effective financial governance, while also playing an important role in the organisation's wider operations. You will be a trusted adviser to the CEO and Board, helping to shape financial strategy, budgets and forecasts and providing the financial insight needed to support grant-making decisions. A particularly interesting aspect of the role is the grant finance oversight . You will work closely with the Head of Grants to assess funding applications, monitor the financial performance of funded projects, review grantee budgets and reports, and help strengthen financial capacity within partner organisations. The role will also have responsibility for statutory accounts and audit, Charity SORP compliance, tax, payroll and pensions, as well as company secretarial and governance responsibilities. There is also an opportunity to contribute to the development of IT systems, risk management and wider organisational processes. What are we looking for? We are looking for a qualified accountant or an accountant qualified by experience who combines strong technical finance expertise with a genuinely strategic and hands-on approach. You are likely to have senior finance experience within a charity, grant-making organisation, international development organisation or another complex not-for-profit environment , although relevant experience from other sectors will also be considered. You will bring: Strong financial management, analysis and strategic planning skills Experience of budgeting, forecasting and financial risk management Experience preparing statutory accounts, ideally within the charity sector and under Charity SORP Experience of financial governance and reporting to Boards or senior stakeholders The ability to critically evaluate existing processes and identify improvements Strong Excel skills and experience with financial systems – ideally QuickBooks Excellent communication skills and the ability to work confidently with both financial and non-financial stakeholders High levels of accuracy, integrity and attention to detail Above all, this role would suit someone who enjoys being part of a small, collaborative organisation , is comfortable rolling up their sleeves, and wants their financial expertise to have a meaningful impact. What’s on offer? This is a rare opportunity to join a growing international philanthropic organisation at an important point in its development. You will have the opportunity to: Shape the finance function of a growing and ambitious charity Work closely with the CEO, Senior Management Team and Board Have a genuine influence on financial strategy, governance and organisational development Play a key role in ensuring grant funding is managed effectively and delivers maximum impact Work alongside experienced partners, healthcare professionals and organisations working to improve children's healthcare Enjoy flexible remote working , with 22.5 hours per week over 3–4 days Benefit from a generous leave policy Receive an enhanced pension scheme and employee benefits Have opportunities for travel where applicable If you are an experienced finance professional looking for a flexible, genuinely influential part-time role and want to use your expertise to support an organisation with a clear and meaningful purpose, we would love to hear from you. Please contact Nicola Shaw at Morgan Law for a candidate pack Closing date: 24th October Interview date: 5th November

And it’s this commitment that unites us across the UK. Our strategy is based on what people affected by MS have told us is important to them. It gives us a clear and determined focus. Our work is based on the hopes and aspirations of our MS community. Together we campaign at all levels, fund ground-breaking research and provide award winning support and information. Our people are our greatest asset and the key to our success. We offer a vibrant, progressive working environment where you'll be able to make a difference. The Shop Manager will be responsible for driving sales, managing a team of volunteers and staff, maintaining high standards of customer service, and ensuring efficient stock control. Manage donations and stock intake, ensuring the shop remains organised and efficient. Adhere to health and safety regulations and ensure the shop operates within budget. item.title: Independent Mental Capacity Advocate (IMCA)/Community Advocate ONE VACANCY – TWO APPOINTMENT ROUTES
item.description: Help people have their voices heard. Make a difference through advocacy. Mind in Havering, Barking & Dagenham is looking for a passionate and committed person to join our Advocacy Service, supporting vulnerable adults to understand their rights, express their views and have a say in important decisions about their lives. We have one vacancy available, with the appointment level dependent on your existing qualifications and experience. If you hold the required National Advocacy Qualification and relevant IMCA/DoLS training, you will be appointed as an Independent Mental Capacity Advocate (IMCA) / Community Advocate, earning £28,954 per annum (£17.40 per hour) for 32 hours per week. If you have the right skills and experience but are not yet qualified, you may be appointed as an Advocacy Project Worker at £15.81 per hour, with support and a clear route to work towards the National Advocacy Qualification. You will work with people across Havering, building trusted relationships and helping ensure their wishes, rights and choices are heard and respected. The role includes casework, working alongside health and social care professionals, community engagement, workshops and promoting self-advocacy. We are looking for someone who is compassionate, organised, resilient and confident communicating with people who may be distressed or facing difficult circumstances. You will need to work independently while also being part of a supportive team. If you are already an experienced advocate or are looking to develop your career in advocacy, we would love to hear from you.

item.title: Senior New Partnerships Lead - Corporate Partnerships
item.description: Salary: £53,500 - £56,268 per annum Contract Type: Permanent Closing date: 7 October 2026 at 11pm Interview date: 14 October 2026 About CARE CARE International is a global humanitarian organisation leading the fight to end poverty in the world’s most challenging situations. Women and girls are at the centre of our work, because we cannot overcome poverty and inequality until all people have equal rights and opportunities. We know that when a crisis erupts, women are often the first to pick up the pieces, so we work alongside women, so they have the power to make change where it’s needed most. Founded in 1945, CARE currently works in over 100 countries and last year alone reached 53.4 million people through nearly 1,500 projects. Why work for CARE International UK? Lead the development of high-value, multi-year corporate partnerships that drive sustainable growth and real impact. You’ll shape and deliver our new corporate partnerships strategy, creating purposeful, winwin collaborations across ESG, brand, commercial and philanthropic opportunities. This is a vital leadership role at the heart of CIUK’s growth ambitions, with real ownership of strategy from design through to delivery-ready partnerships. Working closely with the Head of Partnerships & Philanthropy and teams across CARE, you’ll identify innovative opportunities – from responsible supply chains to microfinance and humanitarian programmes – while managing and developing a high-performing team. With strong leadership support and the autonomy to act, you’ll play a key role in growing income, strengthening partnerships, and advancing CARE UK’s mission. You’ll build on an already impressive portfolio of partners – including Mondelez International, Diageo, Fyffes, Twinings, GSK and Haleon – as you shape what comes next. About you You’re an experienced corporate partnerships professional with a strong track record of securing significant income (£1m+) and building high-value relationships. You bring excellent commercial awareness, strategic thinking and the ability to lead compelling partnership proposals. You have a solid understanding of corporate priorities across employee engagement, brand, ESG and commercial drivers. You’re ready for a senior, strategic role – comfortable owning income and strategy at departmental level, and confident representing new partnerships work to CIUK’s Senior Leadership Team, and the wider CARE confederation. You’re confident influencing and negotiating with senior stakeholders, and skilled at working across different cultures in complex, global organisations. A collaborative leader, you are motivated by delivering impact with corporate partners in line with CARE’s values. About the role You’ll lead the development and delivery of CARE International UK’s new corporate partnerships strategy, securing high-value, multi-year partnerships and building a strong pipeline of opportunities. You’ll drive business development, from prospecting and relationship-building through to proposal development and closing deals. You’ll own a new partnerships income target of seven-figures-plus a year – one of CIUK’s most significant growth areas. Leading a small new corporate partnerships team, you’ll oversee income growth, manage key processes and ensure partnerships are impactful, sustainable and aligned with CARE’s priorities. You’ll work closely with internal and global colleagues, represent CARE externally, and influence corporate audiences to position CARE as a partner of choice. Right to Work in the UK All applicants must have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom at the time of appointment. Proof of right to work will be required as part of the recruitment process. For more information, please visit the UK Government's guidance on right to work. Where you do not have current right to work in the UK, then this will be discussed with you as part of the recruitment process. Please note that not all roles are eligible for sponsorship and further information (should you require sponsorship to work in the UK) on eligibility can be found here. Safeguarding CARE International UK has a zero-tolerance approach to any abuse to, sexual harassment of or exploitation of, a vulnerable adult or child by any of our staff, representatives or partners. CARE International UK expects all staff to share this commitment through our Safeguarding Policy (link here) and our Code of Conduct (link here). They are responsible for ensuring they understand and work within the remit of these policies throughout their time at CARE International UK. Safeguarding the communities we work with is our top priority in everything we do, including recruitment. All offers of employment at CARE International UK are subject to: · Satisfactory references. CARE International UK participates in theInter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (link here).In line with this Scheme, we willrequest information from successful applicants’ previous employersabout any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment,or incidents under investigationwhen the applicant left employment. · Appropriate criminal record checks (including a Bridger check, link here). By submitting an application, the applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures. Equality and Diversity We are committed toEquality and value Diversity. We are aDisability Confident Employerand particularly welcome applications from disabled people. We guarantee interviews to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role (see person specification). If you require the candidate brief or need to submit your application in an alternative format, because of a disability, please do get in touch by sending an email to HR. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We particularly welcome applications from people of underrepresented backgrounds, including those from Black, Asian and other ethnic minority communities, and individuals who identify as LGBTQ+.

We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. Our Youth Impact domain creates impact for children and young people. With highly skilled and experienced staff working across England and Wales, we provide direct support to children, young people, parents and carers, as well as conduct research and influence Government to make changes. About the role:You'll play a key part in our Central Bedfordshire Youth Service, supporting the Youth Workers to provide youth club activities. Are you creative, dynamic and unique? With a passion for making a difference? You will have: -Excellent skills in positively engaging with young people, their families and communities -Working in ways that are empowering and enabling; being able to address barriers to those least likely to engage. -The ability to listen to others and work in a non-judgmental way. -Excellent communication skills (both verbal and written). -One to one working and group working skills. -Practical skills/interests in a relevant area, e.g. arts, music, crafts, mechanics, woodwork and cookery, that can enhance the curriculum offer -Excellent IT skills (Microsoft Office applications and Outlook). -Strong time-management skills -Experience of working with young people, their families and communities. -Knowledge and experience of methods in building positive relationships with children, young people and families. -Experience in a relevant area of work e.g. Youth Work, Social Care, Family support, Youth Offending, Education. -Handling sensitive and confidential issues with tact and diplomacy. -Work under your own initiative and take responsibility for decisions taken -Experience of partnership working and development of multi-disciplinary approaches to work with young people. -Clear understanding of children's rights and commitment to promoting those rights. -Working knowledge of relevant policies and practices relating to child protection and safeguarding of young people, with the ability to make sound judgement in relation to risk and protection. item.title: Community Officer
item.description: Could you help put people and community at the heart of Abingdon’s historic Abbey Buildings? The Friends of Abingdon Abbey Buildings Trust is conserving and enhancing these nationally important Grade I listed medieval buildings and, with support from The National Lottery Heritage Fund, delivering an ambitious programme of activities alongside the building project. We want to build meaningful relationships with local people and organisations – not just for the life of the project, but to help establish the Abbey Buildings as a welcoming, accessible and well-used community and heritage space for the future. We’re now looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Community Officer to join our small team and help make that happen. About the role This is a varied, hands-on and outward-facing role. You’ll be working directly with people as well as doing the practical organisation that turns ideas into successful activities. You’ll: help plan, organise and deliver activities and sessions with community groups, schools and other participants; build and maintain relationships with local groups, organisations, schools and networks; help people find opportunities to engage with and use the Abbey Buildings; take responsibility for agreed areas of work, from planning through to delivery and follow-up; support the development and day-to-day coordination of volunteer involvement; contribute to evaluation, communications and social media; and work alongside the Programme Manager, freelancers, partners, volunteers and others involved in the project. The programme will continue to develop over the three years, so there will be plenty of scope to bring your own ideas, experience and expertise to the role. This job could be for you if… You have practical experience of community engagement and of delivering activities or sessions directly with people. You’re confident making new connections and building positive relationships with different groups and organisations. You’re also organised and practical enough to turn conversations and ideas into things that actually happen. You enjoy working collaboratively, but are equally comfortable taking responsibility for your own areas of work and seeing them through. Most importantly, you’re enthusiastic about involving people and creating opportunities for a wide range of people to participate. Heritage experience is welcome, but it isn’t essential. We’re interested in the skills and experience you can bring from community, voluntary, arts, cultural, education or other relevant settings. The details Salary: £25,600 per year (£32,000 FTE) Hours: 28 hours per week (0.8 FTE) Contract: Three-year fixed-term contract Location: Abingdon-on-Thames, with some flexible/home working by agreement Annual leave: 25 days per year pro rata, plus Bank Holidays Closing date: Sunday 18 October 2026 at 23:30 Interviews: Thursday 29 October 2026 in Abingdon Please download the Recruitment Pack for full details of the role, person specification and benefits. To apply, please send us your CV, a supporting statement of no more than two sides of A4, and completed Candidate Information Form . We welcome applications from people with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you’re excited by the role but aren’t sure you meet every criterion, we’d still encourage you to read the full recruitment pack and consider applying. If you’d like an informal conversation about the role before applying, we’d be very happy to hear from you.

item.description: Chief Executive Officer Remote/Flexible with UK-wide travel as required Circa £75,000 per annum An independent UK charity is seeking an exceptional leader to become its next Chief Executive Officer , providing strategic and operational leadership at a pivotal moment for both the organisation and the wider policy and services landscape in which it operates. item.title: Student Communities Manager
item.description: Student Communities Manager - Reading Students’ Union Location: University of Reading, Whiteknights Campus, Reading, Berkshire Salary: £36,961.59 per annum Contract: Permanent Hours: 35 hours per week Monday-Friday Location: Office based Closing Date: 14 October 2026 About Reading Students’ Union We are a dynamic, student-focused organisation dedicated to empowering students and enhancing their university experience. Our vision is to be a place for everyone, we inspire and empower students to change the world. Student Communities Manager Do you believe that strong student communities have the power to transform the university experience? We're looking for a strategic, innovative and people-focused leader to lead our Student Communities team, ensuring students can create, lead and participate in safe, inclusive and sustainable communities that foster belonging, connection and personal development. This role sits at the heart of Reading Students' Union's mission to create opportunities for students to find their people, develop new skills and make the most of their time at university. You'll lead our approach to sports clubs, societies, volunteering, student media and emerging community opportunities, ensuring students have meaningful ways to connect, contribute and thrive. What You'll Do You'll provide strategic and operational leadership for Student Communities, overseeing everything from community development and student leadership to governance, major projects and partnerships. Working closely with students, staff and University stakeholders, you'll ensure our student community offer remains inclusive, sustainable and responsive to changing student needs. This is an exciting opportunity to shape how students connect, participate and belong, bringing our ambitious strategy to life. Lead the Future of Student Communities Lead the development and delivery of the Students' Union's Student Communities strategy. Create opportunities for students to connect, organise and participate through communities that reflect their interests, identities and aspirations. Develop innovative approaches to engagement beyond traditional clubs, societies and volunteering models. Drive continuous improvement using student insight, sector trends and emerging best practice. Build sustainable and scalable opportunities that support belonging, personal development and student success. Create Opportunities for Belonging and Participation Ensure students can easily join, create, lead and develop student communities. Remove barriers to participation and improve access for underrepresented and underserved groups. Champion inclusion and belonging across all Student Communities activity. Create meaningful opportunities for students to develop skills, confidence and leadership experience. Ensure students play a meaningful role in shaping the future of our communities offer. Support Student Leaders to Succeed Lead the development of a high-quality student leader journey, from recruitment through to succession planning. Oversee training, development and support frameworks for student leaders and volunteers. Equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to govern their groups effectively. Ensure student-led communities operate safely, inclusively and sustainably. Celebrate and champion student leadership across the organisation. Build Partnerships and Community Impact Develop strong relationships with University departments, SportsPark, community organisations and external partners. Create volunteering and community engagement opportunities that benefit both students and the wider Reading community. Identify funding opportunities, partnerships and sustainable models that increase the reach and impact of student-led communities. Represent the Students' Union on relevant University and external groups. Lead Governance, Quality and Operational Excellence Oversee governance frameworks for student groups, including constitutions, elections, financial controls and accountability arrangements. Provide expert guidance on governance, conduct, disciplinary and operational matters. Lead safeguarding, health and safety, welfare and risk management arrangements across student-led activity. Ensure consistent, high-quality support and service standards across Student Communities. Use feedback, complaints and insight to improve services and student outcomes. Deliver Major Projects and Events Hold overall accountability for Varsity, providing strategic leadership and oversight. Lead Student Communities contributions to major Students' Union projects and events, including Welcome and the SU Awards. Ensure key projects and events are effectively planned, governed, resourced and evaluated. Drive continuous improvement across major programmes and activities. Lead People, Performance and Resources Provide strategic and operational leadership for the Student Communities department. Lead, develop and support a high-performing team of Coordinators and student staff. Manage departmental budgets, resources and workforce planning. Establish clear objectives, service standards and performance expectations. Monitor and report on performance, impact and student outcomes. Use Insight to Shape the Future Analyse participation, demographic, financial and feedback data to identify trends and opportunities. Use evidence and student insight to shape decision-making and future investment. Benchmark our performance against the wider sector and identify opportunities for innovation. Demonstrate impact through evaluation, reporting and continuous improvement. About You Essential Significant experience leading and developing student communities, membership services or comparable provision. Experience managing teams, performance, budgets and operational delivery. Experience leading large-scale projects involving multiple stakeholders. Strong understanding of governance and accountability within student-led, volunteer-led or membership organisations. Experience managing complex governance, conduct, complaints or high-risk operational matters. Strong stakeholder management, communication and partnership-building skills. Experience using insight, evidence and performance data to drive service development and improvement. Excellent organisational, project management and decision-making skills. A resilient and confident leader who thrives in a dynamic environment. A passion for building communities, empowering student leaders and enhancing the student experience. Desirable Experience working within a Students' Union, charity or membership organisation. Understanding of Higher Education structures and the student experience. Experience of sports clubs, societies, volunteering, community engagement or student media. Knowledge of BUCS, National Governing Bodies or student media governance. A leadership, management or relevant professional qualification. Please click the link below for the full job description: Student Communities Manager - Why Join Us? · Inclusive and supportive team culture · Flexible working options · 35 days’ annual leave including Christmas and Easter closure days · Professional development opportunities · Unique working environment in the heart of a vibrant Student’s Union, set on a stunning, green campus. Ready to make our data-led strategy a reality? Apply today! Committed to equality, celebrating diversity, and embedding sustainability—building an inclusive workplace and a brighter future for all.

item.title: FACILITIES AND LOGISTIC OFFICER
item.description: About This Job The Cadet Centre for Adventurous Training (CCAT) is the national centre of excellence for the delivery of Adventurous Training to the Army Cadets. It is based in Capel Curig Training Camp in North Wales with a satellite centre located at Halton Training Camp, Lancaster. This post holder is accountable for the delivery of efficient and effective facilities and support services working collaboratively across a range of both military and civilian agencies in order to ensure safe, sustainable and high quality delivery of training. Essential Skills · Proficient in the use of Microsoft 365 applications · Full UK driving licence (Cat B). · Experience of budget management and procurement processes. · Experience of facilities management including contractor liaison · Experience of Logistics operations · Experience of a range of adventurous training equipment – to include paddle sport, climbing, mountaineering, mountain biking & skiing. · Demonstratable success in establishing & maintaining effective working relationships with stakeholders at all levels. · Strong organisational and planning skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities · Ability to work independently and use initiative to resolve problems. · Professional and customer-focused approach. · Reliable, trustworthy and able to maintain confidentiality · Willingness to travel and work flexibly when required Please refer to the attached Job Description for further information. Our charity ACCT UK is a national youth charity dedicated to improving the life chances of young people. The Combined Cadet Force Association (CCFA) is a charity dedicated to the promotion of the ideals and activities of the Combined Cadet Force in schools. Together we want to ensure that every young person has the opportunity to learn new skills, build confidence and be inspired through their cadet experience. We want to develop the youth leadership and training abilities of adult volunteers whilst also helping young people to access cadet activities through fundraising, grant-making, developing new resources and direct support. We strongly believe that everyone benefits when you help young people to develop their character and values through activities that stretch and mature them. We also know that when young people engage with others at a range of levels in their communities it builds confidence and improves empathy for other’s lives. Who we are By joining ACCT UK you will help us to reach more young people and make a greater difference and we look forward to working with you. We actively promote and encourage you to explore ideas that improve all aspects of the charity’s work in pursuit of its charitable aims. The charities are proud of our diverse teams, with people on different working patterns, from different backgrounds and at different life-stages. Our experience has taught us that having people with different perspectives and different lived experiences leads to better outcomes for our beneficiaries. If you are wondering if our organisation is for someone like you, the answer is yes! Please apply and explain how you, your experience, your talent and your potential are the right fit for this role. What we can offer you In addition to your salary, we offer all staff: · Flexible working arrangements (you agree a working pattern with your line manager). · The ability to work both from home and from our Capel Curig office. · Personal Accident Insurance, including loss of earnings cover and death benefit. · 15 days of sick pay in any 12-month period (after 12 months employment - pro-rata for part time staff). · A contributory pension scheme (you contribute at least 5% and we will contribute 10%). · Good leave allowances (which are offered pro-rata for part time staff): o 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays. o Additional privilege leave, on set days each year, such as between Christmas and New Year. o An additional five days of volunteering leave. · Support for qualifications and personal development. · Employee Assistance Programme. · Season ticket loan. · Railcard (if you are eligible) · A caring and supportive team environment. How to apply Please send a CV and Cover letter that details how you meet the requirements of the job description by 2330hrs Sunday 18th October 2026. Interviews will be held in person during the week commencing 2nd November 2026. While AI tools can be beneficial, we value the personal touch and authenticity in job applications. We encourage you to highlight your unique experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, ensuring all information is accurate. Please use AI tools responsibly and with integrity throughout the application and selection process. Please note that as a charity dedicated to improving the lives of young people, we require staff to make a declaration about any relevant convictions, undergo both a Disclosure and Barring Service check and a Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) check (one of the requirements being that applicants must have been resident in the UK for 3 years). In addition, we will follow up references. Please be advised that this position may close earlier than the stated deadline if a sufficient number of high-quality applications are received. To ensure your application is considered, we strongly recommend submitting it as soon as possible. Candidates will be notified of the next stage in the recruitment process if they are shortlisted.

item.title: Partnership Events Coordinator
item.description: Job Title: Partnership Events Coordinator (Inspiring the Future) Reports to: Head of Partnership Delivery Location: Quantum House, 22 – 24 Red Lion Court, Fleet Street, EC4A 3AB. The role is open to hybrid working but the candidate would be expected to be in the office one day per week Purpose: This is a fantastic opportunity to take on the role of Partnership Events Coordinator for Education and Employers on the internationally recognised Inspiring the Future programme. The Charity aims to ensure that all young people have the inspiration, motivation, knowledge, skills and opportunities they need to help them achieve their potential. This key post is part of the Partnerships Team with responsibility for supporting the team to deliver various showcase virtual and face-to-face events and activities involving a diverse range of volunteers from the world of work. The role is rewarding and varied and will include supporting delivery of funded partnerships and general administrative support. Remuneration : £27k per annum Additional Terms: 30 days paid holiday, exclusive of Statutory Holiday plus competitive pension scheme and a volunteering allowance of up to 5 days – pro rata in accordance with the length of contract. Additional family friendly benefits including enhancements to Statutory Payments. Appointment Terms: Permanent and full time Job Purpose: Reporting to the Head of Partnership Delivery and working closely with colleagues in the Partnerships Team, the Partnership Events Coordinator is responsible for working closely with volunteers and school staff to support successful delivery of interactive activities aimed at schools and young people under key funded projects for the charity’s Inspiring the Future and Primary Futures programmes. These programmes leverage technology to raise the aspirations and broaden the horizons of children and young people by connecting them to a huge range of volunteers from the world of work via career related learning activities. The Partnerships team are responsible for relationship management of the key corporate and charity partners for the charity’s Inspiring the Future and Primary Futures programmes. Partners cover a range of sectors and employment areas and our employer partnerships provide partners employees with the opportunity to engage with schools and reach many children and young people across the UK, both virtually and in-person. This role will be split between supporting organisation of activities related to our corporate partners and delivering activities to schools across parts of the country. There is opportunity to interface directly with children and young people from both secondary and primary schools. through facilitating virtual and in person interactive activities with volunteers. The Partnership Events Coordinator will be an integral member of the Partnerships Team as well as working closely with the wider Inspiring the Future team. The role will help coordinate and deliver engaging activities across a diverse portfolio of partnerships such as Bank of America, Amazon, Tritax Big Box, Queen Elizabeth Scholarship Trust, Maritime UK, CIPD and the ERA Foundation. This is a dynamic role for someone looking to gain a breadth of experience in the charity sector and keen to learn about the education sector and career-related learning, social mobility and volunteer engagement. We are looking for someone passionate about motivating and inspiring children who relishes working with a range of stakeholders to create impactful activities. Education and Employers is a friendly, diverse, and welcoming organisation and the successful candidate will be well supported. Key Accountabilities: The exact brief will be finalised with the successful candidate but the role will be expected to undertake the following key accountabilities: Enquiries management and administrative support across the programme team Providing administrative support across the team, including record-keeping, responding to incoming enquiries, data entry, meeting minute-taking, scheduling, event coordination, etc Monitoring new event registrations from schools and sending welcome emails, keeping this up to date with the latest opportunities and messaging for schools Tracking and reporting back to Head of Partnership Delivery and Events Lead on delivery against agreed targets Using Salesforce CRM to support with data management, assisting with maintaining up to date records and supporting data cleansing as needed Setting up virtual and face-to-face activities including school liaison, securing volunteers, organising events via the Inspiring the Future system and hosting on tech platforms (Zoom, MS Teams etc) Supporting the collection of feedback and data after each event to measure impact Managing the enquiries inbox and/or switchboard phone number, responding to enquiries from schools and volunteers about the charity’s work and programmes and how to sign up Delivery Recruiting and engaging schools according to the geographic or sector focus of a funded partnership Supporting the engagement of employers and volunteers in special activities within funded projects. Facilitating interactive virtual and face to face activities to connect pupils with volunteers through themed sessions, Q&A or job guessing-game format. Contributing to the successful delivery of a funded project with the ERA Foundation, supporting the wider team to plan, coordinate and deliver activities including volunteer recruitment, development of resources, and outreach and engagement with schools and teachers. Supporting and co-hosting teacher training sessions, staff meetings and info webinars to promote Inspiring the Future and encourage engagement and independent usage of the platform. Supporting the development of educational resources that provide insight into the world of work and different sectors Other ad hoc tasks to support the team as needed, such as administration of school competitions, etc We are looking for an agile worker, capable of absorbing key information quickly, as well as handle a voluminous workload. Education and Employers is a small charity working at a rapid pace to bring about change and the ideal candidate will be a self-starter with strong communication skills, able to absorb key information quickly and work well with a small team in a dynamic working environment. Person specification: We are looking for someone with the following Skills/ Knowledge/ Expertise Skills/ Knowledge/ Expertise Essential Minimum one year’s experience in a customer service, school engagement or school-based role Experience in successful relationship management – ability to engage confidently and sensitively with schools/colleges and at a range of levels of seniority up to and including headteacher level Outstanding customer service and telephone manner, including handling large volumes of email enquiries and dealing with difficult situations politely and assertively Strong organisational and administrative skills including close attention to detail and effective time management Persuasive and confident communicator who is influential, and effective in presenting a concept both in person and on the phone. Good level of education, demonstrating capability in producing written content to a high standard. Demonstrable experience of managing a diverse workload; being able to prioritise work and working under pressure. Good working knowledge and practical application of Microsoft Office tools Desirable Passion for supporting young people in realising their potential through harnessing skilled volunteers to engage in education Experience in virtual facilitation with children and young people Experience of project management and delivery Experience of client relationships management (CRM) databases, in particular Salesforce Experience of marketing to schools Experience of working in a small team Experience of working with volunteers Understanding of safeguarding, risk management and data protection Comfort and confidence in working with data to inform actions Personal Attributes Uphold our charity’s values - Inspiring, Inclusive, Innovative, Impactful, Integrity Flexible – responsive to changing operational context and new opportunities Team Player: working collaboratively and flexibly to achieve outcomes and is keen to add value to the organisation’s culture and ethos Able to undertake some occasional work in the evenings and at weekends Able to travel in the UK if required Application process The Education and Employers charity values having a diverse workforce. We are committed to equality of opportunity and welcome applications from individuals from all backgrounds. We offer a range of inclusive employment and family friendly policies as well as flexible working arrangements in order to support staff from different backgrounds. The closing date for applications is 9am on Monday 12th October and interviews will take place in the week of the 19th October. The organisation reserves the right to conduct interviews and appoint prior to the closing date dependent on the calibre of applications received. Please send a covering letter setting out your interest in and suitability for the role and a CV. Please include your name and the role applied for in the subject line of your e-mail. *Please note, in your cover letter we have a strong preference for human-written content. We want to hear about you, your genuine interest in the role, and why from your experience, skills, and personality you feel you are a great fit for the role We will only consider applications with both a CV and covering letter and applications will only be accepted from those with the right to work in the UK with a valid passport/visa. item.title: Governance & EDI Officer (12-month Fixed Term Contract)
item.description: The Biochemical Society promotes the future of molecular biosciences, facilitating the sharing of expertise, supporting the advancement of biochemistry and molecular biology, and raising the awareness of their importance in addressing societal grand challenges. We are seeking a Governance and EDI Officer, on an 12-month Fixed Term Contract, to support the Governance and EDI team. Please note that governance meetings are usually held between Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, so applicants should be available to attend meetings on these days as required. The Governance and EDI Officer will work closely with Trustees, the Senior Leadership Team, and other key stakeholders (both internal and external) to help deliver the calendar of governance committee, board and panel meetings ensuring adherence to pre-defined service standards and ensuring that all discussions, decisions and follow-on actions are recorded, communicated and actioned as appropriate, alongside supporting team members with EDI initiatives, including the Society’s EDI Community, the 2026 online EDI Symposium, Society involvement in the 2027 Minoritised Life Scientists Future Forum and organisational mentoring schemes. The post-holder will support with administration and management for various Committees by compiling and preparing agendas and associated papers before each meeting, preparing Chair Notes and producing accurate minutes of meeting within the agreed timelines. You will also act as a liaison between the Society/PPL and Committee members on practical and logistical matters, such as supporting with expenses, as required. The role will provide administrative support for the Nominations process and success planning, including Committee Chair, Trustee and Director inductions, along with drafting and reviewing policy documents and terms of reference. In addition, providing support on EDI initiatives with the wider team on the EDI Toolkit management. Suitable candidates will have experience in Committee work, with excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to build and maintain positive relationships with a variety of stakeholders. The successful candidate will also be able to present information in a concise report format, with strong attention to detail, while being able to work flexibly to manage competing demands as required. For more information about the organisation, please visit our website. Here is some information on our Benefits package. Closing date: 7th October 2026 Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please note that the interviews will be virtual and will be scheduled as suitable candidates apply. The advert may close early if a sufficient number of suitable applications is received before the closing date or an appointment is made. We are interested in every candidate who is eligible to work in the United Kingdom. However, we are not able to sponsor visas. Please send a CV and covering letter. It is important that you DO NOT include your Personal Information i.e. name and contact details in your CV or Cover Letter . This is because the Society is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive community - a place where we can all be ourselves and succeed on merit. We offer a range of family friendly, inclusive employment policies to support staff from different backgrounds. The Society takes the security of your data seriously. It has internal policies and controls in place to ensure that your data is not lost, accidentally destroyed, misused or disclosed, and is not accessed except by our employees in the proper performance of their duties. Please note that due to limited resources it is not possible for the Society to acknowledge receipt of applications. If you do not hear from us within two weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

item.description: Salary: £35,570 starting salary (salary range will increase to max £38,510 via the length of service) per annum (pro rata where applicable). Contract: Permanent basis, (funded currently confirmed until March 2029). Hours: Part-time 28 hours per week (excluding lunch breaks) Location: Bradford. a minimum of 3 days is required to work from the Bradford office. The postholder must be available to travel across Bradford for meetings and home visits About Refugee Action Refugee Action exists to work with refugees and people seeking asylum who’ve survived some of the world’s worst regimes. We are a national charity with more than 40 years’ experience of empowering people who’ve survived some of the world’s worst regimes to secure the protection and support that they need to live with dignity and respect and build a new life in the UK. We do this by providing expert advice and casework, building the capacity of partner organisations and campaigning on the policies that affect them. To succeed in the role you will need to demonstrate: • Commitment to removing barriers to power for people with lived experience, and commitment to anti-racist practices. • Understanding of how the UK’s hostile refugee protection and asylum system impacts those affected by it. • Knowledge and experience of direct work with families who have complex needs and detailed knowledge of the UK asylum system. • Ability to work within a multi-agency setting, representing the needs of RA clients at the same time as understanding the needs of other services. • Understanding of safeguarding practice & statutory social care structures and processes. • Ability to follow an assessment threshold and to engage appropriate tools to ensure thorough assessments • Ability and commitment to reflect on your practice and a commitment to continual professional development and learning. • Understanding of the importance of working in a child-centred way • Excellent inter-personal skills, demonstrating ability to form relationships with a broad range of colleagues across RA, statutory services, and voluntary organisations with the ability to support and challenge. • Excellent teamwork and time management skills and ability to plan and manage own workload including case management experience • Excellent written communication skills and experience in presenting clear and accurate written documents to present evidence and advocate. • Understanding of the benefits and challenges of involving volunteers on services and projects and experience of supporting volunteers within a casework context. • Understanding of and commitment to key advice principles such as confidentiality, impartiality and non-directive approaches and a commitment to equality of opportunity. • Ability to be administratively self-sufficient, including the ability to record data for monitoring purpose. Those with lived experience as a refugee are particularly encouraged to apply Closing date: 23:59 on 05 October 2026 Interviews: 13 October 2026 (on Zoom) Refugee Action only operates in the UK, so all roles are UK-based, and you must have the right to work in the UK. This role is not on the Shortage Occupation List. If you have permission to work that is restricted to the Shortage Occupation List, we will be unable to appoint you to this role. You can find out which roles are on the shortage occupation list via these two links: · Skilled Worker visa: shortage occupations · Skilled Worker visa: shortage occupations for healthcare and education We are currently campaigning for people seeking asylum to have the right to work in the UK, see our Lift the Ban campaign here.

item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: The Glasshouse is the UK’s only not-for-profit plant installation and maintenance provider: a distinctive social enterprise where exceptional planting creates meaningful employment and measurable impact. We design, install and care for beautiful, nature-filled spaces for organisations across London, while opening up practical, paid pathways for women in custody or recently released from prison. Clients choose The Glasshouse because the planting is thoughtful, design-led and expertly maintained — and because every contract helps create second chances. As a Community Interest Company, 100% of their profits go back into impact work, so commercial excellence directly fuels training, employment and support for women with lived experience of prison. The Glasshouse is now entering an exciting new phase. We have a clear vision and business plan for the next few years, and are strengthening the leadership capacity needed to deliver it. The business has grown strongly, with earned income more than doubling in the last year, and the next chapter is about building on that momentum in a sustainable, well-planned way. With a new Growth Manager joining to strengthen the sales function and greater ownership already developing across the wider team, the opportunity now is to make sure growth is financially sound, operationally deliverable and always aligned with the social impact that sits at the heart of The Glasshouse. The Glasshouse is looking for a new Chief Executive Officer to work with the Founder and Board to bring this next phase to life. The successful candidate does not need to have been a Chief Executive Officer before, but will have held significant responsibility for the performance of a business, organisation or business unit. They will be commercially strong and purpose-driven, comfortable moving between the strategic view and the operational detail, and able to turn plans, budgets and a sales pipeline into clear priorities and action. Low ego and high standards will matter here: they will be calm, pragmatic and enabling, building trust across the Founder, Board, Growth Manager and wider team, while ensuring that commercial success creates more meaningful opportunities, greater stability and stronger futures for women with lived experience of prison. To do this role well, the successful candidate will need sound judgement, inspiring leadership skills, commercial confidence and the ability to turn ambition into practical action. To read more about this opportunity and to learn how to apply, please download the full appointment brief. item.title: JUMP Project Coordinator
item.description: Job Description Post: JUMP Project Coordinator Salary: £30,000 (pro-rata/3 days a week) Hours: 21 hours per week. Flexible working; some evening and weekend work may be required. Responsible to: Frontline Support Manager Location: Brighton and Hove Jewish Community Centre (BNJC) Applicants must be UK based either in Brighton or Sussex, or be willing to relocate. We are only able to consider applicants who have the right to work in the UK. HIAS+JCORE is unable to sponsor working visas to the UK. We particularly encourage applicants from people with lived experience of the asylum system. About the role HIAS+JCORE supports refugees and asylum seekers, led by Jewish values. Our work is driven by the belief that the Jewish community should play an active part in building a society in which Refugees are able to live in dignity where the UK is a welcoming place free from racism. Our organisation came into this form through the joining of operations between two organisations: the UK-based JCORE (Jewish Council for Racial Equality) and HIAS, a global humanitarian aid and advocacy organisation. HIAS+JCORE is inspired by Jewish values and history to support those who are displaced, no matter their background. JUMP is a London-based befriending project for young asylum seekers and refugees who have been separated from their families. The three primary ways in which JUMP supports young people are befriending , casework and community . We are currently supporting 30 pairs through our London project and have built a Brighton branch of this project, supporting up to 10 pairs so far. We are looking for a self-starting team member who will help coordinate and continue to build this valuable project in Brighton. You’ll be responsible for the befriending pairs and undertake tasks such as develop and maintain relationships with partner organisations, manage referrals for young people, recruit volunteer befrienders, and setting-up and sustaining pairs. This includes leading an initial training day. Contact with befrienders is through monthly reporting, and bi-annual supervision (initially after three months for new befrienders); alongside ad-hoc communication on safeguarding or other urgent matters. Contact with young people is more regular and varies depending on their casework support needs. Community events take place from time to time and offer a space for all young people and volunteers to come together and celebrate the work they are doing on JUMP. You will need to attend these events, and liaise with your cohort of befriending pairs to ensure everyone has the correct information. JUMP also has Hardship Fund (HSF) available to young people who need financial support with travel, clothing, food vouchers, and phone contracts.. RESPONSIBILITIES Supporting the running of our JUMP project in Brighton, and overseeing and supporting up to 15 pairs, by: Supporting young people and the JUMP Community Where necessary arranging and attending appointments with the young person (GP, Home Office, Job Centre, and Legal appointments); Supervising and supporting volunteers befriending; Publicising JUMP, and engaging with key stakeholders Project monitoring, evaluation and record keeping ABOUT YOU Ability to support, develop rapport and trust with, and motivate both young people and volunteers from a range of backgrounds and ages in challenging circumstances, including the ability to facilitate and engage in cross cultural communication; Necessary Experience Desirable Experience Children and Care Leavers;

item.title: Outreach and Moving On Officer: Young People
item.description: Job description Outreach and Moving On Officer – Young People London There are about 2,000 LGBTQI people claiming asylum in the UK every year because of their sexuality, gender identity or intersex status. When they come to the UK they are still not safe. They are often abused in refugee accommodation by other refugees who come from the same or similar countries to the one they are escaping; they become homeless and depressed; they are rejected by their ethnic community and live in poverty. Micro Rainbow’s work also shows a dramatic need for employability and moving on support. When LGBTQI asylum seekers are granted refugee status, they are often given only 28 days to find new accommodation and a job. 28 days are not enough to prepare for a new life in a new country. This is a critical point for many refugees: without the right support they are at risk of homelessness, exploitation and depression. The Outreach and Moving On Officer role involves meeting with LGBTQI asylum seekers on a regular basis to establish their suitability to access Micro Rainbow’s housing and moving on programmes. It also involves supporting them while they live in Micro Rainbow’s safe houses and to move on from our safe houses. The ideal candidate is someone with lived experience of the asylum system and/or homelessness, someone who is passionate about equality and has the ability to connect and empathise with vulnerable people whilst maintaining strict professional boundaries. Micro Rainbow will provide training and on-going support. We will consider applications for two, three or four days a week from candidates based in London and/or the West Midlands. The ideal candidate will already have another part time job or other sources of income that will compensate for the part-time nature of this position. item.title: Head of Finance (13 month FTC)
item.description: Help accelerate the transition to a safe and stable climate The climate crisis is one of the defining challenges of our time. Meeting it requires bold ideas, ambitious organisations and the resources to turn solutions into action. Quadrature Climate Foundation exists to help drive that change. Through strategic philanthropy, the Foundation supports organisations, research, policy development and advocacy efforts that can deliver meaningful reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and accelerate progress towards a net-zero future. Working across some of the world's most pressing climate challenges, Quadrature Climate Foundation combines urgency, rigour and long-term thinking to maximise its impact. As the Foundation continues to grow its reach and influence, we are seeking a Head of Finance to play a pivotal leadership role at the heart of the organisation. This is an opportunity for an exceptional finance professional who is motivated by purpose and wants to use their expertise to support one of the most important missions of our generation. Reporting to the Finance Director, you will help ensure the Foundation's substantial resources are managed with the highest levels of integrity, effectiveness and accountability, enabling the organisation to deploy capital where it can have the greatest impact on climate outcomes. The Role Finance is a strategic function within Quadrature Climate Foundation. Beyond ensuring strong financial stewardship, the team provides the insight, systems and controls that support effective decision-making across the organisation. As Head of Finance, you will lead the financial control function, oversee financial reporting, planning and compliance, and help shape a finance operation that is fit for a dynamic and ambitious foundation. You will work closely with colleagues across the organisation, translating complex financial information into meaningful insight and helping leaders make informed decisions in support of the Foundation's mission. You will also have the opportunity to drive improvements in systems, processes and reporting, ensuring the finance function continues to evolve alongside the Foundation's growing ambitions. About You We are looking for a qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA) with strong technical expertise and a track record of leading high-quality finance operations. You may already be operating at Head of Finance level, or you may be a talented financial controller ready to take the next step. Either way, you will bring a combination of technical credibility, commercial awareness and excellent interpersonal skills. You will be comfortable operating in a complex environment, leading audits and statutory reporting processes, developing robust financial controls and partnering with senior stakeholders. Experience of charity accounting and the Charity SORP would be valuable, although we are equally interested in candidates with strong experience gained in other sectors who are excited by the Foundation's mission. Most importantly, you will be motivated by the opportunity to contribute to meaningful change and will be energised by working in an organisation focused on addressing the climate crisis. Why Join Quadrature Climate Foundation? This is a rare opportunity to join an organisation deploying significant resources in pursuit of lasting climate impact. You will work with committed and intellectually curious colleagues, help shape the future of a growing foundation and play a key role in ensuring that every pound entrusted to the organisation is managed effectively and deployed responsibly. For finance professionals looking to combine technical excellence with genuine purpose, this is a chance to make a meaningful contribution to one of the most important challenges facing society today. This is a 13 month fixed term contract and we are looking for someone who is able to start in October or November 2026. We are partnering exclusively with Bryony Thomas of Allen Lane. For an informal conversation please contact Bryony through the agency website.
item.dc:creator: Quadrature Climate Foundation

item.title: Advocacy and Policy Officer
item.description: Salary: £27,788 - £28,519 Location: London, United Kingdom Team: Policy, Advocacy and External Affairs (PAEA) Line Manager: Head of Advocacy and External Affairs Line Reports: 0 Hours: 35 hours per week Contract : 6 months fixed-term contract with possibility of extension Grade: 5 Safeguarding: Basic Deadline 9 October 2026 ABOUT THE ROLE Are you passionate about creating change in the humanitarian sector? Are you looking to join a collaborative team working to influence policy, practice and decision-making across the humanitarian sector? As an Advocacy and Policy Officer, you’ll play an important role in supporting evidence-led advocacy, strategic campaigns and policy priorities that aim to create meaningful change. Working within the Policy, Advocacy and External Affairs team, you’ll contribute to research and analysis, stakeholder engagement and campaign coordination, while helping the team identify new opportunities to increase its impact. This is an exciting entry-level opportunity for someone who is curious, proactive and passionate about making a difference. We’re looking for someone who: Is passionate about humanitarian issues and creating positive change. Has strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills. Is highly organised, proactive and able to manage competing priorities. Builds positive, trust-based relationships with colleagues, members and external partners. Is creative, collaborative and open to new ideas, technology and ways of working. Has experience in the humanitarian, development, human rights or a related sector. Pays close attention to detail while taking initiative and finding solutions. WHAT IS START NETWORK? Our purpose is to be a catalyst for system-level change that improves the efficiency, effectiveness and ethics of humanitarian action. We do this by working as a network to develop, test & spread new ways of collaborating and resourcing locally-led crisis response and anticipation. Our current membership is made up of nearly 130 local, national and international NGOs based all around the world. We also support 10 national and regional hubs made up of civil society organisations and NGOs as our vehicle for devolving power, resources and accountability. OUR VALUES WE PUT PEOPLE FIRST: Communities come first in our decision-making and programming. WE ARE BRAVE: We have great ambition and are willing to explore new things and take risks to achieve it WE OPERATE COLLECTIVELY: We leverage the value of working as a network, sharing risk and resources, and learning together. WE ARE INCLUSIVE: We see the value in diverse perspectives and work to remove the barriers that prevent voices from being heard. WE ARE OPEN: We work transparently and with integrity, building mutual trust in all levels of our work, from governance to programming. WE ARE ETHICAL: We behave and operate based on key principles of anti-racism, non-discrimination, and anti-colonialism. This is a work in progress. OUR OFFER TO YOU Being a part of a network involved in bringing change to the humanitarian sector. Hybrid working with options to work from home and remotely to support your work/life balance Employee Assistance Programme through Smart Health (depends on the country based) Family friendly policies, e.g., flexible working, maternity policy, parental leave and more! 25 days’ holiday (if UK based) plus company days over the End of Year period for all staff (depends on the country based) INFORMATION FOR CANDIDATES Our roles are open to discussion about flexible working. For part-time working and job-shares, please get in touch with us before putting in an application. Start Network is committed to protecting people, particularly children, at-risk adults and affected populations from any harm. We are also committed to safeguarding staff from any forms of bullying, harassment, sexual harassment, discrimination, and abuse of power as outlined in the Dignity at Work policy. Start Network embraces diversity, promotes equality of opportunity and eliminates unlawful discrimination. We are an equal opportunities employer and treat every application on merit alone. We particularly encourage applications from disabled, BAME, LGBTQ+ and non-binary candidates. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for disabled applicants who meet our essential selection criteria set out in the Person Profile.

item.title: Community and Hospitals Fundraiser
item.description: If you love making meaningful connections with people and want to make a difference locally, this could be the perfect role for you. As Community and Hospitals Fundraiser at Northamptonshire Health Charity, you'll engage with people in our hospitals, in workplaces, and in the community, helping to transform local healthcare through meaningful relationship building and fundraising. About us We're the charity that supports the NHS across Northamptonshire. By raising funds for Northampton General Hospital, Kettering General Hospital and the community and mental health services provided by Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, we help provide the equipment, environments and patient experiences that enhance care beyond what NHS budgets alone can fund. About the role As our Community and Hospital Fundraiser, you'll be a friendly and familiar presence across Northampton General Hospital, Berrywood Hospital and communities throughout South Northamptonshire. Most of your time will be spent out and about on wards, in workplaces and at community events, building relationships and inspiring support for the charity. You'll be approachable, visible and passionate about helping people make a difference to local healthcare. What you'll be doing Building strong relationships with NHS staff, ward teams and department leads, helping the Charity become a trusted and familiar presence across our hospitals. Connecting with local businesses, schools, clubs and community groups, growing support for the Charity across Northampton and South Northamptonshire. Inspiring people to get involved, whether that's playing our lottery, taking part in an event or supporting a fundraising campaign. Delivering engaging talks and presentations that bring our impact to life and show how supporters make a difference. Keeping accurate supporter records and ensuring every new supporter enjoys a smooth and positive experience. Working towards clear recruitment and income targets, taking pride in the difference you make. What we're looking for We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys meeting new people and building meaningful relationships. You'll be confident striking up conversations, comfortable asking for support and have the skills to foster long term support. You'll be able to work independently, think on your feet and build rapport with a wide range of people, from senior clinicians and NHS colleagues to community groups, local business leaders and supporters. Most importantly, you'll bring warmth, enthusiasm and a passion for making a difference to local healthcare. The details 35 hours per week (part-time and flexible working requests considered) £30,000 per annum plus benefits 12-month fixed-term contract, with the potential to become permanent Based across Northampton General Hospital, Berrywood Hospital, Northamtpon and South Northamptonshire Regular evening and weekend events required How to apply Please submit your CV and a cover letter. Applications close on 23 October 2026 , although we reserve the right to close the vacancy early, so we encourage applications as soon as possible.
item.dc:creator: Northamptonshire Health Charity

item.title: Senior Service Improvement Lead
item.description: Life is looking for an experienced and forward-thinking Senior Service Improvement Lead to drive meaningful improvements across our Supported Housing, Helpline and Community Services. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about improving services, creating positive outcomes for clients, and leading change that makes a real difference. Working closely with senior leaders across the organisation, you will identify opportunities for improvement, develop evidence-based solutions, and lead projects from concept through to implementation and evaluation. About the Role: Reporting to the Director of Housing, you will lead a programme of service improvement activities across the organisation. Using service data, feedback, complaints, staff insight and the lived experiences of clients and residents, you will identify opportunities to enhance quality, consistency, accessibility and efficiency. You will: Lead service improvement projects from diagnosis and planning through to implementation and handover. Facilitate cross-departmental working groups and coordinate stakeholders across multiple services. Analyse complaints, feedback and performance information to identify opportunities for organisational learning. Support the development of effective policies, procedures, SOPs and guidance. Apply continuous improvement and Lean methodologies to improve processes and service delivery. Support managers in developing meaningful KPIs and measuring project benefits. Champion client and resident involvement in service reviews and redesign activities. Influence change and build strong working relationships across all levels of the organisation. Essential Experience: Leading service improvement projects from planning through to delivery and evaluation. Coordinating cross-functional projects involving multiple teams and stakeholders. Reviewing and improving policies, procedures and operational processes. Using complaints, feedback and performance information to drive improvement. Supporting managers to develop KPIs and measure outcomes. Undertaking quality reviews, audits or service reviews and implementing recommendations. Working independently while exercising sound judgement and managing competing priorities. Desirable Experience: Experience working within the charity, housing, health, care or wider public service sectors. Experience of working with or managing volunteers. Knowledge of housing and housing-related support services. Lean Six Sigma, Lean Practitioner, Project Management, Quality Management or Change Management qualifications About Life: Life is a national pregnancy support charity that helps over 60,000 people a year. Through our services, we help people – whoever they are – to meet pregnancy or pregnancy loss with courage and dignity so they can flourish. Our services include: Supported housing and community support Counselling and skilled listening Free pregnancy tests and baby supplies Our values All our work is underpinned by the following universal human values: Humanity – All people are special and equal Solidarity – We’re with you and for you Community – We’re better together Charity – Doing good for one another Common good – Building a better world Information about the role: For further information, please see the attached job description. Salary: £45,000 – £50,000 per annum, depending on experience Hours: 35 hours per week (flexible and compressed working arrangements in line with organisational policy are available) Location: Home Based with travel – please note a full UK driving licence is required for this role Benefits: At Life we are passionate about providing our employees with a supportive and engaging environment. As well as ongoing development and training, we offer our: Generous holiday allowance, starting at 25 days per year (pro rata for part time hours) Birthday Leave (applicable after 1 years service) Extra annual leave for long term service Company Pension Scheme Signed member of the Menopause Workplace Pledge Employee Assistance Programme Paid mileage for travel outside your base location Flexible working arrangements Safeguarding and Equality: Life is committed to protecting all staff, volunteers and service users from harm of any kind. Life expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We are committed to ensuring diversity and equality within our organisation by encouraging applications from all backgrounds. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks. Life takes its obligation to protect the rights of children and vulnerable people very seriously; therefore, the successful candidate for this post will be also subject to extensive background checking, including an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check (DBS) which is paid for by the Charity.
