item.title: Philanthropy Manager
item.description: Are you an experienced major donor fundraiser who loves building meaningful relationships and inspiring people to give? Could you play a key role in growing philanthropy for one of the UK's leading nature and conservation organisations? We're partnering with the British Trust for Ornithology (BTO) to find a Philanthropy Manager , Major Donors to develop and grow their major giving programme, securing significant gifts to help create a better future for birds, nature and people. Salary: £40,354 Contract: Permanent, full -time and part-time hours considers. Location: Hybrid or remote, with offices in Thetford, Bangor, Stirling and Lisburn. Benefits: 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing with service, two paid journey days for more sustainable travel, an 11% employer pension contribution, life assurance, enhanced sick and family leave, health cash plan, Employee Assistance Programme, flexible working, free BTO training courses, retail and wellbeing discounts, cycle to work scheme, coaching and mentoring. Culture: A supportive and inclusive workplace with plenty of autonomy, active staff networks and a strong commitment to sustainability. About the charity: At BTO, birds are more than a passion; they're a powerful lens through which to understand the world around us. For nearly a century, their science has shaped national conservation policy, fuelled grassroots volunteering and helped build one of the most impressive biodiversity datasets in the UK. Working across all four nations, BTO combines robust scientific research with a belief in the power of people to bring about positive change. About the role: As Philanthropy Manager, Major Donors, you'll take the lead on developing relationships with existing and prospective major donors, inspiring them to make significant gifts to BTO. You'll manage a portfolio of supporters and prospects, creating personalised cultivation and stewardship plans that bring people closer to BTO's work and build long term support. Working closely with the Head of Fundraising, senior leadership and trustees, you'll identify and research new prospects, develop compelling proposals and cases for support, and create bespoke opportunities to engage donors through meetings, events and presentations. You'll have real scope to influence how the programme develops and help build a sustainable source of philanthropic income for BTO. About you: We're looking for someone who is: Experienced in securing five and six figure gifts and growing income from major donors or other philanthropic sources. A natural relationship builder who can engage and inspire a wide range of people. An excellent communicator and storyteller, able to develop compelling proposals and donor communications. Strategic and organised, with strong prospect research, pipeline management and planning skills. Confident working independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues, senior leaders and trustees. Creative, proactive and excited by the opportunity to grow a major donor programme. You don't need to be an ornithologist. An interest in birds, nature, biodiversity or the environment would be wonderful, but what matters most is your ability to build genuine relationships and inspire people to support an important cause. If you're excited by the opportunity to connect people with BTO's work and secure the philanthropic support that will help its science and conservation impact grow, we'd love to hear from you. How to apply: Please send a copy of your profile or CV to Ellen Drummond at Charity People as the first step. Deadline: 9am, Monday 12 th October One Stage Interview: 22 nd and 23 rd October (Virtual) Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.
item.dc:creator: Charity People

item.title: Chief Finance Officer
item.description: UNICEF UK is the UK Committee for UNICEF, the world's leading organisation for children. We inspire and engage supporters, raise vital funds, champion children's rights and create lasting change for children in the UK and around the world. We employ over 400 colleagues in the UK and have an income exceeding £150m. At a time when conflict, climate change and inequality are affecting millions of children globally, our mission has never been more important. This is an exciting moment to join us. UNICEF UK is entering a new strategic chapter, built around defending children's rights, growing our influence and diversifying how we generate income and impact. We have grown our income significantly through developing new commercial opportunities, expanding audience engagement, and building on the success of partnerships and ventures like Soccer Aid that have transformed our fundraising model. We're now looking for an exceptional Chief Finance Officer to join us as a key member of the Executive Team. Reporting to our Chief Executive, you will play a central role in shaping organisational strategy, performance and sustainability. This is far more than a stewardship role. You will help define UNICEF UK's future business model, evaluate investment opportunities, support commercial growth and ensure we have the financial insight, governance and resilience required to deliver our new strategy and maximise our impact for children. Key responsibilities include: Providing strategic financial leadership and commercial insight to the Chief Executive, Trustee Board and Executive Team. Providing executive leadership across Finance and the wider portfolio, including risk, governance, legal and facilities… Helping shape UNICEF UK's long-term growth strategy, including investment decisions, commercial partnerships and new income opportunities. Leading financial planning, forecasting, performance reporting and business case development. Working closely with colleagues across fundraising, marketing, partnerships, policy and digital to seize new opportunities whilst maintaining the highest standards of accountability and stewardship. Developing a high-performing, commercially minded team that supports innovation, transformation and growth. Playing a leading role as a member of the Executive Team, contributing to organisation-wide leadership, transformation and decision-making beyond the CFO’s functional portfolio We're looking for a qualified accountant with significant senior financial leadership experience gained within complex organisational settings. You will bring strong strategic capability, commercial acumen and a track record of helping organisations grow income, adapt and innovate. Experience of developing commercial ventures, partnerships or audience-led business models will be attractive. As a leader, you will champion inclusion and model our values in all aspects of your work. This is a rare opportunity to help shape the future of a globally respected organisation, influence decisions at the highest level, and ensure UNICEF UK continues to deliver life-changing impact for children around the world. For further information on how to apply, any queries, and a full recruitment pack, please click through to our recruitment site. The Closing Date for applications will be 11pm on Monday 12th October. UNICEF UK promotes equality, diversity and inclusion in our workplace. We make employment decisions by matching business needs with skills and experience of candidates, irrespective of age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation.

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: Behind every person who gets the right information, every volunteer who feels supported, every grant that reaches someone when they need it, and every community that brings people together, there needs to be an organisation that works well. That is where you come in. Inflammatory Neuropathies UK is growing, developing, and reaching more people. We have big ambitions for what comes next, and we are looking for an Operations Manager who can help us turn those ambitions into reality. A little bit about us We are the only UK charity completely dedicated to people impacted by Guillain Barré Syndrome (GBS), CIDP, MMN, and other Inflammatory Neuropathies. These are rare, life altering conditions, and we are here to make sure nobody has to face them alone. We provide information and support, personal grants, local groups, online communities, and much more. We bring people with lived experience together, fund research, carry out social research, and make sure our community has a voice. We are a small charity, working right across the UK, with big ambitions. And we do things a little differently. We are professional, but we are not very corporate. We are prepared to try things, ask questions, and change things when they are not working. We trust our people, value lived experience, and believe the people we support should help shape what we do. Above all, we put people first. So, what is the job? You will be at the heart of how Inflammatory Neuropathies UK works. You will oversee and develop our services, support our staff and volunteers, improve our systems and processes, help manage our finances and resources, support good governance, and help turn ideas into action. It is a broad role, because we are a small charity. You might be looking at budgets or governance one day, developing a service or supporting a volunteer the next. We need someone who can see the bigger picture, but who is also happy getting into the detail when it matters. Someone organised, practical, curious, and good with people. Someone who takes responsibility, solves problems, and looks for better ways of doing things. But just as importantly, we want someone who listens. Someone who understands that good operations are not just about systems, spreadsheets, and processes. They are about supporting people to do great work, and making sure our community gets the support it needs. Why join us? Because you can make a real difference here. You will work closely with our Chief Executive, staff, Trustees, volunteers, and community. You will have responsibility, trust, and plenty of opportunity to influence how we work and what we do next. We are a small, friendly team. We work hard, we care about what we do, and we enjoy doing it. We want people to bring ideas, challenge us, and help us get better. You do not need to arrive knowing everything. We are much more interested in finding someone with the right values, experience, judgement, and approach. The role is remote, with occasional travel across the UK, including to our office in Lincolnshire, as well as meetings and events across the Country. Applying is easy, we just want your CV, and a covering letter of no more than 1000 words explaining why you are right for the role. If there is a time to blow your trumpet, it's now. But make sure you get it sent before the job closes on 18th October at 11pm. If you want to make a difference for people, like making things happen, and want your work to have a clear purpose, we would really like to hear from you. We are Inflammatory Neuropathies UK, and along with our community, we are IN this together.
item.dc:creator: Inflammatory Neuropathies UK

item.title: Head of Research: Skills and Better Work
item.description: The Head of Research: Skills and Better Work is a new post for L&W. We’re expanding our team so that we can develop and deliver more – and better – policy-relevant research in the key areas of lifelong learning and progression to better work. The post-holder will develop and lead research and insight projects. Those projects will be designed to influence policy change that will get more adults engaged in learning, developing their skills, and achieving their potential and ambitions in work. Income generation is part of this work: sometimes they will respond to reactive tenders, but we expect that they will also seek proactive opportunities to fund their work. They will have the capability to lead a team of researchers, and work with colleagues with different methodological specialisms. The successful candidate will be confident with quantitative data, but might have a qualitative research background themselves, or they might think of themselves more as a ‘policy person’. The most important thing is that they have experience working out what insights are needed to solve a policy problem, and how to get them. They will work across the lifelong learning, essential skills and better work pillars of our strategy – but key areas of focus for them are likely to include: increasing employer investment in skills; improving apprenticeship access and quality; reducing inequalities in lifelong learning; understanding and harnessing the rise of online, self-led learning; career change. See the attached job description for further details. The role can be based in either Leicester or London. Benefits (FTE equivalents, part time pro-rated) -Salary of £47,250- £61,150 (FTE), depending on experience and location - 31 days FTE holiday increasing to 33 days after 5 years’ service, of which 3 are shutdown days in addition to public holidays. - Company pension scheme with 8% employer contribution - Group Life Assurance 3*salary - Hybrid working (with 40%-60% of your time required in the office) - Flexible working practices - Employee Development Scheme - Retailer Discounts - Enhanced occupational maternity, adoption, paternity and shared parental pay - Enhanced occupational sick pay - Eye care scheme - Employee Assistance & Wellbeing Programme - Gold award in Investors in People
item.dc:creator: Learning and Work Institute

item.title: Trainee Governance Consultant
item.description: About Us Counterculture is a creative firm serious about effective governance. Our partners provide clients with specialist professional services across strategy, finance, law, management, creative, governance and capital projects. We are consultants, accountants, solicitors, curators, project managers and fundraisers (we’re also musicians, artists, historians, writers). Our Company Secretarial team provides expert advice to boards and senior managers to ensure the efficient, effective and compliant running of board governance. Our team of governance professionals have a range of experience across charities, education, arts and cultural bodies. The company secretarial team is led by Richard Whitmill, an experienced governance professional, Fellow of the Chartered Governance Institute and prize winner for the highest overall mark on the Institute’s Qualifying Programme in 2024/25. With a client base primarily in higher education, the CoSec team sits within the HE team at Counterculture, led by James Coe who is a nationally recognised expert in higher education. Our students’ union team is led by Phil Benton who is a vastly experienced students’ union leader. Together, they run the fastest growing part of Counterculture’s portfolio and hold a client base which spans all kinds of universities and students’ unions. Role Context Counterculture’s company secretarial offer is rapidly expanding. We work with a range of clients offering outsourced governance and company secretarial solutions. This includes retained offers where we give ongoing support to boards and committees, strategic governance advice and the maintenance of key statutory records. It also includes one-off projects such as training, governance reviews, advice on incorporations and charity registrations. As our work expands we now need additional capacity to grow our practice area. We’re looking for someone who is interested in entering the governance profession to support this work, acting for a range of clients to support their governance. As well as on the job experience, we will support the successful candidate to undertake the Chartered Governance Qualifying Programme. This rigorous programme equips professionals with essential expertise in corporate governance, company secretarial practice and board support. Roles and Responsibilities: The role holder will work closely with an experienced governance team, providing effective governance and administrative support. This will include support to a range of existing clients, primarily in the students’ union and charity sectors. As the post develops there will be an opportunity to support other areas of Counterculture’s practice and client base on governance related matters. Duties Support a range of clients with the following: Support the effective planning of board and committee meetings including preparation of meeting agendas, board packs and action tracking. Attend board and committee meetings, producing accurate and timely minutes. Manage governance calendars, statutory records and filings with Companies House and the Charity Commission. Support the development of key governance policies and procedures. Support the team in the delivery of governance reviews and reviews of board effectiveness Support one-off projects such company and charity formation, delivery of AGMs and constitutional reviews. Learning The role holder will be supported and funded to undertake the Chartered Governance Institute Qualifying Programme. They will also receive personal mentoring from Richard Whitmill, a CGI prize winner and tutor on the qualifying programme. They will be given reasonable time off to prepare for examinations and be expected to undertake sufficient private study to prepare for examinations. The role holder will be expected to undertake at least one examination per sitting (two modules per year). Accountability The role will be line managed by Richard Whitmill, Partner. Skills and Experience The post would suit a junior governance professional looking to develop their career, or a person with board exposure looking for a career change (e.g. Executive Assistant, someone who has served as a trustee). Essential An interest in and commitment to the highest standards of good governance. Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities to deadline. Proactive, organised and detail-oriented. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Confident working with senior stakeholders and handling confidential information. Excellent IT skills and an ability to use Microsoft 365 and board portals. Team player with the ability to work collaboratively Commitment to learning and development and to meet learning expectations (see above). Desirable Experience in governance either in a staff, officer or volunteer role (e.g. previous governance role, executive assistant, students’ union sabbatical officer, volunteer trustee). An understanding of our primary client base in students’ unions, charities and higher education. We would consider applicants who are currently undertaking the Chartered Governance Qualifying Programme. Role details and benefits Salary: £30,000 per annum Location: Home Hours: 36.25 hours. Working pattern to be discussed with the line manager. Travel requirements. Frequent travel required to attend client board meetings and other role related duties. Approx one to two days per month. Holiday: 22 days per annum, increasing to 24 days after one year of service and 27 after a further three years. Pension scheme (employers’ contribution 3%, employees’ contribution 5%) Direct funding to undertake Chartered Governance Institute Qualifying Programme (subject to a Learning Agreement) Equality, Diversity and Inclusion We’re committed to ensuring our workforce reflects the diversity of the world and community we’re based in. We positively encourage applications from all individuals irrespective of their gender, age, home country, ethnic background, sexuality, religious beliefs, socio-economic background or disability.
item.dc:creator: Counterculture LLP

item.title: Regional Grants Manager
item.description: We're looking for an outstanding grants fundraising professional with a proven record of successful bids towards large and complex projects to join our South West team. You'll be responsible for providing advice and generating income across a variety of funders (including statutory and lottery) for a range of projects. Whilst we are seeking someone who can work across a broad range of grant opportunities, we are particularly looking for an expert in unlocking grant opportunities in urban contexts and grants that help deliver the National Trust's ambition to 'end unequal access to nature, history and beauty'. Internally this role is known as Grants Consultant. Hours: 30 hours per week with a degree of flexibility around working pattern, to be discussed further at interview. What it's like to work here We work in a matrix structure where you will be part of both a mixed discipline team directly supporting our places with advice and support and part of the wider regional and central fundraising community. You'll focus on regional priority projects and help identify and maximise opportunities through collaboration with local authorities, strategic partners and other stakeholders. You’ll be part of the Trust’s internal specialist delivery team: a flexible resource of specialist skills and expertise. As one of a multidisciplinary team of experts, including curators, fundraisers, building surveyors and project managers, you’ll be working with others to help make things happen. As this role covers the South West region, you could be based from any of our South West regional offices. Our hybrid working policy means you can balance office and home working with site visits and meetings at other National Trust places. We’ll talk about this in more detail at interview, but you should expect to be at a National Trust site for 40–60% of your working week. What you'll be doing You'll be involved in developing pipelines of projects to submit to key funders and then working with our inspiring teams to ensure that projects meet funder criteria. You'll focus on key projects and funding opportunities across a number of places. A particular area of responsibility will be identifying, developing and securing grant opportunities across urban areas and funding that supports the ambition to end unequal access to nature, history and beauty. You'll develop relationships with external collaborators, including local authorities, funders and partners, to optimise funding opportunities and build strong strategic partnerships. Above all else, this role is about generating income and leading the development of compelling, high quality applications. Who we're looking for · A fundraising professional with sound experience of submitting successful large (six and seven figure) funding applications to grant giving bodies and substantial knowledge of the grants and fundraising environment (or equivalent knowledge). · Specific experience of developing large applications for the National Lottery Heritage Fund (or equivalent experience). · Demonstrable experience of identifying, developing and securing urban grant opportunities and/or funding that supports greater access to nature, history and beauty for underrepresented communities. · Experience of working alongside local authorities, combined authorities and other strategic partners to maximise funding opportunities and deliver shared outcomes. · Someone passionate about fundraising and able to inspire and enthuse others. · Experience of developing complex funding bids as part of a wider project team and bringing general project management/development skills. · Someone able to work to tight deadlines and prioritise effectively. · Strong consultancy skills including listening, collaborative working, relationship building and influencing across a range of stakeholders. · Someone who can write high quality applications while also bringing strategic thinking to support future planning. The package The National Trust has the motto ‘For everyone, for ever’ at its heart. We’re working hard to create an inclusive culture, where everyone feels they belong. It’s important that our people reflect and represent the diversity of the communities and audiences we serve. We welcome and value difference, so when we say we’re for everyone, we want everyone to be welcome in our teams too. • Substantial pension scheme of up to 10% basic salary • Free entry to National Trust places for you, a guest and your children (under 18) • Rental deposit loan scheme • Season ticket loan • EV car lease scheme (for roles that meet the salary criteria) • Perks at work discounts such as gym memberships, shopping discount codes, cinema discounts • Holiday allowance up to 32 days relating to length of service, plus holiday purchase scheme, subject to meeting minimum criteria. • Flexible working whenever possible • Employee assistance programme • Free parking at most Trust places Closing Date: 04 October 2026 Interview Date: 12 October 2026 (Killerton, Exeter)

item.title: Partnerships Manager
item.description: Partnerships Manager Salary: £37,853 per annum Location: Norwich or Cambridge Office – Hybrid working Hours: 37.5 hours per week Contract: Permanent About East Anglian Air Ambulance We are East Anglian Air Ambulance. A charity providing lifesaving critical care every day of the year across Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Norfolk and Suffolk. Whether by air or road, we bring hospital-level care to the most seriously ill and injured, probably on the worst day of their lives. From blood transfusions and pain relief to anaesthesia and emergency surgery, our doctors and paramedics give patients the best chance of survival and recovery. And it doesn’t stop there. We also offer vital aftercare, train people in lifesaving skills, and carry out clinical research to keep improving care. We’re fuelled entirely by donations, without any regular government funding, so our corporate supporters and their fundraising is hugely important to us. About the role We are bringing relationship fundraising (major giving) and partnerships into one team, and you will play a significant role in growing corporate supporters and income for the charity. You will shape the corporate partnerships strategy and lead a great partnerships team who are securing new and stewarding existing, corporate supporters and commercial partnerships across East Anglia. Key responsibilities include: You will be developing and implementing a partnerships strategy, managing a team and delivering a budget. You will also be creating innovative and bespoke supporter journeys, products and propositions, to engage with new and existing corporate partners. Working closely with relationship fundraising colleagues you will help to identify and steward c-suite and senior decision makers in organisations. Through collaboration with other teams, you will find new opportunities to grow additional income and support including, event sponsorship, corporate team event registrations, corporate volunteering opportunities, in kind and pro-bono support and community initiatives. You will also play a part nationally by being our relationship lead with Air Ambulances UK’s (AAUK) national corporate partnerships team. Attending and participating in AAUK meetings, identifying and assisting in securing national partnership opportunities and account managing at a regional level any national partnerships secured. You’ll bring: Recent experience of working as a manager within a charity, a new business or account management team or organisation. You will be great at securing new business, building and stewarding relationships with companies and senior decision makers in organisations, and will have hopefully delivered some fantastic pitches in your time. A good working knowledge of commercial partnership and sponsorship agreements will be a bonus. If you are a whizz at LinkedIn, really like helicopters and inspiring companies to get involved in supporting charities, we want you! N.B. This role will be worked a minimum of 3 days a week from our Norwich or Cambridge office and up to 2 days a week from home. The exact days worked in the office will be agreed with the successful candidate, but you must live within a commutable distance of Norwich or Cambridge. Closing Date: 9am, Thursday 8th October 2026 Interview Date: 15th October 2026 (to be held in person at Helimed House, Norwich) Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. No agencies please.

item.title: Head of Supporter Services & Stewardship
item.description: Head of Supporter Services & Stewardship Magen David Adom UK £45,000-£50,000 depending on experience Finchley Central, London | Permanent | Full-time 4 days per week in the office Make every act of generosity count. Magen David Adom UK is looking for an exceptional Head of Supporter Services & Stewardship to lead the experience its supporters receive after they choose to give. This is a brilliant opportunity for an experienced supporter care, stewardship or relationship-management professional to step into a senior leadership role at an ambitious, growing charity, and to shape a function that sits right at the heart of its future. Magen David Adom is Israel's national emergency medical, ambulance and blood service, providing lifesaving care to anyone who needs it, regardless of ethnicity or religion. In 2025 alone, MDA answered 4.29 million emergency calls, dispatching a response team every 22.8 seconds. Behind that work is an extraordinary community of supporters, donors and volunteers. This role is about making sure their experience of supporting MDA is every bit as thoughtful, professional and meaningful as the generosity they show. Why now? This is an exciting moment to join Magen David Adom UK. The charity has grown significantly, from £4m income in 2016 to £9m in 2026, and is growing in activity, stature and complexity. As MDA approaches its Centenary in 2030, MDA UK has embarked on its ambitious Towards Machratayim campaign, supporting the renovation and construction of ambulance stations, and helping to ensure MDA's staff and volunteers have the facilities, support and equipment they need for the challenges ahead. With that growth comes an opportunity to take supporter care and stewardship to the next level. MDA UK already has a loyal supporter base, alongside significant donors and committees who fund everything from lifesaving vehicles and equipment to major capital projects in Israel. The challenge for you will be to make sure what happens after someone gives is just as exceptional as what comes before it. What will you be doing? Reporting directly to the CEO and joining the Senior Leadership Team, you'll lead a team of two Supporter Services Executives and become the organisational bridge between fundraising, supporter services, CRM and data, operations and colleagues at MDA Israel. You'll bring together the detail, systems and human touch that make brilliant stewardship possible. That means you'll: Lead and develop supporter services, creating a warm, responsive and consistently excellent experience for supporters at every level. Build thoughtful stewardship journeys for significant donors, committees and project supporters, ensuring people understand not only where their money has gone, but the difference it has made. Keep donor promises on track, from recognition and project milestones to dedications, visits and meaningful updates. Turn complexity into compelling communication, translating medical, technical, construction and procurement information into clear, engaging stories and updates for supporters. Strengthen processes and systems, ensuring CRM records, workflows and responsibilities are clear, accurate and reliable. Champion the supporter voice across the charity, spotting opportunities to improve experiences, solve recurring problems and help MDA UK grow responsibly. Crucially, this isn't a frontline major donor fundraising role. You don't need a track record of personally securing six-figure gifts. Your expertise will be in what makes relationships last: exceptional care, thoughtful communication, attention to detail, strong systems and doing what you said you would do. Who are we looking for? You'll probably have spent at least five years working in supporter services, donor care, stewardship, customer or client services, account management, or another relationship-focused environment. You'll have experience of leading or supervising people and be someone who can keep multiple projects, stakeholders and deadlines moving without losing sight of the individual supporter at the centre of them. You'll be equally comfortable talking to a significant donor, briefing a colleague, improving a process, chasing an overdue project update or turning complex information into a warm and engaging supporter communication. You'll bring: A genuinely strong supporter-service mindset Experience of stewardship, donor relations or high-value relationship management Confident people leadership Exceptional organisation and follow-through Excellent written and verbal communication Experience working with HNW individuals, international stakeholders and public figures Strong judgement, discretion and attention to detail Confidence using CRM systems, data and digital tools Diplomacy and persistence, with the ability to bring people together and make things happen. Experience of Raiser's Edge, capital or medical fundraising, donor-funded projects, international partnerships or donor visits would all be helpful, but they are not essential. MDA UK is also keen to find someone with a forward-thinking approach who is open to using emerging AI tools to improve customer and supporter relationships. What's it like to work at MDA UK? MDA UK is a small, close-knit and ambitious team that, in the words of its CEO, consistently "punch above their weight" in the outcomes and impact they deliver. That means this isn't a role where you'll disappear into a large structure. You'll have visibility, responsibility and scope to influence how the organisation develops. MDA UK actively encourages its people to bring themselves to their work: their experience, contacts, creativity, ideas and belief in the humanitarian principles underpinning MDA's work. As the organisation builds towards 2030, the successful candidate will have a genuine opportunity to make their mark, contribute to current strategy and help shape future priorities. The culture is underpinned by four values: Be All In. Be Positive. Be Forward Thinking. Be Trusted. For the right person, there's something particularly special here: the chance to build exceptional supporter experiences while knowing that behind every project, every ambulance and every donor relationship is a humanitarian mission focused on saving lives. A copy of the job description and a letter from the CEO can be found in the Application Resources How to apply If you bring the skills, judgement and drive for this role, we'd love to hear from you. Please email Abi at Charity People to learn more about the role Closing date for applications: Friday 2nd October at 9am, send CV and covering letter. First interview round on Friday 9th October, second interview round to TBC. MDA UK welcomes applicants from a wide variety of backgrounds, experiences and interests. What matters is that you can demonstrate the skills required for the role and share the values and humanitarian principles that underpin the organisation's work. Charity People is a forward thinking, inclusive organisation that actively and deliberately promotes equity, diversity and inclusion. We know organisations thrive when inclusion is at the forefront. We evidence our commitment by matching charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates irrespective of background e.g. age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we believe that greater diversity leads to greater results for the charities we work with.
item.dc:creator: Charity People

item.title: Programme Support and Admin Officer
item.description: Frazzled is a small mental health and wellbeing charity founded by Ruby Wax OBE, based on the power of emotional openness. Our free, volunteer-led meetings run online every single day of the year, alongside face-to-face groups, offering people a chance to share, listen and feel heard in a supportive community. We're looking for a confident, positive self-starter with a high level of emotional intelligence, attention to detail and excellent communication skills to be our new Programme Support and Admin Officer. You will coordinate our meeting schedule, manage busy inboxes and help our volunteers feel supported. Working closely with the Programmes Manager, you will keep services running smoothly and our systems well organised. You will also support the CEO and Head of Fundraising with application administration, reports, meetings and events. Practical confidence with technology is essential. You will investigate everyday Zoom problems and help facilitators resolve them patiently, following through on queries and referring concerns to the Programmes Manager. Working pattern Our meetings run from early morning until late evening, seven days a week. Hours can be spread across the week, with weekday inbox checks and some evening and occasional weekend support for technical or meeting issues. All checks and out-of-hours work form part of your 24 contracted hours, with clear cover arrangements. Key responsibilities Core programme and technical support Coordinate schedules, liaise with volunteers, arrange routine cover and keep booking details, Zoom sessions and meeting documents up to date. Respond helpfully and sensitively to public and volunteer enquiries, following up queries and escalating concerns appropriately. Help facilitators resolve Zoom problems with joining links, host access, audio, video and settings. Create simple guidance and short video walkthroughs. Host Ruby Wax public meetings on Zoom and provide technical support. Volunteer support Support recruitment and onboarding through interview arrangements, DBS checks, induction and training bookings, and accurate volunteer records. Review volunteer feedback and promptly refer safeguarding, wellbeing or performance concerns to the Programmes Manager. Maintain the observation tracker and arrange observations. Following training, support agreed observations under the manager's guidance. Organise and minute monthly volunteer meetings and prepare the volunteer newsletter. Data and internal operations Set up agreed meeting polls and participant surveys, check attendance and feedback data, and prepare clear summaries for review. Work directly with the CEO and Head of Fundraising on agreed application and reporting administration, gathering documents, tracking deadlines and organising meetings or events. Help prepare trustee papers and Annual Report materials, and maintain accessible shared files and clear handovers. Shared responsibilities Support partner correspondence and programme communications, suggest practical improvements and contribute to agreed organisational projects. About you and applying You will bring sound judgement, a compassionate approach and confidence with spreadsheets and online systems. Experience in administration, volunteer support or a charity is useful, as is creating simple instructional videos. Please read the attached job description and include your earliest available start date in your application. We ask that you write your application without AI assistance. This role involves substantial written and verbal communication with stakeholders, and we want to hear your own voice and examples.

item.title: Head of Fundraising
item.description: An exciting opportunity to make a lasting difference We are looking for an ambitious, creative and inspirational Head of Fundraising to join Unity MK at a pivotal moment in our journey. We are a homelessness charity in Milton Keynes about to take a big ambition to the next level. We are developing an exciting capital build project that will transform the way we support people experiencing homelessness in our city . This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to create a lasting legacy for our community - and we need an exceptional leader to help make it happen. The Role As our Head of Fundraising and Communications, you will own our fundraising and communications strategy across individual giving, trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships, major donors, community fundraising and events. A major part of your role will be to lead an ambitious capital fundraising campaign to support our new build. Working closely with the CEO, senior leadership team, fundraising and communications team and our supporters, you will identify and cultivate high-value relationships, develop compelling cases for support and inspire individuals, businesses, trusts and foundations to invest in our vision. You will have the freedom and responsibility to shape our fundraising and communications function; build on the strong relationships we already have and introduce new approaches that will increase our income and our impact. This is an opportunity for someone who wants to do more than deliver a fundraising plan. You will help shape the future of the organisation. About You You will be an experienced fundraiser with a track record of securing significant income and building strong, long-term relationships with donors and funders. You might already be leading a fundraising team, or you may be an experienced senior fundraiser ready to roll up your sleeves and apply your strategic thinking and commercial acumen in a broader strategic leadership role. Most importantly, you will have a commitment to tackling homelessness and be ambitious for the people we support . You will believe that fundraising isn't simply about raising money - it is about bringing people together around a shared vision for change. Why Join Us? This is an exciting time to join UnityMK, with the opportunity to: Lead a transformational capital campaign. Help secure the investment needed to create a major new facility and shape the future of homelessness services in our area. Build something lasting. Your work will leave a legacy that could benefit thousands of people for years to come. Have genuine influence. You will work closely with our CEO, Board and senior team and play a key role in shaping organisational strategy. Make a local difference. Every successful partnership, gift and campaign will directly contribute to helping people experiencing homelessness move towards a safer, more stable future. Grow and innovate. We want someone who will bring fresh ideas, challenge us to think differently and help us build a fundraising operation fit for the next stage of our growth. Ready to Make Your Mark? If you're an ambitious fundraiser and communications professional who wants to combine strategic leadership, relationship-based fundraising and a genuinely transformational capital project , we'd love to hear from you. This is a rare opportunity to use your fundraising expertise to help create something extraordinary for people experiencing homelessness in our community. We know that great candidates don’t always tick off everything in a Job Description. If you’re excited about the role and believe you have relevant skills, experience, or a different perspective to bring, we’d still love to hear from you. We value potential, transferable skills, and a willingness to learn just as much as a perfect match on paper. Please note: All direct applications or speculative CVs to UnityMK will be forwarded to Debbie Burbage Recruitment as part of our exclusive partnership.

item.title: Senior Individual Giving Executive (Retention and Development)
item.description: As Individual Giving Senior Executive, you'll play a key role in developing and delivering multi-channel campaigns that inspire supporters to continue and deepen their relationship with the Charity. You'll manage a varied portfolio of appeals, supporter retention, development, upgrade, cross-sell and reactivation activity, working across channels including direct mail, email and telephone. From campaign planning and creative development through to analysis and reporting, you'll take ownership of projects that help grow supporter loyalty and maximise long-term income. Working closely with colleagues across the Charity and external agencies, you'll lead on the planning and delivery of campaigns and supporter journeys that place supporters at the heart of everything we do. This role also includes line management responsibility for an Individual Giving Assistant, making it an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build their leadership experience. About us At The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, we raise money to save the lives of people affected by cancer. The funds we raise support world-leading research, state-of-the-art equipment and exceptional patient care at The Royal Marsden, helping deliver breakthroughs that benefit people with cancer across the UK and around the world. We're entering an exciting period of growth, with ambitious plans to increase income, grow our supporter base and deliver exceptional supporter experiences. That's why we're looking for a talented Individual Giving fundraiser to join our Supporter Retention & Development team. About you We're looking for someone who combines strong direct marketing experience with excellent project management skills and a genuine passion for creating outstanding supporter experiences. You will have: Experience delivering successful Individual Giving or direct marketing campaigns, ideally focused on supporter retention and development. Strong project management skills, with experience managing multiple campaigns, budgets and deadlines. Confidence analysing campaign performance and using insight to inform future activity and testing. Experience working with databases, data selections and campaign reporting. Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with experience working with agencies and suppliers. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities. Experience of digital fundraising, mid-value giving or telephone fundraising campaigns would be an advantage, but is not essential. Why join us? This is a fantastic opportunity to develop your fundraising career at one of the UK's leading cancer charities and help The Royal Marsden to revolutionise cancer treatment through groundbreaking research, and deliver world-leading care. We offer: 27 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, rising with service Hybrid and flexible working (60% home working) Generous pension contributions Enhanced maternity and adoption pay Life insurance Employee assistance programme Subsidised canteens Access to learning and development opportunities A supportive, collaborative and values-led culture Our values We're proud to be Respectful, Kind, Ambitious, Purposeful and Versatile . If you share our values and want to use your fundraising skills to make a meaningful difference to people affected by cancer, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and help us make life-saving breakthroughs happen for people with cancer, now and in the future.

item.title: Fundraising Assistant
item.description: Help protect one of the most extraordinary places on Earth while building your career in fundraising. Galapagos Conservation Trust (GCT) is looking for an organised, enthusiastic Fundraising Assistant to join our friendly team. This is an entry-level opportunity to gain hands-on experience across trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships, individual giving and major giving. You do not need previous professional fundraising experience: we’re looking for strong organisation and communication skills, attention to detail and a willingness to learn. About GCT GCT is the only UK registered charity focused exclusively on the conservation and sustainable development of the Galapagos Islands. For more than 30 years, we have worked with local communities, NGOs, authorities and researchers to protect the Islands’ unique wildlife and support sustainable livelihoods. Our 2026–2028 strategy focuses on ocean protection and restoring islands. About the role You will provide practical support across our Fundraising team, helping colleagues raise the money needed to protect Galapagos and ensuring our supporters receive thoughtful, timely communications. Your work will include: Maintaining accurate supporter and donation records on our database and helping improve our fundraising systems. Processing and acknowledging donations, preparing thank-you communications and responding to supporter enquiries. Researching potential funders and supporting the preparation of applications, proposals and donor reports. Helping deliver fundraising campaigns, mailings and corporate partnership activity. Preparing meeting materials, briefing notes and supporter communications. Supporting fundraising events through invitations, attendee lists, materials and follow-up. You will report to our Trusts and Grants Manager and work with colleagues across all four income streams. About you You will be comfortable organising tasks, keeping track of details and meeting deadlines. You will bring good written and verbal communication skills, confidence using Microsoft Office or similar software, and a careful approach to working with information and numbers. We welcome experience gained through employment, education, volunteering or other activities. Above all, you will be a helpful, proactive team player who is keen to learn and interested in our conservation mission. Experience with databases, charities, customer service or events would be useful, as would Spanish language skills, but none is essential. What you will gain You will receive training and support from an experienced fundraising team, with opportunities to develop your skills across several areas of charity fundraising. You will join a friendly, collaborative and inclusive team, with a direct connection to cutting-edge conservation work in Galapagos. Key details Salary: £28,000 per annum. Contract: Fixed term for 12 months. Hours: Full time, 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 9am–5pm, with occasional evening events. Location: Central London office, with hybrid working and a minimum of two days per week in the office. How to apply Please send your CV and a cover letter explaining your interest in the role and how your skills meet the person specification. Please write your cover letter in your own words, without using AI. Please see the attached job description and person specification for further details. GCT is an equal opportunities employer committed to creating an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. No agencies, please.

item.title: Community Organiser (Luton)
item.description: The role: Are you passionate about supporting communities to create lasting change? Do you believe that people most affected by climate breakdown, nature loss and inequality should have the power to shape the decisions that affect their lives? Friends of the Earth is looking for a Community Organiser to work alongside local communities, activists and our local action groups to build power, develop leadership and support community-led campaigns that achieve meaningful local change. This is an exciting opportunity to help strengthen grassroots organising locally, supporting people to come together around shared priorities and take action on the issues that matter most to them. Key Skills and Attributes: You’ll be skilled in: Relationship Building: Able to build trusted relationships with diverse communities, partner organisations, activists and decision-makers, engaging people around shared priorities and creating inclusive spaces for participation. Community Organising and Campaigning: Ability to support communities to identify issues, build collective power and develop campaigns that influence decision-makers and deliver meaningful local change. Facilitation and Leadership Development: Skilled in facilitating meetings, workshops and community activities, with the ability to develop the confidence, skills and leadership of others through training, mentoring and support. The team: The England team is at the heart of grassroots organising at Friends of the Earth and is responsible for supporting nearly 200 Local Action Groups across England to build power and campaign for change. Contract Details: Fixed term contract until for 24 months, in relation to funding. Hours: Full time (30 hours over 4 days) Location: Luton – Homebased. Closing date: Wednesday 14th October 2026 (23:59). Please note we only accept applications via the Friends of the Earth Application System. We offer a competitive range of benefits, good work/life balance including a 4-day working week with no loss of pay, excellent learning and development opportunities and a vibrant organisational culture. Our staff body is currently under-representative of People of Colour, LGBTQIA+ people and people with long term conditions or impairments. We are committed to eroding these historic barriers, so as to create a movement in which people from all walks of life see themselves in, and so we particularly encourage you to apply if you belong to one of these groups or sit at multiple intersections of disadvantage. We are committed to the Disability Confident standard and will guarantee an interview to any candidates who declare a disability and who meet the essential criteria for the role. Friends of the Earth staff who publicly represent Friends of the Earth (including all campaigners) are not allowed to also represent a political party. This is to ensure that there can be no confusion in the minds of the public about Friends of the Earth's party-political independence . Affected staff should also seek permission from the Senior Management Team if they wish to hold a non-public facing official role in a political party. If this is an issue, please do raise this with us as soon as possible. Friends of the Earth is an international community dedicated to protecting the natural world and the wellbeing of everyone in it. We lead campaigns, provide resources and information, and drive real solutions to the environmental problems facing us all.

item.title: Advancement Events Manager
item.description: About us Philanthropy & Alumni Engagement (P&A) provides a fundraising and alumni engagement function in support of King’s College London. We are proud to work with colleagues across the university and its health partners to help them serve society through world-leading education, research and healthcare. Our work also includes a partnership with the Maudsley Charity in support of children’s mental health initiatives between the university’s Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience and the South London & Maudsley NHS Trust. We are a committed team that brings together fundraisers working across different channels, alongside colleagues who promote King’s College London’s engagement with its worldwide alumni community. Our work is underpinned and enhanced by a range of dedicated professionals in supporting areas covering proposition development, supporter engagement, supporter operations and business operations. We have an impressive, well-established track record of success in securing support that allows the university and partners to deliver on their missions. This includes our global, award-winning World Questions: King’s Answers campaign, which set the standard in the sector and enabled us to raise substantial funds to help tackle some of the world’s biggest challenges. Ambitious and innovative, the team has won awards such as a CASE Platinum Award for Fundraising and a CASE Gold Award for Donor Relations and Stewardship. We are strongly values-driven with a focus on sustaining an excellent and supportive culture, which we see as key to creating a successful team that can support the university and its partners in making a real and positive difference to the world we live in. More on King’s College London King’s College London is an internationally renowned university delivering exceptional education and world-leading research. The university is dedicatedto driving positive and sustainable change in society and realising our vision of making the world a better place. Through its commitment to exceptional education, impactful research and genuine service to society, King’s College London is creating positive change in its communities, both in London and on the world stage. The Strategic Vision 2029 looks forward to King’s College London’s 200thanniversary in 2029 and sets out ambitious plans in five key areas: · Educating the next generation of change-makers; · Challenging ideas and driving change through research; · Giving back to society through meaningful service; · Working with our local communities in London; · Fostering global citizens with an international perspective. About the role Events play a vital role within Philanthropy & Alumni Engagement, creating opportunities to bring people closer to King’s, strengthen relationships and support philanthropic engagement and giving. As Advancement Events Manager, you will play a key role in delivering an ambitious programme of high-quality events for King’s alumni, donors, prospects and supporters in the UK and internationally. You will take ownership of a varied portfolio of events, from intimate cultivation dinners and senior roundtables to larger receptions and digital engagement, developing experiences that are purposeful, creative and tailored to their audiences. Working closely with colleagues across Philanthropy & Alumni Engagement, academics, senior leadership and external partners, you will lead events through their full lifecycle — from shaping the initial concept and developing the event plan, through to delivery, stakeholder management and post-event evaluation. You will bring strong project management skills alongside creative thinking, ensuring events are delivered to an exceptional standard while continually looking for new and innovative ways to engage our audiences. This is an exciting time to join the team. As King’s moves into a major new Campaign and towards its Bicentenary, events will play an increasingly important role in bringing the University’s ambitions, priorities and propositions to life. You will have the opportunity to contribute directly to these high-profile moments, creating experiences that deepen relationships and help connect our global community to the impact of King’s. The role will also contribute to the continued development of the Advancement Events programme, identifying opportunities to improve processes, share best practice and introduce new approaches that increase the effectiveness and impact of our events. If you are an experienced events professional who combines excellent organisation and delivery skills with creativity, initiative and a genuine interest in building relationships, this is an opportunity to play a central role in an exciting period of growth and change for King’s. Closing date: 04 October 2026. To apply, please click “Apply Now”.

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: We are seeking an experienced, highly organised and proactive Operations Manager to play a central role in keeping our London office running smoothly and supporting our wider team and organisation. The ideal candidate will have strong liberal instincts and support our mission to defend civil liberties in the UK. This is a varied and hands-on role with responsibility across multiple operational areas, ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. It is a new role to the organisation, initially offered as a 12 month fixed term contract, with the possibility of extension. Why join Big Brother Watch? A genuinely flexible, part-time role designed to support work-life balance A dynamic, successful and friendly team in a supportive working environment The opportunity to take ownership of an important and varied role The chance to contribute to an organisation at the forefront of defending freedom in the UK Flexible working that works for you 16 hours per work, with flexibility as to how these are worked We’re open to a range of working patterns (e.g. school hours, shorter days across the week, or compressed hours, potentially variations across term times / school holidays) Hybrid working, in practice will likely require min. 50% office attendance The rest of our team works full time in-office. However, for this particular part-time role we aim to agree on a working pattern that provides consistency and predictability while fitting around your other commitments. We particularly welcome applications from experienced candidates returning to work after a career break, including parents and carers. About you You’ll have strong experience managing or co-ordinating a busy office or operational environment. You’ll be confident in taking on tasks proactively, looking for ways to plan ahead to ensure smooth operational running and improved efficiency, and independently finding solutions. You’ll have excellent communication skills, liaising with all team members and providing the team with essential operational support as needed. You’ll have good IT office skills. Operations Manager job description Take ownership of the day-to-day running of the London office, ensuring it is organised and efficient Support logistics with office move (within same building or very nearby) Help co-ordinate logistics for meetings and staff travel Co-ordinate IT support, equipment and asset management Lead IT migration projects (e.g. changing software/support suppliers, as directed) Ensure the office and kitchen are adequately supplied Support with HR admin including recruitment of staff, volunteers and contractors Organise staff socials Organise cycle to work scheme Liaise with accountants, support basic book-keeping (receipt filing) Support with internal file storage, physical and digital Support with maintenance of databases Assist with postage and physical mailouts to our supporters Commit to highest standards of data protection Periodically undertake required office risk assessments Big Brother Watch Big Brother Watch is a UK civil liberties campaign group fighting for a free future. We’re determined to reclaim our privacy and defend freedoms at this time of enormous technological change. And we fight to win. We’re a fiercely independent, diverse, non-partisan and non-profit group of campaigners and researchers who work to roll back the surveillance state and protect rights in Parliament, the media or the courts if we have to. We publish unique investigations and pursue powerful public campaigns to pursue real change. We work relentlessly to inform and empower the public to collectively reclaim privacy, defend our civil liberties and protect freedoms for the future. We’re a small, dedicated and highly effective team of 7 (growing to 8) staff members and 5+ volunteers.

item.title: Data Selections Analyst
item.description: Job description About the team We have big goals over the next few years. We're going to be fighting for mental health in a way we never have before. Together we'll be working to make sure everyone experiencing a mental health problem gets the support and respect they deserve. Team information Will you join us? Are you confident working with data, have a strong eye for detail and enjoy solving data problems? We're looking for a Data Selections Analyst to join our Data & Analytics team within Supporter Experience and Data. Data plays an important role in how we understand and communicate with our supporters. In this role, you'll help make sure our fundraising campaigns and supporter communications reach the right people, at the right time, using accurate and well-managed data. You'll work closely with colleagues across Fundraising, Communications and Supporter Experience to understand their campaign requirements and turn these into accurate audience selections and data outputs. You'll use data selection and analysis tools, including FastStats, alongside our CRM to produce and validate supporter data. You'll also investigate data issues, manage competing campaign deadlines and help us maintain high standards of data quality. You don't need to have worked in the charity sector before or know all of our systems from day one. We're interested in people with transferable data skills who are curious, methodical and keen to develop their knowledge. This is a hybrid role and you'll be required to work from our Stratford office for a minimum of two days per week. This role will also requires a DBS check. Key duties and responsibilities The post holder will: -Produce accurate and timely audience selections and segmentation for fundraising campaigns and supporter communications. -Work with stakeholders to understand campaign requirements and translate them into appropriate data selections and outputs. -Carry out thorough validation and quality-control checks to ensure data is accurate and complete before it is released. -Manage multiple data requests and competing priorities to meet agreed campaign deadlines. -Use our CRM and data tools to investigate and resolve data issues, escalating more complex issues when appropriate. -Deliver accurate data to internal teams and approved third-party fulfilment partners. -Apply appropriate consent, communication preferences, exclusions and suppressions to supporter selections. -Help identify data quality issues and contribute to maintaining accurate supporter records. -Work collaboratively with colleagues across Data & Analytics, Fundraising, Communications and Supporter Experience. -Contribute to improving our data selection processes, documentation and ways of working. What are we looking for? Do you enjoy working with data and checking the detail to make sure things are right? Can you organise your workload when several deadlines are competing for your attention? Are you comfortable investigating data when something doesn't look quite right? We'd particularly like to hear from you if you have: -Experience of using data selection or analysis tools to produce audience selections or data outputs. Experience of FastStats would be helpful, but equivalent tools are equally relevant. -Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to validating and quality-checking data. -Experience of managing multiple pieces of work and delivering accurate outputs to deadlines. -Experience of using a CRM or customer/supporter database and an understanding of good data quality. -Experience of investigating and resolving data issues using appropriate data tools. -The ability to understand stakeholder and campaign requirements and translate these into appropriate data outputs. -Good communication skills and the ability to work with both technical and non-technical colleagues. -An understanding of audience segmentation and targeted supporter or customer communications. -An understanding of data protection and the importance of handling personal data appropriately. Experience in fundraising, marketing, membership, charities or another customer-focused environment would be useful, but it is not essential. If you enjoy working with data, solving problems and want to use your skills to support work that makes a difference, we'd love to hear from you. Mind's equity statement Mind is committed to equality of opportunity for all staff, and applications from individuals are encouraged regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships. Please refer to the Job Description while completing your application as candidates will be shortlisted based on how closely they match the criteria in the personal specification. Founded over 90 years ago, we provide around 2,500 homes for over 5,000 people across Islington, Hackney and Waltham Forest. ISHA is smaller and more local than many other housing associations operating in London. We are proud to remain a community-based housing association with a strong social purpose and an ambitious future. We offer a wide range of housing choices: social rented, shared ownership, intermediate rent, market rent, supported housing, and options for the elderly. We also provide homes and support for the Vietnamese, South-East Asian and wider communities. About the Role This is a rare opportunity to establish and lead a brand-new service improvement function at ISHA and make a visible difference to the services our residents receive. As Service Improvement Manager, you will lead a small team to help ISHA turn resident feedback, complaints, performance information and operational insight into practical action, ensuring improvements are implemented, embedded and deliver measurable results. Ultimately, you will help ISHA become better at learning, better at improving and better at delivering the services our residents deserve. The job: Building and leading ISHA's new Service Improvement Team. Driving a culture of continuous improvement across the organisation. Using complaints, resident feedback, Tenant Satisfaction Measures, Ombudsman learning and performance data to identify priorities and opportunities. Leading deep-dive service reviews to uncover root causes and implement practical solutions. Managing a portfolio of high-impact improvement projects from diagnosis through to delivery. Working alongside directors, managers and frontline colleagues to remove barriers and improve outcomes. Embedding learning from complaints, audits and regulatory activity into day-to-day service delivery. Ensuring resident voice and lived experience are central to service design and improvement. Measuring and demonstrating the impact of improvement activity through clear outcomes and benefits. About You We're looking for a curious, driven and collaborative improvement professional who combines strategic thinking with a hands-on approach. You'll bring: Significant experience in social housing, local government, social care, public services or another regulated customer-focused environment. A proven track record of leading service improvement, transformation, performance or change programmes that have delivered measurable results. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes and turn insight into action. Experience of leading complex cross-organisational projects and influencing stakeholders at all levels. The ability to challenge constructively, build credibility quickly and bring people with you through change. A passion for resident outcomes and service excellence. A strong understanding of the social housing landscape, including Tenant Satisfaction Measures, Consumer Standards and the Housing Ombudsman's Complaints Handling Code, would be particularly valuable. Why join ISHA? This is an exciting time to join us. You'll have the opportunity to influence how services are designed, delivered and improved across the organisation while helping shape our future approach to organisational learning and resident experience. This role offers you the chance to leave a lasting legacy. You will establish a function that helps ISHA learn faster, improve continuously and deliver better outcomes for residents. Your work will influence services across the organisation and ensure that resident feedback leads to tangible change. Ultimately, you'll help ISHA become better at listening, better at learning, and better at delivering the services our residents deserve. Ready to make a difference? We'd love to hear from you. Inclusion and Diversity We want ISHA to be a great place to work and to ensure that our communities are represented across our workforce. A vital part of this is ensuring we are a truly inclusive organisation that encourages diversity in all respects, including diversity of thinking. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian and those of Other Ethnicities, LGBTQ+, disabled and neurodiverse communities to make a real difference to our residents so that passionate commitment to customers, respect for everyone, pride in Team ISHA and trusted to make the difference remains at the heart of everything we do. Closing date: 9am on Monday, 12 October 2026. Interview date(s) are to be confirmed. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. Once you have landed on our website, you will need to do the following in order to apply for this role: Application Process When you submit your final application with your CV and a covering letter tell us: (a) Why do you believe you are a strong fit for the role, with reference to the job description and person specification? (b) Describe a significant service improvement initiative you have led. What was the challenge, what actions did you take, and what measurable outcomes were achieved? (c) Tell us about a service that frustrates you as a customer. What do you think is causing the problem, and what would you do differently if you were responsible for improving it? (d) What motivates you most about service improvement and delivering excellent outcomes for customers? (e) Is there anything else you would like us to know in support of your application? Please note: We can only be able to accept applications from candidates with eligibility to currently work in the UK. We do not offer a visa sponsorship programme. Applications sent without a covering letter outlining how your skills and experience match the role, as well as expressing your motivation for applying for the role will not be accepted. Asking for adjustments ISHA is committed to making our recruitment practices barrier-free and as accessible as possible for everyone. This includes making adjustments or changes for disabled people, neurodiverse people or people with long-term health conditions. If you would like us to do anything differently during the application, interview, or assessment process, including providing information in an alternative format, you will be able to contact us. No agencies please.
