item.title: Overnight Homeless Shelter Worker
item.description: Team: Night Shelters Location: On-site at Glass Door Night shelter venues in the boroughs of Kensington & Chelsea, Hammersmith and Fulham or Wandsworth Contract: Casual / Bank (ad-hoc shifts available between 21 November 2026 and 22 March 2027) Reporting to: Service Manager – Night Shelters Shifts available: · 7:00pm to 7:15am · 9:45pm to 8:15am (driver) Pay: £15 per hour Job Purpose You’ll provide cover on an ad-hoc basis, filling shifts when needed across our night shelters. As an Overnight Homeless Shelter Worker, you’ll be part of a small, professional team running Glass Door’s night shelters between November and April. Working alongside at least one other staff member, you’ll be awake and engaged throughout the night, supporting up to 35 guests who are experiencing homelessness. Your role is about creating a safe, calm, and welcoming space where guests can rest, feel respected, and be treated with dignity. You’ll build trust through friendly conversation, keep an eye on everyone’s wellbeing with regular checks, and step in when problems arise – from offering reassurance to someone in emotional distress, to calmly handling challenging behaviour, to calling emergency services if needed. Most nights are steady and focused on guest support, but there can be moments of pressure. We’ll provide training so you feel confident and prepared. You’ll also help serve a light breakfast in the morning and ensure our equipment is packed and ready for the next night – with one of you driving the van back to base. If you’re compassionate, calm under pressure, and committed to helping people move forward from homelessness, this role offers the chance to make a real and lasting difference. Job Responsibilities What You’ll Do You’ll be part of the overnight team making sure our night shelters are safe, supportive, and welcoming spaces for everyone staying with us. This is an awake, overnight role, you will be alert and engaged for the whole shift. Your main responsibilities will include: · Welcoming and supporting guests – Create a friendly, respectful atmosphere and build positive relationships with guests, volunteers, and colleagues. · Staying alert all night – Carry out regular checks around the shelter (every 20 minutes) to make sure guests are safe, and comfortable. · Responding to situations – Calmly manage any issues that arise, such as someone feeling unwell, experiencing emotional distress, or showing challenging behaviour. This may sometimes mean calling emergency services. Training will be provided. · Keep the shelter safe and secure – Follow all safety, security, and health and safety procedures. This includes locking and unlocking doors and making sure the space stays tidy and free from hazards. · Recording important information – Write clear, accurate shift reports and note any concerns or observations. Complete incident forms if needed. · Supporting volunteers – Offer direction and guidance to volunteers on shift so everyone works well together. · Enforcing behaviour expectations – Address situations where may display challenging behaviour, using a calm and respectful approach, conflict de-escalation training is provided for all staff. · Packing and unpacking the van – unload equipment and supplies into the van at the start of the shift and repack at the end of the night. The allocated driver will return the van to base (driver shifts are paid for an extra hour). · Restocking supplies – Keep an eye on essentials such as tea, coffee, and toilet paper, and restock from the van when needed. · Preparing a simple breakfast – In the morning, help serve drinks, toast, and porridge, and make sure guests are woken from 6am so they can leave by 7am. · Tidying and closing down – Gather equipment, pack it away, and ensure nothing is left behind. · Training and meetings – Attend occasional in-person training sessions, team meetings, or other activities. From time to time, you may be assigned online training to complete while on shift. · Take on shifts as they become available – These may include evenings, weekends, and public holidays, so flexibility is important. · Help with other tasks as needed – From time to time, you may be asked to help with other reasonable tasks that keep the night shelter running smoothly. Person Specification Essential · A valid driving licence for a manual vehicle and be willing to drive the Glass Door van. · A genuine commitment to providing a high standard of service and treating everyone with respect, kindness, and dignity. · Confidence in handling challenging behaviour calmly and respectfully. · Good communication skills, both spoken and written. · The ability to carry out manual handling tasks such as moving supplies and equipment. · Willingness to work on an ad-hoc basis and pick up shifts, sometimes at short notice. Desirable · Experience working with people experiencing homelessness or other vulnerable groups. · The ability to speak another language, for example Arabic, Tigrinya, Amharic, Polish, Spanish, French, or Russian. · A lived experience of homelessness. · An understanding of, and commitment to, trauma-informed care. · Relevant training such as first aid, fire safety, conflict de-escalation, or Mental Health First Aid. Other · Employment is subject to a satisfactory enhanced DBS check for adults. · You’ll be expected to follow Glass Door’s safeguarding policies and procedures. · A commitment to equality, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of your work. We value diversity, promote equality and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly welcome applications from people with lived experience of homelessness.

item.title: Individual Giving & In-Memory Fundraiser
item.description: St Nicholas Hospice Care is a successful charity serving the local area of West Suffolk and Thetford. Every year we support nearly 2,000 local people, delivering care across multiple settings. Our services are not just for patients, but for their family and friends too, and include everything from specialist medical care to bereavement support and practical help. We are looking for an enthusiastic and compassionate individual with a passion for fundraising, building meaningful relationships, and delivering outstanding supporter care. By joining the St Nicholas Hospice Care Fundraising Team you will play a vital role in raising the funds needed to support people facing dying, death, and grief across West Suffolk and Thetford. As our Individual Giving and In Memory Fundraiser you will help grow our income and supporter community and develop memorable fundraising opportunities that enable people to honour loved ones while supporting local hospice care. In this rewarding role, you'll lead individual giving campaigns, appeals and in memory fundraising initiatives, creating engaging supporter journeys that inspire long-term loyalty and support. You'll work closely with bereaved families, donors, colleagues and local partners to deliver exceptional supporter experiences and generate vital income for our hospice services. We're looking for someone with experience in fundraising, marketing, supporter engagement or relationship management, who is highly organised, creative and confident communicating with people from all walks of life. Sensitivity, compassion and a genuine commitment to our values are essential. Why join us? You’ll be part of a dedicated, compassionate and collaborative team whose goal is to make a real difference in people’s lives, ensuring every supporter feels valued and every donation counts. You will be part of a dedicated, compassionate and collaborative team that is committed to making a real difference in people's lives. Together, we ensure every supporter feels valued, every donation makes a difference, and every person accessing our services receives the care and support they deserve. What we offer • 25 days annual leave increasing to 29 with service • Enhanced Occupational sick pay scheme • Access to a group pension plan • A Health Cash Plan & Wellbeing programme • Free onsite parking • Access to Blue Light Card scheme with a range of discounts

item.title: Advocacy and Policy Coordinator
item.description: Salary: £27,788 - £28,519 Location: London, United Kingdom Team: Policy, Advocacy and External Affairs (PAEA) Line Manager: Head of Advocacy and External Affairs Line Reports: 0 Hours: 35 hours per week Contract : 6 months fixed-term contract with possibility of extension Grade: 5 Safeguarding: Basic Deadline 9 October 2026 ABOUT THE ROLE Are you passionate about creating change in the humanitarian sector? Are you looking to join a collaborative team working to influence policy, practice and decision-making across the humanitarian sector? As an Advocacy and Policy Coordinator, you’ll play an important role in supporting evidence-led advocacy, strategic campaigns and policy priorities that aim to create meaningful change. Working within the Policy, Advocacy and External Affairs team, you’ll contribute to research and analysis, stakeholder engagement and campaign coordination, while helping the team identify new opportunities to increase its impact. This is an exciting entry-level opportunity for someone who is curious, proactive and passionate about making a difference. We’re looking for someone who: Is passionate about humanitarian issues and creating positive change. Has strong analytical, problem-solving and communication skills. Is highly organised, proactive and able to manage competing priorities. Builds positive, trust-based relationships with colleagues, members and external partners. Is creative, collaborative and open to new ideas, technology and ways of working. Has experience in the humanitarian, development, human rights or a related sector. Pays close attention to detail while taking initiative and finding solutions. WHAT IS START NETWORK? Our purpose is to be a catalyst for system-level change that improves the efficiency, effectiveness and ethics of humanitarian action. We do this by working as a network to develop, test & spread new ways of collaborating and resourcing locally-led crisis response and anticipation. Our current membership is made up of nearly 130 local, national and international NGOs based all around the world. We also support 10 national and regional hubs made up of civil society organisations and NGOs as our vehicle for devolving power, resources and accountability. OUR VALUES WE PUT PEOPLE FIRST: Communities come first in our decision-making and programming. WE ARE BRAVE: We have great ambition and are willing to explore new things and take risks to achieve it WE OPERATE COLLECTIVELY: We leverage the value of working as a network, sharing risk and resources, and learning together. WE ARE INCLUSIVE: We see the value in diverse perspectives and work to remove the barriers that prevent voices from being heard. WE ARE OPEN: We work transparently and with integrity, building mutual trust in all levels of our work, from governance to programming. WE ARE ETHICAL: We behave and operate based on key principles of anti-racism, non-discrimination, and anti-colonialism. This is a work in progress. OUR OFFER TO YOU Being a part of a network involved in bringing change to the humanitarian sector. Hybrid working with options to work from home and remotely to support your work/life balance Employee Assistance Programme through Smart Health (depends on the country based) Family friendly policies, e.g., flexible working, maternity policy, parental leave and more! 25 days’ holiday (if UK based) plus company days over the End of Year period for all staff (depends on the country based) INFORMATION FOR CANDIDATES Our roles are open to discussion about flexible working. For part-time working and job-shares, please get in touch with us before putting in an application. Start Network is committed to protecting people, particularly children, at-risk adults and affected populations from any harm. We are also committed to safeguarding staff from any forms of bullying, harassment, sexual harassment, discrimination, and abuse of power as outlined in the Dignity at Work policy. Start Network embraces diversity, promotes equality of opportunity and eliminates unlawful discrimination. We are an equal opportunities employer and treat every application on merit alone. We particularly encourage applications from disabled, BAME, LGBTQ+ and non-binary candidates. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for disabled applicants who meet our essential selection criteria set out in the Person Profile.

item.title: Senior Investment Manager
item.description: Job description The following role profile sets out the focus on capital mobilisation, investment execution and delivery of our Fund Manager Incubator programmes that strengthen Pathway’s institutional capability. Role profile : Senior Investment Manager Reports to : Chief Executive Officer Location : London Contract : Permanent Salary : £58k - £65k Purpose of the role Following the Board’s sign-off of our Investment Strategy, the Senior Investment Manager will lead the implementation phase. The role focuses on: Mobilising capital for Pathway asset classes and Fund Manager Incubator (FMI) programme funds, Executing investments and overseeing portfolio management, and Projects that advance Pathway Fund’s mission, organisational capability, and external profile. This role combines investment leadership with FMI programme management, delivery & oversight. Key responsibilities 1. Capital mobilisation and investment execution Lead fundraising and capital deployment for Pathway’s Asset Class and FMI programme funds. Manage investor relationships, due diligence, and reporting to ensure confidence and accountability. Oversee execution of approved investment strategy, portfolio management, and risk oversight. Engage external advisors, consultants, and asset managers to support high-quality decision-making. Produce regular performance and impact reports for the CEO, Investment Committee, and Board. 2. FMI programme leadership Lead the FMI Programme, ensuring its successful development, delivery, and evolution as a cornerstone of Pathway's 2030 strategy. Drive specific initiatives critical to delivering Pathway’s 2030 strategy, primarily focusing on FMI 3.0 and evolving the FMI programme for future versions. Develop Pathway’s specific approach to and role in community asset acquisition models. Develop and adapt the FMI model to deploy intermediary upskilling frameworks and programmes as soon as funding is unlocked. Work cross-functionally with programme, operations, and communications teams to embed the FMI Programme and ensure successful delivery. Establish key milestones and performance indicators for the FMI Programme, ensuring alignment with organisational objectives and impact goals. Act as a lead custodian of the FMI Programme, ensuring its successful evolution and embedding across Pathway's wider strategic and investment activities while strengthening the organisation's long-term institutional capacity and sector leadership. 3. External representation and partnerships Represent Pathway Fund externally, articulating its investment and strategic approach to investors, partners, and sector stakeholders. Build strategic alliances with funders, intermediaries, and government bodies to advance mission-aligned investment opportunities. Contribute to thought leadership, publications and policy insights. 4. Organisational capability Oversee investment operations, reporting, and monitoring systems. Supervise investment and project deliverables, budgets, and milestones. Support staff development and training in investment, impact finance and project management. Provide strategic input to organisational planning, leveraging insights from both investment and strategic projects. Success indicators (First 12–18 Months) Initial Asset Class capital commitments secured and pipeline established. FMI 3.0 and future iterations delivered to agreed milestones. Investment Committee fully operational with regular performance reporting. Organisational systems strengthened to support efficient investment and project delivery. Pathway’s reputation as a leading racial equity investment wholesaler reinforced through external engagement. Candidate profile Essential experience Senior experience in investment management, fundraising, or strategic finance. Demonstrated success in leading multi-stakeholder programmes or strategic initiatives. Proven track record in capital mobilisation and portfolio management. Strong stakeholder management and influence at senior levels. Advanced analytical, financial modelling, and reporting capabilities. Desirable experience Experience in racial equity, social impact investing, or community wealth-building contexts. Familiarity with fund design, programme delivery, and organisational development projects. Exposure to policy, advocacy, or thought leadership in inclusive finance. Skills and attributes Strategic, innovative, and delivery-oriented. Excellent communicator and collaborator. Comfortable leading across organisational boundaries and driving change. Deep commitment to Pathway’s mission of racial equity and community wealth building. Reporting and governance framework Advisory support: Works with Investment Committee, Endowment Advisory Group (Brain Trust) and external advisors. Internal collaboration: Works across programme, operations and communications teams to embed strategic initiatives. Please note: Applications without a covering letter will not be considered. item.title: Press & PR Officer
item.description: We are seeking a Press & PR Officer to join our ambitious team. We know that incredible work takes place across our organisation every day, and that our services have a meaningful impact on the people and communities we support. We need someone who can ensure those stories, achievements and insights reach the audiences that matter most. This role is focused on leading the day-to-day delivery of our press office function and generating impactful media coverage that supports our organisational objectives. Working closely with the Director of Communications and Marketing, you will drive proactive and reactive media relations activity, identify opportunities for coverage, build strong journalist relationships and deliver PR activity that supports income generating initiatives, organisational priorities and our profile as a leading voice as a women’s employability charity. The role combines hands-on press office delivery with responsibility for developing PR proposals and media approaches for specific campaigns, fundraising initiatives and organisational projects. Strategic communications direction, organisational thought leadership strategy and reputation management remain the responsibility of the Director of Communications and Marketing. Your work will help raise awareness of our impact, support income generation and strengthen our reputation with supporters, partners, policymakers and the wider public. The successful candidate will report to the Director of Communications and Marketing and will work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation to maximise media opportunities and ensure our external profile continues to grow. This role is primarily focused on press office establishment and management, media relations and PR delivery. There may be instances where the post holder will be involved in supporting storytelling on our owned channels and with our corporate partners, especially if there is an intersection with media stakeholders. Whilst this role is part-time, as is the nature of news, media relations activity may not always fall within standard working hours. On occasion, urgent media enquiries may arise outside normal working hours and the postholder will be expected to provide reasonable support alongside the Director of Communications and Marketing. The role will also occasionally require attendance at events, launches, media opportunities outside contracted working hours. Where additional hours are worked and agreed in advance, time off in lieu (TOIL) will be provided in accordance with organisational policy. For full details and how to apply, please see the job pack attached.

item.description: Finance Project Manager Salary: £61,212 1 year FTC, Full-time Hybrid working – 2 days in office Location: Central London A prestigious scientific institution with a global reputation for excellence is seeking a Finance Project Manager to join its finance team. This is a unique opportunity for a qualified accountant to lead high-impact finance projects and play a key role in enhancing financial processes, reporting, and risk management within an organisation dedicated to advancing knowledge, research and innovation for the benefit of society. About the Role Reporting to the Head of Finance Systems and Projects, the Finance Project Manager will lead on the delivery of finance projects that improve the efficiency, effectiveness and transparency of financial operations across the organisation. You will work closely with senior finance leadership to support strategic decision-making by developing enhanced reporting, strengthening financial controls, and delivering process and system improvements. The role also involves collaborating with stakeholders across the organisation to ensure finance initiatives are well understood and successfully embedded. You will oversee projects that span financial and non-financial reporting, fund accounting, and systems optimisation, while contributing to investment reporting, governance processes, and risk management frameworks. This position offers exposure to a wide range of finance activities within a complex and intellectually stimulating environment, where innovation, accuracy and continuous improvement are highly valued. Key Priorities: Lead the delivery of finance projects to improve processes, systems and reporting capabilities Enhance financial and non-financial reporting, including KPIs and impact measures Support fund accounting, restricted fund reporting and donor compliance requirements Contribute to investment reporting and governance, including liaison with external managers Drive process reviews and system improvements across finance and procurement functions Strengthen financial controls, policies and risk management frameworks Engage stakeholders to ensure successful delivery and adoption of finance initiatives Support preparation of papers for senior committees and governance forums About You We are seeking a CCAB-qualified accountant (or equivalent) with significant post-qualification experience and a strong background in financial reporting, project delivery, and continuous improvement within a complex organisation. You will bring : A proven track record in delivering finance projects, process improvements or transformation initiatives Strong technical accounting knowledge, including statutory reporting, audit and regulatory compliance Experience in risk management, internal controls or audit environments Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information to non-finance stakeholders A proactive and solution-focused approach to improving systems, processes and governance Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence at all levels The ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment Desirable experience includes exposure to legacy administration, Board-level reporting, or finance systems such as Xledger or Vena. This role would suit someone who thrives on delivering change, enjoys solving complex challenges, and is motivated by working in a collaborative, mission-driven environment that values integrity, innovation and excellence.
item.dc:creator: Allen Lane Interim & Permanent Recruitment

item.title: Community & Events Officer
item.description: Community and Events Fundraising Officer North London Hospice has been caring for local people since 1984, providing specialist palliative and end-of-life care to people with life-limiting illnesses across Barnet, Enfield and Haringey, and increasingly within Camden and Islington. Our services are completely free of charge however it now costs more than £16m a year to run our charity. We rely on the generosity of our community through donations and our shops to make up the shortfall in funding. Role Purpose Reporting to the Community and Events Manager, you will play a key role in growing income through community fundraising initiatives and delivering an exciting and expanding portfolio of events. This varied role combines creative promotion of fundraising opportunities, excellent supporter relationship management, and the planning and coordination of successful events. No two days will be the same, making this an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys a fast-paced and rewarding environment. Key Responsibilities Community Fundraising and Events · Support the Community and Events Manager to develop and deliver a portfolio of community fundraising activities and fundraising events. · Provide guidance and support to individuals, groups and organisations fundraising for the Hospice, helping them maximise income and deliver successful activities. · Coordinate event logistics, participant communications and administration to ensure a positive supporter experience. · Maintain accurate records of fundraising activity, event participants and supporter engagement on Raiser's Edge. · Contribute ideas to enhance and grow the Hospice's community fundraising and events programme. Marketing and Promotion · Work with the Community and Events Manager and Communications Team to promote fundraising activities and events. · Support the delivery of marketing plans and prepare briefs to assist with participant recruitment and supporter engagement. Supporter and Volunteer Stewardship · Deliver excellent stewardship to supporters and volunteers through a range of communication channels. · Recruit, coordinate and support volunteers involved in fundraising events and activities. · Build strong relationships with supporters, encouraging long-term engagement and identifying opportunities to maximise fundraising income. Product Development and Innovation · Contribute to the development of new fundraising products, events and initiatives. · Support innovation and continuous improvement across the Community and Events programme. General · Work collaboratively with colleagues across Fundraising, Communications, Retail and Volunteering teams to maximise fundraising opportunities. · Ensure fundraising activities comply with relevant legislation, Fundraising Regulator guidance and Hospice policies. · Support the wider Fundraising Team as required and contribute to a positive, flexible and collaborative team culture. · Maintain high standards of confidentiality, health and safety, and infection prevention and control at all times. Person Specification Experience and Knowledge · Experience building and managing relationships with supporters, customers or other external stakeholders. · Experience managing multiple priorities, projects and deadlines. · Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office. · Experience of using a CRM/database, events delivery, fundraising, or volunteer management would be advantageous. Personal Qualities and Skills · A great communicator with excellent relationship-building skills. · Strong organisational skills and attention to detail. · Able to work both independently and collaboratively. · Enthusiastic, proactive and able to remain calm under pressure. · Excellent written and verbal communication skills. · Knowledge of social media and marketing techniques would be beneficial. Essential for All · Commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. · Commitment to the values and objectives of North London Hospice. · Commitment to continuous professional development. · Enhanced DBS check (role specific). · Full UK driving licence (role specific). Why join us? By working at North London Hospice you will make a real difference to the lives of people affected by a life-limiting illness and their families. Our vision is to provide the best of life, at the end of life for everyone. This role is a unique opportunity to build a growing corporate partnerships programme with significant potential. You'll join a passionate, supportive fundraising team and play a key role in helping North London Hospice continue providing exceptional care and support to patients and their loved ones. We offer an attractive package of benefits, designed to support the health and wellbeing of everyone who works with us. In addition, we also offer comprehensive and unique learning development opportunities designed to give you the tools you need to succeed in your career at the hospice, whilst helping you to develop and achieve personal and professional growth. If you're looking for a role where you can combine strategic thinking, relationship building and commercial expertise to create meaningful impact, we'd love to hear from you. North London Hospice is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support you during the application or recruitment process, please get in touch

item.title: Surgical Lead - Gaza
item.description: Role: Surgical Lead Remuneration: Negotiable (dependant on experience) Hours: Full time, with some weekend and evening working required to support the humanitarian programme delivery. Duration: Up to 31st of December 2026 (funding pipeline dependent) with opportunity for extension. Deployment Pattern: Approximately 8 weeks in Gaza followed by 3 weeks out, supporting continuity of leadership while allowing appropriate rest and wellbeing periods. Some flexibility may be possible depending on operational requirements and individual circumstances. Location: Gaza (occupied Palestinian territory) – field-based with potential regional travel to Amman, Jordan. Candidates must be able to travel quickly through Jordan, securing visas on arrival with eligible documentation. If you do not meet this requirement, you can join our register of humanitarian and health professionals for other opportunities. Can you provide clinical and operational leadership to strengthen surgical services across UK-Med's humanitarian responses in Gaza? UK-Med is looking for an experienced Surgical Lead to support our ongoing health response in Gaza. This is a senior clinical leadership role combining hands-on surgical practice with significant service-management responsibilities and quality improvement. You will help ensure that surgical services are safe, effective and responsive to evolving patient needs, while working closely with national colleagues and UK-Med clinical leadership. The role will suit an experienced surgeon who is confident leading in complex environments, supporting multidisciplinary teams and helping strengthen surgical practice and services. A key part of the role will be working alongside national colleagues to support learning, strengthen practice and contribute to sustainable improvements in surgical care. We are looking for someone with strong clinical judgement and leadership capability, ideally with experience working in humanitarian, conflict-affected or resource-constrained healthcare settings. Experience in emergency, trauma, orthopaedic and/or conflict surgery would be advantageous, although the emphasis of this role is on surgical leadership and management rather than a particular surgical specialty. This is an opportunity to combine specialist surgical expertise with leadership and service development, supporting both immediate patient care and the continued strengthening of UK-Med’s surgical response in Gaza. If this sounds like the kind of challenge you are looking for, we would be very pleased to hear from you. We offer competitive benefits, a friendly working environment and the opportunity to make a real difference through humanitarian work. How to apply We strongly recommend that you read the Candidate Information Pack - Surgical Lead - Gaza - Sept 2026 before applying for this role. To apply, please submit a current CV and a supporting letter (no more than 2 pages) that includes a detailed explanation of your suitability for this post with specific reference to the essential criteria in the person specification. Applications must be submitted through our online jobs portal no later than Monday 12th of October 2026 . UK-Med is committed to safeguarding of our personnel and beneficiaries and has a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse. We conduct thorough vetting before any appointment is confirmed. UK-Med is committed to the principles of diversity, equality, and inclusion. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive environment where employees feel respected and supported to be able to fulfil their potential.

item.title: Macmillan Welfare Rights Caseworker
item.description: About Toynbee Hall Based in the East End of London since 1884, Toynbee Hall is a charity working alongside people facing poverty, injustice, and inequality to build a fairer East London. We provide vital advice and support, working in partnership to tackle unfairness and ensure everyone has an equal chance to thrive. Team background The Macmillan Money & More service brings together Toynbee Hall-employed advisers and partner organisations across London to deliver specialist welfare benefits advice for people affected by cancer. The service includes a central triage function, specialist welfare benefits advisers and partner organisations working together to ensure people receive the right support at the right time. The role includes regular outreach clinics at St Bartholomew's Hospital, The Royal London Hospital, Homerton University Hospital, Whipps Cross Hospital and Newham Hospital, working alongside Macmillan professionals and NHS multidisciplinary teams to provide accessible specialist advice. Key Responsibilities The postholder will: Manage a specialist caseload of people affected by cancer from referral through to case closure. Deliver face-to-face advice appointments at Toynbee Hall and outreach clinics within partner NHS hospitals. Provide specialist welfare benefits advice by telephone, video consultation and face-to-face appointments. Prepare Mandatory Reconsideration requests where benefit decisions appear incorrect. Prepare appeals to the First-tier Tribunal, including written submissions, evidence bundles and appeal documentation. Represent clients at First-tier Tribunal hearings where appropriate, advocating on their behalf and presenting complex welfare benefits cases. Liaise and negotiate with the DWP, HMRC, Local Authorities and other statutory agencies to resolve complex welfare benefit issues. Person Specification Essential Knowledge and experience Significant experience of delivering specialist welfare benefits advice and managing complex casework. Extensive knowledge of welfare benefits, particularly Universal Credit, disability benefits and benefits for people over State Pension age. Experience of preparing welfare benefit claims and maximising clients' income. Skills and abilities Excellent written and verbal advocacy skills. Ability to interpret and apply complex welfare benefits legislation. Ability to analyse evidence and prepare persuasive representations. Personal attributes Empathy, professionalism and resilience when supporting people affected by cancer. Commitment to continuous professional development and maintaining technical expertise Desirable Welfare Rights qualification or equivalent professional experience. Experience of preparing written submissions and supporting evidence for the First-tier Tribunal. Experience of working within NHS or hospital settings. Knowledge of Macmillan Cancer Support services. Experience of Advice Quality Standard (AQS) or equivalent. Additional requirements The postholder will be expected to work flexibly across Toynbee Hall, partner NHS sites and community venues as required by the service. Regular travel across London will be required. All duties must be carried out in accordance with Toynbee Hall's policies relating to safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion, health and safety, confidentiality and data protection. Our Benefits Package We believe in supporting our employees with a well-rounded benefits package designed to enhance work-life balance, financial security, and overall well-being. Annual Leave 25 days of annual leave, plus 3 additional days for our Christmas shutdown (on top of bank holidays). After 2 years: +3 extra days of leave. After 3 years: +1 additional day. After 5 years: A total of 30 days annual leave, plus the 3-day Christmas shutdown. Pension Standard Life Pension Scheme – Employer contribution: 4%, Employee contribution: 5% Additional Perks & Support Enhanced Sick Pay for peace of mind during illness Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave to support growing families Employee Eyecare Vouchers to support your vision health Employee Assistance Programme for free, confidential advice and support Mental Health First Aid to ensure workplace well-being Tenancy Deposit Scheme to help secure your home Interest-Free Season Ticket Loan for cost-effective commuting Cycle to Work Scheme to promote a healthier, greener way to travel Charity Mentoring Network to support professional development and networking Westfield Healthcare Cash Plan Perk Box Further information Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. Please refer to the attached job description for more details

item.title: Evaluation Manager
item.description: Use your evaluation skills and research experience to help high-impact organisations working with children and young people learn, strengthen their practice and deliver better outcomes. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who is passionate about evidence-informed practice and motivated to support organisations that help young people thrive. You will join a small mixed-methods evaluation team within Purposeful Ventures, working closely with colleagues and our partner organisations — inspirational charities and social enterprises we partner with and fund — to support their growth and contribution to systemic change. Much of your work will involve supporting colleagues and portfolio organisations at the early stages of programme development, helping them apply evaluation and research approaches in a practical and accessible way. You will help them develop useful theories of change, make sense of evidence and build proportionate approaches to learning and evaluation. Working across the organisation, with an immediate focus likely to be in the maths portfolio, you will work across the full funding lifecycle – from portfolio strategy setting to due diligence through to capacity building, providing hands-on evaluation expertise to organisations and incubations. You will also contribute to developing our understanding of Purposeful Ventures’ organisational impact and how we communicate it. You will bring a strong grounding in social research and evaluation, with particular experience in relevant quantitative research design and analysis. You will also be comfortable undertaking small-scale qualitative research or be excited to develop your skills in this area with support from colleagues. You will be excited by using evidence as a tool for learning and improvement. Experience of working with charities, social enterprises or similar mission-driven organisations would be valuable, as would experience of research or evaluation relating to education initiatives, particularly maths attainment or the teaching workforce. Above all, you will be motivated by helping organisations learn, improve and maximise their impact, using evidence to shape better decisions and better outcomes for children and young people. Please download the full job description on the Purposeful Ventures website Job Description Responsibilities and duties Support development and implementation of evidence-informed portfolio strategies, aligned to organisational goals: Work with evaluation and portfolio colleagues to support the development and review of evidence-informed portfolio strategies, ensuring aims, assumptions, intended outcomes and learning priorities are clear and aligned with Purposeful Ventures’ organisational goals. Assist with the development and review of practical theories of change, monitoring and outcomes frameworks, selection criteria, data sources and learning processes for allocated portfolios, projects and programmes. Contribute to ensuring monitoring, evaluation and learning approaches are proportionate to the scale, maturity, priority, nature and resourcing of the work. Develop evaluation recommendations, tools, templates and written outputs, with appropriate support and quality assurance, that help colleagues make decisions, support partner organisations and track progress. Contribute to Purposeful Ventures’ organisational impact and internal monitoring work where relevant, helping connect organisational goals, portfolio learning and impact reporting. Contribute evaluation expertise to organisation selection and due diligence, assessment and onboarding: Contribute to the assessment and selection of prospective portfolio organisations, programmes and incubations, using agreed criteria and evaluation judgement to assess programme design, theory of change, evidence, monitoring arrangements, evaluation readiness, opportunities and risks. Support the design of proportionate monitoring, evaluation and learning expectations for portfolio organisations, programmes or incubations, within the agreed portfolio approach and aligned with portfolio aims and organisational goals. Provide tailored monitoring, evaluation and learning support to portfolio organisations and incubations: Contribute to the design and delivery of structured monitoring, evaluation and learning support and advice for selected partner organisations and incubations with more substantial evaluation needs. Support organisations to develop and strengthen theories of change, monitoring frameworks, outcome indicators and data collection tools, including survey-based and routine monitoring data, and use quantitative analysis to generate actionable learning and evidence, with guidance and support from more senior evaluation colleagues. Support organisations to plan out their evaluation and evidence building journey and next steps in a way that is proportionate to their stage and capacity. Help organisations improve data quality, timely reporting and learning through practical tools, guidance, templates and proportionate quality assurance. Provide advice and support to organisations to use findings to improve programme design, delivery, learning and communication of impact. Where appropriate, support portfolio organisations and incubations to commission, manage and use external evaluation or specialist research expertise. Manage allocated evaluation projects, discrete parts of projects or workstreams, with senior support: Manage agreed evaluation projects and workstreams, with support and quality assurance from senior evaluation colleagues. Work with colleagues to scope evaluation questions, methods, data requirements, timelines, risks, budgets, outputs and audiences for allocated projects. Develop and review research or evaluation approaches, identifying and advising on improvements, clarifications, feasibility issues, limitations and implications for interpretation, in consultation with evaluation colleagues. Design and conduct data collection, analysis and reporting for in-house research and evaluation projects. Co-ordinate day to day delivery of designated projects to ensure delivery of high quality and timely reports which effectively communicate findings to relevant audiences (e.g. practitioners, academics, policymakers and the general public). The job description is subject to change and the postholder may be required to undertake tasks not specifically referred to above. Such duties, however, will fall within the scope of the job description. Who we are looking for Key requirements Essential Commitment to Purposeful Ventures’ mission and values, with a passion for transforming the life chances of children and young people through entrepreneurship and innovation in education and related fields. Demonstrable track record of taking ownership of commitments and working hard to succeed. Sound knowledge and experience of applied social research, monitoring, evaluation and learning, with deeper expertise in quantitative research design and analysis, alongside broader knowledge of qualitative approaches. This should include experience developing or reviewing theories of change, monitoring plans, outcome indicators, surveys and other data collection tools; designing proportionate process and impact evaluations; analysing monitoring and survey data; and producing clear reports or learning outputs. Experience designing or contributing to proportionate monitoring and evaluation approaches for programmes, projects or organisations at different stages of development. Experience and proven success in relevant evaluation roles in/or with the not-for-profit and/or social enterprise sectors. Experience working with stakeholders to understand programme theory, evidence needs and learning priorities, and contributing to evaluation activity that informs programme and/or policy development, delivery or learning. Right to work in the UK. Desirable Experience working with funders, philanthropists, practice and policy audiences. Experience contributing to published research, reports or learning outputs. Experience commissioning and managing research or evaluation projects. Experience of research or evaluation relating to improving maths attainment, including via teaching-workforce initiatives. Skills The successful candidate will demonstrate: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex information clearly. Strong interpersonal and influencing skills with the ability to gain credibility with internal and external stakeholders, including colleagues, portfolio organisations, charity executives and research or evaluation partners. Strong project management skills with the ability to work across multiple, varied projects, coordinate contributors, manage timelines and support delivery of agreed outcomes. A proactive approach with the ability to work independently, solve problems and seek input where needed. Flexibility and strong organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise work to meet deadlines. Being comfortable working with a degree of ambiguity, creating processes and ways forwards where they might not yet exist and able to respond to changing priorities as Purposeful continues to develop.
item.dc:creator: Purposeful Ventures

item.title: Fundraising and Partnerships Lead
item.description: Avon Needs Trees (ANT) is a charity creating new, permanent woodland throughout the Bristol-Avon catchment to tackle the climate and ecological emergencies. We raise funds to buy land and create woodlands that will stand for generations, locking up carbon, supporting biodiversity, providing natural flood management and creating accessible green space where appropriate. Since our formation in 2019, we have grown from a small group of volunteers into an organisation with over 1,000 volunteers and almost 600 acres of land. We have planted and cared for tens of thousands of native trees across Wiltshire and the Bristol-Avon catchment, including Great Avon Wood and our 420-acre Lower Chew Forest project. We are ambitious about the scale of change we can achieve, while being thoughtful and reasoned in how we work. We are positive about the future and the opportunities to tackle the climate and nature emergencies. Fundraising & Partnerships Lead Reporting to: Head of Fundraising / Director of Income Hours: 0.8 FTE to full time (35 hours per week) Contract: Fixed-term to 31 March 2028, with potential to extend Salary: £33,280 per annum, pro rata as relevant Location: Hybrid working between home, our office at Lower Chew Forest near Compton Dando, and sites across our catchment area. About the role We are looking for an experienced and relationship-focused fundraiser to help grow ANT's income and develop lasting partnerships that support our mission. You will play a key role in delivering our fundraising strategy, with a particular focus on corporate partnerships, major donor development and individual giving . You will identify and develop new fundraising opportunities, manage and grow relationships with existing supporters and partners, and help deliver campaigns and excellent stewardship. The role will give you the opportunity to shape and develop our approach to fundraising as ANT continues to grow. What you'll be doing Corporate partnerships Develop new corporate opportunities, generate leads and manage the partnership pipeline. Build strong relationships with people at all levels, from senior decision-makers to employees. Develop and manage engaging partnership and employee engagement opportunities. Coordinate volunteering and tree planting activities with corporate partners and ANT's project teams. Report on partnership impact and support partners to communicate their involvement. Explore opportunities in biodiversity net gain and natural capital markets. Major donor philanthropy Help develop ANT's major donor programme and build relationships with prospective and existing supporters. Coordinate the major donor pipeline and support colleagues across the organisation with donor relationships. Develop engaging communications, reporting and stewardship for major donors. Individual giving Work with colleagues to deliver individual giving campaigns, including crowdfunders. Help develop and test new approaches to individual giving. Review and improve donor stewardship journeys to provide an excellent supporter experience. You will work closely with the Head of Fundraising and colleagues across the Income, Communications and Engagement teams, as well as working collaboratively across the wider organisation. About you We are looking for someone who can demonstrate: Experience developing new business opportunities, generating leads and managing a pipeline. Strong relationship-building and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work with people at different levels of seniority. Experience managing and developing relationships with external partners, clients, donors or stakeholders. Strong organisational and project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities. Experience using data to monitor progress, evaluate activity and produce clear reports and presentations. The ability to work proactively and independently and take responsibility for delivering outcomes. A willingness to learn, reflect and improve your approach. Experience developing or coordinating communications that engage and influence external audiences. A commitment to addressing the climate and nature emergencies and to woodland creation. Experience with financial management, digital communications, CRM systems and fundraising-related digital channels would be desirable, as would a driving licence and access to a vehicle. You do not need to have experience in every area of the role. We recognise that people bring different strengths and transferable skills, and we would encourage you to apply if you meet the core requirements and are excited about the opportunity.
item.dc:creator: Avon Needs Trees

item.title: Open Education AI Operations Manager
item.description: Build the operational backbone of a start-up having a meaningful and tangible impact on how schools can use data and AI safely and effectively. Open Education AI (OEAI) is a growing, sector-led organisation that is currently incubated by Purposeful Ventures as it develops its independent operating model. We are looking for an Operations Manager to join OEAI at this exciting stage in its development. As OEAI builds its independent operational capacity for the first time, this role will play a central part in creating the systems, processes and ways of working that will enable the organisation to grow and maximise its impact. This is a genuinely broad, hands-on role: one day you might be redesigning how contracts and supplier relationships are managed, the next you'll be preparing papers for our Steering Committee We are looking for someone who thrives in start-up mode: proactive, dynamic and comfortable working through ambiguity to find solutions and forge the path themselves. You will bring experience of operations: defining processes from scratch, getting the right systems in place for a growing team, and thinking creatively about how tools and workflows can accelerate the pace and quality of our work. This role suits someone who is organised, resourceful and calm under pressure, with a natural instinct for spotting what a growing organisation needs next. You will have a track record of taking ownership of operational or administrative functions and making them noticeably better, tightening up governance, improving financial processes, or building infrastructure that didn't exist before. You are someone who is looking to grow into a bigger role as the organisation scales, and who is motivated by the chance to make a tangible difference in education. Ultimately, we are looking for someone who wants to roll up their sleeves, get stuck in, and be a part of shaping this sector leading data governance and AI organisation. In return, you will get real ownership from day one: the opportunity to build OEAI's operational foundations largely from scratch, with visible impact on an organisation leading pioneering work in the ethical use of data and AI within the education sector. As part of the Purposeful Ventures family, you will enjoy the autonomy and ownership of a start-up role alongside access to a network of experienced colleagues, proven ways of working and a strong culture of learning and development. About Open Education AI Open Education AI (OEAI) is a sector-led membership organisation that provides school groups with a governed, open-source data infrastructure and a thriving sector community enabling all schools to use data intelligence and analytics to improve educational outcomes and opportunities. Founded in 2023 and formalised as a non-profit in January 2026, OEAI is now incubated by Purposeful Ventures and is building its independent operational capacity for the first time as it prepares to exit to become an independent charity. Therefore, this role will initially be employed by Purposeful Ventures as OEAI prepares for spin-out. With over 60 school groups representing 1000+ schools already in membership this is a pivotal moment to join a small, high-impact organisation at the start of its journey. Please download the full job description on the Purposeful Ventures website Job Description Purpose This role is central in the effective running and growth of OEAI by building and continuously improving the operational systems, governance, administration and processes that enable the organisation to deliver against its mission with efficiency, accountability and impact. This is a broad and varied role, spanning operational management, governance, finance, communications and organisational effectiveness, requiring a proactive and adaptable approach as we grow. Responsibilities and duties Operational systems and infrastructure Manage OEAI’s systems, platforms and services overseeing procurement, contracts and subscriptions; user and access management, security and governance to ensure our operational infrastructure meets our growing needs. Be the team point of contact and relationship holder for any systems and processes we share with Purposeful Ventures as part of our incubation relationship. Support the roll-out of any OEAI specific new systems, ensuring team-readiness and organising and delivering training where required. Manage contracts and compliance, working with OEAI's legal advisers where required. Financial management Support the OEAI Incubation Lead with annual budget planning, reforecasting and budget management and liaising with the Purposeful finance team as appropriate. Prepare financial reports from the Purposeful managed finance systems for the OEAI Lead and Steering Committee, ensuring timely and accurate information is available for decision-making. Review card purchases and supplier contracts to ensure invoices are accurate and processed in good time and against the budget. Governance and legal Maintain a forward governance calendar and ensure the Chair of each of the respective governance groups are well prepared for all board and governance meetings. Support the OEAI Lead with Purposeful board reporting requirements. Coordinate the logistics and papers and associated governance documentation for the Steering Committee, Technical Advisory Group and the Sector Advisory Group. Maintain a well-organised, version-controlled archive of governance documentation, ensuring papers, policies and records are accurately filed and easy to retrieve. Maintain organisational records, Companies House filings and Charity Commission obligations when and where appropriate for spin out. Communications Manage OEAI’s LinkedIn presence, building an engaged following in the sector’s data community. Manage the OEAI Circle community and platform, including enrolment and content. Maintain and update the OEAI website, ensuring content is current and well written. Help develop and maintain a bank of community case studies demonstrating OEAI impact. Support with fundraising proposals when appropriate. Be the initial point of contact for press or media enquiries, coordinating with the wider OEAI team and PV communications team on responses. Events and Webinars Manage OEAI’s presence at sector conferences including Confederation of School Trusts, BETT and others. Work with the wider OEAI team to plan an annual OEAI programme of events. Own end-to-end event logistics for our events (hackathons)from venue sourcing and speaker liaison to registration and follow-up. Manage all tools underpinning OEAI communications: CRM, Zoom, Circle community platform ensuring they meet team requirements and business need. Team and organisational effectiveness Act as the central operational hub for the team. The person who makes things work smoothly behind the scenes. Identify and resolve operational inefficiencies, building better systems proactively. Support the OEAI Lead with recruitment processes where appropriate (inc. freelancers). As the team scales, willingness to take on line management responsibilities or oversight of shared Purposeful Ventures resource as required. On occasion, step in to tasks beyond those outlined in this job description, as required, reflecting the fast changing work of the organisation. The job description is subject to change and the postholder may be required to undertake tasks not specifically referred to above. Who we are looking for Key requirements Passionate about creating a fairer society where all young people thrive. Demonstrable track record of taking ownership of commitments and working hard to succeed. Well-organised and able to prioritise effectively, managing multiple, competing workstreams while keeping governance, finance and communications moving in parallel. Strong written communication skills are essential with the ability to write clearly for different audiences. Comfortable working within a start-up environment and being proactive in problem resolution. Right to work in the UK. Knowledge Essential Understanding of the operational and governance needs of a growing or start-up organisation, including designing processes and implementing systems and board reporting. Working knowledge of data protection and information governance requirements (e.g. GDPR) as they apply to contracts, systems and member data. Desirable Strong working knowledge of the charity or not-for-profit sector, ideally within education, AI or EdTech. Awareness of the communications and events landscape within the education or membership sector, including relevant channels, conferences and stakeholder groups. Financial acumen — comfortable with budgeting, invoicing and financial reporting processes. Experience Essential Demonstrable experience in an operations, business administration or office management role within a fast-moving or growing organisation. Demonstrable experience of having improved or built operational systems/processes. Experience of leveraging technology in creating and/or improving operational systems. Demonstrable experience supporting governance processes, such as coordinating board or committee meetings, papers and reporting cycles. Desirable Demonstrable track record of managing supplier and contract relationships, including invoicing, financial reporting and budget support. Demonstrable experience in communications, or member/community engagement, ideally across multiple channels. Demonstrable track record of planning and delivering events, webinars or conferences end-to-end.

item.title: Youth Voice Officer (Maternity Cover)
item.description: The Youth Endowment Fund Youth Voice Officer (Maternity Cover) Reports to: Youth Understanding Manager Salary: £34,200 Location: Central London or Hybrid Contract: 12-months fixed term – Maternity Cover Closing date: 5pm, Wednesday, 7th October 2026 Interview dates: week commencing 19th October 2026. DBS requirement: Enhanced + Children’s Barred List About the Youth Endowment Fund All of us will experience violence at some point in our lives. For many children, it is a daily reality. Each year, tens of children are killed, hundreds are hospitalised, 1 in 5 teenage children are victims and the majority admit to feeling afraid of violence. It scares them when they travel home from school, prevents them from going out and makes the most vulnerable feel like they don’t matter. It is taking lives, traumatising families and dividing communities. It robs potential, progress and hope. But it doesn’t have to be this way. The Youth Endowment Fund believes that no child should be affected by violence. We research violence to understand it; we find, fund and test what works to prevent it; and we are building a movement to end it. It's critical to our mission that we understand how and why young people become involved in violence. The YEF’s work combines conducting rigorous evaluations and research studies with hearing directly from young people – their individual stories and perspectives. It is also important to us that young people are central to the messages we share externally. As a part of the Youth Understanding team, you will play a vital role in supporting young people to use their experiences and voices to shape, support, and amplify YEF’s work through the YEF’sYouth Advisory Board (YAB) DBS check This role requires an Enhanced with Children’s Barred List DBS check because the role involves regular direct work with children and young people in both online and in person. Having a criminal record does not automatically prevent you from working at YEF. Any information disclosed will be considered fairly and in relation to the requirements of the role. Key Responsibilities You will: Co-lead an accessible, safe and effective Youth Advisory Board: Planning,leadingand reviewingengaging activities for young people, includingmeetings and events. Most activities take place online, with some evening work, usually 1–2 evenings per week. We plan this carefully: meetings will finish no later than 7.30pm, and you’ll have later starts on the previous or following day to recognise the additional working time. There may also be occasional weekend and in-person activities, with time off in lieu provided for any weekend work. Build and develop trusting relationships with YABmembers providingsupport and pastoral care to members, including personal development planning and safeguarding. Help recruitand inductYAB members (young people aged 16 –25) through interviews and managing recruitment. Monitor attendance and engagement of YAB membersand coordinate YAB attendance at external events. Champion and facilitate lived experience involvementacross YEF’s work Working closely with YEF colleagues to provide engaging opportunities for YAB members,includingleading lived experience focused working groups and supporting young people to play a central role in YEFs emerging priorities. Create safeand trauma informedspaces where young peoplefeel confident and supported tocommunicate their voices ensuring these are heard and feedback on how they have influenced is communicated. Build positive relationships where required with external providerssuch as secure settings to ensure young people within these can also inform and influence our work. Support engagement and preparation of YAB involvementfor external events and conferences. About You You are this sort of person: You believe in young people:You have worked with young people and know thehuge potentialyoung people have tobring change.You have experience and knowledge of adhering to safeguarding processes, and are able to be flexible to suit young people’s needs- understandingwhen plans need to change at short notice. You’re passionate about helping young people to be heard: You have experience in supporting young people to share their stories and experiences in safe, strength-based ways. You can do this in groups and on an individual basis, and understand the care and support this needs. You’reable to juggle many diverse tasks at once: You enjoy moving betweendifferent typesof projects, whether that be leading YAB sessions, supporting the development of young peopleone-to-oneor creating exciting content with young people. You prefer a job that looks different every day. Youdon’tget overwhelmed by a long to-do list andcaneffectivelyidentifywhat’s most important and how to balance different priorities. You love collaborating and supporting:You understand that young people’s voices fit centrally in the mission of YEF. You’ll know how to work with others to find the right spaces and best methods of involving young people that both support YEF’s work and the young person. While it’s not a criterion, we’re especially interested to hear from applicants who have lived experience of youth violence. It’s also important to us that the people we hire do not discriminate. We believe in being inclusive and giving everyone an equal chance to succeed. Applications are welcome from all backgrounds regardless of age, sex, gender identity, disability, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, religion or belief, race, sexual orientation, transgender status or social economic background. Hybrid Working Details Our office is in Central London, and we work in a hybrid way that combines time together in the office with remote working. This role requires the team member to be based in London and to work from the office at least 2 days a week. As part of our commitment to flexible working we will consider a range of options for the successful applicant. All options can be discussed at the interview stage. To Apply To apply, please send a CV and cover letter, and complete the monitoring form click on "Apply for this" buttonby 5pm 7th October 2026. When applying for this role, please ensure that your cover letter can answer, within a maximum of 1000 words, the following questions: Your experience in supporting young people, including those affected by violence, to share their experience and insights How you feel young people can contribute to YEF’s mission Interview Process This will be a 2-stage interview process. The first stage interview will take place on the week commencing 19th October 2026. The second stage interviews are currently scheduled for the week commencing 26th October 2026. PLEASE NOTE: We do not sponsor work permits and you will be required to provide proof of your eligibility to work in the UK. Benefits Include • £1,000 professional development budget annually • 28 days holiday plus Bank Holidays • Employee Assistance Programme – 24hr phone line for free confidential support • Volunteering days - 4 half days per year • Death in service - 4 times annual salary • Flexible hours. Core office hours 10am – 4pm • Financial support including travel and hardship loans • Employer contributed pension of 5% Personal Data Your personal data will be shared for the purposes of the recruitment exercise. This includes our HR team, interviewers (who may include other partners in the project and independent advisors), relevant team managers and our IT service provider if access to the data is necessary for performance of their roles. We do not share your data with other third parties, unless your application for employment is successful and we make you an offer of employment. We will then share your data with former employers to obtain references for you. We do not transfer your data outside the European Economic Area.

item.title: Programme Manager
item.description: Frazzled is a small mental health and wellbeing charity founded by Ruby Wax OBE, based on the power of emotional openness. Our free, volunteer-led meetings run online every single day of the year, alongside face-to-face groups, offering people a chance to share, listen and feel heard in a supportive community. We're looking for a confident, positive self-starter with a high level of emotional intelligence, excellent communication skills and experience supporting volunteers to be our new Programmes Manager. Working closely with the CEO, you will lead day-to-day delivery of our existing programme, support our facilitators and help them develop their practice, addressing concerns thoughtfully and promptly. You will line-manage the Programme Support and Admin Officer, who handles scheduling and practical administration. You will lead on facilitator wellbeing, training and performance, and work with the Head of Fundraising on programme proposals and reporting. Working pattern Our meetings run seven days a week. We welcome flexible arrangements, including school hours. Some evening and occasional weekend work is required for observations and facilitator support, alongside travel to face-to-face meetings. All activity forms part of contracted hours, with cover agreed with the CEO. Key responsibilities Core programme Oversee safe, consistent online and face-to-face delivery in line with the Frazzled model. Resolve cover gaps and operational concerns, escalating significant risks or resource decisions to the CEO. Ensure clear delivery and support arrangements for Ruby Wax public meetings and agreed special sessions. Volunteer support and development Build supportive relationships with facilitators, offering encouragement and help with challenging situations while maintaining clear expectations and boundaries. Lead volunteer recruitment when required, oversee induction and training, and lead monthly volunteer meetings and shared learning. Carry out observations, give constructive feedback and coaching, and follow up development actions. Explore peer observations and provide refresher sessions. Address complaints and performance concerns fairly, and respond to safeguarding and wellbeing issues through Frazzled's procedures. People management Set priorities and provide support and feedback to the Admin Officer, helping them develop independence and maintain clear handovers. Coordinate their fundraising support and supervise agreed observation work. Programme development and reporting Work with the Head of Fundraising on proposals, providing realistic delivery plans, costs and capacity needs. Review attendance and feedback, lead survey design and evaluation, and provide checked evidence for applications, funder reports, trustee papers and the Annual Report. Maintain partner relationships and programme guidance, improve processes and support agreed projects. About you and applying You will bring experience coordinating services, developing volunteers or staff, facilitating groups and delivering or coordinating training. You should be organised and confident supervising colleagues, having sensitive conversations, interpreting data and using Zoom, Google Workspace and spreadsheets. Please read the attached job description and include your earliest available start date in your application. We ask that you write your application without AI assistance. This role involves substantial written and verbal communication with stakeholders, and we want to hear your own voice and examples.

item.title: Supporter Experience Manager
item.description: Supporter Experience Manager Are you looking for a role within an organisation where the work you do makes a real difference to children's? If the answer it's yes, our Supporter Experience Manager role could be exactly what you're looking for. Join the Engagement and Fundraising directorate to make the difference At the NSPCC, we believe every childhood is worth fighting for. With over 100 years of experience, and the collective strength of our staff, volunteers, supporters, and partners, we're working to end child abuse and neglect for good. Over 90 percent of the NSPCC's income comes from voluntary donations, so we reply on the incredible generosity and commitment of all our supporters, large and small. You'll work as part of one of many teams across the UK, which focus on engaging our supporters and ensuring they continue to give their support. You will do this by leading fundraising initiatives or simply sharing our mission with those around you, every conversation and connection can spark change. We encourage everyone across the organisation to get involved, feel confident in championing our cause, and help us grow the support we need to protect children and give them the futures they deserve If you're motivated by purpose, thrive in a supportive team, and want to contribute to creating a safer, brighter world for every child, why not join us as Supporter Experience Manager? What is the purpose of the Supporter Experience Manager? This role plays a key part in supporting the NSPCC's mission. You'll contribute by: Shaping and delivering audience-led supporter experience across public audiences, ensuring every touchpoint reflects the NSPCC's values and deepens supporter relationships Embeding supporter experience thinking and strategy within Engagement Delivery squads. Using data and insight to track and develop key supporter experience metrics, including satisfaction, loyalty and lifetime value to inform continuous improvement. Collaborating across teams to ensure supporter needs are considered in the planning, delivery, and evaluation of public engagement activity. Championing a culture of supporter-centricity, acting as a voice of the supporter and advocating for their experience across the organisation. What skills do I need to be Supporter Experience Manager? Significant experience in customer/supporter experience practices, tools and approaches, including experience driving customer/supporter loyalty and retention Proven experience designing, implementing and optimising supporter journeys and experiences, using insight to improve engagement and loyalty. Excellent analytical skills, with experience interpreting complex data, insight and performance information to inform decision making and drive continuous improvement. An understanding of emerging trends, technologies and innovations in supporter experience, customer engagement, CRM and insight practices. Why join the NSPCC? Any one of our people will tell you that a huge reward in itself is making a difference to children's lives. But we know it's a competitive world, and it's important to feel valued in your role and receive more practical, tangible benefits. We offer salaries that are at least comparable with the top charities in the UK, as well as these benefits. Generous annual leave - 29 days per annum plus bank holidays for full-time employees (pro-rata for part-time). 32 days per annum after five years' continuous service. Employee discounts - Our discounts portal gives you online access to over 3,000 discounts and offers. The Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) - an independent, free, personal support service. It can provide information, support and advice to support your health and wellbeing. Pension - building up a good pension is something we want to help you achieve with our flexible, tax-efficient pension schemes. Life assurance scheme - All employees will be given life assurance of one times their salary, unless they join the NSPCC Group Personal Pension Scheme, where members are given life assurance of five times their salary. Join us and make a difference. You'll grow, be challenged, and help change millions of young lives for the better. Ready to apply? If this is the role for you, please click the button ‘apply' to start your journey. You can find more information on all recruitment stages on the Career page. If you are interested in applying for this role, we encourage you to apply early. To help us manage the process we may close the vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive a strong response to the role. In keeping with our values and our policies, if any individuals who are regrettably at risk of redundancy apply for a role and meet the minimum essential criteria they will be given priority consideration. We hope that you understand our position on this and that this will not discourage from applying. We cannot predict who, internally, will apply for a role, or whether they will meet the minimum essential criteria. Where no at-risk candidates meet the minimum essential criteria, all applications will be considered as normal.
