item.title: Cafe Coordinator
item.description: Location: Coed y Ddraig, Mold, Flintshire Hours: 30 hours per week, part-time Working pattern: Initially Tuesday–Friday, 9am–3.30pm, with flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends in line with service needs Our vision is to create a future where learning disabled people can live the best life possible. We will do this by coming together to campaign for positive change, provide personalised support and create solutions for living independently. Job Purpose At Coed y Ddraig, we’re creating opportunities for people to learn, develop skills, build confidence and play an active role in their local community. We’re looking for a Café Co-ordinator to join our team in Mold and help bring our community café to life. This is a varied role that combines hospitality, horticulture, vocational learning and person-centred support. You’ll help people with learning disabilities and/or autism develop practical skills and confidence in a real working environment, while also playing a hands-on role in running our café. Responsible for Key Accountabilities Run the café day-to-day, providing a welcoming, inclusive and high-quality experience for customers. Prepare and serve drinks, light meals and refreshments, including barista-style beverages, and manage tills, stock and café displays. Support opening and closing procedures and maintain high standards of food hygiene, cleanliness, allergen management and health & safety. Support people to develop catering, hospitality, customer service and transferable workplace skills through meaningful, hands-on experience. Create learning and development opportunities that build confidence, independence and practical skills, based on individual goals and aspirations. Support the field-to-fork approach by helping people harvest and prepare produce grown on site and take part in sustainable horticultural activities. Work with supported employment teams, families and community partners to create pathways into volunteering, training and paid employment. Build positive relationships with customers and the wider community, support events and enterprise activities, and ensure any risks, incidents or safeguarding concerns are appropriately reported. People To support and empower people to achieve their goals and ambitions in line with their Vocational Profiles. Work closely with colleagues including the Employability Coach to offer outcome based support. Other Adhere to and maintain Hft’s Health and Safety policies, standards and guidelines at all times Carry out a range of duties and undertake any other duties as specified from time to time in accordance with Hft business requirements It is the nature of the work that task responsibilities are in many circumstances unpredictable and varied. All employees are therefore expected to work in a flexible way when the occasion arises in order that tasks which are not specifically covered in their job description are covered Professional & Technical Expertise Basic food hygiene qualification and equivalent vocational qualification

item.title: Head of Philanthropy (Trusts & Foundations)
item.description: About Us Philanthropy & Alumni Engagement (P&A) raises philanthropic funds in support of King’s College London and engages with the university’s worldwide alumni community. We are proud to enable the work of colleagues across the university and its health partners, helping them serve society through world-leading education, research and healthcare.Our activity includes a partnership with the Maudsley Charity in support of children’s mental health and initiatives between the university’s Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience and the South London & Maudsley NHS Trust. We are entering an exciting period as a team. Our work is identified as a key enabler of the new King’s Strategy 2030, with associated ambitions that include preparing for our next major philanthropic and engagement campaign. This will accelerate and energise our work in support of the University’s mission to be ‘in service to society through academic excellence’ – be that through exceptional, impact-led research; ensuring our students are supported to thrive during their time at King’s and beyond; or by helping the university to invest over the long-term into its people, ideas and infrastructure. We plan to deepen and scale engagement with our global alumni community, donors and other supporters, mobilising them behind these shared priorities. We are strongly values-driven with a focus on sustaining a strong and supportive culture, which we see as key to creating a successful team that can realise these ambitions. More on King’s College London For almost 200 years, King’s has been a place where ideas turn into action. From revealing the structure of DNA to reimagining nursing, from advances in medicine, law and the study of war and peace to shaping culture and public debate, our work has always been guided by a belief that knowledge should serve society. Over our history, King’s has been home to 14 Nobel Prize winners, and to scholars whose ideas and leadership have shaped thinking, policy and practice around the world. King’s has always been a place where knowledge is put to work for the benefit of others. King’s College London is a world-renowned university that delivers exceptional education and world-leading research. We're committed to creating positive and sustainable change in our local and global communities through outstanding education, impactful research, and genuine service to society. King’s Strategy 2030 sets out how we take that purpose forward, with four key priorities including student success in and beyond university, investment in research and education excellence that responds to the changing world, fostering innovation and entrepreneurship, and delivering sustainable finances for a secure future. More information on King’s, its purpose and strategy can be found online. About The Role King’s has an ambition to significantly scale philanthropic income as we prepare to launch our next major fundraising and engagement campaign in 2027 and mark the university’s bicentenary in 2029. Trusts and Foundations play a vital role in supporting the university’s strategic priorities, funding world-leading research, innovative education, student support, and initiatives that deliver meaningful impact locally, nationally, and globally. The Head of Philanthropy (Trusts & Foundations) is a new role and will lead the university’s Trusts & Foundations fundraising programme, providing strategic leadership to a high-performing team responsible for securing significant philanthropic support from charitable trusts, foundations, and grant-making organisations. The postholder will utilise their substantial fundraising experience, strategic outlook, and exceptional relationship management skills to grow income from this important source of support. This role will provide an exciting opportunity to help shape the Trusts & Foundations team at King’s, operating within a new Cross-University remit. Working closely with the Associate Director, Cross-University Philanthropy, the postholder will play a pivotal role in developing and expanding the Trusts & Foundations fundraising function in advance of the university’s next public fundraising campaign. They will be responsible for leading and nurturing a team of fundraisers to secure gifts and grants at the £100,000 level and above, while developing strategies to secure transformational six- and seven-figure donations. The postholder will also help support the Associate Director in helping shape a wider Cross-University philanthropy team culture. The successful candidate will have a proven track record of developing high-value funding relationships and securing substantial philanthropic grants. They will have demonstrated experience of building and scaling fundraising portfolios, identified strategic funding opportunities, and worked collaboratively across a complex organisation. They should be intellectually curious and energised by the breadth and depth of King’s academic expertise, and motivated by working with senior university leaders, academics, researchers, and professional services colleagues to secure support across a diverse range of institutional priorities. In Philanthropy & Alumni Engagement we are committed to building a truly diverse workforce that reflects the communities served by our partners, recognising the range of benefits that we derive when colleagues bring experiences and perspectives from a range of backgrounds. As part of this work, we have developed a race equality plan and we particularly welcome applications from candidates from Black, Minority Ethnic and Asian backgrounds. This is a full-time post, and you will be offered an indefinite contract. P&A has a hybrid working approach, with a minimum of 40% of time in the office. Typically, this equates to two days per week, but we’re very happy for colleagues to be in more frequently if they so wish. Closing date: 29 September 2026. To apply, please click “Apply Now”.
item.dc:creator: Kings College London

item.title: Head of Policy and Research
item.description: Head of Policy and Research When registering to this job board you will be redirected to the online application form. Please ensure that this is completed in full in order that your application can be reviewed. Head of Research and Policy Maternity cover for approximately 12 months (duration dependent on start date). Salary: £56,574.00 per annum Location: Hybrid – London Contract: Fixed Term Band: E ActionAid UK is a member of the ActionAid Federation, an international charity working with women and girls living in poverty. We work alongside partners and dedicated staff around the world to end violence and fight poverty so that all women, everywhere, can create the future they want. Are you an experienced leader with a passion for feminist research, policy and influencing? Do you have the skills to bring together a multidisciplinary team, strengthen strategic partnerships and drive meaningful change for women and girls? Then we'd love to hear from you! About the Role We are looking for an experienced and collaborative Head of Research and Policy to join ActionAid UK on a maternity cover basis. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Advocacy and Influencing, you will provide strategic leadership to our newly combined Research and Policy team, bringing together expertise across feminist research, women, peace and security, feminist humanitarian action, climate justice, women's economic justice, and women's and girls' protection and leadership. You will play a key role in establishing a shared vision and priorities for the team, supporting colleagues to bring together their specialist expertise and deliver impactful research, policy and influencing work. Working across ActionAid UK and the wider Federation, you will strengthen collaboration, develop strategic partnerships and ensure our work is grounded in the priorities and leadership of women's rights organisations and feminist movements. As a senior leader within the Advocacy and Influencing department, you will contribute to wider organisational priorities, support the development of funding and influencing opportunities, and create an inclusive environment in which your team can thrive. Key Responsibilities Provide strategic leadership to the newly combined Research and Policy team, establishing shared priorities and ways of working while supporting staff development and collaboration. Lead the development of feminist research, evidence-based policy and influencing strategies across the team's thematic areas. Provide strategic oversight of the team's technical expertise, supporting cross-Federation technical assistance, capacity strengthening and programme learning. Develop and strengthen equitable partnerships with women's rights organisations, feminist movements, academic institutions and other key stakeholders. Represent ActionAid UK at national and global forums, strengthening engagement with policymakers, donors and other decision-makers. Work collaboratively across ActionAid UK and the Federation to identify funding opportunities and ensure research and programme evidence inform advocacy, campaigns and influencing. Manage the team's people, resources and budgets, contributing to departmental and organisational planning and leadership. About You We are looking for an experienced and inclusive leader who: Has significant experience of leading multidisciplinary teams, setting strategic direction and supporting staff development. Brings substantial experience in feminist research, policy development and influencing, with a strong understanding of women's rights and gender justice. Has strong knowledge of women, peace and security, feminist humanitarian action and related thematic areas, including climate and economic justice. Has experience of developing equitable partnerships with women's rights organisations, feminist movements and other relevant stakeholders. Can provide strategic or technical oversight of research, policy or women's rights programmes and translate evidence into effective influencing. Has experience of developing strategic plans, managing budgets and contributing to funding opportunities. Can lead through organisational change, bring together different areas of expertise and foster an inclusive and collaborative team culture. Is committed to feminist principles, anti-racism, decolonisation and shifting power to women, girls and their movements. Why Join Us? At ActionAid UK, you'll be part of a global movement working towards a world free from poverty, injustice and gender inequality. Our work is rooted in the leadership and expertise of women and girls and the movements working to advance their rights. This is an opportunity to shape the direction of our newly combined Research and Policy team, bringing together different areas of expertise to strengthen our research, policy and influencing work. You will work alongside committed colleagues across ActionAid UK and the wider Federation, building partnerships and supporting collective action for feminist change. In return, we offer a supportive and collaborative working environment, flexible and hybrid working arrangements, and the opportunity to contribute to lasting change for women and girls worldwide. Additional Information Diversity, equality, inclusion and belonging: Diversity, inclusion and belonging are key to our organisational culture. We are on a journey to become not only an anti-racist organisation but one that proudly celebrates the diversity of all applicants and employees. We look forward to you bringing your full self to work, proudly sharing your unique perspective and helping us to shape our combined future. We especially welcome applications from those from under-represented/marginalised communities. AAUK is a Disability Confident Committed organisation and as such any candidate that declares a disability will be shortlisted for interview if they meet the essential criteria for the role. Referencing and safeguarding: All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, safeguarding, criminal records and terrorism finance checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. ActionAid UK is committed to preventing any form of sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse (including child abuse and adult at-risk abuse) and responding robustly when these harms take place. We expect all ActionAid UK staff and ActionAid UK representatives to share this commitment. We will not tolerate our staff or other representatives carrying out any form of sexual harassment, exploitation or abuse towards anyone we come into contact with through our work. Working practices: ActionAid is committed to supporting flexible working. If you would like to discuss flexible working options, including the possibility of a job share for this role, there will be space to do so during the interview process. ActionAid UK has a hybrid working policy for many of our roles. The requirement will vary from team to team and the responsibilities of individual roles. As a minimum, all colleagues are expected to attend the office 12 days per year, plus additional time for induction, training, and company connection days. Some roles may require in-office attendance on all days and if so, these will clearly be marked as in-office roles. Please note that ActionAid UK does not offer fully remote working options. We encourage you to discuss hybrid working expectations at interview. Recruitment processes: Please note that ActionAid UK may review, shortlist and interview candidates prior to the closing date so we encourage all candidates to apply as soon as possible. If we receive a very high response, we may close the vacancy early and will not accept further submissions. Vacancies close at 23:55pm

item.title: Senior Employment Law Adviser
item.description: Job description The award-winning ISM is the dynamic, change making professional body representing musicians. With a current membership of over 11,000 musicians, the ISM is well known for its outstanding legal services to members and our campaigning work on issues from music education to AI and Brexit. The ISM is now looking for a highly experienced Senior Employment Law Adviser to join our in-house legal team who have a well-deserved reputation for going the extra mile and delivering gold standard services to our 11,000 musician members. You should be experienced in Claimant work with a good knowledge of all aspects of employment law and in particular issues relating to status and holiday pay. You should also have experience of engaging with ACAS and instituting proceedings in the Tribunal should this become necessary. You will have at least 5 years’ experience working in employment law and have a real commitment to going the extra mile and supporting those who work in precarious settings such as musicians. You will be comfortable working to competing deadlines, have great interpersonal skills and have high levels of attention to detail. The role is 35 hours per week. You will be joining a professional staff team who are based in Bayswater, London. The role is hybrid but for at least 3 days per week you will be in the ISM office. item.title: Chief Operating Officer
item.description: Help to lead a remarkable charity that stands alongside refugees and people seeking asylum in the UK About Refugee Council For more than 75 years, Refugee Council has stood alongside refugees and people seeking asylum, providing practical support, influencing policy and campaigning for a fair and humane refugee protection system. Our vision is for a UK where refugees are welcomed, can rebuild their lives safely and with dignity, and are empowered to contribute to their communities. In 2024/25, we supported more than 15,203 refugees and people seeking asylum , including more than 7,022 children and young people through our specialist youth services. Our work combines direct support, advocacy and campaigning to create lasting change. About the role Refugee Council is seeking an outstanding Chief Operating Officer to join our Senior Leadership Team and to partner with our new Chief Executive and amazing colleagues to shape the organisation’s future. This is a pivotal new role providing strategic leadership across finance , people and culture , IT and digital , data , risk , governance and premises . You will lead our Finance & Resources directorate, drive organisational transformation and ensure our systems, resources and culture enable our frontline services and policy and influencing to thrive. You will lead the charity’s financial strategy, ensuring robust stewardship and long-term sustainability, and provide strategic advice and assurance on financial sustainability, operational resilience, governance and organisational performance to the Board and executive team. About you You will be a qualified accountant with significant senior leadership experience and a strong track record in a broad organisational role including financial strategy, the development of robust, sustainable business models, organisational transformation, business planning and governance. You are passionate about people – someone who sees finance, people, digital, data and systems not as back-office functions but as the platform that allows our frontline work to thrive. Confident with charity finances and able to communicate effectively internally and externally, you are truly collaborative and eager to be part of a cohesive Senior Leadership Team. Why join us? This is a moment for you to use all your experience and talents to ensure the Refugee Council’s financial sustainability, operational resilience and organisational effectiveness and to support the wider sector. If you are a highly relational leader with a passion for involving colleagues, refugees and people with lived experience in delivering the charity’s mission, we would love to hear from you. How to apply Click the apply button to submit your application. Closing date: Monday, 12 October 2026 at 11:45pm. We encourage early applications, as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications.

item.title: Business Development Manager
item.description: For over 140 years, the Forces Employment Charity has proudly supported service leavers, veterans and their families in building successful civilian careers. We provide veterans with life-long, life-changing support, jobs and training opportunities regardless of circumstances, rank, length of service or reason for leaving. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are looking for individuals who embody our values and bring them to life every day: Expert, Passionate, Resilient, Supportive, Open and Honest, and Collaborative. Brief role description The Business Development Manager will play a pivotal role driving the acquisition of high-value, multi-year corporate partnerships and funding agreements that deliver meaningful shared value for the organisation and its partners. Working closely with colleagues across the charity, the postholder will identify and secure new income opportunities, develop compelling partnership propositions and oversee stewardship, renewals and growth opportunities. The role is responsible for building a strong pipeline of perspective funders and partners, managing relationships with key stakeholders and contributing to the achievement of ambitious income generation targets. Who we're looking for We are looking for an experienced business development professional with a strong track record of securing long-term partnerships and driving income growth. You will have experience managing income pipelines, targets and forecasts, alongside a proven ability to identify opportunities, develop compelling propositions and build strong relationships with key stakeholders. You will be an excellent communicator with strong presentation, negotiation and influencing skills, and will be comfortable engaging senior decision-makers. You will also have experience in prospect research, networking and CRM systems. You will bring a proactive, entrepreneurial approach, be highly self-motivated and comfortable working towards ambitious targets. As a collaborative and solutions-focused professional, you will be capable of managing competing priorities while supporting the development of others and contributing to the wider objectives of the Income Generation team. Interested? Want to know more about the Charity? Check out our website. Eager to know more about the role? Have a look at the Job Description. What's in it for you? Check out our Benefits. item.title: Head of Income Generation
item.description: For over 140 years, the Forces Employment Charity has proudly supported service leavers, veterans and their families in building successful civilian careers. We provide veterans with life-long, life-changing support, jobs and training opportunities regardless of circumstances, rank, length of service or reason for leaving. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are looking for individuals who embody our values and bring them to life every day: Expert, Passionate, Resilient, Supportive, Open and Honest, and Collaborative. Brief role description The Head of Income Generation is a new and pivotal senior management role responsible for developing and delivering income generation at the Forces Employment Charity. Overseeing all income streams, including high-value fundraising, trusts and foundations, individual giving and other business development opportunities, they will work towards a multimillion-pound income target. They will also line manage a small team of three and work closely with the Director of Engagement and Income Generation and other members of the Senior Management Team to deliver ambitious income-generation plans. Who we're looking for We are looking for an experienced fundraising and partnerships professional with a proven track record of securing income from trusts, foundations, corporate partners and other funding sources. You will be skilled at developing and delivering successful income generation strategies, building strong funding pipelines and achieving ambitious income targets You will be a confident relationship builder and have experience engaging senior stakeholders, securing new partnership opportunities and developing compelling funding propositions that generate results. You will also be comfortable leading and supporting colleagues, working collaboratively across teams and identifying opportunities for growth. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of fundraising best practice, ethical fundraising and supporter stewardship, alongside experience using CRM systems. Most importantly, you will share our values, be motivated by our mission and demonstrate empathy for ex-Forces personnel and the challenges they can face. Interested? Want to know more about the Charity? Check out our website. Eager to know more about the role? Have a look at the Job Description. What's in it for you? Check out our Benefits. item.title: International Partnerships Lead
item.description: 1 x IPL (Europe) - permanent / full time 1 x IPL (MENA) - 12 month FTC maternity cover / full time Unifrog’s mission We’re on a mission to level the playing field when it comes to young people finding and applying for their next step after school. We're achieving this by bringing all the available information into one single, impartial, user-friendly platform that helps students to make the best choices, and submit the strongest applications. We also empower teachers and counsellors to manage the progression process effectively. Our outlook is global - we work with schools and universities all over the world, from the US to New Zealand, and from Italy to Hong Kong. We want to make it so that young people can compare every opportunity taught in English, wherever it is in the world, and have all the support they need to make successful applications. We have a clear social purpose, and we’re hugely ambitious. We already work with over half of UK secondary schools, and hundreds of international schools. We are growing rapidly in terms of the number of our customers, in terms of how much they use our platform, and in terms of the breadth of products we offer. Our team is at the heart of our business and is integral to our success. We work hard to foster a culture of openness, happiness and innovation, and we commit to helping every individual learn and grow so that they can reach their full potential. We want to hire talented people, whatever their background. If you are excited by our mission and are ready to work hard, please don’t hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you! We believe in the power of diversity. If you are from an ethnic minority background, we would like to strongly encourage you to apply. In advance of applying, if you have any questions about working at Unifrog, please contact our Recruitment Lead. What you’ll do As International Partnerships Lead, your role is to provide world class strategic support and customer service to over 250 international schools from around the world. You will build and maintain excellent working relationships with your partner schools, supporting them to make the most of the Unifrog platform. Partnerships and solutions focused, you will make sure that all interactions with Unifrog are prompt, positive and successful. You will cover the schools in your region, with possible opportunities for international travel for school visits or conferences once a year. Your key responsibilities will include: What we’re looking for Essential: Nice to have, but not essential: You will be joining a team of highly motivated people who are passionate about our mission of helping students to find the best next step for them after school. If this excites you, you love building relationships, and you’re an energetic person who is willing to learn, then we’d love to hear from you. Working together You’ll work alongside the Area Manager for your region as well as colleagues in our International Partnerships team and the wider International schools team. You’ll be line managed by our International Partnerships Manager (London-based). Benefits On our jobs page you’ll find a full list of the benefits we offer our team. Here’s a snapshot: Mission focussed Join one of Escape the City’s top 1% employers and help transform careers and destinations in schools. Growing company Become part of a committed, dynamic, and growing company. We want to build our team for the long term: if you do well, we will do our best to make sure you want to stay at the company for a long time. Key details: Application process i. With reference to examples of your recent experience, what would make you an excellent candidate for this role? (250 words) ii. Tell us about a time when you had to build a relationship with someone when it was particularly challenging. What was your approach? (250 words) Standard Q&A from a panel of three, including questions about your experiences and how these relate to the role, and scenario questions based on common situations you might face (plus time for your questions) (50 minutes). Please note, we compare all answers to an AI-generated answer. Where we suspect AI has been used to write the majority of the answer, this will be taken into consideration when scoring. You can find more details and our full policy on AI in applications here . Inclusion and diversity at Unifrog Within the company we try to foster a culture of innovation, and a happy working environment, both because this is the right thing to do, and because we think this results in the most effective team. To this end we believe in open communication, celebrating successes, supporting each other, not being afraid to be wrong or to fail, and promoting good ideas wherever they come from. As a platform that supports teachers and students from a huge variety of backgrounds it’s important that our team and leadership reflects this diversity. This is something we are actively working towards and prioritising. We embed diversity, equity and inclusion across everything we do, continually evaluating policies and practices to make sure they are inclusive and equitable. To make sure everyone’s voice is heard and people have the opportunities to learn to be better allies in the workplace, we encourage the team to share what they’re celebrating, facilitate training and group discussions, and seek regular feedback about what more the company could do to help people feel included. To ensure that our recruitment process is consistent and fair, we anonymise your application and therefore do not see your name, personal, educational or professional background. We also randomise the order of responses so that it’s less likely that a candidate is advantaged or disadvantaged by where their answers appear compared to other candidates.
item.dc:creator: Unifrog Education Ltd

item.title: Head of Communications & Engagement
item.description: About Pathway Fund Pathway Fund is a social investment organisation working to create a more equitable economy and improve access to capital for Black and Ethnically Minoritised communities and organisations. Our work spans investment, community development, social enterprise and community wealth building. We are entering an important period of growth and need to communicate more clearly and confidently who we are, what we stand for and the difference we make. Role profile: Head of Communications & Engagement Reports to: Chief Executive Officer Location: London Contract: Permanent Salary: £58k - £65k About the role As Pathway’s most senior communications leader, the Head of Communications & Engagement will shape our organisational narrative and lead our communications, storytelling and engagement strategy. You will turn complex ideas, investment activity, evidence and community experience into compelling stories for communities, staff, trustees, funders, investors, government and partners. You will strengthen Pathway’s profile, build meaningful stakeholder relationships and help colleagues become confident ambassadors for our work. This is a strategic leadership role requiring sound judgement and hands-on delivery. You will work collaboratively across Pathway and with external support, while retaining ownership of our voice, narrative, brand and engagement approach. Policy leadership sits separately from this role. Key Responsibilities Communications Strategy and Leadership Develop and deliver an organisation-wide communications and engagement strategy aligned with Pathway’s objectives. Set clear priorities, audiences, messages and channels, and establish effective communications systems, governance and performance measures. Advise the CEO, Board and senior leadership on communications, reputation, stakeholder engagement, risks and opportunities. Brand, Narrative and Storytelling Own and strengthen Pathway’s narrative, brand and positioning across all communications. Turn complex investment activity, programme evidence and impact data into clear and compelling stories for different audiences. Develop high-quality content across digital, social, print, film, publications and events. Centre community voices through ethical and authentic storytelling, including the experiences of Black and Ethnically Minoritised communities involved in community-led housing, community assets and wealth building. Internal and External Communications Lead internal communications that connect colleagues with Pathway’s mission, strategy and impact, equipping staff and trustees to act as confident ambassadors. Lead external communications, media activity, thought leadership and major organisational announcements. Build Pathway’s profile and strengthen its reputation across social investment, community development, community wealth building and racial equity. Stakeholder and Community Engagement Build meaningful relationships with communities, government, public bodies, funders, investors, media, partners and sector organisations. Develop engagement plans that strengthen influence, support investment opportunities and advance Pathway’s mission. Create genuine two-way engagement, enabling communities to shape Pathway’s narrative and tell their own stories. Ensure communications are accessible, culturally informed and relevant to diverse audiences. CEO and Board Support Act as senior communications adviser to the CEO and Board. Prepare speeches, presentations, briefings, key messages and talking points. Support high-profile engagements and advise on the external stakeholder environment. Organisational Capability and Delivery Build communications capability across Pathway through guidance, coaching, tools and practical support. Commission and manage agencies, freelancers, suppliers and the communications budget. Combine strategic leadership with hands-on writing, coordination and delivery. Key Relationships Internal: CEO, Board and Chair, senior leadership team, programme and investment teams, and colleagues across Pathway. External: Communities and community organisations, funders, investors, government and public bodies, media, strategic partners, and communications and public affairs advisers. Candidate profile You will bring: Significant senior-level experience in communications, engagement, public affairs, marketing or a related field. A strong track record of developing and delivering communications strategies in a complex or mission-driven organisation. Exceptional writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear, accessible and compelling content. Experience shaping organisational narratives, building reputation and delivering content across digital, social, print and events. Experience developing genuine two-way engagement with communities and stakeholders. Confidence advising senior leaders and boards, managing sensitive communications and building relationships across sectors. Experience managing agencies, suppliers and communications budgets. Strategic judgement combined with a practical, delivery-focused approach. Strong relationship-building, political awareness and digital communications capability. A collaborative, community-centred approach and commitment to racial and economic equity. Knowledge of social investment, community development, community wealth building, community-led housing, social enterprise or the VCSE sector would be advantageous. Experience working with Black and Ethnically Minoritised-led communities or organisations is particularly welcome, but sector knowledge is not a substitute for strong communications and engagement capability. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is: Mission-driven and committed to racial and economic equity. Collaborative, curious and an excellent listener. Authentic, credible and able to challenge constructively. Politically and culturally aware. Comfortable with change and ambiguity. Pragmatic and able to combine strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. What Success Will Look Like Within the first 12 months, the successful candidate will have: Established a clear communications and engagement strategy. Strengthened Pathway’s narrative, profile and reputation. Developed consistent, high-quality communications and ethical community storytelling. Built stronger relationships with priority communities, funders, investors, government and partners. Improved internal engagement and communications capability across Pathway. Established effective systems and measures for communications performance. Developed the narrative and stakeholder proposition around community-led housing, community assets and community wealth building for Black and Ethnically Minoritised communities. You will work collaboratively across Pathway and with external support, while retaining ownership of our voice, narrative, brand and engagement approach. Policy leadership sits separately from this role. Recruitment and Inclusion This is a storytelling role, and candidates will be assessed on their ability to apply their skills in practice. The recruitment process will include a practical exercise assessing strategic judgement, writing, storytelling, audience insight and delivery. Pathway welcomes applicants from backgrounds underrepresented in senior leadership and people with lived experience of the inequalities we seek to address. We are committed to fair, inclusive and accessible recruitment, and will provide reasonable adjustments throughout the process. How to Apply Applications should be sent using the apply link before 5:00pm on 14 October 2026.
item.dc:creator: Pathaway Fund

item.title: Team Leader – STEP
item.description: Lead a dynamic service that makes a meaningful difference to people transitioning from hospital care. As Team Leader – Step Service, you’ll lead a team delivering high-quality accommodation-based support to people with complex health & support needs, helping them move towards safe, sustainable independence. You’ll oversee day-to-day service delivery, referrals, risk & safeguarding, while coordinating personalised support & move-on plans. Working closely with Connection Support, hospitals, health teams & other agencies, you’ll build strong partnerships & ensure residents receive the right support at the right time. This is a rewarding opportunity to combine leadership, partnership working & person-centred support to create positive outcomes. Main Purpose Of Job: The Step service provides two differing services: Step Up service is a model providing accommodation based support and assessment to prevent people having the need to go into hospital. Step Down provides accommodation based support and assessment for people who are being discharged from the hospital using the discharge to assess model. This provision in Oxfordshire is run in partnership between Homeless Oxfordshire and Connection Support. This role is responsible for assessing referrals, line managing a small team to deliver a safe and supportive service to all residents, and identifying appropriate move on options for the 12 individuals living at the Step services. The role holder will have line management and case load coordination responsibilities and work in partnership with Connections and other agencies to create holistic, individualised support and move on plans for clients who are temporarily housed due to their health needs. Main Areas Of Responsibility: · To lead the day to day running of a new and dynamic service with your team and service users. · To ensure the effective delivery of high-quality support and housing management according to Homeless Oxfordshire policies and procedures · To work in partnership with Connection Support Step provision and Out of Hospital Team. · To work with other agencies to provide client centered support & risk management plans for clients with complex needs to identify work towards a suitable move on option within 6 weeks. · To proactively and dynamically assess, monitor, manage and respond to risk. · To liaise with hospitals across the county to respond to referrals (including the Horton, John Radcliffe & Warneford), assess risk and suitability of referrals to the service. · Work within agreed contractual performance targets and organisational targets and objectives: o Monitoring and achieving key performance indictors and standards of service. o Provide support, advice, line management and guidance to staff as appropriate. · Report any safeguarding concerns in line with procedures and to appropriate bodies. · Manage challenging situations to ensure the safety of yourself and others. Lead on any incident follow up alongside Team Manager. · Keep up to date and clear records and ensure information is shared with the team and external agencies as required. · Maintain positive relationships with all stakeholders and represent Homeless Oxfordshire at interagency meetings, as required. · Being a member of Homeless Oxfordshire’s on-call rota. · To ensure that Homeless Oxfordshire’s Equal Opportunities Policies are complied with and promoted in carrying out duties of the post. Safeguarding Statement: Homeless Oxfordshire is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all adults, children and young people who are at risk of harm and that come into contact with our services. We believe that all adults, children and young people have an equal right to protection from abuse, regardless of their age, race, religion, ability, gender, language, background or sexual identity and consider the wellbeing of the vulnerable adult, child or young person is paramount. As a result, we have a robust safeguarding policy to ensure everyone is treated fairly and a whistleblowing policy to enable people raise any concerns confidentially. We expect everyone (employees, trustees, associates, volunteers and anyone working on behalf of the Company) to share this commitment and read, understand and adhere to this policy and related procedures. Equal Opportunities: We employ people on the basis of their abilities. We strive to attract and develop talent that is representative of our clients and all sections of the society, and do not discriminate based on of age, faith, disability, race, gender, sexuality and socio-economic, regional or cultural background. If you are shortlisted and need us to make any adjustments to help you attend for interview, please let us know. About Us: We are an open door for people experiencing homelessness whose lives have been shaped by trauma and disadvantage; providing safety, stability and support when it is needed most. We deliver this support across Oxfordshire by providing a range of accommodation with access to high quality support, offering a safe and welcoming space for people to take control of their own lives. We are an accredited Oxford Living Wage employer, and benefits to the role include: annual leave starting at 26 days (excluding bank holidays), flexible working, enhanced benefits with qualifying service, retail discounts with our Homeless Oxfordshire Benefits Hub, and life assurance up to four times your salary and a £250 bonus if you successfully refer a someone as a new colleague through our Employee Referral Scheme as a thanks from us! What’s Next: Have a look at the job description to find out more about the role and apply on our website. Please be aware that this role is subject to an enhanced DBS disclosure check and will be undertaken for the successful candidate . We reserve the right to close this advert early if we identify a suitable candidate before the advertised closing date.
item.dc:creator: Homeless Oxfordshire, Oxford

item.title: Care Navigator
item.description: Care Navigator Salary: £28,353 - £31,756 per annum + 6% Hours: 36 hours per week Based at: Haringey Multi Agency Care & Coordination (MACC) Team Contract: One year (possible extension) Closing date: 12 October 2026, 12 noon Interviews: w/c 12 October 2026 The Bridge Renewal Trust, in partnership with the NHS, are delivering care navigation services for frail patients in Haringey. As a Care Navigator, you will work as part of a multidisciplinary team to support frail patients in Haringey by providing individual holistic assessments and directing patients to appropriate services, including activities that may help to promote their health, wellbeing and independence. The Bridge Renewal Trust is a charity that delivers practical ways that people can live healthier, long and fulfilling lives – thus playing our part in working towards reducing health inequalities and building stronger communities. Are you a passionate and dynamic individual with excellent organisational and interpersonal skills; can you work in a multi-disciplinary team, working closely with other healthcare professionals, the general public and voluntary sector? We are currently recruiting a Care Navigator who will focus on helping patients to make full use of community and voluntary sector services available locally, as well as those provided by health and social care agencies. The key requirements for this post are experience of working with clients providing person-centred care and being familiar with voluntary and community services to respond holistically to patients’ health and wellbeing needs. This is a unique opportunity to join a progressive organisation where we value and reward the performance of our staff. To apply, please email your CV with contact details of two referees, a supporting statement demonstrating how you meet the requirements set out in the Person Specification and completed equal opportunities monitoring form. For a full job description, please visit the Bridge Renewal Trust website. NB: We reserve the right to withdraw this opportunity early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. As part of our commitment to equal opportunities, we invite you to complete our equalities monitoring form by clicking here. Please use the Job ID 2025036 . Thank you. The Bridge Renewal Trust is an equal opportunities employer and positively welcomes applications from all sections of the community.

item.title: Caseworker (Scotland)
item.description: Rare opportunity : Help those affected by road crashes and create lasting change with Brake, the renowned road safety charity. Not your average job : We are looking for passionate and compassionate people who want to make a real difference in the lives of those affected by road crashes. When someone’s life is changed in an instant, having someone there who listens, understands and truly cares can make an enormous difference. As part of our team, you’ll provide compassionate, trauma-informed support, helping individuals and families feel heard, respected and less alone as they navigate some of the most difficult experiences of their lives. You’ll work alongside each person to understand their individual needs, strengths, risks and concerns, providing support that promotes safety, choice and dignity while helping them find a way forward at their own pace. You’ll manage a caseload of complex and sensitive cases, recognising and responding appropriately to risk and safeguarding concerns, and work closely with Family Liaison Officers, health and mental health services, GPs, the coronial system, children’s services, social care and voluntary organisations to ensure people receive safe, joined-up support. Take a look at our comprehensive job description for more details. What we offer : - A generous 35 days of annual leave (including bank holidays and 3-day shutdown period between Christmas and New Year, pro-rata for part-time working patterns) - Birthday day off (taken any time) - Enhanced sick pay and compassionate leave - Death in service benefit - Pension - Employee Assistance Programme - Flexible working - A rewarding role with purpose - Be part of a skilled, friendly team with an engaged Board of Trustees Who you are : We’re looking for people with the skills and experience to build trusting relationships, manage complex situations, recognise risk and work collaboratively with individuals, families and professionals. Most importantly, you’ll bring a genuine commitment to making a meaningful difference. This is a remote-based role, but you’ll never be working in isolation. We stay connected through regular virtual team meetings, team huddles, Slack and 1:1 and clinical supervision, creating a supportive environment where colleagues can share, reflect, learn and support one another. You’ll also receive ongoing trauma-informed training and opportunities to develop your practice. Specifically seeking candidates with : - Experience with people affected by trauma, sudden bereavement, or serious injury - Understanding of trauma-informed practice and ability to provide support sensitively - Experience identifying and responding to safeguarding and vulnerability concerns - Strong advocacy skills ability to act as a powerful voice for service users, expertly navigating external networks, assemble resources and cross-functional support where required. About us : At Brake, we are committed to creating a truly inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel valued, respected, and supported. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and life experiences, and particularly encourage candidates from the global majority, LGBTQIA+ community, and people with disabilities to apply. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our work and enable us to deliver the best possible support to individuals and families affected by road trauma. As a proud Disability Confident employer, we don’t want you to ‘fit’ our culture, we want you to enrich it Not for traffic offenders : Due to the nature of our work we can't accept applications from traffic offenders. Candidates will be asked to disclose whether they have any unspent points or driving convictions on their licence at interview. An enhanced PVG check is required due to the sensitive nature of our service. If this sounds like the kind of role where you could make a real difference, we’d love to hear from you. Join us today and be part of the solution!

item.title: Humanitarian Management Trainee - Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)
item.description: Role: Humanitarian Management Trainee - Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Hours: Full-time Pay: £35,000 GBP gross per annum Duration: 18 months (with possible extension dependent on funding) Location: UK-based with international deployment Are you looking to kickstart your career in the humanitarian sector? Is your ambition to develop towards leadership roles in humanitarian work? And are you willing to work hard, learn by doing, and contribute to humanitarian work by doing everything it takes to deliver lifesaving health emergency responses? UK-Med is a frontline medical aid charity. Born of the NHS, we’ve been working for over 30 years towards a world where everyone has the healthcare they need when crises or disasters hit. We are excited to launch our Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme, offering three distinct trainee roles in the areas of MEAL, Communications and Human Resources & Membership. The Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme presents an unparalleled learning opportunity for early-career professionals who are committed to a career in humanitarian work. It is an opportunity to accelerate your development towards future leadership roles in the humanitarian sector. The Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme consists of an 18-month pathway designed to provide in-depth exposure to humanitarian health programming through a structured professional development plan. You will embed within a team, gaining practical experience and contributing actively to its work and priorities and those of the wider organisation, both at Headquarters and in the field. Alongside this, you will undertake formal and informal professional development through training, mentoring, shadowing and on-the-job learning. The traineeship is a structured development opportunity and is not intended to fill an established role within UK-Med’s organisational structure. As a trainee, you will: Embed within a team at UK-Med Headquarters, gaining practical experience while contributing to our wider humanitarian preparedness and activities. Deploy internationally to assist in delivering humanitarian health responses. Participate in tailored training, mentoring, shadowing and on-the-job learning to build your skills, knowledge and experience. You will have relevant qualifications or equivalent professional experience, with an established technical foundation in your chosen field. Some professional and international experience is essential, alongside a strong interest in applying your existing skills and developing your career within the humanitarian sector. How to apply We strongly recommend that you read the Candidate Information Pack - Humanitarian Management Trainee - MEAL - Sept 2026 before applying for this role. To apply, please submit a current CV and answer the application questions : Please apply below, as soon as possible and no later than Thursday 8th October 2026. Our selection process is designed to understand your potential, motivation and suitability for the Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme, as well as the skills and experience you would bring to your chosen pathway. Shortlisted candidates will first be invited to an online interview. Following the interview stage, selected candidates will then be invited to attend an in-person assessment in Manchester. The assessment will include a range of individual and/or group activities designed to explore your skills, approach and potential. The in-person assessment is expected to take place on the 19th of November in Manchester. If you progress to this stage, you will be expected to attend in person, so we encourage applicants to keep this date available where possible. UK-Med will provide further information regarding the assessment and associated travel/logistical arrangements to candidates invited to this stage. Please note: Due to the nature of this role, candidates must be deployable without the need for additional visa applications to Schengen countries. This requirement is essential for operational reasons to ensure swift and efficient deployment in humanitarian settings, enabling timely and effective responses to crises. Applications for work in the UK can only be accepted from people with an existing right to work in the UK. UK-Med is committed to safeguarding of our personnel and beneficiaries and has a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse. item.title: Humanitarian Management Trainee - Human Resources and Membership
item.description: Role: Humanitarian Management Trainee - Human Resources and Membership Hours: Full-time Pay: £35,000 GBP gross per annum Duration: 18 months (with possible extension dependent on funding) Location: UK-based with international deployment Are you looking to kickstart your career in the humanitarian sector? Is your ambition to develop towards leadership roles in humanitarian work? And are you willing to work hard, learn by doing, and contribute to humanitarian work by doing everything it takes to deliver lifesaving health emergency responses? UK-Med is a frontline medical aid charity. Born of the NHS, we’ve been working for over 30 years towards a world where everyone has the healthcare they need when crises or disasters hit. We are excited to launch our Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme, offering three distinct trainee roles in the areas of MEAL, Communications and Human Resources & Membership. The Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme presents an unparalleled learning opportunity for early-career professionals who are committed to a career in humanitarian work. It is an opportunity to accelerate your development towards future leadership roles in the humanitarian sector. The Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme consists of an 18-month pathway designed to provide in-depth exposure to humanitarian health programming through a structured professional development plan. You will embed within a team, gaining practical experience and contributing actively to its work and priorities and those of the wider organisation, both at Headquarters and in the field. Alongside this, you will undertake formal and informal professional development through training, mentoring, shadowing and on-the-job learning. The traineeship is a structured development opportunity and is not intended to fill an established role within UK-Med’s organisational structure. As a trainee, you will: Embed within a team at UK-Med Headquarters, gaining practical experience while contributing to our wider humanitarian preparedness and activities. Deploy internationally to assist in delivering humanitarian health responses. Participate in tailored training, mentoring, shadowing and on-the-job learning to build your skills, knowledge and experience. You will have relevant qualifications or equivalent professional experience, with an established technical foundation in your chosen field. Some professional and international experience is essential, alongside a strong interest in applying your existing skills and developing your career within the humanitarian sector. How to apply We strongly recommend that you read the Candidate Information Pack - Humanitarian Management Trainee - HR & Membership - Sept 2026 before applying for this role. To apply, please submit a current CV and answer the application questions : Please apply below, as soon as possible and no later than Thursday 8th October 2026. Our selection process is designed to understand your potential, motivation and suitability for the Humanitarian Management Trainee Scheme, as well as the skills and experience you would bring to your chosen pathway. Shortlisted candidates will first be invited to an online interview. Following the interview stage, selected candidates will then be invited to attend an in-person assessment in Manchester. The assessment will include a range of individual and/or group activities designed to explore your skills, approach and potential. The in-person assessment is expected to take place on the 19th of November in Manchester. If you progress to this stage, you will be expected to attend in person, so we encourage applicants to keep this date available where possible. UK-Med will provide further information regarding the assessment and associated travel/logistical arrangements to candidates invited to this stage. Please note: Due to the nature of this role, candidates must be deployable without the need for additional visa applications to Schengen countries. This requirement is essential for operational reasons to ensure swift and efficient deployment in humanitarian settings, enabling timely and effective responses to crises. Applications for work in the UK can only be accepted from people with an existing right to work in the UK. UK-Med is committed to safeguarding of our personnel and beneficiaries and has a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse. We conduct thorough vetting before any appointment is confirmed. UK-Med is committed to the principles of diversity, equality, and inclusion. item.title: Corporate Partnerships Lead (Partnership Management)
item.description: Job description Do you have a proven track record of growing high-value, strategic partnerships and unlocking new opportunities within complex relationships? Can you combine commercial acumen, entrepreneurial thinking and inspiring leadership to drive long-term income growth and impact from some of the UK's most significant corporate partnerships? About the role We are recruiting for a Corporate Partnerships Lead (Partnerships Management) to join on a full-time basis, working 35 hours per week on a permanent contract. This is a hybrid role with your time split between working remotely and travelling into London to work from our office at Crutched Friars or attending in-person meetings with key partners, colleagues, and other stakeholders. As Corporate Partnerships Lead (Partnership Management), you will lead one of the most significant and exciting corporate partnership portfolios in the charity sector, with responsibility for driving sustainable income growth, partner engagement and long-term strategic value. You will own and deliver our partnership management strategy, determining how we maximise value, impact and growth from existing partnerships. Working with well-known partners including The FA, British Airways and Well Pharmacy, you will ensure partnerships continue to evolve, deepen and deliver meaningful outcomes for both organisations. Leading and developing a high-performing team, you will create a culture of ambition, accountability and commercial excellence. You will support and challenge colleagues to think beyond delivery, identifying new opportunities for growth, innovation and shared value within partner relationships. This is a highly strategic and externally focused leadership role. You will personally lead some of our most significant and complex partnerships, working closely with senior executives and C-suite stakeholders to develop compelling growth strategies, secure investment and build long-term relationships that deliver transformational results. You will act as a senior leader across Corporate Partnerships and the wider organisation, influencing how we approach partner growth, defining what excellent partnership management looks like and embedding a consistently commercial, relationship-led approach across the team. We have provisionally scheduled the first stage interviews for this role to take place via MS Teams on the week commencing Monday 26th October. Second stage interviews will take place in-person at our Crutched Friars offices in London – currently scheduled for Wednesday 11th November. About you You will bring significant experience of having managed, grown and renewed complex, high-value partnerships, with a proven track record of securing substantial income growth from existing relationships. Your experience may have been from the charity, commercial or public sectors. You will be: - An ambitious and inspiring leader with a track record of building, developing and leading high-performing teams. - Commercially astute and highly strategic, with the ability to identify growth opportunities, manage risk and maximise long-term value from complex relationships. - Experienced in managing six and seven-figure partnerships, developing growth strategies and securing investment that delivers meaningful commercial and social impact. - Skilled at influencing and building credibility with senior executives and senior stakeholders, creating trusted relationships that enable long-term partnership growth. - Confident balancing strategic leadership with hands-on ownership of significant partnership opportunities and negotiations. - Experienced in creating a culture of accountability, innovation and continuous improvement, helping teams achieve exceptional results. - Able to interpret corporate priorities, market insight, ESG priorities, and emerging trends to inform partnership strategies and create compelling opportunities for growth. - Collaborative and influential, with the ability to bring together colleagues across a complex organisation to deliver ambitious partnership objectives. Above all, you will be motivated by growth: identifying opportunities others may miss, deepening relationships and creating partnerships that become increasingly valuable, impactful and strategically important over time. What you’ll focus on: - Owning and delivering the Partnership Management strategy, ensuring the portfolio achieves ambitious income, engagement and impact objectives. - Leading and developing the Partnership Management team, creating a culture of ambition, commerciality, collaboration and high performance. - Driving sustainable growth across a portfolio of high-value partnerships, identifying opportunities to increase income, deepen engagement and expand strategic value. - Supporting the delivery of the partnership portfolio, while building strong foundations for future growth. - Working with partners to develop long-term growth plans, ensuring relationships continue to evolve and deliver mutual value. - Personally leading some of Alzheimer's Society's most significant and complex partnerships, including engagement with senior stakeholders. - Influencing and working collaboratively with colleagues across Alzheimer’s Society to develop compelling propositions, campaigns and growth opportunities. - Defining and championing what excellent partnership management looks like, positioning Alzheimer's Society as a sector leader in corporate partnerships. - Ensuring the team maintains a strong understanding of ESG priorities, emerging trends and partner objectives, using these insights to shape growth strategies and opportunities. - Acting as a senior ambassador for Alzheimer's Society, building trusted relationships that strengthen our reputation and long-term partnership success. About Alzheimer's Society - who are we and what’s our mission? Dementia is the UK’s biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer’s Society, we’re the UK’s leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding ground-breaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we’re working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. Our commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging We need to ensure the voices around our table better reflect and understand the communities we exist to serve. We strongly encourage individuals to apply who have a disability, impairment or health condition or individuals who identify as part of a minority ethnic background, as these groups are currently under-represented at Alzheimer's Society. Our hiring process We want you to bring your whole self to the process. Applications are anonymised until interview stage, and we’re happy to support any adjustments. Share your feedback via our candidate survey when applying to help us improve. We may close early if we receive high interest (with 48 hours’ notice). Some roles may require a DBS check as part of our safer recruitment commitment. Thinking about using AI during the recruitment process? we know this can be helpful in many ways but remember to include your personal and authentic self too. Your voice and experience are what really set you apart. Giving back to you At Alzheimer’s Society, we value our people and take a total reward approach to pay and benefits. You’ll enjoy a generous double-matched pension scheme, 27 days’ annual leave (plus bank holidays and wellbeing days), and access to a free Health Shield Cash Plan, 24/7 EAP, Thrive mental wellbeing support, and virtual GP services. Our Society Plus platform offers exclusive discounts, wellbeing resources, and recognition schemes, while our flexible working, family-friendly policies, and life assurance provide peace of mind and work/life balance. We also offer a free Will-writing service and long service awards to recognise your ongoing commitment. item.description: Job Title: Refuge Worker Location: Warwickshire - this is an onsite role Salary: £22,429.14 per annum Contract type: Part Time, Permanent Hours: 31.5 hours per week This is an exciting opportunity to join Refuge as a refuge worker, providing high quality practical and emotional support to survivors of domestic abuse and their children living in our refuge accommodation in Warwickshire. The post holder will work closely with survivors from the point of crisis and admission to the refuge, through to move on from the emergency accommodation. This involves providing a personalised, holistic support and safety plan, enabling survivors to access housing, welfare, benefits and legal advice. A key requirement is to ensure that survivors are provided with a safe, supportive and welcoming environment in accordance with Refuge’s philosophical principles. item.title: Independent Living Manager
item.description: At Radcliffe Housing Society , we believe in putting people first. We provide high-quality, person-centred housing services that empower residents to live independently and with dignity. We're looking for a compassionate and proactive Independent Living Manager to help us achieve this mission across our Independent Living schemes. About the role As an Independent Living Manager, you'll support older and vulnerable residents to sustain their tenancies, improve their well-being, and stay connected to their communities. You’ll offer practical advice, develop support plans, promote independence, and respond to emerging needs — all while managing properties to a high standard, and ensuring compliance with health and safety requirements. What you'll be doing Carrying out holistic assessments and developing tailored support plans Helping residents understand their tenancy and maintain their independence Promoting wellbeing through regular welfare checks and community engagement Managing low-level ASB, hoarding, and tenancy sustainment issues Coordinating social activities to reduce isolation and encourage participation Ensuring schemes meet all health and safety, compliance, and regulatory standards Supporting void management and helping new residents settle in Building strong relationships with residents, families, and partner agencies What we’re looking for · Experience supporting older/vulnerable adults, including those with complex needs · Knowledge of tenancy management and housing-related legislation · Excellent interpersonal skills and a compassionate, person-centred approach · Ability to work under pressure. · Ability to work independently and as part of a team. · Strong organisational skills and confidence using IT systems · Understanding of safeguarding, health and safety, and GDPR · Ability to work flexibly across multiple locations · Possession of, or a demonstratable commitment to working towards a Level 4 Housing Certificate or Diploma · Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle (essential) Why join Radcliffe? We’re a small, committed, high-performing housing provider with big ambitions for our residents. You’ll be part of a supportive team where your voice counts, and your work makes a genuine impact. We offer flexible working, ongoing training, and a culture that values inclusion, integrity, and continuous improvement. Benefits A generous holiday entitlement, plus paid bank holidays Additional out of hours callout benefits Membership to Pension Scheme Career development, training opportunities and access to e-learning Access to eye care vouchers and VDU Glasses Financial assistance for dental care treatment External Occupational Health service Access to EAP Services 24/7 Free parking No agencies please

item.title: Senior Political Engagement Manager
item.description: Senior Political Engagement Manager We are looking for a Senior Political Engagement Manager to lead political engagement with the UK Government and Parliament, building ambitious, high-level relationships with Downing Street, FCDO Ministers and senior civil servants to secure influence and impact on the issues affecting the world's most vulnerable children. With 75 years of experience, the focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. The organisation helps children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by Christian faith. Come join the 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories! Position: Senior Political Engagement Manager Location: Milton Keynes/hybrid Hours: Full time Contract: Permanent Salary: £50,000-£53,000 per annum Closing Date: October 20, 2026 About the Role Working closely with the Head of Policy & Advocacy and Policy Manager, you'll take the agreed policy positions and turn them into political strategy, targeted influencing activity and the relationships that get the charity in the room with the people who matter. You'll also line manage the Child Participation & Advocacy Advisor and play an active role in the leadership of the Policy & Advocacy Team. Key Responsibilities: Political Engagement Strategy Develop and lead the political engagement strategy, targeting Downing Street, FCDO Ministers, senior civil servants and cross-party Parliamentarians. Senior Political Relationships & Influence Build and maintain constructive, senior-level relationships across the political spectrum, and bring creativity to campaign, coalition and relationship-building opportunities that extend the political reach. Political Advice & Horizon Scanning Oversee political monitoring and analysis, providing senior political advice and horizon-scanning so the charity anticipates and responds to developments ahead of the field. Briefings & Correspondence Personally lead high-quality, politically astute letters and briefings for Ministers and senior civil servants, translating agreed policy positions into targeted political asks. Leadership & Management Line manage and develop the Child Participation & Advocacy Advisor, and play an active role in the leadership of the Policy & Advocacy Team. Your love of politics, your instinct for where power really sits, and your skill in building high-level political relationships will transform children's lives around the world About You We are looking for someone with: Extensive, senior-level experience of working across UK political parties, with existing high-level relationships and a track record of delivering ambitious political engagement. In-depth understanding of Whitehall, Parliamentary and political systems, including current Government and governing-party structures. Excellent, politically astute writing skills, with experience translating policy positions into targeted political asks, letters and briefings for Ministers or senior stakeholders. A creative, entrepreneurial approach to identifying campaign, coalition and relationship-building opportunities. Experience of managing, coaching or developing staff, or a clear readiness to do so. Sympathy with the charity’s Christian foundation and approach to social justice. This role requires sympathy with and support for the organisations ethos and values. You do not need to be a practising Christian, but you will be comfortable working within a Christian organisation and supportive of its mission. About the Organisation Join an international children’s charity working with children, their communities, and with supporters and partners, in almost 100 countries. Through long-term development projects, emergency responses and advocacy the organisation has helped bring lasting change to millions of children, over more than 60 years. As a Christian charity, everything is motivated by faith as we strive to reflect God’s unconditional love. An offer of employment is conditional upon the successful completion of applicable background checks, including a criminal records check. We value diversity and aspire to reflect this in the workforce. We particularly welcome applications from under-represented sections of the community. The organisation also operates flexible working policies and practices. As a Disability committed employer we encourage qualified individuals with a disability to apply and request a reasonable adjustment if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access as a result of your disability. You may also have experience in areas such as Policy & Advocacy, Policy Manager, Political Engagement, Political Engagement Officer, Political Engagement Manager, Senior Political Engagement Officer, Senior Political Engagement Manager. Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People. #INDNFP
