item.title: Citizen Engagement Manager
item.description: Job description Job purpose This role will lead our citizen engagement work and oversee the Food Ambassador programme. The Food Foundation’s Ambassador programme is a volunteer programme that consists of passionate food activists from across the UK, aged 14 years and up. The programme aims to amplify the voices of people with lived experience of food insecurity. The Food Ambassadors, as experts by experience, share their stories and insights in campaigns, research, at events, with policymakers and the media. Together, we advocate for food system that ensures everyone can access a healthy and sustainable diet. The postholder will be responsible for supporting the ambassadors and facilitating their inclusion in both The Food Foundation’s work, research and campaigns, as well as that of our partner organisations, in order to bring visibility to the ambassadors and their lived experience. The Citizen Engagement Manager will also work with government departments to strengthen relationships between the Food Ambassadors and civil servants. The postholder will also be responsible for recruitment and onboarding of new recruits alongside the Citizen Engagement Assistant, and ensuring the programme is representative of diverse experiences. The post holder will work with our communications team to increase the impact of our media and social media engagement by giving opportunity to Ambassadors to explain the reality of the food system’s impact through their personal stories. The post holder will also work with our business and policy engagement teams to create opportunities for our Ambassadors to provide advice on priorities for our research, the development of policy and practice recommendations. They will be responsible for the development of strategic thinking on our work with citizens as well as the safeguarding lead for the organisation. item.title: Finance and Operations Officer
item.description: Job title: Finance and Operations Officer Organisation: ILPA Location: Hybrid- one day per week (currently Tuesday) in London Deadline: 5pm, Wednesday 7 October 2026. Reporting to : Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Salary: £40,000 per annum (FTE) pro rata, depending on experience and qualifications Contract Type : 3/4 days a week, permanent Organisation Size : 12 employees, annual income c. £750,000 About Us: The Immigration Law Practitioners’ Association (ILPA) is a professional association and registered charity, the majority of whose members are barristers, solicitors, advocates and IAA regulated advisers practising in all aspects of immigration, asylum and nationality law. ILPA currently has approximately 4500 individual member contacts. Founded in 1984 by leading practitioners in the field, and 42 years on, stronger than ever, ILPA exists to promote and improve advice and representation in immigration, asylum and nationality law, through an extensive programme of training and disseminating information and by providing research and opinion that draw on the experiences of members. Our vision is a fair and effective immigration system that respects human rights and the rule of law. We realise this by empowering members to provide the best possible advice and support for migrants and collaboratively working to improve law, policy and practice. ILPA is represented on numerous Government, official and non-Governmental advisory groups and regularly provides high-level evidence to Parliamentary and official enquiries. ILPA is at the forefront of engagement with the Home Office, NGOs and other Government departments. To our members, ILPA is a community where they come to share knowledge, keep up to date with changes and receive high-quality training to enable them to practise effectively. Members also rely on ILPA to be their voice in seeking change for the better to immigration, asylum and nationality law and practice. This we do through the work of our expert legal team, engaging with policymakers and stakeholders, and drawing on the experiences and expertise of our members. ILPA is an equal opportunities employer. We acknowledge that the legal and charitable sector can be less accessible to people from minoritised or racialised communities and lower socio-economic backgrounds, and we are committed to unsettling the status quo. We particularly welcome applications from individuals who have lived experience of the UK immigration system. Role Purpose: As a dual-registered charity and Company Limited by Guarantee with an annual income of c. £750,000, we are seeking a Finance and Operations Officer. This is a vital “sole-charge” finance role within a team of 12. You will take full ownership of our day-to-day transactional accounting, ensure compliance with both the Charity Commission and Companies House, and help keep operations running efficiently. You will bridge the gap between technical accounting and everyday charity management, providing the CEO and Board of Trustees with the clear financial insights needed to plan our future. Key Responsibilities: Financial Management and and Compliance Fund Accounting: Track, segment and report on restricted grant funding alongside unrestricted income stream using data from accounting platforms Transactional Finance: Manage day-to-day book-keeping using accounting software (e.g. Approval Max, QuickBooks), including processing invoices, expense claims, bank reconciliations, and supplier payments. Budgeting & Cash Flow: Collaborate with the CEO to construct the annual organisational budget and budget reforecasts; overall responsibility for cash flow using data from accounting platforms Audit Preparation: Lead and coordinate the year-end independent financial examination or statutory audit process, acting as the primary point of contact for external auditors. Income Generation: assist CEO prepare grant funding applications, reports to funders, develop and maintain transparent data of grant funded income to ensure continuity of funding and consistent cash flow. 2. Operations & Payroll Payroll & Pensions: Oversee the monthly payroll (which is mainly outsourced). Paycircle our existing platform makes the calculations and payments of salary, tax and pension. Office & IT Facilities: Oversee all operational requirements of our premises, manage relationships with facilities vendors, utilities, and coordinate IT/digital infrastructure, software and facilities: responsible for IT infrastructure and equipment; lead contact with our outsourced IT support helpdesk Procurement & Supplier Management: Oversight and responsibility for procurement processes, develop and maintain supplier register and repository, review vendor and supplier contracts, negotiate commercial terms, and ensure value for money across all spending. 3. Governance & Risk Management Dual-Regulatory Filings: Complete and submit accurate annual returns and statutory updates required by both the Charity Commission and Companies House. Person Specification: Experience & Knowledge Charity Finance Expertise: A minimum of 5 years’ experience in a similar role, ie non-profit finance role, with demonstrated expertise in fund accounting, restricted grants, and Gift Aid. Operational Generalist: Proven track record of handling practical operational environments, such as small-team HR payroll management and administration, basic IT coordination, procurement/supplier oversight, or facilities tracking. Small-Team Adaptability: Experience working as a sole-charge finance professional or within a small team (under 20 staff), proving a willingness to be a “hands-on doer” as well as independent. Skills & Competencies Technical Software Literacy: Proficiency with modern cloud accounting systems (ideally Approval Max, QuickBooks) and advanced Microsoft Excel skills. Financial Communication: Ability to translate dense financial data and balance sheets into clear insights for the CEO to utilise Attention to Detail: Transactional data entry, financial reporting, and timeline management for compliance filings. How to Apply: Please submit a CV and cover letter by 5pm on Wednesday 7 October 2026. Please forward these to the email address on our website (linked).

item.title: Suicide Bereavement Service Manager
item.description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for the appointment of a Service Manager in the award-winning Suicide Bereavement Service , delivered by South East London Mind together with partners Mind in Bexley and South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust. The service offers a community resource with open access to adults and young people bereaved by suicide across South East London (Bexley, Bromley, Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark). The integrated team provides one-to-one and group support, with the aim of reducing the risk of further deaths by suicide in this vulnerable group. We are seeking an experienced manager to lead this exceptional service. You will manage a team whose members are employed across three organisations, creating a shared sense of purpose while developing a strong understanding of each partner’s processes, policies, professional responsibilities and ways of working. You will build constructive relationships across the partnership, working sensitively and respectfully with colleagues. Alongside providing operational leadership and strategic input, you will support and guide a uniquely skilled and compassionate team. You will be non-judgmental, caring and resilient, with a good understanding of the issues presented by bereavement through suicide. You will enable meaningful reflective practice and provide appropriate support to staff and volunteers. The role will include direct contact with clients including assessing new referrals, delivering peer support activities and a limited caseload, enabling you to remain closely connected to the experiences and needs of people using the service. You will be adept at using data and feedback to ensure the service meets its contractual requirements, whilst remaining inclusive and sensitive to service user needs, cultural and local contexts. You will identify trends and conduct targeted outreach and promotion to proactively reach underserved communities. The role will include delivering presentations to a wide range of organisations across South East London. The team’s office is at the Bethlem Royal Hospital in West Wickham, Bromley. Office days must include Thursdays, with flexibility to attend other offices and locations as required. The role will involve occasional evening and weekend working and regular travel across South East London, including home visits. Although it is possible to fulfil the travel requirements of the role by public transport, this would best suit someone with access to their own mode of transport, such as a car or bicycle. We encourage applications from people with lived experience of bereavement by suicide, although this is not a requirement for the role. You will join a close and supportive team who share a passion for helping people cope with the impact of traumatic bereavement. For the right candidate, this unique role will be deeply rewarding. Successful applicants will be expected to undergo an Enhanced Level Disclosure and Barring Service check. Closing date: Tuesday 6th October (11:59pm) Likely interview date: Friday 16th October We encourage early applications as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications. About Us SEL Mind supports people with mental health problems and dementia in the boroughs of Bromley, Greenwich, Lambeth, Lewisham and Southwark. We are proud of our diverse workforce and know that our organisation is made stronger by the variety of backgrounds, experience, and ideas within it. We promote a culture of inclusion and representation, and are working hard to build a workforce that even better reflects the communities we support. SEL Mind is somewhere that you can be your authentic self without fear of discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, neurodivergence, gender, age, lived experience of mental health problems or anything else that’s part of who you are. Read more about staff benefits and why staff love working here on our website.

item.title: Programme Manager
item.description: Who we are The School Food Review is a coalition of organisations spanning charities, educational organisations, caterers, unions and academics, committed to working together to improve children’s health by reforming the school food system. The group’s work is coordinated by founder members School Food Matters, Food Foundation, Bite Back, Sustain and Chefs in Schools, and is supported by Impact on Urban Health. The School Food Review has identified three areas of action required to deliver meaningful change – equitable access, fairer funding and quality assurance. Work across these three areas is delivered through focused working groups, drawing on members of the coalition. This includes public campaigning, advocacy and policy development. About Chefs in Schools The post will be hosted by Chefs in Schools; a charity that exists to improve children’s health and futures through better school food and meaningful food education. We work alongside schools and catering teams to transform what children eat every day, particularly in communities facing the greatest barriers to good health. We combine practical support, training, operational expertise and sector influence to help schools serve fresh, nutritious food that children want to eat. We’re backed by some of the biggest names in food and are ambitious about both impact and scale. We want every child, everywhere, to have access to excellent school food and a real food education. We are a values-led organisation - bold, honest, collaborative, innovative and focused on solutions. About you and the role The purpose of this role is to plan, coordinate and oversee the work of our coalition, the School Food Review, to ensure that we are maximising the potential of the skills and expertise we can draw on from members and driving meaningful impact. You will lead the School Food Review’s Operational Group ('Ops Group'), made up of personnel from key organisations funded to work on the School Food Review, to ensure that the coalition delivers on its mission. Whilst employed by Chefs in Schools, your role will be focused within the coalition. Day to day, you will project manage operational delivery across the School Food Review coalition, ensuring efficient and effective delivery against the agreed work plan, which you will be monitoring and developing in consultation with your colleagues in the Ops Group. You will ensure that the Governance Group and broader coalition membership are kept informed of progress, promptly flagging risks and identifying suitable mitigations. You will have an understanding of the context that we operate in (education and food sectors) and a high-level understanding of the type of work that is being delivered (eg policy, campaigning and advocacy). You will have strong programme and project management expertise. Your expertise in this area will be combined with strong people skills, and the ability to manage effective partnerships with external organisations. Experience of working with a coalition, or in partnership with multiple organisations, is crucial. The responsibilities, skills and experience listed below are intended to give you an idea of what we need for this role. If you don’t meet every single requirement, but feel as though you would be able to work with us to deliver the majority of them, we would urge you to apply anyway. We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and for us the most important ‘experience’ is passion for our mission. You may be just the right candidate for this, or other roles. Key responsibilities: ● Attend workstream meetings to support the development of plans. ● Seek input on planning from workstream leads and the Ops Group, gaining approval from the Governance Group and buy-in from the wider coalition. ● Manage delivery of the work plan to timelines, working in partnership with the workstreams and supporting them to remain effective. ● Manage the development of new delivery and workstreams, ensuring these align with the agreed framework from the Governance Group. ● Ensure measurable actions from the DEI Action Plan are delivered and embedded across the coalition’s work, including workstreams, work plans and evaluation. ● Ensure all workstreams regularly communicate progress and updates to the Ops Group and wider coalition. ● Work with the evaluation team to complete quarterly learning sessions and embed findings back into the work of the coalition. ● Plan and chair regular Ops Group meetings. ● Report regularly to the Governance Group on progress, helping to plan effective Governance Group meetings through timely, insightful reporting. ● Lead all liaison with the Chair of the coalition. ● Prepare budgets and forecasts for sign-off by the Governance Group, and manage and track all coalition spend. ● Prepare six-monthly funder reports to keep funders up to date with progress. ● Oversee effective member communications, including monthly newsletters and bi-monthly membership meetings to drive engagement. ● Lead targeted membership engagement to support specific workstreams as required, and onboard new members. ● Coordinate sign-off for coalition-wide reports, documents and materials, ensuring a consistent tone and adherence to brand guidelines. ● Ensure all coalition-related events are coordinated and delivered to a high standard. ● Keep in touch with external partners and the wider environment to understand issues affecting the sector. ● Represent the School Food Review in wider sector settings when required. Skills & experience: ● You have significant experience working in coalitions, partnerships or other multi-organisation settings. ● You have an interest in and belief in our mission to improve child health through better food and food education in schools. ● You have an understanding of the school food, education, public health or related policy environment. ● You have strong project or programme management experience, ideally involving multiple organisations, workstreams and competing priorities. ● You are highly organised and methodical, strong on detail, and able to plan ahead, manage deadlines and keep others on track. ● You are confident managing senior stakeholders, building consensus and navigating differing views and priorities. ● You are an excellent writer and communicator, with strong presentation, facilitation and meeting-management skills. ● You are skilled at building rapport and trusted relationships, while striking the right balance between being supportive and challenging. ● You have sound judgement and are comfortable working with governance structures, preparing clear information for decision-making and following through on agreed actions. Benefits You would be joining a friendly, supportive team who work hard, but believe in a healthy work/life balance. We seek a diverse range of perspectives, skills, experience and knowledge. Joining a small, collaborative team means you’ll be able to contribute to, and draw on, a variety of projects and strategic insights. ● 33 days (pro-rata for part-time positions) of holiday per year including bank holidays ● Four day working week in summer ● Pension scheme with 4% employer contribution ● Cycle to Work scheme ● Hybrid working ● Free access to the CODE app for discounted restaurants & hospitality venues ● Enhanced parental leave ● £250 allowance towards elective training and development ● Bupa Dental Insurance ● Income Protection Insurance ● Access to the AIG Smart Health Platform offering free rapid access online GP appointments, counselling, and wellbeing support First interview on either 5th or 6th November. Final interview on Friday 13th November afternoon - this interview will be in person and involve preparing and delivering a presentation to a small panel

item.title: Poppy Appeal Finance Officer
item.description: Poppy Appeal Finance Officer Royal British Legion City of London, London (On-site) £19,921 per annum pro rata, inclusive of London Supplement (£33,202 FTE) Permanent Job description Are you an organised finance professional with excellent attention to detail and a passion for supporting a meaningful cause? We are looking for a Poppy Appeal Finance Officer to join our dedicated Poppy Appeal Finance team on a part time basis. This role plays an important part in ensuring Poppy Appeal income is processed accurately, recorded correctly and managed in line with robust financial controls. Working closely with colleagues across Finance, Fundraising and Poppy Appeal Operations, you will help provide the financial administration and operational support that underpins one of the UK's most recognised fundraising campaigns. As Poppy Appeal Finance Officer, you will support the accurate processing and reconciliation of Poppy Appeal income, maintaining high quality financial records and helping to ensure reliable reporting. You will be responsible for a range of finance administration activities, contributing to the smooth and effective delivery of the Poppy Appeal. Reporting to the Poppy Appeal Finance manager, key responsibilities will include: - Process and record Poppy Appeal income accurately - Complete reconciliations of income records and financial transactions - Perform routine financial checks, validations and data quality reviews - Investigate and resolve routine discrepancies - Maintain accurate financial records, databases and spreadsheets - Support the preparation of financial reports and management information - Respond to finance-related queries from internal stakeholders in a professional and timely manner You will have experience of processing and reconciling financial transactions, along with strong numeracy skills and a keen eye for detail. You will be comfortable working with finance systems, Excel and databases, and will enjoy collaborating with colleagues while managing your own workload effectively. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a busy, purpose-driven environment where accuracy, teamwork and continuous improvement are valued. Join us and help ensure the success of the Poppy Appeal, supporting the work that makes a real difference to the Armed Forces community. This is a permamnent part time position, working 21 hours across 3 days per week. You will be contracted to our London, Haig House, Hub with a minimum expectation of one day per week - must be Tuesday - working in person at the Hub and flexibility for working remotely/at home when not on site. The successful candidate will be required to undertake a DBS check as part of pre employment checks process. Employee benefits include – - 28 day’s paid holiday (plus bank holidays) increasing with service, with optional annual leave purchase scheme of up to 5 working days - Enhanced paid maternity, paternity and adoption leave - Generous pension scheme with employer contributions ranging from 6% to 14%, depending on length of service - Range of flexible working options may be available, depending on your role - Employee Assistance Programme providing confidential counselling, financial and legal advice - Range of courses delivered by learning specialists to support your development goals and objectives - Opportunities to volunteer - Travel loans, Cycle to Work, and more! For more detailed information about the role, please see the Job Description attached to our direct advert. Our teams take a personalised approach to shortlisting, which is carried out without the use of AI and is based on the evidence provided in your application against the essential and desirable criteria in the Person Specification. RBL is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive organisation, reflecting the diversity of the armed forces community and of wider society. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and personal characteristics. As part of our commitment to inclusion, we offer interview schemes for candidates who declare an Armed Forces connection and/or a disability. However, candidates are only eligible for this scheme if their application clearly demonstrates that they meet all of the essential criteria listed in the Person Specification for the role. Interview Date: Tuesday 13th October, to be held at London Office, Haig House, Borough High Street We may close this vacancy early if we believe we have enough strong applications to be able to successfully fill the role. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. Posted on: 24 September 2026 Closing date: 09 October 2026 at 01:00 Job ref: 1344 Tags: Finance

item.title: Marketing & Communications Manager
item.description: Job title: Marketing & Communications Manager Location: Hexham, hybrid working will be considered. Hours: Full-time, with some weekend and out of hours working Reports to: Head of Income Generation Salary £35,000 per annum Tynedale Hospice at Home is a well-established charity of over 30 years. We’re here to provide high quality care and support to the approximately 70,000 residents of West Northumberland, Tynedale, and Ponteland. We offer wraparound home-based care and support for adults with palliative needs or undergoing treatment for life-limiting conditions and people of all ages needing pre or post-bereavement support. Join us as Marketing & Communications Manager at a defining moment for Tynedale Hospice at Home. We’re at the start of a new 10-year strategy, with brand development at its heart, and this role will play a central part in shaping how we tell our story, grow our reach and make a lasting impact on the people and families we support. You’ll lead the storytelling, campaigns and channels that raise our profile and drive vital supporter engagement, developing integrated marketing and communications plans that boost awareness, improve access to our care services, recruit and retain supporters, and amplify fundraising activity across digital, print and community touchpoints. This is a hands-on, strategic role where your creativity and data-led approach will directly increase income and deepen community connections. As the lead communicator for a small Hospice at a pivotal point in its history, you’ll have real scope to shape our brand, test new ideas, and see the measurable impact of your work on the people and families we support. This role is perfect for you if: You love turning impact into clear, compelling stories that motivate action. You enjoy planning and delivering multi‑channel campaigns from brief to delivery. You’re comfortable with both creative production and performance analysis. You like working closely with fundraising, programmes and senior staff in a small team. You want to see your work directly support local people and services. You’d relish the chance to help shape a brand and strategy that will define the Hospice for the next 10 years. What you’ll be doing: Playing a key role in our brand development work, helping translate our new 10-year strategy into a clear, compelling identity across everything we do. Developing and owning an integrated marketing & communications plan to support organisational goals across fundraising and Hospice services. Planning and delivering multi‑channel campaigns (digital, email, PR, print, events) that drive awareness, acquisition and retention. Creating and commissioning written, visual and video content that communicates impact and donor journeys. Managing website content, social channels, email marketing and paid digital activity; monitoring performance and optimising campaigns. Collaborating with Fundraising to design supporter communications, stewardship materials and campaign briefs. Managing external suppliers, volunteers and budgets; ensuring brand consistency and compliance. What we’re looking for: 3+ years’ experience in marketing/communications, ideally with charity or fundraising experience. Strong copywriting, content production and campaign management skills. Practical experience with CMS, email platforms, social media and analytics tools. Creative, organised and data‑focused with the ability to prioritise and deliver to deadlines. Excellent interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach. Why join us? Join us at a pivotal moment for the Hospice — help shape the brand, voice and profile that will carry our new 10-year strategy forward. Play a central role in shaping our public profile and increasing vital income for, and awareness of, local Hospice care. A visible, strategic position with freedom to innovate, test new approaches and leave a lasting mark on how we’re known. Opportunities for professional development and varied hands‑on experience. Flexible working and meaningful, direct impact on patients and families. Closing date: 9am 12 October Interviews: w/c 19 October

item.title: Community Organiser - Southampton
item.description: Are you passionate about supporting communities to create lasting change? Do you believe that people most affected by climate breakdown, nature loss and inequality should have the power to shape the decisions that affect their lives? Friends of the Earth is looking for a Community Organiser to work alongside local communities, activists and our local action groups to build power, develop leadership and support community-led campaigns that achieve meaningful local change. This is an exciting opportunity to help strengthen grassroots organising locally, supporting people to come together around shared priorities and take action on the issues that matter most to them. Key Skills and Attributes: You’ll be skilled in: Relationship Building: Able to build trusted relationships with diverse communities, partner organisations, activists and decision-makers, engaging people around shared priorities and creating inclusive spaces for participation. Community Organising and Campaigning: Ability to support communities to identify issues, build collective power and develop campaigns that influence decision-makers and deliver meaningful local change. Facilitation and Leadership Development: Skilled in facilitating meetings, workshops and community activities, with the ability to develop the confidence, skills and leadership of others through training, mentoring and support. The team: The England team is at the heart of grassroots organising at Friends of the Earth and is responsible for supporting nearly 200 Local Action Groups across England to build power and campaign for change. Closing date: Wednesday 21st October 2026 (23:59). Hours: Full time (30 hours over 4 days) Location: Southampton- Homebased Please note we only accept applications via the Friends of the Earth Application System. We offer a competitive range of benefits, good work/life balance including a 4-day working week with no loss of pay, excellent learning and development opportunities and a vibrant organisational culture. Our staff body is currently under-representative of People of Colour, LGBTQIA+ people and people with long term conditions or impairments. We are committed to eroding these historic barriers, so as to create a movement in which people from all walks of life see themselves in, and so we particularly encourage you to apply if you belong to one of these groups or sit at multiple intersections of disadvantage. We are committed to the Disability Confident standard and will guarantee an interview to any candidates who declare a disability and who meet the essential criteria for the role. Friends of the Earth staff who publicly represent Friends of the Earth (including all campaigners) are not allowed to also represent a political party. This is to ensure that there can be no confusion in the minds of the public about Friends of the Earth's party-political independence . Affected staff should also seek permission from the Senior Management Team if they wish to hold a non-public facing official role in a political party. If this is an issue, please do raise this with us as soon as possible. Friends of the Earth is an international community dedicated to protecting the natural world and the wellbeing of everyone in it. We lead campaigns, provide resources and information, and drive real solutions to the environmental problems facing us all.

item.title: Interim PR and Communications Manager (12-month maternity cover)
item.description: Job description Variety is looking for a PR and Communications Manager to join our successful fundraising and communications team for FTC maternity cover. This role includes management of internal and external communication channels at Variety including the website, supporter newsletters, social media and PR. Leading on brand and design, you will oversee freelance support during busy periods including photographers and filmmakers. This role leads and manages brand design on Canva, short film editing and works with the Director of Communications on PR. The PR and Communications Manager is key to achieving Variety’s mission to fund life-changing practical support to disabled and disadvantaged children and young people across the UK. You will be joining the charity at an exciting time as Variety is launching a new three-year strategy and you will play a key role in our collaborative and high-performing team. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES ● Lead the planning, creation and delivery of engaging content across Variety's communications channels. ● Manage the website content, ensuring information remains accurate, accessible and on brand. ● Work with the website developers to deliver improvements and SEO optimisation. ● Manage Variety’s social media content and calendar to ensure children’s voices are at the heart of our storytelling. ● Manage email marketing, including the supporter newsletter on Dot Digital working with the team to grow our mailing list. ● Gather case studies that demonstrate Variety’s impact, working closely with the programmes delivery team and the families we support. ● Oversee Variety’s brand ensuring communications are accessible and consistent with style and tone of voice. ● Work with the Director of Fundraising and Communications to develop and deliver integrated marketing and brand awareness campaigns. ● Review and proof communications produced across the organisation. ● Manager external freelance staff as needed, writing briefs and overseeing work including photographers, filmmakers, PR professionals and designers. ● Write and oversee press releases, responding to media enquiries. ● Monitor, analyse and report on digital communications performance using insights to improve email open rates, content and audience engagement. ● Manage the Senior Social Media Officer overseeing objectives, holding 1-1s and annual appraisals. ● Produce creative assets on Canva to support fundraising and campaigns. ● Attend Variety events, partner schools and community groups to capture engaging content, maximising engagement and representing the charity. ● Store and manage digital assets and the photo library, keeping records and consent up-to-date on the CRM (Salesforce), and manage the communications inbox. ● Participate in staff meetings, fundraising and programmes meetings and contribute to the success of Variety’s strategy. SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES Essential • Experience working in a communications role in the Third Sector • Experience of copywriting, editing and communicating a case for support • Experience managing digital channels and creating content for social media • Experience working with beneficiaries and producing case studies • Experience planning and delivering integrated digital campaigns • Knowledge of digital analytics and creating reports to measure data • Enthusiastic, energetic, self-motivated and passionate about the Third Sector • Knowledge of Canva and Dot Digital or a similar marketing platform • Experience of Adobe Premiere Pro MAIN BENEFITS, TERMS AND CONDITIONS 25 days holiday (we also normally give between Christmas and New Year off, but this is not contractual). In addition, after one year's continuous service, there will be an extra 2 days annual holiday for every complete year of service, up to a maximum of five days' extra holiday. Pension 7%, Life Assurance 4% of annual salary, Company sick pay scheme, medical cover. HOW TO APPLY Please submit your CV with a cover letter explaining why you would make a great candidate for this role and how you meet the job description. Please note, as this is an urgent requirement interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis as soon as suitable applications come in. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible if the role looks of interest. Applications will close at 12noon on Friday, 2 October 2026.

item.title: Gift Operations and Fundraising Data Analyst
item.description: Gift Operations and Fundraising Data Analyst Salary: £34,500 Contract type: Full-time, 35 hours per week, although 28 hours / flexible hours may be considered Contract length: Permanent Working location: Remote. The postholder must attend the office at least once a month. This role may involve some irregular travel throughout England and Scotland. Reporting to: Head of Individual Giving and Engagement BACKGROUND For more than 20 years, we’ve worked alongside schools and communities across Englandand Scotland, listening to children and young people and campaigning with decision makers to ensure their voices are heard. We’re working to create the conditions every pupilneeds to start the day feeling nourished, valued, and empowered to reach for their dreams. Every child and young person should arrive at school hungry to learn, not distracted by arumbling tummy. Yet 2.2 million children across the UK are at risk of going hungry in themorning. That’s five pupils in every class of 30. Breakfast is about so much more than food;it’s about giving children and young people the energy, focus, and confidence to learn,thrive, and dream big. Working with schools in disadvantaged communities across Englandand Scotland, Magic Breakfast is a charity that helps every child and young person reachfor the dreams, one breakfast at a time. Our mission is simple: to champion and provide nourishing breakfasts, ensuring every childand young person has the best possible start to their day. But we know we cannot do this alone. Ending hunger takes all of us; schools, communities, families, policymakers, supporters, and partners, coming together to make sure every pupil has what they need to thrive. By joining Magic Breakfast, you will become part of a passionate, ambitious organisation driving lasting change for children and young people across the UK. The Gift Operations and Fundraising Data Analyst will play a key role in ensuring the accuracy, efficiency, and insightfulness of our fundraising operations. By managing the flow of gift data, maintaining and improving the quality of our Individual Giving CRM records, and delivering data-driven analysis, this role supports Individual Giving and Engagement and the wider Fundraising team in achieving income targets and enhancing supporter engagement. The postholder will act as the bridge between data and strategy – ensuring that every gift is accurately recorded, every donor is thanked, and every decision is backed by meaningful insight. The postholder will make sure donor records are accurate, gifts are processed quickly and ensure we maximise income through Gift Aid. Through strong collaboration with teams across Fundraising, Finance, and Individual Giving and Engagement, this role will help drive both operational excellence and innovation in how we use data to grow our impact. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Coordinate monthly fundraising KPI reporting and reconciliation across Fundraising & Development, holding team members accountable to deadlines. Identify opportunities to improve fundraising insight, efficiency, opportunities and decision-making through automation, AI-enabled tools and more effective use of data. Support the team and wider department in KPI analysis, including working with colleagues across Magic Breakfast, such as Brand and Marketing, to assess how insights from their work impact fundraising. Support the department with monitoring and evaluation projects for reporting to funders or to enable strategic work, where appropriate. Perform A/B testing analysis and share insights to improve email and campaign effectiveness. Process reporting for all income, including text, website, postal, standing orders, direct debits, payroll giving, JustGiving, and more. Ensure all gifts are accurately logged in Salesforce to maintain up-to-date dashboards and supporter records. Support the Head of Individual Giving and Engagement with data selection and segmentation for supporter communications and appeals. Work on data requirements for strategic initiatives such as Sustainability X. For full role details please click the job description below APPLICATION PROCCESS Should you wish to discuss the role before applying please email our People and Culture Team (recruitment @ magicbreakfast .com) Application close date: 11th October Shortlisting: 12th, 13,th 14th October Interview 1: 19th October (afternoon), 20th October (all day) - online interviews Interview: 27th October (online) Due to the high volume of applications, this role is likely to close early and we reserve the right to do so. Do you have resilience & adaptability? Can you work effectively with a focus on customer service and care? Our competitive rewards and benefits package includes: Flexible Working Options : Including hybrid working. Generous Annual Leave : 28 days plus Bank Holidays, increasing to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave. Birthday Leave : An extra day off for your birthday. Pension Plan : 5% employer contribution. Enhanced Allowances : Enhanced sick pay, maternity, and paternity payments. About the role As an Independent Domestic Violence Advocate you will be supporting high risk victims of domestic abuse, who live in Cumbria. This role will be part of our other wider specialist services covering Cumbria. As an IDVA you will be: Providing a high quality support and advocacy service to victims of domestic abuse. Managing a caseload; identifying and assessing risks and needs, providing a tailored crisis intervention service trough individual safety planning, advocacy, emotional and practical support. Working with other agencies and advocating on behalf of service users in order to help them access services to keep them safe. Working within a multi-agency framework consisting of partners as well as MARAC and other local partnerships to offer a coordinated response to domestic abuse. Promoting the service and raise awareness of domestic abuse through the delivery of training. You will need: Experience of working in support and advocacy with victims of domestic abuse is advantageous To be able to prioritise work and deal with competing or conflicting demands/needs and interests and promote organisation interests and values. To ideally hold a Safe Lives IDVA accreditation or work towards the qualification, relevant degree, vocational qualification or relevant experience of delivering a service and working with domestic abuse victim's/service users in a statutory, voluntary or community work setting. Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details. About Us Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. item.title: Multiple Disadvantage Independent Sexual Violence Advocate (Female Applicants Only)
item.description: About the role The Independent Sexual Violence Advocate (Multiple Disadvantage) provides specialist advocacy and support to women who have experienced sexual violence alongside multiple and intersecting forms of disadvantage. Working within WGN's Intersectional Anti-Oppressive Team, you will empower survivors to understand their rights, make informed choices and access the support they need. You will provide trauma-informed advocacy throughout the criminal justice process, while working closely with partner agencies to improve safety, wellbeing and outcomes for survivors. Grounded in feminist, anti-oppressive and survivor-centred practice, this role places survivors' voices, choices and experiences at the heart of support. Job description As the Independent Sexual Violence Advocate (Multiple Disadvantage), you will: Provide trauma-informed emotional support, practical assistance and advocacy to survivors of sexual violence experiencing multiple and intersecting disadvantages. Undertake risk and needs assessments, develop support plans and promote the safety and wellbeing of survivors and their children. Support survivors to access specialist services including housing, mental health, healthcare, legal advice and therapeutic support. Advocate for survivors throughout the criminal justice process, ensuring they understand their rights, options and available remedies. Build effective partnerships with statutory and voluntary sector organisations to strengthen coordinated support and improve outcomes. Maintain accurate case records, monitoring data and safeguarding practices in line with organisational and legislative requirements. Deliver awareness-raising, service promotion and partnership engagement activities to improve understanding of survivors' needs. Contribute to service development, best practice and continuous improvement across the ISVA Service. Champion WGN's feminist values and Holistic Empowerment Recovery Model, helping survivors move towards safety, recovery and empowerment. Closing date and interviews This vacancy will close at 11:59pm on Monday 26 October 2026 . Interviews will take place shortly thereafter, and shortlisted candidates will be notified of the arrangements. We encourage early applications, as we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised closing date should we receive a high volume of applications or identify a suitable candidate. Interviews may be conducted either in person or remotely, depending on panel availability and logistical requirements. About us Women and Girls Network (WGN) is a pan-London organisation that supports women and girls affected by all forms of gendered-based violence. Our overall aim is to promote, preserve and restore the mental health and well-being of women and girls who have experienced, or are at risk of, gendered-based violence, whilst working towards a society free of gendered-based violence. We do this by: Providing women-only holistic and seamless therapeutic services, which meet women and girls’ needs and contribute to total and sustainable recovery from the experiences of violence. Evidencing the impact of gendered-based violence and presenting this information in appropriate forums to affect social change in attitudes towards, and responses to, gendered-based violence. Developing good practice in the sector by providing training and guidance on specialist service provision and the development of culturally appropriate service delivery. WGN is proud to be an accredited Living Wage Employer and a member of The London VAWG Consortium, Halo Code, and Helplines Partnership. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion We are deeply committed to building a workforce that reflects the diversity, resilience and strength of the women and girls we serve. We strongly encourage applications from Black and Global Majority women and applicants with Lived Experience, including those who may not meet every criterion. WGN is an equal opportunities employer. Exemption This post is exempt under the Equality Act 2010, Schedule 9, Part 1 , and is open to female applicants only , due to the nature of the role.

Generous Annual Leave : 28 days plus Bank Holidays, increasing to 33 days plus Bank Holidays, with options to buy or sell annual leave. Birthday Leave : An extra day off for your birthday. Pension Plan : 5% employer contribution. Enhanced Allowances : Enhanced sick pay, maternity, and paternity payments. Exclusive Discounts : High Street, retail, holiday, gym, entertainment, and leisure discounts. Financial Wellbeing : Access to our financial wellbeing hub and salary-deducted finance. Wellbeing Support : Employee assistance programme and wellbeing support. Inclusive Networks : Access to EDI networks and colleague cafes. Sustainable Travel : Cycle to work scheme and season ticket loans. Career Development : Ongoing training and support with opportunities for career progression. About the role This role will work across Staffordshire and Stoke on Trent. Hybrid working will be considered following successful completion of probationary period. Travel across the whole of Staffordshire will be required. As an IDVA you will be asked to: Provide a pro-active, high quality, frontline service to victims of domestic abuse through on-going risk assessment, individual safety planning, advocacy, emotional and practical support. Work within a multi-agency framework consisting of the MARAC and local partnership responses to domestic abuse to keep safety central to all services for victims of domestic abuse Promoting the service and raising awareness of issues arising, minimising barriers and improving access to support You will need: Experience of providing support those affected by domestic abuse Experience of undertaking need and risk assessments and creating safety plans Experience of the MARAC and other partnership processes Experience of multi agency working Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details. About Us Victim Support is an independent charity dedicated to supporting people affected by crime and traumatic incidents in England and Wales. We put them at the heart of our organisation and our support and campaigns are informed and shaped by them and their experiences. Victim Support are committed to recruiting with care and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Background checks and Disclosed Barring Service checks may be required. At Victim Support, we're proud to celebrate diversity and create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. We're committed to being an antiracist organisation, and we actively welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those from Black and Asian and other minoritised communities. As a Disability Confident Employer, we will offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet all essential criteria for a job where it is practicable to do so. We are also happy to make reasonable adjustments during the recruitment and selection process. How to apply To apply for this role please follow the link below to the Jobs page on our website and complete the application form demonstrating how you meet the essential shortlisting criteria. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, if we receive enough suitable applications to take forward to interview prior to the published closing date. If you have already registered & started an application, then we will contact you to advise of the amended closing date wherever possible.

item.title: Lead Youth Advocate
item.description: Location: Cheshire West and Chester, hybrid with regular travel Contract: Temporary, 3 months Hours: Part-time, 28 hours per week Pay: £16.77 per hour (+ £2.02 holiday pay) Start Date: ASAP Prospectus is delighted to be supporting our client, a national children's charity, in the search for a temporary Lead Youth Advocate . This role provides a fantastic opportunity for an experienced youth work professional to make an immediate and meaningful difference in an impactful organisation, supporting children and young people to ensure their voices are heard and their rights are upheld. Please note that will the role is based around Chester and West Cheshire, the successful candidate must attend induction in Wythenshawe, Greater Manchester. This role also requires a valid driving licence and access to your own vehicle (with travel expensed). Please also be aware that this role will be subject to an enhanced DBS check due to the requirement to interact with vulnerable children unsupervised. Key Responsibilities: Manage a caseload of advocacy cases, providing high-quality, child-centred support to children and young people. Deliver advocacy support to ensure children and young people's voices, wishes and feelings are heard and represented in decisions affecting their lives. Support children and young people to understand their rights, options and entitlements, enabling them to participate in decision-making processes. Provide day-to-day guidance, mentoring and practice support to team members, volunteers and student placements. Assess, triage and allocate referrals, ensuring an appropriate and timely response based on need, risk and complexity. Monitor caseloads, service demand and emerging risks, escalating concerns where appropriate. Promote safe practice by identifying, assessing and responding to safeguarding concerns in line with relevant procedures and legislation. Support quality assurance activities, including case audits, record reviews and performance monitoring, to maintain high standards of service delivery. Build and maintain positive relationships with local authorities, partner organisations and other stakeholders to improve outcomes for children and young people. Contribute to service development, continuous improvement initiatives and the promotion of advocacy services and children's rights. Maintain accurate records, reports and case documentation in line with organisational, safeguarding and data protection requirements. Key Requirements: Recent, relevant experience in a similar role, with excellent knowledge of advocacy, safeguarding, and relevant legislation. High level of organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to build strong stakeholder relationships. Collaborative and proactive approach, with the capability to work both independently and in a team. CVs will be reviewed on a rolling basis so if you're interested, please apply ASAP with your CV in Word format. At Prospectus, we believe recruitment should be human-led and we are committed to supporting you throughout your application journey. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on age, gender, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, marital status, or pregnancy/maternity. While AI may be used to support our administrative process, all applications are reviewed by people and all hiring decisions are made by experienced recruiters.

item.title: Training Coordinator
item.description: Birthrights is the UK’s leading charity championing respectful, rights-based maternity care. We believe every woman and birthing person has the right to dignified, personalised care throughout pregnancy and childbirth. As our Training Co-ordinator you will coordinate and deliver Birthrights' human rights in maternity care training across England and Wales, working closely with the Training Manager and overseeing Associate Trainers. Our Training Coordinators possess confident facilitation skills, with the ability to hold inclusive, anti-oppressive, trauma-informed space, and have knowledge of human rights law and healthcare law; particularly how the law applies to pregnancy and childbirth. The role includes the following responsibilities: Training Delivery, Coordination and Preparation : manage end-to-end training logistics and maintain strong communication with Associate Trainers and Organisers. Impact Assessment and Evaluation : develop and embed measurable ways to evaluate training impact and outcomes for participants and maternity service users Communication Management and Team Support: work within the small and remote Birthrights' Training team, whilst also working closely with the Advice and Campaigns teams to ensure insights and trends inform training content. Please see our website for a full job description. Who we're looking for: We're looking for a team player who has a track record of working in training development or delivery, and someone who will show commitment to our values, inclusion, and to working on their own biases and beliefs. Do you consider yourself to be a self-starter, possessing the curiosity to investigate new opportunities and relationships and make recommendations without being asked? Are you highly organised and confident using digital tools such as Zoom and Microsoft Office, and can flex easily between strategic and hands-on tasks? If your communication skills are excellent both verbally and in writing, and you are able to communicate with a wide variety of stakeholders from healthcare professionals to community members, with sensitivity and empathy - this could be the role for you. We'd love it if you had an understanding of the nature of oppression and a specific understanding of anti-Black racism and how it manifests itself in society, coupled with a commitment to challenge the systems of oppression and injustice. Equally we welcome applicants with knowledge of the inequalities and barriers faced within maternity care systems, or people who can demonstrate equivalent knowledge through lived experience, self-directed learning, or community-based work. Please note we will not ask you to disclose details of your lived experience at any point during the recruitment process. Application deadline: Thursday 22nd October 2026 at 12:00pm Online Interview dates: Monday 23rd and Thursday 26th November 2026 Please click the 'Redirect to Recruiter' button below, to find our full job pack and further information about how to apply on our website.

item.title: Support and Development Worker
item.description: Job description Role overview Shine supports a community of over 15,000 members living with spina bifida and/or hydrocephalus, including 10,000 adults (25+). You will be delivering high-quality support and creating opportunities for adults living with spina bifida and/or hydrocephalus and their carers, supporting Shine members to lead healthy, independent, and fulfilling lives by improving condition management and fostering connections within the Shine community. This role will focus on adults (25+), you will be primarily working within the Adult Services Team. However, there will be occasions when you will work across age groups to ensure the best outcomes for our members. The role is home-based, but you will attend clinics in Shropshire, Staffordshire, Derbyshire, Nottingham, Warwickshire and Hertfordshire as required. There would be occasional travel required across wider areas and nationally including attendance at events, conferences and meetings at our head office in Peterborough. The role is part time 21 hours per week, 3 days a week to include Wednesdays. Core working hours are 9am-5pm with some flexibility to cover events evenings/weekends. Key Responsibilities Provide information, advice, and guidance to our adult members and carers, including hard-to-reach communities. Support members to access benefits, services, and resources that promote financial stability, health, and independence. Represent Shine at conferences, provide information, raise awareness among professionals, external organisations, and the public through presentations and training. item.description: Job Title: Child-Focused Court Independent Domestic Violence Advocate (Child-Focused Court IDVA) X2 Location: Warwickshire Salary: £28,419.73 per annum Contract type: Full Time, Permanent Hours: 37.5 hours per week We are looking for two skilled, values driven IDVAs who are committed to challenging inequality, reducing harm, and improving safety for adults and children affected by domestic abuse. You will bring relevant professional experience, strong skills in assessment, engagement, safety planning and communication, and the ability to work safely in complex and high risk situations. We are seeking people who can hold clear boundaries and accountability while offering empathy, curiosity and respect. You will work in a trauma informed, survivor centred and strengths based way, recognising each survivor as the expert in their own life. You will understand how gendered power, oppression and structural barriers shape survivors’ experiences, and you will be confident applying these principles in your practice. item.title: Operations Assistant
item.description: Accountable to: Operations Manager Hours: 37.5 hours per week (with some evening and weekend hours where necessary) Contract type: Permanent Salary: £25,500 plus Cambridge Living Allowance of £2301 a year. Location: Baca office, Cambridge, England with regular travel to Cambridge and locations of service delivery. Help Change Young Lives At Baca, we support young people who have fled war, persecution, and trafficking, providing safe housing, education, and therapeutic care to help them rebuild their lives. We are looking for an Operations Assistant to provide effective administrative and operational support across Baca. Working closely with the Operations Manager and teams across the organisation, you will help ensure that our systems, processes, resources, premises and equipment are well managed so that staff can deliver safe, effective and high-quality services to young people. Key Responsibilities Provide administrative and operational support across Baca’s services and departments. Maintain effective systems, records, processes and resources to support safe and efficient service delivery. Coordinate day-to-day operational needs, including premises, supplies, equipment, utilities and procurement. Provide basic IT support, including laptop setup and troubleshooting hardware and software issues. Support staff, volunteers and young people by ensuring they have the information and resources they need. Liaise with suppliers and external stakeholders to meet operational requirements. Support audits, inspections, quality assurance and compliance with relevant standards, regulations and organisational policies. Identify and report operational issues and risks, contributing to continuous improvement. Work collaboratively across teams and in line with Baca’s values, safeguarding requirements and policies. About You You will be a highly organised, practical and dependable individual who enjoys supporting others and getting things done. You will be confident managing routine administration while responding effectively to changing priorities and unexpected operational needs. You will have a positive, collaborative approach, strong attention to detail and the ability to communicate clearly and sensitively with colleagues, young people, suppliers and external stakeholders. You will be committed to safeguarding and to creating safe, welcoming and inclusive environments for young people who have experienced migration, trauma and displacement. What We Offer The chance to make a meaningful difference A supportive, values-driven team 33 days’ holiday (pro rata), pension, wellbeing support, and more How to Apply If you are passionate about creating lasting change for young people, we would love to hear from you. Please note: You must have the right to work in the UK. A full UK driving licence, or a licence that legally allows you to drive in the UK, is desirable for this role as it involves regular travel to Baca properties and the procurement and transportation of items required to support service delivery, activities and operational requirements. Successful candidates will be asked to apply for an Enhanced DBS Certificate including a check of the children’s barred list.

item.title: Prevention Officer - London & South East
item.description: Prevention Officer - London & South East The Children's Society £29,155 per annum Temporary Job description Youth Impact Advert Fixed Term until 31st March 2027 35 hours per week £29,155 per annum Location: Mobile worker (Home-based) Benefits include but not limited to: -36 days' annual leave, inclusive of flexible bank holidays, increasing with length of service -Enhanced maternity/paternity leave -We match up to 8% pension -Free counselling service -Opportunities to develop and widen your skills -2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us: The Children's Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. Our Youth Impact domain creates impact for children and young people. With highly skilled and experienced staff working across England and Wales, we provide direct support to children, young people, parents and carers, as well as conduct research and influence Government to make changes. We also provide training for professionals. Our value driven team change the lives of children in this country for the better — and with your help and expertise, tomorrow we can support even more. About the role: You'll play a key part in our national Prevention Programme, developing and delivering regional and national learning sessions, workshops and resources for multi-agency audiences, leading systems change projects and contributing to the development of local and regional strategies in order to improve practice and explore new approaches to preventing and tackling child exploitation and abuse. This is a unique opportunity to influence and learn from both practice on the ground and at strategic levels including statutory and third sector organisations, the government and businesses. We're looking for a dedicated and skilled Prevention Officer with the ability to drive forward systems change work to better prevent and improve response to child exploitation and abuse across London and Southeast, making a real impact in the lives of children and young people. Experience: -Multi-agency working, for example with statutory and voluntary sector partners. -Working within and managing effective and innovative projects or services for vulnerable children. -Developing and delivering learning sessions or problem-solving workshops to different audiences. Skills & knowledge: -Sound understanding of child and adolescent development, trauma, exploitation, trafficking and modern slavery. -Commitment to diversity, inclusion and anti-racist ways of working. -Strong planning, organisational, communication and partnership skills. It would also be an advantage if you have any of the following skills and competencies: -Familiarity with local and regional police, local authority and/or health structures. -Experience of multi-agency work at a strategic level -Working within a geographically dispersed team. -Experience of incorporating children and young people's voices to inform systems change work with partners. Closing date: Midnight on Sunday 11th October 2026 Interviews: Week commencing 19th October 2026 The Children's Society is committed to safeguarding and protection of the children and young people we work with. As such, our safer recruitment process includes a Basic or Enhanced DBS check, 5 years of references, and additional vetting checks relevant to the role. We have a comprehensive range of policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices across all areas of our organisation. In support of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, shortlisting is carried out on an anonymised basis. Personal details are hidden from the shortlisting panel, and candidates are referenced by a candidate number only. As part of this process, we ask that your CV is anonymised before submission - this means removing personal information such as your name, contact details, age, and any other identifying details. AI tools can support your application but only when used appropriately. You're welcome to use them to improve clarity, structure, and research. However, overuse or misuse (e.g. inventing experience or using AI during assessments) may lead to rejection at any stage. We want to hear the real you - authenticity matters. item.title: Chief Executive Officer
item.description: Position: Chief Executive Officer Charity: Harlington Hospice Location: Michael Sobell House (at Mount Vernon Hospital)/Harlington, with regular travel across sites. Hours: 37.5 hours (full time, permanent) – flexible working options can be discussed with the successful candidate. Salary: £95,000-£110,000 d.o.e About Harlington Hospice Harlington Hospice and inpatient hospice Michael Sobell House, are here to support people living with serious or terminal illness in the London Borough of Hillingdon and surrounding areas. Harlington Hospice and Michael Sobell Hospice merged operations in 2023. Merging has allowed us to join up the expertise previously spread between the two teams, and to build a more resilient organisation for the future. About the role This is a pivotal leadership role for Harlington Hospice. Reporting to the Chair and Board of Trustees, the Chief Executive will provide visible leadership across the organisation, setting strategic direction, ensuring high-quality, compassionate care, and maintaining the financial stability we have worked hard to rebuild. We are looking for a leader who is equally comfortable setting strategy at Board level and staying close to the day-to-day realities of a small, close-knit organisation. You will inherit a hospice in a stronger position than many of our peers, and your task will be to build on that foundation, growing our services, our income and our impact sustainably, without losing the culture that got us here. Role responsibilities to include: Work with the Board of Trustees to finalise and deliver the Hospice's current draft strategy developing and agreeing plans for delivery, adapting to changing healthcare, funding and regulatory environments. Provide visible, credible leadership in setting and achieving the organisation's strategic goals, policies and objectives, and in embedding our values across everything we do. Ensure the effective, efficient and safe day-to-day operation of Harlington Hospice and Michael Sobell House, across clinical, non-clinical, commercial and retail activity. Be responsible to the Board for the overall financial health of the Hospice, ensuring financial stability and an adequate level of reserves is maintained. Continue to develop and sustain diverse, structured and repeatable income streams including NHS/ statutory funding, fundraising, trading and commercial activity to support sustainable, long-term growth rather than short-term peaks. Lead, inspire and develop the Executive Team and, through them, all staff and volunteers, fostering a culture of continuous learning, professional growth and shared ownership of our mission. Protect and evolve our culture as we grow ensuring that fundraising, care and community engagement remain everybody's responsibility, not just a function of one team. Act as the principal ambassador for Harlington Hospice, building and maintaining relationships with commissioners, NHS and ICB partners, donors, corporate partners and the wider community. Person specification to include: Proven senior executive leadership experience within a CQC-regulated healthcare, hospice or not-for-profit organisation. Strong financial acumen and a demonstrable track record of building sustainable income and commercial activity. Commercially and politically astute, with strong problem-solving and risk-based decision-making skills. Outstanding communication and relationship-building skills, able to engage and influence Trustees, donors, regulators, staff, volunteers and the wider community. A deep, genuine commitment to compassionate, person-centred, end-of-life care. Committed to Harlington Hospice's values: Collaborative, Responsive, Thoughtful and Courageous. A true team player who values shared ownership and can inspire that same spirit across the organisation. Key dates: application deadline - 16th October PSR inital interivews: 19th and 20th October Harlington Hospice interviews: 4th November For a full copy of the job information pack or to have an informal chat please apply via this site.

item.title: Training and Support Manager
item.description: Help the people behind Addiction Family Support’s helpline and support services feel skilled, supported and ready for the conversations that matter. As our Training & Support Manager, you’ll shape engaging learning and reflective practice for volunteers supporting families affected by a loved one’s harmful use of alcohol, drugs or gambling. Addiction Family Support (AFS) supports adults affected or bereaved by someone else’s harmful use. Our client-facing volunteers meet people at difficult moments, often when they feel isolated or unsure where to turn. Your work will help them listen well, maintain clear boundaries and provide safe, consistent support. This is a varied maternity-cover role with two main parts. You’ll plan and deliver induction and ongoing training, bringing topics such as listening skills, safeguarding, professional boundaries and the 5-Step Method to life through discussion, case studies and skills practice. You’ll also provide reflective practice supervision for client-facing volunteers, giving them space to think through their work, recognise learning needs and manage its emotional impact. You’ll work closely with our Services Manager and colleagues across AFS, coordinate contributions from other trainers, and use feedback to keep our learning programme effective and accessible. You’ll know when a concern needs to be passed to a manager, a Designated Safeguarding Lead or someone with specialist expertise. We’re looking for someone who enjoys helping adults learn and has experience of both participative training and structured reflective practice or supervision. You’ll bring sound judgement, warmth and the confidence to give constructive feedback. Experience of supporting volunteers, working with affected family members or using the 5-Step Method would be welcome, but you do not need to have worked in all of these areas.
item.dc:creator: Addiction Family Support

item.title: Development Officer
item.description: Job description The Institute for Research in Schools (IRIS) wants to change the culture in UK education so that authentic research and innovation is part of every young person’s experience. We’re looking for a skilled and thoughtful development professional to join our small, collaborative and ambitious team as Development Officer. This hands-on role offers the opportunity to shape and strengthen IRIS’s fundraising approach by developing persuasive proposals, building funder relationships, developing major-gift opportunities and helping establish sustainable systems for future growth. Reporting to the Director, you’ll work closely with colleagues, consultants and funders to build a strong fundraising pipeline, produce compelling bids and pitches and support effective donor engagement. Your work will strengthen IRIS’s long-term sustainability and help us extend the impact of our mission. What you’ll be doing: Build and manage the fundraising pipeline, maintaining accurate prospect and opportunity records and reporting progress to Directors. Research prospective funders and relationships, producing concise intelligence and briefings to support engagement. Develop high-quality funding proposals, coordinating contributions across IRIS and aligning applications with strategic priorities. Support donor relationships and strengthen internal fundraising capability, coordinating stewardship, tracking follow-up actions and embedding sustainable systems and organisational knowledge. This is an exciting time to join IRIS as we invest in a more strategic and sustainable approach to fundraising. You’ll have the opportunity to help shape this developing function, work directly with senior colleagues and support growth in our reach and impact. We welcome applicants from diverse personal and professional backgrounds, including people living with disabilities and those from underrepresented groups. We are committed to a fair and accessible recruitment process.
