item.title: Director of Social Purpose
item.description: NEBOSH is looking for an inspirational and strategically minded Director of Social Purpose to lead the next stage of our charitable impact programme. Reporting into the Chief Strategy and Governance Officer, this is a key leadership position with the opportunity to shape and deliver an ambitious Social Purpose Strategy, extend our reach beyond qualifications and ensure that our resources, partnerships and influence create lasting, measurable benefits for people and communities around the world. As Director of Social Purpose, you will lead NEBOSH’s social purpose, charitable investment, partner engagement and impact agenda. You will help turn our charitable ambitions into meaningful action, strengthening our contribution to occupational safety, health, wellbeing and sustainability globally. About our Social Purpose Programme NEBOSH’s Social Purpose Programme is central to how we deliver our charitable mission. The programme uses our global reach, expertise and resources to help change lives by keeping people safe and healthy at work. Its priorities include reducing workplace accidents among disadvantaged groups and in industries where occupational safety and health support is limited, addressing barriers to accessing OSH education and increasing diversity and inclusion within the profession. Looking ahead, we want to deepen and broaden this work by investing in high-impact initiatives, responding to unmet needs, developing influential partnerships and demonstrating clearly the difference our work makes. Our future strategy places social purpose at the heart of NEBOSH’s ambition to extend its reach and deliver greater charitable impact. The opportunity You will provide visible and credible leadership for NEBOSH’s Social Purpose Programme, working across the organisation and with external partners to: Develop and deliver NEBOSH’s Social Purpose Strategy, aligned with our organisational strategy, charitable objectives and impact ambitions. Identify emerging needs, opportunities and gaps where NEBOSH can make a meaningful and sustainable difference. Lead a portfolio of social purpose initiatives, ensuring investment decisions are evidence-based and focused on measurable outcomes. Strengthen the governance, monitoring and evaluation of the programme, including the development of impact dashboards and annual reporting. Build strategic partnerships with charities, governments, employers, industry bodies, professional associations and academic institutions in the UK and internationally. About you We are looking for an accomplished senior leader who combines strategic thinking with the energy and credibility to turn ambition into measurable impact. You will bring: Significant senior leadership experience within a charity, social impact, ESG, public benefit, international development or a related environment. A strong track record of developing and delivering strategies that achieve demonstrable social impact. Experience of managing complex stakeholder relationships across different sectors and geographies. The ability to establish strategic partnerships and collaborative delivery models. A sound understanding of impact measurement, performance reporting and benefits realisation. Experience of leading teams and supporting organisational change. You will be an innovative and evidence-led thinker, an outstanding relationship builder and a highly credible communicator. You will be comfortable influencing at senior levels, negotiating shared priorities and creating networks that enable organisations to achieve more together. Why join NEBOSH? This is an opportunity to take on a leadership role with both organisational and global significance. You will join an organisation with an established global presence, a strong charitable mission and the ambition to use its expertise, influence and resources to protect lives today and in the future.
item.dc:creator: NEBOSH

item.title: Partnership Development Lead
item.description: Partnership Development Lead Salary: £32,005 - £34,515 per annum (Specific salary is dependent on experience - Please note that this may change as we are currently reviewing our salaries based on cost of living increase) Contract: Fixed-term for 12 months in the first instance (with the possibility of a contract extension subject to funding and business need) Start Date: As soon as possible (specific date to be agreed with consideration for your notice period) Location: This is a blended-working role with two days per week at our office in Finsbury Park (Tuesday-Thursday) during term time and the flexibility to work from home during school holidays. Occasional travel to schools and events will be required. Working Pattern : 37.5 hours per week. Our core hours are 09:30 - 16:00 from Monday to Friday. Job Purpose Established in 2011, Challenge Partners is a well-respected nationwide network of practitioners who engage in impactful collaboration and mutual accountability to ensure every school community can benefit from the combined wisdom of the education system. Schools and trusts within Challenge Partners subscribe to an annual partnership, partaking in school and trust improvement programmes, engaging in collaborative networks at local, regional and national level, and becoming a member of a national partnership of education practitioners from Cornwall to County Durham. The Partnership Development Lead will play a key role in driving growth and development within our partnership, devising and executing high impact sales and marketing plans aimed at schools and trusts new to the idea of Challenge Partners, and those considering rejoining it, that will result in accelerated growth of the partnership. Key Responsibilities Reporting to the Partnership Development Manager, the Partnership Development Lead will have the following key areas of responsibility and will be expected to undertake other responsibilities commensurate with the role: Partnership Development and Reach Collaborate closely with the Partnership Development Manager to devise and implement sales plans that align with our growth strategy and the wider educational landscape Identify and pursue campaigns in high-growth opportunity areas, using data driven research and insights into Challenge Partners’ existing relationships Build a pipeline of interested school and trust prospects through targeted activity to generate sales meetings for yourself and/or senior members of staff Contribute to the planning and delivery of strategies that enable current partners to effectively represent and endorse Challenge Partners Partner with the Marketing Team to ensure consistency of messaging across all channels and resources in line with Reach Empower colleagues across the team to confidently articulate Challenge Partners’ value, and champion opportunities for wider staff to get involved in Reach activity Stakeholder Management and Ownership Develop and maintain expert knowledge of Challenge Partners’ networks and programmes, as well as their benefits and impact, to accurately and persuasively communicate value to prospective stakeholders Build and manage a portfolio of school and trust prospects, nurturing relationships and delivering high quality, consultative sales conversations, in-person and virtually Identify and engage stakeholders from organisations, local authorities and other relevant bodies to form partnerships and unlock ways to engage with schools and trusts Data Management and Systems Become an expert in Challenge Partners’ Salesforce CRM to track lead schools and trusts, leveraging data to drive sales and process automation Present regular reports on KPIs through data management and reporting, relating to the sales pipeline, conversions, and potential leads and opportunities Actively contribute to the development of our Salesforce CRM, ensuring systems support high standards of sales data tracking and management Event Planning and Support Lead the planning and marketing of a series of introductory webinars for interested schools and trusts to hear an overview of the partnership from senior colleagues and partner speakers Scope and lead on supporting hub events and partner events where prospective schools and trusts can be invited to engage Coordinate prospective partner attendance at wider central team events, ensuring that they have excellent experiences of Challenge Partners on the day, while supporting events more generally Matrix Management At Challenge Partners, we work in a matrix structure which means that individuals collaborate across different work streams and are, at times, task managed by colleagues who are not their direct line manager. Therefore the Partnership Development Lead will: Provide consistent and high quality task management to all Partnership Coordinators supporting activities related to Reach, and cultivate strong relationships with all hub owners Provide consistent and high quality task management to all colleagues involved in school and trust Reach. This includes upwards management of Managers and the Leadership Team Support the provision of training and ongoing support to Partnership Coordinators in Reach and the articulation of Challenge Partners’ value Person Specification Specific skills and attitudes we are looking for in an applicant are as follows: Proven track record of strong project management, ideally in sales pipelines and partnerships from prospect to close Experience in stakeholder management, with a clear approach to identifying and uncovering needs to influence decision makers and articulately communicating value Ability to prioritise effectively to meet competing demands and work under pressure, through excellent organisation and time management Outstanding attention to detail, and pride in your work Strong sense of proactivity, ensuring any issues are recognised and dealt with before they escalate Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to deal with people diplomatically and appropriately, building rapport with those at varying levels of seniority Positivity, optimism and agility - we are a small organisation and all staff are expected to contribute across the organisation (and sometimes beyond their specific job role) to ensure our success and sustainability High information technology literacy - confidence and competence in using Google Suite, Microsoft programmes and Salesforce (or a similar CRM system) would be an advantage Proactive in seeking and applying feedback to continuously improve performance A genuine passion for the education sector, and a desire to make a difference The ability and willingness to travel across the country How to apply Please click here to submit your application on Hireful by 10am on 21st October 2026 . You will be asked to upload your CV and answer four competency and scenario-based application questions. Interviews will take place in-person on 4th November 2026 , at the Challenge Partners office (Oxford House, 49 Oxford Road, London, N4 3EY). Specific details will be confirmed near time. Please note that Challenge Partners is not currently able to offer visa sponsorship. We welcome applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the UK .

item.description: Shop Manager - Stockton Heath The Children's Society £25,760 per annum/pro rata Permanent Job description Permanent 37 hours per week / 5 over 7 days £25,760 per annum/pro rata Location: Stockton Heath, 47 London road Benefits include but not limited to: -36 days' annual leave , inclusive of flexible bank holidays, increasing with length of service -Enhanced maternity/paternity leave -We match up to 8% pension -Free counselling service -Opportunities to develop and widen your skills -2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us:The Children's Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. We run over 100 retail shops covering the whole of the UK - every one of these shops play a vital role in our mission to providing support to children and young adults. Every day we're changing the lives of children in this country for the better - and with your help, tomorrow we can be there for even more. We're looking for a confident and motivated Shop Manager with the ability to lead and inspire others, develop a culture of natural growth leading a strong volunteer network, and drive the shops net profits, whilst also delivering improvements to strengthen the shop's performance and wider community engagement and impact. Key Skills and Competencies: The required skills and competencies for this role are: -Strong people leadership skills with the ability to motivate, coach and develop colleagues and volunteers to achieve shared goals. -Commercial awareness with experience of driving sales, maximising donations and delivering income and profit targets. -Excellent customer service and communication skills, building positive relationships with customers, volunteers and local communities. It would also be an advantage if you have any of the following skills and competencies: -Experience of recruiting, retaining and growing a diverse volunteer team in a retail or community setting. -Knowledge of visual merchandising, stock management and creating engaging shop environments that increase sales. -Experience of using retail systems, analysing performance data and implementing improvements to enhance shop results. item.title: Conservation Officer
item.description: Are you passionate about nature's recovery in our towns and cities? Do you want to play a key role in creating, restoring and managing habitats that help wildlife thrive across Birmingham and the Black Country? If so, we'd love to hear from you. Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust is the leading charity working to protect and restore nature across Birmingham and the Black Country. We manage and enhance important habitats, work with communities to create space for wildlife, and inspire people to take action for nature's recovery. Through practical conservation, ecological restoration, education, advocacy and community engagement, we are working towards a future where wildlife and people can thrive together. We're looking for individuals with strong practical conservation skills, excellent organisational abilities and a collaborative approach to working with others. Whether supporting learners, volunteers, community groups, corporate partners or contractors, you'll be confident building positive relationships and helping others contribute to nature's recovery. Above all, you'll share our commitment to creating a wilder Birmingham and Black Country and be motivated by the opportunity to make a lasting impact for wildlife. This is a flexible role, based in our offices at Centre of the Earth and EcoPark, Birmingham with an expectation of 3 or 4 days per week in the office or at sites. Frequent travel across Birmingham and The Black Country is expected, but with the option of some home working where appropriate. Occasional travel nationally may be required. Take a leading role in managing land at our engagement sites, including EcoPark and Centre of the Earth, while developing and delivering Wild Work Days with corporate volunteers. You'll work with volunteers, contractors and communities to deliver practical conservation projects and help maintain high-quality habitats for wildlife. Job Description Job Title: Conservation Officer Department: Nature Recovery Location: Centre of the Earth & EcoPark or other site/location Responsible to: Conservation Manager Responsible for: Volunteers, placements, contractors, trainees and any team members assisting with project work Purpose of the Post: To be a key member of the Conservation Team, working collaboratively with the wider Nature Recovery and Engagement teams to support the management of the Trust’s nature reserves and engagement sites to a high standard, support the delivery of funded projects and contracts, and engage with local communities. Key Responsibilities Main Objectives: To lead the management of land at EcoPark and Centre of the Earth to enable the Trust’s delivery of nature-centred engagement. To develop and deliver the Trust’s Wild Work Days with corporate groups. To contribute to the delivery of the Trust’s nature recovery projects across Birmingham and the Black Country, including through biodiversity creation and enhancement work on sites outside of the Wildlife Trust’s land holdings. To prepare, implement, and monitor site management plans. To contribute to the management of Wildlife Trust nature reserves to a high standard, as exemplars of urban nature conservation. To assure compliance with health and safety best practice in all aspects of the Wildlife Trust’s work, including contributing to the Wildlife Trust’s Health and Safety Committee where requested. Working with volunteers, communities and partners: Oversee and manage contractors both on the Wildlife Trust’s nature reserves and on other sites as required. Work and consult volunteers, community members, and other stakeholders, to manage Wildlife Trust sites and reserves. Help train and support volunteers in habitat management techniques, species identification, and the monitoring of species and habitats. Attend and deliver events and similar activities on Trust reserves and other sites. Support administration, supervision and management of contractors working for the Trust. Funding and Administration: Contribute to the preparation of funding applications and contract proposals to secure resources for Wildlife Trust sites and reserves. Support project managers in the administration of nature recovery projects, including the collation of project reports and grant claims for project funders. Support the Nature Recovery team to collate and maintain records and data. Complete required documentation and paperwork in a timely manner as required. Support colleagues in identifying and obtaining new contracts and projects in line with the Trust’s aims and objectives. Supporting others internally: Be an active member of the Conservation team delivering the Trust's aims and objectives. Work with and support Conservation colleagues and the wider Wildlife Trust team in all aspects of project management and delivery. Other Responsibilities Contribute to the continuous development of Nature Recovery at BBCWT. Contribute to knowledge sharing, service development and team learning. Represent the organisation positively when engaging withstakeholders, volunteers, visitors and partners. Act as an ambassador for the Trust, forming and maintaining positive relationships with volunteers, visitors and other organisations, and promoting membership wherever possible. Carry out any other reasonable duties commensurate with the level of responsibility of the post, as requested by your line manager or the Chief Executive. Organisational Responsibilities Values All employees are expected to demonstrate Trust and contribute positively to an inclusive, collaborative and respectful working environment and to support the achievement of the Trust's strategic objectives. Health, Safety and Wellbeing All employees have a responsibility to take reasonable care of their own health, safety and wellbeing, as well as that of colleagues, volunteers, visitors, contractors and others who may be affected by their actions or omissions. Employees must cooperate with BBCWT to help ensure compliance with health and safety requirements and contribute to a safe and healthy working environment. Safeguarding Actively support BBCWT's commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults at risk. Carry out responsibilities in line with BBCWT's safeguarding policies and procedures, remain vigilant to safeguarding concerns, and promptly report any concerns or disclosures through the appropriate channels. Access and Inclusion Actively support and promote BBCWT's commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion, ensuring fair and respectful treatment of all colleagues, volunteers, partners, supporters and members of the communities we work with. Learning and Development Take ownership of personal learning and development and participate in training, development activities and continuous professional development opportunities necessary to perform the role effectively and support organisational objectives. Performance Management Actively engage in BBCWT's performance management processes, taking responsibility for achieving agreed objectives, maintaining professional standards and contributing to the success of the organisation. Data Protection and Confidentiality Manage personal, organisational and sensitive information in accordance with UK GDPR and BBCWT policies and procedures. Maintain confidentiality and ensure information is collected, stored, processed and shared appropriately and securely. Environmental Responsibility Support BBCWT's mission to protect and restore nature by embedding environmentally sustainable practices into day-to-day activities and minimising environmental impact wherever possible. Adherence to Policies Be aware of and comply with all BBCWT policies, procedures and organisational requirements relevant to the role. Ensure that all activities are carried out in line with agreed standards, legal obligations and best practice. Other The nature of this post means that occasional out-of-hours and weekend working will be required. In case of working outside working hours, overtime is not paid but time off in lieu will be granted.

item.title: Head of Partnerships and Philanthropy (Hybrid)
item.description: Head of Partnerships and Philanthropy (Hybrid) 💰 Salary: £58,355 📆 Contract: Permanent, full time We also offer: 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) and a discretionary Christmas closure Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay policy Private GP Service Salary sacrifice schemes for gym, bicycles, annual leave buying, and nursery/childcare Free Premium Headspace membership Financial, life and leadership coaching Life Assurance policy of 3x annual salary Access to free online, in-person or telephone therapy 📍 Location: Head office (Fivefields, 8-10 Grosvenor Gardens, London) and travel to our key reserves typically 1-2 days per week, the remaining 3-4 days from home. 🕑 Hours: 9:00am – 5:00pm. We welcome flexible working requests from day one. Role & Responsibilities This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of high-value fundraising at London Wildlife Trust. Building on a small but successful programme, you’ll lead the growth and diversification of our income across corporate partnerships, trusts, foundations, institutional funders and major donors. Leading a small team, you’ll build and steward five, six and seven-figure relationships that help turn our vision of a London alive with nature into reality. You’ll: Lead our partnerships and philanthropy strategy, securing significant new multi-year partnerships and funding that support our strategic priorities. Build and manage a strong pipeline of prospects, identifying new opportunities across major gifts, corporate partnerships, trusts, foundations and statutory funding. Develop and nurture high-value relationships, personally managing a portfolio of major donors, corporate partners and funders capable of five- and six-figure gifts. Create compelling, tailored propositions that connect funder interests with the impact we’re making for London’s wildlife, wild spaces and communities. Work closely with our Director of Development, Senior Leadership Team and Trustees to open doors, develop relationships and secure high-value funding. Deliver excellent stewardship, ensuring our supporters see the difference their funding makes through impact reporting, events, site visits and recognition. Work collaboratively across the Trust, partnering with Nature Recovery, Visitor Experience, Marketing & Communications and Finance to develop strong, accurate and compelling proposals and reports. Strengthen our fundraising infrastructure, ensuring we have effective systems, processes and CRM data to manage relationships and pipelines from prospect identification through to stewardship. Support and develop your team, creating a collaborative, high-performing culture where people are clear on their role, supported to develop and empowered to deliver their best work. Our ideal Head of Partnerships & Philanthropy Significant experience in at least one high-value fundraising discipline (major donors, corporate partnerships, and/or trusts and foundations), with a track record of securing five- and six-figure gifts Excellent relationship-building skills, with confidence engaging senior stakeholders including CEOs, funders and trustees Strong strategic and financial planning skills, including pipeline management, budget management and income forecasting Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex issues into compelling funding propositions Genuine interest in and commitment to nature conservation and environmental issues Good understanding of the high-value fundraising market (in particular corporate) (Please see job description for full person specification) Closing Date: 12th October at 9.30am Interviews: Are scheduled to take place on week commencing 19th October and reasonable adjustments will be offered to all candidates. Does this sound like you? We’d love to hear from you! Our vision is a London alive with wildlife, with nature in everyone's neighbourhood. To achieve our goal of inspiring everyone to help restore London’s wildlife, we recognise that our team must better reflect and represent all of London’s diverse communities. Find out more about London Wildlife Trust’s commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion here: https://www.wildlondon.org.uk/jobs . We are also committed to ensuring that the safety and wellbeing of children, young people and adults at risk is at the heart of our engagement with people. Read about our commitment to safeguarding here: https://www.wildlondon.org.uk/safeguarding . REF-231132

item.title: Supporter Led Fundraising Officer
item.description: Your mission Reporting to the Supporter Led Fundraising Manager, you'll support and inspire people to fundraise for CALM in their own way, providing the tools, encouragement and support they need to make an impact and build a meaningful relationship with CALM. Responsibilities Supporter engagement & stewardship Provide excellent stewardship to CALM's Supporter Led fundraisers, acting as a fundraising coach to help people bring their ideas to life and make the most of their fundraising. Build and develop relationships with supporters across DIY, challenges, in memory, tribute and other Supporter Led fundraising, providing personalised and compassionate support throughout their journey with CALM. Ensure in memory and tribute supporters receive sensitive and appropriate stewardship, recognising the individual needs of people fundraising following a bereavement. Support with the development and delivery of supporter journeys, communications and fundraising materials, including through Marketing Cloud, to deepen engagement and build longer-term supporter relationships. Represent CALM at Supporter Led fundraising activities and events, helping to provide a brilliant experience for our supporters. Fundraising growth & development Contribute to CALM's fundraising targets through excellent relationship management, identifying opportunities to grow income and deepen supporter relationships. Support activity to engage and retain supporter led fundraisers, helping to identify and develop new fundraising opportunities. Collaborative working Work closely with the Supporter Led Fundraising Manager, Lead and wider Fundraising team to deliver our objectives and support the continued development of Supporter Led Fundraising. Build strong relationships across CALM, working collaboratively to create joined up experiences and make the most of opportunities for our supporters. Keep up to date with fundraising trends and best practice, bringing ideas and learning into the team. Work flexibly as CALM continues to evolve Supporter Led fundraising. Your profile Essential You have a good understanding of Supporter Led fundraising. You have experience of delivering excellent supporter care and building strong relationships. You are confident communicating with and supporting people who have been bereaved, approaching sensitive and emotional conversations with empathy, care and good judgement. You have experience of working with CRM databases and fundraising platforms You have experience of working towards and meeting financial targets. You are a confident and engaging communicator, both written and verbal. You have excellent organisational skills and can manage a busy and varied workload, prioritising effectively. You are comfortable working in an evolving environment and can adapt as priorities and ways of working develop. You understand the importance of using supporter insight and data to inform your work. You will be a positive ambassador for CALM, working in line with our values, policies and brand. You have experience working within a charity or fundraising environment. Desirable You have experience of in memory or tribute fundraising, or working with people affected by bereavement. You have experience using a CRM and email marketing systems. You have experience working with fundraising platforms such as JustGiving and MuchLoved. You understand issues relating to mental health and suicide. You have an understanding of key fundraising regulations and compliance requirements, or experience applying these in a fundraising environment. Why us? Reports to: Supporter Led Fundraising Manager Contract: Permanent, full-time Benefits: Unlimited annual leave, Healthcare cash plan, 6% pension contribution, therapeutic services (after completion of probation), hybrid working & nine day fortnight Based: London Waterloo twice a week (Wednesdays and Thursdays) / Remote Working (Mon, Tues & Fri), 9.30am - 5.30pm. Salary: £30k - £33k per annum. We benchmark our salaries to ensure our pay structure remains fair, transparent, and equitable for everyone in our team. A work environment that values creativity, personal growth and collaboration. Applications will close on Thursday 8th October. Right to work in the UK To apply, you will need to have a valid right to work in the UK (such as a British/Irish passport, Settled Status, or Indefinite Leave to Remain). About us We’re Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM), and we’re united against suicide. We’re a suicide prevention charity, on a mission to help people end their misery, not their lives. We run stigma-smashing campaigns, offer loads of digital tools and resources, and run a life-saving helpline - all designed to help people find hope and a way forward. We are - united against suicide. Don't meet every requirement? We’re still interested. Research shows that people from marginalised groups – including women, LGBTQ+ people, people from global majority backgrounds, disabled people, and those from lower socioeconomic backgrounds – are less likely to apply for a role unless they meet the full criteria. At CALM, we know that skills and potential come in many forms, and that diverse perspectives and lived experience of mental health or suicide can be just as valuable as formal qualifications. If you're passionate about our mission but your experience doesn't tick every box, we'd still love to hear from you. You could be exactly who we're looking for. Safeguarding We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people, and adults at risk, both offline and online. We recognise that harm can occur in physical, digital, and virtual environments, and we take our safeguarding responsibilities seriously across all areas of our work.

item.title: Finance Officer
item.description: Department: Finance Reports to: Head of Finance Additional accountability: National Treasurer (UKIM) and Chair, Finance & General-Purposes Committee (Trustees’ sub-committee) Location: Your normal place of work is European Islamic Centre, Werneth House, 79 Manchester Rd, Oldham, OL8 4LN. You may, however, be required to travel from time to time to our London office and other UKIM branches across the country as an when required. Reasonable expenses for such travel will be reimbursed.You will not be required to work outside the UK for any continuous period of more than one month during the term of your employment. Contract: Permanent (or 2-year fixed-term) Hours: 37.5 hours per week Salary: £26,000–£30,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience) Annual leave: 27days (including 2 x days for Eid) Pension: Auto-enrolment pension scheme with employer contribution Probation: 6 months (extendable); formal reviews at 3 and 6 months against agreed objectives Notice: 1 month during probation; 1 month thereafter Line management: No About UKIM UK Islamic Mission (UKIM) is one of the UK’s longest-established Muslim charities, founded in 1962. We are a national organisation with around 60 branches across England, Scotland and Wales, delivering community services, education, welfare projects, and faith-based initiatives. Each week, thousands of people engage with our mosques, centres, and activities. Role purpose The Finance Officer’s role is for supporting the UKIM Branches in gathering information, consolidating the branch accounts, training the branch treasurers/ accounts focal persons, ensuring that the branches upload financial data on the accounting software/ platform. The postholder will be accountable to, the Head of Finance and/ or UKIM Treasurer in maintaining effective financial controls in relation to the UKIM branches, will also be responsible for maintaining the asset register, calculate depreciation, list of UKIM properties. Key responsibilities Assist the Head of Finance in ensuring the efficient and effective delivery of all aspects of Finance across all UKIM; Assist the Head of Finance with financial management, treasury, loans, accounting support and general advice. Responsible for the production and delivery of timely and accurate financial information. Responsible for timely processing of branch accounts and liaising with UKIM branch treasures to obtain financial and accounting records. Ensuring timely data input in accounting software for branches and periodic reconciliations Provide training if required to branch treasurers or nominees. Assist Head of Finance during annual audit of the statutory accounts including management accounts. Maintain systems to enable relevant Managers to have up to date financial overview of UKIM project spending, across all departments. Collection of funds and issuing receipts. Competency required in Accounting software such as Capium. Sage, IRIS, Quick Books and Xero or iPlicit Extracting data from WorldPay Merchant Web Donations, Cardsave Merchant, Cheque Deposit spreadsheets and FastPay direct debit spreadsheets. Dealing with expenses and petty cash. Responding to relevant telephone, post and email enquiries. Dealing with supplier invoices and queries. Depositing cheques in the bank accounts, which includes: Extracting data from the UKIM Info system. Sorting each cheque according to the bank account it needs to be deposited in. Double checking that all amounts on the cheques are correct and correctly entered in the finance system. Going to the bank with all the cheques and relevant deposit slips. Assistance in preparing the branch accounts. Data entry during Appeals. Assistance in the preparation of gift aid claims. The post holder may be required to undertake other reasonable duties within the scope of their role and in line with the needs of UKIM. Person specification Essential Ideally Qualified or Part-qualified accountant (ACA/ACCA/CIMA or equivalent) with significant post-qualification experience. Qualified by experience can be considered. Track record leading finance in a charity or complex multi-site setting; knowledge of Charity SORP, GAAP, PAYE, Corporation Tax, VAT, Gift Aid and charity law. Demonstrable experience of improving financial controls, processes and management information. Strong analytical skills; advanced Excel and competence with modern accounting/ERP systems. Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex information to non-finance stakeholders. People management experience and commitment to coaching and developing teams. High integrity, sound judgement and a collaborative approach. Desirable Experience supporting branch-based or federated charity structures. Experience in capital projects and programme/grant finance. Familiarity with dashboarding/BI tools. Safeguarding, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion UKIM is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and adults at risk. All staff must follow our safeguarding policies and complete mandatory training. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those underrepresented in the charity sector. We will make reasonable adjustments for candidates with disabilities or other needs during the recruitment process and in employment. As a faith-based charity, this role requires alignment with UKIM’s charitable aims and values, in line with the Equality Act 2010. Appointment is subject to satisfactory right-to-work, references, qualification verification, and (role-appropriate) Basic/Standard DBS and financial probity/credit checks. How to apply Closing date: 24th October 2026. We may close early if sufficient suitable applications are received. Right to work: We do not sponsor visas. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK.

item.title: Head of Finance
item.description: Department: Finance Reports to: Executive Director Additional accountability: National Treasurer (UKIM) and Chair, Finance & General-Purposes Committee (Trustees’ sub-committee) Location: UKIM Central Office, European Islamic Centre, 79 Manchester Road, Oldham, OL8 4LN (with occasional UK travel) Contract: Permanent (or 2-year fixed-term) Hours: 37.5 hours per week Salary: £34,000–£48,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience) Annual leave: 27 days (including 2 x days for Eid) Pension: Auto-enrolment pension scheme with employer contribution Probation: 6 months (extendable); formal reviews at 3 and 6 months against agreed objectives Notice: 1 month during probation; 3 months thereafter SMT: Member of the Senior Management Team (SMT); attends F&GPC/Board by invitation for finance items Line management: 2 Senior Finance Officers, 1 Finance Officer, 1 Finance Assistant; oversight of external auditors/consultants About UKIM UK Islamic Mission (UKIM) is one of the UK’s longest-established Muslim charities, founded in 1962. We are a national organisation with around 60 branches across England, Scotland and Wales, delivering community services, education, welfare projects, and faith-based initiatives. Each week, thousands of people engage with our mosques, centres, and activities. Role purpose The Head of Finance leads UKIM’s finance function, ensuring robust financial governance, transparent reporting, and compliant operations across central office, departments, and branches. The postholder is the organisation’s technical lead for SORP-compliant reporting, internal controls, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, and financial risk management, enabling UKIM to deliver its charitable objectives sustainably. The post holder will work closely with, and be accountable to, the UKIM Treasurer in maintaining effective financial oversight and governance across the organisation. Key responsibilities Lead UKIM’s finance function including financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and reporting. Preparation of annual statutory accounts in timely manner for annual audit and submission to charities commission and Companies house. Close liaising with auditors of the organization for timely completion of audit of accounts Prepare and present timely and accurate monthly management accounts, variance analysis and financial commentary to the Executive Director, F&GPC and Board. Oversee accounts team both at head office and branches. Oversee year-end statutory accounts (GAAP/SORP/FRS 102) and manage the audit process. Ensure compliance with Charity Commission, Companies House and HMRC (including PAYE, Corporation Tax, VAT and Gift Aid). Strengthen and embed financial controls, policies and procedures; oversee branch finance support and consolidation. Monitor cash flow and reserves; manage banking relationships; provide investment and treasury advice aligned to risk appetite. Ensure accurate payroll, PAYE and pension contributions. Provide financial modelling and analysis to support strategic planning, bids, tenders and capital/ international projects. Lead and develop the finance team, including objective-setting, reviews and CPD. Coordinate internal and external audit programmes; maintain a proportionate financial risk register and mitigation actions. Champion the effective use of finance systems (e.g., modern cloud accounting) and data quality across UKIM. Work collaboratively with departmental leads and Zonal/Branch leads to build local financial capability and consistent standards. The post holder may be required to undertake other reasonable duties within the scope of their role and in line with the needs of UKIM. Person specification Essential Qualified accountant (ACA/ACCA/CIMA or equivalent) with significant post-qualification experience. Track record leading finance in a charity or complex multi-site setting; knowledge of Charity SORP, GAAP, VAT, PAYE, Corporation Tax, Gift Aid and charity law. Demonstrable experience of improving financial controls, processes and management information. Strong analytical skills; advanced Excel and competence with modern accounting/ERP systems. Able to work with different accounting software(s) including iPlicit. Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex information to non-finance stakeholders. People management experience and commitment to coaching and developing teams. High integrity, sound judgement and a collaborative approach. Desirable Experience supporting branch-based or federated charity structures. Experience in capital projects and programme/grant finance. Familiarity with dashboarding/BI tools. Safeguarding, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion UKIM is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and adults at risk. All staff must follow our safeguarding policies and complete mandatory training. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, including those underrepresented in the charity sector. We will make reasonable adjustments for candidates with disabilities or other needs during the recruitment process and in employment. As a faith-based charity, this role requires alignment with UKIM’s charitable aims and values, in line with the Equality Act 2010. Appointment is subject to satisfactory right-to-work, references, qualification verification, and (role-appropriate) Basic/Standard DBS and financial probity/credit checks. How to apply Closing date: 24th October 2026. We may close early if sufficient suitable applications are received. Right to work: We do not sponsor visas. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK.

item.title: Senior Conservation Officer (12-Month Maternity Cover)
item.description: Are you passionate about nature's recovery in our towns and cities? Do you want to play a key role in creating, restoring and managing habitats that help wildlife thrive across Birmingham and the Black Country? If so, we'd love to hear from you. Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust is the leading charity working to protect and restore nature across Birmingham and the Black Country. We manage and enhance important habitats, work with communities to create space for wildlife, and inspire people to take action for nature's recovery. Through practical conservation, ecological restoration, education, advocacy and community engagement, we are working towards a future where wildlife and people can thrive together. We're looking for individuals with strong practical conservation skills, excellent organisational abilities and a collaborative approach to working with others. Whether supporting learners, volunteers, community groups, corporate partners or contractors, you'll be confident building positive relationships and helping others contribute to nature's recovery. Above all, you'll share our commitment to creating a wilder Birmingham and Black Country and be motivated by the opportunity to make a lasting impact for wildlife. This is a flexible role, based in our offices at Centre of the Earth and EcoPark, Birmingham with an expectation of 3 or 4 days per week in the office or at sites. Frequent travel across Birmingham and The Black Country is expected, but with the option of some home working where appropriate. Occasional travel nationally may be required. Lead the delivery of biodiversity enhancement and habitat creation projects across Birmingham and the Black Country, with a particular focus on freshwater habitats and ecological restoration. You'll work closely with partners, community groups and colleagues to deliver meaningful outcomes for nature and help drive the Trust's nature recovery ambitions. Job Description Job Title: Senior Conservation Officer (12 Month Maternity Cover) Department: Nature Recovery Location: Centre of the Earth & EcoPark or other site/location Responsible to: Conservation Manager Responsible for: Project Officers (where relevant), volunteers, placements, trainees and any team members assisting with project work Purpose of the post: To develop and lead ecological restoration projects across Birmingham and the Black Country and contribute to the development and leadership of the conservation team. Key Responsibilities Main Objectives Develop and lead the delivery of grant and contract-funded biodiversity enhancement and habitat creation projects across Birmingham and the Black Country. Manage team members (at officer level) to support the delivery of biodiversity enhancement and habitat creation projects. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with partner organisations, responding to funding and contract opportunities and delivering presentations and attending events where relevant. Build ongoing and strong relationships with community groups working for biodiversity improvement across the region. Maintain project records and data, working closely with EcoRecord colleagues, using GIS or other digital formats where applicable. Play a proactive role in managing health and safety when working with colleagues, volunteers, community groups, contractors, and partners. Funding and Administration: Work with colleagues and other organisations to identify and develop income generation and funding opportunities for river corridor restoration work, leading on or assisting with grant applications and tenders. Collate and submit project reports and grant claims to project funders and internal audiences. Assist in the preparation of annual budgets, work programmes, and reporting requirements for your area of work. Undertake financial management of projects including tracking income and expenditure, providing budget forecasts, and produce purchase orders and invoices as required. Procure the services of contractors and purchase materials required to deliver projects in line with the Trust’s procurement policy. Recruit, supervise and train employees and volunteers with the appropriate skills to support your area of work. Supporting others internally: Support the Trust’s Content and Communications Officer in managing project communications and by providing content to promote the achievements and impact of projects. Support senior Trust colleagues to develop and deliver the organisational strategy. Work with and support all colleagues in all aspects of project management and delivery. Contribute to the development of relevant competencies across the Nature Recovery team, and deliver internal training for colleagues and volunteers in your area of expertise. Other Responsibilities Contribute to the continuous development of Nature Recovery at BBCWT. Contribute to knowledge sharing, service development and team learning. Represent the organisation positively when engaging withstakeholders, volunteers, visitors and partners. Act as an ambassador for the Trust, forming and maintaining positive relationships with volunteers, visitors and other organisations, and promoting membership wherever possible. Carry out any other reasonable duties commensurate with the level of responsibility of the post, as requested by your line manager or the Chief Executive.

item.title: Senior Community Fundraiser - Scotland
item.description: About the role Do you live in Edinburgh or the surrounding area? As a senior community fundraiser, you’ll be an important part of the team building Breast Cancer Now’s presence in Scotland, with a particular focus on Edinburgh and the surrounding areas. We’re looking for someone who is an experienced relationship builder, someone who can find and develop new supporters. You’ll need excellent local knowledge, and the enthusiasm to develop a brand-new fundraising region. The successful candidate will also be part of the team working on our large-scale project supporting and growing Asda Tickled Pink, our award-winning partnership with Asda and CoppaFeel! which has already raised over £100 million. You’ll work directly with passionate colleagues across Asda stores in your region driving new fundraising initiatives, inspiring communities and celebrating incredible successes. No two days will look the same as you travel, connect and engage supporters to help us grow income to deliver our mission. The role is initially offered as a 12-month contract with the potential to become permanent. About you We’re looking for someone who is: Confident in approaching new contacts and are experienced in building a pipeline, developing new relationships from scratch. This may currently be in a customer service, account management or stewardship role. Experienced in managing and building new and established relationships with a focus on retention and income growth. Enthusiastic, proactive, organised and unafraid to test and try new ideas. This role will involve being out and about in the community you’re building, so you must be able to work independently outside of the office in varying locations and enjoy being busy. A full clean driving license and unlimited access to a car is essential. Previous experience working in a charity is not required. Job description and benefits The job description and our attractive benefits are available for you to download. This is a remote role, and the candidate will need to be based in Edinburgh and able to travel using their own vehicle. Regular travel will be required to meet supporters and visit Asda stores in your region, as well as occasional travel to our London, Sheffield or Glasgow office. Primary location of role and hybrid working This role is home based in the Edinburgh area. The salary range is: £31,000 to £34,000 per annum When applying We hope you choose to apply for this role. To support your application, you’ll be asked to submit your anonymised CV and a supporting statement. Please refer to the essential criteria on the person specification and clearly provide as much information as you can with examples, to demonstrate how and where you meet the criteria. If you’ve any immediate questions please contact the Breast Cancer Now recruitment team. Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion We’re committed to promoting equity, valuing diversity and creating an inclusive environment – for everyone who works for us, works with us, supports us and who we support. We reserve the right to close this advert early. Therefore, to avoid disappointment please submit your application as soon as possible, if you’re interested in this opportunity. Closing date : Wednesday 7 October 2026 11:59 pm Interview date: Wednesday 14 October 2026

item.title: Family and Early Years Coordinator
item.description: Would you like to spend your day supporting children aged 0-5 and their families, helping them access opportunities, services and activities that make a positive difference to their lives? How would you like to be part of a friendly team delivering high-quality early years and family support in an organisation that puts people before profit? If the answer is YES, then we would like to hear from you. Coin Street Community Builders have a fantastic opportunity for a motivated, energetic and enthusiastic Family and Early Years Coordinator to join our Community Hub team. The purpose of the role is to deliver engaging activities and support services for children and families, including stay-and-play sessions, crèche provision and one-to-one family support. You will build positive relationships with families, monitor children's progress, undertake outreach within the local community, and work closely with partner organisations to help families access the support and opportunities they need. The role also includes maintaining accurate records, updating database systems and completing digital documentation. We are looking for people who have: A full and relevant Level 3 childcare or early years qualification (or above) Experience of working with children aged 0-5 and their families Experience of planning and delivering family support, outreach or early years activities An understanding of child development and the importance of parent partnership Experience of working with a range of professionals and community organisations A positive, proactive and enthusiastic attitude A good understanding of safeguarding and child protection Experience of leading, supervising or supporting staff, volunteers or students would be desirable Experience using IT, database and other computer based applications What can we offer you? Competitive salary (based on your qualification and experience) Access to high quality training Coaching and mentoring support Generous pension at 8% - 5% from the employer if you contribute 3% 20% discount of childcare fees 35 days off a year, including 8 bank holidays, 3 days off between Christmas and New Year (additional days awarded for long service) There's more… Six inset days per year (three for nursery staff only and three with the wider Coin Street team) Refer a friend bonus of £500 for existing employees Health and wellbeing package including a confidential employee assistance programme and online therapy sessions plus free gym and daily fresh fruit Season ticket loan and cycle to work scheme (on completion of probation) Staff social events (summer BBQ and Christmas party) Opportunities to join Coin Street committees (for example the Black lives Matter Race & Equality Steering Committee, Inset planning, staff social committee) Local retail (star card) and online discounts Contract Permanent, Part-Time, 28 hours per week (Monday to Thursday) Salary £26,478 per annum (£33,097 FTE)

item.title: Social Care IDVA (Westminster)
item.description: Are you looking for a dynamic and rewarding role working for an organisation with the feminist agenda at the core of its ethos? Then Advance Charity could be the career choice for you! We are looking for a Social Care IDVA Salary: £28,000 - £35,000 (salary dependent on skills and experience and whether you are a qualified IDVA) Location: Westminster Children Social Care (Frampton Street) and Hammersmith Head Office. You will be located in an office 3-4 days per week with the opportunity to work remotely 1-2 days per week. Contract: Permanent Hours: 35 hours per week, 9am-5pm standard hours with occasional duty between 1-9pm done from home This post is open to female applicants only as being female is deemed to be a genuine occupational requirement under Schedule 9, Paragraph 1 of the Equality Act 2010. Please note: Any offer of employment will be made subject to references, confirmation of the right to work in the UK, and satisfactory enhanced DBS check. This role is also subject to Police Vetting. About us Advance is an award-winning and innovative women-only organisation, established in 1998, providing emotional and practical support to women and girls survivors of domestic abuse and supporting women with short-term sentences to reduce offending. We believe in empowering women and girls to lead safe, non-violent, equal lives so that they can flourish and contribute to the community. We are a community-based organisation who lead in best practice approaches to supporting women in their local community. We achieve this by being available to meet and support women in local settings and at our women’s centres, and by working in close partnership with other agencies. Our values are to listen and support, to empower and respect, collaboration, innovation, and accountability. About the role: You will be co-located at Westminster Family and Children’s Services and will help raise their awareness, identification of and response to those experiencing domestic violence. Working jointly with Social Workers on cases you will support service users and improve partnership responses. You will provide high-quality telephone or face to face crisis intervention, information, advocacy and support to women referred to the service, in respect to risk management and safety planning, criminal and civil remedies, housing, health, welfare rights, and children’s legislation. About You: You will have an excellent understanding of domestic violence and its effects on women and children and of best practice within the domestic abuse in various areas of need, with particular knowledge on children safeguarding/legislation. As an experienced domestic violence advocate who has worked with complex and multiple needs, the post holder will be skilled in risk management and safety planning, remaining calm in a crisis and in handling sensitive information on a daily basis. Experience of direct work with female survivors of domestic violence, of supporting women with child safeguarding, needs, and of working within safeguarding procedures is essential for this post, as is the need to adopt and promote a strong partnership approach to service provision. Your abilities extend to assessing the needs and risks of survivors, carry out short and longer-term risk management, safety planning and support and identify and refer to services appropriate to their needs. Advising women of their rights and options for seeking help and support from other agencies and proactively advocate to ensure barriers to accessing support and protection are reduced. You will work as an advocate and educator to raise awareness and upskill professionals within Children Social Care plus work with colleagues to successfully develop and deliver training. How to apply: Please submit your up-to-date CV with a supporting statement. Please note that only applications made via the job advert on the Advance careers page, and those that include a cover letter will be considered. Closing Date for Applications: Sunday 18th October 2026 @23:59 Interviews are taking place on a rolling basis and we may close the advert early if we receive a high number of strong applications, so early application is advised What we can offer you - Employee Benefits: A 35-hour working week An exceptional 30 days of paid holiday per year (pro rata for part time), PLUS public holidays on top (that's nearly 40 days paid holiday per year!) Additional days off to celebrate International Women’s Day, and for religious observance and moving home Perkbox - an employee discount platform where you can receive free rewards as well as take advantage of savings on clothes, groceries, travel, leisure and more Pension scheme Enhanced maternity/adoption provision Access to our Employee Assistance Programme Employee eye-care scheme Clinical supervision for front line staff and first line management roles Refer a Friend Scheme - £250 for each referral who passes probation Organisation wide away days Thorough induction and training Career development pathways ************************************************************** Under the Equality Act 2010, we are required to make any reasonable adjustments. If you have a disability as defined under this act and/or have special needs, please email the Talent Acquisition Team via the Advance website and we will aim to make the necessary arrangements to accommodate your needs. Diversity, Inclusion and Equal Opportunities We are committed to providing equality of opportunity and actively seek to recruit people from groups underrepresented in our current team. We have policies and processes in place to ensure that all employees are offered an equal opportunity in recruitment and selection, promotion, training, pay and benefits. Safeguarding Advance is committed to safeguarding and creating a culture of zero-tolerance of harm and expects all staff, including volunteers to share this commitment. We believe all individuals have the right to live their life free from violence and abuse and the right to feel and be safe. We have a suite of safeguarding policies, procedures and practice guidance, accessible to all staff, which promotes safeguarding and safer working practices across all our services and activities. When we recruit staff, we follow rigorous safer recruitment practices, this involves carrying out pre-employment checks including references, Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks, and identity checks. We ensure all staff undertake mandatory safeguarding training relevant to their role and responsibilities, to empower them to be competent and feel confident in recognising and responding appropriately to safeguarding issues and promote wellbeing.

item.title: Helpline Team Leader (overnight)
item.description: The Silver Line Helpline is recruiting for a Helpline Team Leader to join their fantastic team providing a vital service to older people across the UK. You'll oversee the day-to-day running of our national Silver Line Helpline service, which operates 24 hours a day, providing older people with friendly conversation and support. You'll ensure our staff and volunteers deliver an excellent service to older people across the UK and be the first point of contact when the team needs help or advice. You'll support the team on live calls, managing any issues that arise during shifts, including safeguarding concerns. Working flexibly alongside other Team Leaders, you'll train and manage a team of Loneliness & Support Officers, supporting their development and addressing performance or absence issues. You'll report to one of three Silver Line Managers who oversee the service. Although The Silver Line is a friendship service, many calls are highly challenging, involving older people experiencing severe loneliness, isolation, and complex mental health issues, including suicidal ideation. You'll need strong emotional intelligence, resilience, and empathy, and be skilled in supporting staff and volunteers to manage difficult calls safely, remain within the service remit, and prioritise their own wellbeing. This role offers hybrid working between home and our Blackpool office, with a minimum office attendance of once per quarter. Occasional additional office visits may be required for training or business needs. As a hybrid employee, you will be responsible for your own travel costs. Office attendance requirements will be reviewed in 2026. This is a part-time vacancy working overnight, 108.5 hours over 4 weeks with varying days each week. All shifts start at 22:45 and finish at 07:15. Salary advertised is FTE for 140 hours over 4 weeks. Salary for this role would be pro-rata and would carry an additional overnight supplement of £2.85 per hour. IMPORTANT : Please note - this post requires weekend and bank holiday working on a shift pattern basis. Last day for applications Thursday 1st October 2026.Interviews for shortlisted applicants will take place via Teams on13th 14th and 15th October. If successful, there will be a 3-day induction onsite at our Blackpool office on 16th, 17th & 18th November from 10am to 3pm. Please note : Before joining the National Services team at Age UK, we want to be open that the organisation is in a period of change. Age UK works as a network of over 100 independent partners, with national services delivered by the charity and local services delivered by partners across the UK. Our new strategy means more services will be delivered locally in future, although we think our National Services will continue to play an important role. You would be joining a team that is evolving and changing to develop new ways of supporting older people, and we want you to have this context as you consider your application. Must Haves: The below competencies will be assessed at the indicated stage of the recruitment process. Application = A, Interview = I, Test = T, Presentation = P Experience • Experience of managing or supporting a front-line customer facing service with the ability to work flexibly as part of a team and build and maintain positive and professional working relationships. A, I • Experience in delivering training and coaching, including training and supporting staff on digital databases and systems. A, I • Experience of managing and supporting a team, including supporting delivery of KPIs. A, I Skills and knowledge • Expert knowledge of safeguarding issues with the ability to assess and manage risk independently. A, T • Excellent IT skills including data entry, Microsoft Office and CRM systems . A, T • Excellent interpersonal, written, customer service and communication skills, with the ability to actively listen and adapt communication style, responding in a non-judgemental, empathetic and respectful manner in all situations. A, I, T • Ability to lead and maintain high levels of morale during challenging shifts whilst effectively managing a busy and varied workload. I • Ability to adhere to policies and procedures at all times, with a commitment to promoting equality and diversity. A, I Personal attributes • Having a passion for supporting older people, staff and volunteers, with an understanding of the issues facing older people, particularly in relation to loneliness, isolation and mental health. A, I, T • High levels of personal resilience and the ability to stay calm and empathetic during challenging situations, with the ability to effectively manage complaints and challenging calls. I, T Great to haves The below competencies will be assessed at the indicated stage of the recruitment process. Application = A, Interview = I, Test = T, Presentation = P Experience: • Experience in working in services to support older people. A • Experience in working in with volunteers. A • Experience working with colleagues remotely. A, I • Experience working within services that operate outside of normal working hours. A What we offer in return: Competitive salary, 26 days annual leave + bank holidays + annual leave purchase scheme Excellent pension scheme, life assurance, Health cashback plan and EAP Car Benefit Scheme, Cycle to Work Scheme and Season Ticket Loan Techscheme - buy any tech from Apple or Currys, up to £1000, and spread the cost over 12 months, interest free Blue Light Card Scheme You Did It Awards – recognition awards from £100-250 Many additional benefits Additional Information: Supporting statements and anonymisation Candidates are expected to provide a supporting statement that explains how they meet the competencies, to allow us to assess suitability for the position. Age UK acknowledges and accepts that AI may be used to support the application; we do expect candidates to personalise experience, knowledge and skills and failure to do so, may result in your application being rejected. CVs will be anonymised by our recruitment system when you apply for a role. Our system is unable to anonymise supporting statements. Please could you remove any personal information including your name before you upload to support our inclusive recruitment process. All equalities monitoring information is also anonymised and not shared with the hiring panel. Your name and address will only be known to us if invited for interview. Equal opportunities & Disability Confident Scheme Age UK is an Equal Opportunities employer and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates, regardless of age, sex, race, disability, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, religion or belief, marital/civil partnership status, or pregnancy and maternity. Age UK is a Disability Confident Scheme employer. Due to high numbers of applications received, Age UK reserves the right to limit the overall number of interviews offered, and therefore, it may not always be practicable or appropriate to interview all disabled people that meet the minimum criteria for the job. Reasonable adjustments Disabled job seekers can access reasonable adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. All requests for reasonable adjustments are considered on a case-by-case basis, in collaboration with the disabled job seeker to best meet their needs, by contacting our recruitment team. Disability disclosures will be kept confidential and only shared on a need-to-know basis to support the implementation of adjustments. Disclosures will not be used to inform hiring decisions. Age UK is committed to safeguarding adults at risk, and children, from abuse and neglect. We expect everyone who works with us to share this commitment. Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert at any time. Age UK politely requests no contact from recruitment agencies or media sales. We do not accept speculative CVs from recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them. For a full list of benefits please visit our website.

item.title: Independent Sexual Violence Advisor
item.description: Complete risk and needs assessments to address the specific needs of victims in line with VS operating procedures. Deliver one‑to‑one interventions that promote emotional wellbeing, resilience, and recovery. Work closely with criminal justice process agencies and other partners to ensures that each victim is heard and their needs are prioritised. Proactively promote the service, raising awareness of services & working collaboratively with professionals to improve the access to and quality of services for all victims of sexual violence, abuse or exploitation Follow relevant safeguarding policies and procedures, working with safeguarding leads and other agencies to ensure an integrated approach to address any safeguarding concerns. item.title: Business Development Coordinator
item.description: A little bit about the role Please note that applications for this role will close on Friday 16 October 2026 at 9am The Business Development team is a recently established and growing team at Frontline. The team is responsible for delivering and developing high-quality leadership programmes, workforce development training, and commissioned projects that support practitioners and leaders across the children’s social care sector. We work collaboratively across Frontline to ensure that these offers extend the organisation’s mission impact and contribute to its financial sustainability. The team is ambitious, collaborative, and committed to innovation, equity, and continuous improvement. As Business Development Coordinator, you will play a vital role in supporting the effective delivery of Frontline’s leadership development programmes and workforce development training offers. You will provide high-quality administrative, operational and project support across the Business Development team, working closely with the Business Development Manager and Programme Manager to ensure smooth programme delivery and excellent participant experiences. Your responsibilities will include supporting communications, logistics, resource management, scheduling, and data tracking. This is a key role for an organised, proactive and collaborative individual who is passionate about supporting work that improves leadership and practice across the children’s social care sector. Some key responsibilities include: Providing operational and administrative support for the delivery of leadership development Drafting and managing participant communications, including joining instructions, programme updates, feedback surveys, and certificates. Supporting project planning, risk tracking, and logistics mapping for leadership and training offers. Assisting with reporting tasks, information collation, and maintenance of project documentation. Please review the job pack for full list of responsibilities. A little bit about you We’d like to see applicants who are organised, reliable, and proactive in supporting smooth delivery. You’ll be a clear communicator who works well with others, stays adaptable, and manages priorities effectively. An interest in children’s social work and improving practice will help you contribute to meaningful projects that make a difference. We have a fast-moving culture within the team and organisation, so we’re looking for someone who is who is well organised, details-focused and can use their initiative to do what works. You will have excellent communication skills, be able to build relationships with people and be willing to learn. There are lots of opportunities for growth and development in this role – and for the right candidate to make the role their own. If you feel you have the skills to make a real impact and contribute to creating lasting social change for children and families, we would love to hear from you. Important information We have increased the diversity of Frontline’s workforce in the last 12 months, but we need to do more to have greater global majority representation in our senior roles. We know the value global majority voices bring and therefore, we are strongly encouraging applicants from these backgrounds to apply. We are also a disability confident employer and welcome applicants with disabilities. We recognise that artificial intelligence (AI) such as ‘ChatGPT’ etc can be useful for applicants e.g. to shorten an initial draft, so we do not attempt to have an absolute ban on AI in applications. However we would caution applicants not to rely too much on AI in drafting answers to application questions. We want to hear your authentic voice arising out of your experience, and we will be looking for answers that use examples and experiences that are specific to you. You are more likely to be able to produce that kind of content yourself than an AI will. We reserve the right to close this role ahead of the deadline once we reach a suitable number of applications, so please apply as soon as you can! This role is ineligble for visa sponsorship. For further information about this role, please contact Penny McGee - Head of Business Development (see job pack for contact details)
