item.title: Head of Finance and Compliance
item.description: Purpose of the role This is an exciting opportunity at NEON, working across the whole organisation to ensure good financial practices that are compliant, make sense for how we work, and are values-led. Some days you’ll be working closely with colleagues in the People & Ops Hub, where this role is situated, to figure out better practices and processes, leading a budget kick-off meeting with the whole team, or working with external partners to enhance our data protection work. Other days you’ll be having brainstorming sessions with our Head of Fundraising or programme leads, helping to strengthen their work or contributing to whole team discussions around our mission, analysing the external political moment or pontificating on what finance means for a progressive organisation. This role will suit someone who loves having their head stuck in a spreadsheet as much as working with people: problem-solving, supporting others and generating ideas together. The purpose of this role is two-fold: to lead NEON’s financial strategy, systems and compliance, and to empower people across NEON to understand, engage with and take ownership of finance. This means: Leading finance processes, including budgeting and managing finance support. Providing clear financial information, analysis and recommendations to support good decision-making. Ensuring we have effective tools and systems to manage our finances. Building financial literacy and making finance accessible across the team. Overseeing key compliance and governance responsibilities, including Board governance and data protection. Embedding NEON’s values and anti-oppression principles in how finance and compliance operates. What you will be doing Here are the key responsibilities of this role: 1. Overseeing NEON’s financial systems (including accounting and payment software) to effectively manage NEON’s financial transactions and improve efficiency, ensuring timely reviews and improvements. 2. Leading on financial strategy alongside others in the senior team - working collaboratively with NEON’s senior leadership team to set the direction of travel for NEON and planning our finances over the short, medium and long term. 3. Overseeing regular finance and accounting processes , ensuring they are accurate, timely and well controlled as well as clear, accessible and proportionate, and line managing or coordinating the people responsible for delivering them. This includes: Supplier invoices and payments Payroll Payment card transactions Customer billing and credit control Grant budgets, tracking and reporting Bank reconciliations Supporting fundraising bids 4. Overseeing NEON’s taxation affairs, liaising with our external tax firm advisors and ensuring relevant requirements are met. 5. Leading the annual accounts and audit process, ensuring accurate and timely statutory reporting, compliance with relevant requirements, effective liaison with external auditors, and effective coordination of internal people and processes. 6. Leading cash flow analysis, forecasting and treasury management, to aid management decision-making,ensuring NEON has sufficient liquidity, appropriate financial controls and a sustainable reserves position. 7. Producing management accounts and financial reports, providing clear narrative, analysis and recommendations to support decision-making across NEON. This includes income and expenditure reports, balance sheets and cash flow forecasts. 8. Leading and holding the annual budgeting process from kick-off through to completion , working with Directors and budget holders to develop the budget, facilitate discussions and decision-making, produce clear narrative and practical guidance, and build people’s confidence and skills in managing their budgets. 9. Overseeing key organisational compliance and governance processes , ensuring NEON meets its legal, regulatory and governance obligations, while taking an accessible, proportionate and values-led approach. This includes data protection, Board governance (including Board recruitment and coordinating Board meetings and papers), statutory requirements and compliance deadlines, and identifying and escalating significant compliance risks. 10. Operationalising and democratising finance across NEON , making finance accessible and less intimidating, improving financial literacy and confidence, and empowering colleagues to take ownership of their budgets and financial responsibilities. Building relationships across the organisation and embedding NEON’s values and anti-oppression principles in how the finance function operates. 11. Playing an active part in the whole NEON team, contributing to organisation-wide plans. Who you are Skilled and experienced in leading the many parts of the finance function - from accounting, budgeting and bookkeeping to management accounts, cash flow, audit and financial strategy, managing or coordinating others, as well as: a minimum of five years work experience in a finance role, either within the charity/non profit sector or with a strong understanding of this sector. This means you have a good understanding of non-profit finance, including VAT and managing restricted and unrestricted funds Qualified accountant or qualified by experience Strong knowledge of financial compliance and organisational governance – including statutory accounts and reporting, taxation, financial controls and regulatory requirements. As well as data protection, and all aspects of Board governance (or willing to learn these aspects). You are confident keeping track of obligations, spotting risks and making sure things get done. Able to think strategically while staying close to the detail – you can understand the bigger financial picture, identify risks and opportunities, and turn this into clear analysis, recommendations and practical advice for the senior leadership team and wider organisation. Excellent at turning complex spreadsheets and complicated financial data into simple and clear analysis for others to understand. That might be through data visualisation tools, great written narrative or finding more accessible and creative ways of reporting financial information. Excited about thinking creatively about how finance can work in a progressive, values-led organisation , making finance accessible and empowering colleagues to take ownership. You bring good judgement to risk and controls and are willing to experiment with systems, automation and new technologies to make finance more efficient and user-friendly. Line management experience. You’re a skilled and confident line manager, and able to support with feedback, development and performance. You know how to balance care with clarity and accountability. Experienced in managing grant and funder finance – including grant budgets, restricted funding, financial tracking and reporting, and meeting funder requirements. Able to flex between longer-term projects, regular cycle work and responsive requests – you are self-motivated, can shift priorities when needed, and are comfortable setting boundaries and managing your time, energy and workload sustainably, with support from your manager. Willing to continuously learn and grow - with good emotional intelligence and self awareness including around your own power, and an ability to give and receive feedback well, and sit in (and encourage) healthy conflict and disagreement Committed to NEON’s purpose of building the strength of movements for social, economic and environmental justice, and to learning how to align your actions with the values of NEON: solidarity; generosity and respect How to apply Please find details for how to apply on our website. Dates Application deadline: 25th October, 11.59pm First interviews online: Tuesday 3rd November and Wednesday 4th November 2026. Second interviews in-person at our Bethnal Green office: Tuesday 10th November 2026. If you fancy a chat about the role or have any questions about NEON in general, you can reach out to Janine via our email on our website. You can request a call back via this email if you prefer. We will treat the data you provide in your application in accordance with our Privacy Policy . We know that people from certain backgrounds and identities are often excluded in progressive movements and we’re committed to doing what we can to correct this. So: we particularly welcome applications from marginalised groups, especially people of colour and other ethnic minorities, people who identify as LGBTQIA, Disabled people and those who identify as working class or have done so in the past. we know the work goes way beyond "diversity", it's about making the space inclusive too. So we are continuously working on that at NEON. So far this includes tangible things like a flexible work policy so people have genuine flexibility around where and when they work and a 28 hour week as standard; a gender-neutral parenting/leave policy, an anti-oppression strategy which is held at senior level given how important it is to the organisation. It also includes the day-to-day work of creating psychological safety for everyone at NEON and celebrating the wisdom of black, indigenous, queer, Disabled and other cultures in the way we work and behave There are no formal education requirements for this role. As long as you can show us you have the skills we don’t mind where you got them from! Also important to us is your potential to learn and grow in the role so even if you don’t have 100% of the skills listed we want to hear from you. About us: NEON is a capacity and infrastructure building organisation that seeks to accelerate the transition to a new economy by building the power of social movements - because without strong social movements we lack the power we need to win. We deliver trainings, develop resources, facilitate collaboration and work in partnership with key movement allies, especially in the climate, housing and migration movements. item.title: Interim Partnerships Manager (Ecosystem)
item.description: Fixed-term contract until 31 March 2027 Remote (UK-based) | Full-time - £53,991 + benefits (including 4.5-day week and 11% employer pension) Do your best work, for the right reasons. We’re looking for an experienced partnerships manager to play a key role in driving Oak's growth and impact by increasing adoption of our open data and content tools across edtechs, as well as AI and infrastructure providers. This is a highly collaborative role, combining strong technical and market insight with a proactive, target-driven approach to partnership development. You will work with colleagues across the organisation to generate and qualify opportunities through events, networks, referrals, and outreach, building a focused pipeline aligned to shared priorities. Through structured discovery conversations, you’ll develop a clear understanding of partner needs, technical readiness, and strategic fit, helping shape how we engage and support partners. You will assess and triage opportunities against agreed criteria, working closely with Product and Engineering colleagues to prioritise those with the greatest potential for impact and influence, and to determine where we focus our efforts. Alongside this, you’ll build trusted relationships with developers and edtech leaders, growing peer support networks that facilitate peer-to-peer conversations and community engagement. You’ll maintain clear pipeline visibility through accurate CRM management and data-led insight, using this to inform decisions and drive continuous improvement. Working cross-functionally, you’ll share learnings from the field to influence messaging, product development, and how Oak delivers for the wider ecosystem. Oak is a fully remote, mission-driven organisation offering high levels of flexibility, autonomy, and purpose. We’re a national not-for-profit organisation working in partnership with teachers to create high-quality, sequenced curriculum and lesson resources for pupils across all subjects and age groups. Our culture has been independently recognised through: Flexa verified (93% overall score, including 95% for working hours and 97% for role modelling) Escape the City's Top 1% Employers – based on anonymous colleague reviews of culture, development, and impact Investors in People Gold - through external accreditation and colleague feedback What You’ll Be Doing Lead the continuous improvement of lead nurture processes, including events, networks, referrals and targeted outreach, aligned to the go-to-market strategy. Run structured first conversations, assess readiness, tier opportunities, and maintain accurate CRM records within an active partnerships pipeline. Build and nurture relationships with edtech and infrastructure providers to develop Oak champions, and organise in-person and online community events, including representing Oak at relevant industry events. As a member of the Oak Team, contribute to the planning and culture of the organisation. Work in cross-functional and product-oriented squads with colleagues from across the organisation, as required. Deputise for the Partnerships Lead and take on other general responsibilities as required. What We’re Looking For 3+ years of experience managing a sales pipeline with edtech companies and/or infrastructure providers Experience leading structured conversations with decision-makers to conversion in a business or product context. Strong organisational skills and CRM discipline. Practical understanding of technical integration processes, particularly using APIs and open data. Motivated by long-term ecosystem growth and impact. The successful candidate will have a desire to contribute across all areas to ensure Oak's success. You will be comfortable moving quickly and with agility, and be confident working with a range of digital systems (including proprietary ones, as required). You will continually look for ways that the team can keep getting better. You will be excellent at working as part of a remote team, building relationships and managing your time effectively. Our Benefits 25 days annual leave, plus one extra day for each year of service (up to 28) Additional Oak closure days over Christmas/New Year 11% employer pension contribution (with no minimum employee contribution, which can be varied as you choose). Please note this is a workplace pension rather than the Teachers’ Pension Scheme. A 36-hour working week (not tied to term-time patterns or school-day hours), with half-days on Fridays or every other Friday off. Remote working (with some in-person visits, including representing Oak at relevant in-person events and school visits) — we’ll support your home set-up and offer coworking options if preferred Twice-yearly in-person whole Oak offsites to collaborate, connect, and have fun (with other occasional team events in person) A culture that genuinely supports flexibility, autonomy, and trust Inclusion and Belonging We believe diverse teams build better products. We warmly welcome applicants from all backgrounds, particularly those who are underrepresented in the tech and education sectors. We use the Applied recruitment platform to help reduce bias in our hiring process. Key Info Location: Remote, but you must be based in the UK with the legal right to work here Sponsorship: Unfortunately, we’re unable to offer visa sponsorship at this time Closing date: We’ll be reviewing applications as they come in and may close the role early If this sounds like the kind of role and team where you could do your life’s best work, we’d love to hear from you. Next steps You’ll answer some questions related to your day-to-day job. Your answers will go through our sift process: all answers will be anonymised, randomised, and then reviewed by a panel of reviewers (real humans). If you are shortlisted, we’ll invite you to the next stage, which will consist of a remote interview conducted over Zoom. We love giving feedback, so at the end of the application process, we'll share how well you performed. We aim to begin interviews in the week commencing 19 October 2026. We are receiving excellent responses to our job advertisements. This may lead us to close the role early, so if you are considering applying, then please get your application in early to avoid missing out. We are an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to a policy of Equal Employment Opportunity and are determined to ensure that no applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, or race, or is disadvantaged by conditions or requirements which cannot be shown to be justifiable.

item.title: Youth and Community Lead (Oasis Community Hub South Grimsby)
item.description: Youth and Community Lead Oasis Community Hub South Grimsby Hours: 30-40 hours per week (dependent on successful applicant) Contract: 12 Month Fixed Term Contract Salary: Grade D - £30,806 FTE Location: Oasis Space South Grimsby, with delivery across education and community settings in Grimsby Want to inspire young people through practical learning and youth work? Want to help young people develop confidence, resilience and life skills? Want to lead an exciting community project that combines youth development, sustainability and education? At Oasis, our vision is for community: a place where everyone is included, making a contribution and reaching their God-given potential. We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed Youth and Community Lead to develop and deliver high-quality youth and community work across South Grimsby. This exciting role will lead the development of the Bike Barn Project , using bike maintenance and practical learning as a powerful tool to engage young people, build confidence, improve wellbeing and create positive pathways into education, employment and training. Working alongside schools, families, community partners and Oasis colleagues, you will help young people overcome barriers, build aspirations and access the support they need to thrive. While an interest in cycling and practical learning is important, you do not need to be a qualified bike mechanic. Oasis will provide funded training and ongoing support to develop the technical skills required for the role. Key Responsibilities Develop and deliver engaging youth work programmes that promote belonging, wellbeing, confidence and personal development. Build positive, professional relationships with children and young people, including those facing challenges or barriers to success. Lead the development and delivery of the Bike Barn Project across community and educational settings. Teach basic bike maintenance and repair activities following appropriate training and safety guidance. Work with schools and community partners to identify needs and provide targeted support and intervention. Support young people to develop leadership skills, volunteer opportunities and positive progression routes. Build strong relationships with families and make appropriate referrals to wider support services when needed. Promote environmental sustainability through bike refurbishment, reuse and recycling initiatives. Oversee project budgets, resources, tools and equipment. Identify funding opportunities and contribute to successful grant applications and reporting. Ensure all safeguarding, health and safety, risk assessment and data recording requirements are met. Be a visible and positive presence within the South Grimsby community and actively promote the Oasis ethos. The Successful Candidate Will Have Experience of working with children and young people and building positive, professional relationships. Experience delivering engaging, inclusive activities that support personal development and wellbeing. Strong communication, organisation and record-keeping skills. Knowledge of safeguarding principles and commitment to best practice. An interest in cycling, practical learning, sustainability and community development. The ability to work collaboratively with schools, families, volunteers and partner organisations. Experience of project coordination, funding applications or community development would be advantageous. A commitment to inclusion, equality, hope, perseverance and the Oasis ethos. As Part of the Package, Oasis Offers A pension scheme with a 7% employer contribution. A generous holiday allowance, starting at 25 days per year plus 8 Bank Holidays. Oasis-funded training, including youth work and bike mechanic qualifications where required. Family-friendly policies and wellbeing support. Opportunities for professional development and career progression within Oasis. To Apply Please submit: Your CV A supporting statement (maximum two A4 pages) Please use your supporting statement to explain how your experience, skills and personal qualities meet the requirements of the role. Closing Date: 23rd October 2026 Interview Date: w/c 26th October 2026 We actively encourage applications from people of all ethnic backgrounds and underrepresented groups. If you require any assistance to overcome potential barriers during the recruitment process, please let us know. We appreciate you may wish to use AI to support elements of your application, but we strongly encourage all candidates to submit applications that genuinely reflect their own skills, achievements and lived experiences. It is what makes your application stand out. Oasis is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. All staff are expected to share this commitment. Appointment will be subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks, including an Enhanced DBS check The successful candidate must have the right to work in the UK. Oasis cannot assist with sponsorship or visa application. Oasis supports Equal Opportunities. Oasis supports Equal Opportunities. Registered Charity No. 1163889

item.title: Service Manager (Maternity Cover)
item.description: About the Role: Some services need more than strong management — they need a leader who can hold the whole picture, set the standard and keep young people’s futures at the centre when the work is busy, fast-moving and high stakes. As Service Manager for a service working with 16 plus children and care leavers you'll play a vital role in providing effective leadership to an integrated and multi-functional team providing an assessment, support and move on to the young people we accommodate. You’ll be responsible for the safe, effective and high-quality delivery of the service, bringing confident oversight across safeguarding, housing management, risk, performance, quality, staffing and day-to-day operations. You’ll lead with presence and purpose, supporting your team to deliver consistent, personalised and trauma-informed support that helps young people build stability, independence and stronger future pathways. You’ll also play a key role in strengthening partnership working across Greenwich, including with local authorities, commissioners and partner agencies. From referrals and move-on pathways to Ofsted readiness, data, young people’s feedback and continuous improvement, you’ll make sure the service is not only well run, but constantly learning, improving and ambitious for the young people it supports. At Single Homeless Project (SHP), you’ll also be part of a supportive learning culture, with access to training, development and opportunities to keep growing as a leader while shaping a service that really matters. About you: You bring strong experience managing accommodation-based, residential, youth, housing, social care or similar services, with the confidence to lead a sizeable team and hold service-wide standards. You understand the responsibilities that come with managing a young people’s service, including safeguarding, housing management, health and safety, performance, quality and risk. You’re confident supporting teams to work with young people facing multiple disadvantage, using trauma informed, psychologically informed and strengths-based practice to shape meaningful, personalised support. You can balance warmth with accountability, creating a team culture where staff feel supported, clear on expectations and able to deliver high-quality work. You build trust quickly with staff, young people and partners, and bring the integrity, curiosity and courage needed to lead a service where people can thrive. About SHP: We’re London’s leading homelessness charity – and we get things done. In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we’re not shying away. We’re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up. We’re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own. Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that’s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You’ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that’s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable. We’re not perfect, but we’re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn’t just a job. It’s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind. Important Info: Closing Date: Sunday 18th October at midnight Interview Date: Wednesday 28th or Thursday 29th October at SHP Head Office in Kings Cross Please note there will be a second stage interview in service in Greenwich for suitable candidates This post will require an Enhanced DBS check to be processed for the successful applicant. Please note applications are reviewed for AI use in application questions. Applications with insufficient/without current right to work or requiring sponsorship will not be accepted for this role.

item.title: Digital Communications Officer
item.description: Job Title: Digital Communications Officer Reporting to: PR and Communications Manager Responsible for : No direct reports Based: Our Head Office is based in London, but we have an agile working policy enabling people to work at another UK location up to 4 days/week. Occasional travel within the UK and out of hours work is required (e.g. for the annual British Science Festival) Hours: Full-time (35 hours per week). Requests for part-time or flexible working will be considered. Contract: Permanent Salary: £34,572 to £36,506 FTE per annum About Us The British Science Association (BSA) was founded in 1831 and is a registered charity. We are creating a future where science is more relevant, representative, and connected to society. We have ambitious goals to put people at the heart of science. About the role The Digital Communications Officer will be responsible for delivering communications activity for several British Science Association programmes and campaigns, including the British Science Festival, Smashing Stereotypes, and Equality, Diversity and Inclusion in Science and Health (EDIS). You will create engaging written, short-form video and graphic design content for our websites, newsletters, and social media channels. You will work closely with the PR and Communications Manager and wider Communications Team on the British Science Association’s mix of established and evolving programmes and national campaigns. Key responsibilities Produce the British Science Association’s Smashing Stereotypes campaign by developing an engaging multimedia communications plan, and liaising with external suppliers, freelancers, and partners; Work with the PR and Communications Manager to develop content for the British Science Association’s main social media channels, including TikTok, LinkedIn, BlueSky and Instagram; focusing on the development, filming and editing of short-form video content; monitor and respond appropriately to online comments and enquiries, including escalating as relevant; Design on-brand infographics or visual assets for digital channels for occasional projects not outsourced to contractors; Plan, deliver, and optimise paid advertising campaigns across social media platforms for key campaigns; Oversee the content of the British Science Association website and work with its developers to ensure the website meets the needs of the organisation, and content is engaging, accurate, inclusive and accessible, and optimised for SEO; Produce high quality, engaging, inclusive and accessible copy and content for various formats, including newsletters, news stories, blog posts, social media posts and internal communications to suit the intended audiences of the relevant programme, campaign or project; Produce analysis and reports on any relevant campaigns and outputs, as well as review the performance of the British Science Association website; Contribute to the British Science Festival marketing and communications campaign, including producing social media assets and engaging video and written content before and during the Festival, supporting the Festival team and Head of Marketing and Communications with ticketing reports and analytics, and supporting the PR and Communications Manager with press and media where required; Support Communications team colleagues to proofread and edit copy produced by other colleagues, ensuring it meets the British Science Association’s house style requirements and reflects the relevant programme’s brand, core messaging and tone of voice; Support the wider Communications team as needed; Perform any other tasks as reasonably required by the line manager. About you The successful candidate will bring the following experience, skills and approach. Essential criteria Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Experience of producing engaging written copy for different audiences and various formats/platforms; can demonstrate ability to turn complex information into clear, accurate and accessible content. Experience of using social media platforms in a professional context; including creating, delivering and evaluating organic and budgeted social media campaign plans across multiple platforms. Experience and knowledge of producing engaging video content and digital assets for a variety of platforms, using Canva, Clipchamp or equivalent apps. Experience of evaluating success, which could include producing reports, data analysis or use of analytics platforms, and using this data to adapt and improve future projects. Experience of working on multiple projects at once, as well as able to demonstrate how to prioritise workload effectively. Experience of working on communications campaigns as part of a PR, marketing or communications team. Excellent and adaptable digital skills and an awareness of current trends, issues, and technologies in the platforms, channels and methods used to deliver communications campaigns. Excellent attention to detail, including the ability to proofread and edit copy efficiently. Experience of generating creative ideas for delivering messages to different audiences. Experience using Content Management Systems. Desirable criteria We don’t expect applicants to have all of the following criteria, but having one or more of the following would be helpful in the role Awareness / experience of the ways that equity, diversity and inclusion need to be considered when delivering campaigns and other communications outputs. An interest in future developments or innovative tactics in the communications sector. The closing date for applications is 15 October 2026. N.B. We reserve the right to close early based on application levels. Interviews are due to take place on 18 November 2026. Interested? If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position. As part of the British Science Association’s commitment to being a Disability Confident employer, all disabled applicants who meet the ‘essential criteria’ for this vacancy will be offered an interview under our guaranteed interview scheme. No agencies please.

item.title: Peripatetic Service Coordinator - Mental Health
item.description: We are looking for an experienced and compassionate leader to join our Mental Health Services as a Peripatetic Service Coordinator, supporting teams across Bristol and South Gloucestershire . This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the lives of people with complex mental health needs while supporting and developing high-performing teams. As a Service Coordinator , you will lead teams to support people with complex mental health needs to achieve their goals, build independence, and develop the skills and confidence needed to live fulfilling lives within their communities. You will help people build resilience, develop practical life skills, strengthen community connections, and take greater control of their future through person-centred support. You will be an inspirational and supportive leader with excellent communication and listening skills, able to motivate, develop and empower colleagues to deliver outstanding support. You will have a strong understanding of person-centred practice and a commitment to promoting positive mental health, wellbeing and recovery-focused support. You will ensure services operate safely, effectively and in line with relevant legislation, regulations and organisational standards, while evidencing positive outcomes for the people we support. Key responsibilities include: Managing the day-to-day operation of services, including rota planning and resource allocation, to ensure people receive the right support at the right time. Supporting teams to co-produce and regularly review support plans, risk assessments and positive risk management strategies. Providing regular supervision, coaching and performance support to team members, while ensuring training and development needs are met. Contributing to referrals, assessments and service transition planning. Monitoring service budgets and expenditure in line with organisational expectations. Providing direct, hands-on support when required and leading by example in delivering high-quality care and support. The successful candidate will: Demonstrate strong leadership skills, with experience of supervising, leading or coordinating a team. Be highly organised and able to prioritise competing demands in a fast-paced environment. Have experience supporting people with complex mental health needs and a sound understanding of recovery-focused practice. Be confident in responding to people who are experiencing acute mental illness, in dynamic risk management and developing escalation plans to ensure that people receive the support that they need. Have knowledge of mental health services, legislation and best practice, including experience of trauma-informed approaches. Be flexible to work across a seven-day service, including a variety of shift patterns as required. In return, you will have the opportunity to lead dedicated teams, shape service delivery, and support people on their recovery journey within a values-driven organisation committed to learning, inclusion and continuous improvement. At Milestones Trust we recognise that without the hard work, commitment and passion of our staff, we wouldn’t be the charity that we are today. In return, we are committed to rewarding you with a competitive pay and benefits package including: 34 days ’ annual leave, including recognised public holidays Learning and development to support your career growth Nationally recognised qualifications , from entry‑level care to management Flexible working , with rotas provided in advance Occupational Sick Pay after two years, increasing with service Health Cash Plan after probation, offering at least £695 cashback for health treatments (dental, optical, therapies, maternity/paternity, prescriptions) Enhanced maternity and paternity pay Free enhanced DBS check Dayforce Wallet, giving you access to your earnings before payday Employee referral scheme with financial rewards Employee Assistance Programme from day one, offering confidential 24/7 support Company pension scheme to help grow your retirement savings We pride ourselves with being able to offer staff opportunities to develop and progress their careers within the Trust.

item.title: Campaigns Manager
item.description: The Mental Health Foundation is recruiting for a Campaigns Manager to support our Policy & Influencing team. Deadline: 5pm on Sunday 11th October ( we reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive plenty of suitable applications - if you're interested, we encourage you to apply soon!) Location: London or Glasgow Salary: Starting salary £38,193 rising to £42,385, plus London weighting of £4,000 where applicable Hours: Full-time (32 hours per week) Contract type: Permanent We are looking for a passionate and creative campaigner to lead bold, impactful campaigns that drive real policy change and inspire public action to prevent poor mental health. You'll bring together colleagues across policy, research, public affairs, media and marketing to create powerful, integrated campaigns that influence decision-makers, engage communities and spark lasting social change. What does the role involve? Plan, develop and execute impactful campaigns to drive forward policy changes, increase public understanding and support for prevention of poor mental health, and improve mental health awareness. Identify and develop creative opportunities to amplify campaign messages across various platforms, including digital channels, media, with politicians, and with fundraising audiences. Work with people with lived experience of mental health to improve and coproduce our campaigns. What skills, knowledge and experience are we looking for? Understanding of campaigning and influencing, including campaigning strategy and theory of change. Expertise in using digital communication tools and platforms for campaigning activity. Experience in developing and implementing engaging public campaigns which drive social change. Safeguarding is Everyone’s business – Mental Health Foundation is committed to safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of all its beneficiaries, those who surround them, its staff, volunteers, and anyone else who comes into contact with its services and expects all trustees, staff, and volunteers to share this commitment. The successful applicant will be subject to appropriate vetting procedures (proof of eligibility to work in the UK, proof of residency and satisfactory employment screening, including a Disclosure check and two most recent references) along with 3-year renewals of Disclosure checks. We are unable to provide sponsorship for this post, you must be able to demonstrate your eligibility to work in the UK. How to apply If you think your skills match and you’d like to be part of a dynamic and growing organisation, please complete and submit your application via our website. Please ensure you attach an up-to-date CV and statement of suitability answering all points of the person specification. Applications will close at 5pm on Sunday 11th October and we are unable to accept late applications. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive plenty of suitable applications so we recommend applying as soon as you can. Interviews are planned for Thursday 22nd October. We believe our people should represent the communities, organisations and individuals we work with. Diversity and inclusion is a strategic priority for us as an employer and mental health charity, and we are proud to be signatories of the Business in the Community Race at Work Charter and the Disability Confident Committed Scheme. Applications from under-represented sections of the community are actively encouraged. If you have a disability, require any additional support or have any questions regarding the role, please contact us. We make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process and during employment. Disabled candidates who meet all the essential person specification criteria will be offered an interview. Therefore, please do ensure you tick the relevant box on the application form and clearly indicate in your application/covering letter if you consider yourself to meet the requirements of the Equality Act 2010 / Disability Discrimination Act 1995. We are currently operating mostly digital recruitment (including interviews via video conferencing). We operate a hybrid working model of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office and the rest working from home. We look forward to hearing from you!

item.title: Psychological Therapist
item.description: About the Refugee Council The Refugee Council is the nation’s largest refugee charity. For more than 70 years, we have supported people who have fled war, violence and persecution to find safety and rebuild their lives in Britain. Born in the aftermath of the Second World War, we have extensive experience helping refugees overcome the challenges of displacement and create brighter futures for themselves and their families. Working alongside community groups, partners and volunteers, we support refugees and people seeking asylum to rebuild their lives, integrate into communities, and play an active part in British society. Refugees are at the heart of everything we do, and we believe everyone deserves the opportunity to live a safe, purposeful and fulfilling life. Our Values Our values underpin everything we do: Inclusive: We work with – not for – refugees and people seeking asylum so they have an equal voice, co-producing projects and ensuring their expertise and experiences are at the heart of what we do. Collaborative: Working with others is a priority in order to have the collective impact that is vital to achieving policy and practice reform. Courageous: We speak out when we see injustice, cruelty and unfairness. We always stand up for what we believe is the right thing to do to transform the experiences of those seeking protection in our country. Respectful: We are respectful of all those we interact with. We treat everyone – our staff, volunteers, beneficiaries, partners and people we disagree with – with the same respect, professionalism and understanding. About the Role The Lewisham Sanctuary Seeking Wellbeing Service provides specialist mental health and wellbeing support to people seeking asylum, people arriving through Homes for Ukraine, newly recognised refugees and resettled refugees living in Lewisham. Working within a trauma-informed, human-rights-based and holistic model, you will provide specialist assessments and short-term psychological therapy of up to 12 sessions. Support is delivered both face-to-face and online. You will manage a therapeutic caseload, conduct holistic assessments and provide culturally sensitive interventions designed to strengthen clients’ resilience, safety and wellbeing. You will also work closely with colleagues, interpreters, referral partners, statutory services and community organisations to ensure clients can access the right support. Who We Are Looking For You will have a recognised professional qualification in counselling, psychotherapy, counselling or clinical psychology, or another relevant clinical mental health discipline. You will also be registered or accredited, or eligible for appropriate membership/accreditation, with a relevant professional or regulatory body such as HCPC, BACP or UKCP or another appropriate regulatory body. You’ll have: Experience of working with refugees and people seeking asylum in mental health settings. Experience of delivering trauma-informed counselling or psychotherapy. An understanding of the psychological and psychosocial impact of forced migration. Knowledge of how UK immigration and asylum policy can affect people’s mental health, wellbeing and everyday lives. The ability to undertake holistic biopsychosocial assessments and make appropriate referrals. Confidence in assessing and responding to risk, including suicidal ideation and self-harm. The ability to work sensitively and professionally with people affected by trauma, loss and separation. Strong cultural awareness and an understanding of different attitudes towards mental health. Strong communication, organisational and IT skills, with the ability to manage a caseload effectively. Why Join the Refugee Council At the Refugee Council, we care about our people. We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support your wellbeing, work/life balance and professional development, including: Flexible working and hybrid working arrangements. 28 days' annual leave, rising to 30 days with service (excluding bank holidays), plus the option to purchase additional annual leave. Group personal pension scheme with up to 5% employer contribution. Life assurance. Ongoing learning and development opportunities. Interest-free loans, including season ticket loans and cycle-to-work scheme. Employee assistance programme providing confidential advice and wellbeing support. Our Commitment to Inclusion We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, particularly those with lived experience of the UK refugee protection system. If you meet most of the essential criteria and are excited about the role, we'd encourage you to apply. We value different experiences and perspectives and recognise that skills can be developed in different ways. Reasonable adjustments are available throughout the recruitment process and employment. If you require any adjustments, please let us know, and we will work with you to support your participation. For further information and to apply, please visit our website via the Apply button. Closing date: 23:45 on 8 October 2026. We encourage early applications as we reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications. Interviews: w/c 12 October 2026. Successful applicants may be required to undergo a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, where applicable to the role.
item.dc:creator: Refugee Council

item.title: Network and Funds Coordinator
item.description: Salary - £30,875 - £31,688 Location - London, United Kingdom Team - Network and Funds Directorate Line Manager - Director of Network and Funds Hours - 35 hours per week Contract - Fixed Term (12 months) Deadline - 8 October 2026 (23:59 BST) The Vacancy ABOUT THE ROLE The Network and Funds Coordinator plays a key role within Start Network’s Network and Funds Directorate, providing trusted, high-quality support to the Director of Network and Funds and helping to keep a busy, strategic portfolio of work moving forward. From coordinating priorities, meetings and communications to building strong relationships and keeping actions on track, the role brings organisation, momentum and attention to detail to the Director’s day-to-day work. Working with discretion, initiative and professionalism, the Coordinator will create the structure and connections that enable the Director to focus on strategic priorities and delivering impact. This is a varied and rewarding role for someone who enjoys making things happen, anticipating what is needed and contributing to the smooth and effective running of a dynamic Directorate. WHAT IS START NETWORK? Our purpose is to be a catalyst for system-level change that improves the efficiency, effectiveness and ethics of humanitarian action. We do this by working as a network to develop, test & spread new ways of collaborating and resourcing locally-led crisis response and anticipation. Our current membership is made up of nearly 145 local, national and international NGOs based all around the world. We also support 10 national and regional hubs made up of civil society organisations and NGOs as our vehicle for devolving power, resources and accountability. OUR VALUES WE PUT PEOPLE FIRST: Communities come first in our decision-making and programming. WE ARE BRAVE: We have great ambition and are willing to explore new things and take risks to achieve it WE OPERATE COLLECTIVELY: We leverage the value of working as a network, sharing risk and resources, and learning together. WE ARE INCLUSIVE: We see the value in diverse perspectives and work to remove the barriers that prevent voices from being heard. WE ARE OPEN: We work transparently and with integrity, building mutual trust in all levels of our work, from governance to programming. WE ARE ETHICAL: We behave and operate based on key principles of anti-racism, non-discrimination, and anti-colonialism. This is a work in progress. OUR OFFER TO YOU Being a part of a network involved in bringing change to the humanitarian sector. Hybrid working with options to work from home and remotely to support your work/life balance Employee Assistance Programme through Smart Health (depends on the country based) Family friendly policies, e.g., flexible working, maternity policy, parental leave and more! 25 days’ holiday (if UK based) plus 2 company days over the End of Year period for all staff (depends on the country based) INFORMATION FOR CANDIDATES Our roles are open to discussion about flexible working. For part-time working and job-shares, please get in touch with us before putting in an application. We are committed to ensuring that our recruitment process is accessible, inclusive and fair to all candidates. If you require a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the recruitment or selection process, please let us know. We will work with you to understand your needs and, where reasonably practicable, put appropriate adjustments in place to support your full participation. Start Network is committed to protecting people, particularly children, at-risk adults and affected populations from any harm. We are also committed to safeguarding staff from any forms of bullying, harassment, sexual harassment, discrimination, and abuse of power as outlined in the Dignity at Work policy. Start Network embraces diversity, promotes equality of opportunity and eliminates unlawful discrimination. We are an equal opportunities employer and treat every application on merit alone. We particularly encourage applications from disabled, BAME, LGBTQ+ and non-binary candidates. We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for disabled applicants who meet our essential selection criteria set out in the Person Profile. APPLICATION Please contact the People and Culture Team if you have any questions or need support with your application. We use Recruitment+ IRIS Cascade as our online recruitment platform. Recruitment+ IRIS Cascade allows you to demonstrate your skills and abilities through blind-review by our team to reduce bias. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications and we may review candidates on an ongoing basis, so please apply early where possible to avoid disappointment. Any offer of employment will be conditional subject to relevant checks. Please refer to our privacy candidate privacy notice regarding treatment of your data. Start Network also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. The core of the scheme is that participating organisations share information about safeguarding-related misconduct (i.e., sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment) that a candidate has been found to have committed during employment, or incidents under investigation when the candidate left employment. For more information regarding this scheme, please visit their website. The Company Start Network is made up of more than 90 non-governmental organisations across five continents, ranging from large international organisations to local and national NGOs. Our programmes allow members to deliver humanitarian action around the world. Our mission is to create a new era of humanitarian action that will save even more lives. We aren’t driven by media headlines or political will, we’re here for the communities affected by and at risk of crises. We are an organisation committed to doing things differently. For some roles, we need more technical humanitarian expertise, but for other roles, we are looking for relevant transferable skills, the right attitude, and a passion to bring change.

item.title: Corporate Partnership Executive
item.description: Corporate Partnership Executive Reporting to: Corporate Partnerships Manager Location of work: London-based with at least three days per week required at Deutsche Bank’s London Office at 21 Moorfields. Beyond partner requirements, Magic Breakfast has a hybrid approach including working from home and occasional meetings at the charity’s London office. The role may also involve some occasional travel throughout England and Scotland including to Deutsche Bank’s Birmingham office. Contract type: Ideally full-time, 35 hours per week, although part time / flexible hours may be considered. The role may require occasional evening and weekend work Contract Length: This is a fixed term contract starting 11th January 2027 until 31st January 2028. Salary: £31,500 BACKGROUND For more than 20 years, Magic Breakfast has been helping children and young people start the day with the nourishment they need to learn, grow, and thrive. But the impact of breakfast goes far beyond food. Every morning, we help pupils arrive at school feeling valued, included, and ready to reach their potential. Today, 2.1 million children across the UK are at risk of hunger, the equivalent of four pupils in a classroom of 30. Working with schools in disadvantaged communities across England and Scotland, Magic Breakfast is committed to ensuring no child is too hungry to learn. One breakfast at a time, we are helping children and young people build brighter futures. This is a pivotal moment to join Magic Breakfast. Governments in both England and Scotland have committed to expanding access to free school breakfasts, recognising the vital role they play in children’s wellbeing and attainment. Yet significant gaps remain. Pupils in secondary schools, alongside younger children in nursery and early years settings, are still at risk of starting the day hungry. Hunger does not begin at age five, nor end at age 11, and neither does our mission. By joining Magic Breakfast, you will become part of a passionate, ambitious organisation driving lasting change for children and young people across the UK. JOB PURPOSE Magic Breakfast has a motivated and high performing Corporate Partnerships team which was successful in securing a transformational two-year partnership with Deutsche Bank, beginning in January 2026. We are now seeking a Corporate Partnerships Executive to support the Corporate Partnerships Manager who will together be dedicated to supporting that partnership, whilst also supporting the wider team. Background on the partnership: Deutsche Bank’s UK Charity of the Year programme is a two-year partnership with Magic Breakfast beginning January 2026 with an ambition of raising £2m over that time. The partnership is significant for the charity, comprising employee volunteering and fundraising, match giving and strategic support. The partnership also has the potential ensure a legacy beyond the 24-month partnership. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES As the Corporate Partnerships Executive, you will work with a Corporate Partnerships Manager to deliver one of the charity’s largest, most high-profile and multi-faceted partnerships to date. Together you will work closely with colleagues in the Corporate Partnerships Team and across the organisation, to maximise potential of this transformational partnership. You will also collaborate closely with the CSR Team at Deutsche Bank and their wider employee network. You will seize opportunities to make personal connections and effectively deliver a varied range of activity such as event fundraising, payroll giving and employee volunteering. In addition, you will be expected to support other corporate partnerships and collaborate with the wider fundraising team to deliver projects and implement processes that support Magic Breakfast’s Fundraising & Development team in achieving its income targets and wider success. Please see the job description below for more infromation APPLICATION PROCCESS Should you wish to discuss the role before applying please email our People and Culture Team (recruitment @ magicbreakfast. com) Application close date: 11th October Shortlisting: 12th, 13,th 14th October Interview 1: 21st - 22nd October Interview: 27th and 28th October Due to the high volume of applications, this role is likely to close early and we reserve the right to do so. This is to ensure that we can manage application levels whilst maintaining a positive candidate experience. Unfortunately, once a vacancy has closed, we are unable to consider further applications.

item.title: Financial Resilience Adviser
item.description: Salary: Grade 3 - £32,585 per annum plus £5,023 London Weighting if applicable Contract: Fixed term until 23rd April 2028 Location: Either London or Sheffield Hours: 35 per week – Full time Closing date: Wednesday 7th October 2026 at 11.30pm Join Shelter as a Financial Resilience Adviser in our mission to drive systemic change and fight for housing justice. At a time when the housing emergency continues to deepen, your experience could help transform lives and challenge the systems that perpetuate injustice. Come and play a central role in our mission to defend the right to a safe, and secure home. Working with Shelter means being part of a passionate team that believes a safe home is a fundamental right. Here, your skills don’t just change lives - they shape a fairer housing system. About The Role Delivering advice and advocacy in a variety of community settings, you will provide casework on debt, along with housing and welfare benefits, ensuring that quality assurance and standards are met in all areas and that you keep your own knowledge up to date. Identifying systemic issues by gathering evidence and developing insight will be crucial to bringing about the change we need, as well as working with a variety of stakeholders, building relationships locally and working collaboratively to achieve shared outcomes. About You You have demonstrable experience of providing debt advice and related advice on housing and welfare, in line with current legislation Experience supporting people with multiple disadvantages. You are able to manage your caseload and meet deadlines You have effective communication skills and technical skills, using IT programmes to communicate and record client data. Everything you do will be in line with safeguarding procedures, our anti – racism goals and Equality and Diversity policies and practices. Benefits We offer a wide range of benefits, including 30 days of annual leave, enhanced family friendly policies, pension and interest free travel loans. Our employees also have access to a tenancy deposit loan, payroll giving, cycle to work scheme and an employee assistance programme. About The Team This role will be part of our ongoing work with our Hero Partner which aims to build financial resilience and break the cycles that lead to financial exclusion and poor financial health negatively impacting people’s housing situations. With the ongoing cost of living crisis, we provide support to people in financial crisis and build resilience in the most vulnerable communities. About Shelter Home is a human right. It’s our foundation and where we thrive. Yet every day millions of people are being devastated by the housing emergency. We exist to defend the right to a safe home. Because home is everything. We need ambitious, passionate people to join us. This is your chance to play a part in the fundamental change we are striving to achieve. Our enemy is the social injustice at the core of the escalating housing emergency. To win this fight, we must be representative of the people we are here to help and those who support our movement. In all our people decisions, we take pride in being inclusive, equitable and transparent. We are committed to combating racism both within and outside Shelter. We welcome you on our journey to becoming truly anti-racist. How to Apply Please click ‘Apply for Job’ . You are required to submit your work history and a supporting statement. The supporting statement should include your responses to the first four points in the ‘About You’ section of the job description of no more than 1000 words in total . P lease state at the top of your supporting statement which location(s) you would like to be considered for. Please provide specific examples following the STAR format and ensure you demonstrate how you address the behaviours below in your responses: We prioritise diversity and have an inclusive and open mindset Any applications submitted without a supporting statement will not be considered. Safeguarding Statement Safeguarding is everyone's business. Shelter is committed to protecting the health, wellbeing and human rights of those we support, and enabling them to live free from harm, abuse and neglect.All our staff will be expected to observe professional standards of behaviour and conduct their work in line with our Safeguarding Policies. Recruitment Agencies Shelter does not accept unsolicited CVs from external recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them.

item.title: Community Integration Officer & Community Integration Lead
item.description: Involve Northwest are recruiting for a Community Integration Officer & Community Integration Lead to work in partnership with Standguide Ltd and The Growth Company. Job Title: Community Integration Officer Service/Project: Connect to Work Location: The Community Village, Rock Ferry, and the Wirral community. Reporting To: Contract Manager Direct Staff : None This role is subject to an Enhanced DBS check and subscription to the Update Service in line with internal safer recruitment policy. Connect to Work is a free, voluntary supported employment programme funded by the UK Government's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP). As a core part of the national "Get Britain Working" strategy, it helps individuals facing long-term health conditions, disabilities, or complex personal barriers secure or maintain sustainable employment. Instead of using rigid, traditional job-search methods, Connect to Work relies on a personalised "place, train, and maintain" model. This approach matches participants with a dedicated Employment Specialist to build a custom action plan and offer continuous on-the-job support. The programme specifically supports individuals facing any of the following barriers: People with disabilities or long-term health conditions (including mental health challenges, autism, or ADHD) · Carers and ex-carers · Armed Forces veterans, current personnel, and their partners · Care-experienced young people and care leavers · Refugees (including those on Afghan resettlement or Ukrainian schemes) · Individuals experiencing homelessness · Offenders and ex-offenders · Survivors of domestic abuse or modern slavery · People with a history of drug or alcohol dependence Job Purpose: 1. To support the effective delivery of the Connect to Work programme by and building strong partnerships across internal teams and external organisations to identify individuals suitable for Connect to Work employment specialist support. 2. To act as a point of contact for partners, ensuring services are joined up, referral pathways are effective, and collaborative working supports positive employment outcomes for participants. 3. Contribute to shaping and embedding partnership and integration practices across the delivery team with a wider objective of achieving referral outcomes in line with the Connect to Work contract and IPS fidelity framework. Core Duties and Responsibilities: · Community engagement is an integral part of the role – this role will need to identify a range of engagement methods to support the Connect to Work profile groups requiring support · Co-ordinate partnership activity to ensure services are aligned and focused on positive participant employment outcomes · Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of integrated working partnerships across internal teams and external partners and stakeholders · Market the Connect to Work provision in person and remotely · Support the management of clear referral pathways and operational processes between Connect to Work and partner organisations · Work closely with delivery staff to ensure partners understand programme aims, eligibility criteria, processes, and participant journeys · Identify gaps, risks, or barriers in partnership working and support the development of practical solutions · Working with individuals to help them to develop and work towards their goals. · Connect people to and share information about services, activities, groups, and assets. · Engage a multitude of individuals who are striving to seek employment. · Coordinate and support partnership meetings, multi-agency forums, and working groups, including preparation of agendas, tracking actions, and follow-up · Contribute to continuous service improvement by sharing learning, good practice, and feedback from partners and delivery teams · Maintain accurate and up to date records of engagement and activity in line with data protection, information security and information governance requirements. · Represent Connect to Work at internal and external partnership meetings, events, and forums as required Communication, Quality & Improvement · Produce clear, accurate, and professional communications, and briefings relating to integration and partnership activity to the Community Integration Lead. · Gather feedback from partners and internal teams to inform service development and improvements. · Keep up to date with relevant local, regional, and national developments that may impact partnership working within Connect to Work. Company Duties and Responsibilities: · To work in line with set company policies and procedures, and statutory requirements with particular reference to Health & Safety (including Safeguarding), The Prevent strategy, Equality / Diversity, ‘Access for All’, Discipline and Grievance. · To work to set standards and legislation, including ISO9001:2015 and GDPR 2018. · To always represent the charity in the best manner. · To demonstrate a commitment to the vision, values, and strategic aims of Involve Northwest. · To maintain high standards of professionalism and keep abreast of current legislation, standards, best practice and maintain a focus of continuous improvement. · To work within the practice standards of the Connect Us Service. · Prepare, deliver, or participate in any appropriate learning or development programmes or courses as required by the company; this includes any staff meetings · To maintain continual professional development Person Specification - Essential Experience · Experience working with people facing barriers to employment including health conditions and disabilities · Experience/understanding of working with people with health support needs, or a similar client group within health, local authority, or the voluntary sector · Experience of working with people on a one-to-one basis · Proven experience in developing networks and building strong partnerships to support customers goals · Experience of working or have an understanding of supported employment programmes, such as IPS · Experience of working within communities with a diverse range of stakeholders. · Setting and maintaining appropriate boundaries with community member and professionals. · Experience of working as part of a service delivery team, collaborating effectively with others · Experience of targeted outcomes Knowledge and Skills · Able to use IT and tools such as MS Word, PowerPoint, and Excel · Ability to research information from a range of sources. · Understanding of social isolation and health and wellbeing. · Strong knowledge of the local labour market · Strong communication skills and the ability to build new connections with a wide range of individuals · Very strong written and verbal communication skills · Organisational and time management skills · Outstanding interpersonal skills and ability to build rapport with a range of people · Natural ability to build close, trusting, and productive relationships with people · Team orientated and works collaboratively within a mixed-disciplinary team · Ability to work independently and use initiative to develop and promote a service. · Ability to drive/access a vehicle for work purposes and willingness to travel within the region. Personal Attributes · Be compassionate and empathetic with your client’s situation. · Act with integrity and respect when working with all clients, agencies, and Individuals. · Flexible, adaptable, and strong team player and a good active listener. · Be a team player with an open and honest manner, with the ability to build on effective relationships and work collaboratively with community leaders, local authority, and professionals. · Ability to ‘step back’ and enable communities to do for themselves. · Able to prioritise tasks, workload, and good time management skills. · Be motivational and empowering. · Political awareness with and ability to influence, challenge and support. · Believe everyone has something essential to contribute to build communities regardless of their past experiences or the labels others have placed on them and are focused on the ‘gifts’ of individuals. · The ability to monitor and report case work and statistics and work to specific project targets. · Be optimistic about the possibility of personal growth and change. · Motivate individuals and agencies to move through courses of action and decision-making processes. · Ability to develop knowledge of a broad range of occupations and jobs. · Empathy with the needs of those with health support needs · Passion and drive to make a positive difference to people's lives · Highly motivated with a genuine belief that someone with a health condition can find paid employment · Resilient and tenacious to not give up despite setbacks and frustrations · Self-aware of personal strengths and weaknesses and actively invest in personal and professional development ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Job Title: Community Integration Lead Service/Project: Connect to Work Location: The Community Village, Rock Ferry, and the Wirral community. item.title: Finance Business Partner
item.description: Job Title: Finance Business Partner Location: Home-based, with attendance at the AdviceUK London office (83 Victoria Street, London, SW1H 0HW) and meetings as required. This includes 4 annual All Staff Days. Status: Permanent Reporting to : Financial Controller Responsible for: No direct reports Salary: £40,000–£45,000 per annum; £32,000–£36,000 per annum for 28 hours per week, depending on experience. Working hours: 35 hours per week. We would consider 28 hours per week for the right candidate, within normal operating hours of 8.00am–6.30pm, Monday–Friday. Lunch and other breaks are unpaid. Special conditions: Some evening and weekend work may be required, for which time off in lieu (TOIL) will be granted. Interview Process: The recruitment process will consist of two stages: Stage 1: An informal interview via Microsoft Teams. Stage 2: An in-person interview at the AdviceUK office in Victoria, London, on Monday 9 November. We are committed to diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from all backgrounds, particularly encouraging those from underrepresented groups. CHARITY OVERVIEW Since 1979, AdviceUK has been supporting advice organisations by helping them to be efficient, competent and effective, and by campaigning for a policy environment that supports advice agencies and people needing advice. We are both a membership body and charity. We support our 700+ members to provide advice to around 2 million people every year. We are working towards a world in which every individual, regardless of means, is able to access the advice they need to exercise their rights and deal with any legal and social welfare challenges they may face. JOB PURPOSE The Finance Business Partner provides clear financial analysis, advice and practical support to managers and budget holders across AdviceUK. Working under the direction of the Financial Controller, the postholder helps colleagues understand financial performance, manage budgets, forecast effectively and make well-informed decisions. The role combines business partnering with management reporting and proportionate support for funding, commercial activity, audit and finance improvement. It suits someone who can build trusted relationships, explain finance clearly and take ownership of high-quality work while escalating significant issues appropriately. KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Business Partnering and Advice Act as the main finance contact for allocated teams, programmes or projects, building an understanding of their activities, funding and financial priorities. Work with managers and budget holders to understand performance, pressures, risks and opportunities, and agree practical actions. Explain financial information, policies and delegated authorities clearly to non-finance colleagues. Provide constructive challenge while maintaining positive working relationships and supporting sound decision-making. Help improve financial awareness through guidance, training and practical support 2. Budgeting, Forecasting and Planning Work with budget holders to prepare realistic annual budgets and regular forecasts for allocated areas. Monitor actual performance against budget and forecast, investigate significant variances and agree follow-up action. Identify emerging pressures, risks and opportunities and ensure they are reflected in forecasts and reported to the Financial Controller. Prepare proportionate financial models and scenario analysis for projects, funding bids, business cases and proposed changes. Contribute financial information to workforce and longer-term organisational planning. 3. Reporting and Analysis Produce accurate, timely and accessible budget reports and management information for managers and budget holders. Analyse monthly performance and provide concise commentary on material movements, trends, risks and opportunities. Contribute analysis and commentary to management accounts and reports for the Senior Leadership Team and trustees, as requested by the Financial Controller. Maintain useful reporting tools and dashboards, ensuring information is reliable and suited to its audience. Investigate unusual transactions or trends and escalate material concerns promptly. 4. Funding, Commercial Activity and Compliance Work with relevant colleagues to prepare budgets and financial information for funding applications, grant monitoring and funder reports. Monitor the financial position of allocated grants and flag potential underspends, overspends or compliance risks. Provide financial input to commercial proposals and business cases, including costs, pricing, affordability and financial risk. Support the Financial Controller with information and evidence for the annual audit, grant audits and other external reviews. Apply AdviceUK's financial policies and controls consistently and raise control or compliance concerns promptly. 5. Systems and Continuous Improvement Use finance systems, Excel and other digital tools effectively to analyse data and produce accurate reports. Maintain clear guidance and practical procedures for managers and budget holders. Identify and help implement proportionate improvements to finance processes, reporting and data quality. Contribute as a user to agreed finance system and automation improvements, working within organisational priorities and available resources. 6. General Responsibilities Ensure you effectively communicate AdviceUK's vision, mission and objectives to staff, members and external stakeholders. Ensure you demonstrate AdviceUK's values and behaviours in all aspects of your work. Build and maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, including staff, trustees, members, partners and suppliers. With support from your manager, deliver your agreed personal objectives and undertake any agreed development or training. Maintain a strong understanding of our members and the advice sector more generally by reading internal reports, accessing relevant data reports, following our social media channels and, where possible, attending member and other relevant events. With the agreement of your line manager, ensure you make time to speak to members and visit their services. Adhere at all times to AdviceUK's policies and procedures. Carry out any reasonable duties compatible with the post assigned by your line manager.
