item.title: People Management Officer (7-Month Maternity Cover)
item.description: About Forest Peoples Programme Forest Peoples Programme (FPP) is an international NGO that has been working with Indigenous Peoples and forest peoples for 35 years since it was established in 1990. As of 2026, we work in 18 countries across South and Central America, Africa, and Southeast Asia, with over 50 partners based in the tropical forest belt. We work directly and in solidarity with communities and peoples, supporting them to secure their rights to their traditional lands, territories, and resources, protect their forests and ways of life, and choose their own futures. Working at local, national and global levels FPP supports indigenous peoples and forest peoples to effect change from the bottom up – grounded in struggles to advance the enjoyment of their rights and seek remedy for violations. At the same time, we work to ensure the voices and priorities of indigenous peoples and forest peoples shape national and international law and policy – e.g. relating to business and human rights, climate, and biodiversity – so that resulting regulatory and market reform better serves and respects their rights. We have 70 people on the team including human rights lawyers, anthropologists and social scientists working with communities and local organisations around the global tropical belt. Up to half of the team live and work from their homes around the world. Role Summary The People Management Officer will provide professional people management and HR advisory support to FPP, working closely with the Managing Director and wider FPP team across a range of people matters while the current People Management Officer is on maternity leave. This is a 7-month fixed-term maternity cover position, commencing on 1 January 2027. The maternity cover for the current People Management Officer will have an initial 1 month’s hand over period before she goes on leave in February and will focus on maintaining key people management activities, providing advisory support to managers and ensuring continuity across core people processes during this period. There is a possibility, depending on funding available, following the maternity cover period, the successful candidate could be retained to join the People Management team at FPP to continue supporting FPP’s People Management function, with responsibilities evolving according to organisational priorities. The post holder will provide a combination of operational support and people advice, contributing to a positive working environment while ensuring FPP’s policies, procedures and practices remain effective, inclusive and aligned with organisational values. Initial priorities during maternity cover period During the maternity cover period, the post holder will prioritise: Maintaining continuity of core HR operations, including recruitment, onboarding, contracts, HR system, payroll liaison and employee records. Providing HR advice and support to managers and staff on day-to-day people matters. Supporting employee relations and more complex HR matters, escalating where appropriate. Providing support on safeguarding-related matters, working collaboratively with relevant colleagues to ensure appropriate processes and practices are followed. Supporting the Managing Director during a period of reduced HR capacity. Possibility of Longer-Term Role Development Following the maternity cover period, there is a possibility, funding dependant, that the role could continue to contribute to FPP’s People Management function, working alongside the Managing Director and People Management Officer to provide effective people support across the organisation. The balance of responsibilities will evolve according to organisational priorities, team capacity and the continued development of the People Management function. Key Responsibilities The People Management Officer will: Act as a first point of contact for managers and staff, providing practical HR advice and guidance across a range of people matters. Support employee relations matters, including attendance, performance, conduct, wellbeing and other people management matters. Coordinate recruitment, onboarding and employee lifecycle processes, helping to ensure an inclusive and positive candidate and employee experience. Prepare employment documentation, maintain accurate employee records and support key HR processes and systems. Provide support and advice on safeguarding-related people matters and contribute to the ongoing implementation of safeguarding policies and practices. Liaise with internal and external stakeholders, including payroll providers and external HR advisers, to support effective people management across the organisation. Coordinate learning and development activities, wellbeing initiatives and continuous improvement of HR processes and ways of working. Work closely with the Managing Director and wider team to provide effective people management support across the organisation. For full details of the role responsibilities and person specification, please refer to the attached Job Description. Person specification Essential qualities Experience working in a people/HR advisory role. Experience providing advice and guidance to managers on people-related matters. Experience managing and supporting employee relational matters, including providing advice on sensitive and complex issues. Experience working with HR systems and maintaining accurate employee records. Demonstrable knowledge of UK employment law and HR best practice. Understanding of safeguarding principles and experience applying safeguarding practices within an organisation. Personable and well organised Ability to both work collaboratively and independently, prioritise effectively and manage confidential information. Desirable qualities Experience working within an NGO, charity, international development or similar values-led organisation. HR qualification. Experience supporting employees across different countries and advising on international HR processes and employment requirements. Experience working with safeguarding issues involving partners, communities or external stakeholders. French and/or Spanish language competencies

item.title: Data & Impact Manager
item.description: We are looking for a Data and Impact Manager who will play a central role in ensuring the organisation is able to effectively collect, manage, analyse and use data to improve services, demonstrate impact and support strategic decision making. Reporting to the Head of Data & Impact, the postholder will lead the day-to-day operation of the organisation's data and reporting function. They will oversee reporting, data governance, data quality and impact measurement processes, whilst managing staff responsible for data operations and digital administration. The postholder will also work closely with the Head of Data & Impact to help shape and deliver the organisation's data and impact strategy, contributing to strategic planning and driving key transformation and improvement projects that strengthen organisational effectiveness and data-led decision-making. The role combines technical expertise, analytical thinking and people management, ensuring that robust processes and high-quality insights underpin the organisation's work. The role would require regular presence in London, as well as occasional evening and weekend work as the role holder will provide key events support. Time off in lieu will be given for evening Smart Works London is part of Smart Works Charity, and there will be liaison with the HQ team/centres across the U.K. and liaison with our regional teams to support induction, training and participation in regular meetings, phone calls and conferences with other Smart Works centres across the UK. To apply, please submit a CV, cover letter (no longer than 1 page), and answers to the following questions through our recruitment system by Sunday 11th October. Your application should be addressed to Meg Armishaw. Tell us about a time when you identified an important trend, issue or opportunity through data analysis. What data did you use, what insight did you uncover, and what changed as a result? (max 250 words) Data quality and governance are central to this role. Describe a situation where you identified a significant data quality or governance issue. What actions did you take and what was the outcome? (max 250 words) This role requires influencing colleagues across different teams to improve how data is collected, used and understood. Tell us about a time when you led a change in data processes, systems or reporting that required buy-in from multiple stakeholders. How did you gain support and what was the result? (max 250 words)

item.title: Recruitment Lead
item.description: Unifrog’s mission We’re on a mission to level the playing field when it comes to young people finding and applying for their next step after school. We're achieving this by bringing all the available information into one single, impartial, user-friendly platform that helps students to make the best choices, and submit the strongest applications. We also empower teachers and counsellors to manage the progression process effectively. Our outlook is global - we work with schools and universities all over the world, from the US to New Zealand, and from Italy to Hong Kong. We want to make it so that young people can compare every opportunity taught in English, wherever it is in the world, and have all the support they need to make successful applications. We have a clear social purpose, and we’re hugely ambitious. We already work with over half of UK secondary schools, and more than a thousand international schools. We are growing rapidly in terms of the number of our customers, in terms of how much they use our platform, and in terms of the breadth of products we offer. Our team is at the heart of our business and it is integral to our success. We work hard to foster a culture of openness, happiness and innovation, and we commit to helping every individual learn and grow so that they can reach their full potential. We want to hire talented people, whatever their background. If you are excited by our mission and are ready to work hard, please don’t hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you! We believe in the power of diversity. If you are from an ethnic minority background, we would like to strongly encourage you to apply. People and culture at Unifrog You’ll be joining Unifrog at an exciting time. We now have 2 million students using the platform each year, we work with over 5,000 schools, universities, and employers, and we have 120 people on the team. We’re super proud of the supportive culture we’ve fostered over that time. As a People team, we support that culture by: trusting our team; removing roadblocks and encouraging autonomy; making an effort to understand everyone’s different wants and needs and using that information to tailor what we offer; and caring about each team member while creating processes that allow them to work at their best. If this fits with your view of what a People team should do, we’d love to hear from you. What you’ll do As Recruitment Lead, your key role is to attract and appoint a diverse range of outstanding applicants. To that end, you’ll continue to develop our recruitment ethos: to set candidates up for success through a fair and inclusive process, while testing skills and capability over experience. As a small team, each People team member also has the opportunity to be involved in other areas beyond their core role. This role has a specific focus on developing and maintaining our excellent Unifrog perks and benefits and, alongside support from the team, providing a fantastic experience at our office HQ in Hoxton, London. Your main responsibilities: Recruitment (~70% of the role, varying week to week) Lead recruitment end-to-end, ensuring a high-quality, fair, and consistent candidate experience. Work with hiring managers to design job descriptions, interview processes, and scoring guidelines. Post our live roles on the relevant job boards (e.g. Escape the City, LinkedIn). Manage our Applicant Tracking System (ATS), review applications, update candidates, and schedule interviews. We’re in the process of switching our ATS, and you’ll play a leading role in setting up and developing this. Lead interview panels and support with phone interviews and tasks. Manage offers, including offer calls and contracts. Write regular whole-company updates to keep the team informed about new joiners and new roles, alongside reminders about key Unifrog updates. Lead on projects to improve recruitment, including creating guidance on AI use in recruitment , interview best practice, and the candidate hub . Manage the visa application process and provide support to employees requiring visa sponsorship. Monitor and manage our Recruitment inbox, being the first point of contact for queries from candidates. Work with the rest of the People team on the onboarding process, which is currently led by our People Assistant. Unifrog perks and benefits (~20% of the role) Gather team feedback and data about current and potential new benefits. Use this information to improve existing benefits and introduce new ones. Manage the rollout of new benefits. Recent examples include interest-free loans from Unifrog and a co-working allowance for all remote team members. Administer current benefits, such as SimplyHealth, life insurance, and health insurance for our Hong Kong office. Office support (~10% of the role) With support from the team, take the lead on organising our modest London office space, making sure that the layout supports team needs and wellbeing. Re-stock and check our equipment, tech, and supplies. Be a point of contact for external staff (e.g. building managers) for all our offices, in London, Edinburgh, and Hong Kong. Equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) At Unifrog, everyone is responsible for creating an equitable and inclusive place to work. In addition, each person on the People team also has specific EDI responsibilities which link to their role, and is given training and coaching to support them with this. Make sure our recruitment processes are equitable and inclusive. E.g. create and uphold guidelines to support consistency during interview panels; review our job descriptions to make sure they’re inclusive, accessible, and reflective of the role and skills needed. Review anonymised demographic data from our candidate pool to understand trends and improve our processes. Working together You’ll work closely with our current People team, including our two People Leads, People Assistant, Internal Communications and Events Lead, Head of People Operations, and People and Operations Director. You’ll have regular contact with people across all of our teams. You’ll need to build great professional relationships with team members to deliver an excellent recruitment process. You’ll be line-managed by the People and Operations Director. What we’re looking for Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to build great professional relationships. Excellent attention to detail, especially when creating JDs or rolling out new benefits. Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills. Ability to coach, challenge, and guide team members involved in hiring. Ability to convert hiring data into actionable insights. Experience of managing multiple and competing priorities. Experience of using an Applicant Tracking System (ATS) and ideally designing recruitment processes (including application and interview questions, and scoring guidelines). Ability to work both as part of a team and independently, and happy to ask for support when it’s needed. Strong reflection skills and a proactive attitude, demonstrating the ability to learn and adjust based on feedback. For example, moving beyond active job applicants to proactively identify talent pools and changing our approach based on what works. Benefits On our jobs page you’ll find a full list of the benefits we offer our team. Here’s a snapshot: Mission focused Join one of Escape the City’s top 1% employers and help transform careers and destinations for students. Be part of a growing company Become part of a committed, dynamic, and growing company. We want to build our team for the long term: if you do well, we will do our best to make sure you want to stay at the company for a long time. Grow individually Professional development is important at Unifrog. You will define your own 6-month objectives and will be supported by your line manager and the rest of the team to achieve them. You will have an annual training allowance to spend on what you need to grow and progress. Have impact Influence the company’s direction: we love to promote great ideas, wherever they come from. Key details £38,000 - £42,000 per year dependent on experience (Grade B). Full time. Split your time between home and our office in Hoxton, London (a minimum of 2 days per week). 28 days paid holiday per year (plus bank holidays). Working hours are 8:30am to 4:30pm, or 9:00am to 5:00pm Monday to Thursday, and 8.30am to 4:00pm or 9:00am to 4:30pm on Friday. Start date: as soon as possible, though we will be flexible for the right candidates. We can only consider candidates who have the right to work in the UK. Application process Deadline: 10:00am (BST) on Monday 12th October 2026 . We may need to close applications early if we receive a lot of interest. As long as you’ve already started applying, we’ll give you 48 hours’ notice of the deadline changing - so if you’re thinking of applying, please start an application so we can keep you updated. Stage 1: Application form (~1 hour) ✍️ Visit our website to upload your CV and complete the questions below. Please note that we do not review CVs at this stage of the application process, so please be as specific as possible about your experience. With reference to examples of your recent experience, what would make you an excellent candidate for this role? (250 words) Tell us about a time you improved a recruitment or People process using feedback or data. What changed? (250 words) Tell us about a time you disagreed with a hiring manager about a recruitment decision. How did you reach a resolution? (250 words) Stage 2: Phone interview (15 minutes) 📲 Stage 3: Video call interview (1 hour) 🖥️ Standard Q&A from a panel of three, including questions about your experiences and how these relate to the role, and scenario questions based on common situations you might face (plus time for your questions). Phone interviews will be held throughout the application window. Video call interviews will be held w/c 19th October 2026 . Your answer

item.title: Marketing Officer
item.description: With a 110-year history, we are proud to be able to say that the WI continues to be the largest and most influential UK women’s organisation, with over 170,000 members. Our campaigns push for change on the issues that matter to women and their communities, from equal pay to climate change, mental health and violence against women. The WI has brought about real change, and this record of action shows that we are as relevant today as we were in 1915. The National Federation of Women’s Institutes (the NFWI) is responsible for running the organisation and provides support and advice to members at both regional and local levels. About the role Operating across the full spectrum of media and platforms, you will implement innovative marketing campaigns that build engagement that positions the WI as the UK’s leading women’s organisation. We will look to you to help shape and deliver our marketing and communications strategy whilst championing innovation in print and digital advertising, video, audio, brand and sponsored content, affiliate marketing, influencing, websites and internal communications. Equally importantly, you will actively interpret data to drive campaigning and track your success through in-depth analytics, so you will require a highly analytical mindset and a meticulous approach to everything you do. Location: Hybrid, with one day a week at our London office. About you Experienced in managing multi-channel marketing campaigns and creating both print and digital content, you will be familiar with setting targets, interpreting brand guidelines, using content management systems and briefing external providers. You should be well versed in the digital landscape, including advertising, content optimisation, UX and engagement, and skilled in gathering data and analytics to measure engagement. Finally, exposure to a non-profit or membership organisation would be beneficial, as would a proven track record in copywriting, proofreading and creating training materials. Benefits In return, we will offer you a hybrid working arrangement, which means a minimum of one day a week in your primary office and the rest worked from home, although you can work up to three days in the office if preferred; 28 days’ annual leave, rising to 30 days on completion of 5 years’ service with the flexibility to take your annual leave in hours; membership of our healthcare scheme; enhanced family-friendly policies; a commitment to employee wellbeing; and more. How to apply For further information about this Marketing Officer role, please download the recruitment pack, which includes the job description and person specification. To apply, please visit our website via the Apply button. Closing date: 11 October 2026* *Please note that we reserve the right to close this recruitment campaign before the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage candidates to submit their application at the earliest opportunity. Interview dates First round (virtual): During the week commencing 12 October 2026 Second round (in-person): During the week commencing 19 October 2026 No other media or agencies, please. The WI is proud to be an equal opportunities employer and values diversity. Reg. Charity No. 803793.

item.title: Bereavement Support Manager (Scotland)
item.description: Job description Provide and lead high-quality bereavement support to families, ensuring timely and compassionate responses to all enquiries. Oversee, develop and expand bereavement support services in Scotland in line with the charity’s strategic goal to support all bereaved families whose baby or young child dies suddenly and unexpectedly. Be the primary contact for and manage the bereavement support services in Scotland. Develop and manage, in partnership with the Head of Support and Information, the Befriender programme in Scotland. Work with the Head of Care of Next Infant (CONI) to ensure support is available for any bereaved family in Scotland with subsequent pregnancies. Provide emotional and practical support to families after a baby or young child’s sudden death, maintain ongoing contact and long-term support. Advocate for families to help them navigate the Child Death Review process; liaising with the various multi agency professionals involved including Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service, paediatricians and other professionals working in the child death review process. Act as a ‘Keyworker’ for families within the Child Death Review process where one is not already assigned. Cover and answer the bereavement support helpline and online enquiries responding within the set guidelines and KPIs for the department. Ensure any safeguarding concerns are actioned in accordance with the organisations Safeguarding policy. Send materials to bereaved contacts, including bereavement packs and follow up e-cards. Organise and facilitate face to face events for bereaved families including family days and memorial events to an agreed programme. Collaborate with the Engagement Team to develop and deliver bereavement support content for social media. Ensure the bereavement support services are promoted to bereaved families and professionals working with bereaved families in Scotland Join and participate in stakeholder and baby loss collaboration meetings and events. Represent and present the Lullaby Trust’s work externally including speaking at events to raise awareness of the service and organisation. Raise the profile of the service and organisation throughout Scotland, including networking face to face. Keep up to date with the bereavement support world including joining National Bereavement Alliance, Child Bereavement Network and research around grief and bereavement. Ensure all service records and databases are accurate, up to date, and maintained in line with organisational guidelines. Ensure all paperwork and databases are updated with each contact in line with the department guidelines, including Raiser’s Edge, Excel databases. Maintain ongoing knowledge and training on the Lullaby Trust’s advice and the scientific knowledge behind this advice. Collate statistics, as required on areas of work within the support services team. Assist with the services’ evaluation and impact processes including self-evaluation feedback. Provide other administrative support to the team as required. Other: Organisation Safer sleep for babies, Support for families Posted on: 25 September 2026 Closing date: 19 October 2026 at 13:00 Tags: Volunteering Management, Bereavement Support, Helpline, Safeguarding, Social / Support Work
